We introduce Tokamak-SI, which combines the labels and labeling methods of many earlier studies into a single scalable, time-aligned, and categorical dataset covering observations from confinement, detachment, alfven eigenmodes (AE), edge localized modes (ELM), sawtooth, tearing modes (TM), and resistive wall modes in DIII-D tokamak. Models based on this, which can extend the labels to new shots, match or beat earlier detectors on its labels, including for AE, ELM, and TM detection. Tokamak-SI is intended to enable task-specific benchmarking, physics-searchable archives, and direct identification of key events during an experiment.

Signal Processing.title: SEMAC: Spherical Energy Matching Ambisonics Codec for Efficient Higher-Order Ambisonics Compression
Signal Processing.summary: Higher-order Ambisonics (HOA) is an attractive format for immersive spatial audio, but its high channel count and directional properties present significant audio coding challenges. The widely deployed Opus audio codec supports HOA through Channel Mapping Families 2 and 3 (RFC 8486), which code and transmit every Ambisonics channel, so the bitrate grows quadratically with the spherical harmonic order. We introduce SEMAC, which instead represents an Ambisonics signal by a quantized full-order directional energy envelope together with fewer CELT-coded transport channels. CELT separates a per-band energy envelope from the signal shape and restores it after quantization, and SEMAC generalizes this principle to directional signals. Since the reduced transport spans only a lower-dimensional subspace, the decoder re-imposes the envelope observed at the encoder input, restoring the directional energy distribution at full order. A MUSHRA test on fifth-order material compares SEMAC against Opus CMF~3 in matched configurations at 512 and 768 kbit/s. SEMAC with 16 of 36 transport channels is rated above full-order CMF~3 at both rates, and at equal transport channel count above order truncation. The proposed SEMAC strategy of coding fewer transport channels with the directional envelope is found perceptually preferable to coding all HOA channels at low precision.
Signal Processing.comment: Submitted to IEEE ICASSP 2027

Signal Processing.title: Low-Complexity Wideband Channel Estimation for ISAC in Analog Millimeter-Wave Systems
Signal Processing.summary: Accurate wideband channel estimation is a key enabler for millimeter-wave (mmWave) integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems. In the narrowband scenario, the Transformed Spatial Domain Channel Estimation (TSDCE) method was previously shown to provide fast and accurate angle estimation with substantially lower complexity than conventional compressed-sensing approaches based on orthogonal matching pursuit (OMP). However, wideband ISAC scenarios additionally require delay estimation, making joint angle-delay sparse recovery computationally expensive due to the multidimensional dictionary search. In this paper, we propose a wideband extension of TSDCE, namely TSDCE-TD, which incorporates time-domain support and decouples angle and delay estimation. Two variations are proposed for delay estimation: TSDCE-TD (Dict), which uses a one-dimensional delay dictionary, and TSDCE-TD (FFT), which applies Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) zero-padding interpolation. Path estimates are iteratively refined through successive interference cancellation and alternating angle-delay updates. Simulation results show that the proposed methods outperform OMP-based baselines under practical dictionary sizes, while achieving comparable performance at high-resolution settings with substantially lower computational complexity. Moreover, the angle-delay estimates obtained using the proposed approach enable accurate single-anchor indoor localization in a ray-traced environment, achieving sub-20 cm positioning errors and satisfying practical indoor positioning requirements.
Signal Processing.comment: Accepted for publication in the 2026 IEEE 1st Annual Integrated Sensing and Communication Conference (ISAC)

Signal Processing.title: Reducing 6G Energy Consumption: TDD-Aligned Drain Voltage Modulation for Power Amplifiers
Signal Processing.summary: The Power Amplifier (PA) of a base station operates inefficiently at partial load, where back-off from the peak output power wastes supply headroom. Adapting the PA drain voltage to the instantaneous signal recovers this loss but requires frequent switching, increasing hardware cost. We propose TDD-Aligned Drain Voltage Modulation (TDD-DVM), a drain voltage modulation scheme that instead selects the drain voltage level once per Time-Division Duplex (TDD) period based on the downlink resource load and switches the voltage during the uplink window. This is enabled by the authors' previous work on POLITE link adaptation, which spreads the transmit power over resources left unused at partial load and moves the PA into a regime where a lower drain voltage suffices. In a 3GPP Urban Macro system-level simulation across traffic loads, we compare TDD-DVM against baseline approaches under conventional and POLITE link adaptation. At equal delivered throughput, TDD-DVM with POLITE keeps the packet failure ratio of the full drain voltage while consuming up to 35% less power than it under conventional link adaptation and up to 7% less than it under POLITE, roughly half of the gain of an idealized reference.
Signal Processing.comment: 6 pages, 5 figures. This work has been submitted to the IEEE for possible publication. Copyright may be transferred without notice, after which this version may no longer be accessible

Signal Processing.title: Leaky Coaxial Cable based Generalized Pinching-Antenna Systems with Dual-Port Feeding
Signal Processing.summary: By leveraging the distributed leakage radiation of leaky coaxial cables (LCXs), the concept of pinching antennas can be generalized from the conventional high-frequency waveguide based architectures to cable based structures in lower-frequency scenarios. This paper investigates an LCX based generalized pinching-antenna system with dual-port feeding. By enabling bidirectional excitation along each cable, the proposed design significantly enhances spatial degrees of freedom. A comprehensive channel model is developed to characterize intra-cable attenuation, bidirectional phase progression, slot based radiation, and wireless propagation. Based on this model, both analog and hybrid beamforming frameworks are studied with the objective of maximizing the minimum achievable data rate. For analog transmission, slot activation, port selection, and power allocation are jointly optimized using matching theory, coalitional games, and bisection based power control. For hybrid transmission, zero-forcing (ZF) digital precoding is incorporated to eliminate inter-user interference, thereby simplifying slot activation and enabling closed-form optimal power allocation. Simulation results demonstrate that dual-port feeding provides notable performance gains over single-port LCX systems and fixed-antenna benchmarks, validating the effectiveness of the proposed beamforming and resource allocation designs under various transmit power levels and cable parameters.

Signal Processing.title: On Orthogonal Recurrent Neural Networks Quantization
Signal Processing.summary: In recent years, Orthogonal Recurrent Neural Networks (ORNNs) have gained popularity due to their ability to manage tasks involving long-term dependencies, such as the Copy-task, and their linear complexity. However, existing ORNNs utilize full precision weights and activations, which prevents their deployment on compact devices. In this paper, we explore the quantization of the weight matrices in ORNNs, leading to Quantized approximately Orthogonal RNNs (QORNNs). The construction of such networks remained an open problem, acknowledged for its inherent instability. We propose and investigate two strategies to learn QORNN by combining quantization-aware training (QAT) and orthogonal projections. We also study post-training quantization of the activations for pure integer computation of the recurrent loop. The most efficient fully-quantized models are currently the only alternatives for solving the Copy-task with 1000 timesteps. They also surpass existing quantized models on tasks requiring long-term dependencies, such as permuted MNIST as well as some Internet of Things (IoT) tasks. However, they are less effective on tasks where long short-term memory (LSTMs) and other gated RNNs outperform ORNNs.
Signal Processing.comment: Progress in Artificial Intelligence, In press

Signal Processing.title: Multi-Timescale Context-Aware Radio Resource Optimization for Harmonious NTN-TN Coexistence: A Digital Twin and Open RAN Enabled Framework
Signal Processing.summary: Coexistence between non-terrestrial networks (NTNs) and terrestrial networks (TNs) is essential for future wireless systems, but terrestrial downlink transmissions can generate harmful aggregate interference at low-Earth orbit (LEO) satellite receivers. We present DT-STABLE, an Open Radio Access Network (O-RAN)-enabled, digital twin (DT)-assisted framework for context-aware NTN-TN coexistence. Using site-specific information, the DT estimates interference at LEO satellites, enabling proactive management with reduced real-time measurement overhead. We formulate joint beam activation and user association under RF-chain limits, load balancing, and aggregate satellite interference constraints; prove NP-hardness; and develop an efficient DT-guided scheduling algorithm. DT-STABLE couples short-timescale radio resource adaptation with periodic mid- and long-timescale DT updates through standardized O-RAN interfaces. Site-specific 28 GHz simulations under worst-case satellite geometry and low elevation angles show that DT-STABLE balances rate and interference utility, achieving 89.63% interference-to-noise ratio (INR) satisfaction and a mean sum rate of 210.96 bps/Hz, with nearly 100% INR satisfaction when satellite protection is prioritized. The framework reduces beam measurement overhead by 99.71% relative to exhaustive sweeping and achieves up to 33.1 times lower runtime than the Gurobi-based exact optimization benchmark.
Signal Processing.comment: Submitted to IEEE for possible publication

Signal Processing.title: U-NeXt: General-purpose event detection for neonatal EEG
Signal Processing.summary: We developed U-NeXt, a general framework for neonatal electroencephalography (EEG) event detection based on semantic segmentation. Its convolutional encoder-decoder directly segments individual channels using long input segments to preserve temporal context. A shared architecture and training framework were developed using low-voltage interval, artefact, and seizure datasets containing 51, 98, and 278 neonates, respectively, comprising over 11,000 hours of EEG and 82,000 annotated events. Performance was compared with task-specific ConvNeXt classifiers. For seizure detection, we also evaluated U-NeXt+, trained on an expanded dataset. Both U-NeXt variants and the ConvNeXt baseline were evaluated on two independent held-out seizure datasets, Helsinki and Cork, comprising 130 neonates, with recordings annotated by three experts. U-NeXt improved detection across all three event types, with particular gains in sensitivity for short events. U-NeXt+ achieved Matthews correlation coefficients of 0.862 and 0.891 on Helsinki and Cork, respectively, and improved hourly seizure burden correlations by 30-40% relative to ConvNeXt. U-NeXt+ met the criterion for expert-level performance on both datasets (p < 0.001). In separate computational benchmarks, U-NeXt reduced batch inference time relative to ConvNeXt by 254-fold on a central processing unit and 200-fold on a graphics processing unit. A common segmentation framework improves detection across diverse neonatal EEG event types while substantially reducing inference time. Accurate seizure burden estimates and performance comparable to expert reviewers support its potential use in continuous monitoring and clinical decision support.

Signal Processing.title: Clean-label Poisoning Attack and Defense Game for Federated Learning in Vehicular Networks
Signal Processing.summary: This paper studies interactions between clean-label poisoning attack and defense in vehicular networks using federated learning (FL). Basic Safety Message (BSM) classification for anomaly detection is modeled as a distributed learning problem over a vehicular network with dynamic topology. As a critical threat to FL, a feature-space clean-label attack is introduced, wherein benign samples are perturbed toward malicious feature extremes, degrading class separability while preserving labels. To counter this, a feature-consistency relabeling defense is proposed to detect and relabel suspicious samples. A game-theoretic framework is developed to capture attack-defense interactions and characterize equilibrium strategies based on attack effectiveness and cost parameters. Results show that the attack scales effectively with compromised nodes, while the proposed defense keeps attack success low without degrading clean accuracy and shifts equilibrium regions toward attack-averse regimes.

Signal Processing.title: System Design Framework for Distributed Space Antennas Using Electromagnetic Formation Flight
Signal Processing.summary: Distributed space antennas using electromagnetic formation flight (EMFF) are a promising architecture for large-aperture, long-life space communication systems. Their system design, however, is governed by coupled constraints on antenna performance, satellite mass, power generation, coil geometry, and formation-keeping power. This paper proposes a system-level design framework for EMFF-based distributed space antennas. It links phased-array requirements with satellite and formation-system sizing for a static grid under a fixed total system mass. Before system-level optimization, distributed-control simulations are used to derive a control index that quantifies the formation-maintenance requirement. This index is integrated into an optimization problem with a user-defined objective and sizing, power, coil, and sidelobe-envelope constraints. Parametric case studies examine the margin magnetic moment, prescribed transmit power, and large inter-satellite spacing. Results show that increasing system mass improves footprint reduction or effective isotropic radiated power only while satellite-level design headroom remains. In direct-to-device cases with 0.15-m spacing, generated power and coil-geometry constraints dominate the feasible aperture. In the 0.30-m large-spacing case, the required coil burden can exceed satellite-level mass, size, and power capacities, making the design infeasible despite favorable communication performance. Higher-fidelity simulations of representative designs evaluate formation maintenance under nonlinear $J_2$ dynamics and antenna gain with mutual coupling, further supporting the framework's usefulness for preliminary design. The proposed framework enables the design and evaluation of feasible static grid-based EMFF distributed antennas under coupled antenna, satellite, and control constraints.
Signal Processing.comment: Submitted to IEEE Access and currently under review

Signal Processing.title: Automated Fetal Magnetocardiography Reconstruction Using a Biophysical Forward Model
Signal Processing.summary: Objective: Fetal magnetocardiography (fMCG) enables early detection of cardiac disease by non-invasively measuring fetal electrophysiological activity. However, current signal estimation methods for fMCG require complex, labor-intensive human processing because they rely on blind source separation or template-based projection techniques. Methods: We propose an automated signal reconstruction approach that recovers fetal and maternal cardiac activity from fMCG measurements without manual annotation. Our approach leverages the relationship between measurements and cardiac signals via a biophysically grounded forward model that represents cardiac sources as time-varying magnetic dipoles. This enables reconstruction of physiologically interpretable three-dimensional vectorcardiographic signals along with their spatial position. Results: Validation on synthetic data with known ground truth confirms accurate recovery of cardiac source parameters. On real fMCG recordings, the reconstruction shows strong agreement with established reference methods. Conclusion: The proposed forward-model approach automatically reconstructs fetal and maternal cardiac activity from fMCG recordings and produces signals in an interpretable vectorcardiographic source domain. Significance: Automated, interpretable fMCG reconstruction could make fetal cardiac assessment more reliable and support potential translation into prenatal care.
Signal Processing.comment: 29 pages, 16 figures. Includes supplementary material. Published in IEEE Transactions on Biomedical Engineering. Code: https://github.com/MLI-lab/fetal_magnetocardiography

Signal Processing.title: EMG Tokenization Preserves Movement Information at a Fraction of the Bitrate
Signal Processing.summary: Wireless electromyography (EMG) interfaces must balance electrode coverage against transmission bandwidth. Here, we show that compact EMG tokens substantially reduce payload while retaining information for three-dimensional hand-pose decoding. We evaluate two causal tokenizers fitted without pose labels: an encoder pretrained to reconstruct EMG spectra and one based on SPAR, an engineered spectral-spatial representation of neighbouring electrodes. In personalized, within-session experiments with 320-channel EMG from nine participants, we compare tokenized and continuous features using matched decoder architectures and training procedures. Averaged across decoders, tokenization changed mean error by +0.01 mm for SPAR (95% confidence interval: -0.12 to 0.14) and +0.45 mm for the learned representation (0.10 to 0.82). Both increases met a 1 mm non-inferiority criterion. Stored token arrays reduced payloads 41-fold relative to raw EMG and 36-fold relative to continuous SPAR features. On sampled windows of the public emg2pose benchmark's test partition, absolute differences in mean error between learned tokens and continuous features were below 0.05 mm across 176 participants and in the subset of 20 participants unseen during training. Electrode coverage, calibration, and unseen recordings affected SPAR decoding more than quantization did. In a computational benchmark, optimized SPAR generated tokens for 63 channels within 20 ms on a Cortex-M55 microcontroller. These findings support tokenization as a compact interface between wearable sensing and movement decoding, allowing decoders to be updated while the wearable encoder and transmitted representation remain fixed.
Signal Processing.comment: 11 pages, 7 figures; 12-page supplement included. Supplementary Data 1-9 (CSV) are provided as ancillary files

Signal Processing.title: Channel orthogonalization via movable antennas
Signal Processing.summary: This paper investigates the orthogonalization of far-field multiuser channels through the optimal positioning of the antennas constituting an array. To solve the ensuing continuous geometry optimization problem, a graph-theoretic framework is introduced that maps pairwise user channel correlations to graph edges, translating channel orthogonalization into a discrete graph-covering problem on a complete graph. The minimum number of array antennas required for orthogonalization is established for 1D, 2D, and 3D array geometries, and a binary linear program is formulated that identifies the most compact array attaining such orthogonality. The graph framework is also shown to accommodate null-steering scenarios and multipath channels. Furthermore, a fundamental tradeoff is revealed whereby relaxing exact orthogonality to near-orthogonality reduces the antenna count at the expense of a less compact array, and a method is presented to enforce minimum antenna spacings without sacrificing orthogonality.

Signal Processing.title: An Evidence-Guided Framework for Tissue-Barrier Impedance Review: Deletion and Resistance Sensitivity
Signal Processing.summary: Reviewing tissue-barrier impedance requires connecting spectral anomalies with resistance estimates and experimental context. We present an evidence-guided framework that coordinates numerical checks and traceable actions for human review. In-house simulations assess the effect of removing flagged frequencies, public datasets test model adaptation, and local measurements demonstrate the review workflow. Removing flagged frequencies reduced resistance error under quadratic objectives, whereas robust fitting showed little average benefit from deletion and a mean error increase for endpoint-pair perturbations. High errors clustered around a few fitted circuit parameter sets, highlighting the value of examining parameter identifiability. Under the tested noise and perturbation conditions, these findings support robust full-spectrum estimation, flag-guided inspection, and matched sensitivity checks.
Signal Processing.comment: 5 pages, 3 figures, 3 tables

Signal Processing.title: Beyond Channel Data: Configuration-Enriched Radio Foundation Models
Signal Processing.summary: This paper proposes incorporating channel configuration (CFG) information into Radio Foundation Model (RFM) pre-training and demonstrates that the resulting CFG-enriched embeddings serve as effective inductive priors for downstream tasks under label scarcity. We compare the proposed embeddings with raw channel tokens and multiple baseline models, under three different data regimes, for multiple downstream tasks --- Line-of-Sight/Non-Line-of-Sight (LoS/NLoS) classification, timing advance (TA) estimation, and beam selection. Evaluation is done in both in-distribution and out-of-distribution configuration settings. Experimental outcomes show that the proposed embeddings consistently outperform and/or are competitive to the baselines, across experiments in both seen and unseen configuration scenarios.
Signal Processing.comment: Submitted to IEEE ICC 2027 for review

Signal Processing.title: Short-Range Microwave Interprobe Coupling in a Brain-Mimicking Phantom and Ex-Vivo Brain
Signal Processing.summary: Objectives: Short-range wireless links (microwave range) between closely spaced devices in brain tissue are relevant to neural interfaces and intracranial sensing, yet the change in coupling between two such devices caused by a finite volume of brain-like tissue has rarely been measured directly. Technology or Method: This work characterizes a printed, microstrip-fed, parasitic-strip-loaded tapered-slot coupling probe in which only a partially inserted 12-mm wire enters the medium, while the printed structure remains outside. Results: Two fabricated probes showed a measured free-space -10-dB reflection band of 5.78 to 6.86 GHz and a fractional bandwidth of approximately 17.1%, consistent with full-wave simulation. In a controlled two-probe experiment, a homogeneous agar-gelatin-saline brain-mimicking phantom was introduced and removed while the probe arrangement and measurement conditions were retained. Introducing the phantom increased the measured transmission coefficient near 6.3 GHz by approximately 16 dB, and this differential was reproduced across repeated trials. More than five measurements in ex vivo goat brain followed the phantom transmission response within approximately 1.5 dB across the 5.78-6.86-GHz band. Time-domain analysis of the phantom-present link gave a system root-mean-square delay spread of approximately 210 ps. Full-wave dosimetry predicted a peak 1-g-averaged specific absorption rate of 1.05 W/kg for approximately 0.49 W accepted power. Conclusions and Clinical or Biological Impact: These results provide an experimentally validated reference for short-range probe coupling in brain-like media and support phantom-based bench evaluation of minimally invasive intracranial probes before in vivo studies.
Signal Processing.comment: 8 pages, 10 figures, 3 tables

Signal Processing.title: U-STS-LLM: A Unified Spatio-Temporal Steered Large Language Model for Traffic Prediction and Imputation
Signal Processing.summary: Accurate spatio-temporal cellular traffic analysis is fundamental to the reliable operation of modern mobile networks, as it underpins load forecasting for congestion avoidance and missing-data imputation for continuity despite transmission errors. While deeply connected, forecasting and imputation have historically evolved as separate sub-fields. Existing models are typically task-specific, decouple temporal and spatial modeling, and rely on cascaded designs that accumulate errors and latency. Meanwhile, adapting pre-trained LLMs for this domain often leaves spatial structure under-guided and tends to overfit on limited data. To bridge these gaps, we propose U-STS-LLM, a unified framework built on a partially frozen spatio-temporally attentive (PFSTA) LLM backbone. A Dynamic Spatio-Temporal Attention Bias Generator synthesizes a persistent functional graph with transient nodal states to steer attention, while a lightweight parallel branch yields a stable local estimate fused via a Gated Adaptive Fusion, confining the LLM to residual correction. Trained under a unified multi-task objective, the model attains state-of-the-art results with low trainable-parameter overhead. Extensive experiments on real-world cellular traffic datasets demonstrate the effectiveness and transferability of U-STS-LLM, achieving average RMSE improvements of 23.7% over the strongest baselines in forecasting and 13.1% in imputation, with further gains exceeding 33% in zero-shot transfer to unseen network regions.
Signal Processing.comment: 13 pages, 6 figures

Signal Processing.title: Time-Varying Kernel Density Deconvolution using Random Finite Set Theory for State Noise Identification
Signal Processing.summary: This paper focuses on the noise density identification for state-space models of linear time-varying systems. The density knowledge is essential for the optimal design of any modern state estimator, fault detector, or controller. The proposed method builds on newly derived algorithms for (i) calculation of the measurement prediction residue being independent of the state and linear in state and measurement noises, and (ii) kernel density deconvolution for process with non-stationary statistical properties based on the random finite set theory. The proposed method provides consistent estimate of the state noise density without any prior knowledge on distribution family, which is a unique property in noise identification state-of-the-art. The method is further enhanced by an automatic selection of the user-defined parameters, and is evaluated in numerical examples. The examples demonstrate not only the superior performance of the proposed method in terms of accuracy and robustness among others in ultra-wide-band-inspired tracking scenario, but also the importance of the correct state noise density identification for optimal state estimation and fault detection. The paper is supplemented with a MATLAB implementation.

Signal Processing.title: Type-based Over-the-Air Computation
Signal Processing.summary: Over-the-air computation (OAC) exploits the superposition property of wireless channels to compute functions of distributed data, reducing the communication overhead associated with its multiple access. However, existing OAC frameworks are often designed around specific classes of functions, limiting their applicability to more general nonlinear computations. This paper investigates type-based multiple access (TBMA) as a general framework for OAC, enabling the receiver to recover a histogram of the distributed observations and compute a broad class of functions without modifying the underlying communication scheme. We formulate TBMA as a histogram estimation problem and propose two digital detectors. We prove that a low-complexity successive cancellation algorithm achieves the optimal maximum-likelihood (ML) performance. We derive analytical expressions for the mean squared error (MSE) and compare TBMA with conventional schemes in terms of computation accuracy, transmission duration, bandwidth and energy consumption. Numerical experiments validate the analytical results and demonstrate that, unlike existing OAC techniques, TBMA exhibits an exponential MSE decay with increasing signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and constant transmit energy, independently of the function being computed. These findings position TBMA as a step toward more versatile OAC architectures, compatible with existing transmission schemes, and broadening the range of functions that can be computed directly over the wireless channel and enabling new possibilities for distributed computation and decision-making.
Signal Processing.comment: Manuscript submitted for publication in IEEE Transactions on Wireless Communications

Signal Processing.title: Incremental-Smoothing-Based ARAIM Protection Levels for Tightly Coupled GNSS/IMU Integration in Urban Canyons
Signal Processing.summary: Protection levels (PLs) bound position errors under specified fault hypotheses and risk budgets, but advanced re-ceiver autonomous integrity monitoring (ARAIM) is formulated for snapshot GNSS estimation rather than the correlated poste-rior of tightly coupled GNSS/IMU factor graph optimization (FGO). This paper formulates ARAIM solution separation and PL computation on the FGO posterior. Because current-epoch pseudorange factors enter only the current-state block of the fixed-lag information matrix, the fault-excluded position covari-ance, solution separation, and nominal-bias propagation follow exactly from the linearized current-state marginal, which re-tains correlations with velocity, IMU-bias, and clock states and with historical information. Woodbury updates with selected-output evaluation compute these quantities for fault-free, single-satellite, constellation-wide, and second-order hypotheses with-out repeated full-state inversion or graph re-optimization. Sur-rounding monitoring layers screen measurements, handle post-fit outliers, and determine PL validity and availability. In two road experiments, both nominal sequences achieve 100% hori-zontal and vertical empirical bounding over PL-valid epochs, with a maximum error-to-PL ratio of 0.96. Normalized errors show that the posterior covariance alone does not capture slowly varying ranging biases: a covariance-only bound computed from the same posteriors retains no resolvable margin, and strong temporal correlation limits the empirical evidence to consisten-cy checks rather than validation of the integrity budget. On identical Experiment A posteriors, the proposed method reduces fault-hypothesis evaluation and PL solving time by 65.2% rela-tive to direct full-state inversion with matching integrity deci-sions, and controlled fault injections demonstrate fail-safe PL invalidation while navigation continues.
Signal Processing.comment: 9 figures

Signal Processing.title: Hierarchical Coherent Imaging of Composite Anisotropic Moving Targets in ISAC
Signal Processing.summary: In Integrated Sensing and Communication (ISAC) networks, distributed devices can cooperate to produce radio images of the surrounding environment by exploiting phase-coherent signal processing. However, existing imaging methods are not well-suited for composite moving targets with multiple independently moving extended parts. This is due to simplistic isotropic scattering models and the lack of methods to compensate for distinct Doppler shifts from each component, which leads to image defocusing. We propose MOSAIC, the first hierarchical imaging method for composite moving targets using distributed User Equipments (UEs) and a single ISAC Base Station (BS). MOSAIC generates high-resolution images of each target part and estimates its velocity vector. Coherent imaging is performed within selected clusters of UEs observing a locally isotropic scattering from each part, while cluster-specific images are combined non-coherently across wide angles to improve the reconstruction. To mitigate Doppler-induced defocusing, Doppler components are pre-compensated before coherent imaging, turning a limitation into an additional means of resolving multiple target parts. This also enables low-complexity velocity estimation by associating Doppler frequencies across UEs. Simulations show a 35% to 45% improvement in image quality compared to existing methods, in terms of Wasserstein distance, and dm/s-level velocity estimation accuracy.
Signal Processing.comment: 16 pages, 15 figures, 2 table

Signal Processing.title: NECTAR: Automatic Negative Clue Estimation via Centroid-Space Mapping for Target Speaker Extraction
Signal Processing.summary: Target speaker extraction (TSE) aims to extract a desired speaker from a mixture using auxiliary clues such as enrollment speech. An interferer-related representation can provide a useful negative clue for TSE, but such information is not directly available from the target enrollment. To derive this representation from the observed mixture, we analyze the relationship between the speaker representations of a speech mixture and its constituent speakers. Our analysis shows that the mixture centroid lies near the midpoint of its constituent speaker centroids, whereas this relationship does not hold for single-utterance embeddings. Based on this observation, we propose NECTAR, NEgative Clue for TARget speaker extraction, which automatically derives an interferer-related negative clue from the mixture using the centroid-space relationship. We further introduce a Centroid-Space Mapper (CSM) to estimate the required centroid representations from a mixture and a target enrollment. NECTAR achieves the highest SI-SDRi on Libri2Mix among the compared systems trained on LibriSpeech train-clean-100, reaching 16.18 dB.

Signal Processing.title: Task-Based Evaluation of Raw Radar Data Compression: A Pre-Registered Study of Where Classical Codecs Fail to Preserve Target Detection, and Why
Signal Processing.summary: Synthetic aperture radar (SAR) systems collect raw I/Q echo data at rates that exceed downlink capacity; fielded systems compress onboard with block-adaptive quantization (BAQ/FDBAQ). Proposed replacements, including learned compression, are evaluated with image-quality metrics (PSNR, SSIM, SQNR); none measures whether the data still supports its operational use. We introduce a task-based evaluation methodology for raw radar compression, with a published pre-registration trail: codecs are scored after SAR focusing against a two-sided criterion -- a CFAR detection-retention floor and a spurious-detection budget at matched threshold -- using frozen task models trained once on uncompressed data. On Sentinel-1 stripmap Level-0 data the evaluation brackets the fielded FDBAQ operating point at the resolution of the BAQ grid (3-bit BAQ sustains utility at 6.12 bits per complex sample; 2-bit does not), with a reported lattice artifact found to change retention by at most 0.004. Under the final plane-mapping rule no classical configuration sustains utility below 4.86 bits per complex sample on this scene. Energy concentration after focusing delivers the predicted retention gain (0.888 vs 0.691 at 2 bits) but converts it into target-adjacent false alarms for wavelet and block-transform codecs alike: a retention-only rule certifies focused-domain JPEG2000 at 4 bits while it produces 2.5 times the tolerable spurious count. On AFRL Gotcha GMTI data (airborne, never compressed onboard) the frontier is bracketed at 7.4-8.0 bits per complex sample and the same trade reappears; on an Umbra spotlight image JPEG2000 passes the retention floor at 2, 1, and 0.5 bits while producing 10-14 times the spurious budget. We report the full pre-registration trail, including the chronology of the criterion's two clauses, one retracted overclaim, and a bounded negative result for a small learned codec.
Signal Processing.comment: 16 pages, 9 figures, 5 tables. v2: corrects the retention-only counterfactual (Secs. I, III-A, V-C); states the criterion's commit chronology; adds an Umbra image-domain scene and previously unreported learned-codec runs; scopes the frontier to its mapping rule and grid resolution; reconciles numbers. No new experiments. Code and results log: https://github.com/signalcurrent/radar-codec-eval

Signal Processing.title: Resilience in Wireless: A Lyapunov-Constrained Integrated Sensing, Communication, and Control Approach
Signal Processing.summary: Traditional wireless networks mainly use reliability metrics to evaluate network stability. However, reliable data delivery alone cannot fully characterize network stability under variations in wireless environments and physical tasks. Wireless network resilience provides a broader perspective by describing the ability to maintain acceptable service and recover from disruptions. We develop an integrated sensing, communication, and control (ISCC) framework that incorporates communication reliability and sensing error into a state-dependent Lyapunov constraint for adaptive BS beamforming. The resulting transmit-power minimization problem is non-convex and solved via semidefinite relaxation and successive convex approximation with rank-one recovery. We establish conditional mean-square ultimate boundedness, while simulations demonstrate improved resilience and faster recovery over a static baseline.
Signal Processing.comment: 13 pages

Signal Processing.title: QoE-Driven Hybrid Resource Allocation for Multi-User OFDMA Semantic Communications
Signal Processing.summary: In this paper, we develop a quality-of-experience (QoE)-driven hybrid resource allocation framework for multi-user downlink orthogonal frequency-division multiple access semantic communication systems, where the hybrid framework jointly handles continuous and discrete decision variables. Specifically, we formulate a mixed continuous-discrete optimization problem to jointly optimize transmit power, subcarrier allocation, and semantic decisions under coupled power and spectrum constraints. To better characterize semantic service quality, we propose a preference-inverse multiplicative exponential QoE that is bounded and non-compensatory, capturing the intrinsic ``both-required'' property of semantic rate and similarity. To solve the optimization problem, we develop a projection-based multi-agent deep deterministic policy gradient framework that enforces feasibility for continuous and discrete actions. Furthermore, we integrate Gumbel-softmax relaxation with an adaptive performance-driven temperature annealing scheme to enhance the learning of discrete semantic decisions. Simulation results demonstrate that our proposed framework achieves superior convergence, greater stability, and higher QoE compared to the conventional QoE design and penalty-based or fixed-temperature baselines, highlighting the benefits of our QoE design and the effectiveness of hybrid decision learning in semantic communications.
Signal Processing.comment: 6 pages, 8 figures

Signal Processing.title: Pinching Antenna Systems (PASS): Principles, Positioning and Opportunities
Signal Processing.summary: Pinching-antenna systems (PASS) have garnered significant attention owing to their ability to enhance the capacity and coverage of wireless networks by guiding electromagnetic waves through waveguides before radiation. As such, PASS are regarded as promising enabling technologies for sixth-generation (6G) communication networks. In this paper, we present a comprehensive survey of the state of the art in PASS, covering operating principles, positioning methodologies, performance evaluation, resource allocation, and the application of artificial intelligence (AI) to PASS-enhanced wireless networks. We first introduce the fundamental principles of PASS from both materials and physics perspectives. Building on this foundation, we present positioning methodologies for both the user side and the base station side. We then evaluate the communication performance of PASS in both uplink and downlink scenarios under different blockage models. Furthermore, we systematically review existing designs for PASS-enhanced wireless networks from a performance optimization perspective. Finally, we survey research efforts that leverage AI to address challenges in dynamic and complex scenarios.
Signal Processing.comment: 30 pages, 21 figures

Signal Processing.title: Bistatic Target Detection by Exploiting Both Deterministic Pilots and Unknown Random Data Payloads
Signal Processing.summary: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) plays a crucial role in 6G, enabling innovative applications such as drone surveillance, urban air mobility, and low-altitude logistics. However, the hybrid ISAC signal, which comprises deterministic pilot and random data payload components, poses challenges for target detection due to two reasons: 1) these two components cause coupled shifts in both the mean and variance of the received signal, and 2) the random data payloads are typically unknown to the sensing receiver in the bistatic setting. Unfortunately, these challenges could not be tackled by existing target detection algorithms. In this paper, a generalized likelihood ratio test (GLRT)-based detector is derived by leveraging the known deterministic pilots and the statistical characteristics of the unknown random data payloads. Due to the analytical intractability of exact performance characterization, we perform an asymptotic analysis for the false alarm probability and detection probability of the proposed detector. The results reveal a deterministic-random trade-off: the deterministic pilots enhance detection through a target-induced mean shift, while the random data payloads provide an additional covariance-domain target signature but simultaneously introduce statistical uncertainty due to their unknown realizations. Simulations validate the theoretical findings and demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed detector, which highlights the necessity of designing a dedicated detector to fully exploit the signaling resources assigned to random data payloads.
Signal Processing.comment: Integrated sensing and communications, bistatic target detection, random signals, false alarm probability, detection probability

Signal Processing.title: Automated screening of Parkinson's Disease using Smooth Pursuit Eye Movements
Signal Processing.summary: Smooth pursuit eye movements are frequently altered in Parkinson's disease, but previous studies have relied mainly on conventional parameters that describe the relationship between gaze and target. This study investigates whether complexity and nonlinear dynamics measures of the gaze position sequences can support the automatic screening of Parkinson's disease. Gaze position sequences were recorded with a video eye tracker in 41 participants with early Parkinson's disease and 47 healthy controls during 12 smooth pursuit tasks. Four experimental frameworks and four embedding delay strategies were compared. The selected experimental setting combined baseline wander removal with a fixed embedding delay. After feature selection, a support vector machine was trained for each task and axis and their outputs were combined in a mixture of experts. The pipeline was developed in 70 participants and evaluated on an external test set of 18 participants. On the external test set, the pipeline obtained an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.86. The most informative features described less persistent and more irregular gaze position sequences in Parkinson's disease, mainly along the horizontal axis. These results support complexity and nonlinear dynamics measures of smooth pursuit as candidate markers for Parkinson's disease screening, pending validation in larger independent cohorts.
Signal Processing.comment: 23 pages, 8 figures, including supplementary material

Signal Processing.title: Graph Spectral Series and Its Signatures
Signal Processing.summary: Bandlimitedness is a central modeling assumption in graph signal processing (GSP), but many graph signals exhibit substantial energy throughout the graph-frequency domain. We introduce a new framework for analyzing such non-bandlimited signals by treating their graph Fourier spectra as ordered sequences and representing them with path signatures. Specifically, motivated by the observation that non-bandlimited graph spectra often display rough, time-series like behavior, we introduce the notion of graph spectral series and develop a signature-based representation that captures global spectral structure without frequency truncation. We establish conditions under which the proposed representation is continuous and characterize its information-preserving properties. We further provide an asymptotic interpretation of graph spectral series for sequences of expanding graphs. Experiments on real-world trend-prediction and change-detection tasks show that signature features can improve performance over representations based directly on the original graph signals. The proposed approach provides a novel principled signature-based tool for analyzing non-bandlimited graph signals.

Signal Processing.title: Multi-Functional Chirp Signalling for Next-Generation Multi-Carrier Wireless Networks: Communications, Sensing and ISAC Perspectives
Signal Processing.summary: To meet the increasingly demanding quality-of-service requirements of the next-generation multi-carrier mobile networks, it is essential to design multi-functional signalling schemes facilitating efficient, flexible, and reliable communication and sensing in complex wireless environments. As a compelling candidate, we advocate chirp signalling, beneficially amalgamating sequences (e.g., Zadoff-Chu sequences) with waveforms (e.g., chirp spread spectrum and frequency-modulated continuous wave (FMCW) radar), given their resilience against doubly selective channels. Besides chirp sequences, a wide range of chirp waveforms is considered, ranging from FMCW to affine frequency-division multiplexing (AFDM), to create a promising chirp multicarrier waveform. This study also highlights the advantages of such waveforms in supporting reliable high-mobility communications, plus integrated sensing and communications (ISAC). Finally, we outline several emerging research directions for chirp signalling designs.
Signal Processing.comment: 9 pages, 6 figures, submitted to IEEE Wireless Communications

Signal Processing.title: Physical Layer Security in Chirp Permuted AFBM
Signal Processing.summary: We propose a physical-layer security scheme for affine filter bank modulation (AFBM), a waveform proposed for sixth-generation (6G) integrated sensing and communications (ISAC). AFBM contains two discrete affine Fourier transforms, one for precoding and one for spreading, and the scheme permutes, with one secret key per transform, the chirp sequence that each transform places between two Fourier stages. A wrong key is then conjugated by a discrete Fourier transform into a dense matrix, the restoration of complex orthogonality fails, and the intrinsic filter-bank interference reaches the detector. Over a doubly-dispersive channel, an eavesdropper with perfect channel state information, co-located with the legitimate receiver and holding either key wrong, keeps a bit error rate near 0.5 and a rate below 0.09 bit/symbol, also under a blind carrier-phase attack. Compared with a single-permutation variant, the double scheme costs about 2 dB of peak-to-average power ratio and enlarges the search space from 10^61 to 10^93.
Signal Processing.comment: Currently 6 pages, 6 figures

Signal Processing.title: Impact of Synchronization Offsets and CSI Feedback Delays on Coherent Joint Transmission in Distributed MIMO-OFDM
Signal Processing.summary: This paper studies the impact of synchronization offsets and CSI feedback delay on coherent joint transmission (CJT) in distributed MIMO-OFDM systems. Unlike conventional co-located MIMO, distributed CJT is highly sensitive to transmitter-dependent synchronization impairments because coherent combining requires phase, frequency, and timing alignment across geographically separated transmitters. Received signal models are derived for residual timing offsets, carrier frequency offsets (CFOs), sampling clock offsets (SCOs), phase noise, and channel variations accumulated during channel state information (CSI) feedback delay. The corresponding spectral efficiency (SE) expressions quantify the degradation in capacity due to loss in coherent-combining gain caused by residual phase rotations, inter-carrier interference (ICI), and precoder misalignment. The SE expressions are numerically evaluated to determine synchronization requirements for maintaining negligible SE degradation, yielding the following findings: a Gaussian-distributed start-time jitter with a standard deviation below 10\% of the sampling period results in negligible SE degradation, with the SE loss decreasing from 0.68\% at an SNR of 0 dB to 0.17\% at 40 dB. A normalized CFO standard deviation of 0.001 also results in negligible ICI-induced degradation, with the SE loss increasing from 0.05\% at an SNR of 0 dB to 2\% at 40 dB. At an SNR of 26 dB, limiting the SE loss to 5\% yields feasible operating points with clock-error standard deviations up to 50 ppb, Doppler-delay products up to 0.1, and phase-tracking error standard deviations up to $40^{\circ}$ at carrier frequency of 3.5 GHz with 30 kHz sub-carrier spacing with 15.36 MHz sampling rate.

Systems and Control.title: Classical, Machine Learning, and Hybrid Solvers for Partial Differential Equations: An Evidence-Weighted Review and Decision Framework
Systems and Control.summary: Machine learning for partial differential equations raises a practical question: when are classical, learned, or hybrid solvers justified? This survey compares the three families in a decision framework organized by data availability, query volume, and certification needs. An amortization law, tested on parametric Darcy flow, shows that surrogates trained on solver-generated data break even only after many queries, beyond thirty thousand for errors below one percent. An evidence ladder, a benchmark reanalysis, and three case studies show that claims of speedup and generalization carry the weakest evidence. Solver choice should follow regime, query volume, and evidence quality, not method novelty.

Systems and Control.title: Polyhedral RIS Architecture with Quantum-Assisted Facet Selection for Uniform Coverage
Systems and Control.summary: Reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RISs) direct coverage toward moving user equipment (UE), but practical deployments involve discrete phase control, uncertain facet positions, and UE mobility, which require the problem to be re-solved continually. We consider these challenges for the chamfered hexagonal polyhedral RIS, which provides nearly uniform coverage. With both incidence and departure angles, we bound in closed form the gain loss of its best facet relative to the best possible reflecting facet, include the known b-bit quantization loss, and extend the bound to joint random mounting errors of all facets. For a precoded multi-user downlink, each facet-selection subproblem of the max-min rate design is shown to be an exact quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO) problem, suited to repeated time-constrained solving. The deployment of the base station in relation to the RIS allows the polyhedral surface to bring down the percentage of dead zones in vertical planar panels from 77% to 0.3% and increase the minimum rate by 34% relative to the STAR panel. The simulated annealing algorithm finds the optimum solution in 95% of the cases. The quantum approximation algorithm fails to do so.
Systems and Control.comment: This work has been submitted to the IEEE WCL for possible publication. Copyright may be transferred without notice, after which this version may no longer be accessible

Systems and Control.title: Trust-Region Benders for Scalable Multiperiod Expansion Planning for Transmission and Storage
Systems and Control.summary: Transmission expansion planning (TEP) seeks to identify cost-effective investment strategies that enable power systems to reliably meet future demand, while accounting for the location, timing, and operational impacts of infrastructure upgrades. As demand grows and renewable penetration increases, there is growing interest in jointly modeling energy storage investments to enhance operational flexibility. This work presents a multiperiod formulation that co-optimizes transmission reconductoring and energy storage installation across multiple planning periods. To solve the resulting large-scale problem efficiently, a Benders decomposition with per-period trust-region stabilization and a relaxation-based warm-start procedure is proposed. The approach is demonstrated on a 2,000-bus Texas system, producing an investment plan spanning 2030-2045 with optimality gap below 1.0%, and is compared against a rolling-horizon approach to highlight the benefits of multiperiod coordination.
Systems and Control.comment: Presented at PowerUp 2026, September 9-11, 2026, Boulder, Colorado

Systems and Control.title: Density control of large-scale multi-agent systems via tuning of agent interactions
Systems and Control.summary: Collective behavior in biological systems emerges through adaptive interactions among units, enabling large populations to coordinate without centralized control. This mechanism raises the question of whether collective behavior in engineered multi-agent systems can likewise be regulated by modifying the interaction law between agents, rather than by directly controlling individual units. To answer this question, we consider large-scale multi-agent systems evolving on a ring and treat the interaction kernel as a time-varying control variable whose evolution regulates the collective dynamics. Using a mean-field formulation, we develop a framework for the analysis and design of kernel-based controllers. We derive explicit conditions for controllability in application-relevant scenarios, and synthesize a state-feedback controller to regulate the kernel dynamics, validated on the microscopic, discrete dynamics. Numerical simulations demonstrate the approach's effectiveness and robustness to unmodeled perturbations. This work constitutes a first step in the design of bio-inspired control strategies for large-scale multi-agent systems by modulation of interactions between agents.

Systems and Control.title: Cross-Scenario Controller Parameter Transformation from Real-World Driving Data through Flow Matching
Systems and Control.summary: Advanced Driver Assistance Systems have become increasingly widespread, aiming to support drivers, reduce workload, and improve traffic safety. However, many systems are rarely used because their behavior feels unnatural and does not match individual driving behavior. The growing availability of large-scale, real-world human driving data enables more human-like and driver-individual assistance functions. This paper formulates the adaptation of Adaptive Cruise Control parameters as a driver-individual scenario-to-scenario transport problem, transforming controller parameters from one driving context to another. Using flow matching, we train a generative model to predict the target-scenario behavior of previously unseen drivers from only a few demonstrations in a source scenario. We compare the approach with a linear parameter-shift baseline and evaluate flow-matching variants incorporating driver-consistent coupling, driver embeddings, and classifier-free guidance based on driving profiles extracted from trajectory data using a variational autoencoder.

Systems and Control.title: Privacy-Preserving Fully Distributed Gaussian Process Regression
Systems and Control.summary: Although distributed Gaussian process regression (GPR) enables multiple agents to jointly learn a model of the target function, its collaborative nature poses a risk of private data leakage. To address this, we propose a privacy-preserving fully distributed GPR protocol based on secure multi-party computation, which hides each agent's individual contribution from semi-honest coalitions of bounded size, beyond what is implied by the aggregated value. Building upon a secure distributed average consensus algorithm, it guarantees that each agent's local model practically converges to the same global model obtained by the standard distributed GPR. Formal privacy guarantees are established within the simulation based security paradigm. The protocol is further extended to privacy-preserving optimization of kernel hyperparameters, which is critical yet often overlooked in the literature. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness and practical applicability of the proposed method.
Systems and Control.comment: 12 pages, 3 figures, 1 table, accepted to IEEE Transactions on Control of Network Systems

Systems and Control.title: Safe Leader-Follower Density Control via Higher-Order Mean-Field Control Barrier Functions
Systems and Control.summary: Mean-field control barrier functions (MF-CBFs) enforce safety of large-scale multi-agent systems at the level of densities, but existing formulations require the control to act directly on the population to be kept safe. We consider populations that are not directly actuated and are influenced only through other, controlled populations, possibly in the presence of diffusion. We show that if the constrained population lies at directed graph distance d from the actuated one, then, under a nondegeneracy condition, the safety functional has relative degree d+1 and the control enters its (d+1)-th time derivative affinely. Higher-order safety constraints can therefore still be enforced through a convex quadratic program. We apply the framework to leader-follower density control among dangerous regions, where the follower safety functional has relative degree two and the leader safety functional has relative degree one. We characterize exactly when the two constraints are jointly infeasible and bound the tracking errors induced by the safety correction. Simulations in cluttered environments show that the proposed filter preserves follower safety, whereas enforcing leader safety alone does not.

Systems and Control.title: Foundation Models Meet Power Grid Topology for Cascade Prediction
Systems and Control.summary: Accurate early-stage prediction of cascading failure severity is essential for assessing the vulnerability of power transmission networks. However, existing data-driven approaches often rely on network-specific representations, limiting their generalizability across power system topologies. This work investigates the complementary capabilities of Large Language Models (LLMs) and Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) for cascading failure severity prediction. First, standalone LLM predictors are developed using a LoRA-fine-tuned LLaMA-3-8B-Instruct model with varying degrees of topological information. A hybrid Graph-LLM fusion framework is then proposed, integrating a Topology-Aware Graph Attention Transformer (TAGAT) with the LLM through confidence-gated fusion. TAGAT captures structural dependencies among transmission lines, while the LLM extracts representations from early-stage power-flow observations and aggregated cascade descriptors. The frameworks are evaluated on 30,000 simulated cascading failure scenarios for each of the IEEE 118-bus and IEEE 300-bus systems. Using only the first four cascade steps, the hybrid framework achieves weighted F1 scores of 0.94 and 0.92, respectively. In cross-system transfer from IEEE 118-bus to IEEE 300-bus, it achieves 0.72 zero-shot accuracy, improving to 0.83 with limited target-system calibration, outperforming standalone models and conventional baselines. These results show the potential of combining graph-based structural learning with foundation models to improve cascading failure severity prediction and cross-system transferability.

Systems and Control.title: Robust Offset-Free Lane-Keeping Control Framework for Vision-Only Automated Vehicles
Systems and Control.summary: Achieving accurate, real-time lane-keeping control during high-speed cornering on large-curvature roads while ensuring robust vehicle stability is a critical challenge in autonomous driving. To address this challenge, this study developed a robust offset-free model predictive control (OF-MPC) framework for vision-based autonomous vehicle lane-keeping. The regulation problem in this framework is solved using several algorithms. Numerical simulation results indicated that the interpolation-tube-based constrained iterative linear quadratic regulator (itube-CILQR) algorithm outperformed solvers based on the standard Interior Point Optimizer (IPOPT) and Operator Splitting Quadratic Program (OSQP), achieving a mean computation time of less than 5 ms. The itube-CILQR algorithm was then used for vehicle control in vision-based lane-keeping experiments in a simulation environment to quantify the perceptual uncertainty of a visual perception model (multitask UNet). This quantification was performed using the OF-MPC framework for traffic scenes that were not encountered during model training. Overall, the developed OF-MPC framework and the proposed method for characterizing the perceptual uncertainty of a visual perception system in unseen environments can contribute to the future development of advanced autonomous driving systems.

Systems and Control.title: Iterative Behavioral Identification for Covert Misappropriation Attacks
Systems and Control.summary: We present a data-driven, three-phase framework for covert misappropriation attacks on closed-loop networked control systems. A man-in-the-middle (MITM) adversary, with access only to intercepted input-output data, incrementally identifies the plant's behavioral subspace while maintaining stealth under an infinity-norm intrusion-detection system (IDS). Phase 1 collects an initial rank-deficient Hankel matrix using a low-amplitude probing signal that satisfies an analytical stealth bound. Phase 2 adapts online rank-increasing experiment design to the closed-loop setting, using causal predictor-based masking to limit IDS residuals while the Hankel rank grows from 1 to the full behavioral rank n + mL in exactly n + mL - 1 steps. We show that the identified subspaces are strictly nested and that the projection error of any desired trajectory decreases monotonically, strictly so almost surely at each rank increase. Phase 3 employs the final Hankel matrix in a DeePC-style optimization to synthesize a covert attack that tracks an arbitrary reference while respecting the IDS constraint. Simulations on a DC motor with PI control demonstrate full-rank identification and stealthy tracking. Stealth is guaranteed analytically in Phases 1 and 3 and is numerically supported in Phase 2. The method is model-free and assumes noise-free LTI dynamics.
Systems and Control.comment: Presented at the 17th APCA International Conference on Automatic Control and Soft Computing (CONTROLO 2026), Coimbra, Portugal, September 9-11, 2026

Systems and Control.title: Enabling 3GPP-Driven Services Over Optical Transport Network
Systems and Control.summary: We demonstrate a multi-layer slicing architecture enabling deployment of 3GPP network slices as self-contained, connected functions atop optical transport slices. The system provides Optical Spectrum as a Service (OSaaS) by integrating disaggregated optical control, multi-tenant orchestration, and telemetry-based optimization via standard interfaces.

Systems and Control.title: State Estimation as In-context Tabular Prediction
Systems and Control.summary: This letter poses state estimation (SE) as an in-context tabular prediction (ICTP) problem. The key idea is a tabular arrangement in which historical measurement vectors and corresponding state estimates serve as the context, and a new measurement vector forms the query for which we predict a state vector. We propose to use tabular foundation models (TFMs), pretrained on synthetic data, whose weights are never updated, so power system data is needed only as context. With frozen TFM weights we estimate the state of 14-, 30-, 33-, 70-, and 118-bus transmission and distribution networks, and do so where weighted least squares (WLS) fails or degrades, under low observability and with bad data. ICTP errors are 11 to 57$\times$ below the per-bus average of the context at full metering, and 1.3 to 4.0$\times$ below it with only 5% of measurements available. With measurements at six buses biased by 8$σ$, the ICTP angle error rises 1.8 to 5.0$\times$ over its bias-free value against 2.5 to 12.7$\times$ for WLS with bad-data detection. Without retraining, ICTP has lower voltage error than DSS$^2$ on both of its feeders, and lower than a retrained TAPINE on two of three reconfiguration sets.

Systems and Control.title: Controller-Agnostic Runtime Safety Certificates for Tool-Using AI Agents via Data-Driven Robust Reachability
Systems and Control.summary: Software agents built on large language models act by issuing tool calls, some of which cannot be undone. To control theory the model is an opaque feedback controller, replaced every few months, whose closed loop cannot be analyzed directly. We propose a runtime filter, or shield, between any such controller and its environment that certifies a bound on the probability of reaching an unsafe condition during a bounded task. Given a predicate abstraction and candidate successor sets, everything else comes from logs: the loop becomes a finite controlled Markov chain, the estimated kernel is surrounded by a distribution-free confidence region, and robust reach-avoid value iteration runs over it. The certificate is probably approximately correct and uniform over controllers respecting the filter, so one model may replace another without recomputation. In all tested datasets the true risk stayed within certificate and budget; in a file-system sandbox the filter stays sound against a hazard the logs barely covered, where a plug-in baseline certifies safety and fails; and it holds seven controllers, three of them open-weights models, to zero unsafe outcomes in 1050 episodes.

Systems and Control.title: Solid State Transformer - Next Generation MV Interface for Native DC loads
Systems and Control.summary: About PowerNexa PowerNexa is the project name for a start- up initiative driven by Marco Liserre and Steffan Hansen with the ambition to develop the next generation power grid interface. Battery integration and DC loads Ongoing electrification is fundamentally changing how electrical energy is produced and consumed. DC loads are becoming an integral part of the infrastructure while battery integration is increasingly needed to manage peak demand and address grid capacity constraints. The next generation grid interface PowerNexa aims to combine a fully controllable Medium Voltage grid interface with native battery integration and multiple DC voltage levels, based on an architecture designed for high efficiency, modularity and redundancy.

Systems and Control.title: Do LLM-derived text features improve electricity price forecasts beyond document activity? Evidence from Australia's National Electricity Market
Systems and Control.summary: Large language models (LLMs) can turn market notices and news into features for electricity price forecasting. Such features also record when documents arrive and whether their extraction failed, so a gain measured against a model without text can reflect document activity as well as content. We add the counts of the same documents and of their failed extractions to a no-text LightGBM model and measure each LLM representation against this activity reference, which needs no additional LLM requests. With gpt-6-luna as the extractor, we forecast Australian electricity prices from operator notices (5-30 minutes ahead) and WattClarity news (day-ahead) after the extractor's documented knowledge cutoff, averaging forecasts over three training seeds. For news, the counts alone lower mean absolute error (MAE) by 3.0%, most of the 3.6% reduction that the better LLM representation achieves relative to the no-text model; its increment beyond the counts is not significant. For notices, two of the three LLM representations lower MAE beyond the counts, by 0.14-0.21% and 0.45-0.52%, whether the counts are cumulative or cover recent windows, whereas the third shows no significant reduction. Time-shifted placebos give mixed evidence on whether these gains require text aligned with the target. Benchmarks using the operator's pre-dispatch forecasts (notices) or price history alone (news) are more accurate than all these text models. Gains against the no-text model and the activity reference differ in sign at individual seeds and, for notices with cumulative counts, in seed-averaged forecasts. Text gains should be reported against both references.
Systems and Control.comment: 27 pages, 4 figures, 12 tables. Code and data: https://github.com/ningfanxing-sys/nem-llm-text-activity

Systems and Control.title: A Robust Control Architecture for Multirate Systems and their Interconnections
Systems and Control.summary: We introduce a framework for analyzing and designing linear multirate control systems and their interconnections through the lens of robust control. The proposed approach models multirate systems as impulsive systems with multiple independent jump maps and corresponding jump-time sequences. We tackle analysis and design problems with stability, dissipativity, and robustness objectives, relying on a multi-clock-dependent Lyapunov function parameterization. Further, we develop a compositional approach for analyzing interconnections of multirate systems based on individual dissipativity properties. The theoretical conditions can be verified via linear matrix inequalities and they require weak assumptions on the sampling rates, allowing for asynchronous and time-varying sampling rates with or without separated time scales. The practicality of the framework is demonstrated with numerical examples.

Systems and Control.title: Regret-Based Max-Pressure Traffic Signal Control under Uncertain Traffic States
Systems and Control.summary: Max-pressure (MP) traffic signal control selects phases using pressure scores computed from estimated traffic states, but these states are uncertain and their consequences depend on whether they alter phase ranking and how much pressure is lost. This paper develops a decision-oriented Regret-Based Max-Pressure framework that represents uncertainty through phase-selection regret, defined as the pressure loss of a candidate phase relative to the pressure-maximizing phase under each plausible latent state. We propose Stochastic Regret MP, which minimizes expected regret under a calibrated residual distribution, and Distributionally Robust (DR) Regret MP, which minimizes worst-case expected regret over a Wasserstein ambiguity set. Robustifying regret rather than absolute pressure makes the formulation invariant to state-dependent pressure components shared by all candidate phases, thereby focusing robustness on relative phase quality. We further derive an explicit queue-linear pressure-loss bound and establish strong queue stability when the net-service reserve exceeds the resulting loss coefficient. Numerical experiments show that both methods reduce normalized true-state pressure regret by about 70% relative to Point-estimate MP, while DR Regret MP yields lower network queues than direct robustification of absolute pressure. In microscopic SUMO experiments on a 28-intersection real-world network, Stochastic Regret MP and DR Regret MP reduce mean delay by 18.9% and 14.9%, respectively, and retain benefits under detector undercount and failure. The results show that representing uncertainty through its decision consequences can improve reliable traffic control under imperfect state information.

Systems and Control.title: Decision Timescales in Max-Pressure Traffic Signal Control: Theory, Methodology, and Validation
Systems and Control.summary: Max-pressure (MP) control adapts signal phases to prevailing traffic states, but its decision timescale is typically fixed a priori. This paper treats the decision timescale as an explicit dimension of MP control. We first characterize the trade-off between responsiveness and switching efficiency by quantifying how an equivalent switching loss reduces service capacity over a finite decision interval. This yields a load-dependent critical timescale determined by switching loss and normalized traffic load, together with a performance-oriented operating range above the stability boundary. Building on this result, we propose Variable-Timescale Max-Pressure (VT-MP), in which each intersection selects its decision interval according to local operating conditions, allowing the control timescale to vary across time and space. We establish strong stability of the resulting asynchronous heterogeneous controller under uniformly admissible local loads and bounded decision intervals, and introduce a downstream receiving-supply correction for finite-storage implementation. Three experiments provide mechanism validation and network-level evaluation. A single-intersection experiment confirms that the preferred decision interval increases systematically with traffic load and follows the derived characteristic timescales. In a store-and-forward network, heterogeneous VT-MP reduces total queueing time by 31.0% relative to the best fixed-interval benchmark. In a microscopic 5x5 SUMO network, it reduces mean trip delay by 24.3%, from 213.3 s to 161.5 s, and peak network accumulation by 12.3%. These findings show that the MP decision timescale should be treated as a traffic-state-dependent control variable rather than a fixed implementation parameter.

Systems and Control.title: Heterogeneous Space Data Centers: A Key Paradigm for Future Non-Terrestrial and In-Orbit Services
Systems and Control.summary: Lower space-launch cost and advances in AI are driving space-based data centers (SDCs) that provide AI-centric computing and communication services to in-orbit and non-terrestrial assets. However, architectural principles, service models, and energy provisioning for such SDCs, particularly in low-Earth orbit (LEO), remain largely unexplored. We introduce heterogeneous SDCs composed of large and small nodes, differentiated by computing capability, size, and power budget, to support applications spanning ground, aerial, and in-orbit users. We define use cases, node sizing and placement strategies, and interconnection topologies integrating space-to-space and space-to-ground links. Focusing on dawn-dusk LEO configurations, we analyze solar power availability, visibility windows, and latency-aware coverage. Using baseline workloads for typical scenarios, we evaluate latency and service reliability. We quantify energy requirements of different SDC roles and deployment scales, highlighting trade-offs among node size, orbit selection, and service portfolio, and provide design guidance and future research directions for AI infrastructure in space.

Systems and Control.title: Quadrotor Guidance for Tasks along Elliptical Boundary
Systems and Control.summary: This paper presents a guidance method that enables a quadrotor uncrewed aerial vehicle to perform inspection tasks along an elliptical boundary enclosing a structure of interest. The proposed guidance approach leverages a bifurcation theory-based framework that supports multiple inspection tasks, including convergence to a desired viewpoint, switching between viewpoints along the boundary, constant-speed elliptical circumnavigation, and circumnavigation with sectorial dwell-time constraint. Stability analysis of the proposed guidance dynamics establishes convergence of the generated reference trajectories to the desired behavior. The control parameters in the proposed method further allow the settling time of the reference trajectory to be specified for each task. The resulting reference velocity expressions are closed-form and algebraically simple, facilitating practical implementation. A qualitative comparison with existing guidance methods highlights the flexibility of the proposed approach in achieving different inspection tasks through a unified framework, while relying on simpler guidance computations. The proposed guidance method is validated through numerical simulations using a six-degree-of-freedom quadrotor model with model uncertainties, and a cascaded sliding-mode controller that tracks the generated reference trajectories under bounded disturbances.

Systems and Control.title: Model-Free Output-Admittance Reshaping for Stability Enhancement of Grid-Connected Inverters
Systems and Control.summary: Grid-connected inverters can be unstable when their current-control loops interact with an uncertain external network. Returning the existing controller to improve damping also alters current tracking because tracking dynamics and output admittance are coupled. This paper adds a local model-free control (MFC) loop around the existing current controller to reduce output admittance while closely preserving nominal current-tracking dynamics. The added loop uses local inverter parameters without an external grid or neighbouring converter model. A Norton formulation separates reference tracking from the current response to terminal-voltage disturbances and establishes a tracking-preservation condition for admittance reshaping. Reducing the disturbance response makes the inverter behave more like an ideal controlled current source. Averaged-model simulations show reductions exceeding 65% in the magnitudes of all four dq output-admittance elements over 10-200 Hz, with closely preserved current-tracking dynamics. Generalised Nyquist analysis predicts small-signal stability for all sampled grid-impedance cases with MFC, compared with 90.0% without MFC.
Systems and Control.comment: Accepted at the 2026 IEEE PES Australasian Universities Power Engineering Conference (AUPEC)

Systems and Control.title: Stability Enhancement of Cascaded DC Systems via Source Output-Impedance Reshaping Using Model-Free Control
Systems and Control.summary: Cascaded DC systems may become unstable through source-load impedance interactions even when their constituent converters are locally stable. This paper proposes a source-side model-free control (MFC) method that reuses bus-voltage feedback to reshape the source output impedance while preserving nominal reference-to-output dynamics. The controller uses only nominal source-loop information and requires neither a load-converter model nor load-side measurements. A current-controlled buck source supplying a regulated buck-resistor load that exhibits constant-power load (CPL) behaviour at low frequencies is used as the case study. Impedance analysis predicts that the proposed MFC increases the maximum stable load power by approximately 50%, thereby improving the stability margin of the cascaded system. Switched-model simulations confirm preservation of the nominal reference-to-output response and show that the MFC-controlled system remains stable at load levels for which the baseline system becomes unstable.
