Systems and Control.comment: Accepted at the 2026 CPSS & IEEE International Symposium on Energy Storage and Conversion (ISESC)

Systems and Control.title: A Dynamic Inventory Rationing Model for Last-Mile Delivery of Medication in Liberia's Community Health Program
Systems and Control.summary: We study the dynamic allocation of scarce medications in Liberia's community health program. A central warehouse supplies a health facility and the Community Health Assistants (CHAs) it supervises. When a CHA runs out of medication, patients are referred to the facility, incurring travel costs if they complete the referral and remain untreated otherwise. Allocating inventory to CHAs allows more patients to receive treatment without traveling, while retaining inventory centrally preserves flexibility to respond to uncertain demand. The allocation problem must balance these considerations while accounting for fairness across locations. We formulate this problem as a finite-horizon stochastic control problem whose objective combines the costs of referrals and untreated patients with a demand-weighted fairness utility. Because standard dynamic programming methods are computationally intractable in this setting, we develop a continuous-time approximation that involves controlling the drift rate of a reflected Brownian motion. We then adapt the deep splitting method, using deep neural networks to approximate the value function and its gradient and compute a dynamic allocation policy. We calibrate the model using data on malaria cases among children in the Fangonda region of Lofa County, Liberia, and evaluate the proposed policy in the original discrete-time model. In the baseline setting, our policy reduces operating costs by about 6% relative to the strongest benchmark, the fairness-only policy, while retaining approximately 98% of its fairness utility. Additional experiments show that higher referral costs shift inventory toward CHAs and reduce local unmet demand, while greater demand variability increases our policy's performance over the fairness-only benchmark. Our model and computational approach provide a framework for studying similar last-mile allocation problems.

Systems and Control.title: On Exact Critical-Region Boundaries in Continuous-Time Multiparametric Optimal Control Problems
Systems and Control.summary: Continuous-time multiparametric model predictive control solves the optimal control problem once, offline, for every initial state, and divides the initial-state space into critical regions, each with its own control law and sequence of active constraints. A boundary between two regions is either a hyperplane, given by one linear equation, or curved. The curved boundaries have not been computed to date; a classifier has been trained instead to distinguish the regions, so the partition has been known only approximately. In this paper we show that a curved boundary can be computed exactly, without solving any optimal control problem. The method rests on one property. Once the sequence of active constraints is fixed, together with the instants inside it at which a constraint becomes active or inactive (the switching times) and the instant at which the change of the neighboring region first appears (the event time), every condition on a boundary is a linear equation in the initial state, so the computation of a boundary, curved or not, is exact. We fix one of these instants, a switching time or the event time, and solve the linear equations that correspond to it for the corresponding initial state on the boundary; stepping the fixed instant along the horizon yields the whole boundary. A hyperplane is the case in which no instant is left to fix. We illustrate the method on the Newell-Lee evaporator, which has seven critical regions and eight boundaries, four hyperplanes and four curved, computing one boundary of each type in full with the adjacent regions at its ends.

Systems and Control.title: The BAR-SOT Method: Long-term Average Cost Control as Stochastic Optimal Self-Transport
Systems and Control.summary: We reformulate average-cost (ergodic) control of a Markov jump process as a finite-horizon stochastic optimal transport (SOT) problem that jointly optimizes over the controlled evolution and the marginal law from which it starts and returns to (i.e., a self-transport). The constraint relating the marginal flow to the controlled generator is the basic adjoint relationship (BAR), so we call the resulting problem BAR-SOT. For any time horizon T>0, its optimal value is a constant scaling of the long-run average-cost rate. We give three equivalent formulations (through controlled processes, a Fokker--Planck constraint, and relaxed marginal measures) and show that the optimal dual is a stationary potential plus a term linear in time, with slope equal to the rate. A relative-entropy penalty on the control yields a cost-tilted Schrodinger bridge problem, computable by a Sinkhorn-type iteration when every transition rate is controlled, whose value converges to the unregularized optimum as the penalty vanishes. We develop the theory for finite Markov decision processes and then for general controlled Markov jump processes. A neural parametrization of the dual, trained as a physics-informed neural network (PINN), that encodes Harrison's equivalent-workload formulation (see Harrison 2000) matches the strong reinforcement-learning baseline of Dai and Gluzman (2022); numerically conditioning the fit of a sub-dominant transverse correction then improves on both that baseline and the best priority heuristic. On the input-queued switch, a graph-attention parametrization of the dual improves on the strongest matching heuristic we are aware of, with a parameter count that does not grow with the switch size.

Systems and Control.title: Scalable Reservoir Computing for Disturbance Localization and Identification in Power Grids
Systems and Control.summary: In this paper, we present a novel method for the localization and temporal waveform reconstruction of disturbances in complex power grids using observations of system state variables. Although various methods exist for detecting these events, accurately identifying and responding to them remains a significant challenge due to the grid's size, speed, complexity, and inherently dynamic behavior. We formulate a method for disturbance localization and reconstruction based on reservoir computing, a recurrent neural network architecture. We show that our method is able to recover the time dependence of previously unobserved disturbances, is robust to missing information, and can operate online. The approach requires only observed system data and knowledge of the network topology, without requiring a physical model of the system dynamics, and can recover simultaneous disturbances occurring at multiple locations. We implement a scalable parallelized reservoir architecture and demonstrate our algorithm on test IEEE cases and a reduced WECC system.
Systems and Control.comment: 11 pages, 9 figures, submitted to IEEE: transactions on power systems

Systems and Control.title: Strengthening AC optimal power flow relaxation through offline bound tightening and linear approximations
Systems and Control.summary: The alternating-current optimal power flow (ACOPF) problem is fundamental to power system operation and planning, but its nonconvexity makes globally optimal solutions of large-scale instances computationally challenging. Convex relaxations provide tractable lower bounds for assessing solution quality and supporting global optimization, although their effectiveness depends strongly on relaxation strength. This paper proposes an offline convexification and bound tightening framework for constructing strong linear programming (LP) relaxations for families of related ACOPF instances. Rather than repeating the tightening procedure for each instance, we compute variable bounds and second-order cone outer-approximation (SOC-OA) cuts offline using a demand-slack model and reuse them for subsequent instances with the same topology and admissible demand variations. Computational results on PGLib instances show that the fully offline approach achieves an average gap of $4.32\%$, compared with $3.80\%$ for the fully online approach, while achieving an average speedup of approximately $272\times$. The results demonstrate that offline convexification and bound tightening can recover most of the relaxation improvement of online tightening while significantly reducing the computational burden for repeated ACOPF evaluations.

Systems and Control.title: A SysML v2 Domain Library for ROS2 Robot Architectures
Systems and Control.summary: Systems engineers who model a ROS2 robot in SysML v2 must first model ROS2 itself. Its nodes, communication endpoints, message types, lifecycle states, quality-of-service policies, and coordinate frames have no ready definitions in the language, so each project reconstructs them. We present ros2-sysmlv2, a native SysML v2 domain library that supplies these definitions for reuse. A robot model imports the library and specializes its definitions to declare its own nodes, ports, connections, frames, and parameters. The library maps ROS2 concepts to SysML v2 definitions and usages and organizes them in Primitives, Infrastructure, and Application layers. We check its declarations for parity with the ROS2 Jazzy sources they model. Because every ROS2 element of a model specializes a library definition, a tool can select those elements by type. We state what this selection is and use it for a round trip. A ROS2 package is generated from the selection, and a monitor generated with the package compares the running graph with the same selection and reports every departure against the model. The generation-gap workflow derives topic endpoints and parameter declarations while preserving developer-owned node algorithms. In a case study on a generated ground robot, the generated conformance monitor reported each of the three departures that we introduced in the implementation. The library is distributed as a versioned package that any SysML v2 model can import.

Systems and Control.title: Contract-Based Agentic Systems Engineering: Delegation as Quotient for Assured System Design
Systems and Control.summary: A component an agent builds from a prompt can satisfy it and still break the system it joins, because the prompt omits what its neighbours assume of it. The artifact to hand over is computed, not written. A SysML v2 requirement with assumed and required constraints is an assume/guarantee contract, so when a system requirement is decomposed over fixed neighbours, the open component's requirement is the contract quotient, the weakest sound one, and again a SysML v2 requirement. Its required constraints carry the neighbours' assumptions, which a requirement for the mission alone drops and unit tests with mocked neighbours cannot reach. Signal Temporal Logic is closed under the quotient. We build the requirements, with derivation, allocation, satisfaction and verification, as a SysML~v2 model and compute the quotient from it. A case study delegates the local controller of a simulated warehouse robot, whose route crosses a worker's path and ends at a dock, to one language model under the quotient requirement, a mission-only requirement and a natural-language task, and scores the deliveries on live episodes against the system requirement from ground truth.

Systems and Control.title: Active Reachability Learning for Humanoid Recoverability Monitoring
Systems and Control.summary: Deploying humanoid task policies requires reliable runtime monitors that anticipate unrecoverable falls in time to trigger a fallback. We formulate this task as learning the stochastic, finite-horizon recoverability envelope of a given fallback policy. Synthesizing this monitor is challenging: existing methods assume training data naturally covers the recoverability envelope, yet acquiring such data remains a major bottleneck for contact-rich systems. Consequently, they recover only a fraction of the true envelope, leaving them prone to optimistic hallucinations for out-of-distribution (OOD) inputs. We resolve this via a unified framework that iterates between value learning and active exploration. Data exploration is reframed as a reach-avoid problem, where an uncertainty-guided explorer systematically uncovers unseen states while avoiding confidently unrecoverable regions. This loop is further supported by a combined Temporal Difference and Monte Carlo objective for accurate in-distribution value prediction and reliable uncertainty estimation. By explicitly treating the remaining high-uncertainty regions as unrecoverable, the monitor mitigates optimistic OOD hallucinations. Evaluated on stochastic benchmarks and a 29-DoF Unitree G1 humanoid, our approach drastically improves monitor coverage and accuracy and successfully transfers zero-shot to real-world hardware.

Systems and Control.title: Concurrent Space-Based Observer Placement and Scheduling for Cislunar Space Domain Awareness
Systems and Control.summary: As interest in cislunar space grows, so does the need for space domain awareness (SDA) capabilities to safely support missions. To enhance cislunar SDA capabilities, the use of space-based observers has been proposed. Prior research has explored optimizing observer placement but has not considered scheduling limitations. We propose a mixed-integer linear programming formulation that concurrently optimizes the placement and scheduling of space-based observers for cislunar SDA. Our work considers three aspects of observer scheduling: sensor tasking, communication, and charging. We utilize a scenario-based approach that generalizes observer placement for unknown targets while applying scheduling constraints to each scenario. However, this problem quickly becomes difficult for commercial solvers to handle as the number of scenarios grows. As an alternative, a column generation approach is employed to introduce well-performing schedules into the problem for each orbital slot. A comparative analysis is performed across multiple instances to evaluate the performance of column generation against that of a commercial solver. A case study is then conducted in which the performance of the observers' placement from the concurrent formulation is tested against a set of validation target sets and compared with the performance of two baselines in which placement and scheduling are performed sequentially.

Systems and Control.title: On the Discernibility of Topology Changes in Networked LTI Systems
Systems and Control.summary: This article investigates the discernibility of topology changes in networked linear time-invariant systems, with particular focus on edge disconnection. We introduce a new notion of discernibility motivated by a limitation of the definition commonly adopted in the literature. In consensus networks, topology changes are inherently indiscernible for all initial conditions belonging to the synchronization subspace. To overcome this issue, we first introduce the notion of dynamical discernibility of a topology change for elementary consensus networks. This notion explicitly disregards the intrinsic indiscernibility associated with states in the consensus subspace. We characterize this property for directed communication graphs and then specialize the resulting conditions to topology changes arising from either the disconnection of an edge or a variation in its weight. We then extend the analysis to networks of homogeneous agents by introducing discernibility modulo synchronization, which factors out the unavoidable indiscernibility associated with synchronized trajectories. We derive a general characterization showing how discernibility depends jointly on the topology change and on the dynamics of the individual agents. Finally, we specialize the analysis to undirected communication graphs and show that, under mild additional assumptions, discernibility modulo synchronization is equivalent to the dynamical discernibility of the corresponding topology change. This establishes a direct connection between the two notions and extends existing results on the discernibility of topology variations in dynamical networks. The resulting characterizations are then further specialized to the case of edge disconnection.
Systems and Control.comment: Submitted as an invited paper to the Bicentennial Special Issue of the Journal of the Franklin Institute. Under review

Systems and Control.title: How AI Load Swings Reduce Datacenter Power Conversion Efficiency
Systems and Control.summary: AI training and inference workloads make GPU power swing repeatedly between compute and communication phases. As a result, the cascaded converters in a datacenter rack keep moving between operating points with different efficiencies. This paper uses an energy based, cycle averaged method to quantify that effect along a 240 V AC to 400 V DC to 51 V DC rack power path, using measured efficiency curves of commercially available GaN based PFC and LLC converters. For a 1 Hz, 50% duty-cycle load swinging between 5 kW and 510 W, conversion efficiency falls to 95.97%, compared with 96.82% at the equivalent constant average load, a loss of 0.88%. When 51/48V to 1V point of load conversion to the chip rail is included, it is shown that the loss grows to 1.66% (89.45% vs. 90.96%). These results show that efficiency rated at average load overstates real world performance, and that the penalty grows with each load dependent conversion stage between the grid and the GPU.

Systems and Control.title: Symmetry-breaking in a discrete-choice LQG mean field game
Systems and Control.summary: Mean-field games provide a continuum framework for modeling the dynamics of large, interacting populations of non-cooperative agents. This paper studies symmetry-breaking in a finite-horizon, two-choice min-LQG mean-field game in which identical agents with linear stochastic dynamics choose one of two equally desirable terminal destinations, while trading off control effort against social pressure to conform. The model has an odd symmetry between the two destinations and therefore always admits a symmetric, dynamic Nash equilibrium in which the population splits evenly between them, producing a deadlock collective state at final time. Numerical studies have suggested that, as the penalty for social nonconformity increases, this symmetric equilibrium loses stability as a fixed point of an associated scalar, self-consistency map, and asymmetric consensus Nash equilibria emerge, where most agents select the same destination. By analyzing the linearized forward-backward PDE system through the scalar map representation, we provide a proof of this loss of stability of the symmetric equilibrium. Together with the odd symmetry of the map, this implies the existence of symmetry-broken mean-field game equilibria corresponding to consensus on either destination.
Systems and Control.comment: 26 pages, 4 figures. Originally submitted for review 5/18/26. v2 fixes issue with proof of lemma 4.3 related to terminal differentiability of the linearized scalar map, and other minor issues/typos

Systems and Control.title: Terra-Fi: Decoupling Sensing and Wireless Depths for Sustainable Deep Underground Monitoring
Systems and Control.summary: Wireless underground sensor networks (WUSNs) enable in-situ monitoring of subsurface processes and buried assets to deliver substantial social and economic benefits across diverse verticals. However, meter-scale underground monitoring remains challenging since conventional WUSNs place the entire underground device at the target sensing depth, where severe soil-induced attenuation significantly degrades communication reliability and makes wireless energy transfer (WET) inefficient and even impractical. To address this limitation, we propose Terra-Fi, a novel shallow-hub and deep-sensing architecture that decouples the sensing depth from the wireless communication and energy-replenishment depth. In Terra-Fi, a shallow wireless hub is deployed at a depth favorable for communication, WET, and maintenance, while application-specific sensing probes are extended to meter-scale target layers through power-and-signal feeders. On this basis, we first examine the depth limitations of underground communication and WET and compare representative monitoring architectures. Then, we present its system architecture, operation flow, and potential benefits. Through a precision agriculture case study, our numerical results reveal that Terra-Fi establishes more robust wireless connectivity and a longer operational lifetime than conventional fully buried WUSN architectures, particularly at greater sensing depths and higher volumetric water content. Moreover, its performance gain can be enhanced through time allocation and transmission-configuration optimization. Finally, we pinpoint practical challenges and future research directions for deploying Terra-Fi into WUSN systems.
Systems and Control.comment: 8 pages, 4 figures, 2 tables, submitted to IEEE IoTM

Systems and Control.title: Why the Swing Parameters Are Sloppy
Systems and Control.summary: Evangelou, Stanković, Kevrekidis and Transtrum compared analytic and data-driven assessments of parameter identifiability for the infinite-bus synchronous generator. Fisher information with the manifold boundary approximation method (MBAM), and output diffusion maps with geometric harmonics, report the same six identifiable parameters on the late window $t \in [3, 5]\text{ s}$, and both place the inertia $H$ and the damping $D$ among the unidentifiable ones. We explain this result from the geometry of the dynamics rather than from that of the parameter-to-data map. The rotor swing is a fast fibre that has collapsed onto a two-dimensional normally attracting invariant manifold (NAIM) of the transient fluxes before the window opens. The zeroth-order NAIM is exactly independent of $H$, $D$, $T_{d0}''$ and $T_{q0}''$, four of the five MBAM limits. We prove, under stated smoothness and rank conditions, that each of the four limits is a boundary of the model manifold at a distance equal, to first order in the parameter, to its current profiled speed. The same analysis predicts how identifiability changes with the experiment: neither a larger initial speed deviation nor a load change restores $H$ or $D$ in the late window, whereas the early window $[0, 2]\text{ s}$ makes $H$ the best-determined parameter. Evaluated in a physical metric fixed by synchrophasor accuracy limits, the late window identifies five parameters rather than six and the early window nine. The spiked-covariance structure of the linearised trajectory map explains why the principal components of whitened, sampled trajectories reproduce the prior-scaled Fisher spectrum, and regression on those components attains the Fisher-predicted recovery error in 113 of 114 parameter--scenario pairs.

Systems and Control.title: Modeling Liquid-Cooled Data Centers in EnergyPlus
Systems and Control.summary: As AI workloads accelerate data center transition toward high-density racks with direct-to-chip (DTC) liquid cooling, existing simulation tools remain limited in evaluating whole-building and multi-year efficiency. To bridge this gap, we develop a native EnergyPlus object, ElectricEquipment:ITE:LiquidCooled, that models DTC liquid cooling for chilled-water and warm-water architectures as plant-loop components. It couples facility-water loops, rack-side secondary loops, coolant distribution units, and chip-junction temperatures within a single solver. Validation against an independent Modelica implementation across 21 operating conditions, including two full-year runs compared at one-minute resolution, yields loop-temperature RMSE at or below 0.021 K, well within the 0.1 K acceptance threshold. Our case study demonstrates that warm-water liquid cooling reduces annual PUE from 1.43 to 1.25, eliminates on-site water use, and cuts total facility energy by 37.9% relative to an air-cooled baseline. By embedding liquid-cooling logic into EnergyPlus, our work provides whole-building, long-term energy modeling for high-density AI infrastructure within an open-source framework.

Information Theory.title: Variance of relative entropy over random states
Information Theory.summary: Average relative entropy over major generic random states is recently studied. In this work, the investigation is extended by deriving the variances of relative entropy over the Hilbert--Schmidt and Bures--Hall ensembles, which characterize its fluctuations around the average value. Exact results for the variances of relative entropy between independent states drawn from the same ensemble and from two different ensembles are obtained. These results further indicate that the average relative entropy is typical in the considered limiting regimes. In addition to the matrix-level calculations similar to the average relative entropy, eigenvalue correlation functions of the ensembles are involved in the variance computations through the use of zonal polynomials.

Information Theory.title: Polyhedral RIS Architecture with Quantum-Assisted Facet Selection for Uniform Coverage
Information Theory.summary: Reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RISs) direct coverage toward moving user equipment (UE), but practical deployments involve discrete phase control, uncertain facet positions, and UE mobility, which require the problem to be re-solved continually. We consider these challenges for the chamfered hexagonal polyhedral RIS, which provides nearly uniform coverage. With both incidence and departure angles, we bound in closed form the gain loss of its best facet relative to the best possible reflecting facet, include the known b-bit quantization loss, and extend the bound to joint random mounting errors of all facets. For a precoded multi-user downlink, each facet-selection subproblem of the max-min rate design is shown to be an exact quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO) problem, suited to repeated time-constrained solving. The deployment of the base station in relation to the RIS allows the polyhedral surface to bring down the percentage of dead zones in vertical planar panels from 77% to 0.3% and increase the minimum rate by 34% relative to the STAR panel. The simulated annealing algorithm finds the optimum solution in 95% of the cases. The quantum approximation algorithm fails to do so.

Information Theory.title: Computing the entropy rate of a quantized stationary Gaussian process
Information Theory.summary: The entropy rate of a uniformly quantized stationary Gaussian process is the fundamental limit on its lossless compression. It has no closed form, and the classical high-resolution approximation breaks down whenever the spectral density is small on part of the band, as routine smoothing and filtering produce. Here we present two methods for computing the rate. The first is an analytical approximation, obtained from an exact dithering identity and the Kolmogorov-Szegő formula, in which the quantization noise power acts as a floor on the spectral density. The second is a Monte Carlo estimate of the exact rate: a minimum-phase moving-average representation makes the quantized sequence a hidden Markov process whose optimal particle filter is available in closed form, and the filter's log-likelihood on one long sequence gives the rate. The approximation agrees with the estimate to within a few millibits per sample over most of the parameter range for quantization steps up to the signal standard deviation, including processes on which the classical formula fails; for coarser steps the estimate should be used instead. At a step of a quarter of the standard deviation, linear predictive coding comes within 2 to 4 percent of the rate, FLAC within 3 to 32 percent, and general-purpose compressors remain 12 to 89 percent above it.
Information Theory.comment: Code, data, and an interactive demonstration at https://github.com/magland/entropy-gaussian-process-paper

Information Theory.title: Logarithmic Separation between LZ77 and LZ-End and Grammar Compression
Information Theory.summary: We show that there is a logarithmic separation between LZ77 and LZ-End, and between LZ77 and grammar compression.

Information Theory.title: Beam Search for Error-Correcting Codes via Conditional Diffusion
Information Theory.summary: We introduce a diffusion framework for neural decoding of error-correcting codes (ECCs). We interpret decoding as a conditional diffusion process that progressively predicts codeword bits while treating the physical channel observation as fixed side information. At each stage, a neural model estimates bitwise posteriors conditioned on the physical observation and the current noisy state of the codeword. We focus particularly on masked diffusion, for which the reverse process naturally induces a Maxwell beam search (MBS) procedure inspired by the Maxwell construction of Measson et al. Rather than committing to a single uncertain decision, the decoder maintains multiple candidate trajectories, removes parity-infeasible candidates, and ranks the remaining candidates using accumulated reverse-transition log-probabilities. We evaluate the framework across multiple code families on binary phase-shift keying (BPSK) over additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN). Experiments show competitive decoding performance across Polar, low-density parity-check (LDPC), and Bose-Chaudhuri-Hocquenghem (BCH) codes. The MBS decoder consistently improves upon the corresponding single-trajectory diffusion decoder and, in all evaluated settings, improves upon available neural decoding results.

Information Theory.title: AFRA: Age-Threshold Frame-Based Random Access for Timely Communication in Multi-Agent Systems
Information Theory.summary: Timely state updates are essential for coordination and monitoring in multi-agent systems, such as teams of mobile robots exchanging state information. When agents share a wireless channel, collisions and slow convergence of distributed access schemes can degrade information freshness over finite operating periods. This paper proposes age-threshold frame-based random access (AFRA), a distributed medium access control protocol for minimizing age of information (AoI). Once its age reaches a threshold, an agent starts a local frame with a mandatory transmission and, if unsuccessful, makes one further attempt at a uniformly selected remaining slot. Each attempt carries a freshly generated update. AFRA requires only local state and acknowledgment feedback, with shared slot boundaries but independently timed local frames. We prove almost-sure convergence from any legal initial state to collision-free periodic operation when the frame length $L$ and age threshold $T$ satisfy $L\ge T>N\ge2$, where $N$ is the number of agents. We also derive closed-form expressions for steady-state throughput, average AoI, and average peak AoI. Simulations demonstrate that AFRA combines rapid convergence at small age thresholds with lower window-averaged AoI than the existing age-aware random access schemes evaluated in this study.
Information Theory.comment: Accepted for presentation at IEEE ROBIO 2026

Information Theory.title: Polarization on Bounded Euclidean Spaces and More General Compact Groups
Information Theory.summary: We establish polarization for memoryless sources taking values on the unit-perimeter circle, or on more general compact groups, under Arıkan's polar transform. For sources with finite differential entropy, all but an $O((\log N)^{-1/12})$ fraction of the conditional differential entropies in successive cancellation order lie within any fixed positive distance of zero, where $N$ is the block length. Examples indicate that the true polarization rate is indeed very slow: an inverse-logarithmic rate does not underestimate the polarization speed at moderate block lengths.

Information Theory.title: A probabilistic construction of maximum $h$-scattered subspaces
Information Theory.summary: Let $1\le h\le n-2$ and $g=\gcd(n,h+1)$. We prove that, for every prime power $q$, a maximum $h$-scattered $\mathbb{F}_q$-subspace of $V(r,q^n)$ exists whenever $(h+1)\mid rn$ and $$r\ge\frac{h+1}{g}\bigl(h(n-h-2)+1\bigr).$$ In particular, for fixed $n$ and minimum distance $δ\in\{2,\ldots,n-1\}$, $\mathbb{F}_{q^n}$-linear MRD codes of length $N$ exist for every $q$ and every sufficiently large $N$ such that $n$ divides $(n-δ+1)N$, with a bound on $N$ depending only on $n$ and $δ$. We take the $\mathbb{F}_{q^s}$-span of the columns of a random matrix $A$ over the algebra $R=\mathbb{F}_{q^n}\otimes_{\mathbb{F}_q}\mathbb{F}_{q^s}$, for a suitable $s$. Such a subspace is maximum $h$-scattered if and only if the kernel of $A$ contains no nonzero vector whose expansion with respect to an $\mathbb{F}_q$-basis of $\mathbb{F}_{q^s}$ has rank weight at most $h+1$. When $\gcd(n,s)=1$, $R$ is a field, and a first-moment argument, counting these vectors up to multiplication by $\mathbb{F}_{q^n}^*\mathbb{F}_{q^s}^*$, shows that with positive probability the kernel contains none of them if $s>h(n-h-2)$. When $d=\gcd(n,s)>1$, $R$ is a product of $d$ fields, and vectors vanishing in some factors lie in the kernel with larger probability. We control them by proving that, for an $(h+1)$-dimensional $\mathbb{F}_q$-subspace $D$ of $\mathbb{F}_{q^n}$, the elements of $D\otimes_{\mathbb{F}_q}\mathbb{F}_{q^s}$ vanishing outside $k$ given factors, $0<k<d$, form an $\mathbb{F}_{q^s}$-space of dimension at most $(h+1)k/d$, with equality only if $D$ is linear over a subfield of $\mathbb{F}_{q^n}$ larger than $\mathbb{F}_q$. Taking $s=gr/(h+1)$ gives the bound on $r$. Finally, if $(n-h-1)\mid(h+1)$, then for every $r$ satisfying the above inequality there is an $h$-scattered $\mathbb{F}_q$-subspace of $V(r,q^n)$ of dimension $\lfloor rn/(h+1)\rfloor$, without a divisibility condition on $rn$.

Information Theory.title: Digital-Twin-Referenced Belief-Guided Q-Learning for Jammer Identification and Beam-Power Control in a mmWave Model
Information Theory.summary: Next-generation wireless networks are expected to support high data rates and reliable connectivity while meeting requirements for energy efficiency, resource management, and communication security. Digital Twin (DT) technology represents expected network behavior and enables the actual network state to be assessed against it. Integrating DT technology with reinforcement learning (RL) supports adaptive resource allocation and security-aware decision-making. This paper presents a simulation-based DT reference and a belief-guided Q-learning (BGQL) method for joint jammer identification and beam-power control in a site-specific 28-GHz network model. Receiver-level residuals between attack-free and attacked configurations are combined with candidate spatial jamming footprints and accumulated into a normalized suspicion vector. BGQL incorporates this vector into its state, reward, and exploratory beam-selection rule. Compared with SARSA, Greedy, and Random across 30 paired Monte Carlo runs per configuration, with known jammer counts, BGQL achieves link-rate scores of 437.4-564.2 Mbit/s, rate-to-device-power scores of 60.37-76.79 Mbit/J, and localization recall of 100% for one jammer and 78%-81% for two jammers. BGQL requires 80-130 s per run versus 5-14 s for SARSA. These findings provide a matched-model simulation proof of concept for DT-referenced belief-guided learning for security-aware beam-power control in 6G networks.

Information Theory.title: Distortion-Rate Outage Probability for Non-ergodic Classes of Sources
Information Theory.summary: The concept of outage has been commonly used in the context of transmission rates over non-ergodic channels. For those channels, one channel state or realization may be encountered for the whole transmission duration of a codeword. In the dual setting of source coding and whenever source statistics are not ergodic, we define in this work the notion of outage; we discuss related properties, consider the special case of compact source classes and provide examples.

Information Theory.title: StarRTT: An End-to-End Real-Time Framework for Blind Zone-Free RTT Prediction in Starlink LEO Satellite Networks
Information Theory.summary: Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite mega-constellations such as Starlink require frequent handovers due to high orbital velocities, resulting in substantial Round-Trip Time (RTT) fluctuations. Accurate RTT prediction can mitigate these fluctuations, yet it fundamentally relies on continuously updated serving- satellite information. Existing serving-satellite identification methods typically complete identification only at the end of each scheduling cycle, creating an identification blind zone that limits real-time prediction. To overcome this limitation, we develop StarRTT, an end-to-end real-time framework that eliminates the blind zone by integrating per-second serving-satellite identification with RTT prediction. Within this framework, we propose Real-Time Long Short-Term Memory (RT-LSTM), an LSTM-based RTT prediction model designed to capture both non-stationary RTT evolution and time-varying geometric relationships among the serving satellite, user terminal, and gateways. Specifically, a historical LSTM encodes historical RTT observations and real-time serving-satellite and gateway-relative features, while a future LSTM processes Two-Line Element (TLE)-propagated future features of the identified serving satellite up to the next scheduling instant. Under strict real-time back-testing, RT-LSTM achieves a Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 1.405 ms averaged over all 15 prediction horizons and 15 reference time-slot indices, reducing the error by 4.3 %, 11.6 %, and 22.1 % compared with the existing baseline models, LSTM, StarNet, and Attention-based Spatiotemporal Model (ASTM), respectively. Notably, the reduction over LSTM reaches 12.5 % at the scheduling instant, highlighting the benefit of real-time serving-satellite information when recent RTT observations are limited.

Information Theory.title: Second-Order Schalkwijk-Kailath Coding for Autoregressive Gaussian Channels
Information Theory.summary: We study noiseless-feedback communication over Gaussian channels with stationary autoregressive (AR) noise of arbitrary finite order. We introduce a class of Gaussian linear-feedback coding schemes based on the celebrated Schalkwijk--Kailath (SK) coding scheme, called SK(2), whose message process follows a second-order deterministic recursion, and derive a closed-form characterization of its maximal achievable rate under average power constraint $P$. As a first-order benchmark, we formulate SK(1) as a sign-consistent, branch-complete version of the real constant signed-ratio specialization of Butman's linear-feedback construction. For stationary AR($p$) Gaussian channels, optimizing over recursions with both characteristic roots outside the unit circle gives the same rate supremum as optimizing over all SK(2) recursions and yields a rate no smaller than the maximal SK(1) rate. The SK(2) scheme achieves feedback capacity for the AWGN channel, stationary AR(1) Gaussian channels, and a subclass of stationary AR(2) Gaussian channels obtained by interleaving two independent AR(1) noise processes. For the interleaved subclass, we show that a genuine SK(2) scheme strictly outperforms SK(1). Numerical comparisons illustrate further strict rate gains over a broader range of AR(2) parameters. These results show that the SK(1) scheme is not universally optimal beyond AR(1) noise and disprove a corrected form of Butman's conjecture.

Information Theory.title: A counterexample to Tokareva's conjecture on sums of two bent functions
Information Theory.summary: It is well known that the sum of two bent functions on $\mathbb{F}^n$ has algebraic degree at most $n/2$ for even $n\ge 4$. Tokareva conjectured that the converse holds: every Boolean function with degree at most $n/2$ can be written as a sum of two bent functions. The conjecture has been verified for even $n\leq 6$ and for several special classes of Boolean functions. We disprove this conjecture by showing that $x_1x_2(x_3x_4+x_5x_6+x_7x_8)$ is not a sum of two bent functions on $\mathbb{F}^8$. We extend this construction to obtain counterexamples in every even dimension $n\ge 8$. Using Shaporenko's reduction, we also obtain explicit counterexamples to Tokareva's derivative conjecture in every even dimension $n\ge 10$.
Information Theory.comment: The counterexamples and proofs in this paper were obtained through large-scale automated reasoning with LLM agents while solving Problem~10 in NSUCRYPTO~2026 (MiniMax M3.1-Flash-Preview, 19 rounds of up to 100 independent agents between 12 and 18 October 2026, 1889 reports in all), paired with 8 rounds of independent audits (227 reports)

Information Theory.title: Encoding-Sensitive Nullstellensatz Certificates for Syndrome Exclusion in LDPC Codes: Sharp Local Bounds and a Linear Separation
Information Theory.summary: Certifying that a parity-check matrix has no nonempty set of at most t variable nodes leaving at most b checks unsatisfied arises in minimum-distance and trapping-set analysis. Such absence is the infeasibility of a polynomial system, provable by an independently checkable Nullstellensatz certificate. The degree of these certificates depends strongly on how the two cardinality constraints are encoded, although the encodings have identical solutions. For a local encoding with inclusion-exclusion and cardinality obstructions, we construct explicit certificates of degree at most t + b + K + 1, with K logarithmic in the maximum check degree; this bound is independent of the block length and cannot be improved in general. For a standard counting encoding, a generalized planted-knapsack theorem, which pulls back a knapsack functional with an arbitrary target, gives lower bounds linear in the block length for cycle codes, regular codes of girth at least six near the feasibility boundary, array-based quasi-cyclic codes and minimum-distance certificates for arrays of circulant permutation matrices, where the local degree stays bounded. On array codes and regular codes of girth at least eight, planted column pairs extend these bounds to odd column weight with no unsatisfied checks. The planting argument is optimal among such pullbacks. All computed degrees and certificates are verified in exact rational arithmetic; bounds are distinguished from exact minimum degrees. Local certificates for quasi-cyclic matrices, including a lifted fifth-generation New Radio base graph, pass two independent verifiers.
Information Theory.comment: 48 pages, 4 tables. Extended journal version of a paper submitted to IEEE ITW 2027

Information Theory.title: Differentially Private Synthetic Data via Generalized Moment Matching
Information Theory.summary: We study $(\varepsilon,δ)$-differentially private synthetic data for arbitrary databases of $n$ records in $[-1,1]^d$ under a specified integral probability metric (IPM). We introduce generalized moment matching, which estimates moments privately, fits a probability measure, and samples synthetic records. A general error theorem applies when moment error controls the target IPM. This framework extends Chebyshev moment matching for $1$-Wasserstein distance and smooth queries. We apply the framework to maximum mean discrepancy with Matern and Laplace kernels and a two-layer ReLU neural tangent kernel. We also obtain guarantees for sliced Wasserstein-$1$ and the IPM induced by norm-bounded ReLU networks. With sufficiently many synthetic records,these rates are minimax optimal up to logarithmic factors for fixed dimension.

Information Theory.title: Optimal Average Success Probabilities of Binary $(n,n-1)$ and $(n,n-2)$ Quantum Random Access Codes
Information Theory.summary: A binary $(n,m)$ quantum random access code (QRAC) compresses an $n$-bit classical string into an $m$-qubit quantum state, from which a decoder attempts to recover a randomly selected target bit. Of particular interest is the optimal average probability of success, $P^{Q,\mathrm{avg},\mathrm{opt}}_{n,m}$, which was numerically conjectured to satisfy the bound $P^{Q,\mathrm{avg},\mathrm{opt}}_{n,m}\leq \frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{2}\sqrt{\frac{m}{n}}$. Recent constructions of $(n,n-1)$ QRACs by Suzuki and $(n,n-2)$ QRACs by Akibue et al. meet this bound exactly, raising the question of their strict optimality. In this work, we settle this question by proving the conjectured upper bound for $m\in\{n-1,n-2\}$, thereby precisely determining $P^{Q,\mathrm{avg},\mathrm{opt}}_{n,n-1}$ and $P^{Q,\mathrm{avg},\mathrm{opt}}_{n,n-2}$. The proof utilizes a translation recently studied by Lin and de Wolf from local to global reconstruction via pretty good measurement, along with dimensional and positive-semidefinite constraints on an induced channel.

Information Theory.title: Bistatic Target Detection by Exploiting Both Deterministic Pilots and Unknown Random Data Payloads
Information Theory.summary: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) plays a crucial role in 6G, enabling innovative applications such as drone surveillance, urban air mobility, and low-altitude logistics. However, the hybrid ISAC signal, which comprises deterministic pilot and random data payload components, poses challenges for target detection due to two reasons: 1) these two components cause coupled shifts in both the mean and variance of the received signal, and 2) the random data payloads are typically unknown to the sensing receiver in the bistatic setting. Unfortunately, these challenges could not be tackled by existing target detection algorithms. In this paper, a generalized likelihood ratio test (GLRT)-based detector is derived by leveraging the known deterministic pilots and the statistical characteristics of the unknown random data payloads. Due to the analytical intractability of exact performance characterization, we perform an asymptotic analysis for the false alarm probability and detection probability of the proposed detector. The results reveal a deterministic-random trade-off: the deterministic pilots enhance detection through a target-induced mean shift, while the random data payloads provide an additional covariance-domain target signature but simultaneously introduce statistical uncertainty due to their unknown realizations. Simulations validate the theoretical findings and demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed detector, which highlights the necessity of designing a dedicated detector to fully exploit the signaling resources assigned to random data payloads.
Information Theory.comment: Integrated sensing and communications, bistatic target detection, random signals, false alarm probability, detection probability

Information Theory.title: Fisher Information and the Minimum Mean-Square Error for Locating Closely Spaced Point Sources
Information Theory.summary: We determine the optimal average error of locating closely spaced sources from noisy superpositions of a known smooth response with unknown complex coefficients. Relative phases control how changes in one location can be offset by the other unknowns, so local Fisher information alone does not determine the attainable error. For every fixed number $K\ge2$ of sources with independent uniform phases, we prove matching Bayes risk bounds jointly in separation and noise, for all sufficiently small separations and all noise levels. Odd source counts have two risk regimes; even counts have an intermediate regime in which mean squared error is linear in the noise standard deviation. A projected least-squares estimator attains these orders without knowing the phases or the prior density. Bounded nonuniform phase laws preserve the orders under stated support conditions, whereas priors concentrated near poorly identified configurations can change the exponents. A common finite comparison yields both a global inverse bound and paths controlled by the original prior. These give sufficient conditions under which the risk has the order of the pointwise capped Cramér--Rao bound, and a lower-tail calculation explains the power and logarithmic regimes. We also give conditional guarantees when the cluster center, separation, and source count are unknown, with an additional low-noise requirement for count selection. A calibrated covariance factor model illustrates the same criterion beyond source localization.

Information Theory.title: Multiple Importance Sampling for Guided Speculative Inference
Information Theory.summary: We study an extension of the Guided Speculative Inference (GSI) algorithm for test-time-scaling of large language models (LLMs) to a novel setting where an ensemble of smaller LLMs proposes draft reasoning steps which are later verified by a larger base model and a process reward model. Using the established framework of multiple importance sampling (MIS), we introduce weighting schemes to aggregate samples from a diverse collection of proposal distributions. We provide new bounds on the KL divergence from the optimal reward-tilted target distribution and the expected reward degradation, then demonstrate that the well-known balance heuristic is optimal. Compared to GSI with a single well-tuned drafter, combining several diverse LLMs while retaining the same total number of samples maintains competitive pass-at-$N$ downstream performance while being mathematically robust to situations where the support of a single draft model does not cover that of the target, where GSI may fail.
Information Theory.comment: 9 pages, 1 figure. Presented at the IEEE ISIT 2026 Workshop on Information Theory for Large Language Models (IT4LLM)

Information Theory.title: Pinching Antenna and Relay Assisted Joint Indoor Outdoor NOMA Communications with SWIPT
Information Theory.summary: This paper investigates physical layer security in waveguide-based pinching antenna systems with a mobile eavesdropper. Assuming perfect knowledge of the legitimate user's location and only statistical information about the eavesdropper's position, the ergodic secrecy rate is analyzed under Gaussian and practical finite-alphabet signaling. Since the exact ergodic secrecy rate does not admit a tractable closed-form expression, a closed-form analytical upper bound is derived using Jensen's inequality. The resulting expression serves as an efficient objective for antenna position optimization without requiring exhaustive Monte Carlo simulations. Numerical results verify the tightness of the proposed upper bound and show that the optimized antenna position closely matches the optimum obtained from Monte Carlo optimization. Furthermore, practical finite-alphabet signaling is shown to exhibit secrecy-rate saturation at high SNR, identifying an effective operating SNR region. Although the antenna position is optimized using the Gaussian-based upper bound, it remains effective for practical signaling.

Information Theory.title: Average-Radius List-Decodability of Random Linear Codes
Information Theory.summary: We prove that for every prime power $q$ and every $p \in (0, 1-1/q)$, a random $\mathbb{F}_q$-linear code of rate $1 - h_q(p) - ε$ is $(p, C_{p,q}/ε)$-average-radius list-decodable with probability at least $1 - q^{-Ω(n)}$, i.e., for every center $y \in \mathbb{F}_q^n$, the $C_{p,q}/ε$ codewords closest to $y$ have average fractional Hamming distance at least $p$ from $y$. This extends a similar result for (standard) list-decoding due to Guruswami, Håstad, and Kopparty (2010) to the stronger average-radius guarantee, with the same $O(1/ε)$ list size. For average-radius list-decoding, such a result was previously known only for binary linear codes (Guruswami, Li, Mosheiff, Resch, Silas, and Wootters, 2021) and for general (non-linear) random codes over arbitrary alphabets (Elias, 1991).

Information Theory.title: Multi-Functional Chirp Signalling for Next-Generation Multi-Carrier Wireless Networks: Communications, Sensing and ISAC Perspectives
Information Theory.summary: To meet the increasingly demanding quality-of-service requirements of the next-generation multi-carrier mobile networks, it is essential to design multi-functional signalling schemes facilitating efficient, flexible, and reliable communication and sensing in complex wireless environments. As a compelling candidate, we advocate chirp signalling, beneficially amalgamating sequences (e.g., Zadoff-Chu sequences) with waveforms (e.g., chirp spread spectrum and frequency-modulated continuous wave (FMCW) radar), given their resilience against doubly selective channels. Besides chirp sequences, a wide range of chirp waveforms is considered, ranging from FMCW to affine frequency-division multiplexing (AFDM), to create a promising chirp multicarrier waveform. This study also highlights the advantages of such waveforms in supporting reliable high-mobility communications, plus integrated sensing and communications (ISAC). Finally, we outline several emerging research directions for chirp signalling designs.
Information Theory.comment: 9 pages, 6 figures, submitted to IEEE Wireless Communications

Information Theory.title: Fourier Ratio and Restricted Isometry via Entropic Descent
Information Theory.summary: In this second paper on descent methods as proof mechanisms in harmonic analysis (the first treated Bourgain's $Λ(p)$ selection theorem), entropic mirror descent gives an improved restricted isometry bound, improving sampling and recovery bounds in the Fourier Ratio program. Let $H$ be a complex $n\times n$ matrix with $H^*H=nI$ and $|H_{ij}|=1$. For fixed $0<\varepsilon<\frac14$ and $A_0>0$, independent Bernoulli row selection with expected cardinality $C_{\varepsilon,A_0}r\log\frac{2en}{r}\log(2r)\leq m\leq n/2$ preserves, after normalization by $\sqrt m$, the squared norm of every complex vector $y$ with $\|y\|_1\leq\sqrt r\|y\|_2$ within a factor $1\pm\varepsilon$, with failure probability at most $Cn^{-A_0}$. This includes every $r$-sparse vector and also fully supported ones; support size enters only through this inequality. For $y=\widehat f$ the condition is exactly $\operatorname{FR}(f)^2\leq r$, where $\operatorname{FR}(f)=\|\widehat f\|_1/\|\widehat f\|_2$, giving uniform energy sampling and approximate recovery even for signals with full Fourier support. The same holds for a uniform subset of prescribed cardinality, and for discrete Fourier and real Hadamard matrices. At fixed accuracy the bound removes one sparsity logarithm from the earlier count and replaces $\log n$ by $\log\frac{2en}{r}$; for Walsh matrices it matches, up to constants, the lower bound of Błasiok et al.\ in their range. One relative-entropy potential controls the corrections of an amplitude predictor at every scale; counting them on the symmetric difference of two samples gives the uniform estimate. We also prove the sufficient bound $C_{A_0}\varepsilon^{-5}r\log\frac{2en}{r}\log\frac{2r}{\varepsilon}$, and stable sparse recovery from $Cs\log\frac{2en}{s}\log(2s)$ measurements, with error controlled by the noise and the best $s$-term approximation.

Information Theory.title: Fully Parallelized BP Decoding for Quantum LDPC Codes Can Outperform BP-OSD
Information Theory.summary: This work presents a hardware-efficient and fully parallelizable decoder for quantum LDPC codes that leverages belief propagation (BP) with a speculative post-processing strategy inspired by classical Chase decoding algorithm. By monitoring bit-level oscillation patterns during BP, our method identifies unreliable bits and generates multiple candidate vectors to selectively flip syndromes. Each modified syndrome is then decoded independently using short-depth BP, a process we refer to as BP-SF (syndrome flip). This design eliminates the need for costly Gaussian elimination used in the current BP-OSD approaches. Our implementation achieves logical error rates comparable to or better than BP-OSD while offering significantly lower latency due to its high degree of parallelism for a variety of bivariate bicycle codes. Evaluation on the $[[144,12,12]]$ bivariate bicycle code shows that the proposed decoder reduces average latency to approximately 70% of BP-OSD. When post-processing is parallelized the average latency is reduced to 55% compared to the single process implementation, with the maximum latency reaching as low as 18%. These advantages make it particularly well-suited for real-time and resource-constrained quantum error correction systems.

Information Theory.title: Construction and Decoding of Convolutional Codes with optimal Column Distances
Information Theory.summary: The construction of Maximum Distance Profile (MDP) convolutional codes in general requires the use of very large finite fields. In contrast convolutional codes with optimal column distances maximize the column distances for a given arbitrary finite field. In this paper, we present a construction of such convolutional codes. In addition, we prove that for the considered parameters the codes that we constructed are the only ones achieving optimal column distances. The structure of the presented convolutional codes with optimal column distances is strongly related to first order Reed-Muller block codes and we leverage this fact to develop a reduced complexity version of the Viterbi algorithm for these codes.

Probability.title: General diffusions on metric graphs as limits of space-time Markov chains
Probability.summary: We introduce the Space-Time Markov Chain Approximation (STMCA) for a general diffusion process on a finite metric graph $Γ$. The STMCA is a doubly asymmetric (in both time and space) random walk defined on subdivisions of $Γ$, with transition probabilities and conditional transition times that match, in expectation, those of the target diffusion. We derive bounds on the $p$-Wasserstein distances between a non-explosive diffusion and its STMCA in terms of a thinness quantifier of the subdivision. An extension to absorbed diffusions uses a boundary-adapted Green-kernel thinness that remains finite even at certain singular exit boundaries. Under the stated regularity and subdivision hypotheses, this gives convergence at any rate strictly less than $\frac14\wedge\frac1p$ in the appropriate thinness quantifier. For suitably adapted subdivisions satisfying a quadratic thinness bound, we show that the rate is doubled: we achieve any rate strictly less than $\frac12\wedge\frac2p$ in terms of the maximum cell size. Additionally, we provide explicit analytical formulas for transition probabilities and times, enabling practical implementation of the STMCA, as well as easily verifiable sufficient non-explosion conditions for the bounds to hold. Numerical experiments illustrate our results.

Probability.title: On the continuity of conditional distributions and stratification for derivative pricing
Probability.summary: Stratification can reduce the estimator variance in Monte Carlo simulations by partitioning the sample space according to a low-dimensional factor and sampling separately within the resulting strata, making it well suited to the valuation of path-dependent claims in high-dimensional financial models. Its performance, however, depends critically on the choice of the stratification factor, and effective low-dimensional factors are generally difficult to identify in complex continuous-time models. Neural networks provide a flexible approximation class for this purpose and have proved useful in related variance-reduction problems in quantitative finance. In this paper, we study the construction of neural stratification factors for derivative pricing under proportional allocation in continuous-time models. Since the numerical construction of a stratification factor typically involves approximation, we establish continuity results for the associated conditional expectations and, more generally, conditional distributions, and provide several counterexamples showing the limits of this continuity theory. Combined with density results for neural networks, our findings yield a universal approximation theorem for admissible stratification factors. We conclude with numerical experiments involving a constant-maturity-swap range accrual in a two-factor Gaussian short-rate model and a worst-of autocallable in a Wishart stochastic covariance model, where the learned factors outperform all considered benchmarks.

Probability.title: A Central Limit Theorem for the Driver Site Frequency Spectrum
Probability.summary: We consider a supercritical two-type continuous-time linear birth-death process with mutation and selection, in which wild-type individuals give rise to mutant offspring with a larger net-growth rate. We previously had obtained first-order law of large number results for the driver site frequency spectrum. We return to obtain a second-order central limit theorem, in which we show stable convergence of a scaling of the deviation of the SFS from its first-order limit. We provide a central limit theorem at both large detection times and sizes. Then, we apply these results to obtain confidence intervals for a class of consistent estimators for the fitness advance.

Probability.title: Probabilistic ultraviolet renormalization of the two-dimensional Sine-Gordon model
Probability.summary: We give a probabilistic approach to the ultraviolet renormalization of the two-dimensional Sine-Gordon model. The model is formally described by the density $\exp(α\int \mathopen{:} \cos(βX) \mathclose{:} )$, where $X$ is a log-correlated Gaussian field. Our construction applies on bounded convex domains for every particle activity $α\in\mathbb R$ and throughout the subcritical range $β^2\in[0,4)$, below the Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless threshold. We apply the martingale method introduced by Lacoin, Rhodes and Vargas to two dimensions by using refined estimates based on charge conjugation symmetries. Our result extends existing constructions by treating the full subcritical regime for a broad class of covariances.

Probability.title: The Order Mass Identity of Rooted Forests, with a Direct Proof of the Extended Aldous-Broder Theorem
Probability.summary: The Aldous-Broder algorithm constructs a spanning tree from the first-entrance edges of a covering random walk. Its distribution is known, but deriving it by summing over the orders in which a fixed tree can be discovered remains difficult. In this paper, we evaluate this sum by establishing an order-mass identity for rooted forests. For real matrices with zero row sums, the identity expresses the sum of order weights associated with each root as a principal cofactor of a matrix on the roots, under a nonsingularity condition involving only the sets encountered along the growth orders of the given forest. We prove the identity using linear algebraic tools. With one root, the sum equals one, giving a direct proof of the extended Aldous-Broder theorem for every finite irreducible Markov chain started at a fixed state. With multiple roots, we derive the forest law produced by the stopped covering walk and show how it differs from the weight-proportional forest law. The identity and the resulting tree and forest laws are formalized in Lean 4.

Probability.title: Optimal local laws and CLT for the circular Riesz gas
Probability.summary: We study the circular Riesz gas, a one-dimensional system of particles with long-range power-law repulsion. We establish near-optimal rigidity estimates for the gaps at all scales. We then prove a quantitative central limit theorem for linear statistics, combining Stein's method with a mean-field transport. The main difficulty is to control the fluctuations of the local error terms left by the transport, which we do using the rigidity estimates, convexity and monotonicity. In particular, a comparison principle for the Helffer--Sjöstrand equation allows us to treat test functions with low regularity, including indicators of intervals.

Probability.title: The lower tail of triangle counts in sparse random graphs
Probability.summary: Let $T_n$ be the number of triangles in the Erdős-Rényi random graph $G(n,p)$ with $n^{-1/2}\ll p\ll1$ and fix $η\in(0,1)$. We study the large deviation rate of the lower tail event $T_n\leη\mathbb{E}[T_n]$, and the typical structure of $G(n,p)$ conditioned on this event. By earlier work [16,19,21,49], both the rate and the structure are governed by a variational problem over graphons. In this work we solve this variational problem for every $η\in(0,1)$. We show that every minimizer is either a constant graphon or a step graphon with two blocks of equal size. Correspondingly, the conditioned graph is close to an Erdős-Rényi graph or to a symmetric stochastic block model with two blocks. These two regimes are separated by a first order phase transition at the threshold $η_*=0.009217\ldots$. This resolves a conjecture of Zhao [78] and an open problem of Janson and Warnke [39] on triangles. It thereby gives a complete description of the lower tail of triangle counts in this range of $p$.

Probability.title: Near-critical Ising interfaces in the thermal direction: Absolute continuity with respect to SLE$_3$
Probability.summary: The scaling limits of interfaces in the critical two-dimensional Ising model are described by the Schramm--Loewner evolution $\mathrm{SLE}_3$. While, in the scaling limit, the law of the whole near-critical FK-Ising configuration is known to be singular with respect to the critical law in the thermal direction, and the same is expected for the spin configuration, we prove in this paper that the law of a single interface is not. More precisely, we consider the Ising model with mesh $δ$ in the Dobrushin square at $β=β_c-mδ$, where $m\ne0$ is fixed, and we prove that the Radon-Nikodym derivative of the law of the interface with respect to its critical law has moments of every positive and negative order, bounded uniformly in $δ$, so that the law of every subsequential scaling limit of the interface is mutually absolutely continuous with respect to that of $\mathrm{SLE}_3$. Our analysis explains the mechanism behind this result: the logarithmically growing specific heat (that is, the variance of the Hamiltonian, normalized by the number of edges) cancels between the full domain and the domain slit along the interface.

Probability.title: Second-order perturbation bounds for Gibbs samplers under strong spatial mixing
Probability.summary: The basic question in perturbation analysis of Markov chains is how small changes in their transition kernels affect their stationary distributions. Classical perturbation bounds typically require the kernel error to be much smaller than $1/τ$, where $τ$ is a mixing or relaxation time. Although this scaling is sharp for Markov chains in general, we investigate a general "square-rooting" phenomenon in which one-step errors of order roughly $1/\sqrtτ$ can be sufficient for local updates. We proved a form of this phenomenon in Lin, Liu and Smith (2025) under strong assumptions. Here we substantially weaken these assumptions, and prove this phenomenon occurs using three distinct approaches. First, block factorization applies under structural assumptions on the stationary measures of both chains. Second, approximate block-update arguments extend the result to statistically relevant Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) settings, where structural guarantees are available for the exact posterior and its associated sampler, but not for the perturbed posterior. Third, we use direct calculations for a class of models with hard constraints where neither general result is directly available. We illustrate these results in three MCMC settings and show how they directly inform the tuning of approximate MCMC algorithms.

Probability.title: The Two-Dimensional Narrow Escape Problem with Deterministic Initial Condition: Mean Escape Time and Escape location probabilities
Probability.summary: This paper presents a rigorous asymptotic analysis of the two-dimensional narrow escape problem for a Brownian particle initiated at a deterministic position x. While we address the mean escape time, the main novelty lies in our derivation of the asymptotic escape distribution. We derive explicit asymptotic formulas that characterize the dependence of the escape behavior on the relative configuration of the starting point and the window centers. These results remain valid as the starting position approaches the boundary windows and include refined error estimates. The formulas are obtained with two independent methods, each of them having their own interest. A central feature of this work is the rigorous treatment of the underlying mixed boundary value problems in the absence of a contact angle at the escape window boundaries. By leveraging recent results on the maximal regularity of the gradient of the solutions of such mixed boundary value problems, we ensure the analytical validity of our approach despite the inherent loss of regularity of these solutions at the escape window boundaries. Finally, we apply these general results to provide a full sharp asymptotic equivalents for regimes where window sizes scale at specific relative rates.

Probability.title: The boosted loop-erased random walk
Probability.summary: We consider a near-critical version of loop-erased random walk (LERW) by boosting the weight of the underlying random walk according to its length before loop-erasure. We construct the scaling limit in natural parametrization in the two-dimensional unit disk and the three-dimensional unit ball. The boosted scaling limit undergoes a phase transition in mutual absolute continuity with the classical LERW scaling limit; in the disk the transition occurs at boost rate $m^2=π^2/4$. As the boost increases, the curve becomes macroscopically space-filling, in the sense that unvisited cubes have side length $O(m^{-1})$, while its Hausdorff dimension at each finite boost is unchanged. These results are motivated by Makarov--Smirnov's questions on near-critical lattice models. In the planar chordal setting, we also construct a continuum loop tilt below the spectral threshold of the domain and calculate its Loewner driving function.

Probability.title: Stochastic Inverse Problem: stability, regularization and Wasserstein gradient flow
Probability.summary: Inverse problems in physical or biological sciences often involve recovering an unknown parameter that is random. The sought-after quantity is a probability distribution of the unknown parameter, that produces data that aligns with measurements. Consequently, these problems are naturally framed as stochastic inverse problems. In this paper, we explore three aspects of this problem: direct inversion, variational formulation with regularization, and optimization via gradient flows, drawing parallels with deterministic inverse problems. A key difference from the deterministic case is the space in which we operate. Here, we work within a probability space rather than Euclidean or Sobolev spaces, making tools from measure transport theory necessary for the study. Our findings reveal that the choice of metric---both in the design of the loss function and in the optimization process---significantly impacts the stability and properties of the optimizer.

Probability.title: Non-equilibrium density fluctuations for the stirring process with weak boundary dynamics
Probability.summary: We consider the one-dimensional stirring process on the segment $\{-N,\ldots,N\}$, coupled to boundary dynamics that inject particles from the right reservoir and remove particles from the left reservoir, each acting on a window of size $K$. We investigate the non-equilibrium fluctuations of the system, starting from a product measure associated with a smooth initial profile. The limit Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process is given in terms of the Laplacian and gradient operators acting on test functions satisfying time-dependent Robin boundary conditions that are obtained by linearizing the boundary conditions in the hydrodynamic equation. A central ingredient in our analysis is the derivation of sharp bounds on the space and space-time $v$-functions of arbitrary degree for the centered occupation variables; these bounds were proved in the companion article \cite{birmpa2025nonequilibriumfluctuationsstirringprocess}.
Probability.comment: This paper is the second part of the original manuscript arXiv:2512.12902, "Non-equilibrium Fluctuations for the stirring process with births and deaths", which was split into two papers. The original arXiv entry now contains the first part, retitled "Space-time bounds for the stirring process with births and deaths"; this paper presents the remaining results

Probability.title: Avalanches of the Abelian sandpile on the hierarchical lattice
Probability.summary: We study the Abelian sandpile model on a sequence of finite fractal graphs: the hierarchical, or Migdal--Kadanoff, lattices. Our first main result consists of matching power-law tail bounds for the avalanche and the uniform wave started at certain "pivotal" vertices. We also establish a limiting result for the pivotal reach of the avalanche and, finally, a scaling limit for the size of a uniform wave started at a vertex of high degree.

Probability.title: The Martingale Property in Volterra Volatility Models
Probability.summary: We study martingality and strict local martingality in a broad class of stochastic and path-dependent Volterra volatility models and explain the underlying mechanisms. Our martingality criteria allow rough kernels and rely on non-accessibility of an explosive direction or one-sided growth bounds on the Girsanov drift. For smooth kernels, we derive sufficient conditions for strict local martingality from an explosion criterion allowing multiplicative noise, coupled factors and general initial input curves. Our results recover classical criteria and yield new results for Volterra and path-dependent models.

Probability.title: How much do increasing events occur disjointly?
Probability.summary: We establish two general quantitative lower bounds on the gap in the classical BK inequality for increasing events. The first is an analogue of Talagrand's quantitative FKG inequality (1996) and depends on the influences. The second is specific to the BK inequality and involves both the influences and the probabilities of symmetric disjoint pivots.

Probability.title: Approximating the Gibbs Measure of Spherical Spin Glasses to Within $o(N^{-1/2})$ in the Replica Symmetric Phase
Probability.summary: We study the magnetization vector of mixed spherical spin glasses in a weak external field, in the replica symmetric phase. We derive a coordinatewise expansion of the magnetization which includes the leading cubic correction to the quadratic approximation, with an error that is $o(N^{-1/2})$ per coordinate. We also prove a corresponding high-moment bound for the full vector. Finally, our companion paper applies these estimates to the effective Hamiltonian obtained by restricting a tilted spherical spin glass to a narrow band around a TAP critical point. The resulting sharp approximation is designed for applications in which normalized Wasserstein accuracy is insufficient, including total-variation sampling by stochastic localization.
Probability.comment: Companion paper to the paper Sampling from Spherical Spin Glasses in Total Variation via Algorithmic Stochastic Localization (arXiv:2404.15651) by the same authors

Probability.title: The solution of the Hopfield model with Gaussian patterns
Probability.summary: We prove that the free energy of the Hopfield model with Gaussian patterns has a thermodynamic limit at every load $α$ and temperature $T$, and we give it as an explicit variational principle. The Hubbard--Stratonovich transformation maps the model onto $N$ Ising spins coupled to $M=αN$ Gaussian hidden units, whose radius, the empirical variance of the hidden layer, is a thermodynamic variable with an entropic cost. At fixed radius the model is an Ising--spherical spin glass with Gaussian couplings, which we solve. The principle (i) reproduces the Amit-Gutfreund-Sompolinsky theory as its replica-symmetric restriction, (ii) identifies $T_g=1+\sqrtα$ as the rigorous boundary of the annealed region, (iii) selects a unique spin-glass solution of the AGS equations, and (iv) gives the radius an equation of state. Moreover, (v) below $T_g$ we prove that replica symmetry is broken throughout: the instability of the AGS solution reduces to the zero-field de Almeida-Thouless condition of the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick model.

Probability.title: On Trace Averages and Sharp Asymptotics for Powers of Haar-Unitary Matrices
Probability.summary: For a Haar-distributed matrix $U \in U(N)$, Rains's power-map theorem represents the spectrum of $U^m$, $m \in \mathbb{N}$, as a superposition of independent lower-dimensional CUE spectra. We determine how this exact decomposition appears in trace moments and in sharp Gaussian and Poisson limit laws. For averages of mixed trace products, a Charlier--Ewens convolution separates the stable Wick term from its full finite-$N$ correction. A Fredholm factorisation gives sharp total-variation asymptotics for the normalised trace in four regimes, from fixed powers to $m\geq N$. For a fixed trace power $p$, coherent summation of the leading Laguerre correction yields the exact factor $e^{2/p}$. At the mean-spacing scale, we obtain a sharp Poisson limit for the unfolded spectrum of $U^m$ on a fixed interval as $N, m \rightarrow \infty$; its first-order correction, obtained via the second Charlier polynomial, quantifies the residual under-dispersion of local eigenvalue counts.

Probability.title: Stochastic predator-prey compartment model with cyclic and non-cyclic transition pathways and mortality
Probability.summary: We study variants of a stochastic SEIRS-SEID compartmental model incorporating presymptomatic infectiousness and disease-related mortality, with independent compartmental sojourn times drawn from arbitrary distributions, in particular Weibull distributions. We consider a large population of agents that occupy the states (compartments) S (susceptible to infection), E (exposed: infected but asymptomatic during the latency period and already infectious, including diseases with presymptomatic infections), I (infected and infectious, with symptoms), R (recovered, immune, and non-infectious), or D (dead). We consider (i) cyclic transmission pathways, where compartmental sojourn times are finite and immunity is temporary, and (ii) non-cyclic pathways, where immunity is permanent. In the absence of mortality, cyclic transmission pathways support an endemic equilibrium above the spreading threshold which is either globally stable or oscillatory (Hopf) unstable, whereas for non-cyclic pathways a stationary disease-free state is emerging. From a stochastic perspective, we elucidate the connection between compartmental sojourn-time distributions and the appearance of fractional operators in the evolution equations: fat-tailed compartment waiting-time distributions necessarily lead to fractional derivatives. For cyclic transition pathways we obtain an explicit expression for the expected number of infection cycles that an agent survives. Our model is validated by a combined Monte Carlo -- Runge -- Kutta simulation scheme and random-walk simulations on Barabasi-Albert networks. It has cross-disciplinary applications beyond epidemiology, including wildfire spreading, certain classes of chemical reactions, population dynamics, finance, economics, and biology.
