Probability.title: On the $q$-integrability of $p$-Wasserstein barycenters
Probability.summary: We study the $L^q$-regularity of the density of barycenters of $N$ probability measures on $\mathbb{R}^d$ with respect to the $p$-Wasserstein metric ($1<p<\infty$). According to a previous result by the first author and collaborators, if one marginal is absolutely continuous, so is the $W_p$-barycenter. The next natural question is whether the $L^q$- regularity on the marginals is also preserved for any $q > 1$, as in the classical case ($p=2$) of Agueh--Carlier, or for $W_p$-geodesics ($N=2$). Here we prove that this is the case if one marginal belongs to $L^q$ and the supports of all the marginals satisfy suitable geometric assumptions. However, we show that, as soon as $N>2$, it is possible to find examples of $W_p$-barycenters which are not $q$-integrable, even if one marginal is compactly supported and bounded, thus highlighting the role played by the geometry of the supports. Furthermore, we provide a general estimate of the $L^q$-norm, including a detailed study of the sources of singularities, and a characterization of the $W_p$-barycenters à la Agueh--Carlier in terms of the associated Kantorovich potentials. Finally, we explicitly compute the $W_p$-barycenters of measures obtained as push-forward of special affine transformations. In this case, regularity holds without any additional requirement on the supports.

Probability.title: $Φ^4_3$ measures on compact Riemannian $3$-manifolds
Probability.summary: We construct the $Φ^4_3$ measure on an arbitrary 3-dimensional compact Riemannian manifold without boundary as an invariant probability measure of a singular stochastic partial differential equation. Proving the nontriviality and the covariance under Riemannian isometries of that measure gives a non-perturbative, non-topological interacting Euclidean quantum field measure on curved spaces in dimension 3. To control analytically several Feynman diagrams appearing in the construction of a number of random fields, we introduce a novel approach of renormalisation using microlocal and harmonic analysis. This allows to obtain a renormalized equation which involves some universal constants independent of the manifold. In a companion paper \cite{BDFTCompanion}, we develop all the tools from paradifferential and microlocal analysis that we use to build in our manifold setting a number of analytic and probabilistic objects.

Probability.title: Conditional Stable Laws and Rare-Event Limits for Absorbing Markov Chains
Probability.summary: We establish conditional limit theorems, pointwise in the initial state, for absorbing Markov chains on a compact metric space $M$. We assume $L^1(M,ρ)$-continuous transition densities, irreducibility and aperiodicity. For the observable $f_β(x)=d_M(x,x_0)^{-β}$, with suitable $x_0$ satisfying $ρ(B_r(x_0))\sim C_d(x_0)r^d$, we prove that the point-process of normalised observations converges to a Poisson random measure. This yields totally right-skewed $α$-stable laws for $α=d/β\in(0,2)$ and, at the boundary value $α=2$, a Gaussian limit with the non-standard normalisation $\sqrt{n\log n}$. We also establish a conditional central limit theorem for $L^2$ observables, exponential deviation bounds for bounded observables and a conditional Poisson law for visits to shrinking targets. The results and remarks have been formalised in Lean~4.

Probability.title: On the closure under barycenters of location-scatter families with a normalized generator
Probability.summary: We provide an example of a normalized absolutely continuous probability whose location-scatter family (LSF) does not contain all the 2-Wassertein geodesics passing through its elements. In particular, we find a counterexample for Corollary 4.5 in [2]. Finally, we prove that LSFs with a (possibly singular) radially symmetric generator are closed under 2-Wasserstein barycenters.

Probability.title: Generalized Wasserstein Flow Matching: Nested Couplings for Point Cloud Generation
Probability.summary: We formulate flow matching on probability measures over probability measures. Directly from the Wasserstein-on-Wasserstein (WoW) continuity equation, we show that admissible nested outer and inner couplings induce a valid metameasure flow and non-local velocity field. Validity requires neither optimal plans nor a smooth manifold. Practically, this opens up the design space of multisample flow matching: exact Wasserstein plans are distinguished by energy and straightness, while sliced and lazy linear plans yield scalable alternatives. Point-cloud experiments, including controlled Bures-Wasserstein and Euclidean minibatch baselines, demonstrate the resulting geometry-cost trade-off.
Probability.comment: Keywords: flow matching, Wasserstein over Wasserstein, hierarchical optimal transport, multisample flow matching, minibatch optimal transport, sliced Wasserstein, Bures-Wasserstein, point cloud generation, generative models for distributions, measure-valued data, Wasserstein gradient flow, rectified flow, straight flows

Probability.title: Sharp Error Estimates for a Fully Discrete Approximation of Semilinear Stochastic Convection--Diffusion Equations with Additive Noise and Nonsmooth Initial Data
Probability.summary: We establish sharp strong error estimates for a fully discrete approximation of semilinear stochastic convection--diffusion equations driven by additive noise subject to nonsmooth initial data. The problem is discretized in space using a standard Galerkin finite element method and in time via the linearly implicit Euler scheme. By decoupling the noise regularity index $β\in (0, 2]$ from the initial data regularity index $μ\in (0, 2]$, we derive time-weighted spatial and temporal regularity bounds that isolate the initial singularity at $t = 0$ into an integrable temporal weight. By allowing the drift operator $F$ to map into negative-order fractional spaces to incorporate the convection term, we prove sharp strong convergence rates of order $O(h^β+ k^{β/2})$ for $β\in (0, 2)$ and $O\bigl(h^2 + k(1+\ln(t_n/k))^{1/2}\bigr)$ at the critical endpoint $β= 2$ for any fixed $t_n > 0$, without requiring the regularity of the initial data to match that of the noise. Furthermore, these convergence rates are achieved under a relaxed differentiability condition requiring only a Lipschitz continuous first Gâteaux derivative of $F$. Numerical experiments validate the theoretical results across both trace-class and space-time white noise regimes.
Probability.comment: The title has been updated to reflect the stochastic convection-diffusion framework explicitly. Major revisions include extending the analysis under relaxed first-order Gâteaux differentiability assumptions on the drift and streamlining the presentation to focus on the fully discrete scheme with refined regularity and error estimates

Probability.title: Generalized fluctuation bounds for stochastic algorithms in the presence of compactness
Probability.summary: We provide a convergence result for sequences of random variables taking values in a metric space that satisfy a stochastic quasi-Fejér monotonicity condition, in the context of a (local) compactness assumption. Our result is quantitative in that we derive an explicit and effective construction which, in terms of only a few moduli representing quantitative witnesses to key properties of the sequence of random variables and the underlying metric space involved, provides a metastable rate of pointwise convergence, a type of generalized fluctuation bound. That quantitative result in particular relies on the development of a finitary theory of martingales, culminating in a fully finitary Robbins-Siegmund theorem. We outline how this result particularises to the circumstances of the seminal work of Combettes and Pesquet on stochastic quasi-Fejér monotone sequences in separable Hilbert spaces, and we provide an initial application by illustrating how these results can be used to provide a metastable rate of pointwise convergence for a stochastic Krasnoselskii-Mann scheme solving a stochastic common fixed point problem for nonexpansive maps over proper Hadamard spaces. This work is set in the context of recent applications of the logic-based methodology of proof mining to probability theory, and represents its most sophisticated case study to date.

Probability.title: Limit theorems for supercritical branching processes in Markovian environment with linear fractional offspring distributions
Probability.summary: In this paper, we study the asymptotic behaviour for distribution of supercritical branching process in a Markovian environment with linear fractional offspring distributions. Phase transitions in the behaviour of the process is discovered, through investigating the strongly, intermediately and weakly supercritical cases.
Probability.comment: Current version (Version 2): 35 pages (19 pages in Version 1), 1 figure (0 figure in Version 1). The limit theorem for weakly supercritical case is added. Some typos are corrected, 1 figure is added for illustration, the structure of the manuscript is improved and there is a change of authorship

Probability.title: The Fixed-$q$ Edge Limit of the $q$-Krawtchouk Ensemble
Probability.summary: We study the fixed-$q$ right-edge asymptotics of the ordinary $q$-Krawtchouk ensemble. For $0<q<1$, finite polynomial duality gives a direct proof of convergence of the correlation kernels to an explicit limiting kernel. The local Jacobi limit is a shifted continuous $q^{-1}$-Hermite expression with an indeterminate moment problem, so the limiting Jacobi expression does not determine a unique self-adjoint operator. A single spectral atom, asymptotically saturating the mass bound, selects the realization and yields strong-resolvent convergence. The limiting kernel represents its positive spectral projection and admits spectral-series, Christoffel--Darboux, and partial-theta representations. After a ground-state transformation, the associated dual operator agrees with a two-step spatial Markov operator of Borodin--Corwin. For $q>1$, the limiting Jacobi operator is of Al-Salam--Carlitz~I type and is essentially self-adjoint.

Probability.title: Optimality of finite field dimension expanders
Probability.summary: We show that random tuples of matrices over a finite field are uniform dimension expanders for every expansion coefficient below the optimal one, using elementary counting arguments. The same holds for the optimal coefficient along a set of dimensions of density 1. By contrast, along Fibonacci dimensions random pairs of matrices fail to be optimal dimension expanders with probability bounded away from zero.

Probability.title: Discrete Approximation to Time-changed Brownian Motions
Probability.summary: We develop a general discrete approximation scheme for time-changed Brownian motions on $\mathbb{R}^d$. Our approximation scheme works for any smooth measure with full quasi-support on $\mathbb{R}^d$ with suitable initial distributions. Under some mild conditions on the smooth measure, the discrete approximation scheme works for every starting point. Our results in particular give a discrete approximation scheme for Liouville Brownian motions.

Probability.title: A stochastic mirror descent algorithm for mean-field control problems
Probability.summary: We develop a stochastic mirror descent method for continuous-time McKean-Vlasov control with measure-valued controls and general Bregman regularisation. The dependence on the state law leads to a coupled Wasserstein-Bregman stability problem and to a McKean-Vlasov adjoint equation, which have no counterpart in classical stochastic control. We establish a first-order representation of the cost and prove its relative smoothness in two regimes: nonlinear dynamics with bounded cost derivatives, and affine state-law dynamics with linearly growing cost derivatives, the latter covering linear-quadratic (LQ) and more general nonquadratic models. Our regularity conditions in the control measure are formulated through directional finite increments and do not require second-order flat derivatives. We further introduce relative semiconvexity along admissible forward-backward trajectories, allowing compensation between the dynamics, running cost, and terminal cost beyond pointwise Hamiltonian convexity. This yields energy dissipation, an O(1/n) convergence rate at the convexity threshold, and geometric convergence when regularisation dominates relative nonconvexity. Explicit LQ criteria and numerical experiments illustrate the scope of the results.

Probability.title: Wasserstein bounds for invariant measures in the Smoluchowski-Kramers approximation with stable noise
Probability.summary: We study invariant position distributions in the Smoluchowski-Kramers approximation for Langevin equations driven by rotationally symmetric \(α\)-stable noise, with \(α\in(1,2)\). Under global Lipschitz continuity and dissipativity of the drift, we establish a Wasserstein-1 bound of order \(m^{1/α}\) between the invariant position distribution of the underdamped system and the invariant distribution of its overdamped limit, where $m>0$ is the mass parameter. The proof combines a corrected-position test function with a regularized Stein equation. Cancellation of the transport and friction terms reduces the comparison to a first-moment estimate for the stationary velocity.

Probability.title: Perfect t-Embeddings of Uniformly Weighted Generalized Tower Graphs
Probability.summary: In this paper, we study sequences of perfect t-embeddings of a uniformly weighted family of graphs we call generalized tower graphs. We show that the embeddings of these graphs satisfy certain technical assumptions, in particular, the rigidity assumption of Berggren-Nicoletti-Russkikh. As a result, we confirm the convergence of the gradients of the height function fluctuations of these graphs to those of the Gaussian free field.

Probability.title: Rough path lifts of multifractional Brownian motions
Probability.summary: We show that multifractional Brownian motions (mBms) can be lifted to geometric rough paths. One of the main ingredients in the proof is a decomposition of mBms via the Lemarié-Meyer orthogonal wavelet basis, which is introduced in the context of multiresolution analysis. As a consequence, we are able to construct solutions to rough differential equations driven by mBms.

Probability.title: Construction and sample path properties of diffusion house-moving between two curves
Probability.summary: This study aims to construct a stochastic process called ``diffusion house-moving,'' which is a diffusion bridge conditioned to stay between its starting point and its ending point. To construct this process, statements are prepared on the weak convergence of conditioned diffusion processes, and conditioned diffusion bridges. Moreover, the sample path properties of diffusion house-moving are studied as well.

Probability.title: Counterexamples for lacunary dilates via dyadic spike blocks
Probability.summary:
We construct counterexamples, along dyadic lacunary sequences, to two problems of Erdős on the almost-everywhere behavior of sums $\sum_{j\le N}f(n_jx)$ on the circle. The main device is a dyadic spike block: rare positive spikes, each counted many times by a run of consecutive dilates, make the lacunary averages large, while a deterministic lower bound on every block prevents the rest of the series from cancelling them.
  We obtain a mean-zero $f\in\bigcap_{1\le q<\infty}L^q(\mathbb T)$ and a sequence $n_j=2^{m_j}$ with $n_{j+1}/n_j\ge2$ such that $\|f-S_Nf\|_2\ll(\log\log N)^{-1/2}$ and $\limsup_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\sum_{j\le N}f(n_jx)=+\infty$ for almost every $x$. This answers negatively a question of Erdős on whether the condition $\|f-S_Nf\|_2\ll(\log\log\log N)^{-C}$ suffices for almost-everywhere convergence, and shows that Matsuyama's condition $\|f-S_Nf\|_2\ll(\log\log N)^{-c}$, $c>1/2$, cannot be relaxed to $c=1/2$. A second choice of parameters gives, for every $2\le p<\infty$, functions $f\in L^p(\mathbb T)$ with $\limsup_{N\to\infty}\sum_{j\le N}f(n_jx)/(N(\log N)^{1/p-\varepsilon})=+\infty$ for every $\varepsilon>0$, almost everywhere. This is sharp up to $\varepsilon$, and the case $p=2$ answers negatively a second question of Erdős. Finally, a bounded variant in the spirit of Marstrand's disproof of Khintchine's conjecture gives sets of arbitrarily small measure whose lacunary visiting frequencies have limsup $1$ almost everywhere.
Probability.comment: 26 pages, 1 figure. v3: revised following referee comments; references to Marstrand, Bourgain and Koksma added; exposition revised

Probability.title: On the Propeller Conjecture
Probability.summary: We simplify and improve OpenAI's proof of the propeller conjecture of Khot and Naor from 2008: the sum of the squared lengths of the Gaussian moments of any partition of Euclidean space is at most $9/(8π)$. We show equality only occurs for three 120 degree sectors in the plane (up to symmetries, measure zero changes, and taking orthogonal cross products with Euclidean space). We also remove computer assistance from the three-dimensional case of the conjecture, which previously used an epsilon net traversal.

Probability.title: Graph distance and percolation dimension of three-dimensional Brownian motion
Probability.summary: We prove that the minimum Hausdorff dimension of a continuous curve joining $W_0$ to $W_1$ within the range $W([0,1])$ of a three-dimensional Brownian motion is almost surely a deterministic constant $γ_3\in(1,5/3]$. Moreover, we construct continuum many simple curves with pairwise distinct images that attain this minimum. Each curve has box dimension $γ_3$ and admits a parametrization that is $β$-Hölder for every $0<β<1/γ_3$. To identify $γ_3$, we partition Brownian time into $n$ equal intervals and form a graph by joining pairs with intersecting ranges. We show that its endpoint graph distance and diameter have a common deterministic almost sure growth exponent $θ$ and that $γ_3=2θ$. We also establish $n^{pθ+o(1)}$ growth for their $p$-th moments, for every $p>0$.

Probability.title: Strongly log-concave measures and lattices
Probability.summary: Let $Λ\subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ be a full rank lattice with the property that $\det Γ\ge 1$ for all sublattices $Γ\subseteq Λ^*$. We prove that there exists a symmetric random vector $X \in \mathbb{R}^n$ with a smooth, strictly positive density $f : \mathbb{R}^n \to (0, \infty)$ satisfying that (1) $f$ is $α$-strongly log-concave, where $α= 2π/e$, and (2) $X + Λ$ is uniform on $\mathbb{R}^n/Λ$. Moreover, the existence of such a density characterizes this property up to a universal dilation. There are a few consequences of the above. We list some. First, for such lattices we can bound the covering radius \[ μ(Λ, K) = \max_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n}\min_{λ\inΛ} \left\|x-λ\right\|_K \le \sqrt{\frac{2e}π} \cdot \mathbb{E}\,\left\|G\right\|_K \] of a convex body $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ containing $0$ in its interior, where $G \sim N(0,\mathrm{Id})$. This implies an $O(n \sqrt{\log n})$ bound for the flatness constant and an $O(\log^{3/2} n)$ bound for the subspace flatness constant. We also compare the entire ordered spectrum of the associated flat torus on $Λ^*$ with that of a Gaussian, yielding an alternative proof of the reverse Minkowski theorem.

Probability.title: Differentially Private Synthetic Data via Generalized Moment Matching
Probability.summary: We study $(\varepsilon,δ)$-differentially private synthetic data for arbitrary databases of $n$ records in $[-1,1]^d$ under a specified integral probability metric (IPM). We introduce generalized moment matching, which estimates moments privately, fits a probability measure, and samples synthetic records. A general error theorem applies when moment error controls the target IPM. This framework extends Chebyshev moment matching for $1$-Wasserstein distance and smooth queries. We apply the framework to maximum mean discrepancy with Matern and Laplace kernels and a two-layer ReLU neural tangent kernel. We also obtain guarantees for sliced Wasserstein-$1$ and the IPM induced by norm-bounded ReLU networks. With sufficiently many synthetic records,these rates are minimax optimal up to logarithmic factors for fixed dimension.

Probability.title: Discretization and Statistical Consistency of Functional Flow Matching
Probability.summary: Functional flow matching learns to generate random functions, such as velocity fields or solutions of partial differential equations, by continuously transforming a simple probability distribution into a target distribution. In practice, however, training and sampling use only finitely many grid values or coefficients. Does refining these observations recover the intended function-space model, and how do observation, learning, and numerical errors affect the generated distribution? We address these questions by first proving that the velocity targets used for training converge in mean square when the finite reconstructions converge to the underlying functions and remain uniformly bounded. The observations need not be nested: each refinement may replace earlier sensor locations. We also give quantitative bounds for orthogonal projections and extend the result to point observations under suitable regularity and reconstruction assumptions. We then bound the discrepancy between the generated and target distributions in Wasserstein distance, separating observation, learning, numerical, and endpoint errors without requiring uniqueness of the population finite-dimensional dynamics. For a normalized quadrature neural operator representing the learned velocity field, we establish stability and learning bounds with constants independent of the number of sensors. Under fixed model dimension and boundedness assumptions, the statistical excess risk decreases at an inverse-sample-size rate, up to logarithmic factors. A Gaussian example combines these estimates into an explicit sampling-error rate.

Probability.title: The BAR-SOT Method: Long-term Average Cost Control as Stochastic Optimal Self-Transport
Probability.summary: We reformulate average-cost (ergodic) control of a Markov jump process as a finite-horizon stochastic optimal transport (SOT) problem that jointly optimizes over the controlled evolution and the marginal law from which it starts and returns to (i.e., a self-transport). The constraint relating the marginal flow to the controlled generator is the basic adjoint relationship (BAR), so we call the resulting problem BAR-SOT. For any time horizon T>0, its optimal value is a constant scaling of the long-run average-cost rate. We give three equivalent formulations (through controlled processes, a Fokker--Planck constraint, and relaxed marginal measures) and show that the optimal dual is a stationary potential plus a term linear in time, with slope equal to the rate. A relative-entropy penalty on the control yields a cost-tilted Schrodinger bridge problem, computable by a Sinkhorn-type iteration when every transition rate is controlled, whose value converges to the unregularized optimum as the penalty vanishes. We develop the theory for finite Markov decision processes and then for general controlled Markov jump processes. A neural parametrization of the dual, trained as a physics-informed neural network (PINN), that encodes Harrison's equivalent-workload formulation (see Harrison 2000) matches the strong reinforcement-learning baseline of Dai and Gluzman (2022); numerically conditioning the fit of a sub-dominant transverse correction then improves on both that baseline and the best priority heuristic. On the input-queued switch, a graph-attention parametrization of the dual improves on the strongest matching heuristic we are aware of, with a parameter count that does not grow with the switch size.

Probability.title: Superpixel-Based Image Segmentation Using Squared 2-Wasserstein Distances
Probability.summary: We present an efficient method for image segmentation in the presence of strong intensity inhomogeneities. The approach combines two levels of clustering: pixels are first grouped into superpixels using Power-SLIC, which admits a discrete optimal transport (OT) interpretation, and these superpixels are subsequently merged using squared 2-Wasserstein distances between their empirical distributions. We formulate the merging process as an adjacency-constrained hierarchical optimization problem with a regularized objective that accounts for the heterogeneities of previously formed regions. We establish NP-completeness of the associated global optimization problem, even for two final regions and two-bin histograms. For the proposed greedy algorithm, we prove exact recovery under suitable histogram separation conditions and derive an additive approximation bound for the regularized energy. Numerical experiments demonstrate competitive segmentation accuracy on images exhibiting substantial intensity inhomogeneity, while retaining computational efficiency.

Probability.title: Strong laws, random monotone vector fields and gradient flows on metric spaces of nonpositive curvature
Probability.summary: We establish a probabilistic Lie-Trotter-Kato formula for the gradient flow generated by an integral function over suitable separable Hadamard spaces. This result leverages Stojković's Lie-Trotter-Kato formula for gradient flows of sums of convex functions and Bačák's result relating resolvent and gradient flow convergence, along with a strong law of large numbers for normal convex integrands. For separable Hilbert spaces and locally compact Hadamard spaces, these strong laws follow from results of King and Wets and Artstein and Wets, respectively, but we crucially go beyond these examples by establishing a new such strong law for normal convex integrands on all Hadamard spaces whose tangent cones are isometric to Hilbert spaces, a class that includes non-Hilbertian, non-locally compact examples such as infinite-dimensional hyperbolic space. This new strong law arises as a combination of a strong law of large numbers for integrable random monotone vector fields on Hilbert-Hadamard spaces, that is, Hadamard spaces whose tangent cones all embed isometrically into Hilbert spaces, extending a result of Salim from Hilbert spaces, together with a new result on the interchangeability of the subdifferential and the integral, which we establish for $L^2$-Lipschitz integrands. This latter ingredient provides, to our knowledge, the first nonlinear version of (a particular case of) a previous result due variously to Ioffe and Tikhomirov, Levin, Hiriart-Urruty, Thibault as well as Rockafellar and Wets. On the way to this strong law for random monotone vector fields, we also establish a distribution-uniform generalization of Sturm's strong law of large numbers for inductive means of $L^1$-sequences of i.i.d. random variables on Hadamard spaces via a new effective non-asymptotic concentration inequality. Throughout the paper, we highlight various remaining open problems.

Probability.title: Berry-Esseen bounds for products of random matrices under a $2+δ$ polynomial moment
Probability.summary: Let $(g_{k})_{k \geq 1}$ be a sequence of independent and identically distributed matrices with law $μ$ on $\mathrm{GL}(d,\mathbb{R})$, where $d\geq2$ is an integer. Suppose that the closed semigroup generated by the support of $μ$ is strongly irreducible and proximal and that the polynomial moment of order $2+δ$ is finite, where $0<δ\leq 1$. We establish a Berry-Esseen bound of order $n^{-δ/2}$ for $\log \| g_{n} \cdots g_{1} v\|$, where $v$ is a nonzero vector in $\mathbb{R}^{d}$ and $\|\cdot\|$ is an arbitrary norm on $\mathbb{R}^{d}$. As an application, we also obtain a Berry-Esseen bound of order $n^{-δ/2}$ for $\log \| g_{n} \cdots g_{1}\|$, where $\|\cdot\|$ is any matrix norm. The proof combines an $m$-dependent approximation with Stein's method. The argument uses identities for exchangeable pairs constructed by resampling individual matrices, together with a concentration inequality for sums of the approximating variables.

Probability.title: Wasserstein convergence rates for empirical measures of point processes
Probability.summary: In this paper, we establish upper and lower bounds on the convergence rate of empirical measures of point processes under the Wasserstein distance. To this end, we first introduce a new metric on the space of finite counting measures. Unlike many existing metrics in the literature, our proposed metric incorporates the spatial locations of unmatched points. Drawing on both this new metric and existing metrics from the literature, we identify a set of common structural properties and develop a general framework for Wasserstein distances between point-process distributions based on metrics satisfying these properties. We then use this framework to investigate the convergence rates of empirical measures, providing quantitative guarantees for approximating the distribution of the underlying point process, and further establish corresponding concentration inequalities. These theoretical results may provide ingredients for constructing oracle goodness-of-fit tests for a specified point-process distribution. We also apply our theory to the approximation of Campbell measures and discuss how the resulting bounds can help assess Wasserstein-based learning of generative point-process models.

Probability.title: Gibbs measures on Cayley trees and homoclinic orbits
Probability.summary: We study the question of existence and multiplicity of homogeneous Markov Gibbs measures on Cayley trees with spin space $\mathbb{Z}$. We prove that, under a natural summability assumption on the interaction function, there are always at least two homogeneous Markov Gibbs measures satisfying two natural symmetry conditions. Moreover, any two homogeneous Markov Gibbs measures satisfying a suitable non-degeneracy assumption can be superimposed and produce infinitely many other homogeneous Markov Gibbs measures. When the interaction function $Q$ has bounded support in $\mathbb{Z}$, there is a one-to-one correspondence between homogeneous Markov Gibbs measures and suitable homoclinic orbits of a symplectomorphism of $\mathbb{R}^{2n}$, where $n$ is the smallest natural number such that $Q(i)=0$ for every $i>n$. For $n=1$, results from symbolic dynamics and horseshoes imply the existence of homogeneous Markov Gibbs measures whose single-site marginal is concentrated near an arbitrary finite subset of $N\mathbb{Z}$, where $N$ is a sufficiently large integer. In the case of interaction functions with infinite support, there is a one-to-one correspondence between homogeneous Markov Gibbs measures and suitable homoclinic orbits of a Lagrangian correspondence on the cotangent bundle of a Banach space.

Probability.title: Turning angle analysis reveals hidden anisotropies in intracellular transport
Probability.summary: Molecular motion within living cells provides a window into the physical principles underlying intracellular organization and transport. Yet a fundamental limitation remains: measured trajectories are often short, noisy, and randomly oriented, rendering spatial anisotropies inaccessible to conventional analyses. We show that turning-angle statistics provide a robust approach for uncovering anisotropies in anomalous diffusion. Using a two-dimensional anisotropic fractional Brownian motion model with random orientations, we show theoretically and through simulations that turning-angle distributions preserve signatures of anisotropy. We apply this approach to single-particle tracking data, including quantum dots in the cytoplasm of HeLa cells and membrane proteins in hippocampal neurons. Turning angles reveal hidden anisotropies in the motion of quantum dots and Kv1.4 channels, and in specific dynamical states of glycoprotein CD4. These results establish turning-angle analysis as a powerful strategy for detecting organization in complex environments and reveal that anisotropic anomalous diffusion is an {often} overlooked feature of intracellular dynamics.
Probability.comment: Main text: 22 pages, 6 figures; Supplementary information: 14 pages, 7 figures

Probability.title: Absorption probabilities of random walks without symmetry or general position
Probability.summary: Let $S_1,S_2,\dots$ be a random walk in $\mathbb R^d$ with independent identically distributed increments. We show that, for every distribution of the increments and for every $n\ge1$, \[ \mathbb P\bigl[0\notin\mathrm{conv}(S_1,\dots,S_n)\bigr] = \sum_{m=1}^n\frac1{m!}\sum_{\substack{k_1,\dots,k_m\ge1\\ k_1+\dots+k_m=n}}\frac{1}{k_1\cdots k_m}\,\mathbb P\bigl[0\notin\mathrm{conv}(S^{(1)}_{k_1},\dots,S^{(m)}_{k_m})\bigr], \] where $S^{(1)},S^{(2)},\dots$ are independent copies of the walk. No symmetry, general position or moment assumptions are needed. The result rests on a deterministic identity: for arbitrary vectors $x_1,\dots,x_n$, the number of orderings for which the convex hull of the partial sums avoids the origin equals the number of permutations for which the convex hull of the cycle sums avoids it. We derive it from a permutation-averaging identity for valuations obtained in our earlier work. Consequences include the identities of Sparre Andersen and Spitzer, the distribution-free absorption probabilities of Kabluchko, Vysotsky and Zaporozhets, their generating function found by Petrov, Randon-Furling and Zaporozhets, and a formula for the probability that the origin is never absorbed.

Probability.title: Derivative-Informed Dimension Reduction of Stochastic Differential Equations: A Path-Space Sensitivity Approach
Probability.summary: Uncertainty in the drift of a stochastic differential equation (SDE) induces uncertainty in statistical observables defined as expected functionals on path space. We propose a derivative-informed method for identifying low-dimensional structure in the drift-to-observable map, with the aim of improving the tractability of uncertainty quantification. This approach can be viewed as a generalization of the active subspace method to infinite-dimensional input spaces and to path-space observables of SDEs. Representing uncertainty in the drift by random perturbations in a Hilbert space, we construct a path-space sensitivity operator using first-order Fréchet derivatives of the observable with respect to the perturbation. We establish conditions under which the leading eigenfunctions of this operator correspond to directions of maximum mean squared sensitivity of the observable, thus enabling low-dimensional approximation with certified error bounds. We further introduce a martingale control variate of the Fréchet derivative that reduces error in sample-based estimators of the operator. Using a Galerkin scheme for numerical discretization, we show that reduced representations of the drift from the derivative-informed basis yield more accurate approximations of mean first hitting times of SDEs than the Karhunen-Loève expansion of the same truncation order.

Probability.title: Cutoff profile for the coupon collector with many collections
Probability.summary: We solve the problem posed by Erdős and Rényi in $1961$ about the limiting distribution of the number of draws $T_{n,m}$ that a coupon collector needs to complete $m$ collections of $n$ distinct types of coupons, when $m$ increases with $n$. For fixed $m$, Erdős and Rényi proved that $\mathbb P(T_{n,m}\leq n\log n+(m-1)n\log\log n-n\log (m-1)!+θn)$ converges to $ \mathcal G(θ)$, for every $θ\in \mathbb R$, as $n \to \infty$, where $\mathcal G$ is the standard Gumbel distribution function, and they asked what happens when $m=m(n)$ increases with $n$. We give a complete answer to this question. More precisely, for every increasing sequence $m=m(n)$, we determine explicit sequences $t_{n,m}$ and $w_{n,m}$ satisfying $w_{n,m}/t_{n,m}\to0$ such that $\mathbb P(T_{n,m}\leq t_{n,m}+θw_{n,m})\to\mathcal G(θ)$ for every $θ\in\mathbb R$. We also determine the corresponding asymptotic behavior of $\mathbb E[T_{n,m}]$. To prove these results, we present a methodology, inspired by Poissonization, that can be applied to determine the asymptotic behaviors of standardized hitting times of discrete-time stochastic processes.

Probability.title: Spectra of contractions of the Gaussian Orthogonal Tensor Ensemble
Probability.summary:
In this article, we study the spectra of matrix-valued contractions of the Gaussian Orthogonal Tensor Ensemble (GOTE). Let $\mathcal{G}$ denote a random tensor of order $r$ and dimension $n$ drawn from the density \[
  f(\mathcal{G}) \propto \exp\bigg(-\frac{1}{2r}\|\mathcal{G}\|^2_{\mathrm{F}}\bigg). \] For $\mathbf{w} \in \mathbb{S}^{n - 1}$, the unit-sphere in $\mathbb{R}^n$, we consider the matrix-valued contraction $\mathcal{G} \cdot \mathbf{w}^{\otimes (r - 2)}$ when both $r$ and $n$ go to infinity such that $r / n \to c \in [0, \infty]$. We obtain semicircle bulk-limits in all regimes, generalising the works of Goulart et al. (2022); Au and Garza-Vargas (2023); Bonnin (2024) in the fixed-$r$ setting.
  We further study the edge-spectrum. We obtain a Baik-Ben Arous-Péché phase-transition for the largest and the smallest eigenvalues at $r \ge 4$, generalising a result of Mukherjee et al. (2024) in the context of adjacency matrices of random hypergraphs. For $r = 3$, the fluctuations of the extreme eigenvalues are given by the eigenvalues of a stochastic Airy operator, whereas for $r \ge 4$, the fluctuations are Gaussian.
  Finally, we report some results, in the case $r = 4$, on mixed contractions $\mathcal{G} \cdot \mathbf{u} \otimes \mathbf{v}$, $\mathbf{u}, \mathbf{v} \in \mathbb{S}^{n - 1}$. While the total variation distance between the joint distributions of the entries of $\mathcal{G} \cdot \mathbf{u} \otimes \mathbf{v}$ and $\mathcal{G} \cdot \mathbf{u} \otimes \mathbf{u}$ goes to $0$ when $\|\mathbf{u} - \mathbf{v}\| = o(n^{-1})$, the bulk and the largest eigenvalues of these two matrices share the same limit profile as long as $\|\mathbf{u} - \mathbf{v}\| = o(1)$. Furthermore, it turns out that there are no outlier eigenvalues in the spectrum of $\mathcal{G} \cdot \mathbf{u} \otimes \mathbf{v}$ when $\langle \mathbf{u}, \mathbf{v} \rangle = o(1)$.
Probability.comment: 64 pages, 2 figures; abstract shortened to meet arXiv requirements

Probability.title: Kernelised covariance matrices, dimension reduction and imbalanced spectral clustering
Probability.summary:
The Gaussian Mixture Model (abbrv. GMM) is a classic generative model for clustered data, for which spectral clustering based on dimension reduction via PCA has been an effective framework. In this work, we investigate kernelised covariance matrices as an alternative mechanism for dimension reduction and spectral clustering, focusing on truncation kernels that select pairs of data points with suitable separation constraints. The structure of these matrices is motivated by considerations from statistical mechanics of repulsive particle systems. Our approach is particularly relevant for the setting of imbalanced clusters, where the sizes of the largest and smallest clusters have a diverging ratio with the problem size, and existing PCA-based methods turn out to be of limited effectiveness.
  We demonstrate efficient dimension reduction and clustering performance of these modified covariance matrices, substantiated by quantitative bounds. In particular, they achieve superior dimension reduction guarantees compared to PCA for a wide range of parameters in the regime of imbalanced clusters. For spectral clustering, our approach exhibits improvements over PCA in the imbalanced setting, in particular guaranteeing accurate clustering in a much larger regime of intra-cluster separations. Our theoretical guarantees reflected in a range of simulation experiments that exhibit these improvements for unbalanced clustering problems. Our analytical approach, based on kernel Laplacians, provide a toolbox as well as a relevant conceptual ingredient for clustering problems at large. We believe that our work will motivate the application of such kernelised covariance matrices for related classes of statistical problems, as well as spur new investigations in the theory of random matrices.

Probability.title: A Gaussian Process State Space Formulation for Materials Constitutive Modeling: Application to Quasi-brittle Materials
Probability.summary: Constitutive models for history-dependent, path-dependent materials typically encode this dependence in prescribed functional forms through internal variables such as damage or plastic strain that are phenomenological, model-dependent, and not directly observable. These rigid forms lack flexibility to match observations, make calibration potentially non-unique, and complicate uncertainty quantification. This paper develops a Gaussian-process state-space model (GP-SSM) that replaces the fixed form of the constitutive model with a flexible GP regression, and the prescribed internal variables with latent state variables learned directly from observable stress-strain histories. As a GP, the model is naturally endowed with a measure of uncertainty and can be constrained to satisfy physical principles. We demonstrate this framework for quasi-brittle materials under triaxial compression, where the latent variable evolution is driven by the current-state stress invariants and the increment of equivalent strain to reflect irreversible, pressure-sensitive history. A sparse multi-output GP then maps the latent state and current strain tensor to the six-component stress response, trained by variational sparse inference. The trained model is exported into Abaqus/Explicit through a user material subroutine. Four verification cases are reported: (1) offline rollout on validation and test histories; (2) a single element under changing confinement; (3) a frozen-memory unloading-reloading extension; and (4) a multi-element structural model compared against the Karagozian and Case Concrete (KCC) model. These results show that the learned state-space update reproduces held-out RVE-scale histories in closed-loop rollout, tracks evolving confinement, supports unloading without violating the irreversibility of the learned history state, and reproduces structural-level behavior consistent with KCC.

Differential Geometry.title: Sobolev inequalities for sections and projections of log-concave functions
Differential Geometry.summary: Higher order sharp Sobolev and local Sobolev type inequalities for log-concave functions are established. The new inequalities directly imply the isoperimetric inequalities by Bollobás and Thomason in 1995, by Liakopoulos in 2019, and the recently discovered local isoperimetric inequalities from [1]. In order to do so, we make use of three ingredients. First, sets of functional inequalities proven by Alonso-Gutiérrez, Bernués, Brazitikos and Carbery in 2021. Second, a multidimensional polynomial optimization result that originated in [1] and was initiated by Bollobás and Thomason. Third, a new integral formula for the projection of a log-concave function that links the geometric part with the more functional versions via some dependence on the Hessian matrix restricted to subspaces.

Differential Geometry.title: Instability of mean curvature flow in expander coordinates
Differential Geometry.summary: We study rotationally symmetric graphical solutions to mean curvature flow that are initially close to a homothetic reference expander, in particular near infinity. Based on a computer algebra aided proof, we show that under appropriate conditions, at large times, the solutions are closer to a different expander than to the reference expander.

Differential Geometry.title: A complete Kähler metric on $\mathbb{C}^n$ of nonnegative Ricci curvature with Euclidean volume growth and nonunique asymptotic cone
Differential Geometry.summary: We construct complete smooth Kähler metrics on $\mathbb{C}^n$ , $n\ge2$, with nonnegative Ricci curvature, Euclidean volume growth, and nonunique tangent cones at infinity. More generally, we prescribe the entire tangent cone set within a class of smooth Hopf cones, using a compact connected family of positive transverse Ricci forms on $\mathbb{C}\mathbb{P}^{n-1}$. We identify all metric blow-downs and their Ricci currents, compute the exact asymptotic volume ratio, and classify isometries between the model cones. In particular, the Kähler condition does not ensure uniqueness at infinity under nonnegative Ricci curvature and Euclidean volume growth, even in complex dimension two.

Differential Geometry.title: Finitely many solutions for the prescribed scalar curvature problem at the critical flatness order
Differential Geometry.summary:
We study the following prescribed scalar curvature problem $$
  -Δu=K(y)u^{2^*-1},\ \ u>0
  \,\ \ \text{in}\ \ \mathbb{R}^N, \tag*{$(*)$} $$ where $2^*=\frac{2N}{N-2}$. For $N\geq4$, we construct a positive $K(y)$ with maximum set $\{|y|=1\}$ and critical order of flatness $m=N-2$ at $|y|=1$, such that problem $(*)$ admits only finitely many positive solutions in $D^{1,2}(\mathbb{R}^N)$. To this end, we prove compactness of the solution set of $(*)$ by blow-up analysis and then apply Sard's theorem to choose $K$ for which each solution is nondegenerate and hence isolated, so that the solution set of $(*)$ is finite. Our results give a negative answer to Wei--Yan's conjecture in [J. Wei and S. Yan, JFA, 2010].

Differential Geometry.title: Symmetry Breaking and Moduli for Ancient Yamabe Flows on the Sphere
Differential Geometry.summary: For every $n\ge3$, we construct compact Type II ancient Yamabe flows in the round conformal class of the unit $n$-sphere $\Ss^n$. After stereographic projection and rescaling of time and conformal factor, the solutions are asymptotic backward in time to finite superpositions of Aubin--Talenti bubbles with mutually comparable scales. For integers $h\ge1$ and $k\ge2$, the limiting centers form $h$ coaxial regular $k$-gons; when $h\ge2$, their distinct layer heights may be prescribed arbitrarily in the interval $(-1,1)$. If $hk\ge3$, the resulting flows are not geometrically equivalent to any rotationally symmetric ancient flow. For each flow, there is a fixed point of $\Ss^n$ at which the Ricci tensor has both positive and negative eigenvalues on every time slice. The corresponding volume-normalized Yamabe flows are also ancient. After rescaling each time slice to a fixed volume, the metrics converge to a wedge of $hk$ isometric round $n$-spheres in the Gromov--Hausdorff topology, as time tends to $-\infty$. For fixed $h,k\ge2$, the concentration configurations admit an explicit $(h-1)$-parameter description up to Möbius transformations. Consequently, the construction yields geometrically inequivalent flows indexed by a nonempty open subset of $\R^{h-1}$, all with the same fixed-volume backward Gromov--Hausdorff limit. The proof uses inner--outer gluing for the quasilinear parabolic equation in $n$-dimensional space that exhibits Kelvin symmetry. Weighted Euclidean and spherical Hölder estimates control the nonlinear terms and, together with parabolic regularity, yield smooth extension of the conformal metrics across the north pole of $\Ss^n$.
Differential Geometry.comment: v2: Title and exposition revised; proofs clarified, with a more detailed treatment of the backward geometric limits and the classification of concentration configurations up to Möbius transformations

Differential Geometry.title: Symmetries and Higher-Form Connections in Derived Differential Geometry
Differential Geometry.summary: We introduce a general definition of higher-form connections on principal $\infty$-bundles in differential geometry. These connections are built as infinitesimal parallel transports and thus satisfy the fake-curvature condition. We achieve this by developing the formal differentiation and integration of maps from smooth manifolds to derived stacks with sufficient deformation theory. That allows us to introduce the Atiyah $L_\infty$-algebroid of a principal $\infty$-bundle and establish its global sections as the $L_\infty$-algebra of the derived higher symmetry group of the bundle. We define the space of $p$-form connections on an $\infty$-bundle as the space of order $p$ splittings of its Atiyah $L_\infty$-algebroid. This can be cast equivalently as lifting the classifying map of a bundle on a manifold to the order $p$ truncation of the de Rham stack of the manifold. We demonstrate that our new concept of derived geometric $p$-form connections recovers the known notion of connections on higher U(1)-bundles defined via Čech-Deligne differential cocycles. We further relate the $L_\infty$-algebras of derived higher symmetries of higher U(1)-bundles and higher Courant algebroids. Some applications in higher gauge theory and in supergravity are mentioned.
Differential Geometry.comment: 123 pages; v2: clarifying comments and references added, typos corrected, new Section 4.4; v3: clarifying comments and references added, relation with adjusted connections added

Differential Geometry.title: Local rigidity for the sharp Nash inequality
Differential Geometry.summary: Let $V$ be a nonempty relatively compact open subset of a smooth Riemannian manifold $(M^n,g)$ without boundary. We prove that $C_{\mathrm N}(V,g)\ge C_{\mathrm N}(\mathbb R^n)$ and $\int_V \mathrm{Sc}_g dμ_g\ge0$ imply $\mathrm{Rm}_g=0$ on $V$, where $C_{\mathrm N}$ denotes the optimal constant in the Nash inequality and $\mathrm{Sc}_g$ denotes the scalar curvature. This improves an earlier rigidity result of Druet, Hebey, and Vaugon [Int. Math. Res. Not. (1999), no. 14, 735--779].

Differential Geometry.title: The Eguchi Construction Arises from Bi-Lagrangian Structures
Differential Geometry.summary:
We propose a new geometric interpretation of Eguchi's construction, which associates to a statistical divergence, an essential ingredient of Information Geometry, a statistical structure on a differentiable manifold. Our approach is based on bi-Lagrangian geometry. Building on the work of O.~E.~Barndorff-Nielsen and P.~E.~Jupp~\cite{Barndorff}, we show that a statistical divergence naturally induces a bi-Lagrangian structure, hence a para-Kähler structure. Within this framework, the Riemannian metric $g^D$ and the pair of dual connections $(
abla^D,{}^*
abla^D)$ of Eguchi's construction are induced by the para-Kähler structure: $g^D$ is the restriction to the diagonal of the para-Kähler metric $G$ of signature $(d,d)$, while $
abla^D$ and ${}^*
abla^D$ are obtained, through the two natural projections, from the Bott connections of the two transverse Lagrangian foliations, which are themselves the restrictions of the Levi-Civita connection of $G$ (the Hess, Künneth or bi-Lagrangian connection).
  This perspective shows that the statistical structure associated with a divergence is not merely the formal outcome of successive differentiations, but the manifestation of an underlying bi-Lagrangian geometry. Our approach thus provides an intrinsic and unified understanding of Eguchi's construction, highlights the connections between information geometry, symplectic geometry and para-Kähler geometry, and opens new research perspectives at the interface of these fields.

Differential Geometry.title: Marked length spectrum and area of surfaces with Anosov geodesic flow
Differential Geometry.summary: More than twenty years ago, Croke and Dairbekov showed that a negatively curved metric $g_0$ on a closed surface has minimal area among all negatively curved Riemannian metrics $g$ on the same surface whose marked length spectrum is greater or equal to that of $g_0$. We show that the curvature assumption on the second metric can be removed and extend this result to reversible Finsler metrics. More precisely, we prove that a reversible Finsler metric $F_0$ on a closed surface whose geodesic flow is Anosov has minimal area among all reversible Finsler metrics $F$ on the same surface whose marked length spectrum is greater or equal to that of $F_0$.

Differential Geometry.title: Characterizations of the plane and the catenoid as capillary minimal surfaces
Differential Geometry.summary: In this paper, we prove that an annular capillary minimal surface outside the unit ball in $\mathbb{R}^3$ with one complete embedded end and finite total curvature must be either part of the plane or part of the catenoid. The proofs are based on the use of the Weierstrass data through the Hopf differential and associated holomorphic functions. For a planar end, we control the second fundamental form, while for a catenoidal end, we analyze the Gauss map in more detail using the boundary condition. We also prove nonexistence results for annular free boundary minimal surfaces with one end asymptotic to the end of Enneper's surface, under appropriate conditions. Finally, we establish an exterior analogue of Choe's result on capillary minimal surfaces with vertices.
Differential Geometry.comment: 17 pages, 1 figure. In response to referee comments, an issue with a reference used in Theorem 1.1 has been corrected, and the proof has been revised accordingly. The statement of Theorem 1.2 has been revised to exclude certain boundary umbilic cases

Differential Geometry.title: Soft elasticity of soft shells
Differential Geometry.summary: Soft modes of a shell are one-parameter families of non-trivial deformations that preserve the elastic energy. We identify all soft modes of the soft shells described by the variational theory of put forward by Sonnet and Virga (2025). They are seen to be strictly connected with the Bonnet families, a special class of solutions to the problem posited by Bonnet, who asked whether there exist non-trivial isometries that preserve the mean curvature. Differential geometry deems as equivalent all surfaces in one and the same Bonnet family, but continuum mechanics is interested more specifically in soft deformation modes and the shapes they traverse, as they may describe ways to ignite fluctuations of soft shells that ideally require no energy to be activated. We give a general criterion for the existence of soft modes and a method to construct them based on a cascade of path integrations. We apply both criterion and method to some exemplary cases.

Differential Geometry.title: Fuglede's theorem in the Heisenberg group
Differential Geometry.summary: We prove a Fuglede-type quantitative isoperimetric inequality for the Pansu sphere, the conjectured isoperimetric set in the sub-Riemannian Heisenberg group $\mathbb{H}^1$. We show that, among suitable volume-preserving normal perturbations of the Pansu sphere that are small in a weighted $C^2$-norm, the difference between the sub-Riemannian perimeters of the perturbed and unperturbed regions is bounded below by a positive constant times the square of their $L^1$-distance. The proof is based on a Riemannian approximation argument with uniform estimates.

Differential Geometry.title: The elastic figure-eight knot is not planar
Differential Geometry.summary: We prove that every elastic knot in any non-torus twist knot class is not planar. In particular, this disproves a numerically motivated planarity conjecture for elastic figure-eight knots.

Differential Geometry.title: Gagliardo--Nirenberg extremals on manifolds with small holes
Differential Geometry.summary: We study the sharp homogeneous Dirichlet Gagliardo--Nirenberg quotient on a closed Riemannian manifold with holes of small capacity and connected complements. For each fixed exponent $2<q<2^*$, the nonnegative $L^2$-normalized extremal exists and is unique when the first Dirichlet eigenvalue $λ_D$ is sufficiently small. If the ambient volume is $V$ and $β=n(q-2)/2$, the sharp constant satisfies $C_D=V^{1-q/2}λ_D^{-β/2}(1+O(λ_D))$. For the normalized first eigenfunction $\varphi_D$, we obtain $\|u_D-\varphi_D\|_{H^1}=O(λ_D^{3/2})$ and $C_D/W_{M_D}(\varphi_D)=1+O(λ_D^2)$, together with a quantitative stability estimate in terms of the relative deficit. The constants depend only on the ambient manifold and the exponent. On general compact manifolds with Dirichlet boundary conditions, we prove compactness above the Euclidean sharp constant and describe concentration at equality. Positive scalar curvature at one interior point implies attainment. For the $L^2$-critical nonlinear Schrödinger energy, the mass threshold for negative energy tends to zero as the capacity of the holes tends to zero, whereas the threshold for unboundedness below is unchanged.
Differential Geometry.comment: 17 pages, split off from arXiv:2601.22665v1. Comments highly appreciated!

Differential Geometry.title: Convex Analysis of Relaxation Dynamics in Chemical Reaction Networks and Generalized Gradient Flows
Differential Geometry.summary: We obtain bounds on the Kullback--Leibler divergence to equilibrium for mass-action chemical reaction networks (CRNs) with equilibrium. The associated trajectory-dependent bounds are characterized in terms of the singular values of the stoichiometric matrix, convexity parameters, and time-integrated activities via deformed-exponential-type functions. We further extend these bounds within a generalized gradient flow framework. We highlight the biological relevance of this framework: the resulting bounds apply to quasi-steady-state regimes, where long transients and plateau-like behavior are common and functionally important. We illustrate the framework using a catalytic CRN exhibiting plateaus, where the bounds provide an a posteriori characterization of slow relaxation induced by local convexity and provide a bound-based approach to quantifying relaxation in CRNs.
Differential Geometry.comment: 34 pages, 5 figures (Main Text); 11 pages, 5 figures (Supplementary Material). Accepted for publication in SIAM Journal on Applied Mathematics

Differential Geometry.title: Dirac eigenvalues and the hyper-hemispherical radius
Differential Geometry.summary: On a connected compact Riemannian spin manifold with boundary, we prove an upper estimate for the smallest eigenvalue of the Dirac operator under the boundary condition associated with a chirality operator. This upper bound is expressed in terms of the hyper-hemispherical radius. Moreover, the upper bound is realized if and only if the manifold is a hemisphere. As an application, we get a scalar curvature rigidity result for the hemisphere in the case of Lipschitz maps whose differential has a prescribed trace-norm bound. Our estimate extends Bär's result for closed manifolds, where the upper bound is given in terms of hyperspherical radius.

Differential Geometry.title: Minimal Surfaces in $\mathbb{R}^4$ with Three Planar Ends II: Symmetry and Nonexistence
Differential Geometry.summary: In this paper, we study complete minimal surfaces in $\mathbb{R}^4$ with three embedded planar ends parallel to those of the union of the Lagrangian catenoid and the plane containing its waist circle. We prove that no such complete embedded minimal surface of genus $g\geq 2$ with finite total curvature admits at least $4(g+1)$ symmetries. This contrasts sharply with the genus-one case, where highly symmetric examples do exist and are uniquely determined up to scaling and rigid motion.
Differential Geometry.comment: 43 pages. This paper is Part II of a manuscript originally posted as arXiv: 2504.02282, which has since been divided into two parts

Differential Geometry.title: Group Actions on Aspherical Alexandrov Spaces
Differential Geometry.summary: Conner and Raymond proved that if a connected, compact Lie group $G$ acts effectively on a closed aspherical manifold $M$, then $G$ is a torus and the fundamental group of $G$ injects into the center of $π_1(M)$. We prove the corresponding result for effective isometric actions on closed, aspherical Alexandrov spaces.

Differential Geometry.title: Hyperbolic Monge-Ampère Equation on a Cylinder: Well-Posedness and Stability
Differential Geometry.summary: This paper develops a rigorous analytic framework for the hyperbolic Monge-Ampère equation on strip-like domains, which model wrinkled patterns in thin elastic sheets. Our work addresses the rigid side of the classical rigidity-flexibility dichotomy by defining this regime not by high smoothness, but by the more fundamental property of partial convexity. The hodograph transformation is the natural tool for this setting, as its validity is predicated on partial convexity. It converts the nonlinear Monge-Ampère equation into a linear damped wave equation, allowing us to formulate a well-posed Cauchy-Goursat problem. A key challenge is the corner singularity that arises where characteristic and non-characteristic boundary data meet. To resolve this, we develop a parametrix-corrector decomposition that captures the solution's inherent singular behavior. This method recasts the problem as a singular Volterra integral equation, for which we prove the existence and uniqueness of a new class of hodograph weak solutions. Finally, we derive energy estimates to establish the quantitative stability of these rigid solutions under perturbations of the underlying curvature function.

Differential Geometry.title: Height and distance-squared functions on implicit plane curves
Differential Geometry.summary: We introduce families of Lagrange functions associated with height and distance-squared functions on implicit plane curves. We show that degeneracies of these families characterize geometric properties of the curves, such as inflections and vertices, and give geometric interpretations of the corresponding Lagrange multipliers in terms of contact with lines and circles.

Differential Geometry.title: On polarizations of affine Calabi--Yau varieties
Differential Geometry.summary: Let $(X, Ω)$ be an affine Calabi--Yau variety, by which we mean a klt affine variety $X$ with a non-vanishing algebraic volume form $Ω$. In connection with complete Calabi--Yau metrics of Euclidean volume growth on $(X, Ω)$, we study algebraic aspects of polarizations of $X$ given by a negative valuation. We show that such a valuation is finitely generated with a klt degeneration if and only if $X$ admits a dlt log Fano type compactification, generalizing a compactification considered by Tian--Yau. We further give a valuative criterion detecting K-semistability of the degeneration by a negative valuation.

Differential Geometry.title: Free boundary minimal surfaces of genus zero
Differential Geometry.summary: We prove that any embedded genus zero free boundary minimal surface in the ball has first Steklov eigenvalue $1$. This implies the uniqueness of the critical catenoid.

Differential Geometry.title: On the existence of toric ALE and ALF gravitational instantons
Differential Geometry.summary: We establish existence and uniqueness results for asymptotically locally Euclidean (ALE) and asymptotically locally flat (ALF) gravitational instantons. In particular, we prove the existence of a unique, Ricci-flat, toric ALE and ALF gravitational instanton, for every admissible rod structure, that is smooth up to possible conical singularites. We also give an elementary proof that any toric ALE or ALF self-dual instanton is a multi-Eguchi-Hanson or multi-Taub-NUT solution.
Differential Geometry.comment: 21 pages. v2: minor edits, published version

Differential Geometry.title: Rigidity and deformations of Besse families of minimal hypersurfaces
Differential Geometry.summary: We generalize Zoll families of hypersurfaces to Besse families of hypersurfaces, which are defined differential-topologically and may contain non-embedded and exceptional hypersurfaces. A contact-geometric discussion presents them as double Legendrian fibrations and shows that regular hypersurfaces are either spheres or real projective spaces. In analogy with the Berger conjecture on simply connected manifolds all of whose geodesics are closed, we show that every hypersurface of a Besse family on a sphere other than the 4-sphere is regular. On even-dimensional spheres other than the 4-sphere we obtain a stronger conclusion, generalizing a theorem of Gromoll and Grove about 2-spheres all of whose geodesics are closed: every hypersurface of a Besse family is regular and embedded. Moreover, building on work by Ambrozio and Guajardo, we provide metrics of non-constant curvature carrying Besse families of non-embedded minimal hypersurfaces in every odd dimension at least three, and Besse families of minimal hypersurfaces with exceptional hypersurfaces on orbifolds in every dimension at least two. We also give a short proof that manifolds admitting Zoll families of embedded hypersurfaces are homeomorphic to spheres or real projective spaces, recovering a recent result of Martins up to homeomorphism.

Differential Geometry.title: Existence of rotationally symmetric embedded f-minimal tori
Differential Geometry.summary: Let $n\geq2$, and let $f:[0,+\infty)\to\mathbb{R}$ be a smooth function satisfying $f''\geq0$ and $0<m\leq f'\leq M$ for some constants $m$ and $M$. We prove that $\mathbb{R}^{n+1}$, endowed with the conformal metric \begin{equation*} ds^2=e^{-\frac{f(|x|^2)}{2n}}\sum_{i=1}^{n+1}dx_i^2, \end{equation*} admits a compact, embedded, rotationally symmetric minimal hypersurface diffeomorphic to $S^1\times S^{n-1}$. This extends Angenent's existence theorem for self-shrinking tori, which is recovered when $f(s)=s$.

Differential Geometry.title: Rigidity and Affine Deformations of Foliations on Nilpotent and Solvable Contact Lie Algebras
Differential Geometry.summary: Let g be a Lie algebra of dimension 2n+1, let beta be a contact form, and let alpha be a nonzero integrable 1-form. We study when the affine path alpha_t = (1-t)alpha + t beta consists of contact forms with the orientation determined by beta \wedge (d beta)^n. We first establish an algebraic criterion: affine deformability is equivalent to the non-negativity of a scalar obtained from the interaction form Theta(alpha, beta) = alpha \wedge (d beta)^n + n beta \wedge d alpha \wedge (d beta)^{n-1}. For unimodular Lie algebras this scalar is (n+1)alpha(Z_beta), where Z_beta is the Reeb vector. We also derive a formula involving the modular character tau(X) = tr(ad_X) in the non-unimodular case. On nilpotent contact Lie algebras, every integrable 1-form is closed; using the standard structural properties of nilpotent contact Lie algebras, this implies that every left-invariant foliation is an affine origin for every fixed contact form. An explicit three-dimensional example illustrates that the modular term can yield affine deformability even when alpha(Z_beta) = 0. We discuss the implications for left-invariant forms on Lie groups and compact quotients. We do not claim a general obstruction example in the non-unimodular case; establishing such an example requires a separate verified construction.

Geometric Topology.title: Veering triangulations of once-punctured torus bundles are unique
Geometric Topology.summary: We show that each hyperbolic once-punctured torus bundle has exactly one veering triangulation. We also find manifolds for which the exact number of veering structures is known and is greater than one. Finally, we give new examples of manifolds without veering triangulations.

Geometric Topology.title: Spherical and affine Artin groups, finite quotients, and the isomorphism problem
Geometric Topology.summary: We compute the smallest non-abelian quotients of spherical and affine Artin groups. Usually, these are isomorphic to the smallest non-abelian quotients of the corresponding Coxeter groups. As applications, we deduce that two affine Artin groups are isomorphic if and only if their Coxeter diagrams are isomorphic and that irreducible spherical Artin groups are distinguished from each other by their finite quotient groups.
Geometric Topology.comment: v3. 44 pages, title changed and new result added; v2. 42 pages, minor changes; v1. 42 pages, preliminary version

Geometric Topology.title: A Topological Figiel-Lindenstrauss-Milman Theorem and its Applications
Geometric Topology.summary:
We prove a topological generalization of the Figiel--Lindenstrauss--Milman inequality, answering a recent question of Frick, Hosseini, and Vasileuski: every nonempty strongly regular CW complex with $v$ vertices, $f$ maximal cells, and a free involution that permutes its cells has $\mathbb Z/2$-index at most $4\log v\log f$. The classical inequality for centrally symmetric polytopes is the special case of polytope boundaries.
  As an application, we show that every finite simplicial complex homotopy equivalent to $\mathbb RP^d$ has at least $\exp(Ω(\sqrt d))$ vertices. The previous best lower bound was $Ω(d^2)$. We also construct triangulations with $\exp(O(\sqrt d))$ vertices. Using the same method, we prove a low-dimensional Postnikov factorization theorem, which gives similar vertex lower bounds for several classical families, such as complex and quaternionic projective spaces, the $d$-torus, closed symplectic and aspherical manifolds, Grassmannians, classical Lie groups, and spherical space forms. Further applications include results in learning theory, convex geometry, computational topology, and topological bounds for chromatic numbers and Vietoris--Rips complexes.

Geometric Topology.title: Counting curves with bounded intersection
Geometric Topology.summary: This paper counts curves, and multicurves, on hyperbolic surfaces, providing explicit upper bounds that depend polynomially on length and exponentially in terms of an upper bound on self-intersection.

Geometric Topology.title: Simple homotopy types of smooth four-manifolds with finite fundamental group
Geometric Topology.summary: We construct closed smooth $4$-manifolds with finite fundamental group which are homotopy equivalent but not simple homotopy equivalent, even after taking a connected sum with copies of $S^2\times S^2$. Our explicit examples have remarkably large fundamental groups; in particular, the smallest examples we obtain have fundamental groups of order roughly $10^{10^{42}}$.

Geometric Topology.title: Exact bounded cohomology of measure-preserving homeomorphism groups of nonorientable hyperbolic manifolds
Geometric Topology.summary: Let $M$ be a closed, connected, non-orientable hyperbolic manifold, and let $μ$ be a good measure on $M$. Denote by $Homeo_0(M,μ)$ the identity component of the group of $μ$-preserving homeomorphisms. For every $d\geq2$, we prove that $\dim\overline{EH}_b^d\bigl(Homeo_0(M,μ)\bigr)=\infty$, where $\overline{EH}_b^d$ denotes reduced exact bounded cohomology in degree $d$.

Geometric Topology.title: Angle cocycles, Euler characteristic, and simplicial volume of smooth manifolds
Geometric Topology.summary: A celebrated conjecture of Gromov states that for closed aspherical manifolds, the vanishing of simplicial volume implies the vanishing of the Euler characteristic. We prove Gromov's conjecture for closed convex projective manifolds and, more generally, for closed orientable smooth manifolds admitting an immersed straightening. Generalising the straightening of simplices in properly convex domains in real projective space, we introduce the notion of immersed straightening and prove that, for every integer $d\geq 1$, there exists a constant $C_d>0$ such that every closed orientable smooth $d$-manifold $M$ admitting an immersed straightening satisfies $|χ(M)|\le C_d||M||$.

Geometric Topology.title: The elastic figure-eight knot is not planar
Geometric Topology.summary: We prove that every elastic knot in any non-torus twist knot class is not planar. In particular, this disproves a numerically motivated planarity conjecture for elastic figure-eight knots.

Geometric Topology.title: Conway polynomials of $Th(p,q)$ and $Th(q,p)$: a proof of Takemura's conjecture
Geometric Topology.summary:
Takemura conjectured that the Conway polynomials $\sum a_\ell z^\ell$ of the Turk's head link $Th(p,q)$ and $\sum b_\ell z^\ell$ of $Th(q,p)$ satisfy $a_\ell=b_\ell$ for $\ell\equiv0,1\pmod 4$ and $a_\ell=-b_\ell$ for $\ell\equiv2,3\pmod4$, and proved it for $q=2,3$. We prove it for all $p,q\ge1$, knots and links. Equivalently, $
abla_{Th(q,p)}(z)=c\,
abla_{Th(p,q)}(iz)$ with $c=1$ if $\gcd(p,q)$ is odd and $c=-i$ if it is even. The proof combines a product formula $
abla_{Th(p,q)}(z)^2=\prod_{j=1}^{p-1}\prod_{k=1}^{q-1}(z^2+2\cos rac{2πk}{q}-2\cos rac{2πj}{p})$, which comes from the reduced Burau representation, with the leading coefficients, read off the Seifert surface of the closed braid.
Geometric Topology.comment: 7 pages. Scripts and outputs of the checks: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23183920

Geometric Topology.title: The symmetry group of Turk's head knots
Geometric Topology.summary: For p, q >= 3 with gcd(p,q) = 1 we show that the symmetry group of the Turk's head knot Th(p,q), the closure of the braid (sigma_1 sigma_2^{-1} sigma_3 sigma_4^{-1} ... sigma_{p-1}^{+-1})^q, is the dihedral group of order 4q. This proves Conjecture R of Di Prisa and Şavk for q >= 3; the case p = 3 is due to Sakuma and Weeks. The argument is diagrammatic: by the flyping theorem of Menasco and Thistlethwaite, the symmetries of a knot with a prime, reduced alternating diagram without non-trivial flypes are the symmetries of the diagram (we write out a proof for the diagrams at hand), and we show that the standard diagram of Th(p,q) has no non-trivial flypes and exactly 4q symmetries. The chirality of Th(p,q) for even p, which also follows from a theorem of Murasugi, is visible in the group. We compare the argument with the geometric one of Sakuma and Weeks for p = 3.
Geometric Topology.comment: 17 pages; v2: corrections in the tool-use section and in Section 8, clarifications in Section 5 (proof of Lemma 5.9 and the comparison with the crossing-ball model); author name given in full

Geometric Topology.title: Singular Loci of SL2(C)-Representation Varieties of Torus Knot Groups
Geometric Topology.summary: Let $T(q,p)=\langle x,y\mid x^p=y^q\rangle$, where $p,q>1$ are relatively prime, and let \[ R=\Hom(T(q,p),\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb C)). \] We compute the integral homology of the singular locus of $R$. We show that this locus has complex dimension $2$ and is a disjoint union of $μ=(p-1)(q-1)$ smooth affine surfaces, each homotopy equivalent to the two-dimensional sphere. Consequently, \[ H_0(\Sing R;\Z)\cong H_2(\Sing R;\Z)\cong\Z^μ, \] and all remaining homology groups vanish. Thus both nonzero Betti numbers equal the first Betti number of the Milnor fiber of the plane curve singularity $z^p+w^q=0$, namely its Milnor number $μ$.

Geometric Topology.title: Cluster structures from Legendrian double twist knots: a comparative approach
Geometric Topology.summary: We undertake a systematic comparison of cluster algebras associated to Legendrian knots of the same smooth knot type. We describe a cluster structure on the m-graded augmentation variety of Legendrian representatives of a family of double twist knots that includes all orientably Lagrangian fillable twist knots. For different Legendrian representatives of the same smooth knot type, we show that these cluster structures are equivalent. Along the way, we characterize the representatives that admit Maslov-m exact Lagrangian fillings, construct a Catalan number of such fillings for each representative, and show that any Maslov-0 fillable representative is Legendrian isotopic to the (-1)-framed closure of a positive braid. Finally, we give two Legendrian representatives of a cabled twist knot that yield equivalent cluster structures of infinite type.
Geometric Topology.comment: Revised version includes added remark discussing an example of L. Ng

Geometric Topology.title: The Number of Polytope Trees and Beyond
Geometric Topology.summary: We study the symmetry-weighted enumeration of complexes formed by gluing copies of a regular polytope. For polytope trees and complexes obtained by attaching such trees to a fixed initial complex, we derive cut-and-join recurrences, differential equations for generating functions, explicit counting formulas, and asymptotic estimates. We then extend the method to complexes with cycles in their dual graphs, enumerating them by the numbers of polytopes and free facets. We derive recurrence relations and partial differential equations for the corresponding bivariate generating functions. In this setting, we obtain recurrences for connected configurations and explicit coefficient formulas for possibly disconnected configurations, both with and without a distinguished initial complex.

Geometric Topology.title: On the Upsilon invariant and the Baldwin-Vela-Vick b-invariant of fibered knots
Geometric Topology.summary: For a null-homologous fibered knot $K$ in a rational homology sphere, Baldwin and Vela-Vick define a refinement $b(K)$ of the Ozsváth-Szabó contact invariant. We prove that if the Ozsváth-Stipsicz-Szabó concordance invariant Upsilon has slope $Υ'_K(t)=-g(K)$ for some $t\in[0,\frac{2}{n+1})$, where $g(K)$ is the genus of $K$, then $b(K)>n$. This extends a result of He, Hubbard, and the author on the Upsilon invariant and right-veering monodromies. We also prove that the knot Floer homology of a fibered knot in the $g(K)-b(K)$ Alexander grading is nonvanishing. As an application, we give many families of fibered cable knots whose $b(K)$ invariant grows arbitrarily large. Finally, we prove that if a monodromy of a fibered knot is neither right-veering nor left-veering, then the third-to-top term of knot Floer homology is nonvanishing.

Geometric Topology.title: Lie structures in homotopy and isotopy calculi
Geometric Topology.summary: We establish compatibility of Lie structures that appear in homotopy calculus of functors and isotopy calculus of embeddings. On one hand, we give a new proof of the Johnson--Arone--Mahowald result describing the layers of the Goodwillie tower of the identity functor, and we directly compare the spectral Lie bracket with the classical Whitehead bracket on spaces. On the other hand, we geometrically define a bracket on the layers of the embedding calculus tower for embeddings of arcs. These results are unified through the same technical tool, a newly defined bracket on total homotopy fibres of collapsing cubes of wedge sums.
Geometric Topology.comment: v1: 21 pages, 1 figure v2: Accepted version, substantially revised after the referees' reports, for which I am deeply grateful. 25 pages, 1 figure

Optimization and Control.title: Efficient Ground-State Manifold Amplification for Rydberg Atom Arrays via Houdayer Cluster Updates
Optimization and Control.summary: We demonstrate a hybrid quantum-classical approach for exploring ground-state manifolds of maximum independent set problems, in which quantum hardware supplies the initial solutions and an entirely classical post-processing algorithm expands them, increasing the solution diversity of quantum hardware measurements by up to several orders of magnitude. Quantum optimization devices, while capable of generating high-quality solutions, can suffer from fundamental sampling limitations. This is particularly problematic for applications that strongly depend on a large variety of uncorrelated optimal solutions. We apply the Houdayer cluster update algorithm to systematically expand quantum-generated solution sets through classical post-processing.
