In the plane, for kernels $k(t-s)$ with $k(0)\neq0$ and under strong local nondeterminism, we restrict the double self-intersection local time to $\{t_2-t_1\geqslant\|a\|^{-α}\}$, $α>0$, and establish a phase transition: its expectation decays like $\exp(-c\|a\|^{2-α})$, converges to an explicit positive limit, or grows logarithmically, for $α<2$, $α=2$ and $α>2$ respectively.

Probability.title: The estimates for Boolean surface area of polynomial threshold functions
Probability.summary:
Polynomial threshold functions (PTFs) are an important low-complexity class of Boolean functions, with strong connections to learning theory and approximation theory. Recent work on learning and testing PTFs has exploited structural and isoperimetric properties of the class, especially bounds on average sensitivity, one of the central themes in the study of PTFs since the Gotsman--Linial conjecture recently solved by OpenAI, \cite{GLsol}.
  In this work we study PTFs through the lens of the Boolean surface area (or Talagrand boundary) \[ \mathbf{BSA}[f]=\mathbb{E}|\nabla f|=\mathbb{E}\sqrt{s_{f}(x)}, \] a natural measure of vertex-boundary complexity on the discrete cube. Our main result is that every degree-$d$ PTF has polylogarithmic Boolean surface area: \[ \mathbf{BSA}[f]\le C_d(\log(en))^{C_d}. \] The proof is based on the PTF Restriction Lemma of Kabanets, Kane, and Lu \cite{KKL2017} and proceeds through a tail bound for the pointwise sensitivity. In particular, it controls all subcritical fractional moments of the sensitivity. We also record a random block partition principle for Boolean surface area and an alternative recursive argument following Kane's work \cite{DK} on average sensitivity, which independently yields the second bound \[ \mathbf{BSA}[f]\le \exp(C(d)\sqrt{\log n}). \] This bound was obtained in \cite{FSVZ} without clarifying the magnitude of $C(d)$, which we do below. For lower moments $\bE |\nabla f|^η \le C(d, η)$ there is no dependence on $n$ for $0<η<1$.

Probability.title: Endpoint gradient bounds for centered convex maximal operators and probability kernels
Probability.summary: We establish the endpoint gradient estimate for centered homothetic maximal averages in every dimension $d\ge2$ over each fixed convex body with $C^{1,θ}$ boundary, $0<θ\le1$. In particular, the centered ball maximal operator satisfies the $W^{1,1}$ gradient bound in every dimension. Neither strict convexity nor a lower bound on the support gap is required. The geometric argument combines concentration in gradient values with nonhomogeneous calibrated rows and a summable radial correction. It extends the scalar refinement, direction-history construction and global assembly of the planar centered-disk proof of OpenAI. A separate transfer theorem gives sharp singular-derivative identities for bounded compact probability kernels once local BV output is known, and gradient continuity under an additional spatial-tail condition. Quantitative contact and translation estimates yield further profile and kernel examples. The estimates retain the fixed body's regularity data; the endpoint for arbitrary $C^1$ and nonsmooth convex bodies remains open here.

Probability.title: Entropic hypocoercivity via the Polchinski flow: an application to the lattice sine-Gordon model
Probability.summary: We develop a multiscale criterion for exponential decay of relative entropy in the canonical stochastic quantization of lattice field theories, the underdamped Langevin dynamics of the field and its momentum. For smooth bounded perturbations of Gaussian fields, the criterion requires the uniform operator-norm bound on the smoothed interaction Hessian along the Polchinski flow of Bauerschmidt and Bodineau to have a small $L^2$ norm in the scale variable. The decay constants depend only on this $L^2$ norm and the friction. The proof measures the transfer of momentum dissipation to position on the same scales that decompose entropy. A phase-space extension of the Polchinski flow gives Gaussian coarse-graining that commutes with free kinetic evolution. Integrating position--momentum cross terms over these scales yields a corrector bounded by entropy. A force defect accounts for changes in the averaged interaction force away from equilibrium; its evolution in scale controls the errors in the kinetic estimate. For the massive two-dimensional lattice sine--Gordon model with $0<β<4π$ and small dimensionless local coupling, the criterion gives entropy decay for all finite-entropy initial laws, uniformly in the lattice spacing and the volume. For friction proportional to the mass $m$, the rate has optimal order $m$.

Probability.title: Large Excursions of Reflected Lévy Processes: Local Asymptotics
Probability.comment: 61 pages, 2 figures. We did not use AI to generate any mathematical proofs or to originate any research ideas. All comments are welcomed!!

Probability.title: Characters of symmetric groups: sharp bounds on virtual degrees and the Witten zeta function
Probability.summary: We prove sharp bounds on the virtual degrees introduced by Larsen and Shalev. This leads to improved bounds on characters of symmetric groups. We then sharpen bounds of Liebeck and Shalev concerning the Witten zeta function. Our main application is a characterization of the fixed-point free conjugacy classes whose associated random walk mixes in 2 steps.
Probability.comment: v4: 50 pages, 13 figures. Asymptotic equivalents of the Witten zeta function were added. v3: 50 pages, 12 figures. More general bounds and an application to random maps were added. v2: 44 pages, 12 figures. We added character bounds in terms of the number of cycles and two applications. v1: 37 pages, 11 figures. Comments welcome!

Probability.title: An Abstract Framework for Nonlinear Stochastic Parabolic Systems with Application to a Chemotaxis-Fluid Model
Probability.summary: The purpose of the paper is twofold. Firstly, we want to present an abstract existence Theorem to show the existence of a martingale solution for coupled systems of non-linear stochastic partial differential equations. The idea is first to split the system by rewriting the nonlinear part in a linear part acting on a given process. This is done in such a way that the fixed point with respect to the given process would be the solution of the original Stochastic Partial Differential Equation (SPDE). However, it may be necessary to show the well-posedness of the linearized system using a cut-off argument, which may impose additional constraints. We work out under which conditions on the underlying spaces and the cut-off argument one gets a martingale solution of the original SPDE. A similar strategy was applied by Hausenblas and Tolle in [E. Hausenblas and J. Tolle. The stochastic Klausmeier system and a schauder tychonoff type theorem. Potential Analusis, 310:506-554, 2022] to investigate the stochastic Klausmeier system. Secondly, we want to verify the full applicability of the existence Theorem by showing the existence of a martingale solution of a highly nonlinear chemotaxis system with underlying fluid dynamics.

Probability.title: Functional second-order Gaussian Poincaré inequalities
Probability.summary: In this paper, we work in the framework of Hilbert-valued Wiener structures and derive a functional version of the second-order Gaussian Poincaré inequality that leads to abstract bounds for Gaussian process approximation in $d_2$ distance used by Bourguin and Campese (Electron. J. Probab., 2020). As pointed out by Bassetti, Bourguin, Campese, and Peccati (Statist. Probab. Lett., 2026) this distance alone does not imply weak convergence in infinite dimensions, we also consider $d_2^\dagger$, obtained by adding the absolute difference of the second moments. This metric metrizes $2$-Wasserstein convergence and agrees with $d_2$ for centered variables with matching covariance operators. Our abstract bounds are flexible and can be applied in various examples including functional Breuer-Major central limit theorems, shallow neural networks, and spatial statistics of SPDE solutions. In these applications, the covariance estimates also give the second-moment convergence needed for weak convergence in the corresponding Hilbert spaces.
Probability.comment: 36 pages, v3: d_2^\dagger distance introduced to characterize the weak convergence [Prop. 2.2]

Probability.title: The Riesz representation in submetric spaces and its probabilistic aspects
Probability.summary:
A submetric space is a topological space equipped with a continuous metric that generates a metric topology (usually) weaker than the original one (e.g., a~separable Hilbert space with the weak topology). We show that a positive linear functional on the space of bounded continuous functions on a submetric space is given as an integral with respect to a tight measure if, and only if, it is continuous in the strict topology. Neither local compactness nor complete regularity is required.
  We link the equicontinuity of a family of functionals in the strict topology to the uniform tightness of the underlying measures, and we provide a probabilistic representation (Skorokhod's parametrization) for such families. Finally, we identify the finest topology on the space of probability measures on a submetric space in which uniform tightness implies relative compactness. In non-metric spaces this topology is strictly stronger than the topology of weak convergence of probability measures.

Probability.title: Generalized Wasserstein Flow Matching: Nested Couplings for Point Cloud Generation
Probability.summary: We formulate flow matching on probability measures over probability measures. Directly from the Wasserstein-on-Wasserstein (WoW) continuity equation, we show that admissible nested outer and inner couplings induce a valid metameasure flow and non-local velocity field. Validity requires neither optimal plans nor a smooth manifold. Practically, this opens up the design space of multisample flow matching: exact Wasserstein plans are distinguished by energy and straightness, while sliced and lazy linear plans yield scalable alternatives. Point-cloud experiments, including controlled Bures-Wasserstein and Euclidean minibatch baselines, demonstrate the resulting geometry-cost trade-off.
Probability.comment: Keywords: flow matching, Wasserstein over Wasserstein, hierarchical optimal transport, multisample flow matching, minibatch optimal transport, sliced Wasserstein, Bures-Wasserstein, point cloud generation, generative models for distributions, measure-valued data, Wasserstein gradient flow, rectified flow, straight flows

Probability.title: Extending the V-sequence reduction to arbitrary independent distributions
Probability.summary: Let $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ be independent random variables with arbitrary known distributions, where $n\ge2$. The optimal probability $V_n(X_1,\ldots,X_n)$ of choosing an overall maximum satisfies $V_n(X_1,\ldots,X_n)\ge(1-1/n)^{n-1}$, and this bound is attained. We obtain this known sharp bound by extending the reduction lemma of Allaart and Islas (2016) from continuous to arbitrary distributions. We construct a $V$-sequence whose optimal win probability does not exceed that of the original sequence, and then apply the bound for $V$-sequences. The construction first replaces atoms by uniform observations on strictly ordered intervals and applies the original continuous reduction lemma. The reduced distributions are determined by a common critical level and a common probability for splitting a possible atom at that level.

Probability.title: Cutoff for random walks on nilpotent groups
Probability.summary: We study continuous-time random walks on finite nilpotent groups, allowing non-symmetric and nonuniform increment measures. Under a simple degree condition, sharp up to an absolute constant factor, we prove that total variation cutoff occurs if and only if the relaxation time is of smaller order than the mixing time. We establish a quantitative reduction to the Abelianization that preserves relaxation times and compares mixing profiles. Combining this reduction with a Gaussian approximation and the third-named author's cutoff criterion for diffusions yields the cutoff characterization.

Probability.title: On the number of pioneers in high-dimensional critical percolation
Probability.summary: We prove that for critical percolation in high dimension the expected number of pioneers on any set containing the origin is of the same order as the probability that a simple random walk starting from the origin exits the set. Our proof works in all dimensions $d>6$, under the usual assumption that the two-point function is of the same order as the Green's function. As an application we obtain a sharp uniform quantitative bound on the probability that the cluster of the origin intersects any given ball.
Probability.comment: No use of AI or LLM tools

Probability.title: Berry--Esseen bounds for stochastic approximation with Markovian noise
Probability.summary: This paper studies the convergence rate of the Polyak-Ruppert average estimator in one-dimensional linear stochastic approximation recursion driven by Markov chains, allowing the Markov chain to start from any initial distribution. Under the conditions of positive Harris recurrence, non-periodicity, and one-step domination, combined with the fourth-moment condition of the coefficient function with respect to the stationary distribution, this paper uses the exchangeable pair technique to prove that after deterministic bias correction for the average estimator, a Berry--Esseen bound of order $n^{-α/2}$ can be obtained, where the step size exponent is $α\in (1/2, 1)$. Moreover, for the statistics without bias correction and after variance normalization, the asymptotic normal approximation error is asymptotically equivalent to a normal constant multiplied by $n^{1/2 - α}$.

Probability.title: Poisson occupancy of paths on permuted regular graphs
Probability.summary:
In the classical occupancy problem, $B$ balls are placed independently and uniformly into $d$ boxes. We study a graph analogue of this model. Let $G$ be a directed $r$-regular graph on $d$ vertices and fix a vertex $i$. Consider all paths of length $L$ starting from $i$, and let $N_L(i,j)$ denote the number of such paths ending at a vertex $j$. Thus the vertices play the role of boxes and the $r^L$ paths play the role of balls.
  In general, these occupancies depend strongly on the geometry of $G$. We show that inserting independent uniform permutations between successive layers restores the classical Poisson behavior at the empirical level. Although the path endpoints remain strongly dependent, their empirical occupancy distribution has the same limiting Poisson law as independent balls thrown into boxes.
  More precisely, at the critical scale $r^L/d\toλ\in(0,\infty)$, provided $rL/d \to 0$, the empirical path multiplicity distribution converges in Wasserstein distance to $\operatorname{Pois}(λ)$, independently of the geometry of the underlying graphs. We also prove a local Poisson limit theorem and a Berry-Esseen bound for the empirical distribution functions. These estimates determine the full total-variation transition of the normalized path multiplicities toward uniformity.
  For arbitrary doubly stochastic kernels, we further establish exact covariance and Frobenius norm identities, together with an exact contraction formula for the chi-square divergence. As applications, we study synchronous opinion averaging, obtaining an explicit cutoff profile for equal-size groups and quantitative convergence to consensus for heterogeneous group sizes.

Probability.title: Periodic measures for time-inhomogeneous stochastic differential equations driven by multiplicative $α$-stable processes: Existence, uniqueness and numerical approximation
Probability.summary: In this paper, we study the periodic measures within the context of time-inhomogeneous Markov processes. By extending the Hairer--Mattingly method to the time-inhomogeneous case, we first establish the existence, uniqueness and exponential ergodicity of periodic measures for general time-periodic Markov processes. These results are subsequently applied to time-inhomogeneous stochastic differential equations under the assumption that the drift is weakly dissipative and locally Lipschitz. We further employ the truncated Euler--Maruyama scheme to study numerical approximations of the periodic measures and derive the convergence rate between the exact and discrete periodic measures. These numerical results are new even in the time-homogeneous case under the assumptions considered in this paper.

Probability.title: A multistate approach to disability insurance reserving with information delays
Probability.summary: Disability insurance claims are often affected by lengthy reporting delays and adjudication processes. The classic multistate life insurance modeling framework is ill-suited to handle such information delays since the cash flow and available information can no longer be based on the biometric multistate process determining the contractual payments. We propose a new individual reserving model for disability insurance schemes which describes the claim evolution in real-time. Under suitable independence assumptions between the available information and the underlying biometric multistate process, we show that these new reserves may be calculated as natural modifications of the classic reserves. For estimation of the model constituents, we employ the procedure proposed in [Buchardt, K., Furrer, C., & Sandqvist, O. L. (2025). Estimation for multistate models subject to reporting delays and incomplete event adjudication. The Annals of Applied Statistics, 19(4), 2782-2802. https://doi.org/10.1214/25-AOAS2068]. A real data application illustrates how the proposed estimation and reserving methods can be implemented and compares the resulting reserves with simpler reserving approaches.

Probability.title: Distribution of the First Hitting Point on a Boundary Set for a Random Walk in a Lattice Strip
Probability.summary: We consider a time-homogeneous random walk in a strip of a two-dimensional lattice whose transition probabilities are invariant under shifts along one of the coordinates. We study the limiting distribution of the first hitting point into a boundary set as the initial condition tends to infinity. Explicit expressions are obtained for this limiting distribution for negative and zero mean drift.

Probability.title: Improved well-posedness for the limit flow of differentiation of roots of polynomials
Probability.summary: In this paper, we study the partial differential equation on the circle that was heuristically obtained by Steinerberger \cite{steinerberger2019nonlocal} on the real line and which represents the evolution of the density of the roots of polynomials under differentiation. After integrating the partial differential equation in question, we observe that it can be treated with the theory of viscosity solutions. This equation at hand is a non linear parabolic integro-differential equation which involves the elliptic operator called the half-Laplacian. Due to the singularity of the equation, we first restrict our study to strictly positive initial condition. We obtain a comparison principle for solutions of the primitive equation which yields uniqueness, existence, continuity with respect to initial condition. We then extend these results to general initial data. We finally prove that the system of particles on the circle introduced by Steinerberger indeed approximates the solution of the equation.

Probability.title: Initialization Stability and Convergence of Projected Langevin Dynamics
Probability.summary: The entropic regularized optimal transport (EOT) plays a fundamental role in the computation of optimal transport. In \cite{CLP}, the authors proposed a gradient flow approach to EOT, and derived a projected Langevin diffusion that converges in distribution to the solution of EOT when initialized with a coupling between the two given marginals. In this paper, motivated by samplings of optimal couplings for EOT, we analyze the projected Langevin dynamics with arbitrary initial distribution, and prove that its long time behavior is the same as if it was initialized from a coupling.

Probability.title: Projected McKean--Vlasov Dynamics for Entropic Weak Optimal Transport
Probability.summary:
Unlike classical optimal transport, weak transport costs depend nonlinearly on the conditional law of couplings. This feature is essential in problems involving barycenter, conditional moments, and martingale-type constraints. Meanwhile, such conditional dependence makes ordinary Wasserstein geometry insufficient and calls instead for an adapted Wasserstein viewpoint. In this paper, we investigate the entropy-regularized weak optimal transport via gradient flows in adapted Wasserstein space.
  We derive, from the formal tangent structure of adapted Wasserstein space and the projection onto the set of couplings with prescribed marginals, a coupled McKean--Vlasov SDE. A novel and subtle term is a projection that, at each $Y$-location, averages a weak-transport force that already depends on the conditional law of $Y$ given $X$, thereby preserving marginals while retaining the nonlinear weak-transport structure.
  Under mild integrability and regularity assumptions, we prove weak existence and uniqueness in law for this projected McKean--Vlasov equation. We then prove that the flow converges, in the adapted Wasserstein topology, to the unique minimizer of the entropic weak optimal transport problem. We also describe a particle approximation and illustrate the dynamics on optimal transport and martingale optimal transport examples.

Probability.title: Sharp Fourth-Moment Wasserstein CLT Bounds
Probability.summary:
We prove that for the normalized sum $W=\sum_{i=1}^n X_i/\sqrt{n}$ of independent, mean-zero, $d$-dimensional random vectors with $\operatorname{Cov}(W) =Σ=\operatorname{diag}(σ_1^2,\dots, σ_d^2)$ (the diagonal form of the covariance matrix is assumed without loss of generality), the 2-Wasserstein distance from $W$ to $N(0,Σ)$ is bounded by \[\sqrt{2\sum_{j=1}^d \min \left\{σ_j^2, \frac{\sum_{i=1}^n \mathbb{E} [|X_i'-X_i|^2(X'_{ij}-X_{ij})^2 ] }{n^2 σ_j^2} \right\}},\] where $|\cdot|$ denotes the Euclidean norm, $X_i'$ is an independent copy of $X_i$, and $X_{ij}$ ($X_{ij}'$ resp.) denotes the $j$th coordinate of the vector $X_i$ ($X_i'$ resp.). On the one hand, it gives the optimal rate $O(β\sqrt{d/n})$ if $|X_i|\leq β$ for all $i$. On the other hand, in the isotropic case where $Σ=I_d$, it gives the optimal fourth-moment bound $O\left(\sqrt{\sum_{i=1}^n \mathbb{E}|X_i|^4/n^2}\right)$. Moreover, the coordinatewise minima suggest a tradeoff between the naïve coupling and the normal coupling for each component.
  To prove the main result, we develop a new transportation inequality using a coupling via the Föllmer process with a general covariance matrix and the martingale property of its drift. The resulting bound is then controlled using a Bonis-type expansion together with Bessel's inequality. The method and the result extend to $p$-Wasserstein bounds. As a consequence, we obtain the Hilbert space 4-Wasserstein CLT bound $O(n^{-1/4}[\operatorname{tr}(Q^{1/2})]^{1/2})$, where, in the i.i.d. case, $Q=\mathbb{E}[|X_1'-X_1|^2(X_1'-X_1)^{\otimes2}]$ and the $O(n^{-1/4})$ rate is optimal given the dimension-free form of $Q$. We further strengthen it to a dimension-free strong approximation result with a near-optimal error rate through the KMT embedding construction.

Probability.title: From Stochastic Transport Models to High-Dimensional Bayesian Inference
Probability.summary:
The Stochastic Transport in Upper Ocean Dynamics project introduced a new paradigm for representing uncertainty in geophysical fluid dynamics through stochastic transport models calibrated from data. This paper provides a synthesis of the principal theoretical and data assimilation developments achieved as part of the project.
  The central theme of the paper is the transformation of stochastic transport models from a modelling paradigm into a mathematically rigorous framework equipped with analytical, variational, calibration and Bayesian data assimilation methodologies suitable for geophysical fluid dynamics. We describe the development of the theory of stochastic transport equations, including well-posedness, regularity and approximation results, together with their geometric foundations based on stochastic variational principles, rough paths and fractional transport models.
  We further review methodologies for calibrating stochastic transport structures from observational and high-resolution simulation data, ranging from reduced-order stochastic models to modern generative approaches. Finally, we discuss Bayesian inference and high-dimensional data assimilation techniques developed for stochastic transport models, including particle filter methodologies and machine learning uncertainty quantification.
  Taken together, these developments establish a coherent framework linking stochastic transport modelling, rigorous analysis, calibration and Bayesian inference, thereby providing a foundation for uncertainty quantification and forecasting in geophysical fluid dynamics.

Probability.title: A sharp almost sure upper bound for partial sums of random multiplicative functions
Probability.summary: We prove that, for either a Steinhaus random multiplicative function or a Rademacher random multiplicative function $f$, and every $\varepsilon>0$, almost surely $|\sum_{n\le x}f(n)|\ll_{\varepsilon,f}\sqrt{x}(\log\log x)^{1/4+\varepsilon}$. Together with Harper's almost sure lower bound, this determines the sharp logarithmic exponent in both models. This settles Harper's conjecture on the large fluctuations of random multiplicative functions.

Probability.title: The monotone part of Chatterjee's rank correlation
Probability.summary: Chatterjee's rank correlation $ξ$ measures how strongly a random variable $Y$ depends functionally on a random variable $X$, but it does not distinguish increasing, decreasing and non-monotone relationships. We ask how much of the dependence measured by $ξ$ is explained by an increasing relationship. For continuous marginals, $ξ$ is, up to a factor, a squared distance from independence in a Hilbert space geometry derived from the Sobolev scalar product for copulas. We answer it by the metric projection onto the closed convex set of stochastically increasing copulas in this geometry. The projection is explicit: it replaces every vertical section by its least concave majorant, and it coincides with the smallest stochastically increasing copula dominating the given one. It splits $ξ$ orthogonally into a monotone part $ξ^{\uparrow}$ and the squared distance to the class of stochastically increasing copulas; dually, $ξ^{\uparrow}$ is, up to a factor, the squared distance to the polar cone, which corresponds to negative quadrant dependence. The monotone part vanishes exactly for negatively quadrant dependent copulas, equals $ξ$ exactly for stochastically increasing copulas, and equals one only for the comonotonicity copula. In contrast to $ξ$, it is increasing in the concordance order and continuous with respect to weak convergence. Symmetrisation decomposes the measure of mutual complete dependence in the same way. Finally, the construction extends to arbitrary distributions via isotonic regression of conditional distribution functions. In particular, the plug-in estimator based on the empirical distribution is strongly consistent for every copula, without smoothing or tuning parameters.

Probability.title: Infinite-Particle Determinantal Dynamics from Brownian Motion on $\mathrm{GL}_N(\mathbb{C})$
Probability.summary: We study the edge scaling limit of the logarithms of the squared singular values of multiplicative Brownian motion on the general linear group $\mathrm{GL}_N(\mathbb{C})$ with general initial conditions. Building on earlier work [arXiv:2605.06429], we prove that, for every initial condition in the enhanced state space, the limiting dynamics are determinantal and derive an explicit double-contour formula for their extended multitime correlation kernel. The dependence on the initial state, including information not determined by the particle coordinates, is encoded by the associated Laguerre--Pólya entire function. We further extend the construction of solutions to the corresponding infinite-dimensional system of singular stochastic differential equations to arbitrary initial configurations, including those with coinciding coordinates.
Probability.comment: 48 pages, 5 figures. Added an explicit comparison with Ahn's kernel; minor clarifications and corrections

Probability.title: Comparing and measuring intermediate tail dependence
Probability.summary: The tail dependence function $Λ$ of a bivariate copula, and the tail dependence order based on it, cannot distinguish between copulas whose tail dependence coefficient vanishes; for all of them $Λ\equiv 0$. Such copulas, among them the Gaussian copulas with correlation $ρ<1$ and the lower tails of all extreme-value copulas other than the comonotonicity copula, are nevertheless ordered by the much finer information contained in their tail expansion $C(u w)\sim u^κ\ell(u)\,b(w)$, where $κ$ is the tail order, $\ell$ is slowly varying and $b$ is the tail order function of Hua and Joe. We introduce an asymptotic tail order $\preceq$ that refines the tail dependence order and show that it is lexicographic in the three quantities $κ$, $\ell$ and $b$. As a consequence, every real-valued measure that is monotone with respect to $\preceq$ is constant on all but countably many tail-order classes; meaningful measures of intermediate tail dependence must therefore be defined level-wise, and we construct such measures. Finally we determine where the fine structure resides: if the joint tail is ray-regular on the exponential scale, then $b$ is determined by the tail order and the one-sided derivatives at $ω=1/2$ of the angular dependence function of Wadsworth and Tawn; it is a (possibly broken) product of powers. If the joint tail is log-concave on the exponential scale, $b$ is squeezed between two such products.

Probability.title: Strong convergence of Euler-Maruyama schemes for additive fractional SDEs with Lipschitz drift
Probability.summary: We study the strong convergence rate of the Euler--Maruyama scheme for additive stochastic differential equations driven by a fractional Brownian motion with Hurst parameter $H\in(0,1)$. Assuming the drift coefficient to be Lipschitz continuous, we establish strong convergence bounds of order $1$ if $H\in(1/2,1)$, and $1/2+H-\varepsilon$, for any $\varepsilon>0$, if $H\in(0,1/2]$. The main ingredient is a shifted stochastic sewing argument, which exploits the conditional Gaussian structure of fractional Brownian motion to control the noise discretization error.
Probability.comment: Accepted version with corrections. The supplementary material has been included

Probability.title: Log-Sobolev inequality for 2D $\mathrm{SU}(N)$ lattice gauge theory at all couplings
Probability.summary: We prove that the log-Sobolev inequality holds for the two-dimensional $SU(N)$ Wilson lattice Yang--Mills measure with arbitrary fixed inverse coupling $β$. The log-Sobolev constant depends on $β$ and $N$, but is uniform in the volume of the underlying lattice. The proof relies on a two-scale disintegration argument.

Probability.title: The Integrable Snake Model
Probability.summary: A pure snake configuration is a bijection $σ:\mathbb{Z}^2 \to \mathbb{Z}^2$ containing no two-cycles and such that for each $x \in \mathbb{Z}^2$ we have $σ(x) \in \{ x , x+ \mathbf{e}^1, x+\mathbf{e}^2 , x- \mathbf{e}^2 \}.$ The non-trivial cycles of a pure snake configuration may be regarded as a collection of non-intersecting paths in $\mathbb{Z}^2$ that may travel right, up, or down (but not left) from a given vertex. Pure snake configurations are a generalisation of lozenge tilings, which are in natural correspondence with paths that only travel right or up. We introduce a partition function on a finite version of this model and study the probabilistic properties of random pure snake configurations chosen according to their contribution to this partition function. Under a suitable weighting, the model is integrable in the sense that we have access to explicit formulas for its partition function and correlation function. We utilise the integrable structure of this model in several applications through its various scaling limits, such as to prove a traffic representation of ASEP on the ring, generalising the analogous result for TASEP by the first author.
Probability.comment: 47 pages. To appear in the Annals of Probability

Probability.title: Compatibility-based Bayesian inference: asymptotic limits, variational principles, and Wasserstein geometry
Probability.summary: Approximate Bayesian Computation (ABC) replaces intractable likelihood evaluations with comparisons between observed and simulated data. We formulate discrepancy-based inference through nonnegative compatibility weights. Prior-integrated convergence of rescaled weights gives total variation convergence as the tolerance vanishes. For a fixed positive tolerance and increasing sample size, we give a general representation-based formulation of the conditional-prior limit known from ABC and coarsened Bayesian inference, and establish convergence in expected total variation under stabilization in probability and a prior-null boundary condition. We also derive acceptance-persistence bounds under partial stabilization. The Gibbs variational identity yields convergence of minimum values and stability of approximate minimizers; the fixed-tolerance limit is characterized separately by constrained relative-entropy minimization. For additional penalty-based functionals of the limiting Wasserstein discrepancy, we prove an exact reduction to distributions over model laws and, under a geodesic assumption, a representation by distances from a Wasserstein ball. These penalty-based updates are distinguished from the original fixed-tolerance ABC limit and illustrated through a Gaussian comparison.

Probability.title: Continuity of the phase transition for long-range Bernoulli percolation with exponential decay on $\mathbb{Z}^{2}$
Probability.summary: We prove continuity of the phase transition for long-range Bernoulli percolation on $\mathbb{Z}^{2}$ with connection probabilities that decay at least exponentially fast. This extends earlier work by Duminil-Copin, Sidoravicius, and Tassion on slabs. Our proof establishes a finite-size criterion that allows us to run a renormalisation argument. As a corollary, we obtain supercritical sharpness, in the sense that for every $β>β_c$, there exists a unique macroscopic cluster in large boxes with high probability.

Probability.title: Zero temperature versus long time for diffusions driven by metric projections onto convex sets
Probability.summary: For a closed subset $C$ of Euclidean space, we study the diffusion whose drift pulls the state towards its nearest point in $C$, with noise intensity $T$. We let $T$ tend to zero and time tend to infinity. Convexity of $C$ is equivalent to a pathwise bound of the distance from $C$ by the norm of the process of Ornstein and Uhlenbeck. For arbitrary closed sets the bound holds in law. For compact convex $C$, we describe the invariant law by the curvature measures and the intrinsic volumes of $C$. The limit points of the law of the state form the orbit of reflected Brownian motion in $C$ started from the projection of the initial law. So the two limits commute only when this projection is the uniform law on $C$. Unless $C$ is a point, the mixing time is of order $1/T$ up to a logarithm. For the control problem the two limits of the value function commute for every compact convex set and every bounded Lipschitz terminal cost. A companion paper treats finite disjoint unions of convex sets.

Probability.title: Generalization of Zeroth-Order Method for Quotients of Quadratic Functions
Probability.summary: Optimization of quadratic functions and their quotients is relevant in subspace and iterative optimization methods. In this paper, we consider the matrix-free computation of the generalized operator norm and the maximization of a generalized Rayleigh quotient when only forward evaluations of two linear operators $A$ and $B$ are available. The proposed method samples search directions uniformly from the full unit sphere, thereby avoiding tangent-space sampling and explicit access to the metric matrix $B^{\mathrm T}B$. The exact line search along each sampled direction reduces to a $2\times2$ generalized eigenvalue problem on specific Gram matrices. In the generic case its maximizing step has a closed form. We prove that the objective values converge almost surely to the largest generalized eigenvalue and that the distance of the iterates to the leading generalized eigenspace converges to zero. We also relate full-sphere moment estimators to the Riemannian gradient and Hessian. The numerical experiments on synthetic Gaußian operators illustrate the behavior of the methods, and further studies of the proposed algorithms indicate favorable empirical convergence and weak dependence on the tested problem dimensions.

Probability.title: Inhomogeneous branching trees with symmetric and asymmetric offspring and their genealogies
Probability.summary: We define symmetric and asymmetric branching trees, a class of processes particularly suited for modeling genealogies of inhomogeneous populations where individuals may reproduce throughout life. In this framework, a broad class of Crump-Mode-Jagers processes can be constructed as (a)symmetric Sevast'yanov processes, which count the branches of the tree. Analogous definitions yield reduced (a)symmetric Sevast'yanov processes, which restrict attention to branches that lead to extant progeny. We characterize their laws through generating functions. The genealogy obtained by pruning away branches without extant progeny at a fixed time is shown to satisfy a branching property, which provides distributional characterizations of the genealogy.

Probability.title: Local Search with Correlated Randomness
Probability.summary:
The running-time distribution of a randomized algorithm is computed under independent randomness, but independence is rarely what a source guarantees. We study sources $ν$ satisfying $ν[w]\le DP[w]^s$ for every finite prefix $w$ of the random tape, where $P$ is an independent reference law, $0<s\le1$, and $D\ge1$; individual choices may be predictable, even determined by the past. The worst-case probability of any closed tape event $E$ is exactly $\min\{1,DC_s(E)\}$, where $C_s(E)$ is the infimum cost of covering $E$ by prefixes of varying depth, a tree max-flow/min-cut identity that makes worst-case survival probabilities exact and optimizable over the algorithm's choices.
  Three applications follow. For $n$ tasks on one machine, each retried until the next random symbol lies in its success set, every schedule has the same makespan distribution under independent randomness, yet under our constraint two fixed orders miss a linear deadline with worst-case probabilities $1$ and $\exp[-Θ(n)]$; a static priority rule is optimal at every deadline. For the standard local walk on a $k$-CNF with an assignment that satisfies a majority of each clause, we determine the sharp source threshold $s_*$. Below $s_*$, on some instances a single admissible source forces nontermination however clauses are selected; at $s_*$, with fixed $D$, the expected number of flips is at most cubic in the initial Hamming distance, against linear under independence, with matching worst-case instances; and any fixed margin above $s_*$ restores linear dependence on the distance. Third, verified backtracking for noisy predecessor search remains correct under a sufficiently strong bound on the comparison errors. In every setting the algorithm may also restart, which supplies no fresh randomness; restarting restores exponential tails exactly when the nontermination event has a prefix cover of cost below one.

Probability.title: The conditional expectation of the product of the first $n-1$ Hermite polynomials in a multivariate normal distribution with respect to the $n$-th variable. A fresh perspective on the Kibble-Slepian formula
Probability.summary:
We calculate the conditional expectation of $\prod_{j=1}^{n-1}H_{k_{j}}% (X_{j})$ given $X_{n}=z,$ if random vector $(X_{1},\ldots,X_{n})^{T}$ has multivariate normal distribution and $H_{n}(x)$ denotes $n$-th Hermite polynomial. This expectation is a polynomial in $z$ of order $\sum_{j=1}% ^{n-1}k_{j}$. Our formula has an iterative form with respect to $n$. We also present some auxiliary observations concerning the expansion of the density of the $n$-dimensional normal distribution in the series of the Hermite polynomials. Mostly concerning the properties of the coefficients of this expansion. To perform these calculations, we give a few auxiliary formulas concerning Hermite polynomials and multivariate normal distributions. We apply this result to obtain exact, simple forms of these expansions for $n=2$ and $3$, thus looking at known results from a different perspective.
  We believe that the results can be very useful in Probability Theory, in particular in the Theory of distributions, Statistics, and the Theory of Stochastic Processes, in particular Gaussian ones.

Probability.title: Occupation counts of rarely switching Markov chains: stratified local laws, support selection and the boundary layer
Probability.summary: A Markov chain with exit rates $q_i$ runs for $N$ steps with transition matrix $I+(T/N)Q$. On each irreducible face that carries start mass, we prove a local limit theorem for the occupation counts with an explicit constant and relative error $O(1/T)$, uniformly for $1\le T\le\varepsilon N$ with $\varepsilon\max_iq_i<1$ and on compact subsets of the open face. Up to $O(1)$, minus the log-probability of counts $n$ with support $F$ is $|F|-1$ times $\log(N/\sqrt T)$ plus $N$ times the Donsker and Varadhan functional of $I+(T/N)Q$ at $n/N$. Every admissible face has an explicit power of $T$ in its largest probability for large $T\le N^{1/3}$, and a constant given by a finite-dimensional variational formula. For $T=τ\log N$ the face of the mode minimizes $τλ_F+|F|-1$ at first order, with $λ_F$ the exit rate. If an admissible face has $Δ\ge1$ more states than another and an exit rate smaller by $δ>0$, we locate every crossing of their largest probabilities for large $T\le N^{1/3}$ up to $O(1/\log N)$. For two irreducible faces the crossing is unique for large $N$ in $1\le T\le\varepsilon N$, with coefficient $1/2$ of $\log\log N$. Near a facet, the continuous-time occupation density is the facet density times an explicit kernel, with relative error $O(1/T)$ at times $x\le cT$ off the facet, $c$ small. The counts obey a lattice form with extra error $T^2/N$ for $T\le\varepsilon_1\sqrt N$. The kernel is Bessel for $x=o(T)$ at facet profiles where the removed state has equal entry and exit laws, and at a profile where the rate has a first correction, of order $m\ge3$, if and only if $x=o(T^{1-2/m})$. On the complete graph with the uniform start, each face of at least 2 states crosses a vertex exactly once.
Probability.comment: 82 pages, 2 figures. v2 replaces 'Vertex crossings in a symmetric Markov multinomial model'. Most results of v1 are reproved here, mainly in Sections 7 and 8; Table 1 and the paragraph before it list which, and the others stay in v1. Code and Lean files at https://github.com/apemm/Kagey-Problems

Probability.title: Stochastic analysis of an emergency department with two levels sharing the servers
Probability.summary: In this paper, a stochastic model of an overcrwoded emergency department (ED) with two levels is analysed. A patient care pathway consists of a first consultation, followed by diagnostic tests and then a discharge consultation. The first level includes the patients before or during the first consultation. The second level applies to patients currently undergoing diagnostic tests, and patients waiting for or attending a second consultation. Each level has limited capacity; thus, when the second level is full, patients must remain at the first level. One of the key features of this model is the fact that first and second consultations are handled by the same pool of emergency physicians, which means that their decision to prioritize level 1 or level 2 affects the behavior of the system. Under a scaling assumption, the evolution of the number of patients in each step of the pathway is investigated. It is shown that, depending on the parameters, there is a phase transition between two different regimes: a regime limited by the number of emergency physicians and a regime limited by the second level capacity. Stochastic calculus gives the convergence of the state Markov process to a deterministic solution of a differential inclusion, which is proved to be unique and is explicitly characterized. The equilibrium points of the solution are determined depending on the service policies. It allows to compute the exit rate of the ED and the average length of stay, and find the policies that optimize them.
Probability.comment: 29 pages, 8 figures. Special issue of "European Conference on Queueing Theory" 2026

Probability.title: Martingality in EFM Signature Volatility Models
Probability.summary: We establish a martingality criterion for the Exponentially Fading Memory (EFM) signature volatility model, extending the recent result of Abi Jaber, Gassiat, and Sotnikov (2026). In the proposed framework, the volatility process is given by a linear functional of the EFM signature of a time-augmented Brownian motion, which yields a globally well-behaved, fully non-Markovian volatility model admitting a stationary distribution. The stationary EFM signature volatility model is also covered by allowing for a random initial value of the signature. Moreover, the volatility process can be adjusted to the initial forward variance curve. For this model, excluding trivial cases, we prove that the price process is a true martingale if and only if the truncation order is odd and a sign condition involving the correlation parameter holds.

Probability.title: Optimal Rates in Local and Central Limit Theorems for the Elephant Random Walk
Probability.summary: We determine the optimal rates of convergence in the local and central limit theorems for the one-dimensional elephant random walk in the diffusive and critical regimes, $0\le p\le3/4$. For every fixed initial distribution, we treat both exact finite-time centering and standardization and the normalization $S_n/\sqrt n$ (or $S_n/\sqrt{n\log n}$ at criticality). We establish uniform Edgeworth expansions for local probabilities and distribution functions, and use these expansions to derive the optimal convergence rates, which exhibit several phase transitions depending on the symmetry of the initial distribution, the normalization, and the type of approximation. Our approach uses elephant polynomials for precise characteristic-function expansions and a random recursive tree representation for global Fourier bounds.

Probability.title: Mixing time under monotone censoring
Probability.summary:
We prove the conjecture of Ding and Mossel~\cite{DM}: the lazy random walk on the discrete cube, censored to any increasing set of fixed positive density, mixes in time $O(n\log n)$. More precisely, for every nonempty increasing set $A\subseteq\{0,1\}^n$, with $a=μ(A)$ and $μ$ uniform on the cube, we prove $$
  t_{\mathrm{mix}}(P)\le C_a n\log(en), $$ where $C_a$ depends only on $a$. The proof uses hypercontractivity on the ambient cube to strengthen the Poincaré inequality on coordinate sections. An optimal stopping time occupation inequality for increasing sets converts the resulting local bound into a uniform bound on hitting times of large sets. An appendix by Y.~Peres improves the density dependence to $C_a=13a^{-1}\log(e/a)$, within a logarithmic factor of the conjectured $a^{-1}$ dependence.

Probability.title: Gaussian Exterior Dilation and Schatten Classes of Lévy Area
Probability.summary: We study the skew-adjoint Hilbert--Schmidt operator obtained by evaluating a fixed Hilbert two-form on a centered Gaussian linear map whose covariance is the inner product on its domain multiplied by a fixed nonnegative trace-class operator. We compute the expected regularized determinant of the resulting random operator and compare the random determinant with this expectation by dilation of the scalar parameter. For each fixed covariance and two-form, a single dilation almost surely applies to every nonnegative parameter value and yields simultaneous bounds for all Schatten norms and quasi-norms of orders $0<p<2$. The least admissible dilation satisfies a universal weak-$L^1$ estimate with optimal tail exponent. For Wiener area, a rank-one perturbation identity identifies the mean determinant with the regularized determinant of an explicit deterministic skew-adjoint operator and reduces Schatten membership to conditions on the covariance eigenvalues. Consequently, for each $0<p<1$, the area belongs almost surely to the Schatten class of order $p$ if and only if the covariance of the Wiener process does. At $p=1$, the criterion is finite covariance entropy; for $p>1$, trace-class covariance suffices.

Probability.title: Existence and uniqueness for non-linear forward equations: Addendum to "Mean-field approximations in insurance" (Hornung, 2026)
Probability.summary: Existence and uniqueness of solutions to non-linear forward integro-differential equations related to distribution-dependent Markov jump processes is established under standard boundedness and Lipschitz conditions.

Probability.title: Quasihelix properties of selected Volterra Gaussian processes
Probability.summary: We study local quasihelix and generalized quasihelix properties of several Gaussian Volterra processes with tempered, power-weighted, and logarithmic kernels, including tempered fractional Brownian motions and generalized fractional Brownian motion-type processes. These properties depend significantly on the values of the parameters involved, and we consider all possible cases in detail.

Probability.title: Covariance spectra of random linear systems near instability
Probability.summary: We study how stationary variance is distributed among the principal components of a randomly coupled linear system near instability. The coupling matrix has entries $N^{-1/2}ξ_{ij}$, where the $ξ_{ij}$ are independent copies of a bounded, centered real random variable of variance one. As $N\to\infty$ and the excess damping $δ_N\to0$, we prove that the covariance spectrum, with eigenvalues rescaled by $δ_N^2$ and weighted by their shares of the total variance, converges in probability to an explicit beta-product law. The convergence holds throughout $δ_N\ge N^{-1/2+\varepsilon}$ for every fixed $0<\varepsilon<1/2$. The law describes eigenvalues of order $δ_N^{-2}$ at ranks of order $Nδ_N^{3/2}$. Its limiting rank profile decays as $r^{-4/3}$ at large normalized rank and determines how many principal components retain a prescribed fraction of the stationary variance. The proof combines an exact computation of planar moments, uniform estimates for growing matrix words that accommodate nonsymmetric entry distributions, and resolvent bounds controlling the contribution of long times.

Probability.title: Uniform Large Deviations, Barrier Identity and the Néel--Arrhenius Law for the One-Dimensional Stochastic Landau--Lifshitz--Gilbert Equation
Probability.summary:
We study the one-dimensional stochastic Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert equation with a regularised, multiplicative, degenerate trace-class noise of strength sqrt(eps), the regularisation being Q_delta^{1/2} = (I + delta A^{beta/2})^{-1}, A = -d^2/dx^2, beta > 3/2, and determine the exponential rate of thermally induced magnetisation reversal.
  (i) Uniform large deviations at fixed delta: for every delta > 0 the solution satisfies a large deviation principle on C([0,T];H), with a good rate function, uniformly in the initial datum over a V-bounded set with compact H-closure; no non-degeneracy of the noise is assumed.
  (ii) Removal of the regularisation: as delta tends to 0 the noise tends to space-time white noise. With U_delta the state-space quasi-potential and U_0 that of the limiting control problem (Q_0^{1/2} = I), U_delta converges to U_0 in the Gamma-sense, and the barrier is delta-independent: the infimum of U_delta over the boundary of D equals that of U_0 and equals c_* times the infimum of the micromagnetic energy E over that boundary, c_* = 2 lambda_2/(lambda_1^2 + lambda_2^2), under two structural assumptions only and with no geometric or transversality input. Pointwise convergence fails, so the Gamma-limit is the sharp form of the statement.
  (iii) Neel-Arrhenius law: combining (i) and (ii) with the classical exit-time theorem, the escape time tau from D = {E < r} satisfies both levels of the law - for every fixed delta > 0, eps log E[tau] converges, uniformly on compact subsets of the initial set, to the barrier, and lim_{delta->0} lim_{eps->0} eps log E[tau] = c_* times the infimum of E over the boundary of D. The Arrhenius exponent is therefore stable under the regularisation of the noise and is determined by the micromagnetic energy alone.

Probability.title: The Radon--Nikodym topography of acyclic measured graphs
Probability.summary:
The classical Adams dichotomy [Ada90] characterizes amenability of probability-measure-preserving treed equivalence relations in terms of the ends of a given treeing. We extend this dichotomy to the measure-class-preserving (mcp) setting by analyzing the Radon--Nikodym topography of an acyclic mcp Borel graph, i.e., the interaction between the graph geometry and the associated Radon--Nikodym cocycle. In the general mcp setting one must count not all ends, but only the nonvanishing ends: those ends which have positive upper cocycle-weight.
  More precisely, we prove that a locally countable acyclic mcp graph is amenable if and only if a.e. component has at most two nonvanishing ends, while it is nowhere amenable exactly when a.e. component has a nonempty perfect closed set of nonvanishing ends.
  At the heart of our analysis lies the study of acyclic countable-to-one Borel functions. Our critical result is that, outside of the essentially two-ended setting, all back ends in a.e. orbit are vanishing and have cocycle-finite geodesics. We also give several characterizations, including topographical and cocycle-free, of essential one-endedness of such functions, and show that the number of barytropic ends controls the essential number of ends.
  Our proofs utilize mass transport, end selection, and the notion of the Radon--Nikodym core for acyclic mcp graphs, a new concept that serves as a guiding framework for our topographical analysis.
Probability.comment: Added figures and made improvements of exposition, changed the introduction

Probability.title: Martingale dimensions for a class of metric measure spaces
Probability.summary: We study the martingale dimension of diffusion processes associated with strongly local regular Dirichlet forms on metric measure spaces. The martingale dimension is an intrinsic quantity describing the probabilistic complexity of a diffusion, but its precise determination in non-smooth settings is highly nontrivial. In this paper, we establish a purely analytic criterion, formulated in terms of energy measures and relative capacities, which guarantees that the AF-martingale dimension equals one. Our approach does not rely on self-similarity, heat kernel estimates, or global geometric assumptions, and applies to settings where such structures are unavailable. The proof is based on a blow-up analysis of harmonic functions combined with a push-forward argument for energy measures, which excludes the coexistence of multiple independent martingale directions. As applications, we verify the assumptions of the theory for a class of inhomogeneous Sierpinski gaskets, including genuinely non-self-similar examples, and for the two-dimensional standard Sierpinski carpet, where the criterion yields a new capacity-based proof of the one-dimensionality of the martingale structure. In these examples, self-similarity or local symmetry enters only in verifying the hypotheses; the mechanism that forces the one-dimensionality is the analytic balance condition itself.

Probability.title: Combinatorial Insights into Asymptotic Normality
Probability.summary: In this paper we examine various sequences $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of real random variables arising naturally in connection with certain combinatorial structures. The goal is to investigate sufficient conditions for convergence to the standard normal distribution upon centering and normalization. By studying signed binomial sums, Stirling numbers of both kinds, and factorial moments, we obtain certain cancellations in the computation of centred moments $\mathbb{E}[(X_n - \mathbb{E}[X_n])^k]$. This allows us to conclude that $\frac{X_n - \mathbb{E}[X_n]}{\sqrt{Var \ X_n}} \xrightarrow{d} N(0,1)$ when the factorial moments $\mathbb{E}[(X_n)_k]$ are rational functions satisfying some simple conditions on the coefficients. A particular class of such random variables are those whose factorial moments are products and quotients of falling factorials in $n$; we apply our result in this situation and we discuss specific examples arising from block statistics of $k$-divisible non-crossing partitions and from outdegree statistics of rooted plane trees with $k$-divisible outdegrees.

Probability.title: Backward stochastic partial differential equations with unbounded random coefficients
Probability.summary: We study a linear backward stochastic partial differential equation with unbounded observation-adapted random coefficients, motivated by the duality approach to nonlinear filtering. The coefficients depend predictably on the observation history through a control with almost surely finite time-integrated squared norm. The drift, diffusion, and coefficient multiplying the martingale integrand may grow linearly in space. The diffusion matrix may grow quadratically in space and is allowed to be degenerate. Under bounded positive-order spatial derivatives and bounded smooth observation-measurable terminal data, we prove existence and uniqueness in a polynomially weighted Sobolev class up to control-energy stopping times. The proof combines conditional parameter estimates, entropy bounds for likelihoods, stability under the reference probability, and stochastic-flow reconstruction.

Probability.title: Higher-Order Paracontrolled Calculus for Geometric Rough Paths
Probability.summary:
We study the rough differential equation
  $$
  \frac{du_t}{dt}= F(u_t) ζ_t, \ \ u(0) = u_0 \in \mathbb{R}^d,
  $$
  where $F : \mathbb{R}^d \to L(\mathbb{R}^d, \mathbb{R}^d)$ is a sufficiently regular vector field, and the noise $ζ$ is a distribution in $\mathscr{C}^{α-1}(\mathbb{R})$ for $α\in (\frac{1}{4}, \frac{1}{3})$. We construct solutions to this equation at lower regularity than previous work of Gubinelli-Imkeller-Perkowski and Prömel-Trabs using ideas from the high-order paracontrolled viewpoint of Bailleul-Bernicot. The key tool in our work is the development of a harmonic-analytic framework for proving a set of iterated commutator estimates which are necessary for the solution theory. We also show the procedure of enhancement when the noise $ζ= dZ$, where $Z$ is a realization of fractional Brownian motion with Hurst parameter $H \in (\frac{1}{4}, \frac{1}{3})$.
Probability.comment: 50 pages; small typos with scaling fixed in Lemma 3.3f. Comments welcome!

Probability.title: Exceptional times of compact support for $α$-stable superprocesses
Probability.summary: We consider symmetric $α$-stable Dawson--Watanabe superprocesses on $\mathbb R^d$ for every $d\geq1$ and $0<α<2$, started from an arbitrary nonzero finite measure. We prove that, almost surely, the times at which the spatial support is compact and nonempty have Hausdorff dimension one in every nontrivial interval before extinction. We also prove that, almost surely, the times at which the support is contained in any prescribed neighborhood of the extinction point have Hausdorff dimension one in every nontrivial interval ending at extinction. These results extend the corresponding conclusions for $0<α<2/3$ to the full stable range. The key new ingredient is a uniform zero-set theorem of independent interest for Feller branching diffusions started from zero with deterministic continuous cumulative immigration. It shows that sufficiently small total immigration ensures that the zero set on a prescribed open interval has Hausdorff dimension arbitrarily close to one, with arbitrarily high probability. The estimate is uniform over the immigration profile and allows singular continuous immigration measures.

Probability.title: Linear Hashing Is Poissonesque
Probability.summary:
The Poisson approximation theorem states that when $m$ balls are tossed uniformly and randomly into $n$ bins, the distribution of the bin loads can sometimes be approximated by $n$ independent Poisson random variables of mean $m/n$. We show that when the balls are tossed via a random $\mathbb{F}_2$-linear map, the load distribution is still governed by this Poisson distribution, albeit in a (necessarily) weaker manner. This allows us to show that a random linear map behaves like a fully random map in the following ways:
  1. $\textbf{Expected loads.}$ We show that the expected value of the $r$th largest bin is governed by the $r$th largest value among $n$ independent Poisson random variables of mean $m/n$. Specializing to the canonical setting of $m=n$ and $r=1$, our bounds show that the expected maximum load when $n$ balls are hashed into $n$ bins by a random $\mathbb{F}_2$-linear map is no more than the corresponding expectation for a fully random map $\textit{plus}$ $\frac{3}2 + o(1)$. Specializing to $m\gg n\log n$, we show that the expected max load is $(1+o(1))m/n$ in this regime.
  2. $\textbf{Concentration.}$ When $m\gg n\log (1/ρ)$ balls are tossed into $n$ bins randomly, we expect with $0.99$ probability that $\textit{every}$ density-$ρ$ subset of bins will contain a $(1\pm o(1) )ρ$-fraction of the balls. We show that this remains the case if the $m$ balls are tossed using a random linear map, and our bound matches the $o(1)$-factor produced by the fully random case. This gives a stronger version of the Leftover Hash Lemma for linear maps. An implication of this is that all bins have load $m/n \pm O(\sqrt{(m/n)\log n})$ with probability $0.99$.
  We obtain these results by showing that the average of a log-potential on the bin loads is upper bounded by the cumulant generating function of a Poisson random variable of mean $m/n$.
Probability.comment: Abstract shortened to fit character limit

Probability.title: Beyond Deduplication: Sharp Retrieval Limits for Attention with Correlated Distractors
Probability.summary: Redundant context affects attention through two distinct mechanisms: repeated items add normalization mass, while score variation within correlated groups can produce extreme individual scores. We separate these effects in a planted retrieval model with exponentially many Gaussian distractors arranged in known, exponentially large clusters. The model is a two-level generalized random energy model, whose classical free energy yields exact retrieval thresholds. Gaussian interpolation further shows that increasing positive correlation at fixed token count lowers the distractor free energy, unlike adding duplicates. Our main result identifies a sharp limitation of subtracting log cluster size from pre-softmax scores: this correction removes multiplicity but retains within-cluster extremes. Even a temperature chosen after observing all scores cannot lower the required signal below $\sqrt{2α_1}$, where $α_1$ is the exponential rate of the number of clusters. Averaging scores before exponentiation instead suppresses these fluctuations and achieves $\sqrt{2ρα_1}$, where $ρ$ is the within-cluster correlation. The gap persists after adding exponentially many singleton distractors, so group size alone does not identify the target, and extends to fixed finite hierarchies of light-tailed independent-increment scores. Finite-sample, stability, and participation results complement the asymptotic analysis. A controlled retrieval experiment with frozen sentence embeddings supports this distinction while delineating its scope: averaging helps when the relevant item is a singleton, but can discard useful evidence when a relevant group contains multiple matching items.

Probability.title: Hitting probability for Reflected Brownian Motion at Small Target
Probability.summary: We derive the asymptotic behavior of hitting probability at small target of size $O(ε)$ for reflected Brownian motion in domains with suitable smooth boundary conditions, where the boundary of domain contains both reflecting part, absorbing part and target. In this case the domain could be localized near the target and explicit computations are possible. The asymptotic behavior is only related to $ε$ up to some multiplicative constants that depends on the domain and boundary conditions.

Probability.title: Moment representations for generalized Lehmer polynomials
Probability.summary: We represent normalized generalized Lehmer polynomials as moments of a random variable constructed from two independent negative binomial variables and an independent uniform variable. An integral form of their known exponential generating function yields mixtures of uniform distributions and convergent double series. We recover Eulerian polynomial identities and give a probabilistic interpretation of anti-diagonal sums of poly-Bernoulli numbers. We also prove moment determinacy, characterize the Stieltjes parameter range, derive Hankel total non-negativity and log-convexity, and identify the boundary distributions.

Probability.title: Variations of the harmonic entropy and linear drift on negatively curved surfaces
Probability.summary: For closed negatively curved surfaces, we obtain formulas for the derivatives of the harmonic entropy of its geodesic flow and the linear drift of its Brownian motion along conformal deformations. We deduce that the harmonic entropy of the geodesic flow of a closed surface of non-constant negative curvature (resp. linear drift of the Brownian motion on its universal cover) is strictly decreasing (resp. increasing) along the normalized Ricci flow. We also prove that any hyperbolic metric on a surface admits a neighborhood in the space of conformal negatively curved metrics in which the linear drift is greater or equal to the Liouville entropy, with equality if and only if the metric is hyperbolic.

Probability.title: Dirichlet-Constrained Random Operators and Quenched Reflection Quantum Walks: Tree Spectra and Poisson Criticality at High Degree
Probability.summary:
We study spectral limits of random operators whose incident edge weights are coupled by local normalization, and the reflection quantum walks associated with them. At each vertex of a $d$-regular graph, an independent Dirichlet probability vector distributes unit mass among outgoing directions. At fixed degree, the empirical spectral measures of the associated self-adjoint operators converge almost surely on locally tree-like graph sequences. We give a closed-walk formula for every moment of the limiting tree law.
  Our main result identifies two distinct high-degree scales. After rescaling the deterministic expected root spectral law by $\sqrt d$, a weak limit exists if and only if $dα_d^2$ converges in $[0,\infty]$, where $α_d$ is the Dirichlet parameter. The limits range from a point mass at zero through non-semicircular critical laws to the semicircle law. The critical laws admit a Poisson-tree representation with an explicit Bessel intensity. The extended family, including both endpoint laws, provides a first-Wasserstein approximation uniform over positive Dirichlet parameters.
  In the regime $dα_d^2\to0$, the rescaled law converges weakly to a point mass although its second moment remains one. Weighting spectral mass by its contribution to this moment and rescaling again reveals a different family of limits, classified by $dα_d$. These limits have explicit Beta-product descriptions. A quantitative comparison transfers the variance-scale classification to the centered and rescaled inherited eigenphases of the quantum walk.

Probability.title: Growing-time trace fluctuations and self-averaging form factors of Grover walks on random lifts
Probability.summary: We prove a functional central limit theorem for trace statistics of Grover walks on random $N$-lifts of a fixed finite connected simple $d$-regular graph, $d\geq3$. All observations are computed from the same random lift. The squared centred traces, divided by their observation times, have averages converging in probability to a degree-dependent constant. Their partial sums, centred at this constant and divided by the square root of the window length, converge to Brownian motion. For a window of length $M$ beginning at $t\geq1$, it suffices that $M\to\infty$ and $R^4(d-1)^R/N\to0$, where $R=t+M$. The initial time may remain fixed, with no further restriction on $M/t$. Convergence holds jointly with fixed low-degree polynomial trace statistics; their limiting vector is independent of the Brownian motion. For non-bipartite bases, we also identify Gaussian trace limits at fixed time offsets. Under common initial-time normalisation, subtracting a deterministic growth profile gives an explicit Brownian time change when $M/t$ has a finite limit. Bipartite bases retain the same averaged constant and have twice the Brownian variance rate. The proof combines a growing-dimensional Poisson approximation, a uniform bilinear Chebyshev-energy estimate, a time-decaying Poisson--Gaussian coupling, and a Gaussian quadratic-array theorem. Separate moment estimates give expectation-centred versions under an additional sufficient condition.

Probability.title: Free boundary regularity and well-posedness of physical solutions to the supercooled Stefan problem
Probability.summary: We study the regularity and well-posedness of physical solutions to the supercooled Stefan problem. Assuming only that the initial temperature is integrable, we prove that the free boundary, known to have jump discontinuities as a function of the time variable, is $C^1$ as a function of the space variable, and is $C^{\infty}$ outside of a closed, countable set, which we describe explicitly. We also prove that, as conjectured in arXiv:1902.05174, the set of positive times when a jump occurs cannot have accumulation points. In addition, we prove that short-time uniqueness of physical solutions implies global uniqueness, which allows us to obtain uniqueness for very general initial data that fall outside the scope of the current well-posedness regime. In particular, we answer two questions left open in arXiv:1811.12356, arXiv:2302.13097, regarding the global uniqueness of solutions. We proceed by deriving a weighted obstacle problem satisfied by the solutions, which we exploit to establish regularity and non-degeneracy estimates and to classify the free boundary points. We also establish a backward propagation of oscillation property, which allows us to control the occurrence of future jumps in terms of the past oscillation of the solution.
Probability.comment: To appear in Probab. Theory Related Fields. 31 pages, 2 figures. v3: Extended the local finiteness result to all singular times, including non-jump singularities

Probability.title: Monte Carlo Power Iteration Algorithms: Convergence, Analysis and Application to Reactor Criticality Calculations
Probability.summary: We study Monte Carlo power iteration algorithms in the context of reactor criticality simulations. Under mild conditions on the underlying physical system and the algorithmic structure, we derive explicit error bounds, which are to the best of our knowledge the first rigorous results for such methods which are ubiquitous in nuclear engineering. This is done by exploiting connections to Sequential Monte Carlo algorithms, and extending recent developments about stochastic neutron transport. We demonstrate the applicability of our results by considering a concrete version of the Monte Carlo power iteration algorithm as well as variance reduction schemes.

Probability.title: A Product on Lorenz Hulls, Zonoids, and Vector Measure Ranges
Probability.summary: A Lorenz skeleton and Lorenz hull are the range and the convex hull of the range of an $\mathbb{R}^n$-valued measure, respectively. A Lorenz hull is also known as a zonoid. We extend the tensor product of centered zonoids introduced by Aubrun and Lancien and developed by Breiding et al. to Lorenz hulls without a centering restriction, and further to Lorenz skeletons. We show that this product admits a direct interpretation in terms of the elementary notion of a product measure. Inclusion preservation and Hausdorff continuity, shown by Aubrun and Lancien and Breiding et al., respectively, for centered zonoids, hold in this more general setting as well.

Probability.title: Hierarchical exchangeability of pure states in mean field spin glass models
Probability.summary: The main result in this paper is motivated by the Mézard-Parisi ansatz which predicts a very special structure for the distribution of spins in diluted mean field spin glass models, such as the random K-sat model. Using the fact that one can safely assume the validity of the Ghirlanda-Guerra identities in these models, we prove hierarchical exchangeability of pure states for the asymptotic Gibbs measures, which allows us to apply a representation result for hierarchically exchangeable arrays proved in arXiv:1301.1259. Comparing this representation with the predictions of the Mézard-Parisi ansatz, one can see that the key property still missing is that the multi-overlaps between pure states depend only on their overlaps.
Probability.comment: Corrected minor errors and allowed more general overlap intervals in the definition of clusters

Probability.title: Limit theorems for the distance between two random points in $l_p^n$-balls
Probability.summary: In this paper, we prove that the Euclidean distance between two independent random vectors uniformly distributed on $l_p^n$-balls ($1\leq p\leq\infty$) or on their boundaries according to the cone measure satisfies a central limit theorem as $n\to\infty$. Also, we give a compact proof of the case of the sphere, which was proved by Hammersley. Furthermore, we complement our central limit theorems by providing large deviation principles for points in the balls and on their boundaries when $1\leq p\leq\infty$. The speed is $n$ for $p\geq2$, whereas the regime $1\leq p<2$ has speed $n^{p/2}$ and an explicit rate function.

Probability.title: Computational and Statistical Guarantees of the c-Rectified flow
Probability.summary: Recently, rectified flow has emerged as a fundamental framework for large-scale image generation, powering state-of-the-art systems such as FLUX.1 and Stable Diffusion 3. Despite its remarkable empirical success, the computational and statistical guarantees of iterative rectified flow have remained largely unexplored. We address this problem by studying c-rectified flow, a cost-aware class of rectified flow that projects velocity fields onto a gradient class while preserving endpoint marginals. The ordinary rectified flow can fail to recover the optimal transport coupling: in a Gaussian case study, the iteration converges to the optimal coupling if and only if the source and target covariance matrices commute. More generally, for a Gaussian to log-concave coupling, the ordinary rectified flow can reach a fixed point after one step from independent initialization. In contrast, under suitable regularity and uniform-integrability assumptions, iterative c-rectified flow always converges to the optimal transport coupling. We further establish quantitative one-step contraction and exponential convergence guarantees under projection-stability assumptions for both quadratic and strongly convex displacement costs. Finally, under a Hölder ball assumption, we develop new minimax-optimal score estimation rates and show that, when combined with iterative c-rectified flow, they yield a rate-optimal estimator of the optimal transport for the dimension \(d \ge 3\) and a nearly parametric rate for \(d=1,2\).

Probability.title: Functional limit theorems for Galton--Watson processes with inhomogeneous immigration
Probability.summary: We study the asymptotic behavior of a sequence of Galton--Watson processes with inhomogeneous immigration when the limit of the means of the offspring distributions is less than $1$ or equal to $1$. Under growth conditions on the expected values of the immigration distributions and the variances of the offspring distributions, and assuming the weak convergence of properly scaled immigration processes towards a non-negative stochastic process $\mathcal Y$ with càdlàg or continuous sample paths, we establish functional limit theorems for the sequence of Galton--Watson processes with inhomogeneous immigration in question. The limit stochastic processes can be represented as a constant multiple or an integral functional of $\mathcal Y$ .

Probability.title: A note on the Besov spaces ${\rm B}_1^{Φ_2}$
Probability.summary: Regarding the Besov space ${\rm B}_1^{Φ_2}$, defined by S. Geiss and Ylinen (Memoirs AMS 1335, 2021) by a coupling method, we prove for $ξ\in{\rm B}_1^{Φ_2} \cap L_2$ a distributional estimate in terms of the Lorentz-Zygmund space $L_{1,\infty}(\ln L)^{-1}$ for the Malliavin derivative ${\rm D}(T_uξ)$ uniformly in $u>0$, where $(T_u)_{u\ge }$ is the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck semi-group. Here $ξ$ is not necessarily Malliavin differentiable in the ${\rm D}_{1,1}$-sense. This provides for Theorem 4.22 of the aforementioned reference an extension to the borderline case $p=1$.

Probability.title: Non-local to local limit for stochastic conservation laws
Probability.summary: This work proves the convergence of stochastic nonlocal conservation laws, with spatially inhomogeneous noise, to stochastic conservation laws when the range of particle interaction vanishes. This provides rigorous justification for a class of stochastic conservation laws that has received considerable attention in the last decade. To handle technical challenges such as gradient-dependent noise, modified versions of the equations with specific cutoff boundaries are utilized and new uniform estimates to ensure stability during the limiting process are established. In addition, the work demonstrates that this convergence depends on the presence of a viscous term, as a counterexample shows that without it, the limiting solution may fail to be an entropy solution.

Probability.title: Learning on-the-fly quasi-stationarity diagnostics from low-dimensional surrogates
Probability.summary:
