Accelerated dynamics methods, such as parallel replica dynamics, require estimates of the decorrelation time, after which a process trapped in one of its metastable states is distributed according to the quasi-stationary distribution (QSD).
  In a method proposed by Binder, Lelièvre and Simpson, decorrelation times are defined by coupling a particle approximation of the non-linear conditioned probability flow of the process with MCMC-inspired diagnostics.
  We explore an alternative to MCMC diagnostics, based on coarse-graining of non-linear probability flows and simulation-based inference.
  We first develop a coarse-graining framework for killed Markov jump processes conditioned on survival, proving uniform-in-time, non-asymptotic estimates approximating the non-linear probability flow of
  the true process by the non-linear flow of a surrogate process, defined with a collective variable. The framework does not assume reversibility of the true process, and also gives bounds which scale explicitly in an adiabatic regime.
  Motivated by these results, we then construct a quasi-stationarity diagnostic using simulation-based inference: a recurrent neural network (RNN), trained on particle approximations of non-linear effective flows, estimates posterior probabilities of decorrelation. The learned diagnostic is then transferred to collective-variable traces of high-dimensional particle approximations.
  We investigate the behavior and robustness of this diagnostic on a set of numerical experiments, comparing it to the MCMC diagnostic of Binder et al.\ on both synthetic examples and a molecular system, in and out of its training prior distribution.
  When its prior assumptions hold, the RNN diagnostic outperforms the MCMC diagnostic in ROC analysis, is less conservative, fails less often, and has an interpretable decision threshold.

Probability.title: When is Fine-Tuning Scalable? Certified Recovery from Noisy Data and Linear-Cost Fine-Tuning on Structured Task Shifts
Probability.summary:
Transformers often transfer across related tasks with little fine-tuning; we study this question in noisy nonparametric regression for continuous maps $f,g:[0,1]^d\to\mathbb{R}^D$, representing the source and shifted tasks, using a single-query, single-head transformer $\mathcal{T}(\cdot)=V\operatorname{Softmax}(-α(\cdot,K))$ with $\ell^{\infty}$-based alignment scores $α$. Rather than assume that gradient-based training reaches an empirical risk minimizer, we give a model-specific two-stage procedure \textbf{certifying} source-task recovery and out-of-distribution (OOD) adaptation. With high probability, the resulting attention head recovers $f$ to arbitrary accuracy $\varepsilon>0$ in every fixed $L^p([0,1]^d)$ norm, $1\le p<\infty$, from noisy observations. For Lipschitz targets, its rate is minimax-optimal up to logarithmic factors without assuming oracle access to an asymptotic ERM. If $D=1$ and $f$ is Pfaffian than the values matrix factors into $AC$ with $A$ scaling at-most linearly $\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon^{-1})$ in the reciprocal approximation error $\varepsilon>0$. Importantly, our training procedure encodes all our identified (potentially) shared geometric structure from $f$ only into the values matrix factor $C$ and the keys matrix $K$ allowing for rapid access, and all $f$-specific structure only into $A$.
  Our main result concerns the OOD phase; where we identify geometric structures, which if shared by the source $f$ and OOD $g$ task; then only only the values matrix factor $A$ needs to be fine-tuned to guarantee an $L^p$-recovery of $g$. Critically, fine-tuning only $A$ is a convex problem which involving an \textit{at-most linear} number of parameters $\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon^{-1})$; dramatically cutting down on the worst-case scaling of $\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon^{-\mathbf{d}})$ unavoidable in the source-training phase.

Probability.title: Using the Blackwell-Cover Guessing Strategy to Separate Unobserved Bernoulli Trials - II
Probability.summary: In a prior paper, we investigated what could be said about the number in the pair that was not observed when we employed the BlackwellCover Guessing Strategy. In this paper, we generalize prior results to arbitrary distributions. We use a variant of the BlackwellCover strategy ro take pairs of coins chosen from a mixture of two different distributions G and H such that one of the coins is flipped, and as a result of that flip the unobserved (unflipped) coin is placed in one of two sets A and B. We show that, regardless of which distributions are used for G and H, there are situations in which this can be done so that the mean of the heads probabilities of the unobserved coins in A is less than the mean of the heads probabilities of the unobserved coins in B. What makes this result surprising, in addition to its generality, is a comparison with a corresponding result for marbles. If one knows that one will always be weighing one of two marbles with different specific weights, such as 10g and 20g, knowing the weight of the marble being weighed automatically determines the weight of the other. However, even if one knows that one will be flipping one of two coins with specific heads probabilities such as 1/3 and 2/3, the outcome of the flip of one of the coins will not immediately enable one to conclude anything about the heads probability of the unflipped coin, which is where the BlackwellCover Guessing Strategy comes into play.

Probability.title: Bayesian Inference in Partially Observed Critical Systems
Probability.summary: We ask how much of a large random system must be observed before a global average can be inferred with controlled uncertainty. For the random transposition shuffle, a conjugate Bayesian estimator of the average displacement, computed from $m$ uniformly sampled cards, has relative uncertainty $1/\sqrt{2m}$, independent of the deck size $n$. The law of total variance exposes a second error, the floor $R_n$, which arises because the observed configuration is a single draw from equilibrium: no relative tolerance below $κ\sqrt{R_n}$ can be certified, even by a census. For the shuffle we derive $R_n=(2n^2+7)/\bigl(5(n-1)^2(n+1)\bigr)$ and show that the posterior remains calibrated. At the critical point of the two-dimensional Ising model the floor of the energy vanishes, whereas that of the magnetisation stays near $0.072$; its mean-field limit is $\sqrt{2}-1$. For correlated fields read by sensor networks, the usual 95\% interval covers the ensemble mean in 7\% of cases. Bounding the floor from one realisation, as in single-chain Monte Carlo diagnostics, requires an assumption on the decay of correlations.

Differential Geometry.title: Sharp Riemannian heat kernel estimates on the cut locus and the Parabolic Anderson model
Differential Geometry.summary: Using sharp global heat kernel bounds and geodesic comparison geometry, we show that the Dalang condition for well-posedness of the parabolic Anderson model with measure-valued initial conditions, first introduced on Euclidean space, holds on general compact Riemannian manifolds. We furthermore establish upper and lower moment bounds for all such solutions, providing evidence for intermittency in this generality. This extends and simplifies earlier work that required non-positive curvature.

Differential Geometry.title: Nonabelian Higgs fields from minimal submanifolds
Differential Geometry.summary: We construct $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ Yang-Mills-Higgs fields on a broad class of noncompact Riemannian manifolds, concentrating in the large-mass limit along prescribed nondegenerate minimal submanifolds of codimension three. The solutions have uniformly bounded rescaled energy. On closed manifolds with $b_1(M)=0$, adding a suitably scaled Higgs potential gives an analogous concentration result. Our construction completes one direction of the correspondence proposed by Parise, Pigati and Stern, realising prescribed minimal submanifolds of codimension three as concentration sets of $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ Yang--Mills--Higgs fields.

Differential Geometry.title: Characteristic gluing to extremal Kerr horizons and the third law of black hole thermodynamics in vacuum
Differential Geometry.summary:
We prove a non-perturbative, non-axisymmetric characteristic gluing theorem for the Einstein vacuum equations: every Boyer-Lindquist sphere in the domain of outer communication of a Kerr black hole, in particular every symmetry sphere of a Schwarzschild exterior, can be glued along a single outgoing null hypersurface to a horizon sphere of an extremal Kerr black hole of sufficiently large mass. The gluing is exact at both ends and matches the full sphere data, including the transversal curvature. This proves a conjecture of Kehle and Unger in the extremal case. We first raise the angular momentum to the extremal value by rotating shear pulses of non-axisymmetric gravitational radiation, and then damp the incoming data exponentially along a long non-expanding neck. At the degenerate target horizon we invert the linearised problem at all angular frequencies, using a factorisation of a fourth-order angular operator into an angular Teukolsky-Starobinsky product.
  As an application, we construct one-ended asymptotically flat vacuum initial data whose maximal development contains an exactly Schwarzschild apparent horizon and, at a later advanced time, an exactly extremal Kerr event horizon. This is the first rigorous counterexample to the third law of black hole thermodynamics in vacuum, and proves a second conjecture of Kehle and Unger.

Differential Geometry.title: Morse index characterization of the Veronese projective plane
Differential Geometry.summary: Following Simons' seminal work in 1968, every closed, connected, embedded minimal surface in the four-sphere that is not totally geodesic has Morse index at least five. In this paper, we prove that equality holds if and only if the surface is congruent to the Veronese projective plane. Relying on recent advances by Bernstein and Ketover, this characterization settles Kusner's 1996 conjecture on the minimizers of the Willmore functional in dimension four for surfaces whose normal bundle has nonzero Euler number. This is always the case, in particular, for embeddings of nonorientable surfaces whose orientation double cover has even genus.

Differential Geometry.title: Properly embedded Legendrian surfaces in the tangent sphere bundle of hyperbolic space
Differential Geometry.summary: We show that every open Riemann surface may be conformally properly embedded in the tangent sphere bundle of hyperbolic $3$-space as a Legendrian surface. We achieve this by constructing proper holomorphic Legendrian embeddings in $\mathrm{SL}_2 (\mathbb{C})$ whose projections to the quotient $\mathrm{SL}_2 (\mathbb{C})/ \mathrm{U}_1$ remain embeddings. As another consequence, every open Riemann surface admits a proper holomorphic Legendrian embedding in the projectivised special linear group $\mathrm{PSL}_2 (\mathbb{C})$.

Differential Geometry.title: Parabolic Rectifiable Reifenberg for Measures
Differential Geometry.summary: We announce a structure theory for measures on $\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}$ equipped with the parabolic distance. Our results include a parabolic rectifiable Reifenberg theorem for arbitrary Radon measures, qualitative and quantitative characterizations of regular parabolic rectifiability by Jones square functions, and sharp results for $L^p$ beta numbers. The results hold in every parabolic dimension and extend the theories of Edelen--Naber--Valtorta, Azzam--Tolsa and David--Semmes to space-time. The stated theorems and corollaries, together with their proofs, are formalized in Lean~4 with Mathlib.
Differential Geometry.comment: Comments are welcome. 15 pages, 7 figures, link to a github repository for formalization

Differential Geometry.title: The Weyl Problem for Planar CBB$(-1)$ Surfaces in Hyperbolic $3$-Space
Differential Geometry.summary: In this paper, we study the Weyl problem for noncompact convex surfaces in hyperbolic $3$-space $\mathbb{H}^3$. We prove that any planar CBB$(-1)$ surface with countably many ends can be isometrically embedded as the boundary of a closed convex subset $X\subset\mathbb{H}^3$ such that each connected component of the ideal boundary of $X$ is either a round disk or a single point. By known rigidity results, such an embedding is unique up to isometries of $\mathbb{H}^3$. Moreover, we show that the assumption of countably many ends can be dropped if Koebe's circle domain conjecture holds.

Differential Geometry.title: Yang-Mills-Higgs Limits of Reflexive Higgs Sheaves
Differential Geometry.summary: For stable Higgs bundles, Hermitian-Einstein metrics can be obtained as limits of the Yang-Mills-Higgs (Y-M-H) flow. We study the algebraic structure of subsequential limits of this flow for reflexive Higgs sheaves over compact Kähler manifolds, without assuming stability. We prove that the limiting reflexive Higgs sheaf is isomorphic to the double dual of the graded sheaf associated with the Harder-Narasimhan-Seshadri filtration of the initial sheaf.

Differential Geometry.title: Curvature quotient flows and Alexandrov--Fenchel inequalities in hyperbolic space
Differential Geometry.summary: We study quermassintegral-preserving curvature flows in $\mathbb H^{n+1}$, $n\geq3$, driven by the curvature quotient $(E_k/E_\ell)^{1/(k-\ell)}$. For $1\leq\ell<k$ with $k+\ell\leq n$, we prove that positive sectional curvature is preserved. Starting from a smooth closed strictly convex hypersurface with positive sectional curvature, the flow exists for all time and converges smoothly and exponentially to a geodesic sphere. As an application, we establish sharp Alexandrov--Fenchel inequalities between $W_k$ and $W_\ell$ for smooth bounded convex domains whose boundaries have nonnegative sectional curvature, whenever $0\leq\ell<k\leq n$ and $k+\ell\leq n$. Equality holds if and only if the domain is a geodesic ball. Together with previously known cases, these inequalities give the full family of Alexandrov--Fenchel inequalities for this class of domains in $\mathbb H^6$. We also construct counterexamples showing that $k+\ell\leq n$ is the optimal range for preservation of positive sectional curvature by these flows.

Differential Geometry.title: Simplifying 2-Bundle Descriptions of Invariants and Local Dynamics
Differential Geometry.summary: A string couples to a two-form gauge potential whose local descriptions need not fit together as a single global form. Principal 2-bundles provide a geometric description of this gluing. However, we recover surface amplitudes and quantum partition functions, as well as local classical field dynamics, without the 2-bundle formalism. For global phases, topological and index invariants, and twisted-sheaf moduli, established equivalences give alternative descriptions through cocycles, bundles, operators, or modules, with the required global compatibility data. For three-dimensional finite gauge theories with cohomological actions, Fourier transformation expresses the partition function as a sum of partition functions of ordinary finite-group gauge theories. An invertible local substitution reduces invariant classical actions for a class of 2-bundle connections represented by finite-dimensional crossed modules to ordinary gauge and tensor dynamics. These finite and local reductions explicitly eliminate field variables. A four-dimensional quadratic example instead admits a direct cochain evaluation even when an ordinary gauge-theory reduction fails. These results therefore do not require the additional 2-bundle presentation.

Differential Geometry.title: Index and nullity of critical spherical catenoids in hyperbolic three-space
Differential Geometry.summary: We prove that every critical spherical catenoid in a geodesic ball of hyperbolic three-space has Morse index four and nullity two. This resolves Medvedev's index conjecture throughout the parameter range of the catenoid family. The kernel consists precisely of the normal components of rotations that preserve the center of the ball and tilt the axis of the catenoid. As a consequence, the radius of the supporting ball increases strictly along the family. The proof combines a global boundary inequality obtained from a Wronskian, a positive Dirichlet eigenfunction supplied by the time component of the unit normal, and a Riccati comparison for the angular mode $k=2$. A ground-state identity then yields positivity of every angular mode $k\ge2$.

Differential Geometry.title: On Lorentzian torse-forming structure manifolds
Differential Geometry.summary: In this paper we introduce a class of non-flat Lorentzian manifolds, called Lorentzian torse-forming structure manifolds (briefly, LTFSMs). This class contains Lorentzian concircular structure manifolds (briefly, LCSMs), LSP-Sasakian manifolds, LP-Sasakian manifolds with coefficient $α$, LP-$α$-Sasakian manifolds, LP-Sasakian manifolds, and LP-$α$-Kenmotsu manifolds. The interrelations among these various classes of manifolds are illustrated in Figures 1 and 2. We investigate several geometric properties of LTFSMs. In particular, we show that the expansion scalar, given by the divergence of $ξ$, is nonzero and nonconstant, and that the flow of $ξ$ is irrotational. In an LCSM, the Ricci operator commutes with the structure tensor $φ$ [12]. However, it is shown that, in an LTFSM, the Ricci operator does not generally commute with $φ$. If the gradient of the torse-forming scalar $α$ is collinear with the torse-forming vector field $ξ$, then the Ricci operator commutes with $φ$, and the manifold reduces to an LCSM. It is known that a conformally flat LCSM is quasi-Einstein and hence is a manifold of quasi-constant curvature. We show that a conformally flat LTFSM is a generalized quasi-Einstein manifold in the sense of Chaki [1] and is also a manifold of generalized quasi-constant curvature. Several curvature-related properties of LTFSMs are established, and their sectional curvature is determined. The existence of LTFSMs is demonstrated through several proper nontrivial examples. We also present examples that are simultaneously LCSMs and LTFSMs, examples of LTFMs characterizing twisted cubic spacetimes, and generalized Robertson-Walker (GRW) spacetimes characterizing LCSMs. Finally, we provide examples of LTFSMs in which the vector field $ξ$ is a unit timelike torse-forming vector field but is not concircular; see Examples 5.6--5.8.

Differential Geometry.title: A theory of stratification learning
Differential Geometry.summary: Given i.i.d. sample from a stratified mixture of immersed manifolds of different dimensions, we study the minimax estimation of the underlying stratified structure. We provide a constructive algorithm allowing to estimate each mixture component at its optimal dimension-specific rate adaptively. The method is based on an ascending hierarchical co-detection of points belonging to different layers, which also identifies the number of layers and their dimensions, assigns each data point to a layer accurately, and estimates tangent spaces optimally. These results hold regardless of any ambient assumption on the manifolds or on their intersection configurations. They open the way to a broad clustering framework, where each mixture component models a cluster emanating from a specific nonlinear correlation phenomenon.

Differential Geometry.title: Pure Type-One Generalized Hypercomplex Structures in Dimension Four
Differential Geometry.summary: We classify untwisted generalized hypercomplex structures on four-manifolds whose entire sphere has type one. The three Poisson tensors determine a canonical line field, and the local data are Gauduchon--Tod coframes. We determine local equivalence under diffeomorphisms, common closed real $B$-fields and constant rotations of the triple. On a closed manifold the canonical foliation is automatically Riemannian: a nonzero period obstructs the exact twist required by the non-Riemannian models. The compact structures form four families, distinguished by $b_1=1,2,3,4$: Berger quotients, flat axis quotients, nontrivial circle bundles over flat three-tori, and constant tori. We determine their parameters, equivalences and finite ordered quotients, including nonorientable canonical lines. The underlying manifolds are parallelizable, satisfy $b_2=2b_1-2$, and are symplectic exactly when the intrinsic Gauduchon--Tod invariant vanishes. A twisted Hopf example shows why the untwisted hypothesis is essential. The classification is intrinsic and assumes no initial circle action. These results address the four-dimensional untwisted case of the intermediate-type question of Fino and Grantcharov.

Differential Geometry.title: Classifying Leibniz racks
Differential Geometry.summary: Lie quandles were defined by T. Fritz as a nonlinear generalization of Lie algebras, to serve as a nonlinear algebras of observables in generalized form of Hamiltonian mechanics. These objects were subsequently generalized in a prequel article to objects referred to as smooth Lie group families of smooth racks by the authors. In this article, we investigate a particular system of nonlinear functional differential equations whose solution in general provides a pathway to the classification of smooth Lie group families of smooth rack structures on any given smooth manifold. We then discuss a particularly practical ansatz for solving these equations, and use it to construct new families of examples, as well as prove a result on the sense in which the Bloch sphere is the unique Lie quandle structure on the sphere.

Differential Geometry.title: Geometric aspects of fault tolerance
Differential Geometry.summary: We highlight three geometric aspects of fault tolerance. First, we construct an operator-algebraic formulation of the fiber bundle framework for fault tolerance, and show that a generalization of the Knill-Laflamme conditions implies a flat connection for this framework. Next, we develop this framework for Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill (GKP) codes. We show that, for each polarization type, their moduli space embeds smoothly into a Grassmannian of finite-dimensional subspaces of a regularized distribution space. Finally, we explain how GKP codes associated with Jacobians give rise to magic states that can be obtained by code space projections of Gaussian states and identify a $\rm CCZ$-type magic state arising this way.

Differential Geometry.title: Symplectic singularity as hyperKähler cone
Differential Geometry.summary: We prove that any symplectic singularity has a structure of hyperKähler cone. In particular, it is equivalent to the vertex of a conical symplectic variety, and it is automatically K-polystable.
Differential Geometry.comment: 42 pages. cf., Acknowledgements and use of AI

Differential Geometry.title: Uniform large-genus asymptotics of Weil-Petersson volumes
Differential Geometry.summary: Let $V_{g,n}$ denote the Weil--Petersson volume of the moduli space of genus-$g$ hyperbolic surfaces with $n$ cusps. We obtain an asymptotic expansion in inverse powers of the genus as $g\to\infty$, uniformly for all $n\ge0$. This includes cusp counts of order $\sqrt g$ and larger, where the fixed-$n$ expansion of Mirzakhani and Zograf no longer gives a uniform approximation. The leading term is explicit and has relative error $O(g^{-1})$. Truncating the expansion at a suitably chosen order proportional to $\sqrt g$ gives relative error $O(\exp(-a\sqrt g))$ for some $a>0$, with no restriction on the growth of $n$. For fixed $n$, the leading term identifies the universal constant in the Mirzakhani--Zograf asymptotics as $1/\sqrtπ$, as conjectured by Zograf. We also answer two questions of Mirzakhani: we determine explicit asymptotic profiles for volume ratios uniformly in the number of cusps, and for adjacent coefficient ratios of the one-boundary volume polynomial uniformly over all degrees. The proof uses a positive recursion for mixed $κ_1$--$ψ$ intersection numbers, with the absolute normalization determined by comparison with the known asymptotics of pure $ψ$ intersection numbers.
Differential Geometry.comment: 75 pages, no figures. An earlier version was first made publicly available on Zenodo on 16 October 2026: https://zenodo.org/records/23414478

Differential Geometry.title: Log-Concavity and Fundamental Gaps on Complex Projective Domains
Differential Geometry.summary: We prove quantitative log-concavity and fundamental-gap estimates for Dirichlet Schrödinger operators on complex projective domains. With holomorphic sectional curvature four, the boundary condition $\mathrm{II}\ge\sqrt{44/5}\,g$ suffices in every complex dimension under $\operatorname{Hess} V\ge2|\nabla V|g$ and $\operatorname{osc}V\le4n$. It yields $\operatorname{Hess}(-\logφ_1)>g$ and $λ_2-λ_1>\max\{n+2+\sqrt{n^2+5n+11},\,2n+14/3\}$. The main difficulty is to control the distinguished Hopf direction together with a transverse Hessian block whose dimension grows with $n$. We extend modified-Hessian first-contact arguments by retaining the Hopf term and using longitudinal and transverse rotational tests. A trace minimization reduces all gradient orientations to three extreme directions. A dimension-scaled logarithmic barrier then compares their contact costs with a single limiting profile. A radial spectral estimate supplies the required quadratic-in-dimension spectral threshold from a dimension-independent boundary curvature bound. For $n\ge3$ these are, to our knowledge, the first log-concavity estimates for domains in $\mathbb{CP}^n$ without symmetry assumptions. We also prove a sharp diameter bound and Hessian levels linear in $n$ under larger dimension-free curvature bounds.

Differential Geometry.title: The quermassintegral inequalities for k-convex spiral-star-shaped domains
Differential Geometry.summary:
We extend the quermassintegral inequalities of our earlier work \cite{GuanLi2009} from star-shaped domains to a substantially broader class of domains in Euclidean space, which we call spiral-star-shaped. A smooth domain is spiral-star-shaped if its boundary satisfies \[
  \langle X+A X,ν\rangle>0 \] for some fixed skew-symmetric linear map $ A$, where $X$ is the position vector and $ν$ is the outward unit normal. The vector field $X+A X$ is conformal Killing, with dilation component $X$ and rotational component $A X$; its trajectories combine expansion and rotation, giving rise to the spiral terminology. When $A=0$, it reduces to ordinary star-shapedness, while nonzero $A$ allows domains that are not star-shaped in the usual radial sense.
  For smooth $k$-convex spiral-star-shaped domains, we prove long-time existence and exponential convergence to a round sphere for a locally constrained inverse curvature flow. The positive spiral support function provides the geometric control needed to treat initial hypersurfaces that need not be star-shaped in the usual sense. Monotonicity of the quermassintegrals along the flow yields sharp quermassintegral inequalities in this enlarged class, with equality if and only if the domain is a ball.

Differential Geometry.title: How to Untwist Twisted Gauge Fields
Differential Geometry.summary: This paper provides an isomorphism between the space of twisted gauge fields on a principal bundle $\mathcal{P}(M,H)$ and the space of standard gauge fields on a different principal bundle $\mathcal{Q}(M,G)$ associated to $\mathcal{P}$. This isomorphism extends to local fields on the base manifold, which enables the use of local twisted fields in standard gauge theories (e.g. Yang-Mills-like theories). This allows one to deal with two symmetry groups, coming from $\mathcal{P}$ and $\mathcal{Q}$, respectively. The construction makes use of a larger principal bundle $\mathcal{S}$ which has $\mathcal{P}$ and $\mathcal{Q}$ as quotient bundles. $\mathcal{S}$ is a Hilsum-Skandalis bibundle between the action groupoids $H\ltimes\mathcal{P}$ and $G\ltimes\mathcal{Q}$. The gauge structure on $\mathcal{S}$ encodes both standard and twisted gauge structures on $\mathcal{P}$. In addition, the isomorphism classes of bundles $\mathcal{S}$ up to an isomorphism covering the identity map on $\mathcal{P}$ are in 1:1 correspondence with the equivalence classes of cocycles (up to a coboundary). This paper also provides a new interpretation of (full) dressing fields as dynamic (or active) sections of a principal bundle.

Differential Geometry.title: Determinants of Dirichlet and Neumann Laplacians on Constant Curvature Surfaces with Geodesic Polygonal Boundary
Differential Geometry.summary: We express the zeta regularized determinants of the Dirichlet and Neumann Laplacians on compact Riemann surfaces with constant curvature metrics and geodesic polygonal boundary in terms of the Laplacian determinant on their closed conical doubles. The formulae apply without restrictions on the genus or number of boundary components. They involve explicit corner angle factors and a quotient of the Reidemeister and $L^2$ norms on the determinant line of cohomology. The proof combines a relative BFK gluing formula with the comparison theorem for analytic and combinatorial torsion on manifolds with boundary, due to Lück and Vishik. As an application, we give a rigorous proof of the Aurell-Salomonson formula for Euclidean polygons. We also obtain explicit determinants for spherical and hyperbolic triangles and certain other geodesic polygons from known formulae for their doubles.

Differential Geometry.title: Synthetic geometry of differential equations: I. Jets and comonad structure
Differential Geometry.summary: We give an abstract formulation of the formal theory partial differential equations (PDEs) in synthetic differential geometry, one that would seamlessly generalize the traditional theory to a range of enhanced contexts, such as super-geometry, higher (stacky) differential geometry, or even a combination of both. A motivation for such a level of generality is the eventual goal of solving the open problem of covariant geometric pre-quantization of locally variational field theories, which may include fermions and (higher) gauge fields. (abridged)
Differential Geometry.comment: 72 pages, xypic and tikzcd commutative diagrams; v2: minor technical revisions, close to published version

Differential Geometry.title: Biharmonic Conformal Immersions of Hypersurfaces: Dirac Rigidity and Mixed Clifford Geometry
Differential Geometry.summary:
A biharmonic conformal immersion asks whether a hypersurface can become a critical point of the bienergy after a conformal change of the domain metric. We study when this flexibility can produce compact nonconstant-mean-curvature geometry in space forms. For surfaces in three-dimensional space forms, with $U=λ^2H$, Ou's system is encoded exactly by a Laplace-type operator acting on a restricted ambient Killing spinor. We classify all monic scalar--chiral factorizations of this operator. In nonzero curvature such a factorization exists locally exactly when the principal curvatures are locally constant; the normalized Euclidean branch is equally rigid, and the remaining real spherical non-CMC branch is excluded by a finite-type Frobenius obstruction.
  For $m>2$, this scalar rigidity does not imply geometric nonexistence. The conformal tension has independent normal and tangential components. We prove that $\mathbb Rξ\oplus TM$ is the minimal natural $O(m)$-equivariant carrier, derive the corresponding strongly elliptic Jacobi block and its two-grade Clifford realization, and identify off-diagonal hybridization as the escape mechanism. Exact cohomogeneity-one reductions, combined with validated interval and Chebyshev/radii-polynomial arguments, yield embedded proper non-CMC, nowhere-umbilical examples in round spheres, including $$ S^1\times\mathbb S^n\times\mathbb S^n\hookrightarrow\mathbb S^{2n+2} \qquad(n\ge1). $$ Thus the scalar obstruction is sharp with respect to coefficient bundle: the smallest enlargement forced by conformal tension already supports compact non-CMC solutions.

Differential Geometry.title: Bach-flat metrics and global regularity of conformal structures
Differential Geometry.summary: We study global regularity properties of conformal structures on compact manifolds with applications to conformally invariant variational problems. We find sharp conditions ensuring that a manifold equipped with a Riemannian metric of Sobolev class is conformally diffeomorphic to a smooth one. In particular, we prove that $W^{2,q}$ Bach-flat four-manifolds with $q > 2$ are smooth up to conformal diffeomorphisms. We also solve the Yamabe problem for $W^{2,q}$ metrics with $q > 2$ on three-manifolds under a mild conformal condition.

Differential Geometry.title: General Relativity for Mathematicians - Part I
Differential Geometry.summary: These notes cover the first part of a course of the same title taught by Filippo Fila-Robattino and Manuel Tecchiolli at the University of Zurich in the Winter Semester of 2025. Topics include variational principles in classical mechanics, special relativity, smooth manifolds and tensor calculus, connections and curvature, geodesic motion, and the derivation of Einstein's equations from the Einstein-Hilbert action. The treatment is aimed at a mathematical audience, combining physical motivation with precise definitions, detailed proofs, and explicit calculations.

Differential Geometry.title: Gromov-Hausdorff instability of the positive mass theorem for Kähler manifolds
Differential Geometry.summary: We construct a sequence of AE Kähler metrics on $\mathbb{C}^2$ with nonnegative and integrable scalar curvature whose ADM mass tends to zero but which, for a suitable choice of basepoints, fails to converge to Euclidean space in the pointed Gromov-Hausdorff sense.
Differential Geometry.comment: 21 pages. v2: new title, abstract and AI statement

Differential Geometry.title: Singular Limits of Frame Bundles of Noncollapsing Positively Curved Manifolds
Differential Geometry.summary: For each dimension $n\ge 2$, we construct noncollapsing sequences of metrics on $S^n$ with a uniform positive lower bound on sectional curvature whose oriented orthonormal frame bundles, equipped with the canonically induced connection metrics, converge to nonmanifold metric spaces homeomorphic to $Σ(S^{n-1}\times\SO(n))$. In even dimensions, real projective quotients give connected full frame bundles with the same limits, disproving the manifold conclusion in Yamaguchi's frame bundle conjecture. In odd dimensions, each component of the full projective frame bundle, with its intrinsic metric, converges to the quotient of the spherical limit by a free involution. The singularities are detected by local homology, and we obtain quantitative equivariant Gromov--Hausdorff estimates. We also compare the frame bundle limits with the intrinsic completions of their regular limiting frame metrics, and present and discuss alternatives to Yamaguchi's original conjecture.

Differential Geometry.title: On the Dirichlet boundary value problem on Cartan-Hadamard manifolds
Differential Geometry.summary: We study bounded solutions of Dirichlet boundary value problems for semilinear elliptic equations on Cartan-Hadamard manifolds with pinched negative curvature. We prove nonexistence when the asymptotic boundary has zero Hausdorff measure at an exponent determined by the upper curvature bound and the spectral parameter. The result holds for continuous viscosity solutions under a one-sided bound on the nonlinearity, including the Allen-Cahn equation. The proof combines convex barriers at infinity, distance comparison for $C^{1,1}$ hypersurfaces and a spectral maximum principle. For surfaces, no lower curvature bound is needed.
Differential Geometry.comment: 31 pages, 8 figures. v2: revised version with stronger results

Differential Geometry.title: Type-II Singularities of Immersed Locally Convex Curves Evolving under Generalized Anisotropic Gage Area-Preserving Flows with Slow Curvature Speeds
Differential Geometry.summary: In this paper, we study the singularity behavior of immersed locally convex closed plane curves evolving under generalized anisotropic Gage area-preserving flows with slow curvature speeds of the form $κ_σ^α$, where $0<α\le 1$. Here $κ_σ$ denotes the anisotropic curvature associated with a prescribed anisotropy function $σ$. We prove that every finite-time blow-up is of Type-II provided that the Euclidean length of the evolving curve remains uniformly bounded away from zero. This result holds without any symmetry assumptions on either the initial curve or the anisotropy. When the initial signed area is nonzero, this length lower bound is automatically satisfied, and thus any finite-time singularity is necessarily of Type-II. By means of Hamilton's rescaling method combined with a differential Harnack estimate, we show that along a suitable blow-up subsequence, the rescaled curves at the selected times converge locally to the profile of a translating solution of the corresponding anisotropic curvature flow $V=κ_σ^α$. We also establish sufficient conditions for finite-time singularity formation in terms of the initial signed area and anisotropic length. Moreover, we construct locally convex initial curves arbitrarily close to the Wulff curve for which a finite-time Type-II singularity occurs.

Differential Geometry.title: The $C^0$-inextendibility of Kerr spacetimes
Differential Geometry.summary: We prove the $C^0$-inextendibility of the full Kerr realizations considered in this paper and all their connected covering spacetimes. The result holds for positive mass and nonzero rotation in the subextremal, extremal, and overextremal regimes. The obstruction at the singular ring is expressed by unbounded proper time in a fixed-endpoint causal homotopy class. It persists under every positive continuous conformal rescaling and under continuous widening of the Kerr causal cones, without any global causality assumption. We give sharp bounds in a fixed coordinate norm for stationary and axisymmetric perturbations and describe complete timelike geodesics that encounter arbitrarily large curvature near the ring.
Differential Geometry.comment: 78 pages, no figure. Comments are welcome

Differential Geometry.title: Genus Increase in Closed Mean Curvature Flows
Differential Geometry.summary: We construct counterexamples to Ilmanen's genus-reduction conjecture for closed mean curvature flows. We prove that a compact hypersurface with a single isolated conical singularity and a power rate of convergence to its cone admits a mean curvature flow whose forward rescaled limit is a prescribed expander smoothly asymptotic to that cone. Combining this theorem with closed mean curvature flows with prescribed tangent flows (arXiv:2405.15577, arXiv:2607.23879) and the noncompact counterexample (arXiv:2605.09657) gives the desired examples.

Differential Geometry.title: Aspherical Symplectic Manifolds with Positive First Chern Degree
Differential Geometry.summary: For every integer $n\ge5$, we construct a closed aspherical symplectic manifold of real dimension $2n$ with positive first Chern degree. Each example is a flat torus bundle over the same compact hyperbolic surface, with arithmetic monodromy arising from an explicit indefinite quaternion division algebra over $\mathbb{Q}$. We identify its symplectic first Chern class with the pullback of the canonical class of the base and compute its degree explicitly. Asphericity rules out nonconstant pseudoholomorphic spheres for every tame almost complex structure. Thus these examples give a negative answer to the symplectic uniruledness question of Boucksom--Demailly--Păun--Peternell in every even real dimension at least ten.

Differential Geometry.title: Prolongation rigidity of sub-free Lie algebras
Differential Geometry.summary: We prove that if the 0-th Tanaka prolongation $\mathfrak{g}_0=\mathfrak{der}_0(\mathfrak{m})$ of a fundamental graded nilpotent Lie algebra $\mathfrak{m}=\mathfrak{g}_{-s}\oplus\dots\oplus\mathfrak{g}_{-1}$ is irreducible on $\mathfrak{g}_{-1}$, then $\mathfrak{m}$ is prolongation rigid: $\text{pr}_+(\mathfrak{m})=0$. The only exceptions are given by negative gradations of maximal parabolic subalgebras of a simple Lie algebra.
Differential Geometry.comment: A few minor improvements and an acknowledgement added

Differential Geometry.title: Low Genus Curves on Compact Shimura Surfaces
Differential Geometry.summary: We investigate and compare the behaviors of complex curves on two major types of compact Shimura surfaces: compact variants of Picard and Hilbert modular surfaces. They are quotients of complex hyperbolic balls corresponding to moduli problems for abelian varieties with certain endomorphism types. We prove that if we fix a genus bound, then when the defining discriminant is large enough, low genus curves on the compact variant of Picard modular surfaces do not exist, while low genus curves may persist on the compact variant of Hilbert modular surfaces only if they are special curves, which parametrize those with extra endomorphisms. These results are special cases of a complex function field analogue of uniform boundedness on endomorphism types of abelian varieties. The proof requires understanding the repulsion of special subvarieties and relies on volume estimates in hyperbolic geometry.
Differential Geometry.comment: 48 pages. Major updates compared to the previous version: the case of compact variant of Hilbert modular surfaces is included and it shows different geometric patterns; many of the proofs are upgraded to a more general setting. I will upload a more polished version soon

Differential Geometry.title: Embedded minimal surfaces with three ends associated with the Hoffman-Osserman catenoids
Differential Geometry.summary: For every positive integer $g$ and every Hoffman-Osserman catenoid in $\mathbb{R}^5$, we construct a complete embedded minimal surface of genus $g$ that is not contained in any proper affine subspace of $\mathbb{R}^5$. These surfaces can be viewed as higher-codimensional analogues of the Costa-Hoffman-Meeks surfaces, associated with the union of the corresponding Hoffman-Osserman catenoid and the plane containing its waist circle. We provide explicit Weierstrass data for these surfaces. Our construction can also be interpreted as restoring conformality to a deformed Costa-Hoffman-Meeks immersion by introducing two additional harmonic coordinate functions.

Differential Geometry.title: Characterizations of the plane and the catenoid as capillary minimal surfaces
Differential Geometry.summary: In this paper, we prove that an immersed annular capillary minimal surface outside the unit ball in $\mathbb{R}^3$ with one complete embedded end and finite total curvature must be either part of the plane or part of the catenoid. The proofs are based on the use of the Weierstrass data through the Hopf differential and associated holomorphic functions. For a planar end, we control the second fundamental form, while for a catenoidal end, we analyze the Gauss map in more detail using the boundary condition. We also prove nonexistence results for annular free boundary minimal surfaces with one end asymptotic to the end of Enneper's surface, under appropriate conditions. Finally, we establish an exterior analogue of Choe's result on capillary minimal surfaces with vertices.
Differential Geometry.comment: 16 pages, 1 figure. In response to referee comments, an issue with a reference used in Theorem 1.1 has been corrected, and the proof has been revised accordingly. The statement of Theorem 1.2 has been revised to exclude certain boundary umbilic cases. This revision was posted as arXiv:2610.32447 by mistake. Withdrawal of that duplicate submission has been requested

Differential Geometry.title: A complete parameter classification of left-invariant Bott affine Ricci solitons for two rotated distributions on three-dimensional Lorentzian Lie groups
Differential Geometry.summary: We classify all left-invariant affine Ricci solitons associated with the Bott connections of two fixed rank-two distributions on the seven standard families of three-dimensional Lorentzian Lie groups. The distributions are defined by a fixed orthogonal change of the spacelike frame. A universal adapted-frame calculation provides explicit connection matrices, curvature operators and the symmetrized Ricci tensor. The equation in the orthogonal-complement direction forces every left-invariant solution to be steady. The remaining equations yield elementary parameter families and finitely many real algebraic branches: four normalized branches for $G_2$, six branches for each sign parameter in $G_4$, and two quartic branches in $G_7$ in addition to its elementary families. Resultants, subresultants, exact polynomial reduction and Sturm root isolation establish necessity, sufficiency and exhaustiveness. Degenerate cases are treated separately, including all families with nonunique soliton vector fields. An invertible frame transformation relates the two distribution problems. The classification is in the stated structure parameters; no quotient by isometries, automorphisms or scaling is taken.

Differential Geometry.title: Free maps in critical dimension on low-dimensional tori and closed surfaces
Differential Geometry.summary: We present a method to build free immersions in critical dimension on $m$-tori for $m = 2, 3, 4, 5$ by using a factorization trick inspired by tori immersions in critical dimension. As an application, we show that the set of smooth free maps from a closed surface $M$ to $\mathbb R^5$ is nonempty. In particular, every closed surface embeds freely in $\mathbb R^5$. Finally, we find the homotopy invariants of free maps in our environment and study which invariants are achieved by our maps.

Differential Geometry.title: Constant Chern holomorphic sectional curvature on two-step solvmanifolds
Differential Geometry.summary: Let $M=Γ\backslash G$ be a compact solvmanifold with a left-invariant Hermitian structure whose Lie algebra is two-step solvable. If the Chern holomorphic sectional curvature is constant, then the derived algebra is $J$-invariant and the Chern connection is flat. At the Lie-algebra level, we also prove that constant Chern holomorphic sectional curvature is impossible for a unimodular two-step solvable Hermitian Lie algebra of mixed Freibert-Swann type.

Differential Geometry.title: Failure of the local decay formula for Arnold multiplicities under twisted Kähler--Ricci flow
Differential Geometry.summary: Di Nezza--Guedj--Lu asked whether local Arnold multiplicities under maximal weak twisted Kähler--Ricci flow with fixed cohomology class satisfy $λ(\varphi_t,x)=\max\{λ(\varphi_0,x)-t,0\}$. We construct counterexamples with analytic initial singularities in every dimension $n\ge2$. On the Hirzebruch surface $\mathbb F_e$, $e\ge2$, the initial current $[S]+(e+1)[F]$ yields $λ(\varphi_t,x)=1/2-t/e$ for $x\in S\setminus F$ and $0<t<e/2$, where $S$ is the negative section and $F$ a fibre. Products with smooth stationary factors give higher-dimensional examples. The Zariski negative part of $\{S\}+\{F\}$, the reduced support class, forces extra divisor mass. For pure divisorial data with simple normal crossings support, a smooth semipositive representative of the reduced support class's positive part gives exact short-time formulas. On one surface we construct flows with identical initial current germs, background data and global initial Arnold multiplicity, but different local rates.

Differential Geometry.title: A characterization of Pfaffian embeddings from (2, 3, 5)- into flat (4, 7)-geometries
Differential Geometry.summary: Given two smooth manifolds with tangent subbundle distributions, an embedding is Pfaffian if its differential sends the distribution on the source into the distribution on the target. In this paper, we consider the question of existence of Pfaffian embeddings in the specific case where the source is a (2,3,5)-manifold, the target is the 7-dimensional space of isotropic 2-planes in a 6-dimensional symplectic vector space, and the Pfaffian condition is that the derived 3-distribution on the source be mapped into the natural 4-distribution on the target. This is one of the simpler non-trivial cases of the general question on existence of Pfaffian embeddings, but already the answer here requires solution of an interesting differential equation. It turns out that a generic (2,3,5)-manifold does not embed, the first obstruction being the fact that a Pfaffian embeddable (2,3,5)-manifold necessarily has a double root for its Cartan quartic at each point. We determine a complete characterization of embeddable (2,3,5)-manifolds in terms of their associated Cartan geometries, which characterization depends on higher order (non-harmonic) curvature as well.

Differential Geometry.title: Chern holonomy under the first and second Chern--Ricci flows
Differential Geometry.summary: We compare the Chern holonomy of the first and second Chern-Ricci flows on compact complex manifolds. For the first flow, we construct an explicit immortal pluriclosed solution on a complex two-torus with full and restricted holonomy $U(2)$, except at one finite time when both groups are $U(1)^2$; its smooth limit has holonomy $SU(2)$. The solution is uniformly nondegenerate and has bounds of every fixed differential order for all time. In contrast, the second Chern-Ricci flow preserves full and restricted Chern holonomy under the natural unitary identification, including the initial time and nonclosed groups. The proof combines preservation of a connection reduction, positive-time analyticity, and a path-transport comparison. As an application, the optimal minimum mean curvature on a holomorphic bundle is unchanged when metrics are restricted to any realizable full and restricted holonomy class. An explicit projected-curvature source explains the failure of the corresponding Ricci-flow holonomy argument.

Differential Geometry.title: Curvature of left-invariant complex Finsler metric on Lie groups
Differential Geometry.summary: Let $G$ be an even-dimensional connected real Lie group admitting a left-invariant complex structure $J$. Let $\mathfrak g$ be the Lie algebra of $G$, and $\mathfrak g^{1,0}$ the $(1,0)$-part of the complexification $\mathfrak g^{\mathbb{C}}$ of $\mathfrak g$. We derive explicit formulas for the holomorphic sectional curvature and holomorphic bisectional curvature of any left-invariant strongly pseudoconvex complex Finsler metric $F$ on $G$, expressed in terms of the complex Lie algebra $\mathfrak g^{1,0}$. We also obtain a necessary and sufficient condition for $F$ to be a Kähler-Finsler metric (resp. weakly Kähler-Finsler metric). As an application, we prove a rigidity result: if $G$ is a complex Lie group and $F$ is a left-invariant strongly pseudoconvex complex Finsler metric on $G$, then $F$ must be a complex Berwald metric with vanishing holomorphic bisectional curvature; moreover, $F$ is a Kähler-Berwald metric if and only if $G$ is an abelian complex Lie group.

Differential Geometry.title: The inverse Monge--Ampère flow on klt Fano varieties
Differential Geometry.summary: We establish the long time existence of the inverse Monge--Ampère flow on a klt $\mathbb{Q}$-Fano variety $X$. We further prove that $X$ admits a Kähler--Einstein metric if and only if the flow converges in $L^1$.

Differential Geometry.title: A convexity theorem for proper Dupin hypersurfaces in spheres
Differential Geometry.summary: We prove that if $M$ is a (compact, connected, and embedded) proper Dupin hypersurface in a sphere then, viewing $M$ as a submanifold of the ambient Euclidean space, its orthogonal projection to the normal space at any point is convex. This is a generalization of the convexity theorem of Terng for isoparametric submanifolds in Euclidean spaces.

Differential Geometry.title: Variations of the harmonic entropy and linear drift on negatively curved surfaces
Differential Geometry.summary: For closed negatively curved surfaces, we obtain formulas for the derivatives of the harmonic entropy of its geodesic flow and the linear drift of its Brownian motion along conformal deformations. We deduce that the harmonic entropy of the geodesic flow of a closed surface of non-constant negative curvature (resp. linear drift of the Brownian motion on its universal cover) is strictly decreasing (resp. increasing) along the normalized Ricci flow. We also prove that any hyperbolic metric on a surface admits a neighborhood in the space of conformal negatively curved metrics in which the linear drift is greater or equal to the Liouville entropy, with equality if and only if the metric is hyperbolic.

Differential Geometry.title: Continuum-wise hyperbolicity is exactly the pseudo-Anosov dynamics with spine singularities
Differential Geometry.summary: We establish a complete structural classification for cw$_F$-hyperbolic surface homeomorphisms. Specifically, we prove that a surface homeomorphism is cw$_F$-hyperbolic if, and only if, it is a pseudo-Anosov homeomorphism whose singularities consist exclusively of spines (1-prongs). Furthermore, we classify these systems up to topological conjugacy, showing that every such homeomorphism is conjugate to either an Anosov automorphism on the torus $\mathbb{T}^2$ or to a standard hyperelliptic quotient on $\mathbb{S}^2$ of a hyperbolic affine toral map. As a rigid consequence of this classification, we show that such dynamics are strictly obstructed on surfaces of genus greater than one, the Klein bottle, and the projective plane.

Differential Geometry.title: CMC foliations on Euclidean spaces are minimal foliations
Differential Geometry.summary: In this article, we provide a complete answer to one of the most classical conjectures in differential geometry (of foliations). More precisely, we present a complete positive answer to the classical conjecture, due to Meeks III, Pérez, and Ros (2008), that states that every foliation on $\mathbb{R}^{n+1}$ by (possibly varying) CMC hypersurfaces is a foliation by minimal hypersurfaces. Moreover, if $n\leq 6$, such a CMC foliation must consist of parallel hyperplanes.

Differential Geometry.title: Contact topology and intrinsic characterization of transversely vanishing curl eigenforms
Differential Geometry.summary: We study the geometry and topology of transversely vanishing eigenforms of the curl operator on $3$-manifolds, placing them in the broader framework of near-contact forms. We prove a Gray-type stability theorem for the kernels of near-contact forms, which we call near-contact structures, and derive a local neighborhood theorem around their singularities. As applications, we obtain a stability result for the contact topology of curl eigenforms, a classification of near-contact structures in terms of formal homotopical data, and a proof of the existence of contact structures on closed orientable 3-manifolds based on the spectral theory of the curl operator. We also study the symplectization of curl eigenforms as a possible bridge to symplectic dynamics. Finally, we characterize those transversely vanishing $1$-forms which are curl eigenforms for some smooth Riemannian metric. We deduce a generalization of the classical correspondence, due to Etnyre and Ghrist, between Reeb-like fields of contact forms and nowhere-vanishing rotational Beltrami fields to the setting of transversely vanishing vector fields.

Differential Geometry.title: $L^p$ Convergence of AMV Laplacians on completions of Riemannian manifolds
Differential Geometry.summary: We study conditions for the $L^p$ convergence of the AMV Laplacian $Δ_r$ on completions of Riemannian manifolds $(M,g)$. The condition invloves the Minkowski dimension of the set $\overline{M} \setminus M$ and how much the curvature is blowing up around $S$. We build a concrete family of sets that satisfies these conditions, and provide an example of non convergence when these conditions are not met.

Differential Geometry.title: Total curvature of convex hypersurfaces in Cartan-Hadamard manifolds
Differential Geometry.summary: We show that if the curvature of a Cartan-Hadamard $n$-manifold is constant near a convex hypersurface $Γ$, then the total Gauss-Kronecker curvature $\mathcal{G}(Γ)$ is not less than that of any convex hypersurface nested inside $Γ$. This extends Borbély's monotonicity theorem in hyperbolic space. It follows that $\mathcal{G}(Γ)$ is bounded below by the volume of the unit sphere in Euclidean space $\mathbf{R}^n$. If $n=3$ or $Γ$ is $\mathcal{C}^{1,1}$, it suffices that the curvature be constant on $Γ$.
Differential Geometry.comment: 8 pages; Improvements to the main result

Differential Geometry.title: Quantitative stability and strict inequalities for the Escobar functional
Differential Geometry.summary: For Euclidean domains whose boundaries are sufficiently close to a sphere in $C^2$, we bound the deficit of the Escobar constant from below by the squared $H^{3/2}$ norm of the boundary graph, after fixing its constant and first spherical harmonics. This holds in every dimension $n\ge3$ and implies a bound in Fraenkel asymmetry with optimal quadratic power. Under fixed $C^{6,α}$ and size bounds, the asymmetry estimate also holds for star-shaped domains in dimensions $n\ge6$. For compact Riemannian manifolds with minimal boundary and uniform geometric bounds, we prove $S_\ast-C^*_{\text{Esc}}(M,g)\ge ca^4/\log(Λ/a)$ in dimension six and $S_\ast-C^*_{\text{Esc}}(M,g)\ge ca^4$ in higher dimensions, where $a=\|\mathring{\mathrm{II}}\|_{L^\infty}>0$. A family satisfying the same bounds has deficit comparable to $a^{8/3}$, excluding uniform lower bounds with smaller powers. We also compute the cubic coefficient of the standard boundary bubble quotient and give uniform remainder estimates.
Differential Geometry.comment: 52 pages. Split from arXiv:2601.22665v2 (Part 1/3), with new results on the geometric stability of the Escobar functional. Other parts forthcoming. Comments welcome!

Differential Geometry.title: Spectral $Γ_2$ inequalities for the $V$-Laplacian with evolving weighted measures
Differential Geometry.summary: In this paper, we establish spectral Bakry-Émery $Γ_2$ criteria and their modified counterparts for the $V$-Laplacian on closed Riemannian manifolds equipped with evolving weighted measures. The estimates yield jointly optimized spectral bounds and sharp endpoint constants. When the measures evolve according to the Fokker-Planck equation, these estimates yield monotonicity formulas for the Fisher information associated with Shannon and Tsallis entropies, together with quantitative propagation of Poincaré, logarithmic Sobolev, and nonlinear interpolation inequalities. In the stationary reversible setting, our results specialize to the Witten Laplacian and recover the unweighted Cai-Wang estimates \cite{Cai}.

Differential Geometry.title: Characterizations of the plane and the catenoid as capillary minimal surfaces
Differential Geometry.summary: In this paper, we prove that an annular capillary minimal surface outside the unit ball in $\mathbb{R}^3$ with one complete embedded end and finite total curvature must be either part of the plane or part of the catenoid. The proofs are based on the use of the Weierstrass data through the Hopf differential and associated holomorphic functions. For a planar end, we control the second fundamental form, while for a catenoidal end, we analyze the Gauss map in more detail using the boundary condition. We also prove nonexistence results for annular free boundary minimal surfaces with one end asymptotic to the end of Enneper's surface, under appropriate conditions. Finally, we establish an exterior analogue of Choe's result on capillary minimal surfaces with vertices.
Differential Geometry.comment: This submission is withdrawn because it was posted as a new submission rather than as a replacement of arXiv:1905.07887. The revised manuscript will appear at arXiv:1905.07887

Differential Geometry.title: A Sharp Regularity Threshold for Uniqueness in Riemannian Calderón-type Problems
Differential Geometry.summary: We prove a sharp regularity threshold for uniqueness in two anisotropic Calderón-type inverse problems in dimension $n\ge 3$. The main setting is the Riemannian Schrödinger problem with fixed scalar potential: for a prescribed nonconstant analytic function $V$, we study whether the Dirichlet-to-Neumann map of $-Δ_g+V$ on a domain $Ω\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ determines the unknown metric $g$. The natural gauge is the group of boundary-fixing diffeomorphisms preserving $V$. We show that, while analytic metrics are uniquely determined modulo this gauge by a minor adaptation of the Lassas--Uhlmann reconstruction theorem, uniqueness fails densely in every non-analytic Gevrey class $G^σ$, $σ>1$. In fact, our counterexamples are not isometric in the sense that they are not connected by the pushforward of any diffeomorphism of $\overlineΩ$. We also prove the analogous sharp threshold for the anisotropic Calderón problem at fixed nonzero frequency, thereby upgrading the previously known finite-regularity counterexamples to Gevrey and $C^\infty$ regularity. The two constructions use different scalar mechanisms: for fixed potentials, the nonconstant potential itself provides a local coordinate, while at nonzero frequency one uses a compactly supported prescribed-Jacobian lemma in Gevrey spaces. Thus analyticity is the exact threshold for uniqueness in both problems.
Differential Geometry.comment: Nonuniqueness results (in the smooth and Gevray category) are correct. Uniqueness in the analytic category is not. Details will be provided elsewhere

Geometric Topology.title: The Weyl Problem for Planar CBB$(-1)$ Surfaces in Hyperbolic $3$-Space
Geometric Topology.summary: In this paper, we study the Weyl problem for noncompact convex surfaces in hyperbolic $3$-space $\mathbb{H}^3$. We prove that any planar CBB$(-1)$ surface with countably many ends can be isometrically embedded as the boundary of a closed convex subset $X\subset\mathbb{H}^3$ such that each connected component of the ideal boundary of $X$ is either a round disk or a single point. By known rigidity results, such an embedding is unique up to isometries of $\mathbb{H}^3$. Moreover, we show that the assumption of countably many ends can be dropped if Koebe's circle domain conjecture holds.

Geometric Topology.title: Robert J. Daverman (1941-2026)
Geometric Topology.summary: This is an expanded version of a memorial article that is to appear in the Notices of the American Mathematical Society.
Geometric Topology.comment: This is a small revision of the expanded version of a memorial article that is to appear in the Notices of the American Mathematical Society. (with appendices by John Ewing and Dusan Repovs)

Geometric Topology.title: Classifying Leibniz racks
Geometric Topology.summary: Lie quandles were defined by T. Fritz as a nonlinear generalization of Lie algebras, to serve as a nonlinear algebras of observables in generalized form of Hamiltonian mechanics. These objects were subsequently generalized in a prequel article to objects referred to as smooth Lie group families of smooth racks by the authors. In this article, we investigate a particular system of nonlinear functional differential equations whose solution in general provides a pathway to the classification of smooth Lie group families of smooth rack structures on any given smooth manifold. We then discuss a particularly practical ansatz for solving these equations, and use it to construct new families of examples, as well as prove a result on the sense in which the Bloch sphere is the unique Lie quandle structure on the sphere.

Geometric Topology.title: The Smoothability of Embedded Surfaces in 4-Manifolds Under Stabilizations
Geometric Topology.summary: We study the smooth stabilization number of a locally flat embedded surface in a smooth $4$-manifold, defined as the minimum number of connected sums with $S^2\times S^2$ needed to make the surface topologically isotopic to a smooth embedding. We prove that a nonsmoothable locally flat surface in a closed, simply connected smooth $4$-manifold becomes smoothable after a single stabilization if its homology class is primitive and noncharacteristic and its complement has abelian fundamental group. This yields infinitely many examples of nonsmoothable surfaces with smooth stabilization number one. We also exhibit examples for which a single stabilization produces infinitely many pairwise smoothly nonisotopic representatives in the same topological isotopy class. In contrast, we construct a locally flat genus-eight surface representing $6h$ in $\mathbb{CP}^2$ whose smooth stabilization number is exactly two. More generally, we show that smooth stabilization numbers of locally flat embedded surfaces in $\mathbb{CP}^2$ are unbounded.
Geometric Topology.comment: One section is added on nonsmoothable surfaces whose smooth stabilization number is 2. 13 page, 1 figure

Geometric Topology.title: Knot Floer complexes of generalized L-space knots
Geometric Topology.summary: In this paper, we study height 4 knots, which generalize L-space knots and almost L-space knots studied by Ozsváth--Szabó, Baldwin--Sivek, and Binns. A knot $K\subset S^3$ is called a height $m$ knot if $\operatorname{rank} \widehat{HF}(S^3_n(K))-n=m$ for all integers $n\geq 2g(K)-1$, where $\widehat{HF}$ is the hat version of Heegaard Floer homology introduced by Ozsváth--Szabó. In particular, height 0 and height 2 knots are exactly L-space knots and almost L-space knots, respectively. We prove that the knot Floer complex $CFK^\infty(S^3,K)$ of a height 4 knot $K$ admits a basis that is horizontally and vertically simplified--an hv-basis for short. Moreover, we show that under such an hv-basis, the horizontal and vertical differentials fall into six cases, generalizing the results for L-space knots and almost L-space knots. The hv-basis of the knot Floer complex of $K$ can determine, via an explicit algorithm, the immersed curve of Hanselman-Rasmussen-Watson for the knot complement of $K$. Consequently, our results facilitate further exploration of computations of $\widehat{HF}$ for the gluing of two height 4 knot complements.
Geometric Topology.comment: 89 pages, 122 figures, 26 tables. Most figures depict subquotient complexes by displaying their generators and differentials

Geometric Topology.title: The flipping principle for boundedly acyclic covers and colorings
Geometric Topology.summary: Based on the theory of multicomplexes and other ideas by Gromov, we describe the flipping principle. This is an easy geometric criterion that forces the vanishing of the Gromov norm of homology classes. We use it to provide proofs based on a common geometric principle of the Vanishing Theorem and the Amenable Reduction Lemma by Gromov in the case of amenable and boundedly acyclic covers and colorings. We also strengthen the conclusion of the Amenable Reduction Lemma by showing that it implies the $\ell^1$-invisibility of the homology classes and not only the vanishing of their Gromov norm.

Geometric Topology.title: Non-discrete complex hyperbolic $(p_1,p_2,p_3;p_4)$-triangle groups
Geometric Topology.summary: In this paper, we study complex hyperbolic triangle groups of type $(p_1,p_2,p_3;p_4)$ with $3\le p_1\le p_2\le p_3\le p_4\le \infty$. We show that if the element $R_1R_2R_3$ is elliptic, then the group is either non-discrete or it belongs to a short list of known discrete groups.

Geometric Topology.title: On a family of stably handle-slide trivial R-links
Geometric Topology.summary: An R-link is an n-component link L in S^3 such that Dehn surgery on L yields #^nS1 \times S2. Adapting work of Gompf, Scharlemann and Thompson, Meier and Zupan produced a family of R-links L(p, q; c/d), where the pairs (p, q) and (c, d) are relatively prime and c is even. For most of link in this family, whether it is handle-slide trivial remains open. In this work, we show one subfamily, L(3, 2; 4/d), are stably handle-slide trivial for all d.

Geometric Topology.title: Aspherical Symplectic Manifolds with Positive First Chern Degree
Geometric Topology.summary: For every integer $n\ge5$, we construct a closed aspherical symplectic manifold of real dimension $2n$ with positive first Chern degree. Each example is a flat torus bundle over the same compact hyperbolic surface, with arithmetic monodromy arising from an explicit indefinite quaternion division algebra over $\mathbb{Q}$. We identify its symplectic first Chern class with the pullback of the canonical class of the base and compute its degree explicitly. Asphericity rules out nonconstant pseudoholomorphic spheres for every tame almost complex structure. Thus these examples give a negative answer to the symplectic uniruledness question of Boucksom--Demailly--Păun--Peternell in every even real dimension at least ten.

Geometric Topology.title: Handle decompositions and Kirby diagrams for the complement of plane algebraic curves
Geometric Topology.summary: The complement of plane algebraic curves are well studied from topological and algebro-geometric viewpoints. In this paper, we will describe the explicit handle decompositions and the Kirby diagrams for the complement of plane algebraic curves. The method is based on the notion of braid monodromy. We refined this technique to obtain handle decompositions and Kirby diagrams.

Geometric Topology.title: Free maps in critical dimension on low-dimensional tori and closed surfaces
Geometric Topology.summary: We present a method to build free immersions in critical dimension on $m$-tori for $m = 2, 3, 4, 5$ by using a factorization trick inspired by tori immersions in critical dimension. As an application, we show that the set of smooth free maps from a closed surface $M$ to $\mathbb R^5$ is nonempty. In particular, every closed surface embeds freely in $\mathbb R^5$. Finally, we find the homotopy invariants of free maps in our environment and study which invariants are achieved by our maps.

Geometric Topology.title: A lifting defect for oriented $t_3$ and $\bar t_6$ moves
Geometric Topology.summary: We study oriented $t_3$- and $\bar t_6$-moves through the problem of lifting Fox $3$-colorings to colorings by a nine-element Alexander quandle. We define a nonnegative integer lifting defect $δ$ for oriented links and prove that it is invariant under these moves. For knots, the defect equals the rank of an alternating bilinear form obtained from a Seifert matrix, so it is even. We also prove that it is additive under connected sum. Let $K_s$ be the connected sum of $s\geq 1$ copies of $9_{46}$. Then $δ(K_s)=2s$, so these knots represent infinitely many distinct equivalence classes under the oriented moves, and none is equivalent to an unlink. After forgetting orientation, each $K_s$ can be transformed into an unlink with $2s+1$ components by $3s$ ordinary $3$-moves.

Geometric Topology.title: The Alexander polynomial of twisted torus knots in the complementary range
Geometric Topology.summary: A twisted torus knot T(p,q;r,s) is obtained from the flat-torus diagram of T(p,q) by inserting s full twists along a disk meeting r adjacent strands. Our previous work determined its Alexander polynomial for 1<r<=max{|p|,|q|}. In this paper, we compute it in the complementary range max{|p|,|q|}<r<=|p|+|q| by placing the knot on a standard genus-two Heegaard surface and applying Fox calculus. We then combine the two calculations into a unified Alexander-polynomial formula valid for 1<r<=|p|+|q|. In the complementary range, we prove monicity and give an explicit formula for the breadth. This determines the Seifert genus for nonnegative twists and gives a genus lower bound for negative twists. We also exhibit infinite two-parameter families of non-L-space knots in the complementary range.
Geometric Topology.comment: 21 pages, 4 figures. Comments and suggestions are welcome

Geometric Topology.title: Floer lasagna modules for some 2-handlebodies
Geometric Topology.summary:
Morrison, Walker and Wedrich used Khovanov homology to define the skein lasagna module for a 4-manifold with a link in its boundary. The skein lasagna module was shown to be a deep and powerful invariant; in particular, Ren and Willis proved that it detects exotic smooth structures. Still, computing the skein lasagna module outside some carefully chosen grading range remains an important open problem.
  Motivated by this construction, Chen defined the Floer lasagna module using Heegaard Floer link homology. In this paper, we give a complete, but partially conjectural description of Floer lasagna modules for a class of 4-manifolds obtained by adding 2-handles along plumbed L-space knots (with certain framing constraints).
  In particular, we prove that for $\overline{\mathbb{CP}^2}$ it is infinite-dimensional, and conjecture that for $\mathbb{CP}^2$ it is infinite-dimensional as well. We compute this module for $\overline{\mathbb{CP}^2}$ (and conjecturally for $\mathbb{CP}^2$) in all Alexander and Maslov gradings. This strengthens and extends the recent results of McCulloch.

Geometric Topology.title: Positivity of simplicial volume and uniqueness for the twelve-vertex flag three-spheres
Geometric Topology.summary: We study the twelve-vertex flag triangulation $T_{12}$ of $S^3$ and the Davis $4$-manifold $M(T_{12})$ associated with it. We prove that $T_{12}$ is, up to isomorphism, the unique flag triangulation of $S^3$ with twelve vertices in which every edge is contained in a square; this proves Milizia's Conjecture~6.31. We also prove a general criterion for the tangent Euler class of a Davis $4$-manifold to be bounded, and we verify it for $T_{12}$ by means of an explicit symmetric form. Since the Euler class takes the value $256$ on the fundamental class of $M(T_{12})$, the duality between bounded cohomology and simplicial volume gives $\|M(T_{12})\|>0$. This answers Milizia's Question~1.7.

Geometric Topology.title: On smooth and bundle structures on topological manifolds homotopy equivalent to $S^{4k-1}$-bundles over $S^{4k}$
Geometric Topology.summary: We first verify the expected calculations of the topological structure set, in the sense of surgery theory, for the total spaces of $S^{4k-1}$-bundles over $S^{4k}$ for $k\ge3$, in which manifolds homotopy equivalent to the total spaces are organized. Next, we investigate the question of which of the elements in these structure sets can be realized as such bundles. Moreover, we study the forgetful map from the smooth version to the topological version of the structure set; we determine its image. All elements in the image turn out to have the underlying manifold such a bundle.

Geometric Topology.title: Plane separating continua inscribe rectangles
Geometric Topology.summary: We prove the following: If $X$ is a plane separating continuum, then every embedding of $X$ into $\mathbb{R}^2$ contains the vertices of a Euclidean rectangle. We arrive to this result by extending a known result by H. Vaughan for Jordan curves to a wider class of topological objects via shape theory and Steenrod homology.

Geometric Topology.title: Homological lifts of Arnold strangeness
Geometric Topology.summary: We construct homological lifts of Arnold's strangeness $\operatorname{St}$ for long and closed plane curves. For long curves, we introduce a new $q$-variable quantization polynomial $\operatorname{St}_q$, an edge state sum, designed for categorification and construct a triply graded homology that recovers $\operatorname{St}_q$. We prove strictness by exhibiting long curves with the same number of crossings and the same $\operatorname{St}_q$ (in particular, the same rotation number and $\operatorname{St}$) that are distinguished by the homology. For closed curves, we introduce a corresponding new polynomial $\operatorname{St}_q$ and construct an edge homology. In this case $\operatorname{St}_q$ is recovered from a signed $q$-character $\operatorname{ch}_q$ defined on the canonical cycles of the homology rather than directly from a graded rank. Again, we exhibit closed curves with the same number of crossings and the same $\operatorname{St}_q$ (in particular, the same rotation number and $\operatorname{St}$) that are distinguished by the homology.

Geometric Topology.title: The unknotting problem for surfaces in the 4-sphere
Geometric Topology.summary: We show that there is no algorithm to decide whether or not a closed, connected, orientable, locally flat PL surface in $S^4$ of genus at least 18 (resp. 19) is TOP (resp. PL) unknotted. We prove analogous results for non-orientable surfaces, and for surfaces in any compact PL 4-manifold. We also show that there is an orientable surface in $S^4$ of genus 18 whose group has unsolvable word problem, and an orientable surface in $S^4$ of genus 40 whose group contains an isomorphic copy of every recursively presented group. Similar results hold for non-orientable surfaces.

Geometric Topology.title: Filling knots and essential geodesic systole
Geometric Topology.summary: We prove that every closed, orientable $3$--manifold contains hyperbolic knots with arbitrarily large essential geodesic systole. That is, for any $3$--manifold $M$, and $R> 0$ there is a hyperbolic knot $K \subset M$ such that every closed geodesic in the knot complement which is non-null-homotopic in $M$ has length at least $R$. The construction also produces filling knots, in the sense of Freedman-Krushkal [FreeKrus2023]. This answers two questions of Biringer.
Geometric Topology.comment: 28 pages, 8 figures, comments welcome. No AI use

Geometric Topology.title: Recognizing convergence actions as proper isometric actions on hyperbolic spaces
Geometric Topology.summary: Relying merely on B.I. (a.k.a. Bowditch's intelligence), we show that whenever a group $G$ admits a convergence action on a compact perfect metrizable space $M$, there is a hyperbolic space $X$ along with a proper isometric action of $G$ on $X$ inducing a $G$-equivariant homeomorphism $f:M \rightarrow \partial X.$ This answers a question by Misha Kapovich.

Geometric Topology.title: Filling Links and Essential Systole
Geometric Topology.summary: We answer a question of Freedman and Krushkal, producing filling links in any closed, orientable 3-manifold. The links we construct are hyperbolic, and have large essential systole, contrasting earlier geometric constraints on hyperbolic links in 3-manifolds due to Adams-Reid and Lakeland-Leininger.
Geometric Topology.comment: Paper is more clear now thanks to referee comments; the proofs are largely unchanged. No AI use. To appear in Comment. Math. Helv

Geometric Topology.title: Counting Markov triples and simple geodesics
Geometric Topology.summary: We give an asymptotic formula for the number of Markov triples with largest entry below $x$. We show that the error term is $o(\log x)$, which improves upon the previous best known results due to McShane and Rivin. We give an explicit error based on classical zero-free regions of the Riemann zeta function, and a sharper estimate under the quasi-Riemann hypothesis. The proof uses the correspondence between Markov triples and simple closed geodesics on the modular punctured torus and a careful analysis of the McShane-Rivin unit ball.

Optimization and Control.title: Optimal tradeoffs between variance and sensitivity, via Hellinger-Kantorovich geometry
