Systems and Control.title: VLN on the Fly: An Onboard Vision-Language Navigation Stack for Aerial Robots
Systems and Control.summary: Running vision-language navigation fully onboard an aerial robot is hard, since grounding, planning, and control must share limited compute and a single-stage error is difficult to isolate in flight. End-to-end aerial policies fuse these stages into one network, giving up the observability and safety checks a modular stack keeps available. We propose VLN on the Fly, an onboard stack that keeps grounding, planning, and control as separate, inspectable stages. A quantized VLM grounds an instruction to a coarse image cell, depth lifts it to a 3D goal, a fast B-spline planner returns a feasible trajectory, and a pretrained reinforcement learning policy tracks it to motor commands across quadrotors. Across 15 onboard flights over three everyday referents in a controlled indoor volume, the stack reaches the target in 13 of 15 trials with 5.72 cm mean goal error and 39.3% average GPU utilization. In 6 additional cluttered-environment trials, the stack tracks collision-free trajectories under onboard perception gating.

Information Theory.title: Dynamics-Aware Sampling and Recovery for Tensor-Valued Dynamical Systems
Information Theory.summary:
We study sampling and recovery for tensor-valued dynamical systems evolving under the t-product, using partial spatial observations over time. Although the t-product Fourier transform yields slicewise matrix dynamics, recovery does not generally decouple across slices. Eigenvalues shared across Fourier-domain frontal slices couple the corresponding eigenspaces into aggregated spectral blocks, which determine the tensor-specific recovery geometry and space--time tradeoff.
  We establish deterministic identifiability conditions for the initial tensor state. In the diagonalizable case, these are frame conditions on the aggregated blocks. We extend them to non-diagonalizable systems through generalized eigenspaces and Jordan structure. A temporal--spectral factorization of the finite-horizon stacked recovery system underlying Tensor Dynamical Sampling (DS) yields a decoupled two-stage formulation once the temporal threshold is reached. Under independent spatial subsampling, we prove high-probability recovery guarantees using empirical Gram matrices on the aggregated blocks. The bounds depend on aggregated multiplicities, incoherence, and population conditioning. Stability estimates separate the spatial frame factor from the temporal Vandermonde factor and show that increasing temporal depth may worsen numerical conditioning even after identifiability is ensured.
  We implement Tensor DS and evaluate it on synthetic and real data. Phase transitions track the predicted blockwise sampling thresholds, and stability experiments illustrate Vandermonde conditioning. Experiments on sea surface temperature and turbulence velocity data show that a learned t-product system operator generally yields more accurate and structurally faithful reconstructions than vectorized low-rank, Tucker-type, graph-regularized, graph-spectral, and vectorized dynamical sampling baselines.

Information Theory.title: Binary Cyclic Gradient Coding: Exact Recovery and Robustness to Compression
Information Theory.summary: We introduce binary cyclic gradient coding (BCGC), an exact gradient coding scheme for $n$ workers and up to $s$ stragglers. Its encoding matrix is binary, circulant when $(s+1)\mid n$ and nearly circulant otherwise, and the master decodes by a single summation. Like the fractional repetition coding scheme (FRC) and its generalized version (GFRC), BCGC splits the workers into $s+1$ classes that each cover the whole dataset, but it assigns the data through cyclic supports. Its encoding matrix has rank $n-s$, and $n-s-1$ workers keep the balanced load $s+1$, which is the largest possible number. We prove that encoding matrix of BCGC is not permutation-equivalent to those of FRC and GFRC schemes. Moreover, We also prove that a binary coded scheme with compression is equivalent to an uncoded compressed scheme on a coarser partition of the data. This explains why binary schemes remain stable under compression, whereas the large decoding coefficients of MDS codes amplify the compression error and lead to divergence in our experiments. For every contractive compressor, the standard convergence guarantee of compressed gradient descent holds on each coarse partition. FRC, GFRC and BCGC therefore share the same convergence guarantee and differ only in their partitions, with one partition for FRC, two for GFRC and $s+1$ distinct partitions for BCGC. Choosing among these partitions can recover the exact gradient in cases where FRC and GFRC cannot. Experiments on four datasets confirm the theory. BCGC matches GFRC, keeps its accuracy under top $κ$ sparsification while the MDS codes diverge, and on heterogeneous data its partition diversity reduces the compression error and improves the accuracy.

Information Theory.title: Zero-knowledge and Quantum CSS Codes Are Equivalent
Information Theory.summary: Zero-knowledge codes, introduced by Decatur, Goldreich, and Ron (ePrint 1997), are error-correcting codes in which few codeword symbols reveal no information about the encoded message, and have been extensively used in cryptographic constructions. Quantum CSS codes, introduced by Calderbank and Shor (Phys. Rev. A 1996) and Steane (Royal Society A 1996), are error-correcting codes that allow for quantum error correction, and are also useful for applications in quantum complexity theory. In this short note, we show that (linear, perfect) zero-knowledge codes and quantum CSS codes are equivalent. We demonstrate the potential of this equivalence by using it to obtain explicit asymptotically-good zero-knowledge locally-testable codes.
Information Theory.comment: Instantiated transformation with latest LTC constructions

Information Theory.title: Multi-view Semantic-aware Resource Allocation for Edge AI
Information Theory.summary: Semantic communication is emerging as a pivotal paradigm to overcome wireless resource scarcity in 6G networks. This paper proposes a novel end-to-end framework for semantics-aware resource allocation in multi-user Edge AI. We extend the Opportunistic Information Bottleneck (OIB) to a multi-view setting, termed the Multi-view Gaussian Information Bottleneck (MGIB), by fusing complementary source views without variational approximation or network retraining. A resource allocation framework is then formulated for joint compression-level selection, transmission mode selection (i.e., the number of active sources per group), and PRB assignment. The problem is formulated as a Mixed-Integer Linear Program (MILP), solved efficiently via a proposed Lagrangian Relaxation (LR) algorithm, and benchmarked against the NP-hard optimal solution. Simulations demonstrate that the proposed LR scheme achieves near-optimal utility, and doubles PRB efficiency versus average allocation.
Information Theory.comment: Submitted to IEEE Wireless Communications Letters. Jiawei Luo and Hussein Saleh contributed equally to this work

Information Theory.title: Insdel Decoding Algorithms for Maximum Distance Separable Codes
Information Theory.summary: In this paper, we focus on decoding MDS linear block codes for insdel errors. Building on our recent work for two-dimensional Reed-Solomon codes, we present a decoding algorithm for bounded distance decoding for the general insertion-and-deletion scenario that can be used for any MDS code of rate at most half. Our algorithm employs a sliding window and has a time complexity smaller than brute-force decoding. In particular, for optimal Reed-Solomon codes, it corrects insdel errors up to the half-Singleton bound, which exceeds the scope of existing methods. Additionally, for the special cases of insertion-only and deletion-only insdel error patterns, we present two different algorithms with a time complexity smaller than our general algorithm.

Information Theory.title: Hilbert-Scale Stability of Posterior Diffusion Priors for Ill-Posed Signal Recovery
Information Theory.summary: Indirect and noisy observations are difficult to invert when the forward operator smooths out the unknown signal. In this case, the unstable modes are precisely the modes that the data reveals least, thus the success of any reconstruction method depends on how prior information interacts with the geometry of the operator across regularity scales. Diffusion priors have become ubiquitous for such problems; however, the current theory still does not determine when a learned score remains informative under ill-posed forward operators. In this paper, we study posterior diffusion for linear inverse problems on Hilbert scales and derive a stability theory under an explicit score-amplification condition. Under a smoothing condition on the forward map, a source condition on the truth, and weak-norm control of score error, we derive non-asymptotic recovery bounds in \(\Hs^s\) that separate observation noise, score approximation, and reverse-time discretization. These bounds give a recoverable regularity threshold determined jointly by operator smoothing, truth regularity, score regularity, and the posterior correction. The threshold specifies the Hilbert-scale norms \(\Hs^s\) in which weak-norm score error remains controlled after propagation through the posterior reverse dynamics. For larger regularity indices \(s\), the inverse geometry magnifies the same error, and the Hilbert-scale recovery estimate no longer gives uniform stability. We also prove that a posterior correction adapted to the forward operator improves stability relative to isotropic guidance in the regularity ranges where the smoothing action of the forward map matters most. The recovery estimates give a regularity-sensitive theory of posterior diffusion and show how learned score error, operator smoothing, and reconstruction norm jointly determine the stable range predicted by the analysis.

Information Theory.title: Path-Specific Geometric-Stochastic Channel Model for Scattering from ISAC Targets: A Unified Measurement-Based Characterization of Robots, Humans, and Automobiles at 28 GHz
Information Theory.summary: This paper develops a channel model for scattering from a broad class of integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) targets-robots, humans, and automobiles-based on a unified measurement campaign at 28~GHz. Nine targets are characterized from numerous transmitter--receiver configurations per target, spanning full bistatic and aspect angles and thus covering backward to forward scattering. Repeated acquisitions are collected for each configuration to capture target motion and dynamics, yielding nearly 117\,000 acquisitions in total. Measurements are collected with a 2~GHz-wide channel sounder equipped with a 256-element phased-array antenna, followed by digital beamforming and super-resolution processing for reliable extraction of multiple paths in delay and 2D angle, with average estimation errors of 0.1~ns and 0.2$^\circ$ respectively. From these measurements, we reduce a \emph{path-specific} channel representation in which the scattering is modeled as a cluster of paths whose center is defined by the bistatic specular \emph{geometry}; the cluster shape is described \emph{stochastically}. To ensure physically grounded spatio--temporal consistency, extracted paths are mapped to incident points on the target, each with an associated radar cross section (RCS) that is compatible with the 3GPP TR~38.901 ISAC channel model, and are subsequently mapped back to path properties for channel synthesis. The resulting statistical distributions are well behaved, physically interpretable, and consistent across targets, geometries, and motion. Comparison between measured and synthesized channel realizations demonstrates close agreement in pathloss trends and fluctuation behavior. Together, these results yield a high-fidelity, measurement-derived channel representation suitable for ISAC simulation, target modeling, and system design.

Information Theory.title: Maximum-Likelihood Decoding of Gabidulin Codes Is NP-Hard Even in Dimension One
Information Theory.summary: Fix a prime power q. We prove that deciding whether a received word y in Fnqm lies at rank distance at most n-2 from the one-dimensional Gabidulin code {{λ.g : λ in Fqm } is NP-complete. Thus maximum-likelihood decoding of Gabidulin codes is NP-hard even for k = 1, an analogue of the Guruswami-Vardy theorem for Reed-Solomon codes. In the Hamming metric, by contrast, hardness at this radius requires the dimension to grow with the length, as in the Guruswami-Vardy theorem. The reduction is deterministic; consequently Rank Syndrome Decoding (RSD) and Rank Minimum Distance (RMD) for Fqm -linear codes are NP-complete under deterministic polynomial reductions, whereas the previously known reduction was randomized. The proof goes through a pivot problem that we introduce, Twisted Square Membership (TSM): given Fq-subspaces U, W in FqN , decide whether some non-zero a in U satisfies a^(q+1) in W . Quadratic systems in d unknowns are encoded into TSM, then TSM into Gabidulin decoding. The last step views the received word as an Fq-linear map and decoding at radius n - 2 as the search for an Fq-plane on which it acts as a scalar. With support U + τ W in a cubic extension and map a + τ b to a^(q^2) + τ bq^q , two Frobenius twists force solution planes to encode the relation a^(q+1) in W . All constructions are explicit and polynomial, with N = O(qd^2 ), n less than N + d, and m = 3N .

Information Theory.title: Logarithmic asymptotics for polynomial threshold functions
Information Theory.summary: We count Boolean functions represented as the sign of a real polynomial of bounded degree on the $n$-dimensional cube. We prove that the logarithm of their number is asymptotic to that of the classical hyperplane-arrangement upper bound, uniformly over all degrees, with relative error $O((\log n)^2/n)$. We also obtain sharper additive and relative error estimates in particular degree ranges, including an additive error $O(n^2)$ between the logarithms throughout a small linear degree range and improved bounds just below the central degree. The proof combines probabilistic estimates for Reed--Muller codes with a deletion argument for sets of evaluation vectors, an entropy count, and a sharp-threshold estimate for expected rank deficiency.

Information Theory.title: Exact Minimum Extension Degrees for Reed Solomon Codes under Linear and Nonlinear Repair at the Cut Set Bound
Information Theory.summary: We study the minimum extension degree required for a Reed--Solomon code to admit exact $\mathbb{F}_q$-linear repair at the cut-set bound from every prescribed set of $d$ helpers. Let $s=d-k+1$, and let $Q_s(n)$ be the minimum product of $n$ pairwise coprime integers, each at least $s$. For every prime power $q$ and all $3\le k<d<n\le2d-2$, we prove that the minimum degree over $\mathbb{F}_q$ is exactly $sQ_s(n)$. When all surviving nodes are helpers, we also characterize the admissible extension degrees and bound the number of coordinates that can attain the cut-set bound. The required achievability follows from existing construction methods; we give a short existence proof using splitting subspaces. For a family of parameters with $n>2d-2$, we obtain strictly smaller extension degrees, showing that the range restriction cannot be omitted altogether. Finally, we prove that a nonlinear repair scheme attaining the cut-set bound induces an $\mathbb{F}_p$-linear repair scheme on the same code, where $p$ is the characteristic. Consequently, the extension-degree lower bounds over the prime field remain valid without a linearity assumption.

Information Theory.title: Flexible Beamforming via Fluid Antenna Array: From Discrete to Continuous Array
Information Theory.summary: Fluid antenna arrays (FAAs) reconfigure their effective aperture by activating radiation ports from a dense set of candidate positions within a finite physical region, thereby offering geometry diversity beyond conventional fixed arrays. This paper studies arbitrary-direction far-field beam synthesis with a planar FAA. Since a fixed array adapts its beamforming weights on a predetermined spatial sampling structure, its ability to match desired beam patterns is limited when both the aperture and the number of active elements are constrained. To exploit the geometry diversity of the FAA, we propose a coarse-to-fine scheme that couples discrete port selection with continuous joint refinement. In the coarse stage, a fast Fourier transform (FFT) based phase retrieval step converts the amplitude-only beam specification into an aperture-compatible complex target, after which an FFT-tailored greedy method selects the active ports and least squares initializes their complex weights. In the fine stage, a projected adaptive moment estimation procedure jointly refines the continuous port positions and beamforming weights while enforcing the minimum interelement spacing. For the evaluated two-beam configuration, the proposed scheme increases the mainlobe energy fraction from 35.73% to 48.92% and reduces the peak sidelobe level from -2.30 dB to -3.83 dB relative to a fixed array with the same aperture and active-port count.
Information Theory.comment: 12 pages, 9 figures. Submitted to IEEE Transactions on Wireless Communications

Information Theory.title: Early Selection of Polar Ensemble Decoding with Successive Cancellation Style Component Decoder
Information Theory.summary: Parallel ensembles of successive cancellation (SC)-style decoders improve error-rate performance by decoding multiple representations of the received vector. Conventional ensembles, however, keep every member active until completion. To reduce computational cost while retaining the diversity gain of ensemble decoding, we propose early ensemble selection (EES), which ranks members using intermediate decoding states and retains a prescribed numbers of members at each predefined selection stage. Within the EES framework, we propose two selection rules, namely path-metric-based selection (PM-EES) and neural-network-based selection (NN-EES). We analytically characterize the computational cost of EES through stage-dependent decoder log-likelihood ratio (LLR) update counts and provide an information-theoretically motivated criterion for choosing selection stages. Simulations on the \((128,64)\) extended BCH code and the \(\operatorname{RM}(4,8)\) code show that suitable selection schedules approach full-ensemble error-rate performance with fewer decoder LLR updates.

Information Theory.title: Non-Vanishing Determinant Space-Time Codes from Abelian Crossed Product Algebras
Information Theory.summary: Every explicit non-cyclic crossed product space--time code for more than four antennas has relied on transcendental structure constants, and its coding gain is therefore not bounded away from zero. We explain this phenomenon and show how to avoid it. Over a number field, the commuting-generator (tensor product) construction yields a division algebra only in the cyclic case, and a division crossed product of prime-power degree requires two places with full decomposition group; in particular, no $(\Z/2)^r$, $r\ge3$, crossed product division algebra exists over $\Q(i)$. We then introduce Abelian crossed products with a commutator twist, give the general parametric form of their codewords as a $2\times2$ block matrix of cyclic-algebra codewords, and prove the division property with a centralizer argument and a tame norm-residue symbol. This yields algebraic codes over $\Q(i)$ with non-vanishing determinants and closed-form minimum determinants: an information-lossless $4\times4$ $(\Z/2)^2$ code with $δ_{\min}=1/2000$, and an infinite family of DMT-optimal $8\times8$ $\Z/4\times\Z/2$ codes indexed by primes $p\equiv5\pmod8$, whose commutator and cyclic constants are roots of unity. The member $p=5$, defined over $\Q(ζ_{40})$, has minimum determinant exactly $1/5$ before normalization, at least $34.7$ times that of the $8\times8$ perfect code at equal energy, and its rate-2 subcode for $8\times2$ systems has at least $5$ times the minimum determinant of the punctured perfect code. A determinant-spectrum analysis shows that at practical error rates the multiplicity of small determinants, rather than their minimum, governs performance, and it explains all simulated results.

Information Theory.title: Wireless Signal Point Processes with a Reflecting Wall
Information Theory.summary: A long reflecting wall gives every wireless transmitter a mirror image, pairing its direct and reflected paths. Motivated by intelligent surfaces, we study the resulting signal point processes under two treatments: keeping the powers apart and superposing their point processes, or adding the powers transmitter by transmitter to form a recombined process. A threshold on inverse received power selects a region of transmitter locations, so Campbell's theorem reduces the mean measures to area calculations without assuming Poisson transmitters. For power-law path loss and paired fading marks, we derive the ratio of the recombined and superposed mean measures at large thresholds. The limit is independent of transmitter density and wall distance, but generally depends on the joint fading distribution. Under common fading, that dependence disappears and the limit depends only on the reflection coefficient and path-loss exponent. For Poisson transmitters, we derive paired count fluctuations and convergence of the count ratio. We also calculate the probability that the strongest individual path is direct. When the wall passes through the receiver, this probability has a closed form and the strongest received power has an exact Fréchet distribution. These results provide a reference model for wireless networks with reflecting surfaces.
Information Theory.comment: 13 pages, 8 figures. Submitted to a IEEE journal

Information Theory.title: Secure Integrated Sensing and Communications with Movable Beyond-Diagonal RIS
Information Theory.summary: In integrated sensing and communication (ISAC), when the sensed target is itself an eavesdropper, the illumination required for sensing coincides with the leakage that secrecy must suppress. This paper shows how a beyond-diagonal reconfigurable intelligent surface (BD-RIS) with movable elements decouples the two tasks in a monostatic setting, where the echo returns to the base station through the surface. We prove that a lossless reciprocal BD-RIS maps $K$ incident fields onto $K$ prescribed fields if and only if the two sets share the same Gram matrix and their bilinear Gram matrix is symmetric; unlike a diagonal RIS, it can thus steer a two-dimensional incident subspace onto any prescribed subspace. With a single stream, sensing incurs an unavoidable rate loss, whereas a closed-form zero-forcing design with a confidential and a Gaussian sensing stream nulls the data at the target and the sensing at the user, so that sensing costs only an SNR offset. Since all variables follow in closed form for any placement, the joint design reduces to a monotone search over the element positions, without alternating optimization. Simulations show that the dual-stream design loses only $1.1$ bit/s/Hz when the sensing requirement grows by $30$ dB, against $8.3$ bit/s/Hz for a single stream, while movement, interconnection, and the robust derivative-null design add up to $1.9$, $0.9$, and $2.6$ bit/s/Hz, respectively.

Information Theory.title: MDS codes containing a fixed subcode over finite field extensions
Information Theory.summary: Let $2\le k\le n$ and let $U\le\mathbb{F}_q^n$ be a fixed $(k-1)$-dimensional linear code. We study the $[n,k]$ maximum distance separable (MDS) codes over finite extensions of $\mathbb{F}_q$ that contain the scalar extension of $U$. Our approach constructs an auxiliary linear code from \(U\). Its full-weight words characterize the desired MDS completions. We prove that \(U\) admits an \([n,k]\) MDS completion over some finite extension of \(\mathbb{F}_q\) if and only if \(d(U)\ge n-k+1\). When this condition holds, the number of these MDS codes over $\mathbb{F}_{q^m}$ is \[\#\left\{W\le\mathbb{F}_{q^m}^n:U\otimes_{\mathbb{F}_q}\mathbb{F}_{q^m}\subseteq W,\ \dim_{\mathbb{F}_{q^m}} W=k,\ W\text{ is MDS}\right\}=\frac{χ_{δ_GM(G)}(q^m)}{q^m-1},\] where $G$ is a generator matrix of $U$, $δ_GM(G)$ is its represented derived matroid, and $χ_{δ_GM(G)}$ is its characteristic polynomial. In particular, the formula determines existence over each extension field and the least extension degree for which such an MDS code exists. Examples show that these counts may distinguish different representations of the same column matroid, while monomially inequivalent codes may have identical counts over every finite extension.

Information Theory.title: A class of Niho type four-valued cross-correlation functions between sequences of different periods
Information Theory.summary: Determining the cross-correlation distributions between $m$-sequences and their decimated sequences is an important problem in sequence design. For two positive integers $n$ and $k$ with $n=2k$, this paper investigates the cross-correlation function between a binary $m$-sequence $\{u(t)\}$ of period $2^{n}-1$ and its $2^{\gcd(s,k)}+1$ short-period decimated sequences $\{u(dt+l)\}$, where the decimation $d=\frac{2^s}{2^s+1}(2^k-1)+1$ satisfies $1<s<n$ and $v_2(s)>v_2(k)$. The cross-correlation function is proved to be four-valued and its value distribution is completely determined. Several previously known binary cross-correlation functions are included in our result as special cases.

Information Theory.title: SENECA: Small-Sample Discrete Entropy Estimation via Self-Consistent Missing Mass
Information Theory.summary: Discrete entropy estimation is a classic information theory problem, wherein the average information content of a discrete random variable is estimated from samples alone. Naive approaches, such as the plugin method, fail to account for the probability mass associated with members of the random variable's support that are unobserved in a given sample, known as the "missing mass." The resulting systemic underestimation is particularly problematic when data is time-consuming or costly to gather. We propose SENECA, an entropy estimation scheme based on a novel "self-consistent" missing mass calculation. Extensive numerical experiments indicate that our approach outperforms many state-of-the-art alternatives overall in the small-sample setting. We then apply SENECA to two practical use cases, namely biodiversity estimation and the detection of incorrect large language model responses, where our method is competitive with domain-specific approaches. Our work advances SENECA as an effective drop-in replacement for small-sample entropy estimation, with broad utility across several domains.

Information Theory.title: The Golomb--Welch conjecture for lattice tilings
Information Theory.summary: We prove the Golomb--Welch conjecture for lattice tilings: for every $n\ge3$ and $r\ge2$, the integer lattice $\Z^n$ admits no lattice tiling by Lee balls $B_n(r)$ of radius $r$. Together with the classical constructions for $n\le2$ and for $r=1$, this determines all parameters for which a lattice Lee tiling exists. Equivalently, we show that every abelian Cayley graph of even degree $2n\ge6$ and diameter $r\ge2$ has strictly fewer than $|B_n(r)|$ vertices.

Information Theory.title: Unifying Performance and Equity via Percentile Optimization and Cell-Free Massive MIMO
Information Theory.summary: Improving the throughput of the weakest users is a central objective of wireless resource allocation, and the objective around which the user-centric cell-free massive multiple-input multiple-output (UC-mMIMO) architecture is built. This paper brings the two together by formulating and solving percentile programs for UC-mMIMO networks. We maximize the sum-least-qth-percentile (SLqP) rate via downlink power control, a utility that targets the user equipments (UEs) in the lowest q percentile of the rate distribution and subsumes max-min-rate and sum-rate maximization as special cases. The problem is non-convex, non-smooth and NP-hard. The cyclic maximization approach of one of the previous percentile optimization series does not carry over: the coherent joint transmission technique introduces cross terms in the powers that destroy the block-concavity on which it relies. We develop a change of variables that restores block-concavity, yielding an algorithm with closed-form auxiliary updates and a concave power update, and we give a self-contained proof of non-decreasing convergence to a directional stationary point. Simulations establish two facts: first, percentile optimization retains its value in an architecture with no cell edges; relative to the weighted minimum mean-square error benchmark, it raises the average rate of the lowest-10th-percentile UEs by 56--72% and Jain's fairness index from below 0.92 to above 0.99. Second, compared directly with massive MIMO and small cells under the same SLqP utility, UC-mMIMO delivers the highest lower-percentile rates at every access point density tested, by up to 62% and 2.7$\times$ respectively, at the same fairness, and its advantage widens with densification.

Information Theory.title: Distributed LLM Inference via Communication-Efficient Speculative Decoding
Information Theory.summary: Distributed speculative decoding has emerged as a promising approach for device--server collaborative large language model (LLM) inference, but its decoding speedup is often limited by the vocabulary-scale communication overhead. In existing distributed speculative decoding methods, exact rejection sampling requires transmitting full token distributions over the LLM vocabulary between the device and the server, which becomes costly in bandwidth-constrained environments. To address this issue, we propose DISCO, a communication-efficient framework for distributed speculative decoding, that eliminates vocabulary-scale distribution transfer while preserving the exact target distribution. DISCO achieves this by introducing a server-side replica of the draft small language model (SLM), which enables the server to locally obtain the draft-side distribution required for rejection sampling. As a result, DISCO exchanges only drafted token indices and scalar probability values between the device and the server. Experimental results on multiple datasets show that DISCO consistently achieves higher decoding speedup than existing distributed speculative decoding methods, particularly under stringent bandwidth constraints.

Information Theory.title: Structured Time-Frequency Representation for Channel Prediction
Information Theory.summary: Accurate CSI forecasting is essential for mitigating channel aging and supporting reliable downlink transmission in high-mobility wireless systems. In FDD systems, forecasting future DL CSI from historical UL observations requires joint temporal extrapolation and cross-band inference. However, defining historical UL as the input and future DL as the target does not specify how elapsed time and UL-to-DL band separation should be represented in a pretrained predictor's positional space. FAR-CSI establishes an FDD-aware representation of channel forecasting within a joint temporal and operating-band positional field. Within this field, historical UL observations and future DL targets occupy segregated regions according to their temporal and operating-band roles, preserving the distinction between observed UL context and unobserved DL prediction targets. This representation is instantiated through a unified structured routing rule that governs encoder positional assignment, decoder-field reconstruction, and future-DL target selection, ensuring the same FDD geometry is preserved from contextual encoding to prediction readout. Under matched backbone, initialization, and training conditions, FDD-aware routing reduces NMSE by 21.44\% relative to generic routing. Across the evaluated FDD baselines, FAR-CSI achieves higher CSI prediction accuracy and MRT-based spectral efficiency, while retaining its predictive advantage across mobility conditions, prediction horizons, reduced training-data regimes, and noisy historical observations.

Probability.title: Exchangeable Testing Against an Unknown Benchmark
Probability.summary: We generate infinite binary exchangeable sequences by sequential comparison of data points against a latent benchmark. Assuming a prior distribution of the benchmark rank \(R_0\) within an unobserved group of players, we set up the Bayesian machinery which determines the posterior distribution of the running rank \(R_n\) in purely combinatorial terms, by counting insertion slots in a uniformly random ranking. This yields an explicit predictive probability of winning against the benchmark, which is a rational function of the counts. We identify some cases where the predictive probability has particularly simple form, notably a tournament related to the Topp--Leone distribution. The running benchmark rank is a Pólya urn with random initial composition, and its normalised value converges to a latent strength variable with polynomial density. In a projective time scale, the fluctuations of the normalised rank about this limit are Brownian, with the Wright--Fisher coefficient frozen at the limit, while the associated recurrent up-down Markov chain on a high level $n$ of the Pascal graph is approximated by a Wright--Fisher diffusion with a nonlinear drift expressed through the prior density.

Probability.title: Aperiodic random walks: uniform estimates, local limits and invariance principles
Probability.summary: We prove uniform endpoint estimates, killed local limits, and conditioned-bridge invariance principles for triangular arrays of centered, aperiodic, integer-valued random walks with uniform exponential tails. The endpoint estimates cover all nonnegative heights, while the local limits treat positive diffusive and zero endpoints. The increment law may vary with the scaling parameter.
Probability.comment: 17 pages, 1 figure. Simplified the proof of Lemma 3.1

Probability.title: Airy limit for the Jack process and topological expansion
Probability.summary: For every $β>0$, we establish multi-time soft-edge moment convergence for a class of Jack processes, including the Jack--Plancherel process, a discrete $β$-analogue of Dyson Brownian motion. The limiting moments admit an absolutely convergent expansion in terms of nonnegative Brownian bridges decorated by pairs of equal and opposite jumps. At equal times, we identify this limit with the joint Laplace statistics of the Airy$_β$ process for $β\geq1$. The same Brownian expansion yields an asymptotic $β$-topological expansion of the marginal $b$-conjecture and, at $β=2$, an explicit nonnegative formula for the Witten--Kontsevich intersection numbers.
Probability.comment: 67 pages, 3 figures. Minor revision and added a short section about the moment convergence of the general Jack processes

Probability.title: Quantum wedges and large deviations for SLE with two force points
Probability.summary: We prove a good large deviation principle for chordal $\mathrm{SLE}_κ(W_1-2;W_2-2)$ with force points at $0^-$ and $0^+$, for every fixed $W_1,W_2>0$, as $κ\downarrow0$. The topology is Hausdorff convergence of the entire compact trace. The rate has two equivalent descriptions: the sum of the component wedge energies obtained by cutting a deterministic ambient wedge, and the Loewner driving energy relative to the force-point drift.

Probability.title: The Tamed Subgradient Unadjusted Langevin Algorithm beyond Convexity
Probability.summary: We study the problem of sampling from target distributions whose potentials are simultaneously non-smooth, subject to superlinear gradient growth, and non-convex. We introduce the Subgradient Tamed Unadjusted Langevin Algorithm (SG-TULA), a discretisation of the Langevin diffusion that operates directly on subgradients, without relying on computationally demanding smoothing procedures. To handle the superlinear regime, taming techniques are employed to produce a stable, explicit scheme. We derive non-asymptotic convergence bounds in Wasserstein-2 distance, with all constants tracked explicitly in terms of dimension and inverse temperature, improving upon the currently known rates for subgradient-based Langevin algorithms. We further provide excess risk estimates for the associated optimisation problem. We verify the assumptions, with explicit constants, for the regularized pretraining potential of a LLM in the GPT-2 lineage and the boosted coordinate-wise variant of SG-TULA pretrains the former competitively against finetuned AdamW and Muon, for which no comparable non-asymptotic guarantees are presently available.

Probability.title: The German Tank Problem & Navigating by Scent
Probability.summary: A robot searching for the source of an odor must eventually answer a deceptively hard question: have I arrived? Near the source, concentration gradients flatten, turbulence makes the signal intermittent, and a small robot often lacks the positional accuracy to map the plume. Here, we describe a lightweight remedy inspired by a World War II statistics conundrum: the German tank problem. To approximate enemy armament production, Allied analysts developed an estimator based on serial numbers from captured tanks. Analogously, we use the same procedure over sampled chemical sensor readings from a robot to create estimates for the peak concentration of an odor plume, and therefore the odor's source. Treating each sensor reading as an observation, our unbiased estimator needs only a running maximum and a sample counter. An exact confidence bound turns both numbers into a principled rule that the robot or UAV can use to determine whether to keep searching for the plume source or land. We derive the estimator and its bound, demonstrate its sample efficiency, and examine its robustness even when its assumptions fail. Finally, we summarize the estimator's role as the termination criterion for olfactory navigation.

Probability.title: Concentration of Exponential Tilts Implies Curvature
Probability.summary: We show, under a smoothness assumption, that probability measures whose exponential tilts have a uniformly bounded variance are given by a strongly convex potential, up to a bounded perturbation, yielding a partial converse to the Bakry-Émery theorem combined with Holley-Stroock's perturbation principle. A stronger version enforcing uniform convexity of the potential is obtained by considering the low-temperature regime.

Probability.title: Optimal regret for dynamic matching with static priorities
Probability.summary: We study centralized two-way dynamic matching markets in which agents arrive stochastically over time and wait in queues associated with their types. We focus on static priority policies that assign each agent type a fixed ranking over its neighbors and make online matching decisions using only queue availability. We propose the General Priority ($\mathbf{GP}$) policy, which builds on the Tree Priority ($\mathbf{TP}$) policy introduced in [KAG25]. Under the general position gap condition, $\mathbf{GP}$ selects matches using a nondegenerate optimal basic solution of the fluid relaxation. It prioritizes children over parents within trees and consistently gives clockwise neighbors priority over counterclockwise neighbors on each cycle. We establish the optimal all-time regret scaling $O(ε^{-1})$ for $\mathbf{GP}$ on general two-way matching networks, where the general position gap $ε$ measures the fluid relaxation's distance from degeneracy. In particular, this resolves the conjecture by [KAG25] on the optimal $ε$-dependence for $\mathbf{TP}$.

Probability.title: Stationary Measures and Boundary Correlations for Multispecies Half-Line ASEP
Probability.summary: We construct stationary measures of the multispecies ASEP on the positive half-line, with injection of highest-priority particles at the left boundary, using vertex models. Our results extend existing constructions of Martin and Aggarwal-Nicoletti-Petrov for the full-line ASEP to the half-line. For the two-species process, we compute the joint distribution of occupation colors at the first two sites. We also partially address the connection with the half-space ASEP speed process.

Probability.title: Crossings and diffusion in Poisson driven marked random connection models
Probability.summary: We first study crossing statistics in random connection models (RCM) built on marked Poisson point processes on $\mathbb R^d$. Under general assumptions, we show exponential tail bounds for the number of crossings of a box contained in the infinite cluster for supercritical intensity of the point process, and percolation in slabs, in analogy with the Grimmett-Marstrand theorem. We then present several applications to transport and diffusion phenomena. In particular, we prove the non-degeneracy of the effective homogenized matrix arising in the large-scale limit of random walks, exclusion processes, and resistor networks on the RCM, and the non-degeneracy of the effective diffusion constant for one-dimensional diffusion operators on the Euclidean graph associated with the RCM. As examples, we apply our results to Poisson-Boolean models and Mott variable range hopping random resistor network, providing a fundamental ingredient used in the derivation of Mott's law.
Probability.comment: 33 pages, 2 figures. Minor improvements to the presentation

Probability.title: The norm of the centered Hardy--Littlewood maximal operator
Probability.summary: We determine the exact $L^p(\mathbb{R})$ norm of the centered Hardy--Littlewood maximal operator for every $1<p<\infty$, proving that it equals $p/(p-1)$. This settles the sharp strong-type problem for the centered maximal operator on the real line. For every $p$ in this range, the norm is strictly larger than the constant associated with the critical power $|x|^{-1/p}$, thereby disproving the conjecture of Dror, Ganguli, and Strichartz that this profile determines the unrestricted norm.
Probability.comment: 14 pages. This paper was merged into https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.10247

Probability.title: On maximum likelihood estimation in the $β$-model for random hypergraphs
Probability.summary: We study maximum likelihood estimation in the $β$-model for random hypergraphs, in which a group of vertices succeeds with a probability that depends on the sum of its members' parameters. The data are independent binary outcomes of experiments on groups of vertices, tested according to an arbitrary, possibly incomplete design. Suppose that every tested group has $k$ vertices and success probability in $[ε,1-ε]$. For complete designs in which every group is tested at least $r$ times, a unique maximum likelihood estimator (MLE) exists with high probability if $r\geq C_kε^{-1}\log n/n^{k-1}$, and for $m$ experiments on uniformly random groups, it suffices that $m\geq C_kε^{-1}n\log n$, where $C_k$ depends only on $k$. Both conditions are linear in $ε^{-1}$ and, for fixed $k$, cannot be improved in general beyond the constant; they follow from finite-sample bounds for arbitrary designs. We bound the mean squared error of the MLE over a parameter box by the smallest eigenvalue of the correlation matrix of the design, and show that the rate is minimax optimal for balanced complete designs. Among $k$-uniform designs with a given number of experiments, designs in which every pair of vertices takes part together in the same number of experiments maximize this eigenvalue, and uniform random designs nearly do so with high probability. Finally, the design matrix of a uniform random design has full column rank with high probability if $m\geq\max\{n,c(n/k)\log n\}$ for fixed $c>2$ and $k=o(n/\log n)$, or $m\geq n$ when $k\geq(1+ξ)\log n$. For fixed $k$, the threshold $(n/k)\log n$ is sharp, and above it rank deficiency is asymptotically as likely as some vertex taking part in no experiment.
Probability.comment: 54 pages, 7 figures; based in part on the PhD thesis of Yiliu Wang, with substantial subsequent theoretical developments

Probability.title: Non-Ergodic Markovian Mirror Descent with Unbounded Noise
Probability.summary: We analyze stochastic mirror descent for minimizing a convex objective expressed as an expectation under the stationary distribution of a Markov chain, using noisy subgradient observations along a single sample path. Through Poisson's equation, we decompose the Markovian noise and control its contribution under regularity and moment conditions that allow the stochastic subgradients and the Poisson solution to be unbounded across the state space. We establish an $O(T^{-1/2})$ bound on the expected suboptimality gap of the weighted-average iterate for an appropriately chosen step size. The analysis does not require aperiodicity or convergence of the chain's marginal distributions to stationarity. For irreducible finite-state chains, we verify the required conditions on the Poisson solution and derive explicit bounds that quantify the effect of periodicity. For irreducible countable-state chains, we verify the required regularity and moment conditions under a geometric Lyapunov drift condition and suitable growth bounds on the stochastic subgradients.

Probability.title: Case Studies in Generalized Kantorovich-Rubinstein Duality
Probability.summary:
The classical Kantorovich-Rubinstein duality guarantees coincidence between metrics on the space of probability distributions defined on the one hand via transport plans (couplings) and on the other hand via price functions. Both constructions have been lifted to the level of generality of set functors, with the construction based on couplings referred to as the Wasserstein or simply the coupling-based lifting, and the price-function-based construction as the Kantorovich or codensity lifting, both based on a choice of quantitative modalities for the given functor. It is known that every coupling-based lifting can be expressed as a price-function-based lifting; however, the latter in general needs to use additional modalities. We give an example showing that this cannot be avoided in general. We refer to cases in which the same modalities can be used as satisfying the generalized Kantorovich-Rubinstein duality. We establish the generalized Kantorovich-Rubinstein duality in this sense for two important cases: The Lévy-Prokhorov distance on distributions, which finds wide-spread applications in machine learning due to its favourable stability properties, and the standard metric on convex sets of distributions that arises by combining the Hausdorff and Kantorovich-Rubinstein distances.
  Furthermore we generalize (coupling-based) functor liftings from set functors to functors which act on (pseudo-)metric spaces, thus incorporating new example functors that map to closed subsets respectively Radon measures.

Probability.title: Online Discrepancy of Sparse Random Vectors over Long Horizons
Probability.summary:
We study online vector balancing for independent sparse random vectors: each arrival is supported on a uniformly random set of $s$ of the $n$ coordinates, with nonzero entries equal to one (binary model) or independent random signs (signed model), and an online algorithm must sign each vector upon arrival. The prefix discrepancy is the largest $\ell_\infty$-norm of the signed sums up to the horizon $T$, the terminal discrepancy that of the sum at time $T$. For binary inputs with $2\le s\le n/2$ and $T=Θ(n)$, Altschuler and Tikhomirov showed that both are of order $\sqrt{s}+\log\log n$; they asked how the prefix discrepancy depends on the horizon and whether a matching terminal bound holds at every prescribed time.
  Over long horizons, the two differ. For every fixed $s\ge2$ and $c>0$, every online algorithm, even a randomized one that knows the horizon, incurs with high probability prefix discrepancy $Ω(\log\log n+(\log T/\log n)^{α_s})$ for $n\le T\le e^{cn}$, where $α_s=(2^{s-1}-1)/(2^s-1)$. For $s=2$, quadratic Greedy matches this bound; for fixed $s\ge3$, we give an online algorithm with prefix discrepancy $O(\log\log n+(\log T/\log n)^{1/2})$. In contrast, a deterministic algorithm that knows neither the horizon nor the failure probability keeps the terminal discrepancy $O_k(\sqrt{s}+\log\log n)$ at each prescribed time, with failure probability $n^{-k}$ for every fixed $k$, for $2\le s\le n/2$ (binary model) and $2\le s\le n$ (signed model); for $s=2$, quadratic Greedy itself does so. This answers their terminal question, and the same order is optimal for prefixes at all polynomial horizons $T\ge n$.
  The lower bound uses a finite safety game realized within the input law; the upper bounds use moments of elementary symmetric polynomials and, at terminal times, a $\cosh$ potential or a translated gauge with a Foster inequality at every state.

Probability.title: On the cutoff phenomenon for fast diffusion and porous medium equations
Probability.summary: The cutoff phenomenon, conceptualized at the origin for finite Markov chains, states that for a parametric family of evolution equations, started from a point, the distance towards a long time equilibrium may become more and more abrupt for certain choices of initial conditions, when the parameter tends to infinity. This threshold phenomenon can be seen as a critical competition between trend to equilibrium and worst initial condition. In this note, we investigate this phenomenon beyond stochastic processes, in the context of the analysis of nonlinear partial differential equations, by proving cutoff for the fast diffusion and porous medium Fokker-Planck equations on the Euclidean space, when the dimension tends to infinity. We formulate the phenomenon using quadratic Wasserstein distance, as well as using specific relative entropy and Fisher information. Our high dimensional asymptotic analysis uses the exact solvability of the model involving Barenblatt profiles. It includes the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck dynamics as a special linear case.

Probability.title: On cutoff via rigidity for high dimensional curved diffusions
Probability.summary: We consider overdamped Langevin diffusions in Euclidean space, with curvature equal to the spectral gap. This includes the Ornstein--Uhlenbeck process as well as non-Gaussian and non-product extensions with convex interaction, such as the Dyson process from random matrix theory. We show that a cutoff phenomenon or abrupt convergence to equilibrium occurs in high dimension, at a critical time equal to the logarithm of the dimension divided by twice the spectral gap. This cutoff holds for Wasserstein distance, total variation, relative entropy, and Fisher information. A key observation is a relation to a spectral rigidity, linked to the presence of a Gaussian factor. A novelty is the extensive usage of functional inequalities, even for short-time regularization, and the reduction to Wasserstein. The proofs are short and conceptual. Since the product condition is satisfied, an Lp cutoff holds for all finite p. We moreover discuss a natural extension to Riemannian manifolds, a link with logarithmic gradient estimates in short-time for the heat kernel, and ask about stability by perturbation. Finally, beyond rigidity but still for diffusions, a discussion around the recent progress on the product condition for non-negatively curved diffusions leads us to introduce a new curvature product condition.
Probability.comment: 19 pages, post-publication version, fix some problems

Probability.title: Critical measures and coefficient limits for non-Gaussian holomorphic chaos
Probability.summary: We study critical holomorphic multiplicative chaos with circular iid inputs of unit variance. Writing $R=|X_1|$, we prove that the radially normalized boundary measures converge in probability to a finite measure with almost surely positive mass if and only if $\mathbb{E}[R^2\log(2+R)]<\infty$; otherwise they converge to zero. We obtain distinct sharp criteria for convergence at each fractional order $0<q<1$ for radial approximations and for the full Fourier-radial family. Convergence at every such order is equivalent to an exponential-moment radius of at least two. In the positive-limit class, coefficient vectors normalized by $(\log n)^{1/4}$ and their analytic windows converge stably to Gaussian mixtures determined by the same critical measure. This measure is nonatomic, has full support, and is carried by a set of Hausdorff dimension zero. Coefficient periodograms recover the measure, while scalar and matrix energy normalizations give universal Gaussian limits. Exact weighted tails under $\mathbb{E} I_0(2R)<\infty$, where $I_0$ is the modified Bessel function, and negative mass moments distinguish uncountably many coefficient-limit laws, even modulo deterministic scalar rescaling, within a uniformly bounded input family. This disproves the common-law clause of Gu-Zhang's Question 2 at its fixed normalization. We give conditions for convergence of the original coefficient moments and show that finiteness of the limiting moments alone does not suffice. For inputs with $\log\mathbb{P}(R>u)\sim-λu^α$, $0<α<1$, the coefficient normalization and Gaussian-mixture form persist, but the limit has no finite positive moments; we determine its logarithmic tails. Finally, we prove Hardy nonmembership under finite variance alone and, in the positive-limit class, sharp weighted Bergman criteria for $0<p\le2$ and the boundary Sobolev threshold $s=-1/2$.

Probability.title: A functional central limit theorem for particle systems under polynomial growth conditions, with applications to statistics
Probability.summary: We establish a functional central limit theorem (CLT) for fluctuations of time-integrated functionals of empirical measures arising from interacting McKean--Vlasov particle systems. Our framework allows for coefficients with unbounded spatial growth and dependence on arbitrarily high-order moments of the measure variable, extending the scope of the existing fluctuation theory. The proof uses a novel approach combining linear functional differentiation with new well-posedness results and estimates for perturbed backward parabolic equations in polynomially weighted Schauder spaces, yielding a martingale-type representation of the fluctuations with an asymptotically negligible remainder. The limiting process is shown to be centred Gaussian with an explicit covariance structure. As a statistical application, we derive the asymptotic theory underlying hypothesis tests for both the temporal constancy of population characteristics and parametric restrictions on the drift coefficient.

Probability.title: Enhanced Dissipation by Transport Noise for Stochastic $p(x)$-Laplace Equations
Probability.summary: We are concerned with dissipation enhancement by divergence-free transport noise for stochastic \(p(x)\)-Laplace equations on \(\mathbb T^d\), \(d\ge2\). Spatially variable growth removes homogeneous scaling and produces two flux growth regimes. For periodic log-Hölder continuous exponents satisfying \(2<p^-\le p^+<\infty\), we first establish global variational well-posedness and the exact energy identity in the natural dual spaces. Under the additional condition \(p^+<2d/(d-2)\) when \(d\ge3\), we then prove averaged algebraic decay with any prescribed coefficient, uniformly on bounded zero-mean \(L^2\) balls, by estimating the two flux powers separately. A deterministic lower bound yields strict averaged comparison with the unperturbed flow at prescribed positive times on shells with bounded gradient modular. We also prove optimality of the modular coercivity exponent \(p^+\) near zero. Finally, combining these estimates with intervalwise noise acceleration from the constant-exponent theory gives exponential decay in mean square and almost surely, with moments of the random prefactors bounded uniformly on the initial-data ball. For the exponential estimates, the noise depends on the prescribed rate and moment order; its intensity is fixed in time and its frequency range increases.

Probability.title: Beyond Brown's radial tests: admissibility, parabolicity, and a doubling-Poincaré prior that neither test decides
Probability.summary: For the estimation of a normal mean in $\mathbb{R}^m$ under quadratic loss, Brown (1971) proved that a generalized Bayes estimator $δ_F$ is admissible if and only if a diffusion attached to the marginal $f^*$ of the prior $F$ is recurrent, and gave two radial tests: a sphere-average test for recurrence and a ray test for transience. He observed that both tests can be silent. We read his theory as the potential theory of the weighted Euclidean space $(\mathbb{R}^m,f^*\,dx)$ and ask what the modern theory of recurrence on weighted manifolds adds inside the zone where neither test applies. Three results. (A) If $f^*\,dx$ is doubling and supports a scale-invariant Poincaré inequality, the sphere test is already complete: recurrence, Brown's sphere test and the ball-volume test are equivalent, so geometric criteria can add decidable cases only on the inadmissible side. (B) They do add one. An explicit prior on $\mathbb{R}^3$ whose marginal is small along a lattice of circles at dyadic scales with spacing equal to the square root of the scale, is doubling and Poincaré, silences both of Brown's tests, and is transient by the ball-volume test; its generalized Bayes estimator is inadmissible. (C) Outside the doubling-Poincaré class the zone is two-sided: the same circles placed on one surface per scale give an admissible estimator, decided by a flux bound along a non-spherical exhaustion, and a logarithmic product prior gives an inadmissible one, decided by product heat kernels. A comparison lemma shows that any positive weight with Lipschitz logarithm is, up to constants, the marginal of a prior, so that explicit weights may be used throughout.

Probability.title: Normal approximation, moderate and large deviations for the elephant random walk with stops and random step sizes
Probability.summary: We study the elephant random walk with stops and independent positive random step sizes. Building on fixed-movement estimates, we obtain quantitative normal approximations for an empirically normalized statistic by controlling its random denominator and the independent movement clock. A permutation comparison preserves the diffusive Kolmogorov rate, while variance matching permits third-order Zolotarev estimates. We also derive self-normalized Cramér-type moderate deviations. For regularly varying step-size tails, we obtain uniform precise large deviations and establish the necessity of the diffusive and critical threshold orders. Further applications of the clock representation yield large deviation principles for Weibull-type and light-tailed step sizes, and a precise light-tailed expansion in the balanced case.

Probability.title: Remarks on the Brascamp--Lieb inequality
Probability.summary: We prove several variants of the Brascamp--Lieb inequality which are adapted to additional symmetries, weights, and non-Euclidean radial structures. First, an improved Brascamp--Lieb inequality for even functions yields a strengthened Prékopa--Leindler theorem for even strongly log-concave functions. We also record a Legendre-transform proof of a generalized log-Sobolev inequality for log-concave functions. Further results include a Brascamp--Lieb inequality with a concave weight, an unconditional second-order Poincaré inequality, a rotation-trick improvement for arbitrary even log-concave measures, and a Poincaré-type inequality associated with smooth norms.
Probability.comment: 42 pages, the majority of the paper written before spring 2026

Probability.title: A marked scheme representation for Voronoi volumes in the Brownian map
Probability.summary: For any fixed number $k\ge3$ of independent volume-sampled sites in the unit-area Brownian map, we represent the negative-power transform of their ordinary Voronoi volumes as a finite sum of marked planar scheme integrals. These integrals arise from the critical asymptotics of generating functions for face-constrained labelled planar maps. To connect them to Voronoi volumes, we use Miermont's zero-delay correspondence to interpret the labelled maps as quadrangulations with distinguished sites and then pass to the Brownian map scaling limit.

Probability.title: Gaussian zero-count fluctuations in annuli
Probability.summary: We determine joint zero-count fluctuations of the self-dual weighted Szegő Gaussian analytic function in fixed and thinning annuli. For a fixed annulus, the counts near its two boundary components converge jointly to independent standard normal variables after centering and marginal normalization, at arbitrary relative rates of boundary approach. This answers the simultaneous central limit question of Katori and Shirai for this model. The unscaled covariance converges to a negative constant, which we evaluate in complete elliptic integrals. A sharp variance asymptotic for the difference between an annular winding number and its coupled disk count yields quantitative normal approximation bounds. For thinning annuli with inner radius $q=e^{-h}$, the counts in every fixed finite family of interior transverse bands converge jointly to a Gaussian vector after centering and multiplication by $\sqrt h$. We give its spectral covariance matrix, prove strict negative covariance for disjoint bands, and identify its nullspace from the interval indicators. The fixed-annulus proof couples the Laurent series to two independent Gaussian power series. For thinning annuli, we combine exact periodization of a strip kernel, a uniform Laguerre-chaos tail bound, and connected Gaussian diagrams.

Probability.title: Shaping of invariant measures of iterated function systems
Probability.summary: We study an inverse problem for iterated function systems: given maps $w_1,\dots,w_m$ on a Polish space and a target probability measure $ν$, choose the law $μ$ with which the maps are sampled so that the invariant measure $π_μ$ of the resulting Markov chain is as close as possible to $ν$ in the Wasserstein-1 distance. The minimization runs over the admissible set $A$ of sampling laws for which the chain has a unique invariant measure attracting every initial law; the maps need not be contractions. On bounded state spaces, regions certified by a Doeblin or splitting condition are convex unions of relatively open faces of the simplex, and they exhaust $A$ when the state space is finite; for affine systems with nonnegative matrices $A$ is a spectral sublevel set; in general $A$ is neither open, closed, convex nor connected. Existence of an optimal law reduces to the invariant measures left behind at the missing boundary $\mathrm{cl}(A)\setminus A$: boundary points without invariant measures of finite first moment repel minimizing sequences, which yields existence for all systems of homotheties of $\mathbb R^d$, and for compact state spaces a solution exists for every target if and only if the set of reachable invariant measures is closed; a two-state example shows that existence can fail. A search over a $δ$-net returns an $ε$-optimal law over any region on which $μ\mapstoπ_μ$ is Lipschitz and the chains are uniformly attracting, with explicit constants and, on an interval, an explicit sample size. Under contraction on average, $μ\mapstoπ_μ$ is differentiable, its derivative is injective if and only if the push-forwards $(w_i)_\#π_μ$ are linearly independent, and the objective is weakly convex, so that a projected subgradient method with inexact subgradients converges to near-stationary points.

Probability.title: American Options with Last Exit Times: A Free-Boundary Approach
Probability.summary: We study an optimal stopping problem with a random horizon that is not a stopping time: the last exit time of a geometric Brownian motion from a fixed level $L$. The defaultable American put option serves as the motivating example. Using the theory of enlargements of filtration and the associated Azéma supermartingale, we reduce the problem to a classical optimal stopping problem in a finite time horizon for a Markov process, whose gain function is only upper semi-continuous and has a concave kink at $L$ and a spatial derivative that blows up. These features break the standard free-boundary arguments, including the smooth-fit condition. We describe the continuation and stopping sets according to the position of $L$ relative to $B$, the optimal stopping boundary of the standard American put option. When $B$ lies completely above $L$, the random-horizon problem coincides with the standard American put option pricing problem on the continuation set. When $B$ lies below $L$ for some time interval, the optimal stopping boundary of the random-horizon problem lies below or stays at $L$ until $B$ reaches $L$ and agrees with $B$ when $B$ exceeds $L$. The smooth-fit condition fails at $L$, and we obtain upper and lower bounds for the one-sided derivative of the value function. Under numerically verifiable parameter conditions, we show that the boundary is monotone and continuous, and we derive a nonlinear integral equation and an early-exercise-premium representation with local time terms.

Probability.title: Structured Continuity Equations in Fibred Wasserstein Spaces
Probability.summary: In this article, we develop a comprehensive ODE-theory for structured continuity equations in fibred probability spaces, which represent a class of heterogeneous PDEs arising as the meanfield limit of nonexchangeable particle systems. After investigating in depth the topologies induced by the so-called fibred (or conditional) and classical Wasserstein metrics on such probability spaces, we establish quantitative Cauchy-Lipschitz and qualitative Carathéodory-Peano well-posedness results for structured continuity equations, along with precise correspondences between this class of evolutions, classical Lagrangian dynamics, and continuity equations. In keeping with what has long been known for exchangeable dynamics, we derive a general meanfield approximation result by solutions of nonexchangeable particle systems, along with a quantitative variant thereof under practically reasonable regularity assumptions on the driving field and initial data.

Probability.title: Stochastic quantization and Osterwalder-Schrader axioms for quantum field theory models
Probability.summary: This PhD thesis constructs the $P(Φ)_2$ Euclidean quantum field theory on $\mathscr{S}'(\mathbb{R}^2)$. We first construct the finite-volume measure of the $P(Φ)_2$ model on $\mathscr{D}'(\mathbb{S}_R)$, where $\mathbb{S}_R$ is a two-dimensional sphere of radius $R\in\mathbb{N}_+$. To this end, we rely on Nelson's hypercontractivity estimate. We then use parabolic stochastic quantization and the energy method to construct the infinite-volume measure on $\mathscr{S}'(\mathbb{R}^2)$. This requires establishing the global-in-time existence of solutions to the corresponding stochastic partial differential equations with fixed cutoffs. The remainder of the thesis is devoted to verifying the Osterwalder-Schrader axioms: regularity, reflection positivity, and invariance under translations, rotations, and reflections. This combination of axioms, which is crucial for obtaining a non-trivial local relativistic quantum field theory on Minkowski spacetime, had not been established in earlier constructions based on stochastic quantization.
Probability.comment: PhD thesis submitted in October 2025 and defended in April 2026 at Adam Mickiewicz University, Poznań. Typos corrected and English revised

Probability.title: A superprocess model for eDNA transport in random river environment
Probability.summary: Environmental DNA (eDNA) is increasingly used to monitor aquatic organisms in rivers, yet predicting its concentration and assessing the reliability of such predictions remain challenging because river flow fluctuates with long memory and models of eDNA dynamics are inevitably misspecified. We propose a stochastic modeling framework for eDNA concentration in rivers that addresses both issues. The eDNA concentration is described by a stochastic partial differential equation with transport, decay, source, and square-root multiplicative noise, and the flow velocity is modeled by a superposition of Ornstein-Uhlenbeck-type processes with long memory. We show that the long memory of the flow velocity induces superdiffusive transport of eDNA, with the variance of the transported distance growing superlinearly in the ensemble sense. The proposed model admits a closed-form Laplace functional, based on which we prove the existence and uniqueness in law of the solution on an unbounded domain. We further evaluate the effects of model uncertainty through a robust control formulation based on the relative entropy, in which the lower and upper bounds of the expected eDNA concentration, together with the worst-case distortions, are obtained in closed form. The framework is applied to eDNA and flow velocity data collected for the upstream migration of Plecoglossus altivelis altivelis in a river in Japan. The results demonstrate that the closed-form bounds provide a computationally inexpensive tool for quantifying the range of eDNA concentrations that can be expected under model uncertainty.

Probability.title: From Truncation to Commitment: Persistent Context in Uniform Discrete Diffusion
Probability.summary: Uniform-state discrete diffusion models update all tokens in parallel while keeping every position revisable. Even when the commonly used top-$p$ rule leaves only one candidate at a position, that choice affects only the current reverse step and can be revised at the next sampling step. We ask what changes when selected hypotheses instead become persistent context for later predictions. We therefore propose committed reveal sampling (CRS), a training-free sampler that stores selected argmax tokens and inserts them into subsequent model inputs. Our analysis separates persistent context from truncation. Within one reverse step, adaptive top-$p$, randomized or not, reproduces the update induced by a visible token only when a likelihood-ratio ordering holds, while in a simple latent-mode model, keeping the selected token visible helps later parallel predictions agree on the same sequence-level choice. Empirically, paired experiments on Duo-distilled then separate this persistent effect from single-step top-$p$ restriction and scalar temperature scaling. Under the same finalization rule, CRS without top-$p$ truncation reaches lower generative perplexity (GenPPL) than fixed $p=0.95$ and $p=0.9$ baselines across budgets of 8--64 function evaluations (NFE). At 64 NFE, the comparison at matched unigram entropy also gives lower GenPPL for CRS, shifting the GenPPL--entropy tradeoff under this metric. Base Duo shows the same direction in a descriptive comparison, while other diversity and continuation metrics can rank these operating points differently. A distributional distance to held-out text (SOL) under a fixed GPT-2-Large representation also decreases with persistent context at the same late top-$p$ threshold. These results identify support restriction and persistent context as distinct controls of that tradeoff.

Differential Geometry.title: Existence of static axisymmetric solutions to the Einstein equations
Differential Geometry.summary: We construct smooth Riemannian metrics and scalar potentials that are invariant under a circle action and satisfy the static Einstein equations with positive cosmological constant. The underlying compact three-manifold is a ball with two disjoint open balls removed. The potential (or lapse function) is positive in the interior and vanishes at the boundary, consisting of three non-degenerate horizons. The areas of the two inner boundary components are controlled by two arbitrary parameters, namely the masses of the black holes, which are taken to be sufficiently small and comparable. Each inner horizon radius scales linearly with the individual mass parameters, while the separation of their reference centers scales as the cube root of the total mass. These two scales are assumed to be sufficiently small at different rates, whereas the cosmological length remains fixed. The main analytical challenge is to control the linearized equation and the nonlinear remainder simultaneously near the shrinking horizons, between the centers and in the outer region. Weighted Hölder estimates quantify the growth of the inverse and show that the error of an approximation joining Kottler collars to de Sitter space is small enough to close a contraction argument. Namely, we solve a reduced elliptic Einstein equation that is endowed with two obstruction tensors; varying the two axial positions removes their coefficients. The contracted Bianchi identity and an energy estimate for an auxiliary vector field (Killing field) introduced by the projection to vanish. Finally, for a fixed cosmological constant, the intrinsic metric of one of the two boundary components is sufficient to determine a static solution with simply connected interior and non-vanishing boundary gradient, up to isometry and multiplication of the potential by a positive constant.

Differential Geometry.title: Pluriclosed 3-folds with vanishing Bismut Ricci form: General theory in the quasi-regular case
Differential Geometry.summary: We study compact complex $3$-dimensional non-Kähler Bismut Ricci flat pluriclosed Hermitian manifolds (BHE) via their dimensional reduction to a special Kähler geometry in complex dimension $2$, recently obtained by Barbaro, Streets and the first and third authors. We show that in the quasi-regular case, the reduced geometry satisfies a 6th order non-linear PDE which has infinite dimensional momentum map interpretation, similar to the much studied Kähler metrics of constant scalar curvature (cscK). We use this to associate to the reduced manifold or orbifold Mabuchi and Calabi functionals, as well as to obtain obstructions for the existence of solutions in terms of the authomorphism group, paralleling results by Futaki and Calabi-Lichnerowicz-Matsushima in the cscK case. This is used to characterize the Samelson locally homogeneous BHE geometries in complex dimension 3 as the only non-Kähler BHE $3$-folds with $2$-dimensional Bott-Chern $(1,1)$-cohomology group, for which the reduced space is a smooth Kähler surface. We also discuss explicit solutions of the PDE on orthotoric Kähler orbifold surfaces, extending examples found by Couzens-Gauntlett-Martelli-Sparks in the framework of supersymmetric ${\rm AdS}_3 \times Y_7$ type IIB supergravity. Our construction yields infinitely many non-Kähler BHE structures on $S^3\times S^3$ and $S^1\times S^2 \times S^3$, which are not locally isometric to a Samelson geometry. These appear to be the first such examples.
Differential Geometry.comment: Typos and the statement of Lemma 8.1 corrected. Final version

Differential Geometry.title: Isoperimetric and total curvature inequalities in Cartan-Hadamard manifolds with nullity
Differential Geometry.summary: Using the Chern-Gauss-Bonnet theorem, we establish a sharp inequality for the total Gauss-Kronecker curvature of convex hypersurfaces in Cartan-Hadamard manifolds $M^n$ with nullity index at least $n-3$. Consequently, the Euclidean isoperimetric inequality extends to $M^n$, which proves the Cartan-Hadamard conjecture for these spaces.
Differential Geometry.comment: 8 pages; Minor revisions; Accepted for publication in Proceedings of AMS

Differential Geometry.title: Positive solutions of Yamabe-type equations with general potentials
Differential Geometry.summary: Let $(M^n,g)$ be a smooth closed connected Riemannian manifold of dimension $n\ge3$, and let $ψ\in C^\infty(M,\mathbb R)$. We prove that the equation $$ -\frac{4(n-1)}{n-2}Δ_g u+ψu=u^{\frac{n+2}{n-2}} $$ has a smooth positive solution if and only if its linear part has positive first eigenvalue. In dimensions $n\ge6$, the proof combines an energy estimate under exact local mass constraints with an intersection argument for finite cycles of atomic measures; dimensions $3\le n\le5$ follow from the theorem of Bahri and Brezis.

Differential Geometry.title: Non-Archimedean analogue of the space of valuations on convex sets
Differential Geometry.summary: In the last two decades a number of structures on the classical space of translation invariant valuations on convex bodies were discovered, e.g. product, convolution, a Fourier type transform. In this paper a non-Archimedean analogue of the space of such (even) valuations with similar structures is constructed. It is shown that, like in the classical case, the new space equipped with either product or convolution satisfies Poincaré duality and hard Lefschetz theorem.

Differential Geometry.title: Sharp diameter estimates via integral geometry
Differential Geometry.summary: We prove that the diameter of a closed embedded surface in $\mathbb{R}^3$ is always less than the integral of the magnitude of the mean curvature, divided by $π$. We also prove a sharp variant for surfaces with boundary, and apply it to address a conjecture of Miura.

Differential Geometry.title: Pseudo-Calabi Flow on Toric Variety
Differential Geometry.summary: In this paper, we prove the long time existence of the pseudo-Calabi flow on a compact toric variety for any $T^n$-invariant initial Kähler metric. If the Mabuchi functional is proper modulo automorphisms, the flow converges exponentially to a constant scalar curvature Kähler (cscK) metric. In particular, this gives a flow proof that properness of the K-energy implies the existence of a cscK metric in the toric setting.

Differential Geometry.title: Small eigenvalues of negatively curved manifolds with finite volume
Differential Geometry.summary: We obtain upper bounds for the number of small eigenvalues of complete Riemannian manifolds with negative sectional curvature and finite volume.

Differential Geometry.title: Beyond Brown's radial tests: admissibility, parabolicity, and a doubling-Poincaré prior that neither test decides
Differential Geometry.summary: For the estimation of a normal mean in $\mathbb{R}^m$ under quadratic loss, Brown (1971) proved that a generalized Bayes estimator $δ_F$ is admissible if and only if a diffusion attached to the marginal $f^*$ of the prior $F$ is recurrent, and gave two radial tests: a sphere-average test for recurrence and a ray test for transience. He observed that both tests can be silent. We read his theory as the potential theory of the weighted Euclidean space $(\mathbb{R}^m,f^*\,dx)$ and ask what the modern theory of recurrence on weighted manifolds adds inside the zone where neither test applies. Three results. (A) If $f^*\,dx$ is doubling and supports a scale-invariant Poincaré inequality, the sphere test is already complete: recurrence, Brown's sphere test and the ball-volume test are equivalent, so geometric criteria can add decidable cases only on the inadmissible side. (B) They do add one. An explicit prior on $\mathbb{R}^3$ whose marginal is small along a lattice of circles at dyadic scales with spacing equal to the square root of the scale, is doubling and Poincaré, silences both of Brown's tests, and is transient by the ball-volume test; its generalized Bayes estimator is inadmissible.
