Signal Processing.summary: This paper presents a bioimpedance IC combining an on-demand push-pull driver and continuous-time $ΔΣ$ T-D readout to address the trade-off between SNR, accuracy and power consumption. The driver delivers 200$μ$App with $\leq$0.14% THD while consuming 80.3$μ$A. Using a 6MHz clock, the readout achieves 53.6ps effective timing resolution at a 4k$Ω$ load (0.1-4Hz noise integration). The IC achieves 96.1dB peak SNR, 99.8% magnitude accuracy and 0.13$^{\circ}$ phase error at a maximum power consumption of 140.5$μ$W.
Signal Processing.comment: Accepted for publication in ISSCC 2027, Paper 12.6. 8 pages, 7 figures

Signal Processing.title: Joint End-to-End Training of Weighted BP Decoder Ensembles
Signal Processing.summary: Ensemble decoding improves decoding reliability by combining component decoders with complementary failure events. Existing approaches typically obtain this diversity from code-specific structure, such as code automorphisms, multiple parity-check representations, or targeted modifications of the message-passing graph. In this work, we instead learn the diversity of an ensemble of weighted belief propagation decoders by jointly optimizing trainable Tanner-graph edge weights. A central design question is how the training objective should distribute gradient among the ensemble members to promote complementary decoding behavior. To this end, we compare four ensemble objectives under direct gradient-based optimization and identify best-member training as the most effective approach. For a (64,32) progressive edge-growth (PEG) low-density parity-check (LDPC) code, the resulting ensemble outperforms the considered trained and untrained belief-propagation-based ensemble baselines. With 10 members, it provides a gain of approximately 0.66 dB over a single belief propagation decoder at a target frame error rate (FER) of $10^{-4}$. Similar behavior is observed for a (128,64) CCSDS LDPC code, indicating that the learned complementarity is not specific to PEG. Although the ensemble performance improves substantially, all trained members show a higher standalone FER. The gain therefore results from learned specialization and complementary failure events rather than uniformly improved component decoders.
Signal Processing.comment: 6 pages, 7 figures, submitted to an IEEE conference for possible publication

Signal Processing.title: Cross-Band Movable-Antenna Communications under Frequency-Dependent Multipath
Signal Processing.summary: Movable antennas (MAs) provide additional spatial degrees of freedom by adapting their physical positions to the propagation environment. However, existing studies mainly focus on single-band or contiguous wideband transmission, leaving the cross-band spatial behavior of MAs under frequency-dependent multipath propagation largely unexplored. To address this gap, we investigate a downlink multi-band MA communication system where a common physical MA configuration is shared across multiple communication bands. Such sharing induces an inherent configuration conflict, as different bands often favor substantially divergent MA configurations. We first develop a frequency-dependent multipath channel model with shared propagation geometry but band-dependent multipath component powers and phases. Using this model, we formulate a sum-rate maximization problem by jointly optimizing user-band assignment, MA positioning, and transmit precoding. We further establish a cross-band spatial scaling relationship for the normalized channel power and derive both a position-independent channel gain upper bound and a sum-rate upper bound. Based on these results, we propose a cross-band analysis-guided optimization (CAGO) algorithm and a cross-band graph transformer (CBGT) to reduce online optimization complexity. Numerical results validate the derived cross-band spatial relationship and show that CAGO consistently outperforms the narrowband, wideband, and fixed-antenna benchmarks while remaining close to the idealized independent-MA benchmark. Additionally, CBGT with online refinement achieves near-CAGO sum-rate performance with substantially lower online computational cost, providing a practical framework for exploiting the spatial reconfiguration capability of MAs in multi-band communication systems.

Signal Processing.title: Movable Antenna Empowered Near-Field Sensing via Antenna Position Optimization
Signal Processing.summary: Movable antenna (MA) technology exhibits great promise for enhancing the sensing capabilities of future sixth-generation (6G) networks due to its capability to alter antenna array geometry. With the growing prevalence of near-field propagation at ultra-high frequencies, this paper focuses on the application of one-dimensional (1D) and two-dimensional (2D) MA arrays for near-field sensing to jointly estimate the angle and distance information about a target. First, for the 1D MA array scenario, to gain insights into MA-enhanced near-field sensing, we investigate two simplified cases with only angle-of-arrival (AoA) or distance estimation, respectively, assuming that the other information is already known. The worst-case Cramer Rao bounds (CRBs) on the mean square errors (MSEs) of the AoA estimation and the distance estimation are derived in these two cases. Then, we jointly optimize the positions of the MAs within the 1D array to minimize these CRBs and derive their closed-form solutions, which yield an identical array geometry to MA-enhanced far-field sensing. For the more challenging joint AoA and distance estimation, since the associated worst-case CRB is a highly complex and non-convex function with respect to the MA positions, a discrete sampling-based approach is proposed to sequentially update the MA positions and obtain an efficient suboptimal solution. Furthermore, we investigate the worst-case CRB minimization problems for a 2D MA array under various conditions and extend our proposed algorithms to solve them efficiently. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed MA-enhanced near-field sensing scheme dramatically outperforms conventional fixed-position antennas (FPAs). Moreover, the joint angle and distance estimation results in a different array geometry from that in the individual estimation of angle/distance or far-field sensing.

Signal Processing.title: Extended Target Imaging in Non-Ideal Distributed ISAC Systems: A Hierarchical Off-Grid Approach
Signal Processing.summary: In future integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems, distributed multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) architectures offer high-resolution imaging capabilities. However, reconstructing real-world extended targets is physically challenging due to continuous anisotropic surface scattering and complex occlusions, especially in the presence of system synchronization errors. To overcome these limitations, this paper proposes a hierarchical two-stage computational imaging framework for extended target reconstruction. In Phase I, an incoherent coarse imaging process is performed to serve as a reliable initializer for subsequent high-resolution coherent image generation. By performing line-of-sight (LOS) interference suppression and leveraging network-wide topological constraints, timing and phase offsets are calibrated. This enables image construction by back-projection (BP) and the coarse identification of target contours using the probabilistic Hough transform (PHT). In Phase II, a joint target position and orientation off-grid compensation model is established, capturing Lambertian diffuse and specular reflections on continuous facets via a first-order Taylor expansion. To tackle severe occlusion and spatial grid mismatches, we propose the bilinear off-grid approximate message passing (BiOG-AMP) algorithm. BiOG-AMP iteratively updates surface visibility and dictionary matrices, enforcing physical consistency across distributed transceiver views. Theoretical analysis derives compressed sensing error bounds, Fisher information limits, and linearization error scaling. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed framework effectively eliminates imaging artifacts and exhibits superior robustness against synchronization offsets and grid mismatches compared to state-of-the-art baselines.
Signal Processing.comment: under review in IEEE Transactions on Wireless Communications

Signal Processing.title: Statistical Design of Multi-BD-RIS-Assisted User-Centric Cell-Free Massive MIMO
Signal Processing.summary: We study the uplink of a user-centric (UC) cell-free massive MIMO system assisted by multiple beyond-diagonal reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (BD-RISs), under imperfect channel state information (CSI) and pilot reuse. The BD-RISs are modeled as reciprocal, lossless, group-connected scattering networks. We first derive the minimum mean-square error (MMSE) estimation statistics for each user's aggregate channel to its serving access points (APs). To avoid frequent CSI acquisition and RIS reconfiguration, we optimize the BD-RIS scattering matrices using long-term channel statistics, allowing their configurations to remain fixed over multiple coherence blocks. Specifically, we minimize the sum of normalized mean-square errors (NMSEs) of the MMSE aggregate channel estimators, subject to the symmetry and unitarity constraints of the group-connected architecture. We develop a product-manifold Riemannian optimization algorithm and analyze its convergence and computational complexity. To evaluate uplink spectral efficiency (SE), we separately derive a closed-form expression for the effective SINR under maximum ratio (MR) combining at the central processing unit (CPU) and establish a lower bound on the achievable ergodic SE. The SINR derivation accounts for the statistical dependence among channels associated with different APs due to shared BD-RIS-assisted propagation paths, including cross-AP second-order statistics under pilot reuse. Numerical results show that moderate group connectivity retains most of the NMSE improvements achieved by full connectivity, with larger optimization gains as BD-RIS-assisted paths strengthen relative to direct AP-user links. They also reveal that lower estimation NMSE does not necessarily lead to higher uplink SE.
Signal Processing.comment: 6 pages, 5 figures. Submitted to IEEE ICC 2027 on Oct 16th 2026

Signal Processing.title: Array Rotation in Near-Field ISAC: Communication, Detection, and Estimation Under Low-Complexity Transmit Architectures
Signal Processing.summary: This paper studies near-field integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) with a rotatable base-station array under an exact spherical-wave propagation model. For a general transmit covariance, we derive a Cramér--Rao bound (CRB) decomposition that separates target-side geometry from transmit-covariance-dependent terms. We then specialize the framework to two representative low-complexity architectures: a single-stream superposition architecture, and a dual-waveform split architecture design. We characterize the communication-, detection-, and estimation-optimal rotations for each architecture using the exact finite-array model. In addition, we show how a second-order approximation yields compact approximate expressions for the optimal rotation angles. We also study uncertainty in the target state used for beamforming design through a correlated Gaussian perturbation model, and derive approximations of the optimal robust rotation angles for target sensing and detection. The analysis shows that the two architectures behave differently under rotation: the single-stream design can align communication and detection tasks, whereas the dual-waveform design exhibits a direct communication--detection tradeoff and can incur a larger communication loss when sensing is prioritized. Numerical results show clear gains over a fixed array orientation, especially for range estimation, and close agreement between the approximate and exact rotation choices. Detection is less affected by target-state errors than estimation in the considered cases.

Systems and Control.title: Asymmetric-Information Resource Allocation Games: An LP Approach to Purposeful Deception
Systems and Control.summary: In this work, we introduce the Deceptive Resource Allocation Game (DRAG), which studies purposeful deception within a Bayesian game framework. In DRAG, a Defender allocates resources across the true asset and several decoys to influence an Attacker's beliefs and actions, with the goal of diverting the Attacker away from the true asset. We seek to characterize purposeful deception, whereby the Defender deceives only when doing so improves its performance. To this end, we solve for the Perfect Bayesian Nash Equilibrium (PBNE) of the corresponding game. We show that, despite the coupled belief-policy interdependence, the problem admits an efficient, non-iterative linear programming formulation. Numerical results demonstrate that the resulting policies naturally balance effective allocation and belief manipulation, giving rise to purposeful and emergent deceptive behaviors.

Systems and Control.title: Efficiency--Complexity Tradeoff and Constrained Percolation
Systems and Control.summary: We study the efficiency--complexity tradeoff for resource-limited agents through directed first-passage percolation. Nonnegative i.i.d. edge weights represent physical energy expenditure, while the logarithmic size of a constrained path family measures representational complexity. For translation-invariant families, a path-joining property yields deterministic large-distance costs in rational directions and joint convexity in constraint parameter and direction, under suitable moment and feasibility assumptions. Our main result concerns the limiting cost parameterized by path-family entropy. Using techniques from analytic combinatorics in several variables (ACSV), we establish its almost-sure existence and joint continuity in entropy and direction for nested families satisfying additional generating-function conditions, on the corresponding entropy range. Path-count asymptotics supply the change of parameter linking this cost to the constraint-parameterized cost. Two planar examples constrain the number of turns or the number of East-runs of length at least two.

Systems and Control.title: Data-Driven LQR with Uncertainty Refinement and Domain Randomization---Part~II: Fisher-Majorized Certified Policy Iteration
Systems and Control.summary: Building on the uncertainty description developed in Part~I, this paper introduces a Fisher-majorized domain-randomized generalized policy iteration framework for data-driven linear quadratic regulator (LQR) synthesis. At each iteration, partial Bellman evaluation over a fixed batch of uncertainty realizations produces a structured Sylvester policy-improvement step. A residual-weighted Fisher curvature controls the policy-induced variation in the stationary covariance and converts the Sylvester model into a certified upper bound on the cost change, thereby guaranteeing descent for every accepted step. A check-and-correct mechanism then certifies stability over the entire uncertainty support, rather than only over the sampled realizations. Consequently, every iterate is robustly stabilizing and monotonically decreases the fixed-batch objective. The Fisher truncation and stability correction become inactive after finitely many times. The objective gap then contracts linearly to a floor determined by the dispersion of the realization-wise Riccati targets and by measurement noise. In the absence of measurement noise, this floor vanishes when the realization-wise targets coincide.

Systems and Control.title: Data-Driven LQR with Uncertainty Refinement and Domain Randomization---Part~I: Certified Uncertainty Refinement
Systems and Control.summary: Learning controllers from trajectories corrupted by process and measurement noise is difficult when the system matrices and the noise covariances are unknown: noisy regressors bias least squares, and model uncertainty cannot be quantified without the noise covariance, which can only be estimated from residuals of the uncertain model. This paper, Part~I of a two-part study, resolves both obstacles with a finite-sample framework that certifies, and iteratively refines, uncertainty sets for the model, the noise in the collected data, and the noise covariance. A closed-loop parametrization based on delayed instrumental variables (IVs) removes the bias and assigns to every candidate model exactly one noise sequence that reproduces the data. Learning this noise breaks the circular dependence: the noise sequences give the covariance estimate directly, models whose noise violates the prior or the statistical certificates are discarded, and the surviving models yield a tighter covariance certificate. Several delayed instruments further tighten the model set and give a certified test of data consistency. We prove finite-sample containment of the true model, noise, and covariance, recursive nesting, and convergence at the IV rate. Part~II uses these certificates for domain-randomized linear quadratic regulator synthesis.

Systems and Control.title: Data-based Low-conservative Nonlinear Safe Control Learning
Systems and Control.summary: This paper develops a data-driven safe control framework for nonlinear discrete-time systems with parametric uncertainty and additive disturbances. The proposed approach constructs a data-consistent closed-loop representation that enables controller synthesis and safety certification directly from data. Unlike existing methods that treat unmodeled nonlinearities as global worst-case uncertainties using Lipschitz bounds, the proposed approach embeds nonlinear terms directly into the invariance conditions via a geometry-aware difference-of-convex formulation. This enables facet- and direction-specific convexification, avoiding both nonlinearity cancellation and the excessive conservatism induced by uniform global bounds. We further propose a vertex-dependent controller construction that enforces convexity and contractivity conditions locally on the active facets associated with each vertex, thereby enlarging the class of certifiable invariant sets. For systems subject to additive disturbances, disturbance effects are embedded directly into the verification conditions through optimized, geometry-dependent bounds, rather than via uniform margin inflation, yielding less conservative robust safety guarantees. As a result, the proposed methods can certify substantially larger safe sets, naturally accommodate joint state and input constraints, and provide data-driven safety guarantees. The simulation results show a significant improvement in both nonlinearity tolerance and the size of the certified safe set.

Systems and Control.title: Hyperscale Data Centers as Wide-Area Damping Actuators for Low-Inertia Power Systems
Systems and Control.summary: Low-inertia power systems need fast damping actuators as synchronous generation is displaced by inverter-based resources. This paper evaluates hyperscale data-center loads controlled through Dynamic Voltage and Frequency Scaling (DVFS) as wide-area damping actuators. A DAE-consistent bus-input matrix is validated against the ANDES reduced state matrix and a finite-difference input check. On the Kundur two-area benchmark, Bus 10 ranks highest among non-generator buses for the 0.647 Hz inter-area mode. A classical washout-plus-lead-lag controller raises damping from 3.43% to approximately 6%. Modern 10-50 ms battery and DVFS actuators require comparable peak modulation for the same small-signal damping target. Compared with a closest same-system data-center-frequency-droop baseline, the wide-area controller offers a clearer advantage: at comparable peak MW, droop reaches 4.76% damping, while reaching 6% requires approximately twice the peak modulation. In the Pade-delay model, damping crosses the open-loop value at 443 ms for the 10 ms DVFS actuator versus 374 ms for the 50 ms BESS case. Reduced-order saturation stress tests show that a 2 MW envelope is non-binding for modal, fault-cleared-equivalent, and line-outage-equivalent disturbances, but can bind under generator-trip-equivalent stress. IEEE 39-bus tests confirm the DAE-based ranking procedure and show that high-residue buses may require more phase compensation than a single lead-lag stage can supply.
Systems and Control.comment: 24 pages, 7 figures. Author manuscript of the published journal article

Systems and Control.title: Stability and stabilization of semilinear single-track vehicle models with distributed tire friction dynamics via singular perturbation analysis
Systems and Control.summary: This paper investigates the stability and stabilization of semilinear single-track vehicle models with distributed tire friction dynamics, modeled as interconnections of ordinary differential equations (ODEs) and hyperbolic partial differential equations (PDEs). Motivated by the long-standing practice of neglecting transient tire dynamics in vehicle modeling and control, a rigorous justification is provided for such simplifications using singular perturbation theory. A perturbation parameter, defined as the ratio between a characteristic rolling contact length and the vehicle's longitudinal speed, is introduced to formalize the time-scale separation between rigid-body motion and tire dynamics. For sufficiently small values of this parameter, it is demonstrated that standard finite-dimensional techniques can be applied to analyze the local stability of equilibria and to design stabilizing controllers. Whilst the proposed controllers build on classical approaches, the novelty of this work lies in establishing the first singular perturbation framework for ODE-PDE vehicle models with distributed tire dynamics, providing a theoretical justification for their quasi-static reduction and for the use of finite-dimensional tools for analysis and control design.

Systems and Control.title: Energy-Based Fault Detection and Isolation Framework for Flat Port-Hamiltonian Mechanical Systems
Systems and Control.summary: Fault diagnosis during regulated motion requires informative signals even when feedback attenuates tracking deviations. This paper develops an energy-based diagnostic framework that constructs mechanical port-power residuals without a dedicated dynamic observer. Spectral Hamiltonian Algebraic Power Evaluation (SHAPE) combines port-Hamiltonian variables and differential flatness to generate nominal power references from planned motion for fully actuated mechanical systems with collocated actuation. Subtracting these references from commanded effort multiplied by measured flow yields residuals whose final evaluation requires neither recursive observer updates nor measured-state dynamics calculations. Continuous wavelet transform (CWT) scalograms and a shared-encoder convolutional neural network are used to distinguish nominal operation, actuator loss of effectiveness, anomalous friction, and vibration from complete trajectories. Evaluation uses a simulated six degree of freedom Kinova manipulator under model predictive control and fixed plant-model mismatch, with single faults at a specified joint. Across five training seeds and 3000 held-out test runs, SHAPE-CWT achieves a mean accuracy of 84.69 percent, versus 81.67 percent for torque residuals and 97.17 percent for the generalized momentum observer under common CWT processing. The respective sample standard deviations are 0.70, 0.70, and 0.37 percentage points. These results demonstrate useful fault-type discrimination from algebraic power residuals, while severity-excitation profiles and offline velocity perturbations reveal limits to their diagnostic capability.

Systems and Control.title: Physics-Informed Graph-Based Safe RL with Constraint-Specific Critics for Community Battery Coordination in Distribution Network
Systems and Control.summary: High penetrations of distributed energy resources (DERs) and fast-varying electric vehicle (EV) charging intensify voltage and line-limit violations in distribution networks (DNs), making safe, low-cost operation increasingly challenging. This paper proposes a physics-informed safe deep reinforcement learning (DRL) framework for coordinating community battery energy storage systems to mitigate constraint violations while minimizing operating cost. To represent nonlocal spatiotemporal interactions, we develop a dual-level physics-informed graph representation in which line impedance and capacity shape spatial information propagation, while power-balance, voltage-profile, and flow-reconstruction losses regularize the latent state toward control-relevant physical consistency. Building on this representation, we develop Lagrangian Dedicated-Critic PPO (LDCPPO), which implements constraint-specific value decomposition: independent reward and cost critics preserve heterogeneous voltage- and line-loading-related learning signals and combine their advantages only during the Lagrangian policy update. Case studies on DNs with high rooftop photovoltaic penetration and EV charging demonstrate that the proposed method reduces the key voltage-violation degree by up to 80.5% compared with the tested baselines, while also achieving the lowest voltage-violation count and line-overload degree with competitive operating cost.

Systems and Control.title: Nodal Inertia Pricing for RoCoF Security with Integration of Synchronous and Virtual Resources
Systems and Control.summary: Frequency regulation is becoming a more significant challenge in the undergoing low-carbon transition of modern power systems, which is heavily rely on system inertia provision. In the context of market-based energy allocation, reasonable valuation of the system inertia is crucial to its procurement, namely a worthy price should be determined for inertia providers. However, current research on the value of inertia remains insufficient, particularly during the initial phase immediately following a contingency, a critical period when the system primarily relies on the inherent inertia from conventional units and pre-engaged virtual inertia resources. Furthermore, it is found in existing studies that the Center of Inertia (COI) models exhibit significant deviations from actual physical conditions. For market-oriented reforms that explore individual differences, COI models also fail to capture the heterogeneous contributions of inertia at different nodes to system security. Given these circumstances, this paper proposes a nodal inertia pricing mechanism via a day-ahead unit commitment and inertia co-optimization model with nodal resolution. Following the proposed pricing scheme, the day- or hour-ahead inertia provision is monetized and promoted, providing regional guidance to units and devices with virtual inertia provision, which is further verified by simulation results of the South East Australia Power System.

Systems and Control.title: Hybrid-time PINNs: Discontinuity-Aware Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Learning Hybrid Dynamical Systems
Systems and Control.summary: Hybrid dynamical systems flow continuously but jump at discrete events. Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) fit data while enforcing known dynamics, but a single network is smooth in time and cannot model these jumps. We show that the more closely a PINN follows a jump, the larger its physics loss must be. We propose hybrid-time PINNs (HT-PINNs), which assign one network to each flow interval of the hybrid time domain and train the networks jointly with the jump times and the unknown parameters. The number of jumps and the sequence of modes are found by enumeration. HT-PINNs recover the number of jumps and the restitution coefficient of a bouncing ball. In a MuJoCo simulation of robotic disassembly, where a robot pulls a press-fitted pin out of a housing through a spring, HT-PINNs find the number of jumps and the sequence of modes, and estimate the static and kinetic friction coefficients with small errors of 0.1% and 1.7%.

Systems and Control.title: A Personalized and Adaptive Intelligent Tutoring System for Psychomotor Learning
Systems and Control.summary: Intelligent tutoring systems (ITSs) have advanced learner motivation and personalization in cognitive domains, but extending these gains to psychomotor tasks remains challenging. Existing psychomotor ITSs rely on learner models built before instruction or updated once per module, leaving open how to use real-time assessments of learner cognitive state for finer-grained personalization. Psychomotor learning involves multiple tutoring objectives, including calibrating self-confidence to performance, calibrating workload per the Yerkes-Dodson Law, and driving skill progression toward higher learning stages. How to balance these objectives for learners, and adjust that balance over time, remains open. This study proposes and evaluates an online personalization algorithm that continuously reprioritizes tutoring objectives to match learners' evolving needs. Rather than weighting objectives equally, the actor-critic-inspired algorithm dynamically updates reward weights using recent measures of self-confidence, workload, and performance. These weights inform a multi-input, multi-output cognitive control framework that synthesizes learner-specific tutoring policies via model-based planning. The approach was evaluated in a human-subject study (N = 40) with a 2D quadrotor landing task. Clustering of the learned reward weights revealed distinct prioritization patterns across learners, indicating the algorithm captures heterogeneity in learner needs. Learners whose weights shifted more substantially tended to reach higher final performance, and those whose weights consistently emphasized workload calibration achieved the strongest outcomes. These findings advance online learner modeling and control-based personalization in psychomotor ITSs, showing how adaptive tutoring can better support learning by aligning instructional decisions with learners' evolving cognitive and performance states.

Systems and Control.title: POMDPs with Lipschitz-Continuous Belief-Dependent Rewards Have Lipschitz-Continuous Value Functions
Systems and Control.summary: We establish the vector (or elementwise) Lipschitz continuity of value functions for partially observed Markov decision processes (POMDPs) with reward functions that are Lipschitz-continuous functions of the posterior probability distribution of the state (i.e., the belief). Our results significantly tighten existing Lipschitz results for this class of POMDPs on infinite horizons, with previous results only yielding finite constants for discount factors less than 0.5, while our results yield finite Lipschitz constants for all discount factors less than 1. The significance of our Lipschitz constants is illustrated through their use in heuristic search value iteration (HSVI) to construct (finite) piecewise-linear value function approximations.
Systems and Control.comment: 7 pages, 3 figures, accepted for presentation at 2026 IEEE Conference on Decision and Control (CDC)

Systems and Control.title: Convex Inner Approximations for Safe AC Dispatch With Device Dynamics
Systems and Control.summary: Safe AC dispatch requires both feasible operating points and enough ramping capability to reach the next target. This paper constructs convex inner approximations that connect nonlinear network feasibility, constrained device response, and dispatch-interval tracking. A fixed-point certificate enforces AC operating limits under bounded load uncertainty. Componentwise response envelopes convert heterogeneous device dynamics into affine conditions on measured states and power references. A command governor then combines these conditions with available ramping capability and a hard terminal-error bound. It selects an admissible target through a minimum-deviation objective and holds the corresponding reference while reserved fast regulation remains active. The resulting quadratic program optimizes controllable references and auxiliary variables. Tests on the IEEE 39- and 118-bus systems include 96 single-target executions and 64 transitions in continuous dispatch sequences at five- and fifteen-minute intervals. All 160 transitions satisfy the AC constraints, independent balancing-generator capability checks, and the prescribed regulation-adjusted terminal accuracy. Complete admission-cycle medians are 3.45 and 8.79 ms. A connected synthetic system with 3,200 buses and 1,000 generating units extends the computational assessment to 999 independent references, with a median cycle time of \LargeMedian{} s. The construction provides a tractable link between available ramping capability and safe, timely execution of AC dispatch.

Systems and Control.title: Performance Gaps Between Open-Loop, Certainty-Equivalent, and Optimal Control Under Action-Dependent Observations
Systems and Control.summary: In dynamical systems, feedback can improve performance by allowing decisions to depend on past observations, rather than being designed a priori. Under full observation, the current state is sufficient for decision-making; under partial observation, the controller must instead estimate the state from measurements. When actions also affect observations, control can have a dual role: actions influence both the state and the information available for future decisions. This interaction can invalidate certainty-equivalent (CE) control, a widely used strategy that applies state feedback policies as if the estimated state were the true state. We ask when this suboptimality leads to a quantitative performance gap that grows with the horizon. We study this question in a linear-quadratic system with bilinear observations by comparing the optimal policy, certainty-equivalent control, and the optimal open-loop (OL) policy. We identify an instance-dependent information-strength parameter $q$ and establish distinct performance regimes as $q$ varies. When $q$ is sufficiently small, we show that no policy can improve over OL control by more than $O(1)$ cumulative cost. For large values of $q$, we find that CE achieves an $Ω(T)$ advantage over OL control. Our main finding is that for intermediate values of $q$, we can construct a policy that occasionally probes for information and achieves an $Ω(T)$ advantage over OL control while CE only achieves an $O(1)$ advantage, establishing an $Ω(T)$ gap between CE and optimal control. Our analysis relies on a regret decomposition that captures the tradeoff between the immediate cost of gathering information and its future benefit.

Systems and Control.title: From Caveman to COBA: Coordinated Optimization-Based Attacks on Grid-Edge Smart Inverters in DER-Rich Power Systems
Systems and Control.summary: Aggregation platforms and smart-inverter control channels can allow a compromised coordination layer to alter active- and reactive-power commands across a geographically distributed DER fleet. This paper introduces the Coordinated Optimization-Based Attack (COBA), which uses network information and location-specific DER P/Q setpoints to maximize thermal loading on a selected transmission corridor. COBA is compared with low-information CAV baselines limited to a single uniform fleet command: all-off, all-on, maximum reactive absorption, or maximum reactive injection. The Hawaii Synthetic Grid-37 Buses case is evaluated with rooftop-photovoltaic-like capability aggregated at 20 selected 69-kV buses and verified using MATPOWER power flow. Under the case's single-reference-bus balancing convention, COBA overloads B86 (WAIALUA69-WAIANAE69) near 30% penetration and B51 (COCONUT69-PALM69) near 55%, while same-target uniform loadings remain lower and uniform commands primarily stress other natural weak lines. The results show that topology, target selection, and command capability determine DER-induced thermal risk beyond aggregate penetration alone.

Systems and Control.title: PMU Foundation Model Bridge: A Tool for Connecting Synchrophasor Streams to Time Series Foundation Models
Systems and Control.summary: This paper presents PMU Foundation Model Bridge, an open source tool that connects online phasor measurement unit (PMU) or phasor data concentrator (PDC) streams to publicly available time series foundation models (TSFM). Through a desktop interface or command line interface, users can select measurement channels, define preprocessing, choose TSFMs, and configure outputs. In the initial release, 4 publicly available TSFMs were supported, including Chronos-2, TimesFM 2.5, Timestral, and TimesFM-3. The tool supports both file and synchrophasor streaming outputs, therefore enabling both offline use and integration into C37.118-based online workflow applications. In addition to supporting raw synchrophasor data, the framework provides a preprocessing layer for deriving customized additional quantities for forecasting. The tool is validated using a virtual PMU and real-time laboratory measurements from a frequency disturbance recorder (FDR). The tool aims to support community research on combining synchrophasor technology with TSFMs.

Information Theory.title: The Critical Renyi Order for Sharp Minimax Channel Design
Information Theory.summary: We study categorical channel design under a bound on the maximum directed pairwise Renyi divergence. We determine exactly which orders make randomized response optimal in every dimension and at every finite budget: the orders strictly above one and at most two. In that range we identify the full information-trace frontier and its unique optimal anchored law. The channel is visibly thinned randomized response below a uniquely defined threshold and ordinary randomized response above it. A fixed-second-moment inequality and a second-order variational argument reduce arbitrary channel columns to singleton templates. Above order two, an explicit subset-selection channel beats every mixture of singleton templates in a finite dimension. The trace frontier also gives the exact finite-sample minimax risk among all unbiased real-valued vector estimators, and the asymptotic minimax risk among all estimators for every budget sequence with diverging total information. Appendices compare pure local privacy and distinguish homogeneous shuffle contamination from arbitrary neighboring datasets.
Information Theory.comment: v2: complete rewrite with a new title; 23 pages; ancillary Python script. The v1 shuffle privacy envelope is restricted to homogeneous contamination (Appendix D), with a counterexample for arbitrary neighbors

Information Theory.title: Partial Information Decomposition When Some Sources Are Known: A Source Chain Rule and a No-Go Theorem
Information Theory.summary: Partial information decomposition (PID) splits the information that several sources carry about a target into atoms, distinguished by which collections of sources give access to them. We ask how such a decomposition should behave when some of the sources are already known. The access structure of the atoms suggests one answer: discard the atoms that the known sources provide and regroup the rest according to which further sources unlock them. The classical construction of conditional information suggests another: recompute the decomposition under the conditional distributions and average. We show that the two answers agree, atom by atom, exactly when redundant information obeys a source chain rule, an analogue of the chain rule of mutual information: when the same sources are added to several collections, the enlarged collections share everything the added sources provide and, beyond that, exactly what the original collections share once the added sources are known. The rule divides established measures of redundant information, so that adopting or rejecting it genuinely narrows the choice of measure. Our main result is a no-go theorem: for three or more sources, the source chain rule and local positivity, the requirement that all atoms be nonnegative, cannot hold together in any PID.

Information Theory.title: Learning Representative Port Subsets for Efficient Fluid Antenna Systems
Information Theory.summary: Fluid antenna systems (FASs) provide many candidate ports, but probing all ports for each channel realization incurs substantial online overhead. We study a complementary offline problem: compress the candidate-port space once and reuse the compressed set across future channel realizations. The method collects optimal ports from sampled training realizations, requiring only one scan of the candidate ports per realization. On a DeepMIMO 7-by-7 FAS with 49 candidate ports, 120 training realizations yield 27 representative ports on average while retaining 99.995% of the channel power gain achieved by exhaustive port selection.

Information Theory.title: Extremal diagonal-coherent binary codes: shortened Hamming cores, deep holes, and the 64 I-Ching hexagrams
Information Theory.summary: Each of the 64 hexagrams of the I-Ching, or Book of Changes, is a stack of six Yin-Yang lines and is therefore a binary vector of length 6; the eight hexagrams formed by repeating a single trigram span a doubled-trigram subspace $Δ$. We ask which binary $[6,3,3]$ codes are compatible with this trigram structure. We show that a $[6,3,3]$ code meets $Δ$ in at most four codewords, that the four are then forced to be the doubled trigrams Earth, Fire, Wind and Lake, and that exactly two codes attain this bound: the shortened Hamming code $\mathcal C_A$ and its dual. Since $\mathcal C_A$ has covering radius 2, its eight codewords, their radius-one balls, and its eight deep holes together reconstruct all 64 hexagrams. In general, we call a binary code of length $2m$ with $d \ge 3$ diagonal-coherent if it contains the half of the diagonal subspace $\{(u,u)\}$ coming from even-weight vectors $u$ -- the largest part of that subspace a single-error-correcting code can contain -- and extremal if its dimension is as large as possible. For $m\ge2$ and $r=\lceil\log_2(2m+1)\rceil$, we determine the number $N(m)$ of extremal diagonal-coherent codes with parameters $[\,2m,\ 2m-r,\ \ge3\,]$, show that diagonal coherence entails no loss of redundancy, and determine their minimum distances. We also put these codes in a normal form, determine their hulls, and show that each has covering radius $2$ with exactly $2^r-1-2m$ deep-hole cosets. Finally we propose three open problems.

Information Theory.title: A Proof of the Langberg-Médard Conjecture
Information Theory.summary: In communication networks, network coding allows intermediate nodes to combine messages, achieving transmission rates unattainable by routing alone in many multicast settings. In multiple unicast, where each source sends a message only to its prescribed destination, the precise capability boundary between coding and fractional routing has long remained unresolved. In this context, the Langberg-Médard conjecture asserts that if all sources in a directed network transmit independent messages at a common rate and every destination can recover all source messages by network coding, then replacing every arc by an undirected edge of equal capacity yields a network in which fractional routing can simultaneously deliver each source's message to its prescribed destination at the same common rate. We prove the Langberg-Médard conjecture for any number of source-destination pairs and arbitrary network topology. More generally, for an undirected network with a given source set and a disjoint set of allowed destinations, we establish a necessary and sufficient cut-capacity condition for simultaneous unit-rate fractional routing under every assignment of an allowed destination to each source. Networks satisfying the hypothesis of the Langberg-Médard conjecture necessarily satisfy this cut condition, so the conjecture follows as a direct corollary.

Information Theory.title: Joint End-to-End Training of Weighted BP Decoder Ensembles
Information Theory.summary: Ensemble decoding improves decoding reliability by combining component decoders with complementary failure events. Existing approaches typically obtain this diversity from code-specific structure, such as code automorphisms, multiple parity-check representations, or targeted modifications of the message-passing graph. In this work, we instead learn the diversity of an ensemble of weighted belief propagation decoders by jointly optimizing trainable Tanner-graph edge weights. A central design question is how the training objective should distribute gradient among the ensemble members to promote complementary decoding behavior. To this end, we compare four ensemble objectives under direct gradient-based optimization and identify best-member training as the most effective approach. For a (64,32) progressive edge-growth (PEG) low-density parity-check (LDPC) code, the resulting ensemble outperforms the considered trained and untrained belief-propagation-based ensemble baselines. With 10 members, it provides a gain of approximately 0.66 dB over a single belief propagation decoder at a target frame error rate (FER) of $10^{-4}$. Similar behavior is observed for a (128,64) CCSDS LDPC code, indicating that the learned complementarity is not specific to PEG. Although the ensemble performance improves substantially, all trained members show a higher standalone FER. The gain therefore results from learned specialization and complementary failure events rather than uniformly improved component decoders.
Information Theory.comment: 6 pages, 7 figures, submitted to an IEEE conference for possible publication

Information Theory.title: Movable Antenna Empowered Near-Field Sensing via Antenna Position Optimization
Information Theory.summary: Movable antenna (MA) technology exhibits great promise for enhancing the sensing capabilities of future sixth-generation (6G) networks due to its capability to alter antenna array geometry. With the growing prevalence of near-field propagation at ultra-high frequencies, this paper focuses on the application of one-dimensional (1D) and two-dimensional (2D) MA arrays for near-field sensing to jointly estimate the angle and distance information about a target. First, for the 1D MA array scenario, to gain insights into MA-enhanced near-field sensing, we investigate two simplified cases with only angle-of-arrival (AoA) or distance estimation, respectively, assuming that the other information is already known. The worst-case Cramer Rao bounds (CRBs) on the mean square errors (MSEs) of the AoA estimation and the distance estimation are derived in these two cases. Then, we jointly optimize the positions of the MAs within the 1D array to minimize these CRBs and derive their closed-form solutions, which yield an identical array geometry to MA-enhanced far-field sensing. For the more challenging joint AoA and distance estimation, since the associated worst-case CRB is a highly complex and non-convex function with respect to the MA positions, a discrete sampling-based approach is proposed to sequentially update the MA positions and obtain an efficient suboptimal solution. Furthermore, we investigate the worst-case CRB minimization problems for a 2D MA array under various conditions and extend our proposed algorithms to solve them efficiently. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed MA-enhanced near-field sensing scheme dramatically outperforms conventional fixed-position antennas (FPAs). Moreover, the joint angle and distance estimation results in a different array geometry from that in the individual estimation of angle/distance or far-field sensing.

Information Theory.title: Proof of the Langberg-Médard Multiple Unicast Conjecture
Information Theory.summary: Let $\mathcal{N}=(V,A,S, R)$ be a directed network, where $D=(V,A)$ is a digraph, $S=\{s_1,s_2,\ldots,s_k\}\subseteq V$ is a set of senders, and $R=\{r_1,r_2,\ldots,r_k\}\subseteq V$ is a set of receivers. We prove that if, for each $1\le j \le k$, there exist $k$ pairwise arc-disjoint directed paths in $D$, one from each $s_i$ to $r_j$, then the underlying undirected network of ${\cal N}$, with unit capacities, admits a feasible $(s_1,s_2,\ldots,s_k)$-$(r_1,r_2,\ldots,r_k)$ multiflow of value $1$ for each pair $(s_i,r_i)$, $i=1,2,\ldots,k$. This establishes the multiple unicast conjecture proposed by Langberg and Médard in 2009.

Information Theory.title: Online Covariance Estimation for Averaged Stochastic Gradient Descent on Riemannian Manifolds
Information Theory.summary: We study online inference for averaged Riemannian stochastic gradient descent (RSGD) when the unknown parameter lies on a manifold. Although the averaged RSGD iterate is asymptotically normal, practical inference requires estimating the unknown covariance operator in its limiting distribution. Existing online batch-means methods cannot be applied directly because a general Riemannian manifold lacks an addition operation, and the tangent space containing the Riemannian gradient varies across iterations. Through vector transport, we construct overlapping and non-overlapping covariance estimators that adaptively combine information from successive batches while accounting for the changing tangent spaces. The proposed estimators are online, require neither Riemannian Hessian computations nor a prespecified terminal sample size, and attain the same convergence rates as their Euclidean counterparts (Zhu et al., 2023). Together with asymptotic normality, these estimators enable online statistical inference for RSGD on manifolds. We illustrate the proposed framework through a detailed study of streaming principal component analysis on Grassmann manifolds.

Information Theory.title: Array Rotation in Near-Field ISAC: Communication, Detection, and Estimation Under Low-Complexity Transmit Architectures
Information Theory.summary: This paper studies near-field integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) with a rotatable base-station array under an exact spherical-wave propagation model. For a general transmit covariance, we derive a Cramér--Rao bound (CRB) decomposition that separates target-side geometry from transmit-covariance-dependent terms. We then specialize the framework to two representative low-complexity architectures: a single-stream superposition architecture, and a dual-waveform split architecture design. We characterize the communication-, detection-, and estimation-optimal rotations for each architecture using the exact finite-array model. In addition, we show how a second-order approximation yields compact approximate expressions for the optimal rotation angles. We also study uncertainty in the target state used for beamforming design through a correlated Gaussian perturbation model, and derive approximations of the optimal robust rotation angles for target sensing and detection. The analysis shows that the two architectures behave differently under rotation: the single-stream design can align communication and detection tasks, whereas the dual-waveform design exhibits a direct communication--detection tradeoff and can incur a larger communication loss when sensing is prioritized. Numerical results show clear gains over a fixed array orientation, especially for range estimation, and close agreement between the approximate and exact rotation choices. Detection is less affected by target-state errors than estimation in the considered cases.

Information Theory.title: Distributional statistics of nonequilibrium
Information Theory.summary: We establish a reference modeling framework for random probability distributions subject to constraints. Generalizing the hyperensemble approach of Crooks, we formulate Jaynesian priors of maximal uncertainty over the unit simplex of categorical distributions. This framework is entirely general, but we primarily investigate models with constraints on physically relevant quantities, namely, average energy and Shannon entropy. A constraint on the exact value of average energy uniquely determines a Boltzmann-Gibbs equilibrium, but also defines a hyperplanar subset of the probability simplex consisting of all distributions with that value of average energy. The associated hyperensemble has a uniform probability density across all such distributions, regardless of distance to equilibrium. Such reference models make predictions of generic nonequilibrium properties such as the mean and modal microstate distributions and the expected free energy of a random distribution, which we examine analytically and via exact sampling algorithms. Moreover, introducing constraints on Shannon entropy permits parametric access to tunably nonequilibrium regimes. The approach follows conventional Jaynesian modeling logic and is compatible with standard Bayesian inference, and reduces to Boltzmann-Gibbs statistics when Shannon entropy is maximized. We examine the physical predictions of this scheme, and demonstrate its wide compatibility with other approaches to nonequilibrium modeling. We illustrate the framework in three scenarios: (i) comparison to superstatistics quasi-equilibrium modeling, (ii) generation of random nonequilibrium steady states, and (iii) Bayesian inference under a prior hyperensemble. We highlight numerous prospects for theoretical extensions and empirical application.

Probability.title: Persistent occupation and critical marked sums on branching random walks
Probability.summary: We study two path functionals of a branching random walk at an exponential normalization. For centered integer displacements bounded above by one, we construct on survival one ray whose local time at every large spatial level is bounded below by a positive multiple of the square of that level. For displacements in $\{-1,0,1\}$, overlapping forward profiles give a single ray with lower coefficient $4t/(σ^2j_{1,1}^2)$, where $σ^2$ is the tilted variance and $j_{1,1}$ the first positive zero of $J_1$. The profile energy quotient is optimized exactly. For discounted marked path sums with real displacements, we prove critical-moment sufficiency without a drift assumption, and necessity under a finite ascending-ladder mean and a weighted sibling moment. At positive tilted drift, a stopping-line argument replaces the sibling condition by an $L\log L$ hypothesis. A sparse mark construction identifies an exact universality obstruction in the constant-displacement subclass. At negative tilted drift, weighted powers give explicit sufficient logarithmic-tail conditions for every exponent $t>0$ and examples excluding a universal critical-moment converse. Under our sufficient conditions, path sums converge uniformly and attain their maxima. The exact optimal persistent local-time constant and a general negative-drift converse remain open.

Probability.title: Efficiency--Complexity Tradeoff and Constrained Percolation
Probability.summary: We study the efficiency--complexity tradeoff for resource-limited agents through directed first-passage percolation. Nonnegative i.i.d. edge weights represent physical energy expenditure, while the logarithmic size of a constrained path family measures representational complexity. For translation-invariant families, a path-joining property yields deterministic large-distance costs in rational directions and joint convexity in constraint parameter and direction, under suitable moment and feasibility assumptions. Our main result concerns the limiting cost parameterized by path-family entropy. Using techniques from analytic combinatorics in several variables (ACSV), we establish its almost-sure existence and joint continuity in entropy and direction for nested families satisfying additional generating-function conditions, on the corresponding entropy range. Path-count asymptotics supply the change of parameter linking this cost to the constraint-parameterized cost. Two planar examples constrain the number of turns or the number of East-runs of length at least two.

Probability.title: Between the Semi-Random Process and G(n,p)
Probability.summary: We study a random graph process that connects the Erdős--Rényi random graph with the semi-random process. In each round, a uniformly random vertex is revealed together with a uniformly random candidate set of $s$ possible partners, and Builder chooses one of them. We study how this limited adaptivity $s$ changes the hitting times of monotone graph properties and how the familiar logarithmic ``coupon--collector'' delays in random graphs are reflected in this setting.

Probability.title: Joint Extension Field Point Counts for Superelliptic Curves
Probability.summary: Fix a finite field $\mathbf{F}_q$, an integer $m\ge2$ prime to $q$, and $2\leκ\le m$. For a uniformly chosen $κ$-power-free polynomial $F\in\mathbf{F}_q[x]$ of degree $D$, we determine the limiting joint distribution of the affine point counts of $y^m=F(x)$ over $\mathbf{F}_q,\ldots,\mathbf{F}_{q^n}$ as $D\to\infty$, with $q$ and $n$ fixed. The probability generating function is a finite Euler product with explicit local factors. Equivalently, the limiting vector is a sum of independent closed-point contributions, each of which may affect several extension degrees. We obtain the formula by specializing the equidistribution and motivic Euler product formalism of Bertucci-Howe. We then compute means, covariances, and moment expansions as $q$ varies in a fixed reduced residue class modulo $m$, after the degree limit has been taken. The one-field specialization recovers the power-free affine point-count distribution of Cheong-Wood-Zaman.

Probability.title: Stationary Random Iterations of Lipschitz Maps: A Generalized Displacement Condition for the Existence of Invariant Structures
Probability.summary: We study random iterations generated by infinitely many Lipschitz maps on non-compact complete separable metric spaces. We generalize classical displacement conditions ensuring the existence and uniqueness of invariant structures. We prove two main results. The first uses the graph transform operator to extend Elton's condition [A multiplicative ergodic theorem for Lipschitz maps. Stochastic Process. Appl. 34(1) (1990)] for the existence and uniqueness of invariant graphs. The second uses the Markov operator to generalize a displacement condition for stationary measures, introduced by Diaconis and Freedman [Iterated random functions. SIAM Rev. 41(1) (1999)] and by Kloeckner [Optimal transportation and stationary measures for iterated function systems. Math. Proc. Cambridge Philos. Soc. 173(1) (2022)]. We present several examples illustrating the applicability of our results.

Probability.title: Heavy-tailed random vectros: theory and applications
Probability.summary: In this paper we introduce and study several multivariate, heavy-tailed distribution classes, and we explore their closure properties and their applications. We consider the class of multivariate positively decreasing distributions, and its intersection with other multivariate distribution classes.

Probability.title: Jensen gaps and the decomposition principle
Probability.summary: We provide axiomatic characterizations of Jensen-gap functionals, which have the form $ρ(X)=\mathbb{E}[f(X)]-f(\mathbb{E}[X])$ for some real-valued function $f$ called the generator. This class includes important examples such as the excess growth rate, the utility premium, the Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence, and the variance, and is also closely related to measures of variability. We analyze various forms of convexity for Jensen gaps. To characterize Jensen gaps, we formulate conditional versions of law-invariant functionals, which are needed to state the decomposition principle. On an atomless probability space, we show that law invariance together with a binary decomposition principle is sufficient to characterize Jensen gaps on simple random variables. Under suitable continuity conditions, the characterization extends to broader classes, including compactly supported random variables and integrable random variables. We then identify the generator $f$ by imposing either of two natural invariance conditions: scaling invariance or translation invariance. The former identifies logarithmic, $x\log x$, and power generators, whereas the latter identifies exponential and quadratic generators.

Probability.title: Random-Bridges as Stochastic Transports for Generative Models
Probability.summary: This paper motivates the use of random-bridges -- stochastic processes conditioned to take target distributions at fixed timepoints -- in the realm of generative modelling. Herein, random-bridges act as stochastic transports between two probability distributions when appropriately initialized, displaying either Markovian or non-Markovian, and continuous, discontinuous, or hybrid patterns depending on the choice of the driving process. We show how one can start from general probabilistic statements and branch out into specific representations for learning and simulation algorithms. Essentially, our framework formulates stochastic transports as noisy information processes governing the dynamic translation and propagation of information between arbitrary probability measures. Our theoretical and algorithmic presentation details training and simulation frameworks for both Gaussian and Lévy (specifically, Gamma, Poisson and Stable-$1/2$) random-bridge transports. The empirical validation focuses on the Gaussian case for demonstration and comparison purposes, where our construct delivers high-quality samples, achieving competitive Fréchet Inception Distance scores compared to widely used denoising diffusions and flow matching frameworks.

Probability.title: Limit shapes for centrally excited walks
Probability.summary: A centrally excited random walk on $\mathbb Z^d$ moves like simple random walk, except that its first step from each site other than the origin has a drift of fixed size toward it. Kozma (2007) conjectured that after $n$ steps the visited set approximates a ball with radius of order $n^{1/(d+1)}$. We prove this in every dimension $d\geq 2$ and show that the rescaled local times converge uniformly to a cone, which is the potential generated by the drift on a ball. The same argument shows that, when the drift is opposite to a subgradient of a norm, the visited set approximates the ball of that norm. In the plane, the outer and inner radii of the visited set differ by at most $n^{1/6}$ times a power of $\log n$, and the exponent $1/6$ cannot be lowered. Earlier versions of this work appeared in three independent drafts by Nguyen (arXiv:2610.07724), Bou-Rabee and Peres (arxiv:2610.10162v1) and Singh (arxiv:2610.12138). The present paper brings together the results and ideas from these drafts.

Probability.title: A Bestiary of Brownian Processes: A Field Guide to Boundary Conditions and Conditioning
Probability.summary: The covariance of Brownian motion is the Green kernel of the one-dimensional Laplacian with a pinned left endpoint and a free right endpoint. This correspondence between Green's functions for the Laplacian on an interval and Brownian covariance functions turns out to be a general phenomenon. We use this correspondence to organize Brownian-derived Gaussian processes by three operations: choosing a self-adjoint realization, recentering a path, and conditioning a fixed law. Local Robin and selected nonlocal boundary conditions yield a catalogue of twelve processes with closed-form kernels, Brownian-path constructions, spectra and traces. The periodic and Neumann-Neumann realizations annihilate the constants; projecting the source and imposing zero time average selects the corresponding covariance pseudoinverses. Recentering and conditioning can both give a Brownian path zero time average, but the resulting laws differ: a constraint alone does not specify a process. A rank-one conditioning identity gives a scale-invariant criterion for the covariance effect of a shrinking family of observations. For Brownian finite differences of any fixed positive order, the covariance effect vanishes uniformly as the spacing tends to zero. For $m$-fold integrated Brownian motion, derivative constraints of orders $1,\ldots,m$ remain detectable at interior times. For simulation, we identify which grid constructions are exact and which are approximate.

Probability.title: On optimal stopping problems with full information and rank-dependent reward
Probability.summary: In this paper we consider optimal stopping problems with full information and rank-dependent rewards. Our focus is on the following two problems: selecting one of the r best observations (Gusein-Zade's problem with full information) and minimizing the expected rank (Robbins' problem). In both settings we provide full characterization of the optimal stopping rules and corresponding optimal values. We also present numerical experiments in which the derived dynamic programming recursions are implemented, and approximations to optimal values are computed.
Probability.comment: Keywords: optimal stopping, full information, rank-dependent reward, dynamic programming, Robbins' problem, Gusein-Zade's problem

Probability.title: Limiting moments of sample covariance matrices from large fold tensor vectors
Probability.summary: We study the moments of sample covariance matrices $M_{n,k,m}$ formed from independent $k$-fold tensor products of $n$-dimensional random vectors. The base vectors have independent and identically distributed centered complex entries with unit variance and finite moments of all orders. For every fixed $p \in \mathbb N_+$, under suitable moment conditions, we obtain an asymptotic formula for $p$th moment as $n, k, m$ tend to infinity with $m/n^k \to c \in (0,\infty)$. There is no restriction on the growth rate of $k$ relative to $n$. We also prove a variance bound and obtain the corresponding almost sure asymptotic formula. The results recover known limiting moments in several regimes. When $k/n$ tends to infinity and the modulus of base vector entry is not constant, we establish the asymptotic growth rate for the $p$th moment of normalized matrices. In this regime, we also provide a lower bound for the growth rate of the largest eigenvalue.

Probability.title: The chromatic number of a random graph with $o(n^{3/2})$ edges
Probability.summary: Let $G(n,m)$ be the Erdos-Renyi random graph with $n$ vertices and $m$ edges and let $δ>0$. Alon and Krivelevich [Combinatorica 1997] proved that for any sequence $m\leq n^{3/2-δ}$ there \emph{exists} an integer sequence $q=q(n)$ such that the chromatic number of $G(n,m)$ equals either $q$ or $q+1$ with probability tending to one as $n\to\infty$. In this paper, we give an explicit formula for this sequence $q(n)$ and confirm their result under a less restrictive assumption that $m=o(n^{3/2})$. Furthermore, we show that for all but a vanishing proportion of the admissible values of $m$, the chromatic number of $G(n,m)$ equals $q$ with high probability.

Probability.title: Linear statistics in the Coulomb gas: cumulants beyond rotational invariance
Probability.summary: We consider a classical Coulomb gas of $N$ particles in dimension $d\geq2$, confined by a general external potential $U$ in the large-$N$ limit. In that limit the density of particles has a compact support called the droplet. We study smooth linear statistics ${\mathcal L}_N=\sum_{i=1}^N f({\bf x}_i)$ at large $N$. While the leading variance of ${\mathcal L}_N$ is by now well understood in many settings, much less is known about higher cumulants. When $f({\bf x})=f(|{\bf x}|)$ and the potential is rotationally invariant, these cumulants were computed recently at leading order. We derive explicit formulas for the leading third and fourth cumulants for general smooth droplets, without assuming that either the potential or the test function is radial. The answers are expressed as intrinsic boundary integrals over the equilibrium droplet. The third cumulant depends on the cube of the jump of the normal derivative of the harmonic extension of $f$, while the fourth cumulant also involves the exterior Dirichlet-to-Neumann operator, the mean curvature of the boundary, and normal derivatives of the background density. Our derivation uses the tilted potential $U_s=U+s f/β$, the associated deformation of the droplet, and shape derivatives of the Dirichlet energy. This deformation has a natural interpretation as the infinitesimal motion of the free boundary in the obstacle-problem formulation of the equilibrium measure. Our formulas extend previous studies by Wiegmann and Zabrodin in two dimensions for $β=2$. In their setting, we provide a rigorous proof of the limiting third and fourth cumulants, supporting the proposed formulas for general Coulomb gases. We specialize the general formulas to the disk, the half-plane and the sphere, and check them against exactly solvable non-radial deformations, including translated elliptic droplets in $d=2$ and spheroidal deformations in $d=3$.

Probability.title: Sharp minimax risks and phase transitions in sparse submatrix detection
Probability.summary:
In this paper, we study the minimax risk of detecting a sparse, elevated-mean Gaussian submatrix planted in a larger noisy matrix. When the planted submatrix has size $n\times n$ and the ambient matrix has size $N\times N$ with $N=n^{1+α}$, the seminal work of Butucea and Ingster (2013) identifies the sharp detection boundary around which the risk converges to $0$ or $1$. We extend that zero-one theory by determining sharp risk asymptotics throughout a two-parameter phase diagram. Above the boundary, the risk decays stretched- or super-exponentially fast, and we determine its precise exponent. Below the boundary, where the risk tends to $1$, we obtain matching absolute-constant bounds for its polynomial rate of convergence. In both regimes, the asymptotics change across the line $α+δ=1/2$, where $δ$ parametrizes the signed distance from the detection boundary. Finally, on the boundary, we show that the minimax risk converges to the nondegenerate constant $\frac12$ in a very sparse regime where $n$ remains fixed and $N\to\infty$.
  Each of these rates corresponds to the risk of a suitably calibrated scan or sum test, whence follow the upper bounds. The main problem is to derive the matching regime-specific lower bounds. The mixture likelihood ratio is an average rather than a product and thus its logarithm lacks the additive structure required by standard large deviation formulations. On the other hand, classical second-moment estimates fail to be sharp due to overlap-induced correlations. To address these issues, we develop two general lower-bound principles based on truncated mixture likelihoods, tailored to the target risks on both sides of the detection boundary. The same framework yields sharp risk asymptotics for sparse subtensors with equal side lengths and also applies to more general testing problems including the detection of rectangular subtensors.
Probability.comment: 30 pages, 1 figure. Expanded exposition of the methods; main results remain unchanged. Tensor results are collected inside a single theorem. Abstract modified to meet arXiv's requirement

Probability.title: Zeros of Melnikov functions for periodically perturbed Hamiltonian systems with random coefficients
Probability.summary: Introducing a probabilistic perspective on a classical theme within the study of chaotic dynamics, we investigate the zeros of the Melnikov distance function associated to a periodically perturbed Hamiltonian system when the perturbation has random coefficients. We provide asymptotic estimates (as the period of the perturbation becomes large or small) for the average number of zeros and for the probability of no zeros.

Probability.title: Asymptotic expansions for random walks conditioned to stay positive with arbitrary endpoints
Probability.summary: We consider a one-dimensional random walk $S_n$ with i.i.d. integer-valued increments having zero mean and finite variance. Under suitable moment assumptions, we derive asymptotic expansions for the local probabilities $\pr(x+S_n=y,τ_x>n)$, where $τ_x=\inf\{n\ge1:x+S_n\le0\}$. These extend previous expansions for walks started at zero to arbitrary starting points. We obtain different expansions according to the sizes of the starting point and endpoint relative to $\sqrt n$.

Probability.title: Boundedness of the Density of Wiener Functionals with Low Regularity
Probability.summary: In this paper we prove that if a Wiener functional $F$ is $1+δ$-differentiable in the Malliavin sense for some $δ>0$ and satisfies the nondegeneracy condition, then the density of the law of $F$ exists, is bounded and is Hölder continuous of every exponent $β<δ$. This gives a partial positive answer to a problem proposed by Watanabe [13]; to date, this seems to be the best result available for the boundedness of the density of Wiener functionals. The approach is based on the fractional order Sobolev spaces associated with a probability measure and on the Riesz transform.

Probability.title: Determinantal sampling on general spaces: fast approximation via diffusion geometry
Probability.summary: Determinantal point processes (DPPs) have recently emerged as a kernel-based alternative to standard independent sampling for constructing efficient minibatches, coresets, and other compact representations of large-scale datasets. One of the key strengths of DPP based samplers is that they can be deployed over very general spaces, in contrast to more classical sampling methods beyond i.i.d. which tend to be tailored to particular well-structured settings, principally Euclidean spaces. In this work, we establish explicit rate guarantees for determinantal sampling in spaces that extend far beyond known Euclidean setups, focussing on spectral kernels obtained from eigenspaces of naturally associated Markov diffusion operators, including in particular the Laplacian on manifolds and nearest-neighbour type graphs on data point clouds and the discrete Schrodinger operator on large scale networks. This covers, in particular, the settings of Riemannian manifolds and discrete networks, as well as the problem of batch sampling from discrete datasets. Overall, our approach achieves guarantees comparable to $\big(\text{sample size}\big)^{-\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{2d_{\text{int}}}}$ , which match with the rates for well-known determinantal samplers on Euclidean spaces of comparable dimension. In terms of techniques, we connect to the celebrated Weyl's Law for spectra on general spaces, and leverage tools from the theory of Markov diffusion operators and Dirichlet forms, which could be of independent interest in this area. Our approach is applicable to a very wide plethora of ambient spaces beyond Euclidean as soon as these ingredients are available, including e.g. fractals, leading to guarantees that will be governed by the intrinsic structural constants of such spaces.
Probability.comment: Abstract shortened to meet arXiv requirements

Probability.title: Velocity surface disorder of large deviation rates for high-dimensional random walk in strongly mixing environment
Probability.summary: In this work, we establish the large deviation principles of random walk in strongly mixing environments. We show that the quenched and annealed rate functions share the same zero-set whose shape is either a singleton point or a line segment, with an illustrative example communicated and given by F. Rassoul-Agha. Furthermore, this paper reveals that under sufficiently low disorder, the two rate functions match on compact sets of both the interior and the boundary of the domain under finitely strongly mixing condition.
Probability.comment: To appear on Electronic Journal of Probability

Probability.title: Path space large deviation on a lattice for interacting particle systems
Probability.summary:
We investigate the path space large deviation principle (LDP) for a class of interacting particle systems on a fixed finite discrete torus. As an illustrative example, we use the partial exclusion process with maximal occupation of $s$ particles. We first verify the standard Kurtz-type law of large numbers for the original and tilted processes, thereby identifying the deterministic flows around which the large deviations are formulated. We then establish the path space LDP, with speed $s$, and identify the associated rate function in variational form as the Legendre transform of a nonlinear Hamiltonian. The proof relies on martingale techniques, exponential tightness, and a change-of-measure argument based on exponential tilting, which renders atypical trajectories typical under a modified dynamics.
  We also explain how the same strategy extends to further interacting particle systems. The inclusion process illustrates the conservative non-compact finite-jump case. The harmonic process is qualitatively different: a single transition may move a variable number of particles, and the limiting Hamiltonian is logarithmic with a non-trivial domain. This places the harmonic process outside the usual finite-reaction framework for density-dependent Markov jump processes. Finally, we discuss continuous-state energy-exchange models, such as the Brownian energy process and an integrable heat-conduction model, to indicate how the same Hamiltonian large-deviation formalism appears beyond discrete-state particle systems.

Probability.title: Large spin large deviations for interacting particle systems
Probability.summary:
We propose a novel framework for analyzing the sample-path large deviations of interacting particle systems directly on a lattice by considering a large-spin limit ($s \to \infty$). Through an appropriate scaling of variables, the process concentrates around its deterministic trajectory, governed by the lattice diffusion equation. We quantify the exponential cost of observing atypical trajectories by explicitly computing the path-space large deviation rate function from the scaled microscopic generator, based on a theory due to Feng and Kurtz. The rate function is described in terms of a Hamiltonian on a lattice in terms of classical spin variables. Notably, for our main model, the symmetric harmonic process, the corresponding Hamiltonian is identified with the classical integrable non-compact Ishimori spin chain.
  Furthermore, we show that our large spin large deviation theory is fully consistent with traditional Macroscopic Fluctuation Theory (MFT), smoothly recovering the standard MFT Hamiltonian in the spatial continuous limit. We also perform a Poisson-noise Martin--Siggia--Rose (MSR) computation to derive the non-linear lattice Hamiltonian directly from microscopic dynamics, use a relative entropy argument to obtain the density-current action, and establish the lattice fluctuation theorem alongside its symmetry origin. Overall, our framework provides a naturally regularized, lattice analogue of MFT that circumvents spatial ultraviolet singularities and possible continuous density blow-ups.
  We also apply our new scheme to partial symmetric exclusion process, symmetric inclusion processes, Brownian energy process and integrable heat conduction model, showing how their large-deviation Hamiltonians relate to classical compact and non-compact spin chains.

Probability.title: Almost Sure Convergence of Stochastic Approximation: An Interplay of Noise and Step Size
Probability.summary:
We study the almost sure convergence of the Stochastic Approximation algorithm to the fixed point $x^\star$ of a nonlinear operator under a negative drift condition and a general noise sequence with finite $p$-th moment for some $p > 1$.
