Classical almost sure convergence results of Stochastic Approximation are mostly analyzed for the square-integrable noise setting, and it is shown that any non-summable but square-summable step size sequence is sufficient to obtain almost sure convergence. However, such a limitation prevents wider algorithmic application. In particular, many applications in Machine Learning and Operations Research admit heavy-tailed noise with infinite variance, rendering such guarantees inapplicable. On the other hand, when a stronger condition on the noise is available, such guarantees on the step size would be too conservative, as practitioners would like to pick a larger step size for a more preferable convergence behavior. To this end, we show that any non-summable but $p$-th power summable step size sequence is sufficient to guarantee almost sure convergence, covering the gap in the literature.
  For the regime $p \in (1, 2)$, we show that using the $\|x-x^\star\|^p$-like Lyapunov function and applying the Holder-smoothness bound suffice. For $p > 2$, such an approach is no longer applicable, and therefore, we introduce a novel iterate projection technique to control the nonlinear terms produced by high-moment bounds and multiplicative noise. We believe our proof techniques and their implications could be of independent interest and pave the way for finite-time analysis of Stochastic Approximation under a general drift condition. As a starting point, we establish almost sure convergence results for non-expansive operators under a multiplicative noise condition for $p \in (1,2]$ and an additive noise condition for $p \in (2,\infty)$.

Probability.title: An upper bound on the smallest singular value of dense signed random combinatorial matrices
Probability.summary: Let $M_n$ be an $n\times n$ random matrix with entries in $\{-1, 0, 1\}$, where each row is independently and uniformly sampled from the set of all vectors in $\{-1, 0, 1\}^n$ containing exactly $d$ nonzero entries, with $d=pn$ for some fixed constant $p\in(0,1/2]$. A recent result by one of the authors gives a lower bound of order $n^{-1/2}$ for the smallest singular value $s_n(M_n)$ of this model with high probability. In this paper, we establish a matching upper bound for $s_n(M_n)$. Specifically, there exists a constant $C_p>0$ depending only on $p$ such that \[ \forall \varepsilon >0 \qquad \mathbb{P} \left( s_n(M_n) \le \frac{\sqrt{d}}{\varepsilon^2 n} \right) \ge 1-C_p\left(\varepsilon + \frac{1}{\sqrt{d}}\right). \] Consequently, in the dense regime, the smallest singular value $s_n(M_n)$ of signed random combinatorial matrices is typically of order $n^{-1/2}$.

Probability.title: Distributional statistics of nonequilibrium
Probability.summary: We establish a reference modeling framework for random probability distributions subject to constraints. Generalizing the hyperensemble approach of Crooks, we formulate Jaynesian priors of maximal uncertainty over the unit simplex of categorical distributions. This framework is entirely general, but we primarily investigate models with constraints on physically relevant quantities, namely, average energy and Shannon entropy. A constraint on the exact value of average energy uniquely determines a Boltzmann-Gibbs equilibrium, but also defines a hyperplanar subset of the probability simplex consisting of all distributions with that value of average energy. The associated hyperensemble has a uniform probability density across all such distributions, regardless of distance to equilibrium. Such reference models make predictions of generic nonequilibrium properties such as the mean and modal microstate distributions and the expected free energy of a random distribution, which we examine analytically and via exact sampling algorithms. Moreover, introducing constraints on Shannon entropy permits parametric access to tunably nonequilibrium regimes. The approach follows conventional Jaynesian modeling logic and is compatible with standard Bayesian inference, and reduces to Boltzmann-Gibbs statistics when Shannon entropy is maximized. We examine the physical predictions of this scheme, and demonstrate its wide compatibility with other approaches to nonequilibrium modeling. We illustrate the framework in three scenarios: (i) comparison to superstatistics quasi-equilibrium modeling, (ii) generation of random nonequilibrium steady states, and (iii) Bayesian inference under a prior hyperensemble. We highlight numerous prospects for theoretical extensions and empirical application.

Differential Geometry.title: Extrinsic Curvature Estimation by Closest Point Projection of Rays
Differential Geometry.summary: We propose a parametrization-free framework for estimating the second fundamental form and the principal curvatures of a submanifold of $\mathbb{R}^d$. The method uses the closest point projections of a few short random rays and recovers the curvature from the curves that these projections induce on the submanifold, without coordinate charts or local fitting. We analyze the geometry of the induced curves and characterize when they are geodesics. For hypersurfaces, these results give two algorithms with error bounds: a least squares reconstruction of the second fundamental form from the curvatures of the induced curves, and a direct estimate of all principal curvatures from the eigenvalues of a $d\times d$ matrix built from $d$ rays, which needs no normal information and costs $\mathcal{O}(d^3)$ besides the projections. In higher codimension, we can also recover the second fundamental form one normal direction at a time. On point clouds, where the projection becomes a nearest neighbor query, we bound the additional error. Experiments confirm the predicted rates for hypersurfaces in up to $128$ dimensions, for surfaces of codimension up to $98$, and on point clouds, demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed framework in practice.

Differential Geometry.title: A note on the cohomology of pullback Lie algebroids
Differential Geometry.summary: We give a direct differential-geometric proof of a result of Crainic on the cohomology of pullbacks of Lie algebroids under surjective submersions: If the fibers are connected and have vanishing cohomology through degree $n$, pullback with coefficients in any representation is an isomorphism through degree $n$ and is injective in degree $n+1$. The proof reduces to a vanishing result for leafwise cohomology and uses an exhaustion-and-patching argument due to Buchdahl. No local triviality or finite-type assumption on the fibers is required. We also prove the analogous result for holomorphic Lie algebroids.

Differential Geometry.title: Henneberg-Type Minimal Immersions in $\mathbb{R}^4$
Differential Geometry.summary: We construct a family of higher-order Henneberg-type minimal surfaces in $\mathbb{R}^4$ from explicit holomorphic data in a generalized Weierstrass--Enneper representation. The construction retains the polynomial reciprocal structure of the classical Henneberg data and yields explicit holomorphic primitives and real parametrizations for the family $\mathcal H_{(m,n)}$. We distinguish regular points from branch points, analyze the role of the complex parameter $λ$, and show that the real-$λ$ subfamily $\mathcal H_{(1,1)}$ lies in a three-dimensional linear subspace. For $\mathcal H_{(1,1)}$, we compute the induced conformal metric and Gaussian curvature, proving that the curvature is negative at every regular point. An explicit parametrization is given for $\mathcal H_{(1,1)}$, together with three-dimensional coordinate projections used solely for visualization. We also derive an integral-free formulation in terms of a single holomorphic seed function and identify the exceptional values $λ=\pm i$ for the inverse reconstruction formula.

Differential Geometry.title: Critical metrics for the Dirac-Yamabe eigenvalue ratio and Einstein-Dirac equations
Differential Geometry.summary: Let $(M^n,g)$ be a closed spin manifold of dimension $n\geq 3$ with positive Yamabe constant. We prove that critical metrics for the mixed eigenvalue ratio $\mathcal H(g)=\frac{λ_1(D_g)^2}{λ_1(L_g)},$ where $D_g$ is the Dirac operator and $L_g$ is the conformal Laplacian are characterized by a harmonic section whose energy-momentum tensor satisfies an Einstein--Dirac equation. We discuss consequences of this result for Hijazi's inequality, and we construct an example to prove that $\mathcal H$ is unbounded above within the conformal class of the round sphere.

Differential Geometry.title: Price's law for scalar waves on 1+4 dimensional subextremal Myers-Perry spacetimes
Differential Geometry.summary:
We consider Myers--Perry spacetimes $(M,g_{\mathbf{a},\mathbf{b},\mathfrak{m}})$ in $1+4$ dimensions with two spin parameters $(\mathbf{a},\mathbf{b})\in\mathbb{R}^2$, which are a direct generalization of the well known Kerr spacetime in $1+3$ dimensions. We prove that the Hamiltonian flow associated to $g_{\mathbf{a},\mathbf{b},\mathfrak{m}}^{-1}$ is normally hyperbolically trapped for the full subextremal range \[
  (|\mathbf{a}|+|\mathbf{b}|)^2<2\mathfrak{m}. \] As an application, we prove a Price law with explicit leading order terms for solutions $φ(t,x)$ of the scalar wave equation \[
  \Box_{g_{\mathbf{a},\mathbf{b},\mathfrak{m}}}φ=0 \] under the assumption of real mode stability. Our precise asymptotics imply that $φ(t,x)=ct^{-3}+\mathcal{O}(t^{-4+})$, where $c\in\mathbb{C}$ is an explicitly computable constant.

Differential Geometry.title: An Elliptic Path Fibration and Holomorphic Morita Equivalence
Differential Geometry.summary: We construct an elliptic analogue of the Alekseev-Meinrenken path fibration \cite{alekseev2009atiyah} for a simply connected complex Lie group with a nondegenerate invariant symmetric bilinear form. A natural $2$-form on the correspondence space induces a holomorphic symplectic groupoid over the space of $(0,1)$-connections and a holomorphic quasi-symplectic groupoid over the holomorphic loop group. The correspondence space defines a principal holomorphic Morita bibundle with compatible differential forms.

Differential Geometry.title: Surjectivity of real-linear Cauchy--Riemann operators: from the minimal Harder--Narasimhan slope to automatic transversality
Differential Geometry.summary: This paper relates the minimal Harder--Narasimhan slope to the surjectivity of real-linear Cauchy--Riemann operators. We establish a conformally invariant $L^2$ criterion and an asymptotic slope criterion, which yield higher-rank automatic transversality criteria for pseudoholomorphic curves beyond the classical rank-one framework. Applications to pseudoholomorphic spheres in $S^6$ provide quantitative $L^2$ obstructions to the integrability of almost complex structures.
Differential Geometry.comment: Corrected the proof of the main surjectivity criterion using weighted $L^2$ estimates, with the main results unchanged. 33 pages. Comments welcome

Differential Geometry.title: Multi-marginal optimal transport on sub-Riemannian manifolds
Differential Geometry.summary: In this paper, we study multi-marginal optimal transport on ideal sub-Riemannian manifolds. We establish a sub-Riemannian barycentric balance condition and prove the existence of a solution to the Monge problem under an additional assumption. We also investigate the absolute continuity of Wasserstein barycenters. Our results extend and improve upon those of Pass, Pinamonti, and Vedovato (Methods Appl. Anal. 28 (2021), 61-76) on the Heisenberg group, answering two open questions raised in their work.

Differential Geometry.title: A curvature-ellipse-based Monge normal form of a regular surface in $\mathbb{R}^4$ and its applications
Differential Geometry.summary: We study a Monge normal form of a surface in $\mathbb{R}^4$ based on the principal axes of its curvature ellipse. The curvature-ellipse-based Monge normal form is obtained using only Euclidean motions of the ambient space and local reparameterizations of the surface, and preserves the Euclidean invariants of the curvature ellipse, including its semi-axis lengths up to their ordering. We also give applications of this normal form to the $2$-jet geometry of surfaces in $\mathbb{R}^4$ and to the geometry of their orthogonal projections.

Differential Geometry.title: On flat metric nilpotent Lie algebras
Differential Geometry.summary: We study flat left-invariant pseudo-Riemannian metrics on nilpotent Lie groups. Associated with a flat metric Lie algebra $(\mathfrak{g},\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle)$ there is a canonical affine action of the corresponding group on the vector space $\mathfrak{g}$, whose linear part is the Levi-Civita representation $L$. Combining this action with Scheuneman's theorem on pure translations in nilpotent affine groups, we prove that a flat metric nonabelian nilpotent Lie algebra has a nontrivial kernel of $L$, that is, $\ker L\neq 0$. As a consequence, every $n$-dimensional flat metric nonabelian nilpotent Lie algebra is a double extension of an $(n-2)$-dimensional flat metric nilpotent Lie algebra.
Differential Geometry.comment: Theorem 3.1 is incorrct and so the proof of Theorem 1.1 is wrong. Although the main result might still true

Differential Geometry.title: Isolated singularities of solutions to the Yamabe equation in higher dimensions I
Differential Geometry.summary: We complete, in the general Riemannian setting, the classification of isolated singularities of positive solutions to the Yamabe equation for dimensions \(3\le n\le29\), initiated in the flat case by Caffarelli, Gidas, and Spruck in 1989. Precisely, every isolated singularity is either removable or the solution is asymptotic to a Fowler solution. The sharpness of this range is established by counterexamples for every dimension \(n\ge30\) in our companion paper.
Differential Geometry.comment: 108 pages. submitted. In this new version we first updated the status of our work in sequel, then clarified a few points in the statements and proofs of Lemma 4.2 and Proposition 9.3 and we made minor edits at a few spots in the abstract and introduction for clarity

Differential Geometry.title: Conformal Green functions and Yamabe metrics of Sobolev regularity
Differential Geometry.summary: We provide a full resolution of the Yamabe problem on closed 3-manifolds for Riemannian metrics of Sobolev class $W^{2,q}$ with $q > 3$. This requires developing an elliptic theory for the conformal Laplacian for rough metrics and establishing existence, regularity and a delicate blow-up analysis for its Green function. Most of the analytical work is carried out in dimensions $n \geq 3$ and for $W^{2,q}$ Riemannian metrics with $q>\tfrac{n}{2}$ and should be of independent interest.
Differential Geometry.comment: 63 pages. Minor changes with respect to v1

Differential Geometry.title: Blow-up analysis and compactness for critical Dirac equations on $\mathbb S^n$
Differential Geometry.summary:
We study blow-up and compactness for the critical nonlinear Dirac equation \[ D_{g_0}ψ_i =
H_i|ψ_i|^{\frac{2}{n-1}}ψ_i \qquad \text{on }\mathbb S^n,\quad n\ge 3, \] where $g_0$ is the round metric and $H_i\to H>0$ in $C^0(\mathbb S^n)$. Under a first-threshold bound on the critical mass, we prove that every blowing-up sequence has, after passing to a subsequence, a unique blow-up point $p$ satisfying $H(p)=\max_{\mathbb S^n}H$. The rescaled solutions converge to a ground-state Dirac bubble that carries the entire limiting critical mass. Under local uniform $C^1$ bounds on $H_i$, we use the Kelvin transform and a second rescaling to prove that $p$ is an isolated simple blow-up point. We also derive sharp pointwise and gradient estimates in cylindrical coordinates and identify the normalized Green limit.
  If the coefficients converge in $C^2$ near $p$, the Pohozaev identity yields $\operatorname{Hess}_{g_0}H(p)=0$. Consequently, if a positive $H\in C^2(\mathbb S^n)$ satisfies $Δ_{g_0}H(p)<0$ at every global maximum, then solutions with critical mass bounded by a level slightly above the first threshold are uniformly bounded in $L^\infty(\mathbb S^n)$. This bound remains uniform under small $C^2$ perturbations of $H$.

Differential Geometry.title: Non-maximal quasi-isometric $\mathrm{PU}_{2,n+1}$-representations via alternating surfaces in complex pseudo-hyperbolic spaces
Differential Geometry.summary: For every admissible non-maximal Toledo invariant $t$, we construct a locus of irreducible representations of a closed genus-$g$ surface group into $\mathrm{PU}_{2,n+1}$ with Toledo invariant $t$ whose orbit maps are quasi-isometric embeddings. These loci have real codimension $10(g-1)$ or $10(g-1)+2(n-1)$ in the character variety depending on the Toledo value. Our construction uses $4$-cyclic Higgs bundles and their correspondence with $\partial$-alternating surfaces in complex pseudo-hyperbolic spaces. The associated equivariant minimal maps into the symmetric space are bi-Lipschitz embeddings. We further construct cocompact domains of discontinuity in the Shilov boundary. Their quotients are smooth fiber bundles over the surface with fiber homeomorphic to $S^{2n-1}\times S^{2n-1}$.
Differential Geometry.comment: Several mistakes are fixed. 56 pages, including two appendices and a declaration of AI use, comments are very welcome

Differential Geometry.title: Milnor fibrations and regularity conditions for real analytic mappings
Differential Geometry.summary: When f : R power n to R power p, is a surjective real analytic map with isolated critical value, we prove that the (m)-regularity condition (in a sense we define) ensures that f ||f|| is a fibration on small spheres, f induces a fibration on the tubes and both fibrations are equivalent. In particular, we make the statement of [12] more precise in the case of isolated critical point and we extend it to the case of an isolated critical value.
Differential Geometry.comment: The manuscript is withdrawn due to an error in the proof of a main theorem, which affects the validity of the result as originally stated. The issue was subsequently addressed in a revised mathematical treatment

Differential Geometry.title: Hitchin's $α$-invariant and positive sectional curvature on homotopy $9$-spheres
Differential Geometry.summary: We prove that a smooth homotopy $9$-sphere admits a Riemannian metric of positive sectional curvature if and only if its Hitchin $α$-invariant vanishes, or equivalently if and only if it admits a Riemannian metric of positive scalar curvature.

Differential Geometry.title: Delambre--Gauss Formulas in Complex Hyperbolic Space
Differential Geometry.summary: We establish a Delambre--Gauss matrix identity for oriented right-angled hexagons in the complex hyperbolic plane. The six complex length parameters of a hexagon determine two alternating \(3\times3\) matrices whose product is central in (\mathrm{SU}(2,1)\). The resulting nine entry-wise equations extend the Delambre-Gauss formula of Tan, Wong, and Zhang in 4-dimensional hyperbolic geometry to this complex hyperbolic setting.

Differential Geometry.title: Volume of area-bounded PGL3-Hitchin moduli space
Differential Geometry.summary: For the $\mathrm{PGL}_3$-Hitchin moduli space of unmarked convex $\mathbb{RP}^2$ structures on the surface $S_{g,m}$ with fixed boundary data $\mathbf L$ when $m>0$, we investigate the subset whose canonical Hilbert--Busemann area is bounded above by $t$. We show that the Goldman symplectic volume of this subset is at most $C_{g,m}(t+λ^2)^{8g-8+3m}$, where $λ$ is the largest total-root boundary length for $m>0$ and is set to $0$ for $m=0$. As a consequence, We obtain the explicit upper bound for the $e^{-s\cdot\mathrm{Area}}$-weighted volume.
Differential Geometry.comment: 25 pages, 7 figures. This preprint supersedes the earlier preprint arXiv:2001.01295

Geometric Topology.title: The geometric combinatorics of $k$-shuffle polynomials
Geometric Topology.summary: This paper is the second in a series of two which aims at introducing a new family of groups called $k$-shuffle braid groups, denoted $\mathcal{B}_{n}(k)$. We focus here on the geometrical origins of these groups, as first observed by Calegari in arXiv:2105.11265. The spaces we are interested in are spaces of complex monic polynomials of degree $n$ whose critical values lie in $\mathbb{C} \setminus \{1, e^{\frac{2πi}{k}}, \dots, e^{\frac{2πi (k-1)}{k}}\}$. We show that the $k$-shuffle braid groups are the fundamental groups of those spaces, which correspond geometrically to complements of $k$ translates of the discriminant variety. Moreover, we show that the $k$-shuffle braid groups $\mathcal{B}_n(k)$ inject into the larger braid groups $\mathcal{B}_{nk}$.
Geometric Topology.comment: 47 pages, 37 figures. This paper is the second one in a series of two. The first paper is available at arXiv:2610.28986

Geometric Topology.title: Dancing circles
Geometric Topology.summary: Recent results on diffeomorphisms of $4$-manifolds make essential use of families of embeddings of $1$-manifolds into $4$-manifolds. We survey what is currently known about such families.
Geometric Topology.comment: 26 pages, 9 figures. To appear in the Proceedings of the 2025 Georgia International Topology Conference

Geometric Topology.title: On the closure of irregular orbits of the horocyclic flow on infinite finness
Geometric Topology.summary: The topological dynamics of the horocyclic flow h_R on the unit tangent bundle of a geometrically finite hyperbolic surface is well known. In particular on such a surface the flow h_R is minimal or the minimal sets are the periodic orbits. When the surface is geometrically infinite, the situation is more complex and the presence of possible irregular orbits makes the description of minimal sets complicated. In this text, we construct a family of infinite hyperbolic surfaces for which the horocyclic flow defined on the unit tangent bundle is not minimal.

Geometric Topology.title: Every $S^2$-Bundle over a positive genus($g>1$) Surface has Mapping Class Group of Infinite Rank
Geometric Topology.summary: In 2025, Lin, Wu, Xie and Zhang extend Dax invariant from embedded disks to embedded surfaces and show that there is surjective homomorphism from $MCG(M)$ to $\mathbb{Z}^{\infty}$ for $M= Σ\times S^2$. Let $Σ$ be a closed surface with positive$(g>1)$ genus, in the paper we show that for any nontrivial $S^2$ fiber bundles $X= Σ\ltimes S^2$, whether $X$ orientable or nonorientable, there is a surjective homomorphism from $MCG(X)$ to $\mathbb{Z}^{\infty}$. The proof is an application of generalization of Dax invariants for embedded surfaces and the restriction on pseudo-isotopy subgroup $MCG_0(X)$ also surjects on $\mathbb{Z}^{\infty}$. The property of $MCG(X)$ inherits from trivial fiber bundle $Σ\times S^2$ and main theorem shows that the algebraic size of the smooth mapping class group of $S^2$-fiber bundles does not depend on the triviality of the bundle.

Geometric Topology.title: Towards differential expansion for generic representations
Geometric Topology.summary: We report the first results of phenomenological analysis, based on extended set of explicitly calculated colored HOMFLY-PT polynomials in \cite{knotebook}. They concern differential expansion (DE), which separates the dependencies on the knot ${\cal K}$ and the representation $R$. %of colored HOMFLY-PT polynomials. DE is well understood for symmetric and rectangular representations, while for non-rectangular $R$ even the knot-independent basis $Z_R^X$ of DE is not known. We concentrate on two issues: the possible derivation of DE and on improved characteristic of its defect. We discuss how evolution families -- twist knots, double braids and 3-pretzels -- can be used to find DE by a peculiar triangular transformation of evolution coefficients. Once $Z^R_X$ are found for particular family, they are expected to stay basically the same for arbitrary knots -- modulo controllable reductions, characterized by the defect of DE, which puts knots into different universality classes. Contrary to original expectation, these classes appear labeled not by a single number $δ^{\cal K}$, but by a whole non-decreasing sequence $\{k_j\}$, which is squeezed between two staircases, ${ entier}\!\left(\frac{j-1}{δ+1}\right)\leq k_j\leq{ entier}\!\left(\frac{j-1}{{\rm deg}\,Δ}\right)$, where the upper bound involves Alexander polynomial $Δ(q^2)$ and follows from the continuation of the Melvin--Morton--Rozansky-Kashaev limit to $A=q^{-m}$ with $m>0$, when the limit gives a {\it positive} power of Alexander. The old assumption $δ+1={\rm deg}\,Δ$ is oversimplified and fails for 19 non-alternating knots with 11 and 12 crossings. Last, we list the differences of non-rectangularly colored HOMFLY for various mutant pairs to demonstrate their universality (knot-independence) and nice consistency with the spirit of DE.

Optimization and Control.title: Regularized Unbalanced Optimal Transport with Pearson Marginal Penalties
Optimization and Control.summary: We study quadratically regularized unbalanced optimal transport with Pearson marginal penalties and a lower bound $δ\ge0$ on the plan, including the sparse case $δ=0$. We organize the analysis around the active interface, where the plan switches from its lower bound to larger values. We prove a Newton remainder estimate that depends linearly on the marginal measure of the boundary layer around this interface, and a maximum-norm inverse estimate uniform over all Newton derivatives and cell volumes. Together they give local superlinear convergence of semismooth Newton iteration in function space, of q-order at least $1+α$ when the boundary-layer measure is $O(t^α)$, and a common convergence neighborhood along each refinement sequence whose data converge uniformly. Transverse interfaces give second-order supercloseness of the discrete potentials to the cell averages of the continuum potentials. A directional curvature condition on the input data verifies the interface condition before the solution is known and yields an explicit Newton convergence radius on all sufficiently fine meshes, uniformly in the lower bound. A globalized inexact semismooth Newton iteration has mesh-independent numbers of outer iterations and of full-array operations, that is, passes over the plan array. Its output satisfies an a posteriori error bound relative to the continuum optimal plan. Experiments test the rates at transverse interfaces and at interfaces with tangencies, the curvature criterion, and the algorithmic work. All estimates hold for a fixed regularization parameter and a fixed lower bound on the densities.
Optimization and Control.comment: The paper is a more focused version of the previous one "Control, Optimal Transport and a Sinkhorn-inspired algorithm for Neural Differential Equations". In this version, we focus on the UOT scheme with Pearson penalties, that is, we provide a much deeper analysis, and leave the other contents out for deeper studies in the future

Optimization and Control.title: On the Theory of Bias Tuning in Event Cameras
Optimization and Control.summary: This paper lays the foundation of a theory for bias tuning in neuromorphic cameras, a novel sensing technology also known as "event cameras". We begin by formulating the high-level effect of the sensitivity biases on the camera's event rate in mathematical terms. We then show that, as a corollary of the Poincare-Miranda theorem, the commonly used tuning principles of rate budgeting and polarity balancing lead to a unique configuration of the sensitivity biases. As a corollary, we show how by adopting these principles, the multi-variable bias-tuning problem reduces to a two-parameter problem that can be resolved experimentally.

Optimization and Control.title: EnerGNN: Learning Optimization-Compatible Energy Functions for Exact Constrained Combinatorial Inference
Optimization and Control.summary: Learning-based approaches to combinatorial optimization often predict solutions directly or use predictions to restrict search, while expressive energy-based models typically rely on approximate inference. We introduce EnerGNN, a framework that learns energy functions over complete binary configurations and minimizes them under explicit hard constraints through mixed integer programming (MIP). EnerGNN combines a graph neural network encoder with an optimization-compatible readout and a nonlinear energy head, enabling exact constrained inference over the learned energy. An optimality-aware contrastive loss trains the energy to reflect solution quality and constraint violations. Across Quadratic Knapsack, Combinatorial Auctions, and a personalized cell therapy supply chain problem, EnerGNN achieves near-optimal solutions with 100% feasibility. On the supply chain problem, it achieves a 0.05% mean primal gap and a 17.4$\times$ speedup over the monolithic MIP. The learned energy also generalizes to larger instances and supports zero-shot constraint injection, adapting to changing constraints without retraining while preserving feasibility.

Optimization and Control.title: Minimum-coordinate elimination on a simplex: polynomial first-step safety and coNP-complete correctness
Optimization and Control.summary: We study a deletion rule for strictly convex quadratic minimization on a simplex: compute the affine minimizer on the current face, permanently remove a most-negative coordinate, and repeat. Correctness is required for every linear term and every resolution of ties. We characterize first-step safety by a finite maximum principle for the constrained inverse, and correctness from every initial face by principal-inverse row inequalities. Correctness from the full simplex is a different property. The two properties coincide with at most four coordinates, but an explicit rational five-coordinate example separates them. An exact reachability condition explains the separation: boundary equalities in the constrained inverse restrict the tasks that can be entered on a facet. Away from these equalities, full-start and hereditary correctness coincide. We also determine the recognition complexity. First-step safety is decidable in polynomial bit time, by combining classical strict $n$-step-vector recognition with diagonal regularization. In contrast, full-start and hereditary correctness are coNP-complete, even on a reduction family with strict column diagonal maxima on every face. The proofs include the non-strict boundary and all affine anchors; explicit rational certificates for the finite examples are given in the text.

Optimization and Control.title: Ellipsoid Separation in Data-Dependent Time via Infimal Displacement Vectors
Optimization and Control.summary: The infimal displacement vector of the nonexpansive operator underlying the primal-dual hybrid gradient algorithm (PDHG) is known to encode useful information for infeasible optimization problems. In particular, for the ellipsoid separation problem (ESP), where the goal is to find a separating hyperplane between two collections of ellipsoids, the infimal displacement vector corresponding to an infeasible second-order cone program (SOCP) encodes a separating hyperplane. We show FISTA computes a sequence of approximations to the dual component of the infimal displacement vector and establish that a solution to the ESP can be obtained in $\mathcal{O}(δ_{\mathcal{A}}^{-2})$ iterations. Here $δ_{\mathcal{A}}$ denotes the distance between the convex hulls of the two ellipsoid collections.

Optimization and Control.title: First-order Optimization Methods with Generalized Smoothness for Low-rank Matrix Factorization
Optimization and Control.summary: This paper studies several first-order methods for low-rank matrix minimization in the Burer--Monteiro form, where the target matrix is represented as the product of a nonnegative factor matrix and its transpose. Such a factorization destroys convexity of the objective function and global Lipschitz continuity of the gradient. We prove that for a quadratic objective function that is strongly convex only on the subspace of symmetric matrices, the Burer-Monteiro factorized objective possesses generalized smoothness with a fractional exponent 2/3. For a quadratic objective, the generalized smoothness property requires positive definiteness of the operator A only on the subspace of symmetric matrices, which relaxes the assumptions of Dragomir et al. On this basis, three methods are proposed: an adaptive gradient descent method with Armijo backtracking; an unconstrained SafeAdam method combining the Adam direction with a descent-angle certificate and a fallback to the normalized gradient; and a certified projected version for the nonnegativity constraint. Global convergence and explicit convergence rates for the proposed methods have been proved. The obtained convergence rate is better than the convergence rate of ordinary unaccelerated gradient descent in the case of a sufficiently large gradient. In the small-gradient regime, the convergence guarantee is of square-root type, and the corresponding complexity scales as the inverse square of the desired accuracy. In the large-gradient regime, the convergence guarantee is of three-quarters type, and the corresponding complexity is proportional to the inverse of the accuracy raised to the power of 4/3. Experiments on SymNMF using the TDT2, Reuters and CBCL datasets, which are standard benchmarks for document and image clustering, show that the methods match or outperform Dyn-NoLips without tuning the relative-smoothness kernel parameters.

Optimization and Control.title: Two Answers on Heavy-Ball Dynamics
Optimization and Control.summary: We determine the worst-case behavior of the heavy-ball method on smooth strongly convex functions, first for Polyak's quadratic-optimal parameters and then for arbitrary constant parameters. For Polyak's tuning, the exact dimension-uniform exponential rate is the largest growth factor of an interpolable mixture of rotating geometric sequences. Four algebraic families determine this rate at every condition number. Two frequencies suffice, and one function in dimension five attains the rate at every horizon up to constant factors. We recover the sharp convergence threshold $9+4\sqrt5$ of Badithela and Seiler. For general tunings, an exact linear feasibility criterion characterizes dimension-uniform linear convergence through the angle between the characteristic polynomials of the two extreme quadratics. This gives a continuous condition-number threshold and resolves the second heavy-ball riddle of Goujaud, Taylor and Dieuleveut. The regions between consecutive cycle tongues are Farey gaps, each containing convergent and divergent tunings. Regular portions of the threshold surface are analytic plateaus with fixed periodic frequency support. Every rational rotation number in a gap anchors a single-harmonic plateau; mixed-harmonic plateaus and an exact two-lag threshold point also occur. Along tongue edges, explicit multiplier inequalities and second-order expansions of competing Farey fans bound the transition from single-harmonic to mixed-harmonic extremals. The rate bounds and the extremal constructions follow from a common interpolation and separation argument that preserves initialization with zero momentum.
Optimization and Control.comment: 77 pages, 9 figures, links to Lean formalization and source code

Optimization and Control.title: Using artificial delays for prescribed/fixed-time static output feedback control of linear systems
Optimization and Control.summary: In this paper, we address the prescribed/fixed-time control problem for linear time-invariant systems with relative degree $r\geq 2$ using delayed time-varying static output feedback. In addition to controllability and observability, we assume that a truncated observability matrix is nonsingular. Within the act-and-wait control framework, two types of artificial delays are introduced into the output feedback: one to realize static output feedback and the other to achieve prescribed/fixed-time control. By constructing smooth periodic delayed output feedback controllers, we achieve prescribed-time input-to-state stability (ISS) with respect to matched disturbances and measurement noise. Next, we consider systems with measurement delays. Note that existing predictor methods are not applicable to static output feedback delay compensation. We propose delayed controllers that achieve fixed-time stability in the presence of large known slowly-varying delays (with delay derivatives less than one) and even in the presence of large unknown constant delays for systems with nilpotent matrices. Moreover, we present a design for the case of discrete-time periodic measurements with a small sampling period. When the system reduces to a chain of integrators, prescribed/fixed-time convergence can be achieved with arbitrarily large artificial delays introduced by static output feedback avoiding high gain and managing with large known slowly-varying or sawtooth delays (corresponding to discrete-time measurements) or unknown constant delays. In the case of unknown constant delays, this leads to a low-gain controller that may efficiently attenuate measurement noise. Numerical examples verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

Optimization and Control.title: V-Representability Beyond Singular Times in Time-Dependent Density Functional Theory: The Hubbard Dimer Case
Optimization and Control.summary: We study the global $V$-representability problem in time-dependent density functional theory (TDDFT) for the two-particle Hubbard dimer model in the spin-singlet sector. In particular, we investigate whether the time-dependent density of the interacting system obtained for a given one-body external potential $u$ (the tunable control variable) can be reproduced by a non-interacting Kohn--Sham system beyond the singular times at which the usual inversion formulas break down. We deal with both the conventional formulation of TDDFT based on some time-dependent variational principle and the recently introduced geometric formulation of TDDFT (Phys. Rev. Lett. 136 (2026) 256401, Phys. Rev. A 113 (2026) 062222). For both principles, we prove global-in-time $V$-representability, show that singular times induce non-uniqueness of the time-dependent effective potential, and classify the set of solutions.

Optimization and Control.title: A Cubic Underestimator for Deterministic Global Optimization
Optimization and Control.summary: We propose a new underestimator with pointwise and Hausdorff convergence of order three for deterministic global optimization of twice continuously differentiable functions with Lipschitz continuous Hessians. The proposed underestimator is obtained by augmenting the second-order Taylor expansion with a cubic remainder term of the objective function yielding a valid global underestimator that can be used to obtain lower bounds in a branch-and-bound method to solve nonconvex global optimization problems. The underestimator is nonconvex, and finding its global minimum could be computationally expensive. Accordingly, we derive a sufficient condition under which the proposed cubic underestimator is edge-concave, so that its minimum over a box can be found by vertex evaluation, while retaining third-order convergence. We show that the maximum separation distance between the objective function and the underestimator decreases cubically with the width of the box. This higher order convergence enables the lower bounds to converge more rapidly to the optimal value as the variable bounds are progressively tightened. The proposed underestimator is incorporated into a deterministic branch-and-bound algorithm and compared with the αBB and second-order edge-concave underestimators on a collection of 130 benchmark problems. The numerical results show that the proposed underestimator outperforms the compared underestimators in terms of both the number of explored branch-and-bound nodes and total CPU time, while maintaining a competitive computational cost per node. These results demonstrate that the proposed cubic edge-concave underestimator can provide more effective lower bounds and better computational performance in deterministic global optimization.

Optimization and Control.title: Optimal Control of the 2D Boussinesq Equations with Finite Codimension Constraints
Optimization and Control.summary: We study an optimal control problem (OCP) governed by the two-dimensional (2D) Boussinesq equations, where the right-hand sides of the velocity and temperature equations are projected onto the corresponding tangent spaces of the manifolds $\mathcal{M}_1:=\{y\in\mathbb{H}:\|y\|_{\mathbb{H}}=1\}$ and $\mathcal{M}_2:=\{θ\in H:\|θ\|_H=1\}$, respectively. The resulting evolution is subject to finite-codimensional constraints, under which the state $(y,θ)$ remains on $\mathcal{M}:=\mathcal{M}_1\times\mathcal{M}_2$ throughout the time interval. A Faedo--Galerkin construction provides a unique, global, strong solution to the constrained Boussinesq system for external controls $\mathfrak{H}\in L^2(0,T;\mathbb{H})$, along with uniform energy bounds. In addition, we establish the existence of an optimal triplet $(y^*,θ^*,\mathfrak{H}^*)$ that minimizes the quadratic cost subject to the constrained Boussinesq system. Necessary conditions of the first order are obtained through a coupled state--adjoint--control system. The optimal state $(y^*,θ^*)$ remains on $\mathcal{M}$, while the optimal control lies in the tangent space: $\mathfrak{H}^*(t)\in T_{y^*(t)}\mathcal{M}_1$, for all $t\in[0,T]$. We also show that the map $\mathfrak{H}\mapsto(y_{\mathfrak{H}},θ_{\mathfrak{H}})$ in $(C([0,T];\mathbb{H})\cap L^2(0,T;\mathbb{V}))\times(C([0,T];H)\cap L^2(0,T;V))$ is Fréchet differentiable. The linearized state is the unique weak solution to the constrained linearized Boussinesq system and satisfies the necessary tangency condition. Hence, the well-posedness and first-order optimality conditions are established for the Boussinesq system under nonlinear manifold constraints.

Optimization and Control.title: Multi-cut stochastic approximation methods for solving stochastic convex composite optimization
Optimization and Control.summary: This paper considers the stochastic convex composite optimization problem and presents multi-cut stochastic approximation (SA) methods for solving it, whose models in expectation overestimate its objective function. The multi-cut model obtained by taking the maximum of a finite number of linearizations of the stochastic objective function provides a biased estimate of the objective function, with the error being uncontrollable. Instead, our proposed SA method uses models obtained by taking the maximum of a finite number of one-cut models, i.e., suitable convex combinations of linearizations of the stochastic objective function. It is shown that the proposed methods achieve nearly optimal convergence rate and have computational performance comparable, and sometimes superior, to other SA-type methods.

Optimization and Control.title: Emission-aware operation of residential PV-battery systems: the role of information structure
Optimization and Control.summary: Residential batteries can reduce the carbon emissions of households with photovoltaic (PV) generation, but how much depends on how they are operated under uncertain load, PV generation, and grid carbon intensity. We cast the operation of a residential PV-battery system as a sequential decision problem and compare, under a common and explicit evaluation protocol, a family of linear policies that differ in the information available at decision time, in how they anticipate the future, and in their adaptivity: a rule-based self-consumption policy, an open-loop stochastic schedule, affine feedback policies, receding-horizon policies with deterministic, scenario-based and two-stage lookahead models, and perfect-information benchmarks. Scenarios are generated by a joint principal component model of the three uncertain quantities, which supports conditional sampling during the day. Experiments on Italian data at 15-minute resolution comprise single-day evaluations on 10000 test scenarios in three seasons and a closed-loop simulation over more than eight months of real data. When the state of charge is treated consistently across policies, the self-consumption rule is within 3.2% of the perfect-foresight emissions in closed loop, whereas open-loop schedules and receding-horizon policies that decide before measuring the current period are about 20--35% above it. With real-time measurements, scenario-based receding-horizon control consistently outperforms its deterministic counterpart and, for households that rely more on the grid, reduces emissions by about 5% with respect to the rule. The benefit of emission-aware optimization is therefore determined mainly by the information structure of the controller and by the size of the system relative to the demand.

Optimization and Control.title: Convergence Analysis of Nesterov's Accelerated Gradient Descent under Relaxed Assumptions
Optimization and Control.summary: We study convergence rates of Nesterov's Accelerated Gradient Descent (NAG) method for convex optimization in both deterministic and stochastic settings. We focus on a more general smoothness condition raised from several machine learning problems empirically and theoretically. We show the accelerated convergence rate of order $\mathcal{O}\left(1/T^2\right)$ in terms of the function value gap, given access to exact gradients of objective functions, matching the optimal rate for standard smooth convex optimization in \citep{nesterov1983method}. Under the relaxed affine-variance noise assumption for stochastic optimization, we establish the high-probability convergence rate of order $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}\left(\sqrt{\log\left(1/δ\right)/T}\right)$ and this rate could improve to $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}\left(\log\left(1/δ\right)/T^2\right)$ when the noise parameters are sufficiently small. Here, $T$ denotes the total number of iterations and $δ$ is the probability margin. Up to logarithm factors, our probabilistic convergence rate reaches the same order of the expected rate obtained in \citep{ghadimi2016accelerated} where the assumptions of bounded variance noise and Lipschitz smoothness are required. We additionally establish the convergence rates of the studied algorithms in the non-convex setting.

Optimization and Control.title: When Protection Hurts: A Cytokine Storm Theory of Supply Chain Overreaction
Optimization and Control.summary: Supply chain resilience research has traditionally viewed defensive actions such as safety stock, backup suppliers, expedited transportation, and emergency sourcing as beneficial. However, disruptions such as the COVID-19 pandemic, the 2021 semiconductor shortage, and the Suez Canal blockage highlight how synchronized hoarding, duplicate ordering, and capacity reservation can amplify congestion and operational costs, sometimes worsening the original disruption. Motivated by this observation, we develop a decision-theoretic framework in which Protective Response Intensity (PRI) is an endogenous decision variable. We introduce Response-Induced Loss (RIL) to capture costs generated by defensive actions and characterize a unique optimal response that balances disruption mitigation against self-induced losses. We derive a closed-form critical response threshold beyond which RIL exceeds the original disruption intensity, a phenomenon termed a *Supply Chain Cytokine Storm*. We further propose the Cytokine Storm Index (CSI), measuring response-induced loss relative to the original disruption, and discuss its potential calibration using operational data. Extending the framework to interconnected supply networks, we derive a spectral stability condition distinguishing bounded decentralized responses from network-wide propagation. Numerical experiments show that optimal responses remain below the storm threshold, whereas proportional response heuristics can exceed it. Network responses converge or diverge according to the derived stability condition. Overall, our findings highlight that supply chain resilience depends not only on mitigating disruptions but also on keeping defensive responses proportionate to the shocks they are intended to address.

Optimization and Control.title: Convergence Analysis of Stochastic Accelerated Gradient Methods for Generalized Smooth Optimizations
Optimization and Control.summary: We investigate the Randomized Stochastic Accelerated Gradient (RSAG) method, utilizing either constant or adaptive step sizes, for stochastic optimization problems with generalized smooth objective functions. Under relaxed affine variance assumptions for the stochastic gradient noise, we establish high-probability convergence rates of order $\tilde{O}\left(\sqrt{\log(1/δ)/T}\right)$ for function value gaps in the convex setting, and for the squared gradient norms in the non-convex setting. Furthermore, when the noise parameters are sufficiently small, the convergence rate improves to $\tilde{O}\left(\log(1/δ)/T\right)$, where $T$ denotes the total number of iterations and $δ$ is the probability margin. Our analysis is also applicable to SGD with both constant and adaptive step sizes.
Optimization and Control.comment: The first version was posted on arXiv in February 2025, and the paper was accepted by JOTA in September 2026. This version includes additional numerical experiments and minor editorial revisions

Optimization and Control.title: Multi-marginal optimal transport on sub-Riemannian manifolds
Optimization and Control.summary: In this paper, we study multi-marginal optimal transport on ideal sub-Riemannian manifolds. We establish a sub-Riemannian barycentric balance condition and prove the existence of a solution to the Monge problem under an additional assumption. We also investigate the absolute continuity of Wasserstein barycenters. Our results extend and improve upon those of Pass, Pinamonti, and Vedovato (Methods Appl. Anal. 28 (2021), 61-76) on the Heisenberg group, answering two open questions raised in their work.

Optimization and Control.title: On optimal stopping problems with full information and rank-dependent reward
Optimization and Control.summary: In this paper we consider optimal stopping problems with full information and rank-dependent rewards. Our focus is on the following two problems: selecting one of the r best observations (Gusein-Zade's problem with full information) and minimizing the expected rank (Robbins' problem). In both settings we provide full characterization of the optimal stopping rules and corresponding optimal values. We also present numerical experiments in which the derived dynamic programming recursions are implemented, and approximations to optimal values are computed.
Optimization and Control.comment: Keywords: optimal stopping, full information, rank-dependent reward, dynamic programming, Robbins' problem, Gusein-Zade's problem

Optimization and Control.title: Physics-Informed Graph-Based Safe RL with Constraint-Specific Critics for Community Battery Coordination in Distribution Network
Optimization and Control.summary: High penetrations of distributed energy resources (DERs) and fast-varying electric vehicle (EV) charging intensify voltage and line-limit violations in distribution networks (DNs), making safe, low-cost operation increasingly challenging. This paper proposes a physics-informed safe deep reinforcement learning (DRL) framework for coordinating community battery energy storage systems to mitigate constraint violations while minimizing operating cost. To represent nonlocal spatiotemporal interactions, we develop a dual-level physics-informed graph representation in which line impedance and capacity shape spatial information propagation, while power-balance, voltage-profile, and flow-reconstruction losses regularize the latent state toward control-relevant physical consistency. Building on this representation, we develop Lagrangian Dedicated-Critic PPO (LDCPPO), which implements constraint-specific value decomposition: independent reward and cost critics preserve heterogeneous voltage- and line-loading-related learning signals and combine their advantages only during the Lagrangian policy update. Case studies on DNs with high rooftop photovoltaic penetration and EV charging demonstrate that the proposed method reduces the key voltage-violation degree by up to 80.5% compared with the tested baselines, while also achieving the lowest voltage-violation count and line-overload degree with competitive operating cost.

Optimization and Control.title: Local-to-Global Exactness of SDP Relaxations for Sparse QCQPs
Optimization and Control.summary: We study exact semidefinite programming (SDP) relaxation for a given sparse quadratically constrained quadratic program (QCQP). The SDP relaxation is exact if, whenever it has an optimal solution, it admits a rank-at-most-one optimal solution that corresponds to an optimal solution of the QCQP. Using the maximal cliques of a chordal extension of the aggregate sparsity pattern graph of the data matrices, we formulate the SDP relaxation in terms of clique-wise matrix variables and develop a local-to-global framework for certifying exactness. For each clique-wise matrix variable, we introduce a local sub-SDP with two parameters: a local right-hand-side vector and a consistency matrix specifying the values of entries shared by overlapping clique-wise matrix variables. In the main theorem, these parameters are determined by an optimal solution of the global clique-wise SDP. The theorem shows that if the resulting local sub-SDPs are exact, then the original SDP relaxation is exact. Under the additional assumption that any two distinct cliques intersect in at most one node, we present three classes of local QCQPs that can be incorporated into this framework: convex local QCQPs, local QCQPs characterized by sign-pattern conditions, and separable local QCQPs with a limited number of constraints. Examples illustrate how these different local QCQP classes can be combined in sparse QCQPs.

Optimization and Control.title: A Continuous-Time Actor-Critic Framework for Jump-Diffusion Controls with Normalizing Flows
Optimization and Control.summary: Continuous-time stochastic control with time-inhomogeneous jump-diffusion dynamics is central in finance and economics, but computing optimal policies is difficult under explicit time dependence, discontinuous shocks, and high dimensionality. We propose an actor-critic framework that serves as a mesh-free solver for entropy-regularized control problems and stochastic games with jumps. The approach is built on a time-inhomogeneous little q-function and an appropriate occupation measure, yielding a policy-gradient representation that accommodates time-dependent drift, volatility, and jump terms. To represent expressive stochastic policies in continuous-action spaces, we parameterize the actor using conditional normalizing flows, enabling flexible non-Gaussian policies while retaining exact likelihood evaluation for entropy regularization and policy optimization. We validate the method on time-inhomogeneous linear-quadratic control, Merton portfolio optimization, and a multi-agent portfolio game, using explicit solutions or high-accuracy benchmarks. Numerical results demonstrate stable learning under jump discontinuities, accurate approximation of optimal stochastic policies, and favorable scaling with respect to dimension and number of agents.

Optimization and Control.title: Approximate Controllability of Neutral Integro-Differential Inclusions Associated with Hemivariational Inequalities in Banach Spaces with Uniformly Convex Dual
Optimization and Control.summary: In this paper, we investigate the approximate controllability of neutral integro-differential inclusions driven by hemivariational inequalities with nonlocal inclusion conditions in a Banach space $\mathbb{V}$ whose dual $\mathbb{V}^*$ is uniformly convex, using resolvent operator theory. We first establish an equivalence between the original problem and an associated differential inclusion involving the Clarke subdifferential. Under suitable assumptions, we then prove the existence of mild solutions corresponding to admissible controls in $\mathrm{L}^2(I,\mathbb{U})$. A key contribution of this work lies in the analysis of the control construction in Banach spaces, where the duality mapping $\mathcal{J} = \partial\big(\tfrac{1}{2}\|\cdot\|_{\mathbb{V}}^2\big)$ is generally nonlinear, in contrast to the Hilbert space setting, while such nonlinearity has been viewed as a technical obstruction in earlier studies. Based on this framework, we prove approximate controllability of the original system by relating it to the controllability of the associated linearized inclusion and constructing appropriate controls involving the duality mapping. Finally, we present applications to illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

Optimization and Control.title: Deflation-Based Spectral Preconditioning for the Conjugate Gradient Method on Perturbed Systems
Optimization and Control.summary: We consider sequences of large symmetric positive-definite linear systems in which spectral information from a reference matrix $A$ is reused to accelerate the solution of a nearby system with perturbed matrix $A(t)=A+tE$, where $E$ is symmetric, $\|E\|_F=1$, and $t\geq0$ is the perturbation size. We compare deflated conjugate gradient (deflated CG) with preconditioned CG (PCG) equipped with a scaled spectral preconditioner constructed from the same spectral information of $A$. First, we derive an energy-norm error characterization of deflated CG. We then use perturbation analysis to show that, after one additional PCG iteration, the squared PCG error is bounded, up to terms of order $t^2$, by an explicit multiple of the squared deflated CG error. This result clarifies the role of the scaling parameter in the preconditioner. Experiments show that the scaled spectral preconditioner recovers much of the convergence improvement provided by deflation while requiring fewer products with $A(t)$.

Optimization and Control.title: SLAB: Time-Lag-Aware Deep Reinforcement Learning for Flexible Job-Shop Scheduling in PPVC Module Factories
Optimization and Control.summary: Prefabricated prefinished volumetric construction (PPVC) builds room-sized modules in factories that operate as flexible job shops. A module waits 12 to 48 h after casting, waterproofing, and painting, while its station is free for other modules. Existing learned dispatchers release the next operation before this wait ends, so their plans need repair. This paper presents SLAB (Scheduling under time-Lags with an Admissible Bound), a decision process for dispatchers trained by deep reinforcement learning. Its transition releases a module only after its wait, and its reward is the decrease of a proven lower bound that includes the waits. Training on 10-module orders with halved waits also teaches the policy the station contention of larger orders. On three existing networks, repaired plans are 42% to 133% longer than the same network's schedules inside SLAB. On orders generated from Singapore's PPVC guidebook, one trained policy gives schedules 2.2% to 8.1% shorter than the shortest-processing-time rule at 10 to 80 modules. At 50 and 80 modules, it outperforms a time-lag memetic algorithm by 6.7% and 7.4% and constraint-programming search started from that rule's schedule and given 600 s by 6.6% and 7.6%. The memetic algorithm gives shorter schedules on orders of 10 modules, and the same search given 300 s on orders of 10 and 20 modules. A module factory can therefore train one dispatcher on small orders and run it without a solver on production batches of 50 to 80 modules.
Optimization and Control.comment: 12 pages, 4 figures, with a 31-page supplementary material appended. Submitted to IEEE Transactions on Industrial Informatics

Optimization and Control.title: Mathematical programs with complementarity constraints and application to hyperparameter tuning
Optimization and Control.summary: We consider the Mathematical Program with Complementarity Constraints (MPCC). One of the main challenges in solving this problem is the systematic failure of standard constraint qualifications. Carefully accounting for the combinatorial nature of the complementarity constraints, tractable versions of the Mangasarian-Fromovitz Constraint Qualification (MFCQ) have been designed and widely studied in the literature. This paper looks closely at two such MPCC-MFCQs and their influence on MPCC algorithms. As a key contribution, we introduce a third MPCC-MFCQ, lying between these two, under which we prove the convergence of the inexact sequential penalisation and Scholtes relaxation algorithms. This significantly weakens the assumptions currently used in the literature. We then form the problem of tuning hyperparameters of a nonlinear Support Vector Machine (SVM), a fundamental machine learning problem for classification, as an MPCC. For this application, we establish that the aforementioned new qualification holds under very mild restrictions. Moreover, we program robust implementations and carry out comprehensive numerical experiments on real-world data sets, where we show that the sequential penalisation method applied to the MPCC formulation for tuning SVM hyperparameters can outperform both the Scholtes relaxation technique and the derivative-free methods from the machine learning literature.

Optimization and Control.title: Affine-invariant Cubic Newton with Weak Learners
Optimization and Control.summary: Modern gradient boosting algorithms are based on Newton's method, which excels empirically but lacks global convergence guarantees. While recent work on Gradient-Regularized Newton (GRN) boosting achieved a global $\mathcal{O}(1/γ^{12}k^2)$ rate, its analysis was not able to exploit the natural Hessian geometry and suffers from a heavy $γ^{12}$ dependence on a worst-case `weak gradient edge' $γ$. In this paper, we tackle these theoretical drawbacks by generalizing the Affine-Invariant Cubic Newton (AICN) scheme to convex optimization with weak learners. Our analysis is based on average cosine values $\overlineΘ_k$ along the optimization path and directional improvements $δ_k$ in the Hessian-induced norm. We show that the weak-AICN update reduces to a damped weak-Newton step with an explicit stepsize determined by $δ_k$. Under semi-strong self-concordance, we establish a global $\mathcal{O}(1/\overlineΘ_k^4 k^2)$ rate, significantly improving upon the weak-GRN bound. We further prove a local linear rate, global linear convergence for Hessian-dominated losses, cosine angle lower bounds, and present weak-AdaAICN, which adaptively tunes the cubic regularization. Finally, we demonstrate the broader applicability of this framework beyond gradient boosting by showing that Newton coordinate descent emerges naturally as a special case of optimization with weak learners.
Optimization and Control.comment: Accepted to 40th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2026)

Optimization and Control.title: Almost Sure Convergence of Stochastic Approximation: An Interplay of Noise and Step Size
Optimization and Control.summary:
We study the almost sure convergence of the Stochastic Approximation algorithm to the fixed point $x^\star$ of a nonlinear operator under a negative drift condition and a general noise sequence with finite $p$-th moment for some $p > 1$. Classical almost sure convergence results of Stochastic Approximation are mostly analyzed for the square-integrable noise setting, and it is shown that any non-summable but square-summable step size sequence is sufficient to obtain almost sure convergence. However, such a limitation prevents wider algorithmic application. In particular, many applications in Machine Learning and Operations Research admit heavy-tailed noise with infinite variance, rendering such guarantees inapplicable. On the other hand, when a stronger condition on the noise is available, such guarantees on the step size would be too conservative, as practitioners would like to pick a larger step size for a more preferable convergence behavior. To this end, we show that any non-summable but $p$-th power summable step size sequence is sufficient to guarantee almost sure convergence, covering the gap in the literature.
  For the regime $p \in (1, 2)$, we show that using the $\|x-x^\star\|^p$-like Lyapunov function and applying the Holder-smoothness bound suffice. For $p > 2$, such an approach is no longer applicable, and therefore, we introduce a novel iterate projection technique to control the nonlinear terms produced by high-moment bounds and multiplicative noise. We believe our proof techniques and their implications could be of independent interest and pave the way for finite-time analysis of Stochastic Approximation under a general drift condition. As a starting point, we establish almost sure convergence results for non-expansive operators under a multiplicative noise condition for $p \in (1,2]$ and an additive noise condition for $p \in (2,\infty)$.

Optimization and Control.title: Decentralized Multi-product Pricing: Diagonal Dominance, Nash Equilibrium, and Price of Anarchy
Optimization and Control.summary: Decentralized pricing in multi-product firms and marketplaces can lose revenue because each decision maker ignores how its price affects the demand for other products. We quantify this loss through the price of anarchy of a game in which the price of each product is set to maximize that product's own revenue. Demand is linear, and cross-price effects may be substitutes or complements and need not be symmetric. Under a two-sided diagonal dominance condition with parameter $μ\in[0,1)$, which bounds the aggregate absolute cross-price effects in each row and column relative to the own-price effect, we show that the game has a unique Nash equilibrium and that equilibrium revenue is at least a fraction $4(1-μ)/(2-μ)^2$ of the centralized optimum. This bound was previously known for symmetric gross substitutes; we show that it remains valid for signed and asymmetric interactions, and that it is tight. Because asymmetry breaks the simultaneous diagonalization underlying existing analyses, we instead evaluate the revenue gap at the equilibrium itself. This yields an exact formula for the worst-case price of anarchy of each demand matrix in terms of a normalized interaction matrix, which can be much sharper than the scalar bound in heterogeneous interaction networks. The same argument extends the guarantee to jointly concave nonlinear demand under pointwise dominance of the demand Jacobian, for every pure-strategy equilibrium.

Optimization and Control.title: 0/1 integer programming over polytopes of Chvátal rank one is as hard as lattice problems
Optimization and Control.summary: A rational polyhedron has Chvátal rank at most one if a single round of Chvátal-Gomory cuts yields its integer hull. In 1973, Chvátal asked whether 0/1 integer programs over polytopes of bounded Chvátal rank can be solved in polynomial time. For polyhedra of bounded Chvátal rank, integer feasibility is in NP $\cap$ coNP, so it is unlikely to be NP-hard. We answer Chvátal's question negatively already in its most restricted form: for Chvátal rank one, for integer feasibility, and even for the SAT polytopes of formulas whose clauses have at most three literals. Our answer holds under either of two standard assumptions from lattice-based cryptography. First, a polynomial-time algorithm for integer feasibility on such SAT polytopes of Chvátal rank one would solve bounded distance decoding with polynomial factors in deterministic polynomial time, contradicting the conjectured hardness of approximating lattice problems within polynomial factors. Second, assuming the hardness of learning with errors, an average-case analog of bounded distance decoding, the problem is also hard on average, for a polynomial-time samplable distribution of formulas. This also gives negative answers to related questions of Cornuéjols, Lee, and Li. We first prove these results for parallelepipeds, where they rest on an elementary sufficient condition: a polyhedron has Chvátal rank at most one if its width is less than one along every row of some unimodular matrix. For our parallelepipeds, such a matrix exists but is hard to find. For SAT polytopes, we represent candidate lattice vectors by their residues modulo small integers, and binary arithmetic on additional 0/1 variables checks that these vectors lie in the lattice.

Optimization and Control.title: Online Covariance Estimation for Averaged Stochastic Gradient Descent on Riemannian Manifolds
Optimization and Control.summary: We study online inference for averaged Riemannian stochastic gradient descent (RSGD) when the unknown parameter lies on a manifold. Although the averaged RSGD iterate is asymptotically normal, practical inference requires estimating the unknown covariance operator in its limiting distribution. Existing online batch-means methods cannot be applied directly because a general Riemannian manifold lacks an addition operation, and the tangent space containing the Riemannian gradient varies across iterations. Through vector transport, we construct overlapping and non-overlapping covariance estimators that adaptively combine information from successive batches while accounting for the changing tangent spaces. The proposed estimators are online, require neither Riemannian Hessian computations nor a prespecified terminal sample size, and attain the same convergence rates as their Euclidean counterparts (Zhu et al., 2023). Together with asymptotic normality, these estimators enable online statistical inference for RSGD on manifolds. We illustrate the proposed framework through a detailed study of streaming principal component analysis on Grassmann manifolds.

Optimization and Control.title: Successive Convexification for Passively-Safe Spacecraft Rendezvous on Near Rectilinear Halo Orbit
Optimization and Control.summary: We present an optimization-based approach for fuel-efficient spacecraft rendezvous to Gateway, a lunar space station architecture based on a near rectilinear halo orbit (NRHO) around the Earth-Moon L2 point. Our main contribution is a method that ensures safety at all times in the presence of Gaussian uncertainty while incorporating disturbance compensation feedback through correction maneuvers. Specifically, the approach: i) ensures passive safety and satisfies path constraints at all times, ii) satisfies the specifications for critical decision points along the trajectory, and iii) accounts for common uncertainties arising from orbital insertion maneuvers, actuation, and navigation measurements. To account for these uncertainties, we use both chance constraints and disturbance compensation feedback to bound the effects of errors. We leverage sequential convex programming (SCP) together with an isoperimetric reformulation of continuous-time path constraints, including passive safety, to eliminate the risk of inter-sample constraint violations common in existing methods. This enables sparse time discretization that supports efficient offline mission design and analysis and aligns with operational preferences for less frequent control actions. We demonstrate the method on a case study representative of Gateway rendezvous operations.
Optimization and Control.comment: Accepted to Journal of Guidance, Control, and Dynamics

Computer Science and Game Theory.title: Asymmetric-Information Resource Allocation Games: An LP Approach to Purposeful Deception
Computer Science and Game Theory.summary: In this work, we introduce the Deceptive Resource Allocation Game (DRAG), which studies purposeful deception within a Bayesian game framework. In DRAG, a Defender allocates resources across the true asset and several decoys to influence an Attacker's beliefs and actions, with the goal of diverting the Attacker away from the true asset. We seek to characterize purposeful deception, whereby the Defender deceives only when doing so improves its performance. To this end, we solve for the Perfect Bayesian Nash Equilibrium (PBNE) of the corresponding game. We show that, despite the coupled belief-policy interdependence, the problem admits an efficient, non-iterative linear programming formulation. Numerical results demonstrate that the resulting policies naturally balance effective allocation and belief manipulation, giving rise to purposeful and emergent deceptive behaviors.

Computer Science and Game Theory.title: Computing Evolutionarily Stable Strategies in Multiplayer Games
Computer Science and Game Theory.summary: We present an algorithm for computing evolutionarily stable strategies in symmetric normal-form games with three or more players.

Computer Science and Game Theory.title: Computing Evolutionarily Stable Strategies in Imperfect-Information Games
Computer Science and Game Theory.summary: We present an algorithm for computing evolutionarily stable strategies (ESSs) in symmetric two-player perfect-recall extensive-form games of imperfect information. The algorithm operates directly in sequence form, avoiding explicit enumeration of normal-form supports. In a biologically motivated cancer signaling game, the algorithm recovers all seven symmetric Nash equilibria and identifies all three ESSs, each with a clear biological interpretation. Experiments on random imperfect-information games evaluate scalability as the numbers of private signals and available actions increase.

Computer Science and Game Theory.title: The Conditional Value of Costly Information in Collective-Risk Dilemmas
Computer Science and Game Theory.summary: Many high-stakes collective problems, e.g., climate mitigation and pandemic response, share a structure in which risk materializes unless a group threshold is met. This threshold is often uncertain, but uncertainty can be reduced at a cost. We study this information cost tradeoff in an evolutionary game theoretic model of social learning in the collective-risk dilemma, where individuals must cooperate to reach a possibly uncertain threshold to prevent collective loss. Individuals may pay a fixed cost to observe the threshold's true value and condition their cooperation on it. Across four threshold priors, we characterize risk levels at which cooperative equilibria emerge and show that low cost information increases group success. However, this effect is reversed at higher costs. We define a private \emph{value of information} and show that information is worth buying only when it is considerably cheaper than contributing. When purchased information is shared with the group, the cooperative tipping point shifts to lower risk levels. Despite bearing a private cost, above this tipping point buyers earn more in expectation than information free-riders. We then study these dynamics when information diffuses through a network, allowing nodes to relay it. Although fewer individuals pay for information, relaying increases group success, and noisy relaying does not reduce it. By contrast, false information does, especially when it originates at the hubs of heterogeneous networks, and large attacks can bring collective action close to collapse. Buyers act as a firewall against disinformation, confining it to source neighbourhoods, and once disinformation sources are removed, the population recovers. The value of costly information thus depends on its price, the level of risk, and how it is shared, and, in our setting, the effort of acquiring it also protects the population against disinformation.

Computer Science and Game Theory.title: The Hive Mind is a Single Reinforcement Learning Agent
Computer Science and Game Theory.summary: Decision-making is an essential attribute of any intelligent agent or group. Natural systems are known to converge to effective strategies through at least two distinct mechanisms: collective decision-making via imitation of others, and trial-and-error by a single agent. This paper establishes an equivalence between these two paradigms. We show that the emergent distributed cognition (sometimes referred to as the hive mind) arising from individuals following simple, local imitation-based rules is that of a single online reinforcement learning (RL) agent aggregating action-value samples from many parallel instances of a multi-armed bandit. More specifically, we show that, in the blindly imitative weighted voter model of honey bees' waggle dance, the update rule through which this macro-agent learns is an RL algorithm that we coin Maynard-Cross Learning. Our analysis implies that a group of individuals following simple imitative strategies can be equivalent to a more complex learning entity, substantiating the idea that group-level intelligence may explain how seemingly irrational individual behaviors are selected in nature. Beyond biology, the framework offers new tools for analyzing economic and social systems where individuals imitate successful strategies, effectively participating in a collective learning process. Our findings may further inform the design of scalable RL-inspired collective systems in artificial domains.

Computer Science and Game Theory.title: Strategic Calibration in LLM Multi-Agent Systems: Audited Pivot Scoring for Truthful Elicitation
Computer Science and Game Theory.summary: In large language model (LLM)-based multi-agent systems, reported confidence increasingly determines the allocation of scarce downstream attention, computation, and decision influence. This makes reporting strategic: an agent may overstate the relevance of its contribution even when its underlying belief is well calibrated. Existing calibration methods largely assume passive reporting and therefore do not address strategic incentives created when confidence determines downstream allocation. We formulate strategic calibration as a reporting-layer incentive problem and propose the Audited Pivot Scoring Mechanism (APSM). APSM offsets platform-controlled allocation benefits, uses inverse-propensity-weighted sparse audits, charges the Clarke pivot externality, and applies a strictly proper score. Under the stated model assumptions, truthful reporting is the unique expected-utility best response. We also characterize approximate execution and the audit-variance trade-off. Calculator-free experiments show that LLM agents inflate confidence under Top-$K$ incentives. With a shared agent-local utility interface, LLM agents reduce distortion under both Compensated Proper Scoring (CPS) and APSM. CPS achieves higher exact allocation match, whereas APSM yields lower Brier loss and numerically fewer cutoff crossings. Experiments further show that APSM enlarges the utility margin against allocation-changing deviations by $1.93\times$ and improves robustness under approximate execution. These results support incentive-aware elicitation as a distinct layer for reliable multi-agent coordination.
Computer Science and Game Theory.comment: 22 pages, 12 figures, including appendices

Computer Science and Game Theory.title: A Factor-6 Truthful-in-Expectation Mechanism for Cascade Position Auctions
Computer Science and Game Theory.summary: Position auctions require assigning advertisers to positions and determining their display order. Under cascade behavior, earlier clicks prevent users from reaching later placements, coupling the click probabilities of selected advertisements.
