Under strict privacy budgets, competing schemes remain near random-chance performance, while under relaxed budgets they continue to lag significantly behind the proposed design.

Information Theory.title: The Capacity of Private Information Retrieval from Coded Storage Systems with Colluding, Robust and Byzantine Servers
Information Theory.summary: We consider the problem of private information retrieval from MDS-coded databases with $T$ colluding servers, $U$ robust servers, and $B$ Byzantine servers, referred to as U-B-MDS-TPIR. In the U-B-MDS-TPIR setting, $M$ files are stored across $N$ servers, and in this paper each file is independently encoded using an $(N,K)$ GRS code. We characterize the capacity among linear, full support-rank U-B-MDS-TPIR schemes as $C=\frac{N-U-2B}{N-U}(1+\frac{K+T-1}{N-U-2B}+\cdots+(\frac{K+T-1}{N-U-2B})^{M-1})^{-1}$ when $N-U-2B\ge KT$. When $K=1$ or $T=1$, the same expression gives the capacity without the linearity and full support-rank restrictions. We further extend the construction to the retrieval of $P$ out of $M$ files. For $P \ge \frac{M}{2}$, the resulting multi-file scheme achieves capacity when $K=1$ or $T=1$.

Information Theory.title: Code uniqueness of 4-cell connected disjoint clusters in spatial chromatic model
Information Theory.summary: The spatial chromatic model (SCM) is a novel entity-oriented spatial data model proposed in recent years. Spatial tessellations formed by SCM have been applied in preliminary analyses of spatial point pattern recognition,spatial topology, and Voronoi diagram generation. Unlike previous spatial tessellation models, a key feature of SCM is that each subspace (cell) possesses a chromatic code, which serves as the foundation for various theoretical analyses and applications of SCM. The uniqueness of cell cluster codes in SCM constitutes an important property of the model. Previous studies have demonstrated the uniqueness of the chromatic codes of 2-cell and 3-cell connected disjoint clusters. Building on this analysis of connected cluster code characteristics, this paper proves the uniqueness of the chromatic codes of 4-cell connected disjoint clusters. The proof results and the new concepts introduced in this study help further refine the spatial chromatic model and provide a theoretical foundation for its subsequent applications.

Information Theory.title: A Constructive Method to Maximize Entropy under Marginal Constraints
Information Theory.summary: We study the problem of maximizing R{é}nyi entropy of order $2$ (equivalently, minimizing the index of coincidence) over the set of joint distributions with prescribed marginals. A closed-form optimizer is known under a feasibility condition on the marginals; we show that this condition is highly restrictive. We then provide an explicit construction of an optimal coupling for arbitrary marginals. Our approach characterizes the optimizer's structure and yields an iterative algorithm that terminates in finite time, returning an exact solution after at most $p-1$ updates, where $p$ is the number of rows.

Information Theory.title: It Takes Two Moments: Rigidity and Limits of Continuous Encoders for Over-the-Air Computation
Information Theory.summary: We study over-the-air computation of functions, such as empirical variance, formed by combining two separately postprocessed sums of locally transformed observations. We consider continuous encoders subject to pointwise peak-power constraints over a single use of a complex multiple-access channel. With four or more transmitters, we identify conditions under which exact noiseless recovery forces every continuous encoder collection into a common affine structure that preserves both sums, reducing infinite-dimensional encoder design to selecting a finite set of coefficients. To quantify resilience against channel noise, we introduce a robustness score that measures the separation of noiseless received aggregates relative to variations in the desired function value. Within this characterized encoder family, we formulate robustness maximization as an exact convex semi-infinite program, eliminating rank constraints without a relaxation gap, and construct a decoder that attains the minimum uniform noise-amplification constant. For several function classes, including empirical variance, we derive closed-form robustness-optimal encoders and scores. Under mild regularity conditions, we also establish sharp limits on the Gaussian mean squared error at high signal-to-noise ratios and show how using the input distribution reduces average error at the expense of uniform robustness.

Information Theory.title: Negative Results for Reciprocity-Based Over-the-Air Split Learning Under Channel Aging: Stability, Alignment, and Geometry
Information Theory.summary: In reciprocity-based over-the-air split learning, channel aging rotates and attenuates the derivative signal returned to the transmitter. Seven case studies combine numerical forecasts, mechanism checks, and competing predictions. Near the correlation zero, an archived SGD comparison finds truncated inversion 0.000813 lower in cross-entropy than polar correction, with a paired 95% interval for the difference from -0.001853 to 0.000060, and a retained-mode quadratic proxy slightly favors truncation. Selecting the return port with the largest received power falls short of the predicted five-point alignment advantage over random selection at both tested spacings, gaining at most 0.97 points, while the local inverse relation between amplitude and phase gradient is supported. Seven specified interference-induced accuracy-collapse predictions are rejected, and independent zero-mean interference preserves the conditional mean under a fixed linear chain. Per-subcarrier correction and spherical-wavefront compensation do not deliver their predicted accuracy gains. Focusing leaves both methods near chance in a single-mode model and adds no observed gain in a model with a line-of-sight component plus scattering. A successful port assignment under nonsymmetric motion refutes an exact-symmetry requirement. The competing positioning-error prediction is supported. Gaussian rail jitter with a standard deviation of 0.383 wavelengths yields high terminal test accuracy, whereas a fixed bias of the same magnitude yields near-chance accuracy. These cases distinguish valid local physical relations from unsupported training forecasts through task support, noise injection, and update moments.
Information Theory.comment: 10 pages, 1 figure, 5 tables. Companion to arXiv:2610.23118, arXiv:2610.23135 and arXiv:2610.23137

Information Theory.title: Deep Holes and Aperture: Sign Laws for the Empirical Correlation of Lattice-Sampled Random Wave Fields
Information Theory.summary: A Gaussian random wave field is sampled on a lattice within a bounded aperture. After displacement, re-indexing leaves a residual in the Voronoi cell. We study whether the empirical lag correlation has positive real part throughout the cell. For each realization in a single-output reciprocal link with noiseless over-the-air return, this is equivalent to the negative returned gradient being a descent direction for all residuals and differentiable losses with nonzero error signals. Return noise is treated exactly. For isotropic fields, ball-shaped apertures, unshifted lattice points, and dilations approaching the critical covering radius, every minimizer is a deep hole except with exponentially small probability. A Gaussian vector on the deep holes determines the limiting failure probability, with explicit covariance and lattice-independent limiting normalization. Square, hexagonal, simple cubic, and body-centered cubic lattices have two, three, four, and twelve sign classes. At fixed target failure probabilities below the critical limiting value, this covariance determines the exact leading aperture constant. When the margin and target failure probability vanish jointly, that constant is common to lattice shapes within each dimension. A cubic correction yields vanishing relative tail error in a moderate-deviation regime. A non-asymptotic two-sided aperture law has explicit constants. With a Rayleigh-faded specular path and positive diffuse margin, a failure floor occurs at every positive path power exactly when the cosine of its phase change is negative somewhere in the cell. The floor vanishes for all directions exactly when the covering radius is at most a quarter wavelength.
Information Theory.comment: 22 pages, 1 figure. Submitted to the IEEE Transactions on Information Theory

Information Theory.title: When Multiple-Unicast Feasibility Is Equivalent to Single-Sink Routability
Information Theory.summary: In communication networks, network coding allows intermediate nodes to combine messages, achieving transmission rates unattainable by routing alone in many multicast settings. In multiple unicast, where each source sends a message only to its prescribed destination, a central question is under what conditions fractional routing suffices to attain the transmission rates supported by network coding. We prove that, for any given collection of multiple-unicast demands in an undirected network, if the maximum flow between every pair of distinct destinations is at least the total demand rate, then the following are equivalent in feasibility: multiple-unicast coding, multiple-unicast fractional routing, and simultaneous fractional routing of all source rates to any fixed destination. Verifying this pairwise maximum-flow condition and, when it holds, deciding feasibility of the given multiple-unicast demands require at most as many maximum-flow computations as there are destinations. As a direct corollary, we prove the Langberg--Médard conjecture: if a directed network supports coded multicast of independent source messages at a common rate to every destination, then removing arc directions without changing capacities permits simultaneous fractional routing at that rate for all prescribed source--destination pairs.
Information Theory.comment: 14 pages, 3 figures. Revised exposition and proof presentation

Information Theory.title: Collision-Free Schedule Acquisition through Slotted ALOHA: Scaling Laws and Fluctuations
Information Theory.summary: Goal-oriented sensing, estimation, and control benefit from prompt, regular access to task-relevant updates. Although 1-persistent age-threshold slotted ALOHA (1-pTSA) can self-organize into a periodic collision-free schedule, its acquisition transient can dominate finite-horizon performance. We propose role-protected counter-threshold slotted ALOHA (RP--CTSA), which separates reservation memory from the age of information (AoI). A scheduled singleton retains its phase after colliding with active contenders, whereas a collision involving multiple scheduled nodes releases them immediately; AoI resets only after a decoded update. The protocol requires individual acknowledgments and a binary RELEASE/HOLD indication, but no centralized phase assignment or identification of colliders. Let $n$ denote the number of nodes and $Γ_n$ the counter threshold. Under inverse-population access scaling, the acquisition dynamics admit an exact pure-death representation. When $Γ_n=n$, the acquisition time is $O(n^2)$; when $Γ_n\sim(1+θ)n$, with $θ>0$, it is $O(n\log n)$. Simulations confirm both regimes and show substantial finite-horizon AoI gains over 1-pTSA while preserving every collision-free schedule.

Information Theory.title: On different notions related to APN mappings
Information Theory.summary: An APN mapping $F:\mathbb{F}_{2^n}\to \mathbb{F}_{2^n}$ is a polynomial characterized by the non-vanishing property on 2-flats. In this work, we analyze notions that are closely related to this property. To understand which $k$-flats of $\mathbb{F}_{2^n}$ remain flats under $F$, we study the $k$-breaking. The function $x^{-1}$ has been studied in the past in this context---we extend this study to general mappings and characterize the 2-breaking of APN functions. Recently, two generalizations of the APN property have been introduced: $k$-strongly non-normality and $k$-th-order sum-freedom. Sum-freedom generalizes the non-vanishing property of APN functions to higher dimensional flats. We provide in-depth observations of the relations between the breaking property, strongly non-normality and sum-freedom. We introduce a fourth concept called $k$-strongly breaking, which implies the breaking property. We derive several structural results for both notions and give a characterization of a subclass of APN functions in terms of the 2-strongly breaking property. We propose a different perspective of the non-vanishing property via a natural character transformation, which is closely related to the sum-of-square indicator of the components of $F$. We derive a precise value for the total sum of the sum-of-square indicators of $F$. With this approach, we provide a simple answer to Open Problem 4 in IEEE Trans. Inf. Theory 52(9): 4160-4170, 2006. Moreover, it allows us to explore balancedness properties of polynomials, one of which characterizes component-wise APNness, for odd $n$, and provides a natural extension to any dimension. We show that Dillon's APN permutation and the Gold functions satisfy a related property, termed $k$-balanced, which is presented under our framework.
Information Theory.comment: 30 pages, 2 figures, 3 tables. Example 3.2 has been added. As a consequence, Conjecture 3.1 was modified and renamed as Open Problem 1. The discussion leading to it has been revised. The abstract, introduction, and conclusion are rewritten accordingly

Information Theory.title: A combinatorial description of when a self-associated set of points fails to be arithmetically Gorenstein
Information Theory.summary: We give a combinatorial proof that the set of points associated to a self-dual code with no proportional columns is arithmetically Gorenstein if and only if the code is indecomposable. This answers a question asked by Tohăneanu. We do so by providing a combinatorial way to compute the dimension of the Schur square of a self-dual code through a zero-one symmetrization of a systematic generator matrix. Our approach also allows us to compute the Gorenstein defect. As a consequence, we obtain a combinatorial characterization of arithmetically Gorenstein self-associated sets of points over an algebraically closed field. We also show that, for any finite field, almost all self-dual codes of large length are indecomposable, and hence their associated sets of points are arithmetically Gorenstein.

Information Theory.title: Exploiting Pinching Antenna Systems in NOMA Covert Communication Networks
Information Theory.summary: Pinching antenna systems (PASS) provide flexible transmitter-side radiation reconfiguration for high-frequency wireless communications. This paper applies PASS to non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) covert communication networks, where activated pinching antennas (PAs) transmit superimposed signals to a pair of users stochastically distributed within a rectangle. Two passive wardens respectively monitor the downlink transmissions intended for two users. More specifically, we derive the closed-form detection error probability (DEP) expressions for two wardens under bounded noise uncertainty. Then we analytically determine the optimal detection thresholds and minimum DEPs in the worst-case covert detection scenarios. The covert transmission rates of two users are further characterized by taking into consideration ideal successive interference cancellation and non-ideal successive interference cancellation at near user and intra-NOMA interference at far user. Numerical results are presented to confirm that: 1) PASS-NOMA is capable of providing higher covert rates relative to conventional orthogonal multiple access OMA schemes; 2) As the number of activated PAs begun to increase, the near user has ability to obtain a larger covert rate gain than far user; and 3) The DEP of PASS-NOMA networks is larger than that of both PASS-OMA and traditional antenna based NOMA in specific output power regions.

Information Theory.title: Counting the Fixed Points of Binary Belief Propagation: Generic Degree, Syzygies, and Real Solutions
Information Theory.summary: How many fixed points does belief propagation have on a binary pairwise model? Over complex parameters, the admissible equations of a finite loopless multigraph form an algebraic family whose generic degree we determine: it is a graph state sum over edge sets without vertices of degree one, each vertex of positive degree contributing one less than its degree. We give two geometric realizations of this state sum. The first is the total Betti number of a universal edge-incidence ring constructed without parameters. Its full graded Betti table is the state sum, its Tor algebra is natural for noncontracting graph maps, the alternating numerator recovers the graph polynomial of Watanabe and Fukumizu, and an Artin reduction by a regular sequence realizes the one-variable specialization, corrected for tree components. The second lies in the actual family: at the strong-field boundary each state factor is a ramification index, and at sufficiently strong field the state charts exhaust the admissible complex fiber. For fixed nonzero real couplings, every Eulerian message-sign sector contains a real fixed point at every external field, and strong fields attain this lower bound: one admissible real fixed point per element of the binary cycle space and one positive fixed point. For graphs of maximum degree at most three, this minimum equals the number of minimal module generators of the edge-incidence ring. One state decomposition connects the complex degree, graded syzygies, and an attained minimum real count. The degree, selected ring and resolution statements, and the real counts are formalized in Lean 4.
Information Theory.comment: 33 pages (main text and supplementary material SM1-SM6 in one PDF), 1 figure. Lean 4 formalization of the main results: https://github.com/ywatanabex/bp-degree-syzygies-lean

Information Theory.title: Logarithmic asymptotics for polynomial threshold functions
Information Theory.summary: We count Boolean functions represented as the sign of a real polynomial of bounded degree on the $n$-dimensional cube. We prove that the logarithm of their number is asymptotic to that of the classical hyperplane-arrangement upper bound, uniformly over all degrees, with relative error $O((\log n)^2/n)$. We also obtain sharper additive and relative error estimates in particular degree ranges, including an additive error $O(n^2)$ between the logarithms throughout a small linear degree range and improved bounds just below the central degree. The proof combines probabilistic estimates for Reed--Muller codes with a deletion argument for sets of evaluation vectors, an entropy count, and a sharp-threshold estimate for expected rank deficiency.
Information Theory.comment: 39 pages. Revised exposition and organisation, with expanded explanations. Main results and theorem statements unchanged

Information Theory.title: Digital Twin-Guided Wireless Localization via Probabilistic Inverse Learning
Information Theory.summary: This work investigates how site-specific digital twins (DTs) can support wireless localization using simplified distributed infrastructure. We propose PRISM (Probabilistic Refinement using Inverse learning and a Site-specific Model), a DT-guided probabilistic localization scheme with single-antenna access points (APs). Localization is formulated as a probabilistic inverse problem in which a conditional proposal distribution over UE locations is learned from multi-node channel impulse responses (CIRs). The proposal generates candidate locations, with its spread regularized during training and DT consistency used to reweight candidates and refine the estimate at inference. The DT serves as an approximate forward-consistency model, avoiding assumptions of exact channel fidelity or differentiability with respect to user position. Numerical experiments demonstrate gains over data-driven and classical fingerprinting benchmarks, while achieving a median error of approximately $0.7$ m using 10 single-antenna APs. Without retraining, PRISM remains effective under degraded inference-time DT features. PRISM also yields uncertainty estimates from its proposal covariance, with empirical $χ^2$ calibration approaching ideal behavior as APs increase.

Information Theory.title: Variable-Length Feedback Coding With Universal Decoding and Bandit Channel Selection
Information Theory.summary: We study variable-length feedback (VLF) coding over $K$ additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN) channels whose noise variances are unknown to both terminals but lie in a known interval. The receiver selects one channel at each time, conveys the selection over noiseless feedback, and must learn the channel qualities while decoding, to avoid overusing suboptimal channels. This setting, which we call the VLF-Bandit problem, combines VLF coding, universal decoding, and bandit channel selection. We develop two joint coding and channel-selection schemes. The VLSF-Bandit scheme is a single-phase variable-length stop-feedback (VLSF) scheme based on a Gaussian random codebook, a score formed from a ratio of likelihood mixtures, and the asymptotically optimal $\text{kl-UCB}^{++}$ bandit algorithm applied to the received power. The VLF-Bandit scheme sends the message in packets by Schalkwijk--Kailath transmission, uses its normalized outputs as noise samples to learn the variances, and lets its exploration packets carry message bits. We prove second-order achievability bounds for both schemes, which are first-order optimal. In the logarithm of the achievable codebook size, the magnitude of the $\log N$ coefficient, with $N$ the average decoding time, is a baseline of one plus a channel-exploration term for VLSF-Bandit. For VLF-Bandit, this magnitude is smaller, with a universal-decoding term replacing the baseline and a smaller channel-exploration term. The VLF-Bandit bound improves on the universal VLF bound of Yavas and Tan (2025) for $K=1$ and on the bound of an explore-then-commit strategy whenever $K\geq2$.
Information Theory.comment: 34 pages, submitted to Transactions on Information Theory

Information Theory.title: Rethinking Channel Estimation for Fluid Antenna Systems: A Physics-Informed Operator Learning
Information Theory.summary: Fluid antenna systems (FAS) leverage continuous reconfigurable apertures to transcend the spatial limits of fixed-position arrays, yet acquiring full-aperture channel state information (CSI) from sparse observations remains a formidable bottleneck. In this paper, we establish a continuous-field formulation for FAS by recasting channel estimation as a stochastic inverse field-reconstruction problem constrained by the projected Helmholtz model. Through electromagnetic information theory (EIT)-based spectral leakage analysis, we demonstrate that finite-aperture reconstruction induces an intrinsic convolutional relationship in the spectral domain, rendering the estimation task a fundamental frequency-domain inverse deconvolution problem. To solve this, we propose a U-shaped Fourier neural operator (UFNO) specifically tailored for noisy, underdetermined wireless environments. Furthermore, we leverage the Landau--Pollak theorem to derive an aperture-dependent EDoF bound that guides the spatial mode budget, and employ a physics-aware Sobolev loss to promote consistency in both channel values and spatial variations. Unlike conventional learning-based approaches, a single frozen UFNO can be directly evaluated at unseen spatial--frequency resolutions without resolution-specific retraining or explicit output interpolation. Extensive simulations show that our framework significantly outperforms state-of-the-art benchmarks in accuracy while achieving orders-of-magnitude lower inference latency than iterative solvers at high spatial--frequency resolutions.

Information Theory.title: Sensitivity of RMS Delay Spread Estimation to Power Delay Profile Thresholding in Time-Varying Channels at 33 GHz
Information Theory.summary: Root mean square (RMS) delay spread is a key parameter characterizing temporal dispersion in radio propagation channels. Its estimation from measured power delay profiles (PDPs), however, depends strongly on the adopted power threshold. This paper investigates the sensitivity of RMS delay spread estimates to relative PDP thresholding in a time-varying millimeter-wave channel at 33 GHz. The analysis uses wideband channel sounding measurements conducted in a dynamic road environment with moving vehicles. The temporal evolution and empirical cumulative distributions of RMS delay spread are evaluated for thresholds ranging from -20 to -50 dB. Reducing the threshold increases the median RMS delay spread from approximately 140 to 168 ns and the 90th percentile from 200 to 210 ns. Both statistics converge at lower thresholds, with -40 dB providing a practical convergence level. The results emphasize the importance of threshold selection for reliable channel characterization and consistent comparison of measurements.

Information Theory.title: Hilbert-Scale Stability of Posterior Diffusion Priors for Ill-Posed Signal Recovery
Information Theory.summary: Indirect and noisy observations are difficult to invert when the forward operator smooths out the unknown signal. In this case, the unstable modes are precisely the modes that the data reveals least, thus the success of any reconstruction method depends on how prior information interacts with the geometry of the operator across regularity scales. Diffusion priors have become ubiquitous for such problems; however, the current theory still does not determine when a learned score remains informative under ill-posed forward operators. In this paper, we study posterior diffusion for linear inverse problems on Hilbert scales and derive a stability theory under an explicit score-amplification condition. Under a smoothing condition on the forward map, a source condition on the truth, and weak-norm control of score error, we derive non-asymptotic recovery bounds in \(\Hs^s\) that separate observation noise, score approximation, and reverse-time discretization. These bounds give a recoverable regularity threshold determined jointly by operator smoothing, truth regularity, score regularity, and the posterior correction. The threshold specifies the Hilbert-scale norms \(\Hs^s\) in which weak-norm score error remains controlled after propagation through the posterior reverse dynamics. For larger regularity indices \(s\), the inverse geometry magnifies the same error, and the Hilbert-scale recovery estimate no longer gives uniform stability. We also prove that a posterior correction adapted to the forward operator improves stability relative to isotropic guidance in the regularity ranges where the smoothing action of the forward map matters most. The recovery estimates give a regularity-sensitive theory of posterior diffusion and show how learned score error, operator smoothing, and reconstruction norm jointly determine the stable range predicted by the analysis.

Information Theory.title: Finite Fields: Root Sets, Frobenius, and Algebraic Structure
Information Theory.summary: This monograph develops finite field theory through root sets, Frobenius orbits, trace duality, and cyclic modules, with applications to polynomial constructions and algebraic coding theory. Root-set descent and base extension are expressed through finite reduced algebras, while linearized polynomials connect normal bases, invariant subspaces, and linear recurrences. Coefficient pairings and derivative formulas recover information lost by trace pairings in quotient algebras with repeated factors. Cyclotomic cosets are studied through additive stabilizers, power substitution, and compatible factor lifting, including extensions to Galois rings. A central theme connects low-degree representations of subfields with conjugate root blocks, polynomial composition, and recovery from relative trace data. Return maps on root fibers determine factor degrees and organize constructions of irreducible polynomials, affine symmetries, and permutation polynomials. Applications include cyclic and constacyclic codes, BCH and Goppa distance bounds, rank-metric codes, trace codes, and Fourier support. Character orthogonality and Gauss and Jacobi sums yield counting formulas, a proof of the primitive normal basis theorem, and recurrences for extension-field character sums. Gaussian periods connect these methods with short linear relations in multiplicative subgroups. Proofs of Weil bounds for polynomial character sums combine auxiliary polynomials with generating polynomials and estimates for their reciprocal roots. The emphasis throughout is on explicit arguments connecting field structure, orbit structure, and linear dependence.

Information Theory.title: Coefficient choice in Galois-ring lifts of APN permutations: sharp unit-direction spectra and one-term optimal lifts
Information Theory.summary: Permutation polynomials over the Galois ring $\mathrm{GR}(2^k,m)$ are nonlinear components for symmetric primitives that add keys in the ring, as in secure computation modulo $2^k$. Rønjom and Sandrib showed that their differential uniformity is at least $2q^{k-1}$, where $q=2^m$. For the class studied here it is attained on top-layer differences, while almost all differences are units. We ask how small the difference table can be on unit differences when the residue permutation is fixed and only higher coefficient digits of its lift are chosen. Let $m\ge5$ be odd, $k\ge3$, and let $p$ be a reduced quadratic almost perfect nonlinear (APN) permutation of $\mathbb{F}_q$ whose derivative is nowhere zero and two-to-one. Over all lifts of $p$, the least possible maximum on unit differences is $q$ or $2q$, decided by two invariants of $p$ and the level $k$. We describe every lift attaining it and show that the coefficients modulo $8$ decide optimality at every level. For every odd $m\ge5$, residue permutations with at most $16$ monomials attain $q$ after one $2$-adic digit of one coefficient of the natural lift is changed. For an explicit infinite family, one added monomial lowers the maximum on unit differences from $4q$, or from at least $q^2$, to $2q$ at every level without raising the degree. Under a uniform starting state and independent uniform round keys, valuation preservation yields layerwise bounds for characteristics and two-round differentials that distinguish lifts with the same global uniformity. Core results are formalized in Lean 4.
Information Theory.comment: 25 pages. Version 2 is a substantially revised and extended paper with a new title. Lean 4 formalization, blueprint and finite computations: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23683493 (version 2.0.0; https://github.com/hirokifukui/residue-apn)

Information Theory.title: Ancestor Lifting of Quasi-Cyclic Additive Codes and Certified Quantum Codes
Information Theory.summary: Additive codes over $\Ffour$ that are self-orthogonal under the trace inner product correspond to binary quantum stabilizer codes. We study 1-generator $(1,2)$-quasi-cyclic (QC) additive codes and their exact quantum distances. For composite lengths $n=\ell m$, an ancestor-lifting theorem transports dual words of the folded ancestor to the length-$n$ code. A two-layer decomposition for $\ell=2$ and a CRT splitting for odd $\ell$ yield dimension laws and explain equality, escape, and mixed-branch behavior in the certified examples. A palindromic criterion ensures symplectic self-orthogonality, while reversal pairing and a symplectic Gram rank formula describe broader construction families. Exact distances are established by information-set decoding screening, Brouwer--Zimmermann computation on the additive dual, and independent witness verification. We certify twenty-one record-breaking binary quantum codes across twenty entries of Grassl's code table, with twenty-eight certified members in total. Propagation improves thirty-four further entries, and explicit constructions are supplied for three table-tying GV entries marked Code Missing Construction. Six additional candidates are reported only with rigorous upper bounds and heuristic screening evidence. The results connect divisor-lattice structure in additive quasi-cyclic codes with reproducible certification of exact quantum distances.

Information Theory.title: Black-Box Attack for IRS-Aided Communications with BER-Only Feedback
Information Theory.summary: Intelligent reflecting surface (IRS) has emerged as a promising wireless technology for enhancing legitimate communications. In this paper, we investigate an IRS-assisted multiuser MISO downlink network in which an attacker reconfigures the IRS to degrade legitimate data transmission. Specifically, we consider a black-box attack setting in which the attacker has access to neither channel information nor symbol-level observations and can observe only the BER reported by each user. The objective of the attacker is to identify an IRS configuration that maximizes the minimum BER among all users under a limited budget of non-repeated tests. To address this BER-only black-box attack problem, we propose PRIS, an online search method that learns effective phase transitions from previous trials and progressively narrows the search from large-block modifications to single-element refinement. Specifically, an annealed user-balancing reward and prioritized replay are incorporated to exploit noisy BER feedback. Numerical results demonstrate that PRIS achieves a higher minimum BER than existing benchmarks.

Information Theory.title: The Exact Weight Spectrum of $\RM(m-7,m$): A Counterexample to the Carlet-Solé Conjecture
Information Theory.summary: Boolean functions are widely used in cryptography and coding theory. A key challenge lies in finding the weight spectrum for all $n$-variable Boolean functions of degree at most $r$, also known as the Reed--Muller code $\RM(r,n)$. In 2023, Carlet and Solé determined the weight spectra of $\RM(n-c,n)$ for $c=3,4$, and conjectured the weight spectrum of $\RM(n-c, n$) for $n\ge2c$. The weight spectra of $\RM(n-5, n)$ and $\RM(n-6,n)$ were determined by Carlet in 2024 and by Lou and Wang in 2025, respectively, confirming the Carlet-Solé conjecture for the cases $c=5,6$. Very recently, Leuenberger et al. and Wei et al. investigated the weight spectrum of $\RM(7,14)$ independently, and there are eight potential weights which have not been determined. Up until now, the weight spectra of the Reed--Muller codes $RM(r,n)$ are still unknown for $r=3,...,n-7$. In this paper, we determine the exact weight spectrum of $\RM(m-7, m)$ for every $m\ge 14$. By combining affine geometry and Fourier analysis, we exclude the conjectured eight weights for $\RM(7,14)$. We then extend the exclusions to all higher dimensions using a geometric transfer. Consequently, we provide a counterexample to the Carlet-Solé conjecture.

Information Theory.title: Design of DoF-Robust MIMO via Generalized Pinching Antennas
Information Theory.summary: Spatial degrees of freedom (DoF) are fundamental to the performance of multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems. However, the use of conventional fixed-location antennas introduces disparities in the users' distances to a common base station, which makes the multi-user channel matrix more susceptible to rank deficiency and, consequently, a loss of spatial DoF. This paper shows that generalized pinching antennas can be used to design a new form of MIMO robust to the loss of spatial DoF. In particular, by deploying pinching antennas in close proximity to the users, the resulting multi-user channel Gram matrix can have a well-conditioned, almost diagonal structure, which reduces its sensitivity to the users' spatial deployment as well as the risk of rank deficiency. Two performance metrics, namely the rank-deficiency probability and the outage probability, are used to evaluate the performance of pinching-antenna-assisted MIMO transmission. The presented analytical and simulation results demonstrate the capability of pinching antennas to preserve spatial DoF and provide ubiquitous connectivity by effectively supporting users at spatially separated locations.

Information Theory.title: PDE-Based Bounds on Optimal Exponents in Active Simple Hypothesis Testing
Information Theory.summary: We present general upper and lower bounds on the optimal error exponent for the Active Simple Hypothesis Testing (ASHT) problem. ASHT has been extensively studied across diverse fields including Information Theory, Bandits, and Operations Research, a precise characterization of this optimal exponent has remained elusive. This work combines a recent Partial Differential Equation (PDE) characterization of the optimal exponent by Vijayan (2025) with the comparison principle of viscosity solutions of Hamilton-Jacobi PDEs. This leads to bounds that are parametrized by convex functions, sets and lower Hamiltonian relaxations, a flexibility that generalizes many known results in the literature.

Information Theory.title: Pinching Antenna and Relay Assisted Joint Indoor Outdoor NOMA Communications with SWIPT
Information Theory.summary: This paper presents a unified downlink architec- ture for serving indoor and outdoor users from a shared multi-antenna rooftop base station (BS). To overcome severe building-penetration loss, the BS transfers information and radio- frequency (RF) energy to an indoor access point (AP) using simultaneous wireless information and power transfer (SWIPT). The AP harvests this energy and performs amplify-and-forward (AF) relaying, enabling self-sustained indoor communication. A movable waveguide-mounted pinching antenna (PA) further improves indoor coverage by adapting its position to the prop- agation environment. For outdoor transmission, zero-forcing (ZF) beamforming suppresses inter-group interference, while power-domain non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) supports multiple users within each group. We maximize the outdoor weighted sum rate (WSR) while satisfying stringent indoor and outdoor quality-of-service (QoS) requirements. The resulting nonconvex problem jointly optimizes the BS power fraction, SWIPT power-splitting ratio, PA position, and NOMA power allocation. To obtain an efficient solution, we develop a two-stage method based on alternating optimization (AO) and sequential quadratic programming (SQP). Numerical results show that the proposed architecture improves outdoor spectral efficiency while maintaining reliable, energy-sustainable indoor coverage. Increasing the BS array size further raises the indoor QoS- satisfaction probability toward unity, even under demanding rate targets.

Information Theory.title: ATEMPO: Amortized Transfer Entropy Model Per-lag Over-Time
Information Theory.summary: When one time series informs another, the delay at which that information arrives determines if models can utilize this relationship effectively. A source may be strongly predictive at one delay but uninformative at neighboring lags. Therefore, fixed input windows may obscure this structure by bundling informative and irrelevant history together. Transfer entropy (TE) can recover these delays by measuring how much a source's past tells us about a target beyond the target's own history. However, existing TE estimators require separate fits across source and conditioning depths, with further estimation on local windows to track delays over time. We introduce ATEMPO, a diffusion-based transfer entropy estimator amortized over lags and time. ATEMPO samples source and conditioning depths during training and conditions explicitly on temporal position, allowing a single score network to estimate the full TE surface without refitting. Differencing this surface recovers when information arrives. Across synthetic datasets with ground-truth TE, ATEMPO achieves the lowest mean relative error among baselines, and on datasets with known lags, ATEMPO achieves $0.98\pm0.04$ lag-detection accuracy. ATEMPO requires a single fit across source depths $K=6$ and target depths $L=3$, whereas existing estimators require 18 separate fits to evaluate the same $K \times L$ grid. On three systems with time-varying lag, ATEMPO is the only estimator to maintain perfect lag-detection accuracy across all evaluated window lengths. These recovered delays improve downstream forecasting: ATEMPO-selected inputs reduce MSE on WEATHER-5K by 7.25%, while 120 selected inputs outperform the benchmark's 240-feature default by 4.6%. Across three brain-computer interface tasks, using ATEMPO-selected lags achieves the highest or equal-best $R^2$, improving mean $R^2$ by 4.1% relative to the strongest competing baseline.

Information Theory.title: A Simple Presentation of Robust Membership Inference Attacks
Information Theory.summary: In a membership inference attack, an attacker is given the data of a particular individual, and tries to determine if that individual was included in a particular dataset, given some kind of statistics derived from the dataset or a model trained on the dataset. Roughly, a membership inference attack is robust if it succeeds even when the statistics are highly noisy, regardless of how that noise is introduced. We give a simple presentation of robust membership inference attacks for mean estimation, covering both multivariate Gaussian distributions and binary product distributions. We also give a summary of the literature on robust membership inference, covering history, extensions, and connections to other research areas.

Information Theory.title: Integral Probability Boundaries
Information Theory.summary: Bounds based on Integral Probability Metrics (IPMs) are ubiquitous in machine learning and statistics, appearing, e.g., in generalization, alignment, fairness, and privacy. IPMs reduce the discrepancy between two distributions to a single worst-case gap between expectations. This compression is costly: for rare events, safety failures, or under-represented groups, IPM-based bounds are loose or vacuous. We introduce a non-linear generalization of IPMs, which we term Integral Probability Boundaries (IPBs). Unlike IPMs, IPBs provide bounds that are tight at the extremes. We derive their basic properties and present algorithms for estimating them in practically relevant settings. We demonstrate the usage of IPBs in both theoretical and practical applications for alignment, judge-free performance estimation, and fairness, where they enable us to obtain sharp bounds on performance and fairness gaps, e.g., 15 p.p. more precise estimates on fairness gaps for rare groups in a realistic generative modeling task, compared to the state of the art.

Information Theory.title: On the burst-covering radius of binary cyclic codes
Information Theory.summary: We define and study burst-covering codes. We provide some general bounds connecting the parameters of a code with its burst-covering radius. We then provide stronger bounds on the burst-covering radius of cyclic codes, by employing linear-feedback shift-register (LFSR) sequences. For the case of BCH codes we prove a bound on pattern frequencies in LFSR sequences, and using this tool, we bound the burst-covering radius of binary primitive BCH codes and Melas codes. We then present an efficient burst-covering algorithm for cyclic codes. Finally, we present a bound on the critical exponent of cyclic codes based on the burst-covering radius.

Information Theory.title: An Improved Johnson Bound for List-Decoding with Hints
Information Theory.summary:
This paper studies when list-decodability guarantees for error-correcting codes of good distance can go beyond the classical Johnson radius and gives a corresponding efficient list-decoding algorithm for Reed-Solomon codes up to this new radius. The Johnson bound shows that any error-correcting code with distance $δ$ is automatically list-decodable with small list size up to a certain radius $J(δ)$ around any received word $r$. We show that if the received word $r$ is known to have some codewords that are somewhat close to it (we call these ``hints"), then $C$ is list-decodable with small list size up to an even larger radius around $r$.
  We determine the optimal list-decoding radius in this setting for single and multiple hints over both large and small alphabets and show that this radius is the optimum of a natural convex program. Remarkably, even a single hint that is $(J(δ)-ε)$-close to $r$ improves the list-decoding radius around $r$ to $J(δ)+ε'$.
  Finally, we give an efficient algorithm, based on the weighted Guruswami-Sudan decoder, that list-decodes Reed-Solomon codes up to this optimal radius.

Information Theory.title: On the $b$-Symbol Weight Distribution of Dual Melas Codes and a Poisson Randomness Postulate
Information Theory.summary:
We prove a new lower bound on the $b$-symbol weight of codewords in dual Melas codes, which is strictly better than known results. We employ a new strategy that translates a pattern counting problem in linear-feedback shift register sequences to a problem on orbits of binary polynomials under a certain action. We use the same techniques to provide an improved lower bound on the burst-covering radius of Melas codes and a new upper bound on the critical exponent of dual Melas codes.
  We then define a new randomness postulate on (families of) binary sequences, based on the definition of infinite Poisson generic sequences. We conjecture that codewords in the dual Melas code satisfy this postulate, and we show partial progress in establishing this conjecture. We also show how a relaxed version of the problem can be completely resolved, and relate the conjecture to the first part of the paper, giving a justification of why the improved bounds on the $b$-symbol weight were somewhat to be expected.

Information Theory.title: The list size of random linear and LDPC codes at capacity
Information Theory.summary: We show that for every prime power $q$ and $ρ\in(0,1-\frac1q)$ there exists $\varepsilon_0(q, ρ) > 0$ such that for all positive $\varepsilon < \varepsilon_0(q, ρ)$, a random linear code over $\mathbb{F}_q$ of rate $1-h_q(ρ)-\varepsilon$ has list size $\lfloor h_q(ρ)/\varepsilon\rfloor$ or $\lfloor h_q(ρ)/\varepsilon\rfloor+1$ with probability $1-o(1)$. Before this work, the list size was known only up to a constant factor for $q\ge3$, and for $q=2$ it was known to be either $\lfloor h_2(ρ)/\varepsilon\rfloor-1$, $\lfloor h_2(ρ)/\varepsilon\rfloor$ or $\lfloor h_2(ρ)/\varepsilon\rfloor+1$. We also show that the same two-point concentration holds for the list size of random LDPC codes. This follows from a general theorem establishing that random LDPC codes and random linear codes have the same threshold rate for distance, list decoding, list recovery from errors and any other \emph{convex} property, which answers a question of Mosheiff, Resch, Ron-Zewi, Silas and Wootters.

Information Theory.title: The LQ Digital Mode Family: Protocol Architecture and Reference Specification for Weak-Signal Communications
Information Theory.summary: This paper introduces LQ8, an open-source weak-signal digital mode for amateur radio that completes structured two-way contacts in 4 transmissions (60 s), achieving a 1.50x speedup over canonical 6-transmission exchanges (90 s) and 1.25x over 5-transmission RR73 exchanges (75 s) while preserving complete bidirectional exchange of Maidenhead grid locators, signal reports, and mutual acknowledgments. By replacing fixed-width message-type headers with variable-length prefix codes matched to physical-layer bit budgets, LQ8 packs the answering station's grid locator and measured signal report into a single 77-bit reply. In multi-station pileup operations, LQ8 confirms up to two answering stations simultaneously within a single-carrier 50.0 Hz transmission with a 0.0 dB RF power-splitting penalty, achieving a peak rate of 240 QSOs/h in continuous pileup (4x over single-carrier FT8; 480 QSOs/h dual-carrier) while retaining -21.0 dB SNR sensitivity. The protocol family also defines three extended profiles (LQ16, LQ4, and LQ2) tailored for extreme sensitivity, VHF/UHF contesting, and fast-burst channels.
Information Theory.comment: 8 pages, 1 figure, 7 tables. Reference library and portal at https://lq8.org

Information Theory.title: Federated Learning for Semantic Communications over Multiple Access Channels
Information Theory.summary: This paper presents a federated learning (FL) framework for semantic communication (SemCom) over the multiple access channel (MAC), where multiple distributed transmitters simultaneously convey semantic information to a common receiver using end-to-end learned semantic representations. Semantic feature extraction, compression, wireless transmission, and semantic inference are jointly optimized through FL-based SemCom. Unlike conventional SemCom systems that train users independently, simultaneous semantic transmissions over the MAC enable concurrent training of multiple transmitters within the same transmission interval, thereby reducing training overhead and channel usage. Federated semantic aggregation is incorporated with shared and personalized encoder components, allowing transmitters with limited local training data to benefit from semantic representations learned from transmitters possessing larger datasets while preserving local adaptation. Evaluated using the CIFAR-10 dataset over fading channels, the proposed approach maintains high semantic inference accuracy under shared wireless access and significantly improves performance under severe data imbalance. In the meantime, simultaneous semantic transmissions can significantly reduce training overhead while preserving robust semantic performance across distributed transmitters with heterogeneous local datasets. These results highlight the potential of combining FL and SemCom to support scalable and communication-efficient edge intelligence in future wireless networks.

Information Theory.title: A Poisson Transition and Bias Law for KSG Mutual-Information Estimation
Information Theory.summary: We quantify the error of the strict-radius Kraskov--Stögbauer--Grassberger (KSG-1) mutual-information estimator on a Gaussian channel as the sample size \(n\) grows and the channel becomes nearly deterministic. For fixed dimension \(p\) and neighbor index \(k\), we define the resolution parameter \(u_n=ne^{-I_n}\), where \(I_n\) is the true mutual information in nats. When \(u_n\to u\in(0,\infty)\), we prove that the estimation error converges in mean square to a computable deterministic bias \(B_{p,k}(u)\). Sampling fluctuations therefore vanish, while an additive bias can persist. We derive this bias from an explicit marked-Poisson law for the neighborhood counts, characterize its small-\(u\) asymptotics, and show that it tends to zero as \(u\to\infty\). The same law describes how often neighborhoods saturate, meaning that they make the largest possible contribution to the estimate. The limiting saturation probability decreases continuously and strictly from one to zero, allowing a Gaussian-model bias correction on fixed critical intervals. Finite-sample experiments show substantial bias even when the true information lies below the estimator's logarithmic ceiling and saturated neighborhoods are rare. Saturation-based correction reduces estimation error in these experiments, though recovering the resolution parameter from the observed saturation fraction can remain difficult when saturation is rare.

Information Theory.title: Efficient Joint Trajectory Optimization and Resource Allocation for Secure UAV Networks: A Deep Reinforcement Learning Approach
Information Theory.summary: Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) are increasingly deployed in wireless networks; however, ensuring secure communication and efficient energy usage remains challenging. This paper addresses the joint trajectory optimization and resource allocation problem in UAV networks in the presence of a tethered UAV flying center and a malicious ground eavesdropper. In the proposed model, UAVs are equipped with energy harvesting capabilities and can adaptively switch between transmitting, jamming, and relaying roles to deliver data to a tethered UAV center for optimized network performance. An optimization problem is formulated to maximize a utility function that balances secrecy rate, energy consumption, and interference. To address the high non-convexity of the problem and its real-time decision requirements, a Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO)-based Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) algorithm is proposed to solve the problem and learn the network dynamics. Extensive simulation results demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves superior secrecy performance, lower energy consumption, and reduced interference compared to conventional and DRL-based methods.
Information Theory.comment: This paper has been submitted for possible publication as a journal paper and is currently under review

Information Theory.title: Twisted Fourier Analysis of Quantum Weight Enumerators
Information Theory.summary: A unified Fourier framework for quantum weight enumerators of prime-power-dimensional qudits is developed in this paper. We introduce the notions of Weyl power spectrum and Weyl-conjugation autocorrelation for the Weyl-operator quantities nderlying the Shor--Laflamme weight enumerators. Representing these quantities as formal vectors, we show that they form a symplectic Fourier transform pair, from which the quantum MacWilliams identity follows by applying the Hamming-weight functional. This framework extends to a family of twisted Fourier transforms, including the Rains shadow transform. We show that identical-copy Bell sampling corresponds to a twisted autocorrelation related to the shadow enumerator through Weyl translation and Hamming projection. We further prove that all twisted Fourier transforms are Weyl translations of either the ordinary MacWilliams transform or the Rains shadow transform. This two-class reduction implies that the twists yield no additional independent coefficientwise positivity constraints under compatible projections. Nevertheless, the framework leads to refined MacWilliams and shadow identities that retain more Fourier information than ordinary Hamming weight enumerators. We employ these refined identities in linear programming, together with simplex mapping and shadow-coset counting, to exclude surviving candidate weight distributions. These techniques yield tighter bounds for binary and qutrit quantum codes, including nonexistence results for specific code parameters.

Information Theory.title: Finite-Length Empirical Comparison of Polar, PAC, and Invertible-Extractor Secrecy Codes over the Wiretap BSC
Information Theory.summary: We compare three secrecy-coding schemes for the degraded wiretap binary symmetric channel (BSC) in the finite-blocklength regime: (i) polar wiretap coset codes, (ii) PAC codes used as wiretap coset codes, and (iii) the invertible-extractor (IE) framework of Bellare--Tessaro. Our comparison is empirical and uses a common semantic-secrecy metric (distinguishing advantage). For polar coset codes, we compute Eve's polarized bit-channel capacities (via the Tal--Vardy construction) to obtain explicit finite-length upper bounds on mutual-information leakage, yielding strong secrecy bounds. For PAC coset codes, we prove that Eve's synthesized bit-channels are equivalent to those of polar codes (up to a permutation), so the same leakage bounds apply; we then convert these strong-secrecy bounds into semantic-secrecy guarantees for symmetric wiretap channels. For the IE scheme, we use the closed-form semantic-secrecy bounds already established. Finally, we report finite-length results that jointly characterize (a) semantic-secrecy guarantees against Eve and (b) frame-error-rate performance at Bob. Our simulations indicate that Polar and PAC codes exhibit comparable reliability performance under the considered finite-length settings, while PAC codes retain the same secrecy bounds as Polar codes. More broadly, our results highlight that non-universal designs of wiretap codes provide tighter secrecy guarantees than universal design based on invertible extractors.

Information Theory.title: Universal Short-Time Fourier Transform: Data-Adaptive Window-Length Selection for Time-Frequency Analysis
Information Theory.summary: The short-time Fourier transform (STFT) characterizes the local frequency content of time-varying signals by evaluating the discrete Fourier transform over a sliding analysis window. The STFT is governed by a fundamental resolution trade-off: a short window localizes rapid transients in time at the cost of frequency resolution, whereas a long window resolves closely spaced harmonics at the expense of temporal resolution. The Universal Short-Time Fourier Transform (U-STFT) resolves this trade-off sequentially by modeling the analysis window duration as a data-adaptive state variable that indexes the number of hops included in the current observation interval. At each frame, a bank of candidate window durations is scored using normalized order-three Rényi entropy to quantify joint time-frequency concentration. A window length trellis aggregates the resulting $\mathcal{O}(3^M)$ candidate window schedules with linear complexity per frame, guaranteeing a cumulative mix-loss regret bound of $\mathcal{O}((k+1)\log M)$ relative to any hindsight window schedule with $k$ resolution changes over $M$ frames. By linearity of the Fourier transform, posterior expectation across the candidate bank yields a single spectrum equivalent to an STFT evaluated with a data-adaptive effective window, while an envelope-normalized synthesis stream guarantees exact overlap-add reconstruction. Evaluations on synthetic and marine bioacoustic signals demonstrate adaptive resolution tracking, enhanced spectral concentration, and exact time-domain invertibility.

Information Theory.title: The Interference-Conjugate Transform: The Tightest Interference-Linear Surrogate for Power Control, Scheduling and Beamforming in Wireless Networks
Information Theory.summary: Closed-form fractional programming (FP), weighted MMSE (WMMSE), and the 2026 surrogate-enhanced methods SEFP and XMMSE all maximize the weighted sum rate by iteratively maximizing a surrogate linear in the interference power. We show that this family admits a unique best member: the interference-conjugate transform (ICT), which replaces each rate term $\log(1+a/b)$ by $\max_{κ\ge0}[Ω(κa)-κb]$, where $Ω$ is the closed-form partial convex conjugate of the rate in the interference variable and the optimal multiplier is the interference price $a/(b(a+b))$. We prove that, for any fixed price, $Ω(κ\,\cdot)$ is the pointwise largest own-signal function compatible with a valid interference-linear lower bound, and that tightness at an anchor forces the price. Hence all four benchmark surrogates, which share this price and differ only in their own-signal term, are dominated pointwise by ICT. At SINR $γ$, the benchmarks' own-signal curvature exceeds the true curvature by factors behaving as $γ/2$ (FP/WMMSE) and $(\logγ)/2$ (SEFP/XMMSE), against $1+1/(γ(γ+2))$ for ICT, and this ordering carries over to the certified ascent per iteration and the asymptotic linear convergence rate. ICT yields closed-form updates at the benchmarks' per-iteration cost for single-antenna power control, uplink joint scheduling and power control, and multi-cell MISO beamforming, and the first solver-free algorithm for sum-least-$q$th-percentile rate maximization, via a $K$-dimensional convex dual with closed-form gradient and Hessian and a certified duality gap. In uplink scheduling, ICT improves proportional-fairness utility over FP by +7.03 and over SEFP by +3.35 (60/60 drops) using 18.7 iterations per slot vs. 49.7 and 38.0; in MISO beamforming with $M=8$, it reaches 99.9% of its final value in a median of 9 iterations vs. 16 (XMMSE) and 1160 (FP/WMMSE).

Information Theory.title: Pooled Testing under Congestion: Operational Scaling Laws for Pool-Size Selection
Information Theory.summary:
Classical pooled-testing rules choose pool sizes to reduce the number of tests. In practice, however, samples arrive over time, pools take time to form, testing capacity is finite, and positive pools create bursts of follow-up work. These operational features can make the test-efficient pool size far from the delay-efficient one.
  We formulate pooled testing with stochastic arrivals and finite testing capacity as a queueing system, and derive exact performance representations and asymptotic scaling laws for fixed-batch Dorfman testing and a dynamic two-threshold policy. The analysis reveals three distinct design regimes. When test usage is the main concern, the classical Dorfman rule is recovered and the optimal pool size scales with the inverse square root of prevalence. When delay accumulated while the laboratory is busy testing another batch matters, positive pools create service-time variability that grows more rapidly with pool size than the mean retesting burden, and the optimal scale shifts to the inverse cube root of prevalence. When waiting to assemble a pool is itself costly, the optimal fixed pool size remains bounded even as prevalence becomes very small. Under severe capacity scarcity, congestion remains relevant at the classical Dorfman scale: the square-root law survives, but with a capacity-dependent constant.
  Dynamic pooling separates two operational decisions that fixed pool sizes conflate. A lower threshold determines when routine testing should begin, while an upper threshold limits pooling when backlog is high. The lower threshold follows the cube-root scale, whereas the upper threshold primarily acts as congestion control. The results show how prevalence, capacity, and delay jointly determine pooling decisions and explain why operationally optimal pools can be much smaller than those suggested by test-efficiency calculations alone.

Probability.title: Sharp Stability of Brenier Potentials and its Link to Poincaré Inequalities
Probability.summary: We prove a new functional inequality for uniformly log-concave measures, stronger than the Poincaré inequality. This new inequality bounds the variance of differences of convex functions and is motivated by the stability theory of optimal transport: for a fixed uniformly log-concave source measure, it provides a sharp stability bound for Brenier potentials with respect to variations of the target measure. Applying this inequality to Gaussian measures, we recover the fact that the Bures-Wasserstein distance between two positive semidefinite matrices is equivalent to the Frobenius distance between their square roots. Our proofs hinge upon linearization arguments for the Monge-Ampère equation governing the quadratic optimal transport problem.

Probability.title: Sharp approximations for the stationary measures of the open ASEP I: The shock region
Probability.summary: We investigate the role of asymmetry in the stationary measures of integrable probabilistic models with boundary interactions. This paper is the first in a series of three focusing on the open asymmetric simple exclusion process (ASEP). The stationary measure of open ASEP admits a two-layer Gibbs representation in which a correction term, which we call the Bryc polynomial, encodes the dependence on the asymmetry parameter. We give a probabilistic interpretation of the Bryc polynomial in terms of a birth-death-type Markov chain. As an application, we obtain sharp total variation approximations of the stationary measure by Bernoulli product measures in the high- and low-density phases of the shock region. These approximations yield further applications, including moderate deviation estimates for the stationary measure of open ASEP, as well as asymptotic results for the related model of open ASEP with light particles.

Probability.title: Sharp approximations for the stationary measures of the open ASEP II: The coexistence line
Probability.summary: We study the stationary measure of the open asymmetric simple exclusion process (ASEP) on the coexistence line. Our starting point is Bryc's two-layer Gibbs representation, together with the probabilistic interpretation, established in the first paper in this series, of the associated Bryc polynomial in terms of an inhomogeneous birth--death chain. Our main result gives a sharp approximation of the stationary measure. Specifically, we identify the shock location as an explicit observable of the particle configuration and obtain optimal bounds on the total variation distance between its law and the uniform measure on the lattice. Conditional on the shock location, we approximate, in total variation distance, the joint law of the occupation variables away from the shock by Bernoulli product measures with different densities to its left and right. These approximations lead to further applications, including fluctuation limits, moderate deviation bounds for the particle density, and limits for correlation functions under the stationary measure.

Probability.title: Approximate Counting for Mixed $p$-Spin Glasses in Weak External Fields via Cluster Expansion
Probability.summary: We give algorithms for approximating the partition function $Z_N$ of the Sherrington--Kirkpatrick (SK) model and finite mixed Ising $p$-spin models with $p\ge 3$. The algorithms apply at a fixed margin below the second-moment threshold $β_{\mathrm f}$ with homogeneous weak external fields $|h|\leqρ_0N^{-1/4}$, for fixed $ρ_0>0$. For any accuracy $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$ and failure parameter $δ\in(0,1)$, they approximate $\log Z_N$ to additive error $\varepsilon$. The number of exact operations is polynomial jointly in $N$, $\varepsilon^{-1}$, and $δ^{-1}$. The disorder variables have i.i.d symmetric distribution with unit variance. The failure probability is at most $δ$ plus an explicit disorder tail bound. This tail bound tends to zero under a finite fourth moment condition. Our approach builds on the cluster expansions of Aizenman--Lebowitz--Ruelle~\cite{ALR87} and Dey--Wu~\cites{DW23,DW26}. For higher-order mixtures, we retain hypergraphs using few vertices and evaluate their total weight deterministically through local spin averages and inclusion--exclusion. For SK, we impose cutoffs on the number of vertices of degree at least three and on the total number of edges. We estimate the retained sum using randomized color coding~\cite{AYZ95}. A lower tail control based on reverse hypercontractivity~\cite{MOS13} converts the mean-square approximation of the normalized partition function into logarithmic accuracy.
Probability.comment: 38 pages, 3 figures. AI-assisted and a companion lean formalization in https://github.com/qiangwu2/approximate-counting-spin-glasses

Probability.title: Shape exclusion for diffusion-limited aggregation
Probability.summary: For diffusion-limited aggregation on $\mathbb{Z}^d$ with $d \geq 2$, we rule out convergence in volume to bounded regions with boundary measure zero. Moreover, the number of boundary edges grows linearly. For Euclidean DLA in dimensions $2$, $3$, $8$, and $24$, we prove an analogous shape exclusion.

Probability.title: Linear-quadratic mean field games with Volterra dynamics
Probability.summary: We study a class of linear-quadratic mean field games in which the state of each agent follows a stochastic Volterra equation of convolution type. The resulting dynamics are non-Markovian and account for memory effects through a completely monotone kernel, while the mean field interaction enters both the drift and diffusion coefficients. Exploiting a Markovian lifting of the Volterra dynamics, which restores the Markov property at the price of moving to an infinite-dimensional state space, we characterize the optimal response of a representative agent for a given population mean through a system of Riccati equations in Banach spaces, thereby obtaining a feedback representation of the optimal control. We then study the consistency condition defining the mean field equilibrium, which reduces to a forward-backward fixed point equation for the equilibrium mean: we prove existence and uniqueness of the equilibrium on short horizons and, when the control does not act on the diffusion coefficient, on arbitrary horizons under a monotonicity condition on the interaction. Finally, we consider the corresponding finite-player game and establish a quantitative propagation of chaos result. As a consequence, the feedback control of any mean field equilibrium, when implemented by each agent on its own state, yields an $\varepsilon_N$-Nash equilibrium for the $N$-player game, with an explicit rate as the number of agents tends to infinity.

Probability.title: Sharp approximations for the stationary measures of the open ASEP III: The fan region
Probability.summary: We study the stationary measure of the open asymmetric simple exclusion process (ASEP) in the fan region with general boundary rates. The stationary height fluctuations in the maximal current phase and on its boundaries within the fan region are known to have limits involving Brownian excursions or meanders. We establish discrete counterparts of these limits: on intervals away from the boundaries, the joint law of the occupation variables is approximated in total variation distance by particle configurations constructed from lazy simple random walk excursions and meanders. In the high- and low-density phases of the fan region, we establish Bernoulli product approximations with errors that decay exponentially in the distance from the relevant boundary. Our methods combine refined combinatorial estimates for Motzkin paths and the matrix product ansatz in the totally asymmetric case with a Fourier-type decomposition (based on Askey--Wilson polynomials) of the change of measure for general asymmetry. In addition, in the maximal current phase and on its boundaries within the fan region, we prove moderate deviation estimates for particle counts on arbitrary sets of sites. These estimates rely on a covariance identity for an auxiliary path measure, through which total nonnegativity (of order two) of the matrices yields negative correlations.

Probability.title: Stationary measures of the open KPZ equation: A short proof
Probability.summary: In this note, we give a short probabilistic proof of the two-layer Brownian representation of the stationary measure of the open Kardar--Parisi--Zhang (KPZ) equation on a finite interval with arbitrary Neumann boundary parameters, conjectured by Barraquand and Le Doussal and recently established in full generality by Dunlap, Gu and Rosati. Our starting point is Bryc's two-layer Gibbs representation of the stationary measure of the open asymmetric simple exclusion process (ASEP) under Liggett's condition, together with our previously established probabilistic interpretation of the associated Bryc polynomials in terms of inhomogeneous birth--death Markov chains. Martingale estimates yield uniform asymptotics for these polynomials under weakly asymmetric scaling. Combined with known convergence results from open ASEP to open KPZ, these estimates recover the stationary height profile of the open KPZ equation as the first marginal of a reweighted pair of Brownian motions.

Probability.title: The packing and covering number of trees are local
Probability.summary: For a graph, its $r$-packing number is the size of the largest $r$-separated set and its $r$-covering number is the size of the smallest $r$-net. We show that the $r$-covering number and $r$-packing number are continuous in the fringe topology on locally finite trees. This recovers convergence results by Meir and Moon for e.g. uniform binary trees, uniform plane trees, uniform Polyá trees and random recursive trees, and proves new results for many other tree models, such as size-conditioned Bienaymé trees, simply generated trees, $m$-ary search trees, the minimum spanning tree of the complete graph and preferential attachment trees. Moreover, our formulation provides an intuitive interpretation of the limiting constant, that also provides an easy route for explicit computations in the case of size-conditioned Bienaymé trees. Our method relies on the definition of a canonical minimum $r$-net, and a relation between covering numbers and packing numbers due to Meir and Moon.

Probability.title: Global Hölder solvability for parabolic equations with interior Morrey data
Probability.summary: We prove global Hölder solvability for uniformly parabolic divergence-form equations with locally finite measure data under an interior Morrey growth condition and a capacity density condition on the spatial domain. The parabolic distance to the initial and lateral boundary is assumed bounded on the source support. For nonnegative data, we establish necessity results that demonstrate the sharpness of the growth and domain assumptions. We also derive estimates for divergence forcing, prove solvability for equations with lower-order terms, and obtain convergence rates in periodic homogenization.

Probability.title: Approaching Optimal Scaling of Queue Size for an Input-Queued Switch
Probability.summary: We study the scaling of the expected total queue length in an $n\times n$ input-queued switch. It has been conjectured that the optimal scaling is $O(n/(1-ρ))$, up to logarithmic factors, where $ρ$ is the system load. This conjecture has been established in the traditional heavy-traffic regime and in certain sub-regimes of the large-system regime. But it remains unresolved over a wide range of load scalings in the large-system regime. In this paper, we develop a family of scheduling policies parameterized by a positive integer $k\ge 2$. We show that under uniform traffic, our policy achieves an expected total queue length of $O\bigl({n\log\max\{n,1/(1-ρ)\}}\big/{(1-ρ)^{2^k/(2^k-1)}}\bigr)$, as long as $ρ\to 1$ in the large-system regime. As $k$ increases, the exponent $2^k/(2^k-1)$ approaches $1$, bringing our bound arbitrarily close to the conjectured scaling. The expected amortized scheduling cost of the policy is $O(n^3 k)$ per time slot. Our policy is of a batching type, with a novel recursive design that allows an arbitrary number of batching levels. This design principle may also be useful for other scheduling problems in which combinatorial constraints restrict which jobs can be served simultaneously.

Probability.title: Local Law and Eigenvector Delocalization for Random Lifts
Probability.summary: We establish a quantitative local law for random $N$-lifts of a fixed finite connected simple graph with minimum degree at least three. Away from the singular energies of the universal-cover spectrum, we obtain high-probability entrywise Green's function estimates down to spectral scales $(\log N)^C/N$, uniformly in the bulk and near regular edges and cusps. As a consequence, we establish complete eigenvector delocalization: every normalized eigenvector $u$ whose eigenvalue stays a small but fixed positive distance away from the singular energies satisfies $\|u\|_\infty\leq(\log N)^C/\sqrt{N}$ with high probability.

Probability.title: Phase-type representations for Strong Stability Preserving Runge--Kutta methods
Probability.summary: We develop a phase-type (PH) representation of strong stability preserving (SSP) Runge--Kutta (RK) methods. This representation provides a probabilistic interpretation of the RK coefficients and translates the chain order conditions into absorption-time moment identities. Using moment ratio bounds for PH distributions, we prove the conjectured optimal SSP coefficients for general implicit RK methods of orders two and three. The equality characterizations also establish uniqueness of the optimal RK tableaux.

Probability.title: Statistics on Yau's conjecture: Variance asymptotics
Probability.summary: We investigate the probabilistic counterpart of Yau's conjecture on the nodal volume of Laplace eigenfunctions on compact manifolds, by studying the high-frequency variance asymptotics of Riemannian random waves. Theorem A gives quantitative bounds on the fluctuations of their nodal volume for all regimes of spectral windows, including the monochromatic one, of spectral size 1. For every non-monochromatic window the variance has the exact order $1/N$, where $N$ is the dimension of the underlying space of eigenfunctions, on any compact manifold. In the monochromatic regime, on manifolds without conjugate points and in particular on negatively curved ones, we prove that the variance is $o(1/N)$: this improves the previous best bound, cf. Canzani and Hanin 2020, to its square divided by a logarithmic factor, and exhibits a form of Berry's cancellation, relative to the natural scale $1/N$, for monochromatic random waves on such chaotic manifolds. Our proofs rely on a local and global analysis combining the Kac-Rice formula, the Wiener--Itô chaos decomposition recently obtained by the authors Stecconi and Todino 2025, and a sharp analysis of the error in the pointwise Weyl law associated to an arbitrary spectral window (Theorem B). We also introduce a general machinery (Theorem C) that yields variance decay for the nodal volume of an arbitrary Gaussian field under broad geometric conditions, subject to correlation decay assumptions.

Probability.title: Displacement Moments and Path-Terminal Separation in Brownian Interpolant Sampling
Probability.summary: Brownian stochastic interpolants connect paired endpoint samples, yet their sampling error can depend on displacement moments even when neither endpoint has a first moment. For arbitrary Borel couplings, we prove early-stopped, target-to-output KL guarantees for standard Euler sampling from the true source. A fourth displacement moment gives an explicit $O(N^{-1})$ bound; a second moment suffices for fixed-law convergence as drift error vanishes. For one fixed coupling with no displacement moment above two, original bridge-path KL stays of order one, comparison-path KL is of order $1/\log N$, and terminal KL is at most $C/N^2$ on the same grid. The path decomposition identifies the information about the source discarded by Markov projection. When the original bridge is Markov, current-state Euler sampling instead has a second-moment $O((M_2+d)/N)$ bound; finite-entropy Schroedinger bridges for the probability Brownian reference are included. We also construct a current-state learner with expected output KL consistency from iid endpoint pairs. Numerical diagnostics illustrate the distinct errors. Conditional diffusion identities specify a restoration interface, while image controls find no iterative advantage over cheap probabilistic predictors. Uniform terminal rates for general second-moment couplings remain open.
Probability.comment: 56 pages, 4 figures; 8-page main text and complete appendices

Probability.title: A general-purpose multi-path stacked coupling for stochastic reaction networks
Probability.summary: Stochastic reaction networks are continuous-time Markov chain models for interacting populations, with applications in biochemistry, epidemiology, ecology, and related areas. Coupling multiple stochastic reaction networks effectively is a fundamental challenge in stochastic simulation. Existing variance-reducing coupling methods are typically designed for pairs of processes, though specialized multi-path constructions have been developed for particular applications.
