We show that the dimension of the space of symmetric differentials is bounded by a constant depending on the augmented irregularity, generalizing a result of Kobayashi. If we endow such a variety $X$ with a metric $ω$ whose Ricci curvature is non-negative, then we show that the holonomy of the regular locus is compact. If we assume that $X$ has canonical singularities, then we show that the general fiber of the Albanese map can be decomposed into a product of irreducible Calabi-Yau varieties, irreducible holomorphic symplectic varieties and hereditarily rationally connected varieties by the holonomy generalizing a structure theorem of Campana, Demailly and Peternell. To conclude, we show that the fundamental group of the regular locus of such varieties is virtually abelian.

Differential Geometry.title: Quantitative Rigidity of Ricci Nonnegative Manifolds via the Regular Green Constant
Differential Geometry.summary: For a Ricci non-negative non-parabolic manifold $(M^{n\ge3},g)$, assuming the minimal normalized Green function admits the asymptotic expansion $G=r^{2-n}+H_p+O_1(r)$, we prove the scaling invariant defect $H_pR^{n-2}$ controls the geometry of the geodesic ball quantitatively, $\frac{1}{R}d_{GH}(B_p(R),B_0^{\mathbb{R}^n}(R))\le C_n \left(H_p R^{n-2}\right)^{\frac{1}{88(n+1)(4n+1)}}$.

Differential Geometry.title: Unimodular random ideal hyperbolic polyhedra: geometric characteristics and random walks
Differential Geometry.summary:
We initiate a systematic study of unimodular random infinite ideal hyperbolic polyhedra in three-dimensional hyperbolic space, developing a geometric and probabilistic theory of their global behavior. At the heart of this theory is an intrinsic geometric characteristic, determined entirely by the dihedral angles surrounding a polyhedral face. We establish a unimodular Gauss-Bonnet identity and show that the expectation of this local geometric invariant completely determines the global conformal type: under suitable assumptions, a random ideal polyhedron is almost surely parabolic precisely when the expected characteristic vanishes, and hyperbolic precisely when it is negative. This provides a sharp geometric classification of random infinite ideal polyhedra.
  Building on the correspondence with ideal circle patterns, we further develop a refined Ring Lemma that yields quantitative geometric control without bounded-degree assumptions. Combining these geometric tools with unimodular probability methods, we identify the Poisson boundary of the face random walk and establish positive linear hyperbolic speed. Together, these results establish a local-to-global framework linking intrinsic dihedral geometry, conformal uniformization, and stochastic behavior at infinity for unimodular random infinite ideal hyperbolic polyhedra.
Differential Geometry.comment: We have revised the title, abstract, and introduction, and clarified several statements

Differential Geometry.title: Submanifolds with boundary in sub-Riemannian Heisenberg Groups
Differential Geometry.summary: We discuss the notion of submanifolds with boundary with intrinsic $C^1$ regularity in sub-Riemannian Heisenberg groups and we provide some examples. Eventually, we present a Stokes' Theorem for such submanifolds involving the integration of Rumin's differential forms in Heisenberg groups.
Differential Geometry.comment: 9 pages, 6 figures; to appear in the series "Actes et Congrès" of the "Société Mathématique de France" (Proceedings of the "Winter School in Geometric Measure Theory", held in Hangzhou, China, 2025)

Differential Geometry.title: Topology, Morse Index, and Area of Minimal Surfaces in Three-Manifolds
Differential Geometry.summary: We prove that, in every closed Riemannian three-manifold $(M^3,\bar g)$, there exists a constant $C=C(M,\bar g)>0$ such that every closed smoothly embedded minimal surface $Σ\subset M$ satisfies $b_1(Σ;\mathbb{Z}_2)\le C\bigl(\operatorname{Ind}(Σ)+\operatorname{Area}(Σ)\bigr)$, establishing Song's additive genus-index-area conjecture. For closed connected orientable two-sided minimal immersions, we prove the universal inequality $γ(Σ)\le8\operatorname{Ind}(Σ)$ in positive Ricci curvature and the estimate $γ(Σ)\le C(M,\bar g)\operatorname{Ind}(Σ)$ in positive scalar curvature. In the latter case, we also bound both area and total curvature by $C(M,\bar g)(1+\operatorname{Ind}(Σ))$.

Differential Geometry.title: Reconstruction of Heat Geometry from a Scalar Process
Differential Geometry.summary: A smooth scalar process with one fixed Gaussian covariance kernel determines any finite graded family of symmetric Hilbert tensors up to a common orthogonal isomorphism of their minimal supports. For two heat tensors, its law determines a closed positive-dimensional Riemannian manifold, a Euclidean bundle, its connection and potential, and the unknown heat time, up to isometry and gauge. The quadratic tensor recovers the scaled generator; the quartic tensor recovers the spatial norm and volume, which fix the time scale. For compact finite-dimensional RCD spaces, the same law determines the measured space with distance divided by the square root of the heat time.

Differential Geometry.title: Pontrjagin Classes of Locally Spherically Symmetric Projectively Affine Sprays
Differential Geometry.summary:
By Chern--Weil theory, rational Pontrjagin classes are represented by curvature forms. Sprays, which require no metric and include all Finsler and Riemannian geodesic sprays, provide a natural setting for the vanishing problem. Shen and Zhao proved that if a manifold admits a locally projectively flat spray, then all of its rational Pontrjagin classes vanish. We ask whether this rigidity persists for the wider class of projectively affine sprays.
  We prove that if a smooth manifold admits a locally spherically symmetric projectively affine spray, then all rational Pontrjagin classes vanish. Stronger, the Pontrjagin forms of the associated Berwald spray vanish identically as differential forms, a genuine geometric rigidity. Hence a manifold with nonzero rational Pontrjagin class cannot carry such a spray; in particular, it admits no Riemannian metric whose geodesic spray is locally spherically symmetric. We also construct non-Berwald, non-projectively-flat examples with identically vanishing Pontrjagin forms, showing the phenomenon is not a byproduct of projective flatness.

Differential Geometry.title: On $q$-convex hypersurfaces in Riemannian manifolds
Differential Geometry.summary: We prove that any closed, convex hypersurface in an $(n+1)$-dimensional Riemannian manifold with $\lceil \frac{n}{2} \rceil$-positive curvature operator is a rational homology sphere with finite fundamental group. The same conclusion holds for any $\lceil \frac{n}{2} \rceil$-convex hypersurface, provided that the mean curvature satisfies a sharp pinching condition. Both results follow from more general vanishing and estimation theorems for the Betti numbers of closed $q$-convex immersed hypersurfaces in $(n+1)$-dimensional Riemannian manifolds, under a lower bound on the average of the smallest $(n-p)$ eigenvalues of the curvature operator.

Differential Geometry.title: Cartan-Ambrose-Hicks theorems and dual geodesic symmetries on statistical manifolds
Differential Geometry.summary:
We establish Cartan-Ambrose-Hicks (CAH) theorems for statistical manifolds and characterize statistical symmetric spaces by dual geodesic symmetries. These theorems determine statistical structures up to local statisticmorphism by comparing the curvature of an alpha-connection and the skewness tensor using radial geodesics and parallel displacement of that connection. The Levi-Civita formulation characterizes local statisticmorphisms by comparing the radial Jacobi operators of Riemannian curvature and the skewness tensor using Levi-Civita parallel displacement. The same characterization holds with statistical curvature in place of Riemannian curvature. For Hessian manifolds, comparison of the skewness tensor alone is necessary and sufficient.
  For connected statistical manifolds, we prove the equivalence between the homogeneous definition of statistical symmetric spaces and the existence of global dual geodesic symmetries at every point. The CAH theorems give the necessary and sufficient conditions for maps constructed from exponential maps of dual connections to be local dual geodesic symmetries, preserving the metric and interchanging the dual connections. Such local symmetries exist at every point if and only if the Riemannian curvature and skewness tensors are Levi-Civita parallel. For Hessian manifolds, this condition is equivalent to the equality of the Hessian and dual Hessian curvature tensors.

Differential Geometry.title: The Costa surface with a free-boundary hole: an embedded exterior free-boundary minimal surface with three ends
Differential Geometry.summary: An exterior free-boundary minimal surface is a properly immersed minimal surface outside the unit ball whose compact boundary lies on the unit sphere and meets it orthogonally. By Mazet and Mendes, in $\mathbb{R}^3$ every such surface with one regular end is a catenoidal piece, and every stable one with parallel embedded regular ends is catenoidal. We construct connected embedded examples with three ends from the Costa surface $M$, placed so that its central saddle point is at the origin. For every sufficiently small $\varepsilon>0$ we perturb $\varepsilon^{-1}(M\setminus B_\varepsilon)$ into a properly embedded exterior free-boundary minimal surface of genus one with one boundary circle and three ends, two catenoidal and one planar. The construction is a small-hole perturbation. The only error of the initial surface is in the boundary condition. The symmetry group of the Costa surface removes all obstructions: at the hole it forbids the logarithmic and the tilting modes, and globally it kills the bounded Jacobi fields of the Costa surface, which is nondegenerate by Nayatani. In the conformal compactification the Jacobi operator is smooth also at the ends, so the linear analysis takes place on a compact torus with one small hole. The same construction applied to the Costa-Hoffman-Meeks surfaces gives such examples of every genus $k\geq1$, of index at least $2k+3$. We also report numerical experiments with two independent implementations of the Costa surface. They confirm the period condition, the symmetries, the boundary error, the index and nullity of the Jacobi operator and the absence of an equivariant kernel. They also compute the free-boundary correction near the hole, which gives pictures of the surfaces.
Differential Geometry.comment: 26 pages, 7 figures. Interactive 3D models: https://surfaces.igorkozyrev.com/#costa . The scripts for the numerical experiments are attached as ancillary files (anc/scripts)

Differential Geometry.title: Grassmannian Realizations of Classical Pseudo-Riemannian Symmetric Spaces
Differential Geometry.summary: We establish a unified fixed-point Grassmannian framework for the classical pseudo-Riemannian symmetric spaces from Berger's classification. For a classical group $G=\mathop{\mathrm{Aut}}(V,b)$, we identify $G$ with the open graph-like locus inside an ordinary or maximal-isotropic Grassmannian $\overline{G}$. Natural involutions of $\overline{G}$ are constructed via classical forms, compatible scalar structures, and subspace configurations. We explicitly describe the full fixed loci of these involutions in terms of classical Grassmannians. The corresponding graph-like fixed loci (or their signature strata) are identified, respectively, with the moduli spaces of classical forms, compatible scalar structures, and subspace configurations; these moduli spaces coincide with classical pseudo-Riemannian symmetric spaces. In summary, the 54 classical series are organized into four families: 10 group-type models, 7 classical-form Grassmannians, 20 scalar-structure Grassmannians, and 17 subspace-configuration Grassmannians.

Differential Geometry.title: Kähler landscapes for complex neural network descents and guarantees including a search and destroy of the Calabi-Yau manifold
Differential Geometry.summary: We study landscapes for complex-parameterized networks. Our approach is motivated with an information-theoretic manifold perspective of the parameter and via classical optimization guarantees although of complex geometric variety such as through Dolbeault asymptotics. The descent path admits a Kähler information metric under a cross-entropy via the Wirtinger Hessian on the log-likelihood potential. We restrict attention to a descent update rule with natural gradient descent via a differentiated loss scaled by the inverse metric, so the descent path remains in the holomorphic tangent bundle. We emphasize Calabi-Yau information manifolds which profane theoretical guarantees via an ill-curvature-conditioned, or lack thereof, landscape. We focus on Calabi-Yau metrics specifically in a non-compact setting with a global potential, so defined geometrically rather than invoking the topological requirements of the Calabi conjecture. In non-compact settings, we can write the metric determinant with respect to a background in terms of a function, pluriharmonic or real. Using Yau's Liouville theorem, we get a partial eigenvalue blow-up effect. In an empirical setting, a Ricci-flat metric will not form, but a blow-up can be a local condition and can hold empirically on open sets even partially in generalized Kähler cases due to lower bounds on the Ricci potential. Moreover, it has been discovered that negative curvature subverts the loss landscape, specifically sectional curvature, so we expand on this and draw interconnections to negative-definite Ricci curvature. Our arguments primarily exist via geometric modality, although we establish roots in deep learning theory such as through asymptotics at initialization and connections through failure modes of neural network guarantees under vanishing and negative Ricci curvature.

Differential Geometry.title: Examples of topological sphere $λ$-self-expander
Differential Geometry.summary: A $λ$-self-expander $F: M^n\to \mathbb{R}^{n+1}$ is the solution of the isoperimetric problem of weight $e^{\frac{|x|^2}{4}}$. In this paper, for sufficiently large $λ$, we construct an immersed non-embedded spherical $λ$-self-expander in $\mathbb{R}^{n+1}$ with the mean curvature $H>0$. Moreover, we obtain the explicit solution for $n=2$.
Differential Geometry.comment: 32 pages Version 2: Minor correction, fixed misspelling of Florian Johne's surname in the text and references

Differential Geometry.title: $O(3)$-symmetry of four-dimensional steady Ricci solitons
Differential Geometry.summary: We prove that a complete connected four-dimensional gradient steady Ricci soliton with positive curvature operator that is $κ$-noncollapsed at all scales admits an effective isometric $O(3)$ action preserving the potential function and having principal orbits diffeomorphic to $S^2$.

Differential Geometry.title: Silent Orbits and Cancellations in the Wave Trace
Differential Geometry.summary: This paper shows that the wave trace of a bounded and strictly convex planar domain may be arbitrarily smooth in a neighborhood of some point in the length spectrum. In other words, the Poisson relation, which asserts that the singular support of the wave trace is contained in the closure of $\pm$ the length spectrum, can almost be made into a strict inclusion. To do so, we construct large families of domains for which there exist multiple periodic billiard orbits having the same length but different Maslov indices. Using the microlocal Balian-Bloch-Zelditch parametrix for wave invariants developed in our previous paper, we solve a large system of equations for the boundary curvature jets, which leads to the required cancellations. We call such periodic orbits silent, since they are undetectable from the ostensibly audible wave trace. Such cancellations show that there are potential limitations in using the wave trace for inverse spectral problems and, more fundamentally, that the Laplace spectrum and the length spectrum are inherently different mathematical objects, at least insofar as the wave trace is concerned.
Differential Geometry.comment: 74 pages, 9 figures, to appear in Analysis & PDE

Differential Geometry.title: Non-collapsing of fibers in warped-product Poincare--Einstein manifolds
Differential Geometry.summary: Let $g=g_M+u^2h$ be a Poincaré--Einstein (asymptotically hyperbolic Einstein, AHE) metric of class $C^{3,α}$ on $N^{n+1}=M^q\times F^p$, where $(F,h)$ is compact with unit volume and $\Ric_h=λh$, $λ\le 0$. We show that if the conformal infinity $[γ]$ has positive Yamabe constant, then \[ u\;\ge\;Θ[γ]:=\sup_η\Big(\min_{\dN}ψ_η\Big)\Big(\frac{\min_{\dN} s_η}{n(n-1)}\Big)^{1/2}>0, \] the supremum being over representatives $η\in[γ]$ of positive scalar curvature and $ψ_η$ the boundary warping function of $η$. In particular $u\ge (\Y[γ]/n(n-1))^{1/2}\minψ_{η_Y}$ for the Yamabe metric $η_Y$. The estimate rests on a comparison principle between $\ln u$ and Lee's eigenfunction, which also applies to each factor of a multiply warped product, and pointwise yields $u\ge(\minψ_η)\,w_η$ when $\Y[γ]\ge 0$. We give an explicit bound in terms of the product representative of $[γ]$, show that the hypotheses force $q\ge 3$ and $\partial M$ connected, prove lower semicontinuity of $Θ$ in the boundary data, and discuss examples (hyperbolic Fermi coordinates, AdS--Schwarzschild) showing that the hypothesis $λ\le0$ cannot be removed.

Differential Geometry.title: Calabi-Yau Hyperbolicity
Differential Geometry.summary: The goal of this paper is to introduce a new notion of hyperbolicity for compact complex manifolds with trivial canonical bundle, called \textit{Calabi--Yau hyperbolicity}. We investigate its fundamental properties and establish a characterization in terms of the fundamental group. In particular, we show that no compact Kähler Calabi--Yau manifold is Calabi--Yau hyperbolic, highlighting the genuinely non-Kähler nature of this notion. We also investigate different techniques for constructing examples of such manifolds. Finally, we examine the relationship between Calabi--Yau hyperbolicity and Kobayashi hyperbolicity in the examples considered, highlighting obstructions to the latter in the Calabi--Yau setting.

Differential Geometry.title: Fisher Geometry of Circular Wrapped Normals: Completion and Curvature
Differential Geometry.summary: We determine the intrinsic Fisher geometry of the two-parameter circular wrapped normal family. Although its finite parameters form a cylinder, its metric completion is a disk: adjoining the uniform law extends the Fisher metric to a positive-definite real-analytic metric. The Gaussian curvature vanishes at the added point, is positive nearby, and tends to $-1/2$ as the underlying standard deviation tends to zero. We prove that the curvature has exactly one nonuniform zero radius and exactly one critical radius, the latter a nondegenerate positive maximum. Opposite points sufficiently close to uniformity are joined by a unique minimizing geodesic through the uniform law, so their intrinsic distance is not attained inside the nonuniform family. In contrast, identifying the means of real normal distributions modulo a period retains a complete hyperbolic cylinder with an infinitely distant cusp. Wrapping strictly decreases Fisher information in every nonzero tangent direction, while the information deficit and its fixed-order derivatives are exponentially small as the standard deviation tends to zero. The curvature theorem is proved by convergent series and explicit analytic remainder estimates; numerical figures serve only as illustrations.

Differential Geometry.title: A Converse to the Archimedes Sphere Theorem
Differential Geometry.summary: We show that a convex surface in Euclidean 3-space is a sphere if the area cut off from it by a slab of some fixed width depends only on the direction of the slab. This result generalizes theorems of Blaschke and Stamm, which assumed the slab-area property for every width. It holds also for any smooth closed embedded surface, and we obtain analogous results in higher dimensions. The proof is based on an averaging identity, which relates slab areas to the Newtonian potential of the surface, the electrostatic characterization of spheres by Mendez and Reichel, and analytic microlocal properties of the Radon transform, which are used to show that the slab-area property forces real analyticity, via theorems of Kashiwara and Boman.
Differential Geometry.comment: 17 pages; The main result extended to higher dimensions

Differential Geometry.title: Invariant Reduction for Partial Differential Equations. III: Poisson Brackets
Differential Geometry.summary: We establish that local Hamiltonian operators admitted by systems of partial differential equations (PDEs) induce Poisson bivectors on suitable finite-dimensional subsystems describing invariant solutions. This correspondence is governed by the mechanism of invariant reduction, which applies uniformly to point, contact, and higher symmetries. We show that the induced Poisson bivectors relate constants of invariant motion to symmetries of such subsystems. Applying the same reduction mechanism to invariant conservation laws, we further deduce that the corresponding Poisson brackets on the reduced systems agree, up to a global sign, with those of the original systems. The results are illustrated by two examples in which the induced Poisson brackets and constants of invariant motion yield integrability of the reduced systems. The construction is independent of the choice of an $\ell$-normal inclusion of a PDE system into jet spaces, with the corresponding odd cotangent covering being $\ell$-normal.

Differential Geometry.title: The Einstein-Hilbert functional and the Donaldson-Futaki invariant
Differential Geometry.summary: Given a Kaehler manifold polarised by a holomorphic ample line bundle, we consider the circle bundle associated to the polarisation with the induced transversal holomorphic structure. The space of contact structures compatible with this transversal structure is naturally identified with a bundle, of infinite rank, over the space of Kaehler metrics in the first Chern class of the polarisation. We show that the Einstein-Hilbert functional of the associated Tanaka-Webster connections is a functional on this bundle, whose critical points are constant scalar curvature Sasaki structures. In particular, when the group of automorphisms is discrete, these critical points correspond to constant scalar curvature Kaehler metrics in the first Chern class of the polarisation. We show that the Einstein--Hilbert functional satisfies some monotonicity properties along some one-parameter families of CR-contact structures that are naturally associated to test configurations, and that its limit on the central fibre of a test configuration is related to the Donaldson-Futaki invariant through an expansion in terms of an extra real parameter. As a by-product, we obtain an original proof that the existence of constant scalar curvature Kaehler metrics on a polarized manifold implies K-semistability. We also show that the limit of the Einstein-Hilbert functional on the central fibre coincides with the ratio of the equivariant index characters pole coefficients of the central fibre.
Differential Geometry.comment: 44 pages. Submitted version of the paper

Differential Geometry.title: Distance Functions, Curvature and Topology
Differential Geometry.summary: We discuss some properties of the distance functions on Riemannian manifolds and we relate their behavior to the geometry of the manifolds. This leads to alternative proofs of some "classical" theorems connecting curvature and topology.

Differential Geometry.title: A gluing construction of $Z$-extremal Kähler metrics and new examples of Bismut Hermitian-Einstein $3$-folds
Differential Geometry.summary: We present a gluing construction for a class of 6th order geometric non-linear PDE's on a Kähler manifold or orbifold, arising in the study of Bismut Hermitian Einstein complex $3$-folds, the supersymmetric supergravity models in physics, and in Dervan's Z-critical Kähler metrics. As applications, we obtain a desingularization theorem for orbifolds with crepant singularities admitting a solution of the PDE, as well as a blowing-up of points theorem for smooth complex $3$-folds admitting such solutions. These results yield new examples of regular Bismut Hermitian Einstein structures on the smooth manifolds $3(S^2\times S^4)\sharp 4(S^3\times S^3)$, $5(S^2\times S^4)\sharp 6(S^3\times S^3)$ and $S^1\times 9(S^2\times S^3)$, as well as infinite topological types of smooth compact $7$-dimensional manifolds $Y_7$, providing new solutions to the supersymmetric ${\rm AdS}_3 \times Y_7$ type IIB and ${\rm AdS}_2 \times T^2 \times Y^7$ type $D=11$ supergravity models.

Differential Geometry.title: An $L^2$ Ahlfors--Beurling inequality in every dimension
Differential Geometry.summary:
Let $Ω\subset\mathbb{R}^N$ ($N\geq2$) be measurable with $0<|Ω|<\infty$, and let $u_Ω$ be its logarithmic potential ($N=2$) or Newtonian potential ($N\geq3$), normalized so that $Δu_Ω=χ_Ω$. We prove the sharp inequality \[
  \int_Ω|\nabla u_Ω|^2\,\mathrm{d} x
  \leq\frac{1}{2Nω_{N-1}}
  \iint_{Ω\timesΩ}\frac{\mathrm{d} x\,\mathrm{d} y}{|x-y|^{N-2}}, \] where $ω_{N-1}=|\mathbb{S}^{N-1}|$, with equality if and only if $Ω$ is a ball up to a null set. In dimension two this settles the $L^2$ Ahlfors--Beurling conjecture of Fleeman and Khavinson. For $N\ge3$ it is equivalent to the scale-free bound that at most the fraction $(N-2)/(2N)$ of the total field energy lies inside $Ω$. We also obtain an explicit deficit identity, a sharp extension to bounded nonnegative densities, and consequences for torsional rigidity, Bergman analytic content, Brownian motion, and aggregation equations.

Differential Geometry.title: Sobolev Inequalities Relating Rough Riemannian Metrics to their Distance Functions
Differential Geometry.summary: In previous papers, the first named author and E. Bryden explored Sobolev like inequalities relating the norm of a Riemmanian metric $g_1$, in terms of a background Riemannian metric $g_0$, in order to estimate the distance function $d_{g_1}$. Although $|g_1|_{g_0}$ is not the gradient of the distance function $d_{g_1}$, it was shown that a Morrey and Sobolev inequalities hold in their appropriate domains. In this paper we see that these results can be extended to the case where $g_1$ is a Rough Riemannian metric, something roughly analogous to an $L^{\infty}$ metric. We show that the proof of the Morrey and Sobolev inequality go through, with appropriate adjustments, as well as convergence results. We also adapt previous examples from the literature to the rough Riemannian metric case which show the hypotheses from the main theorems are necessary.

Differential Geometry.title: Area and antipodal distance in convex hypersurfaces
Differential Geometry.summary: We establish a lower bound for the surface area of a closed, convex hypersurface in Euclidean space in terms of its displacement under continuous maps. As a result, a hypothesized lower bound for the volume of a Riemannian $n$-sphere, proved by Berger in dimension $n=2$ and disproved by Croke in dimensions $n \geq 3$, is valid for convex hypersurfaces in all dimensions. We also establish a sharp lower bound for the mean width of a convex hypersurface.
Differential Geometry.comment: 24 pages; 3 figures; added one figure, multiple references, and other background material; made other minor edits

Differential Geometry.title: The generalized Cartan-Hadamard conjecture
Differential Geometry.summary: We establish the generalized Cartan-Hadamard conjecture, including rigidity in the equality case. As a corollary, we obtain that isoperimetric regions are bounded. We prove the conjecture for Alexandrov spaces with two sided curvature bounds as well. A sharp Michael-Simon-type inequality for hypersurfaces in these spaces is also shown.

Differential Geometry.title: Stationary integral cycles asymptotic to a pair of oriented $n$-planes in $\mathbb{R}^{2n}$
Differential Geometry.summary: We prove a uniqueness theorem for stationary integral $n$-cycles asymptotic to a pair of n-planes satisfying the symmetric angle condition. For the general angle condition, we obtain a classification for complete smooth embedded oriented minimal submanifolds with vanishing first de Rham cohomology that are asymptotic to a pair of $n$-planes.

Differential Geometry.title: Interior curvature estimates for convex solutions of a prescribed curvature quotient equation
Differential Geometry.summary: In this note, we prove a priori interior curvature bounds for convex solutions to an elliptic Weingarten curvature quotient equation. The proof avoids integral estimates, doubling inequalities and compactness arguments. It relies on a concavity inequality for the equation operator and a novel choice of the auxiliary function to carry out an elementary maximum-principle argument. As an application, we obtain interior curvature bounds for convex solutions of a prescribed special Lagrangian curvature equation in dimensions three and four.
Differential Geometry.comment: v3: title changed; the introduction revised; multiple typos were fixed throughout the manuscript; to appear

Differential Geometry.title: A proof of the Cartan-Hadamard conjecture for small volumes under a Ricci curvature lower bound
Differential Geometry.summary: We prove the generalized Cartan-Hadamard conjecture, also known as the Aubin conjecture, in the small volume regime under a lower Ricci curvature bound, for any dimension $n\geq 2$. More precisely, we show that if $(M^n,g)$ is a Cartan-Hadamard manifold satisfying $\mathrm{Sec}_g\leq\bar k\leq 0$ and $\mathrm{Ric}_g\geq (n-1)\underline k$, then its isoperimetric profile is at least that of the model space of curvature $\bar k$ for small enough volumes. We also reduce the proof of the generalized Cartan-Hadamard conjecture to establishing rigidity in the equality case.
Differential Geometry.comment: We weakened Assumption 1 and added explanations for a few inequalities and steps

Differential Geometry.title: Finite-energy solutions to Einstein-scalar field Lichnerowicz equations on complete Riemannian manifolds
Differential Geometry.summary: We consider the singular elliptic problem of the form \[ -Δu + V(x)u = \mathcal{B}(x)|u|^{2^*-2}u + \frac{\mathcal{A}(x)}{|u|^{2^*}u}, \qquad u\in H^1(M), \] where the coefficients are allowed to have low regularity. Under natural spectral assumptions on $-Δ+V$, geometric assumptions on the manifold $M$ ensuring the Sobolev embedding $H^1(M)\hookrightarrow L^{2^*}(M)$, and a suitable global integrability/smallness condition involving $\mathcal{A}$, $\mathcal{B}$, and a function $ψ\in H^1(M)$, we prove the existence of a nonnegative finite-energy supersolution. If, in addition, the Ricci curvature is nonnegative and $\mathcal{B}\ge 0$, we obtain a positive finite-energy solution. The proof relies on a family of $\varepsilon$-regularized problems, mountain pass arguments, and a limiting procedure in which Harnack's inequality plays a crucial role in handling the singular term on noncompact manifolds. We also prove a nonexistence result showing that the global integrability condition on $\mathcal{A}$ is, in a precise sense, necessary for the existence of nonnegative supersolutions.

Geometric Topology.title: On Khovanov local equivalence groups
Geometric Topology.summary: Inspired by work in Seiberg--Witten and Heegaard Floer homology, Dunfield, Schütz, and the author constructed an abelian "local equivalence group" built from pairs of chain complexes, and a homomorphism from the smooth concordance group to this group that uses the odd Khovanov complex and the Bar-Natan deformation of the even Khovanov complex. Lewark independently gave a related local equivalence group and concordance invariant, using only the Bar-Natan deformation. In this paper, we construct $(\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z})^\infty$ subgroups of Lewark's local equivalence group and the kernel of the map from our local equivalence group to Lewark's, as well as $\mathbb{Z}^\infty$ direct summands of Lewark's group and this kernel, invisible to the $s$-invariants. The construction gives at least six $\mathbb{Z}$-valued concordance homomorphisms linearly independent from $s$, $τ$, and Dai--Hom--Stoffregen--Truong's invariants.
Geometric Topology.comment: 40 pages. Research largely carried out by Anthropic's Claude models; paper written by the author. See methodology section and AI disclosure

Geometric Topology.title: Systolic pants decompositions with polynomial growth
Geometric Topology.summary: We investigate improved bounds on the kissing number of a hyperbolic surface under the assumption that the systole set contains pants decompositions with volume growth constraints. Namely, when the dual graph of the pants decomposition has polynomial volume growth, we obtain a power-savings improvement for the upper bound on the kissing number in terms of systolic length. We also construct super-exponentially many (in $g$) pants decompositions with exponential volume growth for which our techniques still imply stronger upper bounds for kissing numbers. The proofs use the technology of ``stem systems'' and ``tulips'' developed by the first and second author to study $1$-systems of curves.

Geometric Topology.title: Counting Saddle Connections on Hyperelliptic Translation Surfaces with a Slit
Geometric Topology.summary: We consider saddle connections on a translation surface in a hyperelliptic connected component of a stratum that do not intersect the interior of a distinguished saddle connection. For this restricted set of saddle connections, we show that it satisfies an $L (\log L)^{d-2}$ growth rate, where $d$ is the complex dimension of the hyperelliptic stratum. The upper bound holds for all translation surfaces in the hyperelliptic stratum while the lower bound holds for almost every surface in the hyperelliptic stratum. The proof of the lower bound uses horocycle renormalization.
Geometric Topology.comment: Revisions following referee report. 76 pages, 7 figures

Geometric Topology.title: Localization of weighted Goldman volume on $\mathrm{SL}(3,\R)$-Hitchin Component
Geometric Topology.summary: We compute Goldman volume on the moduli space of convex real projective structures on a closed oriented surface of genus at least two, with exponential weight defined by the shifted Blaschke area. For every positive parameter, the integral converges and is a finite sum of inverse powers of that parameter. Its coefficients are intersection numbers involving the bundle of regular cubic differentials on the moduli stack of stable curves. The proof establishes absolute convergence and vanishing signed boundary integrals of the transgression under simultaneous plumbing degeneration. The pushforward of Goldman measure by the shifted Blaschke area therefore has a polynomial density on $[0,\infty)$, and its sublevel volumes are polynomial in the threshold.
Geometric Topology.comment: Preliminary version; all comments are welcome

Geometric Topology.title: Three-manifolds that do not admit veering triangulations
Geometric Topology.summary: We show that if a three-manifold $M$ admits a veering triangulation, then the dual spine of every essential triangulation of $M$ can be smoothed to a branched surface. We use this criterion to identify a large collection of cusped hyperbolic three-manifolds that do not admit veering triangulations. We then use the same criterion to construct the first infinite family of cusped hyperbolic three-manifolds without veering triangulations.

Geometric Topology.title: Unimodular random ideal hyperbolic polyhedra: geometric characteristics and random walks
Geometric Topology.summary:
We initiate a systematic study of unimodular random infinite ideal hyperbolic polyhedra in three-dimensional hyperbolic space, developing a geometric and probabilistic theory of their global behavior. At the heart of this theory is an intrinsic geometric characteristic, determined entirely by the dihedral angles surrounding a polyhedral face. We establish a unimodular Gauss-Bonnet identity and show that the expectation of this local geometric invariant completely determines the global conformal type: under suitable assumptions, a random ideal polyhedron is almost surely parabolic precisely when the expected characteristic vanishes, and hyperbolic precisely when it is negative. This provides a sharp geometric classification of random infinite ideal polyhedra.
  Building on the correspondence with ideal circle patterns, we further develop a refined Ring Lemma that yields quantitative geometric control without bounded-degree assumptions. Combining these geometric tools with unimodular probability methods, we identify the Poisson boundary of the face random walk and establish positive linear hyperbolic speed. Together, these results establish a local-to-global framework linking intrinsic dihedral geometry, conformal uniformization, and stochastic behavior at infinity for unimodular random infinite ideal hyperbolic polyhedra.
Geometric Topology.comment: We have revised the title, abstract, and introduction, and clarified several statements

Geometric Topology.title: Dehn quandles of surfaces and their bounded cohomology
Geometric Topology.summary: We introduce new families of quandles associated with closed orientable surfaces that can distinguish surfaces up to homeomorphism. These quandles generalize the classical Dehn quandle and are defined, respectively, on isotopy classes of unoriented essential closed curves and on integral weighted multicurves. We establish their fundamental algebraic properties and construct a natural quandle covering relating the two families. We further investigate their large-scale geometry and prove that they are unbounded with respect to the quandle metric. We determine their second bounded quandle cohomology and show that its dimension equals the cardinality of the continuum. We also establish a quandle-theoretic analogue of the Gromov Mapping Theorem, showing that the natural projection from an abelian quandle extension onto its base quandle induces an injection on bounded quandle cohomology in every degree. Finally, motivated by recent developments in quandle algebras, we study idempotents in the integral quandle algebras associated with the classical Dehn quandle. In particular, we prove that the integral quandle algebra of the Dehn quandle of the torus admits no non-trivial idempotents.

Geometric Topology.title: Essential-Surface Complexes of Knot Exteriors: Image, Kernel, and Reconstruction
Geometric Topology.summary: This is an expository article. The curve complex of a surface is deliberately forgetful, yet in most cases its automorphism group recovers the mapping class group. We explain what happens when the same question is asked for the essential-surface complex $\mathcal{ES}(E)$ of a knot exterior $E=E(K)$, equivalently Schultens's initial surface complex $\mathcal{S}_0(E)$. The discussion is organized around three questions: which combinatorial symmetries are geometric (the image), which homeomorphisms are invisible (the kernel), and how much of $E$ can be read off from the complex (reconstruction). The basic objects are first drawn in classical examples, and the general framework is introduced only afterwards. We collect the elementary structural facts that organize the subject -- the flag property, the layering by boundary slope, finite dimension, unbounded dimension for iterated cables, and Kakimizu's complexes as full subcomplexes -- and compare with handlebodies and connected sums of $S^2\times S^1$, where image and kernel are known completely. Along the way we record two short consequences that we have not found stated in this form: for a slope-separated knot every orientation-preserving mapping class acts trivially, and the image is $\mathbb{Z}/2$ exactly when the knot is amphichiral and a nonzero boundary slope occurs; and for a connected sum of nonfibered prime knots the decomposing-annulus twist translates Banks's winding coordinate. A table separates what is classical from what is recorded here. The article closes with a three-task formulation of the rigidity problem, a list of problems with their current status, a worked two-bridge recipe, and a guide to further reading.
Geometric Topology.comment: 41 pages, 17 figures, 1 table. v3: rewritten as an expository article; added a status table of classical vs. new results, a comparison with handlebodies and #S^2xS^1, a problem list with status, and further references; corrected the two-bridge continued-fraction convention

Geometric Topology.title: On the $d$-invariants of Brieskorn spheres and $\mathrm{GL}(2,\mathbb{Z})$
Geometric Topology.summary: We study the $d$-invariant from Heegaard Floer homology for Brieskorn spheres $Σ(p,q,r)$. Using surgeries on two singular fibers, we establish new relations of the $d$-invariants among various Brieskorn spheres. For $p=2$, we show that $d$ never vanishes if $q/r$ lies in certain intervals on the rational line. Altogether, we completely classify Brieskorn spheres $Σ(2,q,r)$ with $d=0$. The zero set is expressed using submonoids of $\mathrm{GL}(2,\mathbb{Z})$ and the Stern--Brocot tree. As an application, we prove that most Brieskorn spheres $Σ(2,q,r)$ do not bound a rational homology $4$-ball.

Geometric Topology.title: Quasi-ribbon but non-ribbon surface-link of trivial components
Geometric Topology.summary: An operation on a surface-link preserving the surface-knot components called a quasi-equivalence is introduced, which induces an equivalence relation on the surface-links. A quasi-ribbon surface-link is a surface-link quasi-equivalent to a ribbon surface-link. It is shown that a surface-link of trivial components is a quasi-ribbon surface link if it has only at most one non-spherical component, whereas there exist examples that are not quasi-ribbon surface-links of trivial components when it has at least two aspherical components. For every closed disconnected, orientable surface, a quasi-ribbon but non-ribbon surface-link of trivial components is constructed. This construction is done by applying a positive solution to Cochran's conjecture, meaning that the sphere-knot obtained from the anti-parallel sphere-link of every non-ribbon sphere-knot by surgery along an s-nontrivial or s-trivial fusion 1-handle is a non-ribbon or trivial sphere-knot, respectively.
Geometric Topology.comment: Minor revisions made in conjunction with the revision of a closely related paper

Geometric Topology.title: Fusion of boundary surface-link and ribbonness
Geometric Topology.summary: A boundary surface-link of at least two components in the 4-sphere is proved to be a ribbon surface-link if the surface-link obtained from it by surgery along a local S-nontrivial fusion 1-handle system is a ribbon surface-link. This paper presents a detailed proof of this result, including an appendix, although a similar result was previously published with a portion of the proof missing. The result is stated using the concept of a \lq\lq local fusion 1-handle\rq\rq, which is more precise than the earlier concept of a \lq\lq pairwise fusion 1-handle\rq\rq.
Geometric Topology.comment: This is a detailed version of the previous paper

Geometric Topology.title: Loop Space Models and Integral Homology of Connected Quandles
Geometric Topology.summary: We construct a marked integral delooping of a connected quandle's covering monoid, realizing its rack space as a homotopy fiber. For finite connected quandles at primes $p$ not dividing a point-stabilizer order, we determine the local $A_\infty$ type and the ordinary rack cohomology shuffle algebra over fields of characteristic $p$. We compute integral quandle homology in all positive degrees for finite connected regular cyclic Alexander quandles and the tetrahedral quandle. At such primes dividing the quandle order, rack-space homotopy groups have exponentially many cyclic direct summands of fixed $p$-power order in each sufficiently large degree.

Geometric Topology.title: Smallest quotients and profinite rigidity of irreducible spherical type Artin groups
Geometric Topology.summary: We prove that irreducible spherical type Artin groups are profinitely rigid within the class of all spherical type Artin groups. As part of the proof, building on ideas of Kolay for the $n$-strand braid group, we compute the smallest non-abelian quotient of every spherical type Artin group. In particular, given an irreducible spherical type Artin group, its smallest non-abelian quotient is always that of the corresponding Coxeter group, except for dihedral Artin groups of weight divisible by $4$, which all have $\mathfrak S_3$ as a non-abelian quotient. Parts of the proof also rely on the computation of the cohomological dimension of the profinite completion of certain Artin groups.

Geometric Topology.title: A short proof of the universality of the fundamental shadow links
Geometric Topology.summary: We give a constructive three-dimensional proof of Costantino and Thurston's universality theorem for fundamental shadow links. More precisely, every compact connected oriented three-manifold with empty or toroidal boundary can be obtained by integral Dehn filling along a subset of the boundary components of a fundamental shadow link exterior.

Optimization and Control.title: MuonGS: Pretraining LLMs with Relaxed Weight-Norm Control
Optimization and Control.summary:
Weight decay and explicit weight-norm constraints improve optimizer performance in language model pretraining, yet a unified understanding of why such control helps and how much is needed remains incomplete. We analyze norm control in Muon over the entire training trajectory using the \emph{accumulated effective learning rate}, $C_T=\sum_{t<T}η_t/\|W_t\|_F$, where $η_t$ is the nominal learning rate and $η_t/\|W_t\|_F$ is the effective learning rate relative to the weight norm. For bounded update directions, accumulation over any training interval bounds relative weight displacement. We show that vanilla Muon can accumulate only logarithmically, potentially limiting exploration and helping explain its slower empirical progress, whereas MuonW and MuonH guarantee at least linear accumulation under the stated conditions. Going beyond bounded-norm control, we show that sufficiently slow norm growth guarantees faster accumulation than the logarithmic worst case, opening up less restrictive optimizer designs.
  Based on this insight, we propose MuonGS, which uses Gram--Schmidt (GS) projection to remove the radial component of each Muon update without fixing the weight norm. With bounded update directions and a constant nominal learning rate, we prove that the weight norm grows at most proportionally to $\sqrt{t}$ after $t$ steps. Consequently, MuonGS guarantees $C_T=Ω(\sqrt{T})$, with accumulation sustained even in later training. Further, for smooth scale-invariant objectives we establish its $O(T^{-1/2})$ stationarity guarantee. In pretraining experiments with 160M- and 400M-parameter dense models as well as a 135M active- and 1B total- parameter MoE model, MuonGS achieves lower validation perplexity than MuonH at long training horizons. In particular, for the dense model it achieves an estimated token-equivalent speedup up to about $15\%$ at matched validation loss to MuonH.

Optimization and Control.title: Lower- and upper-$C^2$ integrands: a structured class of functions for stochastic nonconvex optimization
Optimization and Control.summary: We study nonconvex stochastic functions that admit a structured second-order representation, a generalization of lower- and upper-$C^2$ functions to normal integrands. Similarly to the deterministic case, lower-$C^2$ normal integrands are defined as the pointwise maxima over a compact random index set of functions that are twice-continuously differentiable in the decision variable with an integrable bounded Hessian. Our main result is a local value function characterization of this class of functions, namely, that they satisfy a local sufficient ascent property almost surely. Equivalently, they differ from a convex normal integrand by a random quadratic. The upper-$C^2$ theory follows by a change of sign, and delivers the corresponding lower envelopes, the form in which these integrands appear as second-stage value functions of stochastic programs with compact recourse. We also show that for this class integrability of the function values, of the local Lipschitz moduli, and of the minimum-norm Clarke subgradients are equivalent. We then study smooth integrands, finite lower envelopes, difference-of-convex integrands, Moreau and forward--backward envelopes, compositions with a smooth map, monotone convex compositions, and compact-recourse stochastic programs within these classes of nonconvex stochastic functions. As an application, we show that the optimistic loss of partial-label regression and the variational formulation of the conditional value-at-risk fit within this framework.

Optimization and Control.title: Linear-quadratic mean field games with Volterra dynamics
Optimization and Control.summary: We study a class of linear-quadratic mean field games in which the state of each agent follows a stochastic Volterra equation of convolution type. The resulting dynamics are non-Markovian and account for memory effects through a completely monotone kernel, while the mean field interaction enters both the drift and diffusion coefficients. Exploiting a Markovian lifting of the Volterra dynamics, which restores the Markov property at the price of moving to an infinite-dimensional state space, we characterize the optimal response of a representative agent for a given population mean through a system of Riccati equations in Banach spaces, thereby obtaining a feedback representation of the optimal control. We then study the consistency condition defining the mean field equilibrium, which reduces to a forward-backward fixed point equation for the equilibrium mean: we prove existence and uniqueness of the equilibrium on short horizons and, when the control does not act on the diffusion coefficient, on arbitrary horizons under a monotonicity condition on the interaction. Finally, we consider the corresponding finite-player game and establish a quantitative propagation of chaos result. As a consequence, the feedback control of any mean field equilibrium, when implemented by each agent on its own state, yields an $\varepsilon_N$-Nash equilibrium for the $N$-player game, with an explicit rate as the number of agents tends to infinity.

Optimization and Control.title: GNBG-C: A Unified and Configurable Benchmark Generator for Constrained Continuous Optimization
Optimization and Control.summary: Many real-world optimization tasks are governed not only by what should be optimized, but also by what is allowed: a solution must first satisfy physical, operational, safety, budgetary, or structural requirements before its objective value becomes meaningful. Yet benchmark design for constrained continuous optimization often treats these restrictions as fixed properties of predefined test instances. Existing generators and benchmark suites provide essential foundations for reproducible comparison, but they either focus primarily on configurable objective landscapes or expose constraint properties within limited, predefined regimes, making it difficult to ask targeted questions about constraint-induced difficulty: whether an optimizer struggles because feasible regions are small, boundaries are restrictive, variables are tightly coupled, or constraint information is poorly scaled. We introduce GNBG-C, a Generalized Numerical Benchmark Generator for Constrained Continuous Optimization. The central idea is to treat the feasible region itself as a configurable object rather than as an inseparable attachment to a fixed test function. By generating controlled constraint regimes around the known GNBG global minimizer, the generator enables systematic studies in which feasibility pressure can be varied while preserving that point as a global minimizer of the constrained problem. This allows researchers to examine how optimizers discover feasibility, handle constraint pressure, and improve objective quality under diverse and controllable feasibility conditions. GNBG-C therefore provides a flexible and auditable framework for probing the strengths and weaknesses of constrained continuous optimizers under targeted forms of feasibility-side difficulty.

Optimization and Control.title: No closed-form formula for Stiefel geodesics
Optimization and Control.summary: We use differential Galois theory to prove that given two arbitrary points $X$ and $Y$ on the Stiefel manifold, there is no closed-form analytic expression for the Riemannian logarithm $\log_X Y$, the geodesic between $X$ and $Y$, or the geodesic distance between $X$ and $Y$. In other words, these cannot be expressed in terms of elementary functions of the coordinates of $X$ and $Y$; in fact, our result goes further --- even if we allow for repeated integrals of elementary functions, there is still no such expression.

Optimization and Control.title: GPU-accelerated wind farm layout search with a distilled endogenous wake model (EndoWake)
Optimization and Control.summary: We build on EndoWake, an endogenous wake model that links the wind speed at every grid cell to its upwind neighbors by linear constraints, so that wake field, siting decisions and project constraints share one mixed-integer model. Its four parameters are calibrated once on the single wake of a Reynolds-averaged Navier-Stokes (RANS) simulation, and a graphics processing unit (GPU) scores over a million layouts per second per wind direction. At Lillgrund, we compare searches guided by EndoWake and by PyWake under a RANS judge that no search calls: the fidelity of a wake model is not the quality of the layouts optimized under it. Two diagnostics separate a quadrature error between the sampled wind directions from a surrogate bias localized off each wake edge, not reported before to our knowledge; at random directions, five paired starts detect no difference between the pipelines. The main result puts the speed to use: EndoWake ranks the moves of a local search on the GPU, and PyWake confirms every accepted move. On twenty unseen starts, with one GPU and thirty CPU processes, screen-and-confirm reaches similar mean gains to a search on PyWake alone, 7.9 times faster at one wind speed and 14.9 times faster on the annual energy (3.0 and 4.7 with a proof of local optimality charged to the timed search); on a second site it keeps its speed, and its local optima fall slightly short of those of PyWake alone. Code and data are deposited on Zenodo.
Optimization and Control.comment: v2, revised (October 2026): formal terms replace the metaphors of v1; new comparisons with TOPFARM and on a second site (Horns Rev 1); sensitivity to the length of the candidate list; speedups with and without the final certificate. The replication package (doi:10.5281/zenodo.22017446) now includes the local searches, the sector quadrature and the fast evaluator. 39 pages, 5 figures

Optimization and Control.title: Constructing Data-Driven Budgeted Uncertainty Sets for Robust Optimization
Optimization and Control.summary: In robust optimization, budgeted uncertainty sets offer a popular trade-off between modeling flexibility and computational tractability. Data that is observed in practice is often discrete in nature, which creates the need for tools to construct budgeted uncertainty sets based on observed data. This paper presents a principled approach for this purpose, which ensures that any solution found through the robust problem with respect to the constructed budgeted uncertainty set offers an approximation guarantee with respect to the optimal value of the problem with discrete data. Our approach is purely based on the geometry of data and can be applied to any nominal optimization problem. We discuss the problem of evaluating budgeted uncertainty sets, and how to construct them using exact and heuristic methods. In computational experiments, we show that it is possible to construct sets with little computation time that offer guarantees that are close to optimality.

Optimization and Control.title: StablePCA: Distributionally Robust Learning of Shared Representations from Multi-Source Data
Optimization and Control.summary: When synthesizing multi-source high-dimensional data, a key objective is to extract low-dimensional representations that effectively approximate the original features across different sources. Such representations facilitate the discovery of transferable structures and help mitigate systematic biases such as batch effects. We introduce Stable Principal Component Analysis (StablePCA), a distributionally robust framework for constructing stable latent representations by maximizing the worst-case explained variance over multiple sources. A primary challenge in extending classical PCA to the multi-source setting lies in the nonconvex rank constraint, which renders the StablePCA formulation a nonconvex optimization problem. To overcome this challenge, we conduct a convex relaxation of StablePCA and develop an efficient Mirror-Prox algorithm to solve the relaxed problem, with global convergence guarantees. Since the relaxed problem generally differs from the original formulation, we further introduce a data-dependent certificate to assess how well the algorithm solves the original nonconvex problem and establish the condition under which the relaxation is tight. Finally, we explore alternative distributionally robust formulations of multi-source PCA based on different loss functions.
Optimization and Control.comment: 72 pages. Revised presentation, proofs, and numerical illustrations

Optimization and Control.title: Observability of wave equations with time- and space-dependent potentials: a counterexample under GCC and a positive criterion on the disk
Optimization and Control.summary:
We show that the geometric control condition (GCC) does not guarantee internal observability for a wave equation with a smooth time-dependent potential. On a bounded connected domain with analytic boundary, we construct a nonempty open observation set such that the pair satisfies GCC and the free Dirichlet wave is observable. For this same domain and observation set, we construct a smooth $2π$-periodic potential for which there exists a nonzero smooth Dirichlet wave that vanishes on the observed cylinder for all time. The wave is the unique mild solution in the space $X_Ω=L^2(Ω)\times H^{-1}(Ω)$ on every finite time interval, so no finite observation horizon yields an observability inequality for this fixed potential.
  The construction starts from a real-valued local counterexample to unique continuation across a noncharacteristic hyperplane. This local statement is of independent interest, since earlier constructions for the wave operator use complex-valued waves and potentials. The global counterexample is then obtained by joining flat oscillatory solutions along the edges of a polygonal observation set, repairing their sum at the vertices without changing its zero set, and using a spatial transition to a common time-independent pair near the boundary. The planar construction also yields counterexamples in every space dimension $n\ge3$.
  For comparison, and to identify a geometry that supplies both propagation and continuation, we show on the unit disk that an observation region containing a central disk and a neighborhood of an embedded cross-cut yields observability for every weak wave at sufficiently large observation time, with constants uniform over bounded measurable potentials. The proof uses a cut, logarithmic polar coordinates, and a Carleman weight whose favorable flux is confined to the observed artificial boundary.

Optimization and Control.title: DREAM: Delay-Resistant Acceleration with Momentum
Optimization and Control.summary: With exact, delay-free gradients, Nesterov's accelerated gradient (NAG) achieves optimal $\sqrtκ$ dependence for $L$-smooth, $μ$-strongly convex objectives, where $κ=L/μ$; heavy-ball (HB) achieves the same scaling on strongly convex quadratics. In asynchronous and distributed settings, gradients can be inexact, with delays varying across workers and iterations. We isolate staleness using a fixed delay $τ\ge1$, replacing $\nabla f(y_k)$ with $\nabla f(y_{k-τ})$ at iteration $k$. Arjevani, Shamir, and Srebro establish a worst-case lower bound of $Ω(τ\sqrtκ\log(1/\varepsilon))$ iterations to reach objective error at most $\varepsilon$ as $\varepsilon\to0$. We show that for any fixed positive delay, neither NAG nor HB retains $\sqrtκ$-acceleration on strongly convex quadratics when updating every iteration, for any stable constant step size and positive momentum. We introduce delay-resistant accelerated momentum (DREAM), which decouples gradient-query extrapolation from momentum and uses explicit delay-dependent parameters. DREAM attains a linear convergence rate $1-Θ(1/(τ\sqrtκ))$ for all smooth strongly convex objectives as $κ\to\infty$, yielding complexity matching the delayed first-order lower bound up to logarithmic factors. Our proof combines characteristic-polynomial stability analysis on quadratics with an analytic Zames--Falb integral quadratic constraint certificate. We extend DREAM to smooth convex objectives, obtaining near-optimal iteration complexity up to logarithmic factors for sufficiently small target accuracy. Experiments on strongly convex quadratics and regularized logistic regression corroborate DREAM's accelerated condition-number dependence under delay, unlike NAG and HB, and suggest this scaling persists when parameters use a conservative bound on the true delay.

Optimization and Control.title: SD-DPC: Sparse Dictionary Differentiable Predictive Control
Optimization and Control.summary: We present sparse dictionary differentiable predictive control (SD-DPC), a framework for learning sparse, interpretable feedback policies for nonlinear systems from data. A prediction model is first identified by rollout-based sparse identification of nonlinear dynamics (SINDy), building on gradient-based and multistep formulations. The policy is then parameterized as a sparse combination of dictionary functions and trained by differentiating a constrained finite-horizon predictive-control objective through this model, so that its terms are selected by closed-loop performance rather than by imitating a previously trained controller. The result is an explicit feedback law with only a handful of terms. Across three benchmark control problems, SD-DPC satisfies the constraints in almost all test scenarios, outperforms a policy distilled onto the same terms by up to an order of magnitude, and requires orders of magnitude less memory and online computation than an optimization benchmark, while admitting explicit sensitivity bounds.
Optimization and Control.comment: Revised the experimental setup details in Table I and the evaluation reporting, corrected the numerical results in Table II, and clarified the training and validation protocols. The main conclusions are unchanged

Optimization and Control.title: Measuring Sudoku Difficulty: Formulation, Propagation and Uniqueness Certification
Optimization and Control.summary: Finding a Sudoku completion and proving that the completion is unique are different computational tasks. Despite both concerning the same puzzle, their computational effort need not be closely related. In this paper, we investigate how this relationship depends on the mathematical formulation, solver and measure of computational effort. Using 32,000 uniquely solvable puzzles and 64 harder instances, we compare integer programming formulations and CP-SAT. Further, we prove that the raw natural formulation has an extremely weak linear programming relaxation, even with uniqueness exclusions. Computational experiments show that the relationship between completion and certification effort depends on the formulation, puzzle population, solver and effort measure, rather than on the puzzle alone.

Optimization and Control.title: Phases of Muon: When Muon Eclipses SignSGD
Optimization and Control.summary: Muon and related spectral optimizers have recently demonstrated strong empirical performance as scalable stochastic methods, often outperforming Adam. Yet their behavior remains poorly understood. We analyze stochastic Muon, which orthogonalizes an exponential moving average of minibatch gradients, on a high-dimensional matrix-valued least squares problem, and we compare it with stochastic SignSGD, a simple baseline comparable to Adam. We derive explicit deterministic dynamics that provide a tractable framework for studying learning behavior. We show that Muon has non-linear sensitivity to the effective batch $B_{\rm eff}=B(1+β)/(1-β)$. With exact whitening and small $B_{\rm eff}$ Muon fails to resolve smaller eigenmodes, slowing down convergence. Momentum and finite Newton--Shulz iterations can act as a ridge which lessen this effect. This behavior is in contrast with SignSGD which has no transition, leading to different optimal learning rates, but with matching convergence rate up to a constant factor in the isotropic setting. For anisotropic data, large batch setting Muon performs a square-root preconditioning with respect to the data covariance spectrum while SignSGD provides no preconditioning for generic covariances. We analyze time to target loss in a power law covariance model and derive a phase diagram in the data exponent $α$ and target exponent $ζ$. Muon is favored for steep covariance spectra with rich targets ($α>2$, $ζ<α+1$), SignSGD is favored for flat spectra ($α<1$), and in other regions the winner depends on how the target loss scales with dimension. Our results shed light on why replacing Adam with Muon is not trivial even from a pure optimization perspective.

Optimization and Control.title: A switching proximal gradient method for constrained difference-of-convex optimization problems
Optimization and Control.summary: We study difference-of-convex optimization problems with several composite inequality constraints and develop a majorization-guided switching proximal gradient (MGSPG) method. Specifically, at each feasible outer point, quadratic majorization and linearization yield a strongly convex composite surrogate problem. To solve this surrogate approximately, we employ a switching proximal gradient (SPG) method, which takes a proximal gradient step for the objective when the current point is nearly feasible and for a most violated constraint otherwise. This construction requires neither projection onto the joint surrogate feasible set nor multiplier computation. By establishing a common invariant ball and using an increasing weight argument, we obtain an \(O(τ^{-1})\) inner complexity bound for SPG. Building on this bound, we show that, under boundedness of the feasible level set and a uniform Slater condition for the surrogates, MGSPG finds an \(\varepsilon\)-KKT point in \(O(\varepsilon^{-2})\) outer iterations and \(O(\varepsilon^{-4})\) selected component proximal gradient updates. Numerical experiments on SCAD-constrained and groupwise-constrained regression problems demonstrate the viability and computational efficiency of our method compared with existing optimization algorithms.

Optimization and Control.title: The Price of Failure Risk: Clipped Barrier Policy Gradients with Convex Regularization
Optimization and Control.summary: Many operations run on a budget that must rarely run out, such as a wear allowance. A wrapper keeps the remaining budget in the state, subtracts a barrier that grows as the budget shrinks and clips the combined reward from below at -m, and a standard policy-gradient learner trains unchanged. The clip level m is a price of failure risk, since the trained value splits exactly into utility before failure, the cost of a margin and the price times the risk, so whatever policy training returns earns the most such utility net of that cost among policies with no greater risk, up to its optimization error. Its risk exceeds a comparison policy's by at most order 1/m when charged costs stay bounded, and value or validation data certify it. The main theoretical result is exponential convergence of the population training flow under any parameter regularizer convex along the motions of the network's units and strong enough against the price, biased toward the prior policy. This extends mean-field convergence of policy gradients from relative entropy to weight decay, which covers continuous-time training of finite networks. Relative entropy adds noise that lets learning leave flat regions, weight decay pulls the parameters toward a reference, and action regularization bounds the risk change by the distance to a trusted rule. Experiments on an exact maintenance benchmark, a fuel-tank controller, a solvable flow and a benchmark-suite task measure the bounds' slack. We state when another method is better, without claiming this one outperforms them.
Optimization and Control.comment: 38 pages, 7 figures, 2 tables; Online Resource 1 (44 pages) as an ancillary file. Revised and corrected version, replaces v2 (title changed). Code: https://github.com/pma-papers/bpg-replication

Optimization and Control.title: Optimal Control of Scalar Diffusions with Finite Action Sets
Optimization and Control.summary: We study a scalar finite-horizon controlled diffusion with a finite action set. An action may affect the drift, the instantaneous variance, or both, and performance is assessed by a uniformly convex terminal deviation cost. The model represents systems in which decisions are made continuously in time but only finitely many operating settings are available. Under uniform nondegeneracy and an explicit shape condition on the terminal cost, we show that the value function is classical at positive times, establish global positive upper and lower bounds for its second state derivative, and prove that the ratio of its first and second state derivatives is strictly increasing. This ordering implies that each action's optimality region is connected, the active actions occur in monotone order, and adjacent regions are separated by unique switching boundaries. It also yields an exact coefficient-based screen that removes actions that cannot be optimal on any open state region. For smooth continuous-action benchmarks, both the value loss from restricting the action set and the additional loss from rounding the continuous optimal feedback to the nearest available action decrease quadratically with the action-set resolution. Numerical experiments illustrate the resulting action screens, threshold policies, and implementation losses.

Optimization and Control.title: Demand Estimation with Unobserved Stockout Substitution: Exact Likelihood Maximization
Optimization and Control.summary: When a product is sold out, customers who prefer it may buy a substitute or leave without purchasing. Efficient demand estimation in this setting is challenging when inventory is observed only at replenishments, because the stockout times, and hence the products available to each customer, are unobserved. Estimating demand efficiently under stockout substitution has been a challenging problem since Anupindi et al. (1998), and it has become more pressing as the scale of such problem instances grows thanks to innovations in retailing such as unmanned stores. We provide a complete solution to this problem for the multinomial logit (MNL) model, the most widely used model of customer choice. Using a continuous-time representation of the purchase process developed in Zhou et al. (2026), we show that the exact likelihood and its gradient are one-dimensional integrals, no matter how many products, customers, or stockouts there are. Both can be evaluated at a cost linear in the numbers of products and periods. Our method estimates demand for 2,000 products from 2,000 selling periods in under ten minutes.

Optimization and Control.title: Equilibrium Singular Dividend Control with Regime Switching and Bankruptcy under Non-Exponential Discounting
Optimization and Control.summary: This paper studies an infinite-horizon equilibrium dividend problem for a firm whose surplus follows a diffusion with observable Markov regime switching and is absorbed at bankruptcy. Dividend payments are modeled as singular controls, and non-exponential discounting gives rise to time inconsistency. We formulate equilibrium control laws and establish a verification theorem for a general finite-state model with surplus-dependent coefficients. For a two-state model with constant positive drifts and volatilities and bi-exponential discounting, we prove the existence of a regime-dependent equilibrium barrier strategy for arbitrary positive switching intensities. The proof relies on uniform estimates for a system of coupled boundary-value problems and the Poincaré-Miranda theorem. We also verify that the resulting strategy satisfies the equilibrium variational inequalities. Numerical results show that greater dispersion in discount rates, with the initial average discount rate held fixed, raises both barriers. The effect of switching intensity can be nonmonotone and may reverse the ordering of the barriers.

Optimization and Control.title: From Global Optimization to Exact Coordinates: Heilbronn's Triangle Problem on the Unit Square Using Mixed-Integer Nonlinear Optimization
Optimization and Control.summary: We develop a mixed-integer nonlinear programming (MINLP) approach for the Heilbronn triangle problem on the unit square. The formulation exploits the boundary structure of optimal configurations, which we establish rigorously, to fix coordinates and orientation variables a priori. With this formulation, a general-purpose global solver solves the case $n=9$ to global optimality within its numerical tolerances in about eight minutes on a laptop and without any precomputation, compared with about 23 hours of total computation for the best previous approach. The same model also solves $n=10$ for the first time, in under seven hours, and confirms the configuration of Comellas and Yebra (2002). The numerical solutions then guide an exact symbolic reconstruction, and the minimum triangle area of every reconstructed configuration is verified in exact arithmetic. This yields exact coordinates for all $n\le 10$, including the configurations of Comellas and Yebra (2002) for $n=9$ and $n=10$, together with rigorous lower bounds. Finally, we derive structural properties of optimal configurations, formulate a conjecture on the number of critical triangles, and pose an open question. All code and data are publicly available.
Optimization and Control.comment: 31 pages, 9 figures, 16 tables. Revised version, submitted to Mathematical Programming Computation. v3: new title, n=10 solved, revised status of results. Code and data: https://github.com/spiralulam/heilbronn

Optimization and Control.title: It Takes Two Moments: Rigidity and Limits of Continuous Encoders for Over-the-Air Computation
Optimization and Control.summary: We study over-the-air computation of functions, such as empirical variance, formed by combining two separately postprocessed sums of locally transformed observations. We consider continuous encoders subject to pointwise peak-power constraints over a single use of a complex multiple-access channel. With four or more transmitters, we identify conditions under which exact noiseless recovery forces every continuous encoder collection into a common affine structure that preserves both sums, reducing infinite-dimensional encoder design to selecting a finite set of coefficients. To quantify resilience against channel noise, we introduce a robustness score that measures the separation of noiseless received aggregates relative to variations in the desired function value. Within this characterized encoder family, we formulate robustness maximization as an exact convex semi-infinite program, eliminating rank constraints without a relaxation gap, and construct a decoder that attains the minimum uniform noise-amplification constant. For several function classes, including empirical variance, we derive closed-form robustness-optimal encoders and scores. Under mild regularity conditions, we also establish sharp limits on the Gaussian mean squared error at high signal-to-noise ratios and show how using the input distribution reduces average error at the expense of uniform robustness.

Optimization and Control.title: ROAR: Restricted 2-Opt And Ruin-and-recreate Heuristic for Large and Extreme Scale Traveling Repairman Problem
Optimization and Control.summary: The Traveling Repairman Problem minimizes cumulative arrival times rather than the total route length, as in the classical Traveling Salesman Problem. The literature contains several legacy metaheuristics for the TRP; however, most are evaluated on small- and medium-scale instances and show limited scalability for large and extreme datasets. GILS-RVND, the current gold standard in metaheuristic algorithms, performs well on small and medium instances but struggles to scale due to the exhaustive neighborhood search in the RVND phase. To address this limitation, we introduce Restricted 2-Opt And Ruin-and-recreate (ROAR), a Large Neighborhood Search-based method that integrates ruin-and-recreate with greedy insertion and a restricted, insertion-anchored 2-opt operator. Computational experiments demonstrate that ROAR produces high-quality solutions for large-scale instances and outperforms existing methods under strict time limits. We further introduce an O(1)-time, O(1)-space algorithm for evaluating 2-opt moves during a contiguous systematic sweep, which, to the best of our knowledge, is unprecedented. Finally, we evaluate ROAR on instances with up to 200,000 nodes, substantially exceeding the largest instances previously reported in the literature (11,849 nodes).
Optimization and Control.comment: Accepted at RIVF 2026 20th International Conference on Computing and Communication Technologies

Optimization and Control.title: A model predictive control framework with robust stability guarantees under unbounded disturbances
Optimization and Control.summary: To address feasibility issues in model predictive control (MPC), most implementations relax state constraints by using slack variables and adding a penalty to the cost. We propose an alternative strategy: relaxing the initial state constraint with a penalty. Compared to state-of-the-art soft constrained MPC formulations, the proposed formulation has two key features: (i) input-to-state stability and bounds on the cumulative constraint violation for unbounded disturbances; (ii) close-to-optimal performance under nominal operating conditions. The idea is initially presented for open-loop asymptotically stable nonlinear systems by designing the penalty as a Lyapunov function, but we also show how to relax this condition to: i) Lyapunov stable systems; ii) stabilizable systems; and iii) utilizing an implicit characterization of the Lyapunov function.
