Systems and Control.title: Safe Unicycle Navigation Among Multiple Obstacles Under Bounded Disturbances: A Learning-Augmented CLF-CBF Approach (Extended Version)
Systems and Control.summary: This paper presents a robust control framework for safe navigation of a unicycle robot to a goal among multiple static obstacles under an unknown, time-varying disturbance. The controller solves a single real-time quadratic program (QP) that combines a goal-reaching term with one safety term per obstacle. The goal-reaching term is a cross-track control Lyapunov function built from body-frame tracking errors rather than a bearing angle, which keeps its Lie derivatives bounded everywhere, including the goal. Safety is encoded using robust control barrier functions, one per obstacle, each tightened by a closed-form, state-dependent disturbance bound. When stabilization and safety conflict, a slack variable relaxes only the convergence requirement, so that the safety constraints remain strictly enforced. Whenever the QP is feasible, the robust barrier constraints guarantee forward invariance of every obstacle's safe set under all admissible disturbances. Complementing this safety guarantee, a Lyapunov analysis yields an explicit ultimate bound on the distance to the goal. A learning-augmented variant replaces the fixed objective with a reinforcement-learning reference, which accelerates convergence when multiple constraints are simultaneously active. We further derive the obstacle separation below which the gap between two obstacles becomes too narrow to pass through under the robust constraints. For such gaps, a learned virtual goal for the Lyapunov function steers the robot around the obstacles without compromising safety. Simulations, a Monte Carlo study, and a comparison against a sampled-data robust baseline support the theoretical results.

Systems and Control.title: Safe World Model for Joint Trajectory and Beamforming Design of Mobile Base Stations
Systems and Control.summary: Mobile base stations (MBSs), including aerial and ground-based platforms, provide flexible wireless coverage through adaptive positioning. However, jointly optimizing their trajectories and digital beamforming is challenging because movement changes channel conditions and interference, while beamforming determines the resulting signal and interference powers. These coupled decisions also account for how current movements affect future positions and communication performance under mobility and safety constraints. We formulate this problem as a constrained Markov decision process that maximizes the time-averaged sum signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR), subject to mobility, obstacle region avoidance, and transmit-power constraints. To support long-term planning and reduce the extensive environment interactions required by model-free reinforcement learning, we develop a SafeDreamer-based world model framework that learns latent system dynamics from experience and optimizes a joint trajectory and beamforming policy through imagined trajectories. Feasibility-preserving action mappings and safety cost signals incorporate operational constraints into policy learning. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves higher time-averaged sum SINR than the proximal policy optimization and deep Q-network baselines, while exhibiting improved sample efficiency and more reliable constraint satisfaction.

Systems and Control.title: Computing with Coupled Oscillator Networks: Optimization, Memory, and Modern AI Primitives
Systems and Control.summary: We explore how synchronization in coupled oscillator networks may be employed to perform a variety of computing tasks. These systems are becoming more attractive as an alternative to conventional digital computers due to the increasing energy demands of the latter, particularly for large-scale problems in machine learning and artificial intelligence. The ubiquity of coupled oscillator networks means that oscillator-based computing can be thought of as a universal computing paradigm encompassing systems with a diversity of physical realizations, e.g. as analog circuits, neurological systems, spintronic systems. The bridge between the dynamics of coupled oscillator networks and computational primitives they implement is the Ising model, which originates in statistical physics, and when applied to oscillator networks, explains the emergence of globally complex and disordered synchronization patterns from local interactions in the network. We discuss the application of coupled oscillator networks to three fundamental computing operations. First, oscillator networks as specialized hardware solvers of NP-hard combinatorial optimization problems, with the solution encoded in the synchrony patterns. Second, oscillator networks as associative memory systems, enabling storage and retrieval of data represented through phases of oscillations. Finally, oscillator networks as a dynamical implementation of attention, with synchronization providing the mechanism for the alignment of keys to queries. The ability of oscillator networks to implement these computational primitives paves the way for novel realizations of intelligent systems through a variety of physical substrates.

Systems and Control.title: Global Parameter Identification and Uncertainty Quantification of reduced-order ADM1 using Maximum Likelihood Estimation and Bayesian Inference
Systems and Control.summary: Anaerobic digestion (AD) models can be challenging to calibrate against real data due to limited practical identifiability, data scarcity, and model complexity. Weighted least squares objective functions and gradient-based solvers using finite differences are often used in literature, but result in suboptimal parameter estimates and large uncertainty bands. This paper identifies the parameters of a reduced-order ADM1 by comparing the frameworks of maximum likelihood estimation (MLE) and Bayesian inference (BI), and quantifies uncertainties of parameters and outputs. Multirate experimental data are taken from a lab-scale AD reactor fed with agricultural substrates and operated at organic loading rates of 3$\,$g VS $\mathrm{m^{-3}d^{-1}}$. Global optima are found via global and gradient-based local search algorithms using forward sensitivities. Enhanced scatter search provides the best global search results. These are refined by the Gauss-Newton algorithm as the best local search, which delivers $R^2$ values of 0.95 for acetic acid and 0.77 for biogas production. BI yields substantially narrower uncertainty bands than MLE and avoids the need for a global search by incorporating prior knowledge about parameter distributions. The search space is captured efficiently by log10 scaling of parameters. Algorithmic details on its implications are provided. Despite a high-resolution lab-scale dataset, the ADM1-specific inhibition parameter $K_\mathrm{I,nh3}$ is practically not identifiable with MLE, and shows a low output sensitivity, whereas a parameter for the effective ion concentration shows superb practical identifiabilty at high confidence with both MLE and BI. The present work lays a scalable base for calibration of nonlinear AD models by providing reliable simulations. It thus advances model-based monitoring and control applications of multirate processes such as agricultural AD plants.

Systems and Control.title: From Airspace Degradation to Deconfliction: Predicting Safety-Critical Traffic States through the Evolution of Multiscale Complexity Metrics
Systems and Control.summary: Growing air traffic demand is pushing airspace management towards the limits of its operational capacity, with steadily increasing workload for air traffic control officers, with direct consequences for safety. Understanding which traffic conditions give rise to safety-critical situations is therefore an essential open problem. Here we compare a large number of deconfliction events with equivalent conflict-free scenarios, extracted from thirteen weeks of air traffic control data over the Swedish Flight Information Region. We describe the traffic structure before each event through thirty sector-complexity metrics computed at multiple spatial and temporal scales, and use them as inputs of Machine Learning models. We find that the need of deconflictions can be predicted with an accuracy reaching $70\%$, but only when the traffic is described at the sector spatial scale. Predictability increases monotonically in the minutes preceding the clearance, showing that situations requiring deconflicting actions are not sudden occurrences, but rather the endpoint of a progressive degradation process. Additionally, the information needed for such prediction mainly resides in specific characteristics of the overall traffic structure, and not only in the conflicting pair. These results numerically demonstrate that safety-critical airspace states can be anticipated from the collective behaviour of the traffic, paving the way for early-warning systems that flag degraded, safety-relevant conditions before an intervention is required.

Systems and Control.title: Cybersecurity Practices in Industrial Automation and Control Systems: a Study of Croatian System Integrators
Systems and Control.summary: Given the increasing frequency of industrial cybersecurity incidents, governments, industry, and the research community are all working to find ways to protect industrial automation and control systems (IACSs). A key regulatory effort in the European context is the EU's Network and Information Security Directive 2 (NIS2), which aims to strengthen cybersecurity requirements and improve resilience across critical and important sectors. Nevertheless, translating cybersecurity requirements into practical engineering remains challenging within IACS environments. This paper explores how Croatian IACS system integrators perceive cybersecurity requirements, implementation challenges, and current practices in the industrial environments in which they operate. The findings are based on three focus groups with system integrators working with clients in the energy, chemical and pharmaceutical, and food and beverage sectors. Participants reported limited cybersecurity awareness among IACS owners, as well as perceived differences in practices between smaller and larger companies and between domestic and foreign firms. Participants were divided in their expectations regarding regulatory pressure: while some believed it could improve cybersecurity, others expected only minimal compliance focused on cost reduction. The results of this study provide a basis for developing more practical cybersecurity practices and offer a deeper understanding of the key challenges faced by IACS system integrators and owners when dealing with cybersecurity.

Systems and Control.title: Non-Asymptotic Confidence Regions for Separable Nonlinear Models
Systems and Control.summary: This paper studies robust uncertainty quantification for separable nonlinear least squares (SNLLS) problems. We propose two identification methods, (i) Residual-Perturbed Gradient (RPG) and (ii) Global-Fit-Gap (GFG), to construct joint distribution-free confidence regions for both the linear and nonlinear parameters. By exploiting assumed group invariance of the noise (such as symmetry or exchangeability), we apply random perturbations (such as sign-changes or permutations) to build the regions based on resampling and ranking. We prove that both methods guarantee non-asymptotically exact coverage (type I error). Finally, we illustrate the constructions through two numerical experiments: (i) identifying generalized finite impulse response (GFIR) systems using Laguerre polynomials with an adjustable decay rate and (ii) fitting Gaussian radial basis function (RBF) models with variable knots and widths.
Systems and Control.comment: Accepted for publication at the 65th IEEE Conference on Decision and Control (CDC 2026)

Systems and Control.title: Assuring Learning-Enabled Cyber-Physical Systems with Foundation Models: A Neuro-Symbolic Agenda for Testing, Verification, and Runtime Assurance
Systems and Control.summary: Learning-enabled cyber-physical systems (CPS), including autonomous vehicles and UAVs, increasingly incorporate foundation models, yet fragmented assurance practices provide insufficient support for system-level guarantees. We argue that restoring engineering control across stochastic neural, symbolic, and physical boundaries requires a shift from model-centric evaluation to system-level assurance. We introduce the Foundation Model Assurance Stack, connecting three directions: (i) neuro-symbolic architectures that constrain foundation models through explicit symbolic world models, reasoning layers, and interfaces; (ii) semantically grounded, conformance-based testing that combines formal specifications and symbolic world models with foundation-model-assisted specification mining, scenario generation, and test synthesis; and (iii) compositional verification and runtime assurance that target formally tractable components and interfaces through modular contracts, equivalence checking, verified synthesis, uncertainty-aware reasoning, and runtime monitoring and enforcement. Symbolic abstractions establish assurance boundaries between stochastic learning and formal reasoning, connecting testing, verification, and runtime evidence across the system lifecycle. Foundation models serve as constrained assistants whose outputs are independently checked wherever correctness can be formally specified. We identify research challenges in specification engineering, abstraction fidelity, evidence composition, and lifecycle certification, and outline a staged agenda toward trustworthy, deployable, and certifiable learning-enabled CPS.

Systems and Control.title: On the Performance of AoA-Based Physical-Layer Authentication Under Multi-Source Impersonation Attacks
Systems and Control.summary: This paper investigates cooperative impersonation attacks against angle-of-arrival (AoA)-based authentication for a wireless communication receiver equipped with a digital uniform linear array. Specifically, we characterize the vulnerability and robustness of this authentication system in relation to adversarial angular diversity and the relative numbers of adversarial sources and receive antennas. To this end, we first derive the optimal precoding vector for multiple spatially distributed adversarial sources by minimizing the mean squared error between legitimate and adversarial received signals. By means of the rank property of Vandermonde matrices, we then establish necessary and sufficient conditions under which the adversarial sources can reproduce the legitimate transmitter's spatial signature. With fewer adversarial sources than receive antennas, perfect reproduction is not possible without at least one adversarial source satisfying a specific AoA condition. In the other case, increasing the number of receive antennas can reduce impersonation success probabilities when none of the adversarial sources has an AoA satisfying this condition. Numerical results validate the theoretical analysis and evaluate the security performance of AoA-based authentication.

Systems and Control.title: Information-Driven Collaborative Autonomy for Heterogeneous UAV/UGV Teams
Systems and Control.summary: This paper considers coordinating a heterogeneous team of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) and unmanned ground vehicles (UGVs) traversing a domain containing an unknown number of potentially hazardous targets. The UAVs provide aerial sensing using onboard optical cameras, adapting their trajectories to ground routes and target information. We formulate the aerial search problem using ergodic control, which distributes sensing effort according to a spatial information density to balance exploration and target localization. The formulation incorporates dynamic camera field-of-view footprints and pose-dependent probabilistic detection models. Angles-only measurements are processed through Bayesian inference and marginalization over data-association hypotheses to obtain a Poisson multi-Bernoulli (PMB) approximation of the target posterior, representing both detected and undetected targets. This belief directs aerial sensing toward unexplored regions along the ground routes and viewpoints that improve target localization. Ground planning combines chance-constrained target avoidance, enforced through confidence sets, with a void-probability objective that favors routes unlikely to contain threats. We solve each team's optimization problem in a fully decentralized manner using a nested SCvx*--C-ADMM scheme, with outer sequential convex programming iterations and inner distributed consensus optimization, accounting for nonlinearities, nonseparable objectives, and continuous-time inter-agent separation constraints. A closed-loop scheme updates both fleets' trajectories as information becomes available and permits ground motion when the remaining route risk falls below a prescribed threshold. Numerical case studies examine sensing geometry and target uncertainty, compare decentralized and centralized solvers, and demonstrate full closed-loop collaboration between multiple UAVs and UGVs.

Systems and Control.title: Limit Theorems and Optimal Policies for Flock Flight through Poisson Forests
Systems and Control.summary: Inspired by birds flying through cluttered environments, Karaman and Frazzoli showed that high-speed flight through an ergodic random forest exhibits an ultimate speed limit: above a critical speed, almost surely no infinite collision-free trajectory exists for a single bird. This paper formulates a corresponding bulk-transport problem for many birds. We construct an explicit directed corridor network in a Poisson disk forest and impose a common temporal headway at its waypoints. The maximum current equals a minimum vertex-cut capacity and is achieved by repeated flight along vertex-disjoint paths. The same schedule maximizes completed traversals at every finite horizon, with constant forward speed and no internal waiting. For a forest belt of fixed depth, exact transverse superadditivity yields an almost-sure deterministic current-density limit. A uniform shape theorem for an asymmetric planar dual identifies the current when depth and width grow together. For diverging depth bounded by a constant times width, this current equals the width-first, depth-second limit and is independent of the positive aspect ratio. When diagonal corridors are available, bulk current is positive at sufficiently low obstacle intensity and zero at sufficiently high intensity. For stochastic demand, an upstream admission queue is stable at every rate below the finite-network capacity.

Systems and Control.title: Minimum-Energy Control for Stochastic Linear Systems: A Data-Driven Approach with Finite-Sample Guarantees
Systems and Control.summary: The open-loop minimum-energy control (MEC) problem asks for control inputs that minimize the control energy while ensuring the terminal state reaches a desired value. In this paper, we study the open-loop MEC problem for stochastic linear time-invariant systems. We consider a variety of stochastic constraints that enforce the terminal error to be small, and show that Stochastic MEC (SMEC) problem can be formulated as a QCQP. We obtain the optimal solution for SMEC and show that it generalizes the well-known Deterministic MEC problem by introducing novel stochastic variants of controllability and Gramian matrices. When the system dynamics is unknown, we obtain a direct data-driven solution to the SMEC problem using maximum-likelihood estimation and conformal calibration approaches. Finally, we quantify the sub-optimality and constraint violation of our data-driven solutions via finite-sample high-probability upper bounds, and highlight their dependence on the number of experiments, system dimension, and noise-to-signal ratio. We present numerical simulations to validate the theoretical results.

Systems and Control.title: LLM eBay: A Simple and Truthful Marketplace for Fine-Tuned LLMs Trading
Systems and Control.summary: Personalized fine-tuning of Large Language Models (LLMs) enhances user experience but incurs substantial computational costs. Recent studies show that initializing training from a style-similar fine-tuned model reduces adaptation overhead, turning such checkpoints into reusable, tradable assets. A marketplace for these checkpoints, however, faces information asymmetry: sellers may misreport a checkpoint's style, while buyers cannot verify its usefulness before purchase, which invites adverse selection. We introduce LLM eBay, a simple single-round marketplace for trading fine-tuned LLMs. Sellers are paid per purchase at a posted price, and a truncated quadratic proper scoring rule adjusts each payment according to how well the seller's style report agrees with a style signal that the platform measures by generating text on hidden prompts. We show that the score elicits the verifier's expected signal, characterize exactly when truthful reporting is a seller best response under per-purchase demand, and bound the downside risk from noisy verification. In an end-to-end study with real LoRA checkpoints on two base models and three buyer tasks, LLM eBay reduces measured convergence steps by 8.5\% relative to retrieval over self-reported style (95\% CI [1.0\%, 15.9\%]). In model-based market simulations built on a measured style-to-cost relationship, it cuts style-claim error by 96.5\% (from 0.424 to 0.015), recovers 96.3\% of Oracle welfare, saves 72.4\% of the cost of fine-tuning from the base model, and keeps all providers profitable in the default setting.

Systems and Control.title: BEVLight: Generalizable Traffic Signal Control from UAV Bird's-Eye Views
Systems and Control.summary: Learning-based traffic signal control (TSC) has achieved promising performance, but most methods rely on structured traffic states that must be estimated from sensor observations in real deployments. Visual TSC learns signal decisions directly from images, yet existing methods depend on fixed roadside cameras and remain tied to specific intersection configurations and visual domains. UAVs offer on-demand bird's-eye-view (BEV) observations that jointly capture intersection topology and traffic dynamics, making them a promising sensing platform for visual TSC. We present BEVLight, a generalizable TSC framework that directly maps BEV observations to signal actions. BEVLight grounds visual features onto individual lanes and composes them along the junction topology into movement and phase representations, allowing a shared policy to score candidate phases across heterogeneous intersection layouts and signal plans. To train the policy, we develop a web-based virtual teleoperation platform and collect over 5K human control decisions together with their underlying traffic states. Simulator-provided traffic states first supervise lane- and movement-level representations, after which human phase selections and rankings supervise the phase scorer. Re-rendering the recorded trajectories under diverse appearances preserves both forms of supervision and encourages robustness to visual changes. Closed-loop experiments demonstrate zero-shot generalization across traffic demands, signal plans, and intersections: BEVLight reduces average waiting time by 7--9\% relative to perception-to-control visual baselines and matches or outperforms structured-state RL controllers that receive ground-truth traffic states, achieving the lowest waiting time in 12 of 16 scenarios. An offline study further shows that BEVLight transfers to real UAV observations without target-domain adaptation.

Systems and Control.title: Compound Climate Risk-Aware Electricity Dispatch: Trajectory-Based Modeling for Power System Resilience
Systems and Control.summary: In recent decades, emerging compound hazards in a changing climate have increasingly threatened power system resilience and posed new challenges to electricity dispatch. Conventional Value-at-Risk (VaR)-based risk-aware dispatch provides a tractable means of managing stochastic net demand deviations caused by distribution feeder outages. However, when applied to temporally compounding events such as tropical cyclone (TC)--blackout--heatwave, conventional net demand risk formulations may assign similar risk levels to a brief outage and an outage with the same instantaneous net demand impact that persists into a subsequent hazard, despite their different requirements for sustained operational flexibility. Moreover, directly incorporating compound risk into electricity dispatch models faces a structural mismatch: the risk is defined by the joint distribution of feeder restoration and subsequent hazards over exponentially many joint states, whereas dispatch models require risk formulations that are tractable in the scheduling decisions. To address these issues, this paper proposes a compound climate risk-aware dispatch framework with a trajectory-based compound risk model, which defines the loss on operating deviations determined by entire feeder connection trajectories, parameterized by uncertain restoration times and coupled with subsequent hazards. Analytical moment-generating functions and equivalent exponential-cone reformulations provide a compact representation of the resulting risk constraints, preserving the relevant dependencies without explicit joint-state enumeration. By leveraging a physics-based spatiotemporal TC--blackout--heatwave hazard model, case studies demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method with real-world time-series power outage data from Puerto Rico, including data collected during Hurricane Fiona in 2022.

Systems and Control.title: Tracking analysis of compressed-communication distributed adaptive estimation for time-varying parameters
Systems and Control.summary: This paper studies the problem of distributed time-varying parameter tracking over communication-constrained networks. To mitigate the accumulation of induced compression errors across the network, we propose a differentially compressed distributed least mean squares (LMS) algorithm.In the proposed scheme, each sensor updates a local auxiliary state recursively based on the compressed difference between the current parameter estimate and the previous auxiliary state, and then transmits only this compressed difference to its neighbors for auxiliary-state reconstruction. This differential recursion mechanism helps control the accumulation of compression errors and accommodates a general class of randomized compressors including randomized quantizers and sparsifiers.We establish the mean-square boundedness and explicit steady-state tracking-error bound under a cooperative excitation condition on stochastic regression vectors, which captures both temporal and spatial information to reflect the joint excitation effect of sensors.Notably, our stability analysis requires neither temporal independence nor stationarity of regressors, nor persistent excitation at individual nodes, thereby accommodating correlated and nonstationary signals from stochastic feedback systems. Numerical simulations demonstrate the theoretical results under correlated and non-stationary regression data.

Systems and Control.title: REALM: Identifying Minimal Task Assets for LLM Agents
Systems and Control.summary: Large language model (LLM) agents often receive access to more files, accounts, and services than a task requires. Prompt injection turns this excess access into an opportunity to redirect execution toward unrelated resources. Applying least privilege therefore requires identifying the assets needed by a task, including assets whose identities emerge only during execution. We present REALM (Required Execution Assets Linked to a Mission), an approach to identifying and maintaining a task's required assets and their permitted uses. The approach represents required assets as Dependency Graph nodes, resolves prerequisite relationships, and admits newly discovered assets through source-scoped selection. It separates discovering an asset from authorizing its use, while preserving the agent's freedom to choose its computation. The REALM Builder maintains the selected grants and projects Asset Files; the Partial API Manager exposes resource-bound Partial APIs to the Agent inside a Task Container. Across 60 clean tasks and 560 injected cases in AgentDyn, it completes 40.0% and 36.4% of tasks and decreases ASR from 16.6% to 0.2% with qwen3.5-flash as the base model.

Systems and Control.title: Unlocking with the Heart: Investigating User Perceptions of ECG-Based Biometric Authentication
Systems and Control.summary: Password-based authentication remains challenging for many users, especially for those who face usability and accessibility issues. The burden of maintaining security can cause user fatigue, frustration and non-engagement. To address these issues, we conducted a pilot study to assess ECG-based biometric authentication as a passwordless alternative and to gather adult participants' perspectives on this approach. The research consisted of a survey study, an authentication prototype and a follow-up usability experience questionnaire. Our approach combined an online survey of 337 adults examining authentication practices and perceptions, with a separate usability evaluation in which 49 participants interacted with a simulated ECG-authentication and password interface in a health-care application prototype, then completed a post-test usability test questionnaire. The survey examined how adults across age groups use and perceive various authentication techniques, their experiences with biometrics, their views on security and convenience, and their willingness to adopt ECG authentication. In parallel, the usability prototype and questionnaire captured participants' responses after hands-on interaction with an ECG authentication prototype.

Systems and Control.title: From Reconnaissance to Response: Quantitative Risk Parameterization and Game Theoretic Containment in Modern Enterprise Attack
Systems and Control.summary: Modern Security Operations Centers struggle with delayed manual incident response, enabling adversaries to advance through the Cyber Kill Chain during early stage reconnaissance. While classical game theoretic defense models optimize strategic resource allocation, they rely on static utility matrices that fail to adapt to dynamic telemetry. This paper presents an integrated, metrics driven decision engine that bridges quantitative risk parameterization and continuous automated response time. Common Vulnerability Scoring Systems exploitability parameters are mapped to attacker success probabilities and evaluate defender log distributions via Factor Analysis of Information Risk Monte Carlo simulations. Real time SIEM logs streams are modeled as Poisson process arrival rates, dynamically updating defender posterior threat belief through sequential Bayesian filtering. A closed form threshold is derived by framing the interaction as a dynamic Bayesian Stackelberg game, where the expected unmitigated risk exceeds proactive containment cost. Parameterized against empirical data from the 2023 MGM Resorts and Caesars Entertainment cyber incident, simulation results demonstrate that the engine suppresses transient background noise while triggering automated SOAR network isolation within seconds of adversarial probing. Multi parameter sensitivity analysis confirms that the decision boundary dynamically adjusts to live perimeter vulnerability, offering a control theoretic foundation for sub minute automated threat containment.

Information Theory.title: Classical communication over quantum channels: does entanglement help in nature?
Information Theory.summary: Can entangling codewords across independent uses of a quantum channel improve the rate of classical communication? An old conjecture states that there is no such entanglement advantage for all channels. Although Hastings's result and follow-up works disproved this conjecture, it turns out that enormous dimension is required to construct a channel where entanglement enhances classical communication. This indicates that there might be no entanglement advantage for many physical channels, or for all low dimensional channels. Motivated by recent progress on (generalized) amplitude damping channels, we propose a general Schur-weighted block entropy inequality, and show that there is no entanglement advantage for all phase-covariant channels including multi-level amplitude damping channels, generalized dephasing channels, and damping-dephasing channels. As a by-product, we also recover the recently established result that there is no entanglement advantage for all qubit channels.
Information Theory.comment: See the companion github repository https://github.com/pxwu24/additivity-of-classical-communication for the presentation of the results and a complete Lean verification

Information Theory.title: Power Adjusting Games Under Block-Dependent Pool Payout Schemes
Information Theory.summary: Advanced power adjusting block withholding attacks such as PAW and T-PAW have been analyzed so far under a global-reset version of the proportional scheme (GRP), which is rarely used in practice. In this paper, we analyze T-PAW, which contains FAW and PAW as special cases, under the block-dependent payout schemes deployed in practice: Pay-Per-Last-N-Shares (PPLNS), round-based Proportional (PROP) and exponential-decay (EXP). We derive the revenue ratios analytically, by renewal arguments for PPLNS and through the stationary carry process of an open round for PROP and EXP. We further introduce Power Adjusting Hopping (PAH), where an adversary of any size adjusts its power allocation towards the pool according to the blockwork age of the round without withholding any block, and derive its revenue ratios under PROP and EXP. We show that GRP misestimates the T-PAW gain in a scheme-dependent direction: it overstates the gain under PROP up to an order of magnitude and understates it under EXP for the original slush decay rate. PROP is highly vulnerable to PAH, while EXP faces a trade-off: a slow decay invites PAH and a fast decay invites T-PAW. PPLNS is the least vulnerable scheme: it is immune to PAH and it mitigates, but does not eliminate, T-PAW. All analytical results are verified by Monte Carlo simulations.

Information Theory.title: On the Fundamental Limits of Prefill-Based Decoding Length Prediction
Information Theory.summary: Predicting how many tokens a large language model (LLM) will decode, using only prefill-phase hidden states, is a key primitive for inference scheduling. We show that current benchmarks conflate predictor quality with task hardness: when the target model, dataset, or sampling configuration changes, reported accuracy collapses even though the predictor is unchanged. We trace this instability to an overlooked error source---the inherent stochasticity of autoregressive decoding---and derive bounds that every prefill-side method must obey. Our analysis treats decoding as a stopped stochastic process. The per-step stopping probability of a response is not constant but ramps up over hundreds of steps, so the decode length inherits a central limit theorem from the many local decisions that determine where a response ends; this yields per-prompt normality with an explicit error term, together with an affine variance law $σ=αμ+b$ whose slope is the coefficient of variation of the number of response segments. Empirically, the normal law reproduces the per-prompt MAE and the central mass of the decode-length distribution to within a few percent, and the residual departures from normality (mild right skew, slight excess kurtosis) are the ones predicted by the sampling-noise correction. Under fixed model, data, and sampling conditions, a broad design space of predictors (MLP, EGTP, FiLM, soft-label, and Mixture-of-Experts variants) converges to similar performance close to the bound, confirming that \emph{system error dominates model error}. We argue for a benchmarking protocol that fixes the model, data, and sampling parameters and that reports relative-error metrics alongside absolute ones. Code and analysis tools are available at https://github.com/ShwStone/DecodingPredict.

Information Theory.title: An SCL-Aware Design of PAC Codes
Information Theory.summary: We develop design methodologies for the rate profile of polarization-adjusted convolutional (PAC) codes tailored to successive cancellation list (SCL) decoding. The crux of our approach is two-fold: first is the creation of a modified density evolution Gaussian approximation (DEGA), called conditional DEGA (CDEGA), to analyze the decoding process in the presence of errors; second is the creation of a dangerous-path occupancy metric to find the conditional occupancy of bit-errors in a finite list. Our approach not only illuminates the role of rate-one precoding, but also provides insight into why certain information sets are particularly well suited to PAC codes. We demonstrate the usefulness of CDEGA and dangerous-path metrics with algorithms that create new information sets, as well as precoders that are extremely sparse yet competitive. In particular, we design codes of length $N \leq 512$ with various rates and list sizes, all of which offer at least half a dB gain over traditional PAC codes at an FER of $10^{-3}$ and improve upon state-of-the-art results.

Information Theory.title: Fast and accurate neural triage decoding of ultra-high-rate quantum LDPC codes
Information Theory.summary: Quantum error correction is essential for fault-tolerant quantum computing. High-rate quantum low-density parity-check (qLDPC) codes have emerged as a promising approach to reducing the substantial physical qubit overhead of quantum error correction, enabling encoding rates exceeding $1/2$ in blocks of approximately one thousand physical data qubits. However, their practical implementation requires decoders that combine high accuracy with low latency to keep pace with quantum hardware. Existing decoders of high-rate qLDPC codes can achieve high accuracy but often incur substantial computational latency, whereas neural network decoders have yet to be demonstrated for high-rate qLDPC codes. Here, we introduce \emph{neural triage decoding}, a framework that uses syndrome consistency to adaptively allocate neural computation. A local neural message-passing network rapidly predicts error corrections, additional iterations reduce residual syndrome violations, and a rarely invoked diversification stage searches for consistent corrections to the remaining shots. We demonstrate that the \texttt{Triage} decoder can decode ultra-high-rate qLDPC codes encoding a few hundred logical qubits, including lifted-product and Kasai codes, achieving state-of-the-art accuracy comparable to the near optimal algorithmic decoders while reducing decoding latency by approximately one to two orders of magnitude. Our framework is inspired by a rigorous analysis of the exact bitwise marginal decoder, revealing a distance-independent syndrome-inconsistent error floor. In addition, we show the robustness of neural network decoders to mismatched error priors. Our results establish adaptive neural decoding as a promising route towards fast, accurate, and scalable quantum error correction in the near term.
Information Theory.comment: 5 pages, 4 figures with Methods. We will release the fully supplementary information in the second update soon

Information Theory.title: Average pairwise Hamming distance of a subset in a hypercube
Information Theory.summary: In this note, we prove that for a subset $\mathcal{F}$ of $\{0,1\}^n$ of density $\frac{1}{8}$, its average pairwise Hamming distance is at least $\frac{n-3}{2}$, with equality attained only by $(n-3)$-dimensional subcubes. This answers a question of Lei Yu, and solves an important open case of a more general question posed by Ahlswede and Katona in 1977.

Information Theory.title: Quantum communication: a discrimination approach
Information Theory.summary: We develop a state discrimination approach to unassisted quantum communication through a noisy quantum channel. Starting from the operational duality between entanglement recovery and state discrimination, we construct entanglement-generation codes with explicit decoders constructed from Petz recovery maps. The resulting error bounds hold for every number of channel uses and are expressed in terms of Petz-Rényi coherent information. For product sources, they yield exponential error decay at rates below coherent information.

Information Theory.title: A Unified Complexity Framework for Quantum Property Testing
Information Theory.summary:
We develop a unified framework for analyzing the complexity of quantum property testing through functionals of the form $\mathcal{L}_φ(ρ) = \operatorname{tr}(φ(dρ))/d$, where $ρ$ is an unknown $d$-dimensional quantum state and $φ$ is a given function. A master theorem is established that derives sample complexity lower bounds for estimating $\mathcal{L}_φ(ρ)$ from properties of $φ$, combining Haar-random moment encoding with moment matching and best polynomial approximation. Corresponding query complexity lower bounds follow from quantum sample-to-query lifting.
  The framework yields (nearly) tight bounds for a broad class of problems, including entropy estimation (von Neumann, Rényi, and Tsallis), closeness estimation (trace distance and Uhlmann fidelity), spectrum estimation, rank testing (operator rank, Schmidt rank, and matrix product states). In particular, combined with known upper bounds, we show that the sample complexity of von Neumann entropy estimation is \[ Θ\!\left(\frac{d^2}{\varepsilon\log^2(d)\max\{1, \varepsilon\log^2(d)\}} + \frac{\log^2(d)}{\varepsilon^2}\right), \] and the sample complexity of spectrum estimation is \[ Θ\!\left(\frac{d^2}{\varepsilon^2\log^2(d)\max\{1, \varepsilon^2\log^2(d)\}}\right). \] In summary, our results resolve several open problems and establish the optimality of 37 quantum algorithms since 2015, up to constant or polylogarithmic factors.

Information Theory.title: Measuring the Value of Communication in Multi-Agent Tracking Under Finite-Rate Belief Sharing
Information Theory.summary: This paper investigates the value of communica- tion (VoC) in cooperative multi-agent tracking under rate- constrained information exchange. Although prior work has studied distributed tracking, quantized communication, and robust fusion, it remains unclear at what communication rate most of the achievable tracking gain is obtained, beyond which additional communication resources yield only marginal benefit. We consider stationary agents that observe a moving target through heterogeneous range and bearing measurements, perform local extended Kalman filtering (EKF), quantize their posterior state means, and fuse exchanged information via covariance intersection (CI). Performance is evaluated versus communication rate relative to no-communication baselines, a centralized oracle, and a CI-perfect reference. The results show that communication is not uniformly beneficial: very low rates can degrade performance due to coarse quantization, whereas moderate rates recover most of the achievable gain. In the considered scenario, increasing the rate from 4 to 12 bit/s per agent reduces the root-mean-square error (RMSE) from 13.93 m to 6.35 m, while a further increase to 32 bit/s per agent improves it only marginally to 5.93 m. This reveals a clear knee region at moderate rates, beyond which the remaining loss is mainly due to the conservatism of the fusion architecture. Overall, the proposed framework characterizes low-rate degradation, communication-efficient operation, and diminishing returns, while highlighting the joint role of rate and sensing geometry in determining communication benefit.

Information Theory.title: Level Crossing Rate Bounds for Products of Independent Nonstationary Fading Processes
Information Theory.summary: We develop a unified framework for the instantaneous total level crossing rate (LCR) of products of independent positive nonstationary fading processes. Universal upper and lower bounds are first derived from an exact decomposition of the product derivative and signed crossing imbalance, requiring only factor-wise crossing statistics. We then introduce the drifting Gaussian-derivative (DGD) class, in which each conditional derivative is Gaussian with possibly nonzero drift. For products of DGD factors, an exact Gaussian-mixture representation yields bounds that jointly capture aggregate drift and derivative fluctuations. The lower bound reduces under stationarity to a known $\ell_2$ bound, whereas, to the best of the author's knowledge, the upper bound is new even in the stationary case. Furthermore, the bounds are asymptotically exact in drift-dominated regimes. The framework is specialized to nonstationary Double-Rayleigh fading and to quasi-identically distributed DGD factors, with closed forms for products of $α$-$μ$ envelopes. Numerical results show that the DGD bounds closely bracket the exact LCR.

Information Theory.title: Optimal self-orthogonal binary linear codes
Information Theory.summary: We complete the determination of the minimum possible length of eight-dimensional binary self-orthogonal codes with given minimum distance. For dimension nine we give exact values and bounds for minimum distance at most $64$. By exploiting the geometric reformulation of linear codes as multisets of points, we fully redo the classification for dimension at most seven in a simplified and computer-free manner. As a by-product we prove the non-existence of $[93,9,44]_2$ codes and show several divisibility results for putative optimal nine-dimensional binary codes.

Information Theory.title: The information geometry of the Sinkhorn divergence on a Hilbert manifold
Information Theory.summary: The Sinkhorn divergence, the debiased entropic optimal transport cost, determines a metric tensor on probability measures defined along curves, due to Lavenant et al. We construct a real-analytic Hilbert manifold of measures, the smooth stratum, on which this tensor is a weak Riemannian metric, and we continue Eguchi's construction of a geometry from a divergence to the third order. The stratum consists of the measures with a positive Sobolev density on a closed Riemannian manifold, and the strata form a scale whose intersection is the Fréchet manifold of smooth positive densities of Ay. Following it, we characterize the metric through the gradients of mean values: its cotangent form is a spectral reweighting of the Dirichlet form of a Markov chain, so the metric is of the same kind as the Fisher-Rao and the Otto metric, and on the stratum it is bounded by a multiple of the Fisher-Rao metric (but not conversely). At third order, the Sinkhorn divergence is self-dual: both connection forms of Eguchi's construction coincide with the Levi-Civita form of the metric, and the cubic tensor vanishes, as a consequence of the transposition symmetry of the transport problem. On every stratum, the Levi-Civita form is represented, so the stratum has a real-analytic Levi-Civita connection, which on the Fréchet manifold is the connection of Ay and Schwachhöfer.

Information Theory.title: Deep Reinforcement Learning for Blind Passive Beamforming in RIS-Assisted MIMO Systems
Information Theory.summary: Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces (RIS) are a promising solution for improving millimeter-wave (mmWave) communications by controlling signal propagation. Yet, selecting the optimal RIS configuration remains challenging due to the high-dimensional search space and signaling overhead. We propose a Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) framework for blind passive beamforming, where a Deep Q-Learning (DQL) agent learns an adaptive policy to select near-optimal RIS configurations while sounding only few codewords, without channel state information. Results show that our approach outperforms Q-Learning (QL) and conventional baselines in convergence, performance, and overhead reduction.
Information Theory.comment: Accepted at AIxNET 2026. 6 pages. Copyright may be transferred to IEEE after publication, after which this version may no longer be accessible

Information Theory.title: Self-Referential $K$-SAT and the Finite Analogue of Gödel's Incompleteness Theorem
Information Theory.summary:
We study self-reference and solution independence in Boolean $K$-SAT as a finite analogue of Gödel incompleteness. Independence is defined through factorial moments of the solution count. Constant-width random formulas fail this criterion due to correlations among overlapping assignments. At a covering threshold, logarithmic-width random CNFs have a Poisson solution count, with positive probabilities of unsatisfiability and unique satisfiability. Replacing a redundant clause by one falsified by the unique solution yields an unsatisfiable companion preserving the unsigned incidence graph.
  For every permitted local view of a good uniquely satisfiable formula, an unsatisfiable companion preserves that view. Irreducibility defeats deterministic and bounded-error evaluators using $N^c$ clause queries, for fixed $0<c<1$. It establishes a local information obstruction, not an unrestricted time lower bound. For fixed $δ>0$, transcripts of $N^{1-δ}$ queries leave $N-o(N)$ bits of witness entropy. On typical support graphs, expansion yields linear Resolution width, linear PC/PCR and SOS degree, and exponential proof size. Bounds hold for semantic Cutting Planes under a partition condition and for Positivstellensatz with bounded product width, uniformly over unsatisfiable support-preserving signings.
  Structural evidence and the limits of acceleration strategies motivate the self-referential $K$-SAT exhaustive-search hypothesis (SRK-ESH): no uniform deterministic algorithm deciding the promise family achieves a fixed proportional saving in the exponent. This dual-evidence criterion combines intrinsic hardness mechanisms with algorithmic evidence. We interpret this hypothesis as a quantitative projection of the Gödel-style local--global gap. The information obstruction constrains quantum local observation and statistical learning from bounded local information.

Information Theory.title: The Support-Distribution Conditions for MSRD Codes Reduce to a Single Inequality
Information Theory.summary: Byrne, Gluesing-Luerssen, and Ravagnani determined the number of codewords with a prescribed nonzero support in a linear maximum sum-rank distance code whose blocks have a common number of columns. Their formula depends only on the code parameters and the support dimensions. Evaluating it for arbitrary parameters gives a family of necessary nonnegativity conditions for existence. We prove their conjecture that this family is equivalent to the condition at the vector of total dimension $d+1$ obtained by filling the longest blocks first, where $d$ is the distance parameter. The resulting explicit criterion applies over every finite field $\mathbb F_q$, for all row numbers $n_i\leqslant m$ and $1\leqslant d<N$, where $m$ is the common number of columns and $N$ is the total number of rows. It also covers the boundary cases in which this vector fills each of its nonzero blocks completely, not explicitly included in the conjecture's displayed parameter range. The proof uses a generating function and an exchange identity to reduce the problem to vectors obtained by filling the longest blocks first. We then estimate alternating sums of elementary symmetric polynomials, with a separate argument for $q=2$. The dual conditions admit the same reduction. For codes that exist, the joint condition follows from sphere-packing bounds for the code and its dual. An infinite family of parameters satisfies the joint condition but admits no such linear code.

Information Theory.title: Quantum XYZ Stabilizer Codes
Information Theory.summary: Stabilizer codes are often constructed within the Calderbank--Shor--Steane (CSS) framework, where two mutually orthogonal binary classical codes define $X$ and $Z$-type stabilizer generators. While this structure is algebraically convenient, additional non-CSS constraints may help suppress low-weight logical operators and improve decoding performance in the finite-length regime. We thus introduce quantum XYZ stabilizer codes, whose parity-check matrix (PCM) is built from three pairwise orthogonal binary PCMs associated with $X$-, $Y$-, and $Z$-type stabilizer generators. A nontrivial point is that an XYZ code instance is not automatically genuinely non-CSS: the same stabilizer group may admit a CSS generating set. We characterize this collapse, obtaining algebraic and rank conditions for deciding when the $Y$-type checks are redundant and when they define genuinely non-CSS stabilizer constraints. We also derive upper and lower bounds on the quantum minimum distance, including bounds for mixed Pauli logical operators. The novel framework includes a known non-CSS topological code, namely the XYZ$^2$ hexagonal code, and yields also sparse finite-length quantum low-density parity-check (qLDPC) constructions from intersecting-subset and quasi-dyadic code families. Simulations under depolarizing code-capacity noise and quaternary belief propagation decoding show that the proposed XYZ qLDPC instances can outperform representative CSS qLDPC instances with similar finite-length parameters.

Information Theory.title: Improving Energy Efficiency of Uplink RSMA via Rydberg Atomic Quantum Receiver
Information Theory.summary: This paper investigates an uplink rate-splitting multiple access (RSMA) network empowered by a Rydberg atomic quantum receiver (RAQR) to maximize energy efficiency (EE). To overcome the amplitude-only measurement limitation of the considered direct readout RAQR, we devise a phase alignment mechanism that linearizes the received signal while retaining full channel energy, thereby enabling tractable optimization. The resulting non-convex fractional EE problem is transformed via Dinkelbach's method. For IoT scenarios with symmetric rate requirements, we derive exact closed-form power allocation from the Karush-Kuhn-Tucker (KKT) conditions, which yields a globally optimal bisection search with negligible computational latency. For asymmetric rate requirements, we develop a generalized block coordinate descent-based power allocation (BCD-PA) framework that eliminates reliance on expensive interior-point solvers. We further propose a low-complexity paired allocation (LC-Paired) that exploits user pairing and closed-form bandwidth solutions via the Lambert-W function. Simulation results confirm that the KKT-based scheme attains the highest EE, while the BCD-PA offers a flexible complexity-performance trade-off. The LC-Paired scheme drastically reduces computational cost with only moderate EE degradation.

Information Theory.title: Log Density Spectrum Based Decoding of Polar Codes for Channels with Strong Phase Noise
Information Theory.summary: A decoding method is proposed for polar codes under channels with strong phase noise. In contrast to traditional SC decoding, where recursions are performed on scalar soft information such as probabilities, the proposed decoding recurses over probability density functions defined on the phase-noise variable. To make the density-level recursion computationally tractable, we represent each log-density by its spectrum, and derive approximate formulas for the spectrum recursion, therefore, the proposed method is termed log-density spectrum recursion (LDSR). Numerical results are given under strong phase noise and AWGN, showing that a prominent superiority of error performance is achieved by LDSR in comparison with traditional SC and Kalman-based methods.

Information Theory.title: Length Bounds for MDS Algebraic Geometry Codes of Arbitrary Positive Genus
Information Theory.summary: We study the length of maximum distance separable algebraic geometry codes from curves of arbitrary positive genus. For fixed genus, we prove that the asymptotic ratio of the length to the field size is at most $1/2$ when both the dimension and the codimension grow faster than the logarithm of the field size. We also give explicit bounds under logarithmic dimension conditions. The bounds hold in every characteristic and are uniform in the curve and the evaluation set. The proof combines character sums on the Jacobian with an estimate for sums of distinct points.

Information Theory.title: Coded Computing for Dynamic System via Cartesian Products
Information Theory.summary: Coded distributed computing (CDC) mitigates the Shuffle communication bottleneck through coded multicast, but existing schemes with predetermined worker populations do not directly adapt to worker arrivals and disconnections. To address these dynamics, we propose a dynamic CDC scheme that preserves surviving workers' caches and Reduce assignments while exploiting the storage brought by arriving clusters. The model accommodates general MapReduce tasks under a placement that is partly fixed and partly new. The scheme uses Cartesian products of cluster-wise placement delivery arrays (PDAs) for file placement. A delivery-aware greedy algorithm reassigns abandoned Reduce functions, and a Communication Array allows workers with no Reduce function to serve as coded transmitters. For arbitrary feasible disconnections, the scheme's exact communication load is derived. A converse bound under one-shot communication shows that, in the absence of disconnections, the scheme lies within a factor of 2 of the lower bound under these assumptions when new clusters arrive, and within a factor of 4 otherwise.

Information Theory.title: The Maximum Nonlinearity of 8-variable Balanced Boolean Functions is 116
Information Theory.summary: Does there exist an 8-variable balanced Boolean function with nonlinearity 118? This is a famous and long-standing open problem in Boolean functions. In this paper, we give a negative answer to this open problem, and prove that the maximum nonlinearity of balanced Boolean functions in 8 variables is 116, establishing the 8-variable instance of Dobbertin's conjectured recursion for the minimum Walsh peak of balanced functions. Equivalently, the covering radius of the Reed--Muller code RM(1,8) in 0-resilient Boolean functions is 116. We deduce the result by obtaining a quadratic form of polar rank 6, and reducing the problem to the existence of a 6-variable Boolean function with nonlinearity greater than 26 whose Hamming distance to a bent function is between 4 and 6.

Information Theory.title: A Uniform Upper Bound on the Length of MDS Codes from Genus-Two Curves
Information Theory.summary: We study the maximal length of MDS algebraic geometry codes from genus-two curves over finite fields. Let $C_\mathcal{ L}(D,G)$ be such a code over $\mathbb F_q$, with length $n$ and dimension $k$. Assume that $3\leq k\leq n-3$. We prove that $n<(2q+10\sqrt q+16)/3$. This bound holds for every prime power $q$ and for both parities of $k$. It gives a uniform upper bound of $2q/3+O(\sqrt q)$ for the maximal length. The explicit bound is strictly smaller than $q+1$ when $q\geq125$.

Information Theory.title: A Sharp Fisher-Information Inequality for Boolean Pairs: Proof of the Amari--Kobayashi Conjecture
Information Theory.summary: Consider two terminals that observe correlated uniform binary vectors and separately compress their observations to one bit. We prove that, for every blocklength and every correlation parameter in $(-1,1)$, the Fisher information retained by the resulting pair of bits is maximized by matching parity functions of an appropriate degree, thereby resolving a conjecture of Amari and Kobayashi. The proof combines a Fourier-based bound on the derivative of the normalized covariance with a scalar inequality for signed polynomials subject to a global range constraint.

Information Theory.title: Secure Wireless Communications with Flexible Reflectors: Joint Position and Rotation Optimization for Physical Layer Security
Information Theory.summary: By exploiting the spatial selectivity of wireless channels, physical layer security (PLS) protects confidential wireless transmissions. Flexible reflectors (FRs), which are passive metallic plates mounted on movable platforms, offer a low-cost and low-complexity solution for reshaping the propagation environment. However, their potential for secrecy-oriented signal propagation shaping has not been explored. In this paper, we study an FR-aided secure communication over non-line-of-sight links and jointly optimize the positions and rotations of FRs to maximize the secrecy rate under geometric reflection and mutual-blocking constraints. For the single-FR case, we propose a Fibonacci segmentation search (FSS) method, which partitions the feasible region into multiple unimodal intervals and obtains the optimal solution with Fibonacci search over the unimodal intervals. To reduce the computational overhead, we also propose a low-complexity cross-entropy search (CES) method, which employs Gaussian mixture model-based adaptive importance sampling to localize promising search intervals before deterministic refinement. After deriving the blocked placement interval induced by the deployed FRs and integrating it into a sequential deployment scheme, we extend the FSS and CES methods to the multi-FR case. Simulation results show that our proposed FSS method achieves significant secrecy rate performance gains over various benchmark schemes, and our proposed CES method achieves a favorable runtime-performance tradeoff. These results indicate that FRs provide a low-cost and reconfigurable mechanism for PLS.
Information Theory.comment: This work has been submitted to the IEEE for possible publication. 13 pages, 13 figures

Information Theory.title: On Proximity Gaps for One-Point Algebraic Geometric Codes
Information Theory.summary:
Proximity gaps and correlated agreement underpin the soundness of interactive oracle proofs. We establish these properties for general one-point algebraic geometry (AG) codes, extending corresponding results for Reed-Solomon codes. For codes of length $n$ over $\mathbb F_q$ with designed distance $n-m$, write $ρ=m/n$ and fix $ρ\in(0,1)$. For polynomial curves of degree at most $\ell$ and any $0<\varepsilon<1$, we prove correlated agreement with multiplicative slack $\varepsilon$ and soundness $O(\ell(\ell+1)/(\varepsilon q))$ whenever $e\le(1-\varepsilon)(n-m)/2$, with no additional genus penalty. This gives asymptotically good AG code families from Garcia--Stichtenoth tower of unbounded length over a fixed field with soundness bounds independent of $n$, beyond the RS restriction $n\le q$. We also establish mutual correlated agreement up to radius $(1-\sqrtρ-η)n$, with soundness $O(\ell n/(η^3q))$ for $0<η<1-\sqrtρ$. Our half designed distance proof combines auxiliary divisors, simultaneous Berlekamp-Welch interpolation, and error-incidence counting to obtain a common polynomial representation without a Polishchuk-Spielman divisibility lemma.
  Finally, two counterexamples on the Garcia-Stichtenoth tower show limitations beyond half the minimum distance, at radii below the Johnson bound and with positive slack. The first requires a positive constant soundness lower bound independent of $q$ and $n$, precluding a uniform $O(1/q)$ guarantee throughout the Johnson regime. The second fixes the field and lets the relative gap above half distance tend to zero while ruling out correlated agreement for every soundness parameter $σ<1$, with positive limiting rate and relative error radius.

Information Theory.title: Bregman projections and partition design for accelerating finite Markov chains
Information Theory.summary: We study Gibbs averaging of finite Markov chains with a prescribed stationary distribution $π$. Given a transition matrix $P$ and the Gibbs kernel $G$ induced by a state-space partition, we prove that $GPG$ is an information projection for every admissible Bregman generator $φ$, with divergences defined using transition probabilities relative to $π$. A Pythagorean identity characterizes this projection and recovers the relative entropy and weighted Frobenius cases. A dual characterization identifies $GPG$ as a kernel closest to stationarity among those with the same projection chain as $P$; for relative entropy, it maximizes the entropy rate. The identities also give monotonicity under partition coarsening. For every reversible ergodic baseline $P$, Gibbs averaging cannot increase the squared weighted Frobenius distance to stationarity at any positive integer time, and the inequality is strict unless $P=GPG$. The corresponding mixing time therefore cannot increase. To choose the partition, we identify the divergence of $G$ from stationarity as the exact worst-case divergence of $GPG$ over all $π$-stationary baselines $P$. This objective depends only on the block masses. We give an exact algorithm for concave block costs, including those arising from relative entropy and power generators $φ(u)=u^p$ with $1<p<2$, and a greedy approximation algorithm with a provable guarantee for $p>2$. For power generators $φ(u)=u^p$ with $p>1$, the objective is proportional to Tsallis entropy of order $2-p$: its minimization favors imbalanced block masses when $1<p<2$ and balanced block masses when $p>2$, while all $k$-block partitions have the same objective value when $p=2$. A numerical experiment compares the resulting projected chains with a local Metropolis sampler on a multi-modal $π$.

Information Theory.title: Pair-Dependent Judge Errors Change the Minimax Rate of Semantic Entropy
Information Theory.summary: Semantic entropy, the entropy of the meanings among a language model's sampled answers, is estimated from the verdicts of a judge that declares pairs of answers equivalent or not, and automatic judges err in ways that depend on the answers they compare. The existing minimax theory covers only judges whose false-equivalence probability is the same for all pairs. We model a known judge that declares two answers with meanings $a$ and $b$ equivalent with probability $q+ΔM_{ab}$, for a symmetric matrix $M$ and $q$ bounded away from $0$ and $1$, and show that for three meanings the rate is set by tree statistics on four answers, while on an open set of channels the consistency threshold is set by trees on five. For every channel in an explicit open class, the minimax squared risk is of order $N^{-1/3}$ with $N=n^4Δ^6$ on polynomial weak windows on which $n^5Δ^8$ exceeds a multiple of $\log n$, and of order $\min\{1,N^{-1/3}\}$ on every polynomial weak window when the tree functions on at most four vertices are injective. The exponent comes from a cubic degeneracy at the equitable point. On an open set of channels in the class, the four-vertex tree functions take equal values at two distributions with different entropies. For such a channel, on every polynomial weak window, the minimax risk is of the order of the sum of $\min\{1,N^{-1/3}\}$ and a term that decays exponentially in $n^5Δ^8$, so no estimator is consistent while $n^5Δ^8$ stays bounded, even as $N\to\infty$. For $Δ=n^{-β}$ with $β>1/2$, channels of the class with injective four-vertex tree functions allow consistent estimation exactly for $β<2/3$, and the channels of this open set exactly for $β<5/8$, at which the risk exponent drops from $1/12$ to $0$. Computer-assisted certificates show that both kinds of channels occur on open sets.

Information Theory.title: Optimal Universal Coding of Integers
Information Theory.summary: Universal coding of integers (UCI) provides prefix codes for positive integers such that, for every nonincreasing source distribution $P$, the average codeword length under $P$ stays within $K$ times $\max\{1,H(P)\}$. For a given UCI $\mathcal{C}$, the smallest such constant $K$ is called the minimum expansion factor of $\mathcal{C}$, denoted $C_{\mathcal{C}}^{*}$. Let $C^{*}\triangleq \inf \{C_{\mathcal{C}}^{*}\}$ over all UCIs. A UCI attaining $C^{*}$, or a family of UCIs attaining $C^{*}$ in the limit, is called optimal. It is currently known that $2\le C^{*}\le 2.0386$. In this paper, we construct a family of one-point plus uniform-tail distributions and prove that, for every UCI, a distribution in this family attains the worst-case ratio; thus, the family is least favorable for the UCI problem. We further establish an inequality, called the \emph{UCI inequality}, which plays the same role for UCI as the Kraft inequality does for prefix codes: for any real number $B\ge 1$, it decides whether $B$ lies below or above $C^*$. The UCI inequality gives an equivalent definition of $C^*$. By numerical computation, we determine $C^* = 2.00012475703610197861701176297579886254\cdots$, the first $38$ decimal digits being certified. Once $C^*$ is known, we can theoretically construct the optimal UCI.

Information Theory.title: Phase Retrieval of Bandlimited Signals Using a Morlet Wavelet and an Admissible Companion
Information Theory.summary: In this paper, we demonstrate that complex bandlimited signals can be uniquely recovered (up to a global phase factor) from two families of wavelet transform magnitudes, sampled at twice the Nyquist rate in two frequency bins. These families come from translations of the fixed dilated Morlet wavelet and a fixed companion wavelet. The companion wavelet admits an augmented Morlet--Gaussian representation. We rewrite the two families as two modulated Gaussian convolution measurements of an auxiliary bandlimited signal. Using a Gaussian convolution uniqueness result, we prove that samples on \((4B)^{-1}\mathbb{Z}\) determine every signal in \(PW_B^2\) (up to a global phase factor). Compared with earlier wavelet phase retrieval results, our approach requires significantly fewer sampling points.

Information Theory.title: Communication and Privacy Trade-Offs in Distributed Storage With Shared Secret Keys
Information Theory.summary: We study distributed storage over public communication channels where privacy is realized using shared secret keys. Specifically, a user wishes to store a file across $L$ servers such that any subset of at least $t$ servers can reconstruct the file, while any subset of at most $z$ colluding servers learns no more than a fraction $α$ of the file. Unlike classical secret-sharing models that assume secure communication channels between the user and each server, we consider a setting where all transmissions occur over a public channel and the user shares an individual secret key of length $n$ bits with each server. For a fixed key length $n$, we characterize the trade-off between the privacy leakage parameter $α$ and the maximum file size that can be securely stored. Additionally, we determine the minimum local randomness, public communication, and storage required to achieve this optimal trade-off.
Information Theory.comment: A preliminary version of this work was presented at the 2023 Allerton Conference on Communication, Control, and Computing

Information Theory.title: Sensing Fast and Distant Targets in Overspread Channels with Zak-OTFS and Modular Arithmetic
Information Theory.summary: Delay-Doppler (DD) modulations, such as Zak-transform-based orthogonal time frequency space (Zak-OTFS) modulation, represent the channel as a sparse set of delay and Doppler shifts, which makes them well suited for radar sensing. Sensing with a single DD frame, however, is unambiguous only when the channel spread factor, i.e., the product of the delay and Doppler spreads, is below one. Long-range mobility scenarios, including drones, airplanes, low Earth orbit (LEO) satellites, and underwater acoustic links, typically violate this crystallization condition, so that a single frame aliases the target delays, Doppler shifts, or both. Existing methods add a time-frequency pilot to a conventional DD frame and resolve the aliasing in only one dimension. We propose a frame design that combines multiple DD bases with different delay and Doppler periods, which together cover an overspread channel, on the same bandwidth and frame size. For two frames, we show that modular arithmetic on the wrapped peak positions uniquely recovers each target by pairing the peaks through their common projection and their gains, and we derive the condition under which this pairing is ambiguous. We implement the design with two superimposed Zak-OTFS frames and propose two receivers: dual-frame sensing (DS), which performs the joint detection directly, and DS with cross-pilot cancellation (DS-XC), which additionally cancels the cross-pilot interference, re-estimates the gains by joint least squares, and removes ghost targets. Both receivers keep a detection rate close to one as the spread factor grows, and DS-XC also achieves the lowest false-alarm rate and channel normalized mean squared error (NMSE). In a 100 km drone scenario, DS-XC detects 98% of the targets, compared with 81% for the best baseline, with a complexity that grows near-linearly with the time-bandwidth product for a fixed number of targets.

Information Theory.title: Time-Switching Energy-Harvesting Quantum Relay-Assisted FSO Communication with Displaced Squeezed Signaling
Information Theory.summary: This paper investigates a quantum relay-assisted free-space optical (FSO) communication system in which a decode-and-forward relay is powered by time-switching optical energy harvesting and forwards the decoded information using displaced squeezed signaling (DSS). To obtain a physically con sistent description of turbulence-induced loss for non-classical signaling, each hop is modeled as a pure-loss bosonic chan nel whose random transmissivity follows a truncated Gamma Gamma law, i.e., the Gamma-Gamma irradiance conditioned on the physically admissible range of a transmittance. Under this channel, coherent states remain pure, whereas squeezed states are mapped to mixed Gaussian states. Under Helstrom-optimal detection, the average error of the coherent hop is derived in exact Laplace-series form. For the DSS hop, we derive the output states, a closed-form Gaussian fidelity with rigorous two sided bounds on the Helstrom error, and prove the existence of a loss-aware optimal photon partition. Furthermore, we prove that optimized squeezing preserves both the turbulence-induced diversity order and the leading asymptotic constant of coherent relaying, so that its benefit is a finite-photon-budget effect, and that an interior throughput-optimal harvesting fraction exists. A covariance-preserving benchmark with an exact series representation yields an analytical upper bound on the achievable throughput whose absolute gap vanishes as the relay photon budget grows. Numerical results based on the exact mixed-state Helstrom error quantify the benefit of squeezing and the regime in which it is useful.

Probability.title: JT gravity as a conformal scaling limit of random flat combinatorial disks
Probability.summary:
We prove that flat Jackiw--Teitelboim (JT) gravity arises as a conformal scaling limit of random flat combinatorial disks. We give a clean criterion, formulated in terms of branching explorations, for a discrete model to converge to this conjecturally universal limit. For simplicity, we apply this criterion to a Boltzmann ensemble of disks with rectilinear boundary, defined by summing over combinatorial types and integrating over lengths. As the length of a distinguished side tends to infinity, the rescaled surface converges in law to a continuum random surface prescribed by Ferrari's path-integral formulation of JT gravity. Convergence is in the topology of smooth convergence of the conformal factors on compact subsets of the interior when uniformizing in a fixed domain; the limiting conformal factor is described by a harmonic Gaussian field closely related to holomorphic multiplicative chaos.
  The crux is a branching exploration of flat JT gravity whose lengths evolve as conditioned Cauchy processes and whose unexplored components are conditionally independent. We construct this exploration using a conformal welding theorem proved in a companion paper, and show that it is the scaling limit of Budd's row-by-row exploration of the discrete disks, analogous to the peeling of random planar maps. Under a tightness condition, our criterion upgrades this convergence to a conformal scaling limit for the discrete disks. Other natural combinatorial disk models admit analogous first-row recursions, providing a route to their scaling limits.

Probability.title: A self-normalized law of the iterated logarithm for Rademacher random multiplicative functions
On Zeros and Algorithms for Disordered Systems II: The Antiferromagnetic Ising Model up to Kesten-Stigum
Probability.summary:
We give the first polynomial-time algorithm to estimate the partition function of the antiferromagnetic Ising model on the uniformly random $d$-regular graph to arbitrarily high accuracy for all inverse temperatures up to the Kesten-Stigum threshold. This is the entire regime in which the model is "replica symmetric," and is conjectured to be optimal for polynomial-time counting and sampling. To achieve our algorithmic result, we establish the absence of Fisher zeros for the partition function in a constant-width strip around the interval from $0$ up to the Kesten-Stigum threshold, with high probability over the randomness of the input graph.
  AI Disclosure: The overarching vision and proof architecture were developed solely by the authors without AI input. GPT 5.5 Pro was used, with extensive guidance from the authors, for only a few minor technical aspects of the proof. The authors independently verified correctness and wrote everything by hand. We take full responsibility for its contents. A more detailed statement can be found in Section 1.2.

Probability.title: Nearly-Optimal Time-Sample Trade-off in Consensus Dynamics
Probability.summary:
How does the number of sampled opinions affect the time required to reach consensus in distributed consensus dynamics? We study the synchronous $h$-\textsf{Majority}, in which every node independently samples $h$ nodes uniformly at random with replacement in each round and adopts a most frequent sampled opinion, breaking ties uniformly at random. We show that $h$-\textsf{Majority} achieves the nearly-optimal trade-off between the sample size and the consensus time, among a broad class of consensus dynamics. In particular, we prove the following results.
  For every sample size $h \ge 3$ and for every initial configuration, we prove that the process reaches consensus with high probability within $\widetilde{O}\left(1+\min\left\{\frac{1}{\min\{h^2p_{\max},1\}},\frac{\sqrt{n}}{h}\right\}\right)$ rounds, where $n$ is the number of nodes and $p_{\max}$ is the largest initial fraction of nodes supporting any single opinion. This is the first bound on the consensus time for $h$-\textsf{Majority} that holds for every $h\ge3$ and every initial configuration.
  When the initially most popular opinion has a sufficiently large lead over every other opinion, we show that all nodes adopt this opinion with high probability within $O(\log n/\min\{h^2p_{\max},1\})$ rounds.
  We establish a matching lower bound up to polylogarithmic factors for any fixed update rule that treats all opinions symmetrically and that selects either a sampled opinion or the node's current opinion.

Probability.title: Power Adjusting Games Under Block-Dependent Pool Payout Schemes
