Probability.summary: Advanced power adjusting block withholding attacks such as PAW and T-PAW have been analyzed so far under a global-reset version of the proportional scheme (GRP), which is rarely used in practice. In this paper, we analyze T-PAW, which contains FAW and PAW as special cases, under the block-dependent payout schemes deployed in practice: Pay-Per-Last-N-Shares (PPLNS), round-based Proportional (PROP) and exponential-decay (EXP). We derive the revenue ratios analytically, by renewal arguments for PPLNS and through the stationary carry process of an open round for PROP and EXP. We further introduce Power Adjusting Hopping (PAH), where an adversary of any size adjusts its power allocation towards the pool according to the blockwork age of the round without withholding any block, and derive its revenue ratios under PROP and EXP. We show that GRP misestimates the T-PAW gain in a scheme-dependent direction: it overstates the gain under PROP up to an order of magnitude and understates it under EXP for the original slush decay rate. PROP is highly vulnerable to PAH, while EXP faces a trade-off: a slow decay invites PAH and a fast decay invites T-PAW. PPLNS is the least vulnerable scheme: it is immune to PAH and it mitigates, but does not eliminate, T-PAW. All analytical results are verified by Monte Carlo simulations.

Probability.title: Convergence of a drainage network model with branching to the Brownian net
Probability.summary: We consider a drainage network model represented by a system of coalescing random walks exhibiting long range dependence before coalescence. This model was introduced by Gangopadhyay et. al. [GRS04] and Coletti et. al. [CFD09] proved its convergence to the Brownian web under diffusive scaling. Santos et. al. [SVZ24] considered a branching version of this model where branching occurs with low probabilities varying with the scaling parameter and showed that any sub-sequential limit contains a copy of the Brownian net. It was conjectured that the limit is indeed the Brownian net. In this work we prove this conjecture. Further, compared to [SVZ24], we explore the question of scaling limit in a wider spectrum of scaling regime. This work contributes to the broader understanding of the basin of attraction of the Brownian net.

Probability.title: Quantitative sub-ballisticity of self-avoiding walk on $\mathbb{Z}^d$
Probability.summary: We prove quantitative sub-ballisticity for the self-avoiding walk on the lattice $\mathbb{Z}^d$, $d\geq 2$. Namely, we obtain an explicit exponential rate of decay for the probability that a self-avoiding walk of length $n$ reaches distance at least $vn$, in terms of $v>0$. As a consequence, we show that the displacement of an $n$-step self-avoiding walk is at most $n/\exp(c\log^* n)$ with very high probability. Previously, only a non-quantitative $o(n)$ bound was known from the work of Duminil-Copin and Hammond. Along the way, we show that at criticality the partition function of bridges of length $n$ is on average bounded by $C/\log\log n$, which we believe to be of independent interest. Our approach is based on a quantitative analysis of the original nonconstructive proof of Duminil-Copin and Hammond using ideas from proof theory.

Probability.title: The Ornstein$-$Uhlenbeck process on $\mathscr P_2$ with a volatility operator
Probability.summary: We analyze diffusion processes ${(μ_t)}_{t\geq 0}$ on the $2$-Wasserstein space $\mathscr P_2$ over $\mathbb R^d$, which can be classified as Ornstein--Uhlenbeck processes by means of their Fukushima decomposition. Characteristically for this class, $ | μ_t|_2^2-|μ_0|_2^2-2ct+2\int_0 ^t|μ_s|_2^2\,d s,\, t\geq 0,$ is a martingale, where $c\in(0,\infty)$ is a constant and $|μ_t|_2:=(\int_{\mathbb R^d}x^{\text{T}} xμ_t(d x ))^{1/2}$ denotes the second moment. Making a particular choice from this class, we obtain a process ${(μ_t)}_{t\geq 0}$ such that all moments exist and ${μ_t(θ)}-{μ_0(θ)}-\int_0 ^tμ_s\big(Δθ-\langle \text{id}_{\mathbb R^d},\nabla θ\rangle\big)d s$, $t\geq 0$, is a martingale for each multivariate polynomial $θ:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R$.

Probability.title: Zero-freeness for Random Regular Graphs up to the Replica Symmetry Breaking Threshold
Probability.summary:
We study antiferromagnetic spin systems on random regular graphs through the lens of the phase transitions characterized by the complex zeros of the partition function. Our motivating examples include the hardcore model and the antiferromagnetic Potts model (including proper $q$-colorings at $β=0$). For both models on random $d$-regular graphs, we establish, with high probability over the graph, zero-free regions throughout the interior of the replica-symmetric regime. Asymptotically, this regime extends up to tree occupation density $$α< α_{\mathrm{RSB}}(d) = (2\log d - 2\log\log d + 2 - 2\log 2 + o_d(1))/d$$ for the hardcore model and up to degree $$d < d_{\mathrm{RSB}}(q) = (2q-1)\log q - 2\log 2 + o_q(1)$$ for proper $q$-colorings.
  Leveraging the standard algorithmic implications of zero-freeness, we obtain deterministic polynomial-time algorithms that multiplicatively approximate the corresponding partition functions at fixed rational parameters throughout this regime, with high probability over the graph. Our algorithmic guarantees significantly improve upon prior work and extend beyond the parameter ranges reached by previously known search algorithms.
  To establish our results, we first develop reinforced small subgraph conditioning, which resolves short-cycle fluctuations in the complex plane by lifting classical small subgraph conditioning on random regular graphs to random holomorphic functions. Second, we overcome the standard second-moment barrier caused by the exponential blowup of the bare second moment inside the replica-symmetric phase, by showing that replica symmetry implies a nonpositive Bethe functional and upgrading planted overlap concentration to an exponentially small bound, which enables a typical-graph truncation that controls complex second moments up to the replica symmetry breaking threshold.

Probability.title: Random Matching Between Distinct Distributions in Two Dimensions
Probability.summary:
Given two independent $n$-point samples drawn from possibly distinct probability distributions on a compact 2-dimensional surface, we minimize the total squared distance over all perfect bipartite matchings. Under regularity assumptions, the expected matching cost minus $n$ times the squared 2-Wasserstein distance between the sampling distributions grows logarithmically with $n$. We determine this difference up to an additive $o(1)$ error, including the dependence of the logarithmic coefficient and constant term on geometry and sampling distributions, and establish the existence of a universal constant shared by these formulas.
  Our analysis expresses the expected matching cost in terms of the cost of transporting a heat-smoothed sample back to its original points. The reductions giving this relation hold in every dimension and for general costs under suitable assumptions, with consequences beyond the setting studied here. In two dimensions, the relation is exact up to an additive $o(1)$ error, so determining the matching cost amounts to evaluating the smoothing cost with the same accuracy. We obtain this evaluation by subdividing the domain and exploiting cancellations between the sample and its own smoothing.

Probability.title: Mutant invasion in stochastic individual-based models with cyclic resident dynamics
Probability.summary: When a resident community oscillates, can a rare mutant invade, and with which probability? We study a multitype birth-and-death process with interactions, in which population sizes are of the order of a carrying capacity $K$, and whose large-population limit, as $K\to\infty$, has a hyperbolically stable limit cycle for the $D-1$ resident types. We introduce a single individual of a new type. We prove that, as long as the mutant population is smaller than $\varepsilon K$ for a small $\varepsilon>0$, the resident population sizes divided by $K$ stay close to a moving point of the cycle, whose asymptotic phase moves by at most $O(\varepsilon)$ per period. We deduce that, for large $K$, the mutant dies out quickly if its growth rate averaged over one period, $f(\bar{\mathbf n})$, is negative, and that it invades with positive probability, in a time close to $\ln K/f(\bar{\mathbf n})$, if $f(\bar{\mathbf n})$ is positive. This justifies a criterion used heuristically in ecology for decades. The invasion probability, unlike $f(\bar{\mathbf n})$, depends on the phase of the cycle at which the mutant arises. We give it explicitly through Kendall's formula, and show that its average over the cycle, weighted by the birth rate of the mutant, equals $f(\bar{\mathbf n})$. In predator-prey, competitive and mutualistic examples, the invasion probability varies by a factor between $2$ and $600$ along the cycle, and individual-based simulations agree quantitatively with the theory. After invasion, the oscillations may vanish, persist on a cycle of higher dimension, or give way to chaotic coexistence.

Probability.title: The velocity is deterministic in random walk in 2-valued i.i.d. random environment
Probability.summary: We prove that the limiting velocity for (nearest-neighbour) random walk in i.i.d. random environment is deterministic when the local environment is supported on two points. No ellipticity is assumed. The proof uses a clever adaption (suggested by ChatGPT) of coupling arguments previously developed by the authors. It extends to i.i.d. environments where the local environments are mixtures of two such points.

Probability.title: Sums of two dependent uniform random variables: a characterization by joint tail bounds
Probability.summary: Which laws can the sum of two uniform random variables have when nothing is known about how they depend on each other? For three or more uniform summands, convex order gives the answer; for two it does not, and the question has been open. We show that the attainable laws are exactly those that satisfy a family of explicit joint bounds on sums of tail probabilities, one bound for each finite set of thresholds. For laws with a density at most one, convex order alone decides. For densities at most two, convex order implies the simplest of the joint bounds, and the constant two cannot be raised for single-threshold bounds. The number of thresholds a law needs is set by the spacing of its atoms, not by how many atoms it has.
Probability.comment: 25 pages, 1 table; 8-page supplementary material as an ancillary file. Code: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23231387. Companion paper: arXiv:2610.30058. v2: cites the companion paper by its arXiv identifier and states the two companion results used; code, data and results unchanged

Probability.title: Sampling Sphere Packings with Continuum Glauber Dynamics
Probability.summary:
Continuum Glauber dynamics is a spatial birth-death process whose stationary distribution is a Gibbs distribution. We establish a spectral gap for Continuum Glauber dynamics applied to Gibbs point processes with repulsive pair potentials, a well-known special case of which is the hard sphere model. For arbitrary-range repulsive pair potentials, we show that a continuous version of Spectral Independence suffices to establish a spectral gap. This extends the regime of activity for which Continuum Glauber dynamics is known to mix, yielding a simple efficient sampling algorithm for arbitrary-range pair potentials that matches the known efficient sampling regime for finite-range pair potentials currently based on specialized algorithms. As a consequence, we also improve the threshold up to which packings of fixed size/density can be efficiently sampled from a bounded domain, the first improvement since Kannan, Mahoney and Montenegro (2003).
  To prove these results, we develop continuous analogs of Spectral Independence and negative fields localization. We show that a stronger variant of zero-freeness implies Spectral Independence, which in turn allows us to run the localization scheme to boost the spectral gap of Continuum Glauber dynamics from smaller activity to larger activity. While this follows the high-level blueprint of Chen and Eldan (2022) for the discrete setting, we have to address several novel difficulties due to the continuous setting. Notably, we avoid discretization in the algorithm and the analysis and work directly in the continuous setting.
Probability.comment: 85 pages, 1 figure. Fixed typos, streamlined proofs and added references. Extended main result from R^d to complete separable metric spaces. Accepted to SODA 2027

Probability.title: Exponential Convergence of the Lifted Gradient Flow of the Bass Functional
Probability.summary: We establish multidimensional exponential convergence of the lifted Bass gradient flow in martingale optimal transport. Let $μ\le_{cx}ν$ be an irreducible pair, with compact convex target support, source support strictly inside the target support, and target density bounded above and bounded away from zero almost everywhere on its interior. For every bounded $σ(X)$-measurable initial state, the flow converges exponentially in $L^2$ to the global minimizer with the prescribed mean, and the functional value gap decays exponentially. Both bounds hold at every nonnegative time with the exact initial errors as prefactors. The quantitative step is strong convexity on sets with a common $L^\infty$ bound and a fixed mean. We prove it by interpolating entropic endpoint potentials, using two conditional copies to cancel the unknown potential increment, and obtaining a Hessian lower bound uniform in the regularization parameter. Removing the regularization yields curvature for the original functional; the known qualitative theory supplies a common bound for the orbit. This extends the one-dimensional exponential-convergence result of Backhoff-Veraguas, Pammer, and Schachermayer. The main result is formalized in Lean 4. AI was used in preparing the paper (see Section 8).
Probability.comment: 38 pages, 8 figures (4 in each language). Complete English version followed by the Russian version. Lean 4 verification sources included as ancillary material

Probability.title: Terminal Localization of Empirical Reverse Diffusions under Singular Score Errors
Probability.summary: For a finite empirical target, the exact reverse diffusion is driven toward training points by an attraction whose strength diverges as the forward noising time decreases to zero. We study whether this terminal localization persists under progressively measurable score errors that may themselves be singular. For reverse Ornstein--Uhlenbeck diffusions, from an arbitrary initial law and under a deterministic error envelope \(E\) imposed along the perturbed trajectory satisfying \(t\int_t^T E(σ)/σ\,dσ\to0\), we prove almost-sure convergence to a training point, together with explicit uniform bounds on a terminal window with probability arbitrarily close to one. Every training point has positive terminal probability, although the terminal selection probabilities need not match the empirical weights. The results cover power-law errors \(E(t)=O(t^{-γ})\), \(0<γ<1\), including infinite squared-error energy. For suitable errors in this range, the exact and perturbed full path laws can be mutually singular while their terminal laws share the same finite support. For suitable switched perturbations at the critical scale \(t^{-1}\), arbitrarily small positive amplitudes can produce a nonzero terminal displacement with arbitrarily high probability. These results quantify stochastic robustness of empirical terminal attraction without requiring absolute continuity of the full path laws.

Probability.title: A Note on a Result of Chen Li: the Thinning Problem via the Kernel Method
Probability.summary: Recently, C. Li posted a preprint that resolves the fractional version of Talagrand's discrete convexity problem. In this note, we use the method of C. Li to answer another problem of Talagrand.

Probability.title: Limiting ESD for a weighted sample covariance matrix
Probability.summary: We study the empirical spectral distribution (ESD) of the random matrix $M_N=\frac1N\sum_{i=1}^N f(|πY_i|^2)\,Y_iY_i^\top$, where $π$ is a rank $k$ orthogonal projector on $\R^p$, $Y_1,\dots,Y_N$ are i.i.d. standard Gaussian vectors, and $k\to \infty$, $p/N\to γ$. We here assume that $f(x)=g(x/k)$ for some function $g$ discontinuous at $x=1$. We show that the asymptotic ESD is characterized by a Marchenko--Pastur equation, independently of $k$. We also show that the result extends to sub Gaussian random vectors $Y_i$ and to the case where the projector is replaced with a more general weight $φ(Y_i)$. Last, in the Gaussian case, we study the emergence of outliers due to the weighting.

Probability.title: Symmetries and exact solutions of stochastic differential equations: the CIR model
Probability.summary: It is well known that in the celebrated Cox-Ingersoll-Ross process for interest rates there exists a critical relation among the model parameters. In the present work, we explain this critical relation by studying the symmetries of the stochastic differential equation and compute the solution of the model using this symmetry. In this way we also recover results of a recent paper where this property has been studied within a broader context by analyzing the relationships among the symmetries of stochastic differential equations and their corresponding forward Kolmogorov equations.

Probability.title: Ricci curvature of semigroup walks on graphs and generator representations
Probability.summary: We present an operator-theoretic framework for the Ollivier--Ricci curvature of (one-parameter families of) random walks generated by positive semigroups on graphs. On a metrically complete graph $(G,d)$ that is $d$-locally finite, we introduce a class of admissible semigroup random walks whose infinitesimal first-order approximation is itself a random walk. We prove that the Ollivier--Ricci curvature of an admissible semigroup random walk is well-defined and completely determined by its first-order approximation. We then establish a variational representation of the curvature of random walks in terms of a notion of the initial-time generator. This representation applies in particular to admissible semigroup random walks. Finally, we use this representation to define an operator-theoretic Ollivier--Ricci curvature for operators acting on spaces of functions over general metric spaces and establish sufficient conditions for well-definedness. This framework contains, in particular, Markovian random walks associated with discrete Laplacians.
Probability.comment: 20 pages. Comments and suggestions are welcomed

Probability.title: Classification of commutation relation for multi-chordal SLE
Probability.summary:
We classify the linear solution spaces of the chordal Belavin--Polyakov--Zamolodchikov (BPZ) equations, which arise in Dubédat's commutation relations for multiple Schramm--Loewner evolutions (SLE). Without imposing growth conditions, we determine the subspaces selected by successive conformal Ward identities and their exact dimensions. For every $κ>0$ and BPZ spectral parameter $λ\in\mathbb{R}$, we determine the spectrum and Jordan structure of the translation operator. When $λ=0$ and $κ\in(0,8)$, we further determine all admissible scaling exponents and the dimensions of the corresponding translation-invariant solution spaces. A triangular change of derivative coordinates yields a first-order system of rational Knizhnik--Zamolodchikov type, allowing us to represent the Ward operators explicitly and reduce the classification to finite-dimensional linear algebra.
  For $2N$ boundary points and $κ\in(0,8)$, translation-invariant BPZ solutions with $λ=0$ and the homogeneity required by Möbius covariance automatically satisfy the third Ward identity and the usual power-law bound. This recovers, under weaker assumptions, the Catalan dimension formula previously established by Flores and Kleban. At $κ=8$, the third Ward identity imposes an additional constraint when $N\ge2$, but the full Möbius-covariant solution space still has Catalan dimension, establishing completeness of the partition functions constructed from uniform spanning trees. Finally, at $κ=4$ and $λ>0$, we construct an explicit basis of positive BPZ solutions and identify its elements as partition functions for level lines of a Gaussian free field with suitable harmonic means.
Probability.comment: 49 pages, 3 figures. v2: Added a Section 2 overview, Coulomb gas constructions (Section 3.1-3.2), multi-time martingale details in Appendix A, an alternative proof for Proposition 2.12 (Remark B.9). Main theorems unchanged

Probability.title: The German Tank Problem & Navigating by Scent
Probability.summary: A robot searching for the source of an odor must eventually answer a notably hard question: have I arrived? Near the source, concentration gradients homogenize, turbulence corrupts the signal, and a small robot often lacks the positional accuracy to map the plume. Here, we describe a lightweight remedy inspired by a World War II statistics conundrum: the German tank problem. To approximate German armament production, Allied analysts developed an estimator based on serial numbers from captured tanks. Analogously, we use the same procedure over sampled chemical sensor readings from a robot to create estimates for the peak concentration of an odor plume, and therefore the odor's source. Treating each sensor reading as an observation, our unbiased estimator needs only a running maximum and a sample counter. A confidence bound turns both numbers into a principled rule that the robot or UAV can use to determine whether it should keep searching for the odor source. We derive the estimator and its bound, demonstrate its sample efficiency, and examine its robustness even when its assumptions fail. Finally, we summarize the estimator's role as the termination criterion for olfactory navigation.

Probability.title: Consumption-Investment Problem in Rank-Based Models
Probability.summary: We study a consumption-investment problem in a multi-asset market where the returns follow a generic rank-based model. Our main results are an HJB equation with Neumann boundary conditions for the value function, together with a corresponding verification theorem. The control problem is nonstandard due to the discontinuous nature of the coefficients in rank-based models, requiring a bespoke approach of independent mathematical interest. The special case of first-order models, prescribing constant drift and diffusion coefficients for the ranked returns, admits explicit solutions when the investor (a) is unconstrained, (b) abides by open market constraints or (c) is fully invested in the market. The explicit optimal strategies in all cases are related to the celebrated solution to Merton's problem, despite case (b) being intractable in the classic Merton setting.
Probability.comment: 13 pages; Forthcoming in SIAM Journal on Financial Mathematics

Probability.title: Optimal subtrees of finite metric graphs
Probability.summary: We consider a metric graph analog of a classical extremal problem for Riemann surfaces studied by Teichmüller, Jenkins, Strebel, and others. In particular, we prove that on any finite metric graph with a marked point, there is a unique open subtree which maximizes a metric graph analog of the reduced modulus, and we also give an equivalent characterization of this optimal subtree in terms of balanced harmonic measures.
Probability.comment: 13 pages. No AI tools were used

Probability.title: Packing and covering random trees
Probability.summary:
We study the sizes of optimal packings and coverings of conditioned branching processes by balls with growing radii. We find a universal limiting constant, and thereby establish universality of packing and covering numbers across different scales and different offspring distributions.
  To be precise, for $μ$ an offspring distribution with mean $1$ and finite variance $σ^2$ we let $T_n$ be a Bienaymé tree with offspring distribution $μ$ conditioned to have size $n$. We prove that the packing number (resp. covering number) of $T_n$ with balls of radii $1\ll γ_n \ll n^{1/2}$ is asymptotically equivalent to $\mathfrak{C} n /(σ^2 γ_n^2)$ (resp. $\mathfrak{C} n /(4σ^2 γ_n^2)$), for a universal constant $\mathfrak{C}$.
  We also show that the order of limits can be exchanged and that the same limit occurs when we first consider the limiting covering number of $T_n$ by balls of fixed radius $R$, and thereafter let $R$ tend to $\infty$.
  We then extend these results to the Brownian continuum random tree conditioned to have mass $1$. For this model, we prove that the packing (resp. covering) number with balls of radii $\varepsilon$ are asymptotically equivalent to $\mathfrak{C}/\varepsilon^2$ (resp. $\mathfrak{C}/(4\varepsilon^2)$), for the same constant $\mathfrak{C}$, in contrast with a conjecture by Aldous.
  Finally, our results answer a question by Devroye, Eide and Pralat on the asymptotic burning number of mean $1$ finite variance Bienaymé trees of size $n$, by showing that it lies between $(c+o(1)) n^{1/3}$ and $(2c+o(1))n^{1/3}$ with high probability, for a constant $c$ that only depends on the offspring variance.

Probability.title: An approximate zero bias transformation for random sums: Applications to sampling with outliers, auto insurance, and generative AI
Probability.summary: We develop $L^1$ bounds for the difference between a test function of a random sum and a standard normal random variable, where the summands are assumed to be independent but not necessarily identically distributed. The bounds are obtained through a new version of the approximate zero bias transformation specifically developed for random sums. Although the identical distribution assumption is relaxed, the bounds are of order $1/\sqrt{n}$, matching the order of existing bounds in the literature under the same distributional assumption on the number of summands. The main results are then applied to three real-world settings: random sums obtained from simple random sampling with outliers, total insurance claims, and generative AI response times.

Probability.title: Gaussian and non-Gaussian limits for the total edge-length of random directional nearest-neighbour graphs
Probability.summary: We study planar random spatial graphs defined by inserting an edge between every point of a homogeneous Poisson process on the unit square and a nearest-neighbour within a fixed cone of directions (if there is such a point). We prove large-sample distributional limit theorems for the total Euclidean edge length of the graph, where the limit distribution is either Gaussian (due to contributions from the bulk) or, when one or both of the boundaries of the cone of directions align with the edges of the square, a convolution of Gaussian with a non-Gaussian law arising from boundary effects due to long edges near a boundary. This work extends previously known cases, including the ordinary nearest-neighbour graph (full cone of directions), where the Gaussian limit theorem was obtained by Bickel & Breiman and Avram & Bertsimas, and Bhatt & Roy's minimal directed spanning forest (with 'south-west' directions), where the non-Gaussian limit theorem was obtained by Penrose & Wade.

Probability.title: Exit times from time-dependent random domains: continuity, weak convergence, and exit-time profiles
Probability.summary: We study exit times from time-dependent domains under joint perturbations of the trajectory and the domain. Representing a moving domain as the negativity set of a continuous barrier on space-time, we reduce the exit problem to a one-dimensional first-passage problem for the scalarized path, namely the barrier evaluated along the trajectory. Our first main result is a deterministic continuity theorem: the exit-time functional is continuous, under Skorokhod J1 convergence of the path and locally uniform convergence of the barrier, at every configuration satisfying an explicit nontangency condition (NT). This condition is sharp: it characterizes the continuity set of the functional. As a consequence, exit times converge in distribution whenever paths and barriers converge jointly in distribution and the limiting pair satisfies (NT) almost surely; no independence or other structural restriction between trajectory and domain is required. Our second main result is a functional limit theorem: the profile of exit times indexed by the barrier level, regularized to be right-continuous on a compact level interval, converges in distribution in the Skorokhod M1 topology under the same joint convergence, provided the limiting pair satisfies (NT) almost surely at the two end levels; an example shows that J1 convergence can fail. Verification routes for (NT) are provided, including a non-characteristic criterion for Ito diffusions. The framework is illustrated by two Donsker-type examples; in the second one, the domain is random, is approximated jointly with the trajectory, and is coupled to the state.
Probability.comment: This new version (version 2) supersedes version 1, which was titled "Exit times from time-dependent random domains: continuity, weak convergence, and exit-time profiles Draft - currently under review at Stochastic Processes and their Applications". It corrects errors in version 1 and extends and strengthens its results. The manuscript is currently under review at SPA (round 2)

Probability.title: Langevin equations solved by Markov chains (instead of integrals), two solutions with multiplicative noise and their properties
Probability.summary: Langevin equations are usually understood as integral equations, since continuous and Markov solutions are nowhere differentiable. This is avoidable by the fact that white Gaussian noise can be seen as a generalized derivative of the Wiener process. The simplest LE is thus solved by Wiener paths, which can be computed by a Markov chain. That crucial property persists for functions of these paths, and solutions of the general LE are therefore assumed to have that form. In short time steps these functions must be linear or quadratic. Both cases lead to sampled versions of existing stochastic intrgrals ('Ito' and 'anti-Ito' respectively). In physics they apply for Brownian motion in presence of a temperature gradient: without a feedback to the medium in the linear case, and for a tagged molecule in the quadratic one; in the latter case the Fokker-Planck equation describes a local equilibrium.
Probability.comment: Removal or explanation of the existing ambiguities, and a simple computation of the paths

Probability.title: Ergodicity for the Two-Dimensional Stochastic Navier-Stokes Equations with Shear-Thickening Viscosity
Probability.summary: The two-dimensional stochastic Navier-Stokes equations with a shear-thickening viscosity driven by multiplicative noise are studied. After the problem is formulated as an abstract stochastic evolution equation on suitable function spaces, the existence and uniqueness of strong solutions are established through local monotonicity methods. Moment estimates are then obtained and used to prove the existence of an ergodic invariant probability measure via the Krylov-Bogolyubov technique. The uniqueness of the ergodic invariant measure is subsequently established by constructing a generalized coupling through a controlled auxiliary equation. Finally, the results are extended to other types of viscosities as well as to different stochastic hydrodynamical models.

Probability.title: Multi-excited random walks on general trees
Probability.summary: We study multi-excited random walks on infinite locally finite trees. The model is described by placing a stack of ``cookies'' at each vertex, with one cookie consumed on each successive visit. As long as cookies remain, the walk is in an excited regime and makes nearest-neighbour steps according to a prescribed sequence of biases. Once the stack is exhausted, the walk is in a non-excited regime and moves uniformly among the neighbouring vertices. The model is closely connected to foraging ecology, where repeated visits to a location can deplete local resources and thereby influence the attractiveness of that location for future visits. We prove that the process exhibits a sharp phase transition between recurrence and transience. The critical threshold is determined by the branching-ruin number of the tree, which is equal to the Hausdorff dimension of the tree's boundary under a suitable metric. Our result substantially extends Zerner's recurrence-transience criterion for multi-excited random walks on $\mathbb Z$ [Probab. Theory Related Fields 133 (2005)] to general trees.

Probability.title: A total variation threshold for the first coordinates of uniform parking functions via Lorentzian polynomials
Probability.summary: Let $π_n$ be a uniform parking function of size $n$. We determine the scale at which its first $k$ coordinates cease to be close in total variation to $k$ independent uniform variables on $\{1,\ldots,n\}$. The distance is comparable to $1\wedge \sqrt{k\log(k+1)/n}$, uniformly for $n\ge2$ and $1\le k\le n$, and tends to one above the scale $n/\log n$. At the critical scale $k\simλn/\log n$, it converges to $2Φ(\sqrt{λ/π})-1$, where $Φ$ is the standard normal distribution function. A key ingredient is the Lorentzian property of the occupation generating polynomial of parking functions. Together with a strengthened Han inequality, this yields a relative entropy estimate for approximation by the product of the one-coordinate marginals.
Probability.comment: 9 pages, 1 figure. Includes a 1.5-page section on AI use (in writing the paper and formalizing its results in Lean 4)

Probability.title: A particle system approach towards the global well-posedness of master equations for potential mean field games of control
Probability.summary: This paper studies the $N$-particle systems as well as the HJB/master equations for a class of generalized mean field control (MFC) problems and the corresponding potential mean field games of control (MFGC). A local in time classical solution for the HJB equation is generated via a probabilistic approach based on the mean field maximum principle. Given an extension of the so called displacement convexity condition, we obtain the uniform estimates on the HJB equation for the $N$-particle system. Such estimates imply the displacement convexity/semi-concavity and thus the prior estimates on the solution to the HJB equation for generalized MFC problems. The global well-posedness of HJB/master equation for generalized MFC/potential MFGC is then proved thanks to the local well-posedness and the prior estimates. In view of the nature of the displacement convexity condition, such well-posedness is also true for the degenerated case. Our analysis on the $N$-particle system also induces an Lipschitz approximator to the optimal feedback function in generalized MFC/potential MFGC where an algebraic convergence rate is obtained. Furthermore, an alternative approximate Nash equilibrium is proposed based on the $N$-particle system, where the approximation error is quantified thanks to the aforementioned uniform estimates.

Probability.title: Singularity of harmonic measure on Poisson--Voronoi tessellations in hyperbolic spaces
Probability.summary: We prove that the harmonic measure of simple random walk on the Poisson--Voronoi tessellation in $\mathbb{H}^d$ is almost surely singular with respect to Lebesgue measure on the boundary. This answers a question of Benjamini, Paquette, and Pfeffer in the hyperbolic plane and establishes the analogous result in higher dimensions. Our proof is based on ergodic theory of rerooting relations and their boundary extensions.

Probability.title: Brownian motion in Minkowski normed spaces
Probability.summary:
A Minkowski normed space is the Euclidean space equipped with a (possibly asymmetric) uniformly convex and smooth norm, forming a particular class of Finsler manifolds.
  We construct a stochastic process with one-dimensional time marginal densities given by the fundamental solution to the nonlinear Finsler heat equation in Minkowski normed spaces.
  This process is constructed as a solution to a singular McKean--Vlasov stochastic differential equation and constitutes a nonlinear Markov process in the sense of McKean.
  We show that solutions to this stochastic differential equation are pathwise unique, and, thus, probabilistically strong solutions, though the equation has singular coefficients beyond the subcritical regime.
  Since our construction is a natural extension of the construction of standard Brownian motion from the standard heat kernel, we call this process \emph{Brownian motion in Minkowski normed spaces.}
  Furthermore, we obtain a universality property, namely that whichever Minkowski norm is chosen, the radial part of this process is the standard Bessel process.
  To the best of our knowledge, this is the first construction of stochastic processes associated with nonlinear heat equation in Finslerian spaces.

Probability.title: Variational derivation of the homogeneous Boltzmann equation
Probability.summary: We introduce a variational formulation of the homogeneous Boltzmann equation, with hard-sphere cross section, which selects the unique energy conserving solution. We prove that this solution arises from the microscopic dynamics, namely Kac's walk, and we establish the propagation in time of entropic chaoticity, under the minimal assumption that the initial distribution is entropically chaotic.

Probability.title: Flexible random graph modelling for cell-cell interactions
Probability.summary: In this paper we explore generalisations to a random digraph model designed for modelling cell-cell interactions (RaCInG). In its baseline model -- tested both theoretically and in biological practice -- a fixed number of arcs are assigned uniformly at random to vertices that have suitable types to accept them. Generalisations to this model are explored in two directions: constructing an undirected graph version of the model, and incorporating spatial information. Both directions are driven by biological demands: better interpretability and adaptation to technological advances. We show not only that these generalisations are theoretically possible within the framework of RaCInG, but that they can be made rigorous, proving that RaCInG creates a flexible random graph framework to model cell-cell interactions.

Probability.title: A Sharp Joint Bias-Energy Envelope for Radial Clipping
Probability.summary: Radial clipping does two things at once: it cuts off the part of a vector outside a ball and leaves a bounded vector inside the ball. The part cut off defines the residual. For a random vector, we study the magnitude of the bias in the mean and the energy, defined as the centered second moment of the clipped vector. Controlling these effects is important in stochastic optimization with heavy tails, where the choice of the clipping threshold affects convergence bounds for algorithms. In the deterministic problem, for a fixed threshold $τ>0$, $1\le p\le2$, and nonnegative coefficients $α,β$, we find the smallest constant that simultaneously bounds the residual and energy in terms of $\lVert x\rVert^p$. This same constant remains sharp in the stochastic counterpart for random vectors in a Hilbert space. We also find the exact supremum of the corresponding linear combination of normalized bias and energy for arbitrary $α,β\in\mathbb R$. We then give a geometric picture in the energy-bias plane. Varying the weights, we describe the smallest closed convex region containing all normalized pairs and the attainable set itself, identifying unattainable boundary values. Every attainable pair at a fixed threshold can be realized by a real-valued random variable taking at most two values. We also consider all thresholds simultaneously. For any integrable random vector in a Hilbert space, we construct a single $\mathbb R^3$-valued random vector preserving its norm distribution, bias magnitude, and energy simultaneously at every threshold $τ>0$. Finally, we apply the joint bound to risk-adjusted reinsurance costs for a prescribed retention threshold and to the logarithmic shortfall of a clipped portfolio strategy relative to any constant-fraction strategy. AI was used in preparing this paper (see Section 8).
Probability.comment: 61 pages, 14 figures (7 in each language). Complete English version followed by Russian version. Revised and expanded; includes simultaneous three-dimensional realization for all thresholds and two applications

Probability.title: On self-similar random quotients of the line
Probability.summary: A surprisingly wide variety of important random fractal metric spaces in modern probability theory can be viewed as self-similar random quotients of the real line, including the continuum random tree, Liouville quantum gravity surfaces, the trace of Brownian motion in $\mathbb{R}^d$, and self-similar ($s=2d$) long-range percolation on $\mathbb{R}$. We prove that the metric and resistance growth dimensions are well-defined in a certain sense for every random metric space in a class containing all of the above examples. Our results are new for the trace of Brownian motion.

Probability.title: Level Crossing Rate Bounds for Products of Independent Nonstationary Fading Processes
Probability.summary: We develop a unified framework for the instantaneous total level crossing rate (LCR) of products of independent positive nonstationary fading processes. Universal upper and lower bounds are first derived from an exact decomposition of the product derivative and signed crossing imbalance, requiring only factor-wise crossing statistics. We then introduce the drifting Gaussian-derivative (DGD) class, in which each conditional derivative is Gaussian with possibly nonzero drift. For products of DGD factors, an exact Gaussian-mixture representation yields bounds that jointly capture aggregate drift and derivative fluctuations. The lower bound reduces under stationarity to a known $\ell_2$ bound, whereas, to the best of the author's knowledge, the upper bound is new even in the stationary case. Furthermore, the bounds are asymptotically exact in drift-dominated regimes. The framework is specialized to nonstationary Double-Rayleigh fading and to quasi-identically distributed DGD factors, with closed forms for products of $α$-$μ$ envelopes. Numerical results show that the DGD bounds closely bracket the exact LCR.

Probability.title: On record behaviours of returns for interval maps
Probability.summary: Given a dynamical system $(X,T)$ and an ergodic invariant measure $μ$, a $μ$-typical point $x\in X$ under $T$ visits arbitrarily small neighbourhood of $x$. We will use techniques based on extreme value theory and Laplace functional for point process to show that, for interval maps with suitable mixing and anti-clustering conditions, the limiting distributions of the record times and values of the return process $Y_j(x)=-\log d(T^jx,x)$, after possible normalisation, has Poisson-type laws.

Probability.title: Lie point symmetry analysis of a dependent jump-diffusion risk model with exponential claim sizes
Probability.summary: We carry out a Lie point symmetry analysis of the coupled integro-differential system satisfied by the conditional Gerber--Shiu functions of a dependent jump-diffusion risk model. In the model, claim sizes are exponential, the intensity of the next claim arrival depends on whether the current claim exceeds a random threshold, and both the volatility and the premium rate may depend on the surplus. We write the system as the restriction to the half-line of a far-field operator with prescribed exterior data, derive the complete set of determining equations, including the condition imposed by the nonlocal convolution term, and solve them. The resulting group classification holds for every surplus-dependent volatility and premium of the form considered and for every absolutely continuous or constant threshold distribution. A non-trivial symmetry beyond scaling and superposition exists if and only if the volatility and the premium rate are constant, and it is then exactly the translation in the surplus variable. We construct the optimal system of one-dimensional subalgebras. We show that the invariant solutions of the combined translation--scaling generators exist precisely when a $2\times2$ generalized Lundberg determinant vanishes, and we give this determinant for an arbitrary threshold distribution, with explicit forms for the constant and exponential thresholds. We prove existence and sign properties of the adjustment coefficient, derive its sensitivities to all model parameters, and establish Cramér--Lundberg-type asymptotics for the Gerber--Shiu functions, including the limit of the ratio between the two regimes. A numerical study shows that claim-size-driven dependence lowers the adjustment coefficient markedly below that of an independent model with the same mean claim intensity.

Probability.title: Interacting particles in random irregular media
Probability.summary: In this paper, we first develop novel tools of independent interest in the field of stochastic calculus related to SDEs with distributional drift, namely the formulation of a quasi-Stroock-Varadhan martingale problem in the sense that the test functions are of class $C^{1,2}$ instead of solutions of Kolmogorov type PDE. This has several applications, among which, the time restriction and the notion of conditional rough martingale problem and related solution.

Probability.title: Strong rate for one-dimensional driftless continuous strict local martingales
Probability.summary: For one-dimensional strict local martingales of the form $\mathrm{d} X_t=σ(X_t) \mathrm{d} W_t$ starting from $X_{0}=x_{0}>0$, we prove the strong rate $\mathbb{E}\left[|X^h_N-X_T|\right] \lesssim h^{\min\{θα,\frac{1}{2}\}}$ for a discrete scheme~$X^h$ truncated at a level $h^{-α}$, with time step~$h$, as $h\downarrow 0$, where~$θ$ depends on the truncation property. For the CEV model $σ(x)\equiv x^{1+γ}$ in particular, the rate is~$\frac{1}{2}$ for any $γ\in (0,1)$ (up to a logarithmic pre-factor at $γ=\frac{1}{2}$).

Probability.title: Gaussian inequalities with different covariance matrices - the Heterovariant Gaussian Brunn-Minkowski inequality
Probability.summary:
We establish the following novel heterovariant Gaussian Brunn-Minkowski inequality (involving general covariance matrices $Σ_1,Σ_2,Γ$) for origin-symmetric convex sets $K,L \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ and $p,λ\in (0,1)$: \[
  γ_{Σ_1}(K)^{1-p} γ_{Σ_2}(L)^p
  \le
  \left( \left( \frac{1-p}{1-λ} \right)^{1-p} \left( \frac{p}λ \right)^p \right)^{n}
  γ_Γ((1-λ) K + λL) , \] whenever $Γ\leq Σ_1 \sharp_p Σ_2$, the $p$-geometric mean of $Σ_1,Σ_2$. This immediately implies both the dimensional Gaussian Brunn-Minkowski inequality of Eskenazis-Moschidis (by using $Σ_1 = Σ_2 = Γ$ and optimizing over $p$) and the strong Gaussian (B)-theorem of Cordero-Erausquin-Fradelizi-Maurey (by using $K=L$, $p=λ$ and diagonal covariances), fusing them into a single unified statement. In fact, the inequality applies to convex sets whose appropriate Gaussian barycenter is at the origin. Furthermore, it reveals a new *bilinear* version of the strong Gaussian (B)-theorem (involving *two* convex sets); in particular, for all $a,b > 0$ and $λ\in [0,1]$: \[ γ(a K)^{1-λ} γ(b L)^λ \leq γ\left ( a^{1-λ} b^λ\left ((1-λ) K + λL \right) \right ) . \] A more general heterovariant version of the (bilinear) (B)-theorem replaces dilation by general linear transformations. A different version yields a heterovariant form of the recently established Gaussian conjugate Rogers-Shephard inequality. By averaging these Gaussian inequalities with respect to the covariance matrices, we obtain dimensional Brunn-Minkowski and conjugate Rogers-Shephard inequalities for Gaussian mixtures. The proofs are based on the Gaussian Forward-Reverse Brascamp-Lieb inequality established in our previous work.
Probability.comment: 26 pages. Added a more general heterovariant Gaussian BM inequality for arbitrary covariances Σ_1,Σ_2,Γ, identifying the sharp constant in that generality. Also added a remark that the bilinear (B) theorem logically implies the dimensional Gaussian BM inequality

Probability.title: Limit shape, avalanches, and stabilisation of abelian sandpiles on comb lattices
Probability.summary: We study two aspects of the abelian sandpile model on comb lattices. First, we prove that the infinite-volume limit of the stationary measures is supported on the saturated configuration. We then investigate the shape of avalanches induced by adding a particle at the origin in finite boxes of size $(2n+1)\times(2n+1)$ around the origin. In the stationary distribution on these finite boxes, we show that avalanches reach the boundary along the vertical teeth with probability tending to $1$, while the horizontal spread is of order $\sqrt{n}$. Finally, we establish that the single-source limit shape for abelian sandpiles on the comb lattice agrees with the corresponding limit shapes for the divisible sandpile, internal diffusion-limited aggregation (IDLA), and rotor-router aggregation models. This establishes limit shape universality on the comb lattice.

Probability.title: PDE-based Bayesian Inverse Problems in All-at-once Framework
Probability.summary: We propose a modern all-at-once framework for PDE-based Bayesian inversion by introducing the PDE residual as probabilistic information. In this framework, the PDE residual is treated as a soft constraint with a residual covariance and is directly incorporated into the likelihood function. The new hybrid likelihood function eliminates PDE solves, thus reducing expensive computational costs, while performing rigorous Bayesian inference. Theoretically, we establish the well-posedness of the posterior with uncertainty quantification, and numerically, we propose two efficiency inversion algorithms based on two posterior sampling methods. In particular, one algorithm is based on Metropolis-within-Gibbs MCMC method with a PDE-informed block- diagonal Gaussian prior, and the other is based on a joint sampling strategy. Numerical experiments for a semiconductor inverse problem confirm that the proposed Bayesian all-at-once approach yields a speedup of approximately a factor of two, while having a comparable reconstruction quality as the conventional reduced-based setting.

Probability.title: Brownian motion and stochastic areas on complex partial flag manifolds with blocks of equal size
Probability.summary: We construct a Brownian motion on complex partial flag manifolds with blocks of equal size as a matrix-valued diffusion from a Brownian motion on the unitary group. This construction leads to an explicit expression for the characteristic function of the joint distribution of the stochastic areas on these manifolds. The limit law of these stochastic areas is shown to be a multivariate Cauchy distribution with independent and identically distributed entries. By relating the area functionals on flag manifolds to the winding functional on the complex Stiefel manifold, we establish new results about simultaneous Brownian windings on the complex Stiefel manifold. To establish these results, this work introduces a new family of diffusions, which generalise both the Jacobi processes on the simplex and the Hermitian Jacobi processes.
Probability.comment: 28 pages, v2: Minor edits, v3: Updated some sign conventions, corrected a minor normalisation discrepancy in expressions for the horizontal Brownian motion and the contact process + additional minor edits

Probability.title: The longest increasing subsequences of Luce permutations and permutons
Probability.summary: We investigate the longest increasing subsequences (LIS) of random permutations distributed under the Luce model with weights $θ_1^{(n)} \ge \ldots \ge θ_n^{(n)}$. Our first main result provides a general formula for the growth rate of the LIS. For example, we get that the LIS of Luce permutations with Sukhatme weights $θ_k^{(n)} = n-k+1$ grows like $\sqrt{n}$. We also give simple conditions for the LIS to be of order $n^β$, for any given $β\in[1/2,1)$. Our second main result states that, if the weights are of the form $θ_k^{(n)} = f\big( (k-1)/n \big)$ for a sufficiently regular function $f$, then the LIS divided by $2\sqrt{n}$ converges in probability to a constant $K(f)$ described by a variational problem. Throughout, we make extensive use of coupling techniques; in particular, to prove our second main result, we argue that Luce random permutations behave similarly to random permutations sampled from the ``Luce permuton''.
Probability.comment: 29 pages. v2: minor changes in the introduction

Probability.title: Functional limit theorems for Galton-Watson processes with inhomogeneous immigration towards a deterministic limit function
Probability.summary: We study the asymptotic behavior of a sequence of Galton-Watson processes with inhomogeneous immigration when the limit of the means of the offspring distributions is equal to 1. Under a growth condition on the variances of the offspring distributions, assuming the locally uniform convergence of the expectation functions of properly scaled immigration processes towards a càdlàg function, and the locally uniform convergence of the mean absolute deviation functions of the scaled immigration processes in question towards zero, we establish a functional limit theorem for the sequence of Galton-Watson processes with inhomogeneous immigration in question towards a deterministic limit process. We also provide some applications, among others, we show that a recent result of Rahimov and Sharipov (2024) on a functional limit theorem for a sequence of nearly critical Galton-Watson processes with dependent immigration can be recovered using our result.

Probability.title: Moderate deviations for the Maki--Thompson rumour model
Probability.summary: We consider the classical Maki--Thompson rumour model with $n$ initially ignorant individuals and one initial spreader. The final number of ignorants, divided by $n$, is known to satisfy the law of large numbers, the central limit theorem and the large deviation principle. We establish a moderate deviation principle for fluctuations of this proportion of order $b_n/\sqrt n$, where $b_n\to\infty$ and $b_n^2=o(\log n)$. The proof rests on the exact final-size distribution, sharp asymptotics for the associated automata numbers, and a uniform point probability expansion at the moderate deviation scale. Numerical comparisons of both tails illustrate the intermediate scale and the effect of early extinction on upper tail probabilities.

Probability.title: Learning on-the-fly quasi-stationarity diagnostics from low-dimensional surrogates
Probability.summary:
Accelerated dynamics methods, such as parallel replica dynamics, require estimates of the decorrelation time, after which a process trapped in one of its metastable states is distributed according to the quasi-stationary distribution (QSD).
  In a method proposed by Binder, Lelièvre and Simpson, decorrelation times are defined by coupling a particle approximation of the non-linear conditioned probability flow of the process with MCMC-inspired diagnostics.
  We explore an alternative to MCMC diagnostics, based on coarse-graining of non-linear probability flows and simulation-based inference.
  We first develop a coarse-graining framework for killed Markov jump processes conditioned on survival, proving uniform-in-time, non-asymptotic estimates approximating the non-linear probability flow of
  the true process by the non-linear flow of a surrogate process, defined with a collective variable. The framework does not assume reversibility of the true process, and also gives bounds which scale explicitly in an adiabatic regime.
  Motivated by these results, we then construct a quasi-stationarity diagnostic using simulation-based inference: a recurrent neural network (RNN), trained on particle approximations of non-linear effective flows, estimates posterior probabilities of decorrelation. The learned diagnostic is then transferred to collective-variable traces of high-dimensional particle approximations.
  We investigate the behavior and robustness of this diagnostic on a set of numerical experiments, comparing it to the MCMC diagnostic of Binder et al.\ on both synthetic examples and a molecular system, in and out of its training prior distribution.
  When its prior assumptions hold, the RNN diagnostic outperforms the MCMC diagnostic in ROC analysis, is less conservative, fails less often, and has an interpretable decision threshold.

Probability.title: The Berry--Esseen estimate in the Boolean central limit theorem
Probability.summary: We estimate the Lévy distance to the symmetric Bernoulli distribution for normalized Boolean convolution powers of a probability measure with mean zero and variance one. If the absolute moment of order $r$ is finite, we obtain the upper bounds $o(n^{-(r-2)/6})$ for $2<r<5$ and $O(n^{-1/2})$ for $r\ge5$. The proof relies on an inequality that controls the Lévy distance to the Bernoulli law by the values of the reciprocal Cauchy transform at two points. For each $r\ge2$, we also construct a single fixed distribution whose absolute moments are finite exactly up to order $r$, and show that the exponent $\min\{(r-2)/6,1/2\}$ cannot be improved. Under only a finite second moment assumption, the convergence can be arbitrarily slow.

Probability.title: A shape theorem for a radially excited random walk in dimensions $d \ge 2$
Probability.summary:
NOTE (October 2026): This paper has been superseded by the joint paper "Limit shapes for centrally excited walks", by Ahmed Bou-Rabee, Tuan-Minh Nguyen, Yuval Peres and Arvind Singh (arXiv:2610.10162), which brings together the results and ideas of three independent drafts.
  We consider a once-excited random walk on $\mathbb{Z}^d$, $d \ge 2$, where the walk on its first visit has a bias of constant strength $β>0$ toward the origin and moves like a simple symmetric random walk on subsequent visits to that site. We show that the walk is recurrent and prove an almost sure spherical shape theorem: the trace after $n$ steps is asymptotically a Euclidean ball centered at the origin, with radius proportional to $n^{1/(d+1)}$, and the local times have an asymptotically conical profile. This result confirms a conjecture of Kozma (2007) on the shape of the trace for this model.
Probability.comment: 12 pages. Superseded by arXiv:2610.10162. Abstract and comments updated; article text unchanged

Probability.title: Diffusion Processes on $p$-Wasserstein Space over Banach Space
Probability.summary: To study diffusion processes on the p-Wasserstein space $\mathscr P_p$ for $p\in [1,\infty)$ over a separable, reflexive Banach space $X$, we present a criterion on the quasi-regularity of Dirichlet forms in $L^2(\mathscr P_p,Λ)$ for a reference probability $Λ$ on $\mathscr P_p$. It is formulated in terms of an upper bound condition with the uniform norm of the intrinsic derivative. We find a versatile class of quasi-regular local Dirichlet forms on $\mathscr P_p$ by using images of Dirichlet forms on the tangent space $L^p(X\to X,μ_0)$ at a reference point $μ_0\in\mathscr P_p$. The Ornstein--Uhlenbeck type Dirichlet form and process on $\mathscr P_2$ are an important example in this class. We derive an $L^2$-estimate for the corresponding heat kernel and an integration by parts formula for the invariant measure.

Probability.title: Random semigroups á la Gromov
Probability.summary: We introduce a model of random semigroups analogous to Gromov's density model for random groups. For a fixed number $n\ge 2$ of generators and a density parameter $δ\in (0,1)$, we impose a uniformly chosen set of $\lfloor n^{2δl}\rfloor$ relations of the form $u=v$, where $u,v$ are distinct words of length at most $l$, and study the resulting semigroup as $l\to\infty$. We prove that, with overwhelming probability, above density $1/2$ the semigroup is trivial, while below density $1/2$ it contains a free subsemigroup of rank two, has a Golod-Shafarevich semigroup algebra over every field, and has a homomorphic image which generates a non-elementary hyperbolic group. We also show that the small cancellation condition $C(m)$ holds with overwhelming probability whenever $δ<1/2m$. Finally, for $n\ge 3$, at critical density $1/2$ we obtain a subsequential limiting distribution on finite semigroups, with positive mass at the trivial semigroup and unbounded support in size. This contrasts with random groups, which have order at most two with overwhelming probability at critical density.

Probability.title: Distributionally robust approximation property of neural networks
Probability.summary: The universal approximation property uniformly with respect to weakly compact families of measures is established for several classes of neural networks. To that end, we prove that these neural networks are dense in Orlicz spaces, thereby extending classical universal approximation theorems even beyond the traditional $L^p$-setting. The covered classes of neural networks include widely used architectures like feedforward neural networks with non-polynomial activation functions, deep narrow networks with ReLU activation functions and functional input neural networks.

Probability.title: Emergence of the transformer architecture as the score of entropic laws of random measures
Probability.summary: We show that the transformer architecture emerges as the score of last-token laws in a natural statistical model of language, where sentences are empirical measures of tokens, a language is a law on $P(S^d)$, and our prior belief is that sentences carry no structure at all. By the maximum-entropy principle, we select the law closest to this prior in relative entropy among those reproducing an observed sentence-level statistic. We discuss the relevance of the statistic in the posterior interaction between tokens and we build a statistic, able to capture that interaction, with Luce's choice axiom truncated at the lowest relational order. This procedure gives the softmax choice rule, with the attention cross-moment as its mean parameter. The query--key matrix is then the Lagrange multiplier of a maximum-entropy problem inside each sentence, and the value matrix the multiplier of the constraint over the language, so that the two are untied. Under the optimal entropic law we then show that a transformer head appears in the score of the last-token law. For ordered sentences, causal masking follows from the masked reference choice rule, and with a next-token cross-moment the score equals one causally masked attention head. We also discuss multi-head attention, weight-tied unembedding, and a heuristic reading of residual blocks as projected Langevin steps.

Probability.title: Fractal dimensions of paths on three-dimensional random-walk traces
Probability.summary: We study four paths that join the starting site to the final position of a simple random walk of \(N=L^2\) steps on the infinite cubic lattice. The paths are selected on the walk trace---the graph of visited sites and traversed bonds---by different rules: the undirected shortest path \(S_1\), the directed shortest path \(S_2\), the time-respecting shortest path \(S_3\), and the depth \(D_e\) of the final site in a depth-first-search tree. Monte Carlo simulations for \(L\) up to 32768 give mean lengths scaling as \(L^{d_O}\), with \(d_{S_1}=1.48005(9)\), \(d_{S_2}=1.49868(5)\), \(d_{S_3}=1.51205(5)\), and \(d_{D_e}=1.7099(7)\), so that \(d_{S_1}<d_{S_2}<d_{S_3}<d_{\rm LE}<d_{D_e}\), where $d_{\rm LE}=1.62400(5)$ is the known loop-erased-random-walk exponent. Imposing traversal directions increases the shortest-path exponent, and imposing time order increases it further; these constraints therefore change the scaling exponent, not only the amplitude. For every path, the standard deviation scales with the same exponent as the mean, so it is scale-invariant, unlike the visited-site mass; the rescaled length distributions collapse onto a finite-width scaling function. No analytical theory currently predicts these exponents; our results provide precise numerical benchmarks for future studies of path geometry on random-walk traces.

Probability.title: The mean-field limit of non-exchangeable particle systems with non-conservative dynamics and adaptive weights
Probability.summary: In the paper we introduce vector-valued dynamic extended graphons in order to obtain the mean-filed limit for certain class of problems with adaptive weights. We impose fairly general assumptions on the matrix of initial connections, which allows us to cover the case of sparse graphs.

Probability.title: The Price of Failure Risk: Clipped Barrier Policy Gradients with Convex Regularization
Probability.summary: In many control problems, actions consume a resource budget, such as a wear allowance, and the probability of exhausting it within a given horizon must stay below a tolerance. A simple, widely used approach is to augment the state with the remaining budget, subtract an interior barrier from the utility and penalize exhaustion, so that policy-gradient methods can be applied unchanged. We clip the combined one-step reward from below at a level m to keep the returns of exploratory policies finite. The clip level is a price of failure risk, since the clipped value decomposes exactly into the utility before failure, the cost of the interior margin and m times a geometric failure risk. Consequently, an approximately optimal policy maximizes utility net of margin cost among policies with no greater risk. Its risk exceeds that of any comparison policy by at most order 1/m and can be certified from its value or from validation data. Our main result proves exponential convergence of the population policy-gradient flow for every parameter regularizer that is convex along generalized geodesics and sufficiently strong relative to the price. This extends the mean-field analysis from relative entropy to weight decay and to finite networks. Relative entropy adds parameter noise and a pull toward a prior, whereas weight decay provides only the pull. Action regularization bounds changes in failure risk by the relative entropy to a reference policy. The bounds are evaluated on an exact maintenance benchmark, a fuel-tank controller, a solvable flow and a benchmark-suite task.
Probability.comment: 40 pages, 8 figures, 1 table; Online Resource 1 (36 pages) as an ancillary file. Revised version; replaces v3 (text revised, the paper made independent of the Online Resource). Code: https://github.com/pma-papers/bpg-replication

Probability.title: Continuous stochastic flows driven by white noise and their duals
Probability.summary: We study a class of continuous stochastic flows driven by a space-time white noise and characterize their dual flows by explicit stochastic differential equations. A key ingredient of the proof is the convergence of solutions under coefficient approximations. As an application, we derive the dual flows in two illustrative examples, the squared Bessel flow and the Jacobi flow. We also introduce a new model of polynomially self-repelling (PSR) flow and show that it enjoys a self-duality property.

Probability.title: The Mézard-Parisi formula
Probability.summary: This paper proves the Mézard-Parisi formula for the free energy of random $K$-sat and diluted $p$-spin models with even $p$, completing an approach developed in earlier work of the author and collaborators. The upper bound was established by Franz and Leone. Here the matching lower bound is proved for a general class of diluted models under symmetry and integrability assumptions. The main new contribution is a proof of an approximate form of the Mézard-Parisi reproducibility hypothesis without assuming that the overlap distribution has finite support.

Probability.title: Ghirlanda-Guerra identities and cavity equations for diluted spin glass models
Probability.summary: This note supplies the details of the cavity lower bound used in "The Mézard-Parisi formula" [8]. Specifically, we show that small perturbations that do not change the limiting free energy can be chosen so that the asymptotic Gibbs measures arising in the Aizenman-Sims-Starr lower bound satisfy both the Ghirlanda-Guerra identities and the cavity equations. These calculations are standard and require only minor modifications of arguments already available in the literature. We record them here for completeness, avoiding a lengthy repetition of these arguments in [8].

Probability.title: Local Convergence of Triadic Closures of Sparse Random Graphs
Probability.summary: Triadic closure is a natural mechanism for modeling the clustering phenomenon observed in many real-world networks. Given a possibly random undirected graph $H$, we consider pairs of non-adjacent vertices that have a common neighbor. Conditional on $H$, each such pair is joined by an edge independently and simultaneously, with a probability depending on the degrees of its endpoints and on the number of their common neighbors. The resulting graph is called a triadic closure of $H$. We study the effect of this operation on local convergence. More precisely, we prove that if a sequence of potentially random finite undirected graphs of $\left( H_n \right)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ converges locally in probability to a rooted graph $H^*$, then the corresponding sequence of triadic closures converges locally in probability to the same triadic closure of $H^*$. As a consequence, we obtain a general limit theorem for the clustering coefficients of triadic closures. In particular, we show that the triadic closures can have a strictly positive limiting clustering coefficients even when the limiting clustering coefficients of the parent graph sequence is zero. Finally, we apply our results to several classical sparse random graph models including Erdős-Rényi, configuration, preferential attachment models and compute the limiting clustering coefficients of their triadic closures.

Probability.title: Hausdorff dimension of the graph of a random vector-valued Weierstrass function
Probability.summary:
Let $\{θ_n,λ_n:n\geq0\}$ be mutually independent random variables, each uniformly distributed on $[0,1]$, and write $Θ=(θ_n)_{n\geq0}$ and $Λ=(λ_n)_{n\geq0}$. The random vector-valued Weierstrass function is given by $$f_{Θ,Λ}(x)= \left( \sum_{n=0}^{\infty} a^n\cos\bigl(2π(b^n x+θ_n)\bigr),\
  \sum_{n=0}^{\infty} a^n\sin\bigl(2π(b^n x+λ_n)\bigr)
  \right), \; x\in[0,1],$$ where $0<a<1<b,\ ab> 1$. The Hausdorff dimension of the graph of this function is proved to be $$\dim_H G(f_{Θ,Λ}) = \min\left\{-\frac{\log b}{\log a}, \, 3 +2\frac{\log a}{\log b}\right\} \quad \text{a.s}.$$

Probability.title: Weighted Harris--oscillation contraction and invariant expectations for nonlinear Markov semigroups
Probability.summary:
We establish a weighted contraction principle for sublinear Markov semigroups on noncompact state spaces. Its abstract inputs are a Lyapunov drift condition and a strict local contraction of oscillations on a Lyapunov sublevel set. For locally uniformly parabolic diffusion semigroups, the latter is obtained by applying the parabolic Harnack inequality to both the upper evolution and its conjugate lower evolution: if $u=T_t\varphi$, then $u-m$ and $M-u$ solve the upper and lower Bellman equations, respectively. Combining the resulting local oscillation contraction with the Lyapunov drift yields a strict contraction in a weighted oscillation seminorm, a unique invariant sublinear expectation in the finite-Lyapunov-moment class, and weighted exponential convergence for Borel observables controlled by the Lyapunov function.
  To treat bounded Borel data for $G$-SDEs, we use a canonical covariance-law representation, progressively measurable state maps compatible with conditioning and pasting, and a stopped dynamic programming principle. A probabilistic Krylov--Safonov argument then gives positive-time Hölder regularisation before viscosity identification, thereby avoiding a measurable-data envelope argument. The abstract result is verified for ordinary locally uniformly elliptic SDEs, multiplicative $G$-SDEs, and the full equation with quadratic-variation drift \[
  dX_t=b(X_t)\,dt
  +\sum_{i,j=1}^m h_{ij}(X_t)\,d\langle B^i,B^j\rangle_t
  +\sum_{j=1}^mσ_j(X_t)\,dB_t^j. \] For the full equation the hypotheses are expressed through the effective drift and covariance and are required uniformly over all covariance scenarios. Finally, the contraction and stochastic continuity of the associated stationary process yield ergodicity in the sense of Feng and Zhao.

Probability.title: Exponential Ergodicity and Invariant Distribution of a Degenerate Reflected SDE with Stable Noise
Probability.summary: We study a two-dimensional degenerate stochastic differential equation with oblique reflection and spectrally positive strictly stable noise of index in $(1,2)$, motivated by join-the-shortest-queue systems with heavy-tailed interarrival times. A polynomial-exponential Lyapunov function and fixed-time minorization establish positive Harris recurrence and exponential ergodicity in weighted total variation. We construct the invariant law from a stable path and prove its absolute continuity. Regulator identities describe stationary dependence and recover the joint Laplace transform from the queue marginal. Idleness inherits the classical stable Ornstein-Uhlenbeck tail; the queue has a sharp exponential tail with a polynomial prefactor whose power is half the stable index and a positive constant represented through regeneration. Conditional on small idleness, idleness divided by the conditioning threshold and the queue converge to independent beta and size-biased limits. Under large-queue conditioning, normalized idleness and queue excess converge to independent Mittag-Leffler and exponential limits.

Probability.title: Exponential singularity and rank bounds for random symmetric matrices
Probability.summary:
Let $A$ be an $n\times n$ real symmetric random matrix whose entries above the diagonal are independent, each with largest atom at most $β\in (0,1)$. The diagonal entries have an arbitrary joint distribution and are independent of the entries above the diagonal. We prove that \[
  \mathbb{P}[\mathrm{rank}(A)\le n-k]\le 2e^{-c_βnk},\qquad 1\le k\le n, \] where $c_β>0$ depends only on $β$. This extends Han's corank bound to the full range $1\le k\le n$. No moment assumptions are needed, and the entries need not be centered or identically distributed. In particular, the case $k=1$ gives an exponential singularity bound under the uniform atom assumption. Our argument also gives a new proof of the exponential singularity bound for symmetric Rademacher matrices obtained by Campos, Jenssen, Michelen, and Sahasrabudhe. For every fixed $p\in (0,1)$, it yields the exponential singularity bound conjectured by Costello and Vu for the adjacency matrix of the Erdős--Rényi random graph $G(n,p)$, where the case $p=1/2$ was previously proved by Han.

Probability.title: A Functional Central Limit Theorem for Locally Stationary Time Series in Banach Spaces
Probability.summary: We establish a functional central limit theorem for locally stationary time series in a separable Banach space $B$. The result requires no type-2 or cotype assumptions and thus covers spaces central to functional data analysis, such as $C([0,1])$ and $L^p([0,1])$. Under moment conditions, summable physical dependence coefficients and a bracketing entropy condition controlling the infinite-dimensional tails, the centered partial sum process converges weakly in $D([0,1],B)$ to a centered Gaussian process, whose covariance is the integrated local long-run covariance, an element of the projective tensor product. We also obtain a stochastic integral representation with respect to a cylindrical Brownian motion. As the limit depends on the unknown long-run covariance, we prove consistency of a block multiplier bootstrap for the partial sum process. This yields CUSUM tests for a constant mean of the full process, based on arbitrary continuous seminorms and valid under a time-varying long-run covariance. For linear projections, we derive a self-normalized test with a pivotal limit. In simulations, the supremum norm test detects localized changes that its $L^2$ counterpart largely misses, and applications to EEG and temperature data illustrate the methodology. Examples in $C([0,1])$ and $W^{1,p}_0([0,1])$ show how the entropy condition can be verified.
Probability.comment: Keywords: Locally stationary time series; Banach-valued time series; functional central limit theorem; functional data analysis; block multiplier bootstrap; change point detection

Probability.title: Optimal fiber comparisons for random tensors
Probability.summary: We extend Seginer's matrix norm comparison to tensors with optimal dependence on the tensor order. For a real tensor $T$ of order $k\ge2$ with centered, integrable, independent and identically distributed entries, we prove $\mathbb{E} f(T)\le\mathbb{E}\lVert T\rVert_{\mathrm{inj}} \le C\sqrt{k\log k}\,\mathbb{E} f(T)$, where $f(T)$ is the largest Euclidean norm of a one-dimensional fiber and $C$ is universal. The comparison holds for every finite rectangular format, and the entry law may depend on both the dimensions and the tensor order. We show that the factor $\sqrt{k\log k}$ is optimal by considering Rademacher tensors on $[2]^k$.

Probability.title: Limit Theorems and Optimal Policies for Flock Flight through Poisson Forests
Probability.summary: Inspired by birds flying through cluttered environments, Karaman and Frazzoli showed that high-speed flight through an ergodic random forest exhibits an ultimate speed limit: above a critical speed, almost surely no infinite collision-free trajectory exists for a single bird. This paper formulates a corresponding bulk-transport problem for many birds. We construct an explicit directed corridor network in a Poisson disk forest and impose a common temporal headway at its waypoints. The maximum current equals a minimum vertex-cut capacity and is achieved by repeated flight along vertex-disjoint paths. The same schedule maximizes completed traversals at every finite horizon, with constant forward speed and no internal waiting. For a forest belt of fixed depth, exact transverse superadditivity yields an almost-sure deterministic current-density limit. A uniform shape theorem for an asymmetric planar dual identifies the current when depth and width grow together. For diverging depth bounded by a constant times width, this current equals the width-first, depth-second limit and is independent of the positive aspect ratio. When diagonal corridors are available, bulk current is positive at sufficiently low obstacle intensity and zero at sufficiently high intensity. For stochastic demand, an upstream admission queue is stable at every rate below the finite-network capacity.

Probability.title: Stopping Rules and the Poisson Boundary of Random Walks on Countable Groups
Probability.summary: In this paper, we study the terminal laws and Poisson boundaries obtained by stopping random walks on countable groups.
