For a transient walk, we give a direct Green-potential characterization of randomized stopping distributions and show that the terminal law determines the mean stopping time. On free groups, this yields finitely supported randomized stopping distributions at a positive total variation distance from every ordinary stopping distribution. We construct symmetric, fully supported recurrent measures of finite entropy on countable locally finite groups and obtain ordinary strict boundary enlargements when the group is not Choquet-Deny. For generating source and terminal measures of finite entropy, positive asymptotic entropy of the source forces the stopping time to have finite mean. A direct proof of the finite-mean entropy formula and boundary preservation then shows that a finite-entropy stopping chain has at most one strict enlargement. An exact stopped-word entropy identity shows that infinite-mean ordinary stopping with a finite-entropy terminal law has infinite conditional history entropy.

Probability.title: Convergence of stochastic integrals with applications to transport equations and conservation laws with noise
Probability.summary: Convergence of stochastic integrals driven by Wiener processes $W_n$, with $W_n \to W$ almost surely in $C_t$, is crucial in analyzing SPDEs. Our focus is on the convergence of the form $\int_0^T V_n\, \mathrm{d} W_n \to \int_0^T V\, \mathrm{d} W$, where $\{V_n\}$ is bounded in $L^p(Ω\times [0,T];X)$ for a Banach space $X$ and some finite $p > 2$. This is challenging when $V_n$ converges to $V$ weakly in the temporal variable. We supply convergence results to handle stochastic integral limits when strong temporal convergence is lacking. A key tool is a uniform mean $L^1$ time translation estimate on $V_n$, an estimate that is easily verified in many SPDEs. However, this estimate alone does not guarantee strong compactness of $(ω,t)\mapsto V_n(ω,t)$. Our findings, especially pertinent to equations exhibiting singular behavior, are substantiated by establishing several stability results for stochastic transport equations and conservation laws.
Probability.comment: 29 pages; some proofs and examples have been revised

Probability.title: Bounding martingale dimension by spectral dimension
Probability.summary: We prove that the martingale dimension of a broad class of strongly local regular Dirichlet forms is bounded above by a small-scale version of spectral dimension. This resolves a conjecture of Hino for this class of spaces, extending his earlier results beyond self-similar fractals. Our proof uses differentiation of energy measures to select good blow-up scales and construct approximately harmonic coordinates. We then study weak limits of their Euclidean image measures and combine an integration-by-parts argument with uniform Sobolev inequalities to establish the dimension bound.

Probability.title: Sharp potential and Brenier map $W_2$-stability for log-concave sources
Probability.summary: We study stability of Brenier potentials and maps under changes of the target measure. Let $κ>0$, for a full support $κ$-strongly log-concave source $ρ$, possibly with a non-smooth potential, the normalized transport potentials satisfy \[ \|u_μ-u_ν\|_{L^2(ρ)}\leqslant\sqrt{2/κ}\,W_2(μ,ν) \] for arbitrary targets with finite second moments. The proof controls normalized Laguerre cell barycentres by their mass derivatives and centers the potential velocity to remove unbounded source cell locations. Bounded variation interpolation then yields the sharp map exponent $1/3$ for targets in a common compact set, \[ \left\Vert T_μ-T_ν\right\Vert _{L^{2}(ρ)}\leqslant \operatorname{Const} \cdot W_{2}\left( μ,ν\right) ^{1/3}. \] Sharpness of the exponents for both the potential and Brenier map stability are established.

Probability.title: A Class of Gaussian Fields on $\mathbb{Z}_q^d$
Probability.summary: Complex Gaussian fields $(g_x)$ on $\mathbb{Z}_q^d$ are constructed from a class of reversible long range random walks $(X_t)_{t\in \mathbb{N}}$ on $\mathbb{Z}_q^d$ in \citeauthor{GM2025a} (\citeyear{GM2025a}). The construction is from taking $\mathbb{E}\big [g_x\bar{g}_y\big ]= (1-α)G(x,y;α)$, where $G(x,y;α)$ is the Green function of a random walk with killing in each transition at rate $1-α$. Another real Gaussian field $(h^\circ_x=\Re g_x + \Im g_x)$ is constructed such that also Cov$(h^\circ_x,h^\circ_y) = (1-α)G(x,y;α)$. If the random walk is not reversible, then a different approach is needed because $G(x,y;α)$ is not exchangeable in $x,y$. It is shown that there exists two real Gaussian fields $(h^+_x)$, $(h^-_y)$ such that Cov$(h^+_x,h^-_y) = (1-α)G(x,y;α)$. A decomposition of the Gaussian field $(g_x)$ into a sum of independent Gaussian random variables is made. By letting $q\to \infty$ the Gaussian field becomes defined from an infinite-dimensional random walk on a torus. The random walk model is also extended to $d=\infty$ by considering a de Finetti random walk where entries in the increments of the random walk are exchangeable. A limit Gaussian field on $\mathbb{R}^d$ arises from a central limit theorem approach. The transform of this Gaussian field, which is again a Gaussian field, is calculated. It has a simpler covariance matrix than the original field. The Hamiltonian connected to the Gaussian field is calculated. A limit theorem for the partition function arising from the Hamiltonian is found.

Probability.title: Bregman projections and partition design for accelerating finite Markov chains
Probability.summary: We study Gibbs averaging of finite Markov chains with a prescribed stationary distribution $π$. Given a transition matrix $P$ and the Gibbs kernel $G$ induced by a state-space partition, we prove that $GPG$ is an information projection for every admissible Bregman generator $φ$, with divergences defined using transition probabilities relative to $π$. A Pythagorean identity characterizes this projection and recovers the relative entropy and weighted Frobenius cases. A dual characterization identifies $GPG$ as a kernel closest to stationarity among those with the same projection chain as $P$; for relative entropy, it maximizes the entropy rate. The identities also give monotonicity under partition coarsening. For every reversible ergodic baseline $P$, Gibbs averaging cannot increase the squared weighted Frobenius distance to stationarity at any positive integer time, and the inequality is strict unless $P=GPG$. The corresponding mixing time therefore cannot increase. To choose the partition, we identify the divergence of $G$ from stationarity as the exact worst-case divergence of $GPG$ over all $π$-stationary baselines $P$. This objective depends only on the block masses. We give an exact algorithm for concave block costs, including those arising from relative entropy and power generators $φ(u)=u^p$ with $1<p<2$, and a greedy approximation algorithm with a provable guarantee for $p>2$. For power generators $φ(u)=u^p$ with $p>1$, the objective is proportional to Tsallis entropy of order $2-p$: its minimization favors imbalanced block masses when $1<p<2$ and balanced block masses when $p>2$, while all $k$-block partitions have the same objective value when $p=2$. A numerical experiment compares the resulting projected chains with a local Metropolis sampler on a multi-modal $π$.

Probability.title: Well-posedness of Rough Differential Equations at the Krylov-Röckner Integrability Threshold
Probability.summary:
We study rough differential equations (RDEs) driven by Brownian (Itô) rough paths with uniformly locally integrable drifts. The diffusion coefficient is assumed to be uniformly elliptic, of class $C^{2+}$ in space and of bounded variation in time, while the drift is $q$-integrable in time and $p$-integrable in space, uniformly on balls of a fixed radius, for some $p,q$ satisfying the Krylov--Röckner condition $\frac dp+\frac2q<1$. We show that, for almost every realization of the Itô rough path lift of the Brownian motion, such an RDE has a unique solution for every initial value. In other words, for almost every realization of the Itô lift, the corresponding rough differential equation has exactly one solution in the class of Davie-type solutions, for every initial value; this is the appropriate notion of path-by-path uniqueness for the corresponding stochastic differential equation (SDE) with multiplicative noise.
  The proof follows the strategy of Shaposhnikov (2016). The principal new ingredients are the stability of RDEs with bounded variation perturbation and Davie-type estimates for the flow of the driftless equation with non-constant diffusion coefficients, which we derive from known maximal regularity estimates for the corresponding parabolic partial differential equations (PDEs).

Probability.title: A New Modifications of the Milstein and Euler Methods and the Taylor-Ito Expansion for Ito Stochastic Differential Equations with Drift and Diffusion Coefficients Having Non-Differentiable or Singular Time-Dependent Multipliers
Probability.summary: The article presents a new modifications of the Milstein and Euler methods for systems of Ito stochastic differential equations with drift and diffusion coefficients having differentiable and non-differentiable or singular power-law time-dependent components (the latter depending only on the time variable). By iteratively applying Ito's formula to the mentioned differentiable components of the drift and diffusion coefficients, a new modification of the Milstein method is derived in the paper. A key feature of this modification of the Milstein method is the presence of time-dependent weight functions in the iterated Ito stochastic integrals of the second and first multiplicity (the specified weight functions are identically equal to unity in the classical Milstein method). To approximate the specified iterated Ito stochastic integrals (with respect to the components of a multidimensional Wiener process) that involve time-dependent weight functions, the paper proposes using the method of generalized multiple Fourier series, introduced by the author in 2006. The article also provides a modification of the Euler method and the Taylor-Ito expansion for Ito SDEs with non-differentiable or singular drift and diffusion coefficients. The convergence rates of the proposed modifications of the Milstein and Euler methods are established.

Probability.title: An Autonomous Spectral Representation for Fully Asymmetric Spherical Sherrington-Kirkpatrick Dynamics
Probability.summary: We study the large size dynamics of a fully asymmetric spherical Sherrington- Kirkpatrick model, allowing for a distinguished random signal that interacts with the evolving spin configuration. We first derive the large-N dynamical mean-field limit and characterize the law of a typical coordinate by an effective Gaussian process whose covariance must satisfy a self-consistency relation. The resulting formulation is intrinsically nonlocal in time and is not, in its usual form, a closed finite-dimensional dynamical system. Our main contribution is an autonomous spectral representation of this limiting dynamics. We introduce an auxiliary stationary chain of Gaussian replicas whose one-step marginal reproduces the effective field appearing in the dynamical mean- field equation. Applying a matrix-valued Herglotz representation, or equivalently Fourier analysis in the replica index, converts the covariance structure of the chain into a family of finite-dimensional matrix-valued evolution equations indexed by the unit circle. The macroscopic observables, including the signal overlap, are then recovered from explicit spectral integrals. This representation replaces the original two-time self-consistency problem by an autonomous spectral closure and provides a convenient framework for both analysis and numerical computation. We prove the validity of the representation and compare its predictions with direct simulations of the finite-dimensional system

Differential Geometry.title: Multicomplexes in Action: Strong Formality of Compact Hyperkähler Manifolds
Differential Geometry.summary: We show that all compact hyperkähler manifolds are bigraded strongly formal in the sense of Milivojević and Stelzig, proving that in the context of pluripotential homotopy theory they play the same role as compact Kähler manifolds in rational homotopy theory. Indeed, the main result arises from general algebraic considerations on categories of objects with more differentials, that of multicomplexes and commutative $n$-differential graded algebras. For them we discuss a standard model category structure, introduce a generalization of the $\partial\bar{\partial}$-Lemma and establish an algebraic formality theorem.

Differential Geometry.title: Some remarks on robust features of surfaces in 4-space
Differential Geometry.summary: We study robust features of smooth surfaces in 4-space associated with contact with lines and hyperplanes. We investigate the local and multi-local singularities of orthogonal projections and height functions that describe these contacts and their corresponding geometric loci on the surface. At an $A_4$-singularity of a height function, we show that the $A_3$-curve and the $A_1A_2$-curve are generically tangent with contact of order $2$. We further establish criteria for the versality of the families of height functions and orthogonal projections in terms of the regularity of the $B_2$-curve and $S_2$-curve, respectively. Finally, we obtain the $[A_2]$- and $(A_0S_0)_2$-curves arising from multi-local singularities of orthogonal projections and describe their tangency properties at the $B_3$- and $H_3$-singularities.

Differential Geometry.title: Willmore inequalities beyond the injectivity radius
Differential Geometry.summary: We generalize a method first introduced by Li, Yau, Simon, and Topping (for closed surfaces immersed in the flat Euclidean space), and we establish a global-in-nature estimate, with an explicit cut-locus contribution, on the Willmore energy of closed surfaces that are immersed in a complete Riemannian three-manifold and need not be embedded. Our estimate applies to ambient spaces whose sectional curvature is bounded above and whose injectivity radius may be finite. For positive upper curvature bounds, the global weighted estimates require an explicit radius restriction. The Willmore energy is bounded below by a functional involving the self-intersection number of the surface and the injectivity radius of the ambient space. Furthermore, by investigating in what sense our inequalities are optimal and realized by geodesic spheres in constant curvature spaces, we are led to introduce a weighted version of the Willmore functional, which is adapted to geodesic spheres in the model spaces and takes the sectional curvature of the ambient space into account. As a corollary, we obtain sufficient conditions for an immersed surface in a curved space to be embedded.

Differential Geometry.title: Localization in Seven-Dimensional Supergravity
Differential Geometry.summary: Seven-dimensional supergravity provides holographic access to strongly coupled six-dimensional superconformal theories through its highest-dimensional supersymmetric AdS vacua. Its unique spinor-bilinear geometry and massive higher-form dynamics make systematic analysis and solution-finding distinctively challenging. Relative equivariant localization can obtain supersymmetric observables in odd dimensions from fixed-point data on an auxiliary even-dimensional filling, without an explicit solution. We extend this approach to seven dimensions in maximal Cartan-gauged supergravity with all gauge fields active. We formulate the Euclidean action and Killing-spinor equations in terms of field strengths, and construct a bilinear system adapted to the change in spinor reality conditions from symplectic-Majorana to Majorana. On the non-null gauged active spinor branch, independent, oppositely R-charged spinors are paired by Majorana conjugation on the same complex background. One algebraic gauging correction and two algebraic bilinear projections suffice to extend the equal-charge sector to independent Cartan charges, and the underlying efficient reorganization also applies in the Lorentzian theory. Massive 3-form self-duality fixes the quartic anomaly class and determines the higher-form fixed-point datum from Abelian moment maps. Localization at the single fixed point of the filling recovers the general supersymmetric AdS$_7$ black-hole action, without extending the solution. We prove gauge-covariant Killing-spinor invariance under the combined supersymmetric Killing flow and R-symmetry action, deriving the linear chemical-potential constraint. Extremizing the constrained entropy functional and requiring real positive stationary entropy yields the nonlinear charge relation within the Euclidean analysis, equivalent to Lorentzian horizon extremality for the known spherical black-hole family.

Differential Geometry.title: Existence and uniqueness of radial bound states with prescribed number of nodes for nonlinear dispersive equations on spherically symmetric manifolds
Differential Geometry.summary: Standing waves $e^{iωt}u(x)$ of nonlinear dispersive equations, such as the nonlinear Schrödinger and Klein--Gordon equations, have a profile $u$ that solves the semilinear elliptic equation $Δu+f(u)=0$. We prove the existence of radial bound states with a prescribed number of nodal surfaces for this equation on a large class of spherically symmetric manifolds and for a broad class of nonlinearities $f$. Under further assumptions on the metric, we prove uniqueness of such bound states for the model nonlinearity $f(u)=|u|^{p-1}u-u$. Both existence and uniqueness results apply to the hyperbolic spaces $\mathbb{H}^n_λ$ of any curvature $-λ^2$ and dimension $n\geq 3$, and to some manifolds with a singularity at the origin.

Differential Geometry.title: Scalar curvature bounds and tangent cones for Kähler--Ricci shrinkers
Differential Geometry.summary: We prove a uniform scalar curvature bound, depending only on the dimension, for Kähler--Ricci shrinkers. We also prove that every noncompact Kähler--Ricci shrinker has a unique tangent cone at infinity, naturally homeomorphic to the base of its polarized Fano fibration. For shrinkers with maximal volume growth, this cone is isometric to the metric completion of the regular part equipped with the intrinsic distance induced by the limiting Kähler metric.
Differential Geometry.comment: v2: Added metric-completion results for Kähler-Ricci shrinkers with maximal volume growth and finite-time singularities of volume-noncollapsed Kähler-Ricci flows

Differential Geometry.title: Complete Kähler Manifolds with pinched Ricci curvature
Differential Geometry.summary: In this paper, we prove that a connected complete Kähler manifold of complex dimension at least two satisfying $\Ric\geq\varepsilon Rg\geq0$ for a fixed $\varepsilon>0$ is compact or Ricci-flat.

Differential Geometry.title: Uniform large-genus asymptotics of Weil-Petersson volumes
Differential Geometry.summary: Let $V_{g,n}$ be the Weil--Petersson volume of the moduli space of hyperbolic surfaces of genus $g$ with $n$ cusps. The fixed-$n$ large-genus expansion of Mirzakhani and Zograf has correction terms polynomial in $n$ of degree $2i$ at order $g^{-i}$, and ceases to be uniform when $n$ is of order $\sqrt g$. We prove an asymptotic expansion in powers of $1/g$ that holds uniformly in all $n\ge0$, with coefficients analytic in a density parameter that ranges over a compact interval, including the limits $n/g\to0$ and $n/g\to\infty$. Its leading term is explicit, contains no undetermined constant and has relative error $O(1/g)$; truncation at an order proportional to $\sqrt g$ gives relative error $O(\exp(-a\sqrt g))$ for some $a>0$. For fixed $n$ this confirms Zograf's conjecture that the constant in the Mirzakhani--Zograf asymptotics is $1/\sqrtπ$. We also determine, at every cusp density, the limits of the volume ratios $V_{g,n}/V_{g-1,n+2}$ and $V_{g,n+1}/(2gV_{g,n})$ and, in all degrees, the asymptotics of the ratios of adjacent coefficients of the one-boundary volume polynomial; this answers two questions of Mirzakhani. The proof deforms mixed $κ_1$--$ψ$ intersection numbers into pure $ψ$ intersection numbers along a family whose recursion has nonnegative coefficients, fixes the overall constant through Painlevé I without assuming resurgence, and recovers individual volumes by a local limit theorem in the number of cusps. As an application, the spectral gap of a Weil--Petersson random surface with $n\gg\sqrt g$ cusps tends to zero in probability; this removes the restriction $n/g\to0$ from a theorem of Shen and Wu.
Differential Geometry.comment: 111 pages, no figures. v3: added the critical-scale primitive length spectrum; revised and expanded proofs, exposition and references. An earlier version (Zenodo v1) was published on 16 October 2026: https://zenodo.org/records/23414478

Differential Geometry.title: Irreducible groups and ergodicity in the boundary
Differential Geometry.summary: We show that if $G$ is a real semi-simple Lie group, and $Γ$ is a discrete subgroup of $G$ containing a subgroup $Σ$ acting ergodically (in a strong sense) on the Furstenberg boundary of $G$, then $Γ$ is not isomorphic to a free product of $Σ$ with $\mathbb{Z}$. Moreover, if $Σ$ has algebraic entries, then $Γ$ has algebraic entries as well. As a consequence, we show that if all irreducible discrete subgroups of ${\rm SL}_2(\mathbb{R}) \times {\rm SL}_2(\mathbb{R})$ act ergodically on $\mathbb{S}^1\times \mathbb{S}^1 $, such groups cannot be free groups (or even Gromov hyperbolic). In the appendix, we discuss a connection between the existence of discrete irreducible groups and diophantine properties of Lie groups.
Differential Geometry.comment: Theorem 1.1 is added, and some minor revisions and corrections are made

Differential Geometry.title: Ricci curvature of semigroup walks on graphs and generator representations
Differential Geometry.summary: We present an operator-theoretic framework for the Ollivier--Ricci curvature of (one-parameter families of) random walks generated by positive semigroups on graphs. On a metrically complete graph $(G,d)$ that is $d$-locally finite, we introduce a class of admissible semigroup random walks whose infinitesimal first-order approximation is itself a random walk. We prove that the Ollivier--Ricci curvature of an admissible semigroup random walk is well-defined and completely determined by its first-order approximation. We then establish a variational representation of the curvature of random walks in terms of a notion of the initial-time generator. This representation applies in particular to admissible semigroup random walks. Finally, we use this representation to define an operator-theoretic Ollivier--Ricci curvature for operators acting on spaces of functions over general metric spaces and establish sufficient conditions for well-definedness. This framework contains, in particular, Markovian random walks associated with discrete Laplacians.
Differential Geometry.comment: 20 pages. Comments and suggestions are welcomed

Differential Geometry.title: A complete solution to the reverse isoperimetric problem for $λ$-convex bodies
Differential Geometry.summary: For a given $λ> 0$, a convex body in $\mathbb{R}^n$ is called $λ$-convex if it is the intersection of balls of radius $1/λ$. We show that among all $λ$-convex bodies in $\mathbb R^n$ of a given surface area, volume is minimized by the $λ$-convex lens, that is, the intersection of two balls of radius $1/λ$. This confirms a conjecture of Borisenko in all dimensions $n \geq 2$. Moreover, we extend this reverse isoperimetric inequality to all model spaces of constant curvature in arbitrary dimension and arbitrary $λ> 0$.

Differential Geometry.title: Levi-Civita's type theorem for projectively equivalent sub-Riemannian metrics on step 2 distributions
Differential Geometry.summary: This paper extends the classical results of Eisenhart (1923) and Levi-Civita (1896) on the classification of pairs of germs of Riemannian metrics with the same geodesics, either as parametrized curves (affine equivalence) or as unparametrized curves (projective equivalence), to sub-Riemannian metrics on arbitrary step 2 distributions: at every stable point in the projective case and at every point in the affine case. This extends the results of Zelenko (2004) for contact and even-contact distributions and the affine result of Lin and Zelenko (2024) for step 2 distributions with ad-surjective Tanaka symbols; our projective result covers the ad-surjective case as well. In the affine case, we prove that if a sub-Riemannian metric admits an affinely equivalent metric that is not constantly proportional to it, then locally it is a product of two sub-Riemannian metrics. In the projective case, we prove the 2019 conjecture of Jean, Maslovskaya, and Zelenko on generalized Levi-Civita pairs; in particular, the distribution admits a product structure, the squares of its components are involutive, and the restrictions of the two metrics to each leaf of the corresponding foliation are conformal to each other under the appropriate pullback. The proof is based on a new graph-theoretic formalism, in which compatible moving frames are represented by the vertices and edges of certain graphs. As a byproduct, we introduce a new discrete invariant of step 2 nilpotent graded Lie algebras, the characteristic tuple. The compatible graphs are used on the open dense set where this tuple is locally constant; the resulting bracket relations are identities between smooth tensors, so they extend by continuity across the points where the tuple jumps. Consequently, our classification holds without any assumption of local constancy of the characteristic tuple.
Differential Geometry.comment: 81 pages, 1 table. Based on the PhD thesis of the first author, written under the supervision of the second author and defended at Texas A&M University in September 2026

Differential Geometry.title: Whitham Deformations of Nodal Spectral Curves of the Sinh-Gordon Equation
Differential Geometry.summary: Spectral curves of constant mean curvature tori in Euclidean three-space are real hyperelliptic curves carrying two meromorphic differentials with integral periods. Deformations that preserve the periods, called Whitham deformations, are well understood for nonsingular curves, where the isoperiodic sets are manifolds. We extend Whitham deformations to curves with ordinary double points that are fixed by the real involution. At such curves the isoperiodic sets remain manifolds and are transverse to the curves with double points, so Whitham deformations can change the genus of the spectral curve. We describe how the double points open, and when the derivative of the normalized Willmore energy vanishes at a nodal curve. By inserting double points, we show that every value of a discrete invariant of the isoperiodic sets found in previous work occurs.

Differential Geometry.title: Index and nullity of critical spherical catenoids in hyperbolic three-space
Differential Geometry.summary: We prove that every critical spherical catenoid in a geodesic ball of hyperbolic three-space has Morse index four and nullity two. This resolves Medvedev's index conjecture throughout the parameter range of the catenoid family. The kernel consists precisely of the normal components of rotations that preserve the center of the ball and tilt the axis of the catenoid. As consequences, the radius of the supporting ball increases strictly along the family, and each critical spherical catenoid admits a smooth family of free boundary constant mean curvature deformations in its supporting ball. The proof combines a global boundary inequality obtained from a Wronskian, a positive Dirichlet eigenfunction supplied by the time component of the unit normal, and a Riccati comparison for the angular mode $k=2$. A ground-state identity then yields positivity of every angular mode $k\ge2$.
Differential Geometry.comment: 14 pages. v2: added a corollary on equivariant nondegeneracy and free boundary CMC deformations (Corollary 11) and a self-contained proof that $r(a) \to 0$ as $a \to 1/2$ (Lemma 10); references added. Main theorem unchanged

Differential Geometry.title: Hypersurface and Foliation Isoparametric Transfer for Generalized $(α,β)$-Metrics
Differential Geometry.summary: Let $F=αΦ(q,s)$ be a regular generalized $(α,β)$-metric, where $q=\|β\|_α^2$ and $s=β/α$, endowed with the Busemann--Hausdorff or Holmes--Thompson volume. We derive explicit comparison formulas for the induced hypersurface volume and the associated volume mean curvature and use them to study two transfer problems suggested by the Randers case. The first asks whether the same hypersurface is isoparametric for $α$ and $F$; the second asks whether the same regular foliation is isoparametric for both metrics. Exact local and global criteria are obtained. Their Randers specializations recover the corresponding hypersurface transfer and the condition $df(W)=\varphi(f)$. We also prove an all-normal induced-volume rigidity theorem and construct a complete non-Randers example realizing both transfer mechanisms.

Differential Geometry.title: Alexandrov--Fenchel inequalities for weighted curvature integrals in space forms
Differential Geometry.summary: We establish two types of Alexandrov--Fenchel inequalities for the weighted curvature integrals of static convex domains in space forms. The first type consists of a complete family of inequalities involving three weighted curvature integrals, with the second Minkowski type inequality of Xia [Calc. Var. Partial Differential Equations 55 (2016), Art. 96] and the weighted almost Schur lemma of Li and Xia [J. Differential Geom. 113 (2019), pp. 493--518] as special cases. The second type consists of a complete family of inequalities involving two weighted curvature integrals, confirming a conjectured geometric inequality by Hu and Li [Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. 375 (2022), pp. 5587--5615]. The key novelty lies in observing that, via the orthogonal projection map, the weighted curvature integrals for domains in space forms admit a natural interpretation in terms of mixed volumes of Euclidean convex bodies, thus reducing the problem to the classical Alexandrov--Fenchel inequalities in convex geometry.

Differential Geometry.title: A Dolbeault complex for the contact quantised flag manifolds of type $\mathrm{C}_{2}$ and $\mathrm{D}_{4}$
Differential Geometry.summary: Differential calculi on non-irreducible quantised flag manifolds of the $\mathrm{A}$-series have recently been investigated using Lusztig positive root vectors, revealing that several features of classical differential geometry persist in the noncommutative setting. We extend this investigation to quantised flag manifolds associated with the lowest-rank quantum groups of types $\mathrm{C}$ and $\mathrm{D}$ whose classical spaces are holomorphic contact manifolds. Building on the Heckenberger--Kolb framework, we construct covariant first order differential calculi. The maximal prolongations of calculi restricted to contact directions have lower dimensions than their classical counterparts. In type $\mathrm{C}_2$, however, adjoining the Reeb direction yields a three-dimensional calculus on the contact flag manifold whose maximal prolongation has classical dimension. Adjoining the remaining simple-root direction yields a four-dimensional calculus on the full flag manifold, again with a maximal prolongation of classical dimension. For both calculi, we explicitly present the exterior algebras and identify them with those of the corresponding framing calculi on the quantum group. In type $\mathrm{D}_4$, we show that adjoining the Reeb direction yields a nine-dimensional calculus on the contact flag. We conjecture that its maximal prolongation also has classical dimension.

Differential Geometry.title: Brownian motion in Minkowski normed spaces
Differential Geometry.summary:
A Minkowski normed space is the Euclidean space equipped with a (possibly asymmetric) uniformly convex and smooth norm, forming a particular class of Finsler manifolds.
  We construct a stochastic process with one-dimensional time marginal densities given by the fundamental solution to the nonlinear Finsler heat equation in Minkowski normed spaces.
  This process is constructed as a solution to a singular McKean--Vlasov stochastic differential equation and constitutes a nonlinear Markov process in the sense of McKean.
  We show that solutions to this stochastic differential equation are pathwise unique, and, thus, probabilistically strong solutions, though the equation has singular coefficients beyond the subcritical regime.
  Since our construction is a natural extension of the construction of standard Brownian motion from the standard heat kernel, we call this process \emph{Brownian motion in Minkowski normed spaces.}
  Furthermore, we obtain a universality property, namely that whichever Minkowski norm is chosen, the radial part of this process is the standard Bessel process.
  To the best of our knowledge, this is the first construction of stochastic processes associated with nonlinear heat equation in Finslerian spaces.

Differential Geometry.title: Minimal Products via Weighted Spheres
Differential Geometry.summary:
We establish an exact composition principle for spherical immersions coupled through coefficient profiles and norm-preserving bilinear maps. Under explicit mixed orthogonality, the spherical mean curvature vector splits into orthogonal input and profile contributions. The composition is minimal if and only if every input is minimal and the profile is $W$-minimal for the induced monomial weight. Tensor iteration allows weighted profiles to serve as inputs in further compositions.
  At fixed weights, Hsiang--Lawson reduction and Kapouleas--McGrath doubling yield closed embedded $W$-minimal profiles. When the effective exponents tend to infinity in positive limiting proportions, Gaussian transfer produces interior coefficient profiles from closed embedded self-shrinkers that are nondegenerate modulo rotations. The number of distinct corresponding profiles is bounded below by the Lusternik--Schnirelmann category of the rotation orbit.
Differential Geometry.comment: improved version with updated title and references

Differential Geometry.title: Integrable and non-integrable LR geodesic flows on 5-dimensional 2-step nilpotent Lie groups
Differential Geometry.summary: We investigate sub-Riemannian geodesic flows on 5-dimensional nilpotent Lie groups endowed with left-invariant Riemannian metrics. Up to isomorphism, there are exactly two such groups: the Heisenberg group $H_5$ and the 5-dimensional nilpotent Lie group with a 2-dimensional commutator subgroup. For each group, we study geodesic flows associated with both left-invariant (LL) and right-invariant (LR) distributions, deriving explicit descriptions of the corresponding geodesics and comparing their integrability properties. While the LL systems are known to be Liouville integrable, and even superintegrable, we show that LR systems are Liouville integrable only in two cases: on the Heisenberg group and, for the second group, on a distinguished invariant level set.

Differential Geometry.title: Modified support measures and Alexandrov-Fenchel type inequalities for nonsmooth h-convex bodies in hyperbolic space
Differential Geometry.summary:
We establish the Alexandrov-Fenchel inequality and its modified version for arbitrary, possibly nonsmooth, horospherically convex bodies in hyperbolic space $\mathbb{H}^{n+1}, n\geq 2$, and prove that equality in each inequality holds if and only if the h-convex body is a geodesic ball. A key ingredient is a rigidity theorem characterizing geodesic balls via proportionality between modified support measures of adjacent orders. Its proof combines the $C^{1,α}\cap W^{2,k+1}$ approximation of the outer parallel hypersurfaces by smooth strictly h-convex hypersurfaces with the estimates for the total variation norm of the signed measure associated with the proportionality relation along the shifted curvature flows independent of initial curvature bounds.
  For $0\leq k\leq n-1$, we construct weak flows preserving the $k$-th modified quermassintegral $\tilde{W}_k$ with arbitrary h-convex initial bodies as Hausdorff limits of the smooth flows. The rigidity theorem above characterizes the limit shape of the flow and gives a positive lower bound on the rate of decrease of $\tilde{W}_{k+1}$ for a short time whenever the initial h-convex body is not a geodesic ball, which characterizes the equality cases in the modified Alexandrov-Fenchel inequality.
  For the Alexandrov-Fenchel inequality, we establish the Hausdorff stability independent of curvature bounds described by the Alexandrov-Fenchel deficits for h-convex bodies, which characterizes the equality cases in the Alexandrov-Fenchel inequality.

Differential Geometry.title: Three-dimensional noncompact trans-Sasakian $η$-Einstein manifolds
Differential Geometry.summary: We classify connected, simply connected, noncompact three-dimensional trans-Sasakian $η$-Einstein manifolds. In [1], we showed that, in the compact case, such a manifold is either of $β$-Kenmotsu type or homothetic to a Sasakian manifold. In this paper, in the noncompact case, we find families of trans-Sasakian $η$-Einstein manifolds that are neither $β$-Kenmotsu nor homothetic to Sasakian manifolds. These families have infinitely many degrees of freedom. We give these nontrivial metrics explicitly. We also give a structure theorem for the case in which the characteristic vector field is Palais-nonregular.

Differential Geometry.title: A New Invariant for Doubly Periodic Solutions of the Sinh-Gordon Equation
Differential Geometry.summary: Spectral curves of constant mean curvature tori in Euclidean three-space are real hyperelliptic curves carrying two meromorphic differentials with integral periods. These transcendental period conditions are studied through Whitham deformations, which deform the curve while preserving the periods. We extend Whitham deformations to all real hyperelliptic curves of this type, by holding fixed the plane spanned by the periods, or this plane together with its complex structure. Under mild nondegeneracy conditions the resulting isoperiodic sets are manifolds of dimensions three and one, respectively. Along the one-dimensional isoperiodic sets, a generalization of the Willmore energy is a local parameter away from its critical points, to which the spectral curves of tori belong. Finally, using homology bases adapted to the branch points, we find discrete invariants of the isoperiodic sets of doubly periodic curves: a triple of integers and a refined conformal type.

Differential Geometry.title: Planarity estimates and codimension reduction for ancient flows at the Andrews-Baker threshold
Differential Geometry.summary: We derive an interior planarity estimate for space-time proper mean curvature flows of $n$-dimensional submanifolds of $\mathbb R^{n+p}$, $n\geq5$, that are uniformly quadratically pinched up to the Andrews-Baker threshold $\frac{4}{3n}$. The estimate is parabolically scale-invariant and it requires neither curvature nor entropy bounds. The proof combines Naff's gradient estimates with a localization argument in the spirit of Ecker and Huisken. In dimensions five and six, Naff's estimates alone do not give the gradient terms a sign. We bound these terms from below with an argument we developed in a previous work. As a consequence, for $n\geq5$, and by known results for $2\leq n\leq4$, every space-time proper ancient solution that is uniformly $\frac{4}{3n}$-pinched is either a static affine $n$-plane or lies in a fixed affine $(n+1)$-dimensional subspace. This replaces the finite entropy and polynomial curvature growth assumptions of Lee, Naff and Zhu by space-time properness, and improves their pinching constant in dimensions two, five and six. For closed flows, we extend Lynch's planarity estimate to a larger range of exponents.

Differential Geometry.title: Isospectral congruence manifolds, spectral rigidity, and a converse to Vignéras
Differential Geometry.summary: Let $B$ be a quaternion division algebra over a number field $k$ that gives rise to arithmetic Fuchsian or Kleinian groups, and let $\mathcal{O}$ be a maximal order of $B$. We show that every closed orientable Riemannian manifold isospectral to a principal congruence hyperbolic surface $X_\mathcal{O}(\mathfrak{a})$ is isometric to $X_{\mathcal{O}'}(\mathfrak{a})$ for some maximal order $\mathcal{O}'$ of $B$, provided that no prime factor of $\mathfrak{a}$ ramifies in $B$ and that $\mathfrak{a}$ satisfies a mild condition at the primes over $2$. This is a converse to the construction of Vignéras, which produces isospectral manifolds from maximal orders of different types. In particular the spectral genus of $X_\mathcal{O}(\mathfrak{a})$ has at most $t(B)$ elements, and $X_\mathcal{O}(\mathfrak{a})$ is spectrally rigid when the type number $t(B)$ is one. In dimension three we prove the same statements for manifolds that, in addition, have the same complex lengths of closed geodesics. The proof rests on a local result that characterizes, by traces alone, the subgroups of $\mathrm{SL}(2)$ over a $p$-adic ring that are conjugate into a principal congruence subgroup by traces. As applications, every principal congruence Hurwitz surface is spectrally rigid, among them Klein's quartic, the Fricke-Macbeath surface and the surfaces of the first Hurwitz triplet, which partially answers a question of Reid.

Differential Geometry.title: Centro-Affine Differential Geometry and the Log-Minkowski Problem
Differential Geometry.summary: We interpret the log-Brunn-Minkowski conjecture of Böröczky-Lutwak-Yang-Zhang as a spectral problem in centro-affine differential geometry. In particular, we show that the Hilbert-Brunn-Minkowski operator coincides with the centro-affine Laplacian, thus obtaining a new avenue for tackling the conjecture using insights from affine differential geometry. As every strongly convex hypersurface in $\mathbb{R}^n$ is a centro-affine unit-sphere, it has constant centro-affine Ricci curvature equal to $n-2$, in stark contrast to the standard weighted Ricci curvature of the associated metric-measure space, which will in general be negative. In particular, we may use the classical argument of Lichnerowicz and a centro-affine Bochner formula to give a new proof of the Brunn-Minkowski inequality. For origin-symmetric convex bodies enjoying fairly generous curvature pinching bounds (improving with dimension), we are able to show global uniqueness in the $L^p$- and log-Minkowski problems, as well as the corresponding global $L^p$- and log-Minkowski conjectured inequalities. As a consequence, we resolve the isomorphic version of the log-Minkowski problem: for any origin-symmetric convex body $\bar K$ in $\mathbb{R}^n$, there exists an origin-symmetric convex body $K$ with $\bar K \subset K \subset 8 \bar K$, so that $K$ satisfies the log-Minkowski conjectured inequality, and so that $K$ is uniquely determined by its cone-volume measure $V_K$. If $\bar K$ is not extremely far from a Euclidean ball to begin with, an analogous isometric result, where $8$ is replaced by $1+ε$, is obtained as well.
Differential Geometry.comment: Appended an erratum at the end of the published version. We replace the widthdrawn Theorem 6.4 with a corrected lemma, stressing that this does not change the validity of any of the other results in the paper. In particular, we give corrected proofs of Theorems 1.2, 1.5 and 1.7, with their original statements and constants unchanged

Differential Geometry.title: On the geometry of asymptotically conical Ricci shrinkers (I): weighted analysis
Differential Geometry.summary: We develop the weighted Sobolev and Hölder analysis needed to study perturbations of complete asymptotically conical (AC) Ricci shrinkers. Weighted elliptic estimates yield a global weighted divergence-free slice in spaces that retain the asymptotic data at infinity. As a geometric application, we prove pointed Gromov-Hausdorff rigidity of nontrivial AC shrinkers with vanishing infinitesimal solitonic deformation space.

Differential Geometry.title: Brownian motion and stochastic areas on complex partial flag manifolds with blocks of equal size
Differential Geometry.summary: We construct a Brownian motion on complex partial flag manifolds with blocks of equal size as a matrix-valued diffusion from a Brownian motion on the unitary group. This construction leads to an explicit expression for the characteristic function of the joint distribution of the stochastic areas on these manifolds. The limit law of these stochastic areas is shown to be a multivariate Cauchy distribution with independent and identically distributed entries. By relating the area functionals on flag manifolds to the winding functional on the complex Stiefel manifold, we establish new results about simultaneous Brownian windings on the complex Stiefel manifold. To establish these results, this work introduces a new family of diffusions, which generalise both the Jacobi processes on the simplex and the Hermitian Jacobi processes.
Differential Geometry.comment: 28 pages, v2: Minor edits, v3: Updated some sign conventions, corrected a minor normalisation discrepancy in expressions for the horizontal Brownian motion and the contact process + additional minor edits

Differential Geometry.title: A generalization of the Perelman gluing theorem and applications
Differential Geometry.summary: We extend a positive Ricci curvature gluing theorem of Perelman to a range of positive intermediate curvature conditions, ranging from positive scalar curvature up to (and including) positive sectional curvature. As an application of this, we demonstrate that the observer moduli space of metrics with positive intermediate Ricci curvatures can have non-trivial higher homotopy groups. Further applications include deriving a sufficient condition for the existence of a metric with positive intermediate Ricci curvature and totally geodesic boundary.
Differential Geometry.comment: Final version, minor changes, to appear in Mathematische Annalen

Differential Geometry.title: Spectrum of Complete Kähler Metrics on Bounded Hyperconvex Domains
Differential Geometry.summary: Let $Ω\subset\mathbb{C}^{n}$ be a bounded domain, and let $ρ:Ω\to[-1,0)$ be a smooth strictly plurisubharmonic exhaustion function. We consider the logarithmic potential $g=-\log(-ρ)$ and the associated complete Kähler metric $ω=dd^{c} g$. We prove that if $ρ$ satisfies the finite weighted Monge-Ampère mass condition with weight $(-ρ)^{\varepsilon}$ for every $\varepsilon>0$, then the spectrum and the essential spectrum of the Laplace-Beltrami operator of $(Ω,ω)$ both coincide with $[n^{2},\infty)$. In particular, the bottom of the spectrum satisfies $λ_{0}(Δ_ω,Ω)=n^{2}$, and $n^{2}$ is not an $L^{2}$-eigenvalue. For each $α> \frac{n}{2}$, we set $f=(-ρ)^α$ and prove that $f$ belongs to $W^{1,2}(Ω,ω)$ if and only if the Monge-Ampère mass of $ρ$ weighted by $(-ρ)^{2α-n}$ is finite. The integral identities underlying this equivalence, applied to the complex powers $(-ρ)^{α+it}$, give, after normalization, a singular Weyl sequence at every $n^{2}+4t^{2}$, $t\in\mathbb{R}$, as $α\downarrow\frac{n}{2}$. Combining our theorem with Cegrell's finite-mass exhaustion theorem, we obtain a complete Kähler metric with spectrum and essential spectrum equal to $[n^{2},\infty)$ on every bounded hyperconvex domain.
Differential Geometry.comment: 15 pages, no figures. Results extended to determine the full spectrum and essential spectrum

Differential Geometry.title: Reducible Holonomy in Closed Torsion Geometries
Differential Geometry.summary: The purpose of this note is to show that a connection with closed skew-symmetric torsion and reducible holonomy admits a locally defined Riemannian submersion together with a projected geometry on the base. We reframe known submersion results for non-Kähler Bismut-Hermite-Einstein manifolds and sHKT structures in this context. For homogeneous SKT structures on semi-simple Lie groups, we obtain the holonomy decomposition leading to holomorphic submersions over generalized flag manifolds.

Differential Geometry.title: Integral Points and Volume of Integral-Integral Affine Manifolds
Differential Geometry.summary: Using rational Ehrhart theory and Fourier analysis, we give an elementary proof that the volume of a closed manifold equipped with an integral-integral affine structure equals the number of its integral points.

Differential Geometry.title: Three-Dimensional Almost Contact Metric Manifolds Revisited via the Newman-Penrose Formalism
Differential Geometry.summary: This paper applies the Newman-Penrose formalism-a technique primarily used in General Relativity-to the analysis of three-dimensional almost contact metric (ACM) manifolds. We reformulate and discuss several known notions and properties within the Newman-Penrose framework, demonstrating the applicability of the method in this geometric context. Furthermore, as an application showcasing the utility of the formalism, we address the classification of three-dimensional compact normal ACM manifolds, or equivalently trans-Sasakian manifolds, that admit an $η$-Einstein metric.

Differential Geometry.title: A new sharp Sobolev inequality between the $Q$-curvature and the scalar curvature on Euclidean space
Differential Geometry.summary: We establish a sharp Sobolev-type inequality on $\mathbb{R}^n$, $n\geq 5$, that interpolates between the second-order energy and a weighted first-order term. Specifically, we determine the sharp constant $S_{4,2}$ in the inequality \begin{equation*} \int_{\mathbb R^n} (Δu)^2\,dx \ge S_{4,2} \left(\int_{\mathbb{R}^n}|\nabla u|^{2}|u|^{\frac{4}{n-4}}\,dx\right)^{\frac{n-4}{n-2}}, \end{equation*} for any $u\in\dot H^2(\mathbb{R}^n)$, and we classify the cases of equality. This solves the problem of minimizing the total $Q$-curvature of among metrics on the sphere, conformal to the standard metric, with fixed total scalar curvature.

Differential Geometry.title: Lipschitz regularity of Sobolev maps from $\mathrm{RCD}(K,N)$ spaces to $\mathrm{CAT}(0)$ spaces
Differential Geometry.summary: We establish a quantitative criterion for local Lipschitz regularity of Sobolev maps in the sense of Korevaar and Schoen from finite-dimensional \(\RCD(K,N)\) spaces into complete \(\CAT(0)\) spaces, without assuming harmonicity. We quantify the failure of local energy minimality by the harmonic replacement potential, a dyadic sum of the square roots of normalized energy gaps between a map and its harmonic replacements. We prove that this potential, together with an averaged energy term, controls the minimal weak upper gradient pointwise, with constants depending only on the curvature-dimension bounds and the scale. In particular, local boundedness of the replacement potential implies that the map admits a locally Lipschitz representative.

Differential Geometry.title: Riemannian Deep Learning: Modules, Networks, and Geometries
Differential Geometry.summary: Deep neural networks on manifold-valued representations have attracted growing interest, but many basic components remain tied to specific manifolds, rely on Euclidean approximations, or require costly and numerically fragile geometric operations. This thesis develops a unified framework for Riemannian deep learning from three complementary perspectives: reusable neural modules, manifold-specific network architectures, and the design of underlying geometries. It generalizes batch normalization from Euclidean spaces and individual manifolds to broad classes of Lie groups and gyrogroups, and extends multinomial logistic regression from Euclidean space to SPD manifolds and then to general Riemannian manifolds. It further develops neural networks for several important geometric representations, including an unconstrained model of hyperbolic space, Busemann-based hyperbolic learning, and full-rank correlation matrices. Finally, it introduces adaptive and computationally efficient Riemannian metrics on SPD manifolds, including learnable Log-Euclidean geometries and fast, stable Cholesky-based geometries. The proposed methods are supported by theoretical analysis and validated through numerical experiments and applications in vision, signal processing, graph learning, and genomics.
Differential Geometry.comment: PhD thesis manuscript, University of Trento; defense pending

Differential Geometry.title: Observing minimal submanifolds with isolated singularities on open sets of metrics
Differential Geometry.summary: We develop a perturbative theory for minimal submanifolds with only (strongly) isolated singularities, with respect to varying background Riemannian metrics. As an application, we obtain a general "sporadic persistence" criterion, thus naturally complementing the non-persistence theorem by the authors. In particular, such a criterion is satisfied by the spherical suspension in $\mathbb{S}^{3m+2}$ of the Veronese embedding of $\mathbb{K}\mathbb{P}^2$ for $\mathbb{K}=\mathbb{R},\mathbb{C},\mathbb{H},\mathbb{O}$ (the normed division algebras) in the round spheres of dimension $3m+1=4,7,13,25$ respectively, thereby providing families of continuously varying $(2m+1)$-dimensional stationary varifolds with isolated singularities that are observable on an open set of metrics. By our previous results, these phenomena cannot possibly occur in the codimension one scenario.
Differential Geometry.comment: v2: added one item to the bibliography

Differential Geometry.title: Lipschitz volume rigidity for non-collapsed $\rm RCD$ spaces with boundary
Differential Geometry.summary: We study Lipschitz-volume rigidity for non-collapsed ${\rm RCD}(K,N)$ spaces, possibly with boundary. We prove that a measure-preserving $1$-Lipschitz map between such spaces restricts to an isometry from the interior of the domain onto its image, where the latter is equipped with the intrinsic length distance. We then characterize when this interior rigidity extends to an isometric bijection between the whole spaces, in terms of the behavior of the map on the boundaries. Along the way, we establish a rigidity result of independent interest in a more general class of rectifiable metric spaces.

Differential Geometry.title: Formal Neighborhood Equivariant Cohomology and Kirwan Surjectivity at Singular Values
Differential Geometry.summary:
Let \(G\) be a compact Lie group acting Hamiltonianly on a symplectic manifold \(M\) with moment map \(μ:M\to\g^*\). For a singular value \(a\) of \(μ\), the symplectic quotient \(μ^{-1}(a)/G\) is stratified and the classical Kirwan map is not defined. We introduce a \emph{formal neighborhood equivariant cohomology} \(\cH_G^*(a)\) using the slice-groupoid Cartan sheaf and the closed embedding \(μ^{-1}(a)/G\hookrightarrow N_a/G\) for a \(G\)-invariant neighborhood \(N_a\) of \(μ^{-1}(a)\). We define a formal Kirwan map \[κ_{\mathrm{formal}}:H_G^*(M)\longrightarrow \cH_G^*(a).\]
  We prove that it is surjective under a local equivariant homotopy retraction condition on the slice level sets
  \[
  C_x=μ_x^{-1}(a|_{\g_x})\subset S_x,
  \]
  which is satisfied.
  We also prove an equivariant tubular neighborhood theorem for singular level sets: under real analytic/proper or \(G\)-invariant Whitney stratified assumptions, there exists a \(G\)-invariant open neighborhood \(U\) of \(μ^{-1}(a)\) and a \(G\)-equivariant strong deformation retraction \(U\toμ^{-1}(a)\). When such a neighborhood exists, the formal cohomology is canonically isomorphic to the Borel equivariant cohomology of the level set, and the formal Kirwan map is the classical restriction map. The formal framework therefore yields a Kirwan-type map at the singular value with the surjectivity property.
  As an application we recover the even-degree surjectivity theorem of Delarue--Ramacher--Schmitt for \(S^1\)-actions and clarify why odd-degree surjectivity fails in general.

Differential Geometry.title: Montel's theorem and tautness in calibrated geometry
Differential Geometry.summary: We relate the hyperbolicity of a calibrated manifold $(X, φ)$ to the analytic properties of the space of Smith immersions $\mathrm{SmIm}(B^k, X)$ from the Poincare $k$-ball into $X$. In particular, we establish the following calibrated analogue of a theorem of Royden: if $X$ is $φ$-saturated, then $R_φ$- and $K_φ$-hyperbolicity coincide, and either implies the equicontinuity of $\mathrm{SmIm}(B^k, X)$ with respect to the $φ$-distance. This yields a Montel theorem for compact $φ$-saturated calibrated manifolds as an immediate corollary. Our primary technical tool is a new Schwarz lemma for Smith immersions from $B^k$ into $X$, which is of independent interest. In a similar spirit, we also prove a calibrated analogue of Kiernan's theorem to the effect that the $K_φ$-hyperbolicity of $X$ is almost equivalent to $\mathrm{SmIm}(B^k, X)$ being a normal family. Finally, we prove that bounded domains in flat euclidean space are $R_φ$-hyperbolic for any calibration $φ$, and we investigate the hyperbolicity of products and discrete quotients.
Differential Geometry.comment: 31 pages. Version 3: Corrected the statement of the Schwarz lemma, replaced one hypothesis in some theorems with the weaker $φ$-saturation condition, and defined the Kobayashi $φ$-pseudo-distance in full generality

Differential Geometry.title: Uniform estimates for complex Monge-Ampère equations II: Hermitian manifolds
Differential Geometry.summary: We establish uniform estimates for degenerate complex Monge--Ampère equations on compact Hermitian manifolds under weak Orlicz integrability assumptions on the densities. Our estimates apply uniformly to Hermitian metrics and to semipositive uniformly non-collapsing reference forms. For arbitrary big reference forms, we obtain uniform relative $L^\infty$-estimates with respect to the extremal function with minimal singularities, and establish continuity of the resulting solutions on the regular locus. As an application, we prove the existence of solutions with minimal singularities to degenerate complex Monge--Ampère equations associated with big forms. The proofs combine local Orlicz estimates with pluripotential-theoretic envelope techniques and uniform control of the Monge--Ampère masses, overcoming the lack of invariance of the total Monge--Ampère mass in the Hermitian setting.

Differential Geometry.title: Dually flat structure of von Mises-Fisher distributions
Differential Geometry.summary: The von Mises--Fisher (vMF) distribution is the natural exponential family analogue of the normal distribution on the unit hypersphere. We bring together previous results of its dually flat structure and establish new results on the information geometry of the family of vMF distributions. In particular, we characterize the exponential and mixture autoparallel submanifolds, and give the classification of doubly autoparallel submanifolds. Furthermore, we derive explicit formulas for the unique minimizers of the Kullback-Leibler divergence on these submanifolds and establish the corresponding projection theorems.

Differential Geometry.title: Finitely many solutions for the prescribed scalar curvature problem at the critical flatness order
Differential Geometry.summary:
We study the following prescribed scalar curvature problem $$
  -Δu=K(y)u^{2^*-1},\ \ u>0
  \,\ \ \text{in}\ \ \mathbb{R}^N, $$ where $2^*=\frac{2N}{N-2}$. For $N\geq4$, we construct a positive $K(y)$ with maximum set $\{|y|=1\}$ and critical order of flatness $m=N-2$ at $|y|=1$, such that the equation admits only finitely many positive solutions in $D^{1,2}(\mathbb{R}^N)$. To this end, we prove the compactness of the solution set for this equation by blow-up analysis and then apply Sard's theorem to choose $K$ for which each solution is non-degenerate and hence isolated, so that the solution set is finite. Our results also give a definite answer to Wei--Yan's conjecture in [J. Wei and S. Yan, JFA, 2010].

Differential Geometry.title: Gray $\mathcal{A}$-metrics on nilpotent Lie groups and the quasicentroid condition
Differential Geometry.summary: We study left-invariant Gray $\mathcal{A}$-metrics (cyclic-parallel Ricci tensor) on nilpotent Lie groups, focusing on the algebraic condition that the Ricci operator belongs to the quasicentroid $\operatorname{QC}(\mathfrak{n})$ of the Lie algebra $\mathfrak{n}$. We review and develop the abstract structure theory of quasicentroids, and prove a Central Decomposition Theorem: any nilpotent Riemannian Lie algebra with $\operatorname{Ric} \in \operatorname{QC}(\mathfrak{n})$ decomposes as a central product of ideals $\mathfrak{i}_j = E_{λ_j} \oplus \mathfrak{z}$, where $\mathfrak{z}$ is the center of $\mathfrak{n}$ and $E_{λ_j}$ are the negative Ricci eigenspaces. Endowed with the restricted metric, each factor $\mathfrak{i}_j$ is itself a Gray $\mathcal{A}$-space. Finally, we investigate when the general $\mathcal{A}$-metric condition reduces to $\operatorname{Ric} \in \operatorname{QC}(\mathfrak{n})$. We prove this equivalence unconditionally for two-step nilpotent algebras and whenever the metric admits a nice basis, and provide a general characterization via the vanishing of two trace identities.
Differential Geometry.comment: Any comments, corrections, or suggestions are deeply appreciated. 25 pages

Differential Geometry.title: A short proof of Bernstein's theorem via the Omori--Yau maximum principle
Differential Geometry.summary: We give a short, self-contained proof of Bernstein's theorem: every entire minimal graph in $R^3$ is a plane. The only global tool is the Omori-Yau maximum principle, which holds on entire minimal graphs with their induced metric. We apply it exactly once to a single explicit function $F$ built from the surface's angle function and principal curvatures. A pointwise differential inequality for $F$, combined with the Omori-Yau principle, forces it to attain its minimum value everywhere, which yields the planarity of the surface and hence Bernstein's theorem. As a by-product of our approach, we show that the same method, with a different function and with some extra work, also proves in a simple and self-contained way the generalization of Bernstein's theorem given by Osserman that a complete minimal surface in $R^3$ whose normals omit a neighbourhood of some direction must be a plane.
Differential Geometry.comment: 11 pages. New version including new Remark 3.4 (about Simons' formula) and new Remark 5.1 (about the choice of the functions f and F)

Differential Geometry.title: Degeneracies of Lagrange functions and geometric interpretations of Lagrange multipliers
Differential Geometry.summary: We introduce Lagrange functions associated with height and distance-squared functions on implicit plane curves. We show that degeneracies of these functions characterize geometric properties of the curves, such as inflections and vertices, and give geometric interpretations of the corresponding Lagrange multipliers in terms of contact with lines and circles.

Differential Geometry.title: Covariant derivatives in the representation-valued Bott-Shulman-Stasheff and Weil complex
Differential Geometry.summary:
For a Lie groupoid $G$, the differential forms on its nerve comprise a double complex. A natural question is if this statement extends to forms with values in a representation $V$ of $G$. In this paper, we research two types of covariant derivatives which commute with the simplicial differential, yielding two types of curved double complexes of forms with coefficients in $V$. The naive approach is to consider a linear connection $
abla$ on $V$, in which case $d^
abla$ commutes with the simplicial differential if and only if $
abla$ satisfies a certain (restrictive) invariance condition. The heart of this paper focuses on another, more compelling approach: using a multiplicative Ehresmann connection for a bundle of ideals. In this case, we obtain a geometrically richer curved double complex, where the cochain map is given by the horizontal exterior covariant derivative $D$, which generalizes the well-known operator from the theory of principal bundles. Moreover, both differential operators $d^
abla$ and $D$ are researched in the infinitesimal setting of Lie algebroids, as well as their relationship with the van Est map. We conclude by using the operator $D$ to study the curvature of an (infinitesimal) multiplicative Ehresmann connection.

Differential Geometry.title: Minimally-coupled Quasilinear Symmetric Hyperbolic Systems, Naturally
Differential Geometry.summary: We consider symmetric hyperbolicity and well-posedness in the context of natural equations, which are closed subobjects of jet bundles over natural bundles. We show how non-natural equations can be "naturalized", and we discuss how a precise version of "minimal coupling" offers a (provably unique, up to isomorphism) method for constructing natural equations from certain equations defined on a single manifold. We discuss how to define symmetrizers, hyperbolizations, and constraints for minimally coupled natural equations, and we show how these can be used to recover standard existence and uniqueness results, relative to any choice of background structure (a metric, for minimally coupled systems). Additionally, we show that minimal coupling and naturality together imply that the causal cones associated with a (first order, quasilinear, minimally coupled) naturally symmetric hyperbolic natural equation must always coincide with the metric lightcones, and that a certain rank-2 tensor, associates with a natural hyperbolization, must always be divergence free relative to the associated Levi-Civita derivative operator.

Differential Geometry.title: Logarithmic transformations on the six-sphere
Differential Geometry.summary: We show that there are infinitely many choices of the multiplicities in the logarithmic transformation step of the Alpöge--Claude construction which produce a complex threefold diffeomorphic to the six-sphere. Moreover, distinct choices of the multiplicities yield biholomorphically inequivalent complex structures.

Geometric Topology.title: Presentations for sisters of one-cusped Picard modular groups
Geometric Topology.summary: We generalize a method devised by Mark and Paupert for finding group presentations of the single-cusped standard Picard modular groups $\text{PU}(2, 1; \mathcal{O}_d)$, where $\mathcal{O}_d$ is the ring of integers of $\mathbb{Q}(i\sqrt{d})$, to a more general class of lattices in $\text{PU}(2, 1)$. As an application, we give presentations for the so-called \textit{sisters} of the standard Picard modular groups for $d=3, 7,$ and $11$. In particular, this shows that the sister of $\text{PU}(2, 1; \mathcal{O}_7)$ is a perfect group.

Geometric Topology.title: Skein reduction and stabilization for the odd Khovanov spectra of $T(2,m)\sqcup T(2,n)$
Geometric Topology.summary: For split links the even Khovanov spectrum is a smash product of the spectra of the pieces; the odd one is not. For $T(2,m)\sqcup T(2,n)$ we show that the odd spectrum is, in each quantum grading, a wedge of spheres and copies of a suspension of $\mathbb{CP}^{2}$. Using the skein cofiber sequence at the level of spectra, we prove that for fixed $q-m-n$ the number of these copies is determined by finitely many small links and stabilizes for large $m$ and $n$. The $\mathbb{CP}^{2}$ summand of $T(2,3)\sqcup T(2,3)$, due to Schütz and Rajapakse, persists in quantum grading $m+n+8$ for all $m,n\ge3$. We conjecture that the number of copies of $\mathbb{CP}^{2}$ equals the number of copies of $\mathbb{RP}^{2}\wedge\mathbb{RP}^{2}$ in the even spectrum.

Geometric Topology.title: Linking-form splitting and four-dimensional genera of knots
Geometric Topology.summary: By Gilmer's splitting lemma, the linking form of a rational homology sphere that bounds a 4-manifold is the orthogonal sum of a metabolic summand and a summand presented by a form of the rank of the intersection form. The lemma underlies Gilmer's slice genus theorem and the rank criteria of Murakami-Yasuhara and Gilmer-Livingston for nonorientable surfaces and the 4-dimensional clasp number. We show that the lemma and these results, as stated, are false. For each prime $p \equiv 3 \pmod 8$ we construct knots bounding smooth Möbius bands, and knots bounding smooth punctured tori with clasp number one, whose linking forms have no such summand of rank at most two. We then determine what remains true: the lemma holds up to Witt equivalence and for cube-free orders, and its conclusions about summands hold away from exceptional primes and for orientable surfaces of genus at least two. Finally, we find the optimal Witt-class bound for the topological nonorientable 4-genus.

Geometric Topology.title: G-equivariant Alterfold TQFT in any dimension
Geometric Topology.summary: For a discrete group $G$, we construct an $(n+1)$-dimensional $G$-equivariant Alterfold topological quantum field theory from a $G$-equivariant $S^n$-algebra satisfying strong semisimplicity, complete finiteness, and Morita invariance. We use state sum on triangulation to define a partition function and prove that it is invariant under local surgery relations and is invariant under gauge transformations relative to the boundary. If the input is given a reflection-positive structure, the theory is unitary. For $n=2$ and input reconstructed from a strict faithful spherical $G$-fusion category, the restriction to ordinary $G$-cobordisms is naturally isomorphic to the Turaev--Virelizier state-sum HQFT \cite{turaev20123}. A Tambara-Yamagami example recovers the Quon language \cite{liu2017quon} as a $\mathbb{Z}_2$-equivariant Alterfold TQFT.

Geometric Topology.title: The Torelli Group and Euler Class Zero $\mathrm{PSL}(2,\mathbb{R})$ Representations
Geometric Topology.summary: We prove that every representation of a closed surface group of genus at least $3$ into $\mathrm{PSL}(2,\mathbb{R})$ that is sufficiently close (but not equal to) a representation that has non-compact solvable image has a simple closed separating curve that is mapped to a non-trivial elliptic element in $\mathrm{PSL}(2,\mathbb{R})$. This can be seen as evidence for an affirmative answer to a question of Bowditch and a conjecture of Goldman.

Geometric Topology.title: Diamonds: Homology and the Central Series of Groups
Geometric Topology.summary: We establish an analog of a theorem of Stallings which asserts the homomorphisms between the universal nilpotent quotients induced by a homomorphism $G \to H$ of groups are isomorphisms provided a pair of homological conditions are satisfied. Our analogy does not have a homomorphism between $G$ and $H$ but instead $G,H \leq G_0$ that satisfies a similar homological condition. We derive a few applications of this result. First, we show that there exist pairs of non-isomorphic number fields whose absolute Galois groups have isomorphic universal nilpotent quotients. We show that there exists pairs of non-isometric hyperbolic $n$-manifolds whose fundamental groups are residually nilpotent and have isomorphic universal nilpotent quotients. These are the first examples of residually nilpotent Kleinian groups with arbitrarily large nilpotent genus. Complex hyperbolic 2-manifold examples are given as well. Considering Riemann surfaces and complex hyperbolic 2-manifolds as projective curves and surfaces defined over a number field, we show the (outer) action of the absolute Galois group of the field of definition on the universal nilpotent quotients of the geometric fundamental groups are equivalent. This is in contrast to fact that the (outer) Galois action on the geometric fundamental group of a projective hyperbolic curve determines the curve by work of Mochizuki. In particular, the nilpotent representation theory of the geometric fundamental group is not anabelian.
Geometric Topology.comment: Theorem 1.9 is false as stated. The correct version requires additional assumptions and we no longer have an examples. There is nothing that can be salvaged

Geometric Topology.title: Isospectral congruence manifolds, spectral rigidity, and a converse to Vignéras
Geometric Topology.summary: Let $B$ be a quaternion division algebra over a number field $k$ that gives rise to arithmetic Fuchsian or Kleinian groups, and let $\mathcal{O}$ be a maximal order of $B$. We show that every closed orientable Riemannian manifold isospectral to a principal congruence hyperbolic surface $X_\mathcal{O}(\mathfrak{a})$ is isometric to $X_{\mathcal{O}'}(\mathfrak{a})$ for some maximal order $\mathcal{O}'$ of $B$, provided that no prime factor of $\mathfrak{a}$ ramifies in $B$ and that $\mathfrak{a}$ satisfies a mild condition at the primes over $2$. This is a converse to the construction of Vignéras, which produces isospectral manifolds from maximal orders of different types. In particular the spectral genus of $X_\mathcal{O}(\mathfrak{a})$ has at most $t(B)$ elements, and $X_\mathcal{O}(\mathfrak{a})$ is spectrally rigid when the type number $t(B)$ is one. In dimension three we prove the same statements for manifolds that, in addition, have the same complex lengths of closed geodesics. The proof rests on a local result that characterizes, by traces alone, the subgroups of $\mathrm{SL}(2)$ over a $p$-adic ring that are conjugate into a principal congruence subgroup by traces. As applications, every principal congruence Hurwitz surface is spectrally rigid, among them Klein's quartic, the Fricke-Macbeath surface and the surfaces of the first Hurwitz triplet, which partially answers a question of Reid.

Geometric Topology.title: A generalization of the Perelman gluing theorem and applications
Geometric Topology.summary: We extend a positive Ricci curvature gluing theorem of Perelman to a range of positive intermediate curvature conditions, ranging from positive scalar curvature up to (and including) positive sectional curvature. As an application of this, we demonstrate that the observer moduli space of metrics with positive intermediate Ricci curvatures can have non-trivial higher homotopy groups. Further applications include deriving a sufficient condition for the existence of a metric with positive intermediate Ricci curvature and totally geodesic boundary.
Geometric Topology.comment: Final version, minor changes, to appear in Mathematische Annalen

Geometric Topology.title: Local wild mapping class groups and cabled braids
Geometric Topology.summary: We will define and study some generalisations of pure $\mathfrak{g}$-braid groups that occur in the theory of connections on curves, for any complex reductive Lie algebra $\mathfrak{g}$. They make up local pieces of the wild mapping class groups, which are fundamental groups of (universal) deformations of wild Riemann surfaces, underlying the braiding of Stokes data and generalising the usual mapping class groups. We will establish a general product decomposition for the local wild mapping class groups, and in many cases define a fission tree controlling this decomposition. Further in type A we will show one obtains cabled versions of braid groups, related to braid operads.
Geometric Topology.comment: v4 (43pp., 7figg.): more minor improvements (e.g., added remarks on type-D parts of Levi root subystems), added references, updated funding acknowledgement/addresses and metadata; v3 is closest to published version; comments welcome!

Geometric Topology.title: Topology of irregular isomonodromy times on a fixed pointed curve
Geometric Topology.summary: We will define and study (moduli) spaces of deformations of irregular classes on Riemann surfaces, which provide an intrinsic viewpoint on the `times' of irregular isomonodromy systems in general. Our aim is to study the deeper generalisation of the G-braid groups that occur as fundamental groups of such deformation spaces, with particular focus on the generalisation of the full G-braid groups.
Geometric Topology.comment: v4 (34pp., 3 figg.): more minor improvements (e.g., generalized statement/proof of Lem. 2.2), added references, updated addresses and metadata; v3 is closest to published version; comments welcome!

Geometric Topology.title: Topological Insights and Combinatorial Frameworks for Twist Knot Complements
Geometric Topology.summary: The complement of a knot in $\mathbb{S}^3$ is a fundamental object in $3$-manifold topology and serves as a primary building block in the study of geometric structures on manifolds. For a large class of knots, these complements admit complete hyperbolic metrics, motivating the development of various frameworks for their classification and analysis. A twist knot is formed by applying a series of half-twists to a closed loop and linking the ends. In this article, we present explicit topological and combinatorial descriptions of all twist knot complements via the construction of suitable cell structures. Our method produces a closed $3$-dimensional pseudomanifold with a single vertex, arising from prescribed face pairings of a faceted $3$-ball. Removing the vertex yields the complement of the corresponding twist knot. The construction naturally induces ideal triangulations of these knot complements, several of which are shown to be facet-minimal. Beyond providing concrete models, our approach offers new perspectives on the topology of knot complements and leads to some open research problems.

Geometric Topology.title: Higher order unknotting numbers for knots and links
Geometric Topology.summary: Ohyama, Taniyama and Yamada showed that finite type knot invariants are insensitive to the unknotting number: for any integer n and any knot K, there is an unknotting number 1 knot which cannot be distinguished from K by any finite type invariant of order $\le n$. We generalize this result in three directions. First, we prove an analogous result for all higher order unknotting number given by $C_n$-moves. Second, we give several extensions to the link case. Third, we show that a similar result holds for ribbon 2-knots.
Geometric Topology.comment: 18 pages; no AI tools were used at any stage

Geometric Topology.title: Links and singularities of stable maps from $3$-manifolds to surfaces
Geometric Topology.summary: For any two links in the $3$-sphere, we provide a visual construction of a stable map $f$ from the $3$-sphere to the Euclidean plane such that $f$ has no cusp points, the set of definite (resp. indefinite) fold points of $f$ is isotopic to the first (resp. second) given link, and $f$ does not have a certain type of singular fibers. Moreover, we obtain a similar result for any $3$-manifold by setting the target space to the $2$-sphere.

Geometric Topology.title: The Smoothability of Embedded Surfaces in 4-Manifolds Under Stabilizations
Geometric Topology.summary: We study the smooth stabilization number of a locally flat embedded surface in a smooth $4$-manifold, defined as the minimum number of connected sums with $S^2\times S^2$ needed to make the surface topologically isotopic to a smooth embedding. We prove that a nonsmoothable locally flat surface in a closed, simply connected smooth $4$-manifold becomes smoothable after a single stabilization if its homology class is primitive and noncharacteristic and its complement has abelian fundamental group.
