This yields infinitely many examples of nonsmoothable surfaces with smooth stabilization number one. We also exhibit examples for which a single stabilization produces infinitely many pairwise smoothly nonisotopic representatives in the same topological isotopy class. In contrast, we construct a locally flat genus-eight surface representing $6h$ in $\mathbb{CP}^2$ whose smooth stabilization number is exactly two. More generally, we show that smooth stabilization numbers of locally flat embedded surfaces in $\mathbb{CP}^2$ are unbounded.

Geometric Topology.title: The Liouville property for geometric graphs in the plane
Geometric Topology.summary: We show that every bounded discrete harmonic function with respect to the cotangent Laplacian on a Delaunay triangulation of the Euclidean plane is constant; equivalently, the cotangent-weighted triangulation has the Liouville property. Our main theorem establishes this property for a more general class of connected weighted geometric graphs in the plane. Furthermore, we show that a planar Delaunay triangulation with cotangent weights could be transient but is recurrent if edge lengths are uniformly bounded.

Geometric Topology.title: Categorical Tiling Theory: Constructing Directed Planar Tilings via Edge Reversal
Geometric Topology.summary: Tilings of the plane resemble the simplicial and other complexes from algebraic topology, but have not been studied from this perspective. We construct finite categories corresponding to polygons with labeled directed edges, and introduce the problem of modeling tilings of the Euclidean or hyperbolic plane as presheaves over such a category. Combinatorially, this amounts to choosing an ``alignment'' for a tiling: a direction for every edge and consistent labels for the edges of each polygonal tile. We show that for a fixed tiling, given a single alignment we can characterize every other alignment of the same tiling by comparison of the edge directions. We then construct a ``reflective'' alignment for any tiling with an even number of polygons at each vertex, and from this generate a large family of alignments with elegant symmetry properties.
Geometric Topology.comment: 38 pages + 4 page appendix. v2: Minor edits and corrections, accepted for publication at Involve

Geometric Topology.title: Sections, pseudosections, and multisections of Lefschetz fibrations
Geometric Topology.summary: We show that not every symplectic Lefschetz fibration over the $2$--sphere admits a smooth section, settling a long-standing open problem. To prove this, we develop a method for studying sections via lifts of monodromy factorizations with point-pushing maps and the induced handle decomposition of the total space, and apply it to an infinite family of Lefschetz fibrations. In contrast, we show that every Lefschetz fibration over $S^2$ admits positive multisections. Some of these examples admit no multisections with spherical components. We also construct signature-zero Lefschetz fibrations of every odd genus $g\geq 7$, which in turn give symplectic Lefschetz fibrations of any prescribed signature in each of these genera.
Geometric Topology.comment: 46 pages, 21 figures in color. v2: added an explicit calculation of a pseudosection for the genus-7 example and an appendix constructing four disjoint sections of Xiao's genus-2 Lefschetz fibration of type (6,7). Minor editorial changes throughout

Optimization and Control.title: The Number of Tropical Order Types and Coherent Matching Fields
Optimization and Control.summary:
We investigate counting problems for discrete (geometric) structures in tropical settings, motivated by the comparison of the expressivity of linear programs and mean-payoff games.
  First, we give an upper bound on the number of coherent matching fields of type $(n,r)$ and a lower bound on the number of combinatorial types of $n$-hyperplane sequences in the max-plus tropical space of dimension $r-1$. These structures are closely related, and our bounds establish that as $n \to \infty$, for every fixed $r$ their number equals $n^{(r-1)^2n+o(n)}$. This in turn implies that the number of regular triangulations of the products of simplices $Δ^{n-1}\timesΔ^{r-1}$ is also $n^{(r-1)^2n+o(n)}$, thereby answering a question of Santos.
  Second, we obtain that the number of labeled order types over the reals and over the signed tropical numbers coincide at first order, establishing a comparison of the expressivity of mean-payoff games and linear programs as measured by labeled order types.
  Last, the subclass of mean-payoff games known as parity games arise from linear programs by a ``double tropicalization.'' We show that the number of labeled order types obtained after this double tropicalization collapses.

Optimization and Control.title: Improved Gradient Complexity for Quasi-Newton Proximal Extragradient Methods via Certified Curvature Reuse
Optimization and Control.summary: We study how curvature estimated from gradient differences can accelerate proximal-extragradient quasi-Newton methods. Existing global guarantees for QNPE, A-QNPE, and OL-OQN learn Hessian approximations online and incur dimension dependence through regret bounds. We introduce certified curvature reuse: one finite-difference probe per iteration refreshes a group of Hessian columns, while a path-length certificate controls the error of stale columns and determines the step. Each iteration uses at most three gradient queries and one regularized linear solve (or trust-region step), without a gradient line search or an inner oracle-querying loop. In the convex and strongly convex settings, bisection on stored scalar quantities selects a near-maximal certified stepsize; in the nonconvex setting, a uniform certificate gives an explicit learning rate. With other problem parameters fixed, the convex method attains $O(\min\{k^{-2},dk^{-3}\})$ in a single run, with no logarithmic factor or additive dimension term, matching accelerated gradient descent (AGD) for $k\lesssim d$ and improving on A-QNPE thereafter. In the strongly convex setting with condition number $κ$, a single run matches AGD's $(1-Θ(κ^{-1/2}))^k$ rate for $k\lesssim d\logκ$ and achieves a superlinear upper envelope, eventually scaling as $(1+k^2/B^2)^{-k}$ with $B=\tilde O(dκ)$, improving on QNPE. In the nonconvex setting, the method finds an $\varepsilon$-stationary point in $O(\min\{d^{1/3}\varepsilon^{-3/2},\varepsilon^{-7/4}\})$ gradient queries, improving on OL-OQN's $O(d^{1/4}\varepsilon^{-13/8})$. For sparse Hessians, $d$ is replaced by an effective dimension $χ\le d$. We also compare our bounds with lazy-Hessian, double-loop, and cutting-plane methods.
Optimization and Control.comment: Full version, 5 figures. Includes all proofs in the appendix

Optimization and Control.title: On-Trip Matching and Pricing for Shared Rides
Optimization and Control.summary: Shared rides, which match compatible riders in one vehicle, have the potential to increase vehicle utilization and reduce congestion and emissions. However, this service has seen limited success outside dense urban areas due to insufficient matching opportunities. The dominant model in the literature, which we refer to as the pre-trip model, matches riders before dispatch using non-bipartite matching, and dispatches unmatched riders solo. In practice, augmenting this pre-trip matching mechanism with an on-trip matching phase, where riders initially dispatched solo can still match with later arrivals, can expand matching opportunities. Yet the addition of the on-trip phase complicates the dynamic matching problem, as riders' matching opportunities evolve as they travel: both the set of compatible riders and the value of matches can diminish as a rider progresses towards her destination. To address this challenge, we formulate a Markov decision process that tracks riders' evolving states and weighs immediate matches against future matching opportunities. Within this framework, we incorporate pricing decisions to maximize long-run average profit, where we develop a fluid relaxation for static pricing and use value function approximation for dynamic (state-dependent) pricing. Experiments using Chicago ridesharing data show that pre-trip matching performs well with concentrated demand, whereas on-trip matching is particularly beneficial in the sparse outskirts where operating shared rides is especially challenging. Across both static and dynamic pricing settings, adding on-trip matching increases platform profit and match rates while lowering average quoted prices, showing the value of capturing matching opportunities along the route when demand is too dispersed for effective pre-trip matching.

Optimization and Control.title: Debiasing optimal transport: classical and entropic
Optimization and Control.summary: We study the notion of debiasability for cost functions arising in optimal transport. We call a symmetric cost function $c:\mathscr{X}\times\mathscr{X}\to R\cup\{+\infty\}$ debiasable if it satisfies $c(x,y)\ge \tfrac{1}{2}c(x,x)+\tfrac{1}{2}c(y,y)$ for all $x,y\in\mathscr{X}$. Building on an equivalent characterization by an inf-representation $c(x,y)=\inf_{z\in\mathscr Z}ψ(x,z)+ψ(y,z)$ for some set $\mathscr Z$ and some function $ψ:\mathscr X\times\mathscr Z\to R\cup\{+\infty\}$, interpreted as a generalization of the midpoint identity for squared geodesic distances, we investigate the debiasability of costs defined on spaces of probability measures. Our primary focus is the entropic regularization of optimal transport across the different regimes of the regularization parameter $\varepsilon\in[0,+\infty]$, encompassing classical optimal transport ($\varepsilon=0$), entropic optimal transport ($\varepsilon>0$), and the Maximum Mean Discrepancy ($\varepsilon=+\infty$). For $\varepsilon\in(0,+\infty)$ we obtain debiasability under negative definiteness of the ground cost, through an explicit Gaussian factorization, and, more generally, under positive semidefiniteness of the kernel $e^{-c/\varepsilon}$ alone, conditions also proved necessary. All our results extend naturally to unbalanced optimal transport settings. Extending our factorizations to include a time parameter $t\in(0,1)$, we construct an entropic interpolation curve given by an intermediate measure $η_t\in\mathscr P(\mathscr Z)$ based on a barycentric formulation, which coincides with the marginals of the Schrödinger bridge between $μ$ and $ν$. As a byproduct, we derive a new proof for the entropic Benamou-Brenier formula under very mild assumptions.

Optimization and Control.title: The Value of Experiments in Assortment Optimization
Optimization and Control.summary: Retailers can learn customer preferences by experimenting with different assortments. However, the cost of each experiment and the operational burden of repeatedly changing product offerings can make extensive experimentation impractical. We study how much a retailer can improve its final assortment decision using customer observations from one (or a very small number of) fixed experimental assortments. We consider the multinomial logit model, where product revenues are known but customer preferences are unknown. In this setting, we jointly design the experimental assortment and the rule for selecting a final assortment from observed customer choices to minimize worst-case regret: the expected revenue loss of the final assortment relative to an optimal assortment under the true preferences, maximized over possible customer preferences. We first characterize exactly the minimax regret and an optimal assortment when no experimentation is possible. We then show, surprisingly, that offering a single experimental assortment to just one customer can already substantially reduce regret, depending on how the products' revenues compare. We derive the exact minimax regret and an optimal experimental policy in this setting. When a single fixed experimental assortment is offered to many customers, we give a geometric characterization of the limiting minimax regret and construct an asymptotically optimal policy. Depending on product revenues, this single experiment can yield no improvement over no experimentation or nearly complete regret reduction. Finally, we extend our analysis to multiple experimental assortments chosen in advance, characterizing the limiting minimax regret, constructing asymptotically optimal policies, and identifying which collections of assortments allow worst-case regret to vanish as the number of customer observations grows.

Optimization and Control.title: A Behavioral approach to Constrained Linear Quadratic Control: Feasibility and Optimality
Optimization and Control.summary: This paper develops a constrained linear-quadratic (LQ) optimal control framework within the behavioral approach. Unlike classical formulations that rely on state-input representations, our method treats both the system dynamics and the constraints as trajectory-level objects. The system is modeled through a kernel representation, while inequality constraints are captured using behavioral inequalities defined over infinite-dimensional convex cones. Using quadratic differential forms (QDFs) to encode performance indices, we formulate the constrained LQ problem as a convex variational optimization over trajectories. By employing Gateaux differentials, we derive the stationarity and complementarity conditions and show that they admit a representation as an augmented behavioral system whose unique decomposition into autonomous and controllable sub-behaviors yields a complete parameterization of all optimal constrained trajectories. The resulting conditions constitute a behavioral analogue of the Karush-Kuhn-Tucker (KKT) framework. A numerical example illustrates the effect of inequality constraints on the optimal behavior. The framework provides a general, trajectory-level representation for constrained optimal control and opens avenues for closed-loop and data-driven extensions.
Optimization and Control.comment: Accepted for publication at IEEE Indian Control Conference 2027

Optimization and Control.title: Single-Temperature Ranked Greedy Cluster Exchange for Max-Cut on Two-Dimensional Tori
Optimization and Control.summary: Ground-state search in two-dimensional Ising spin glasses on large toroidal lattices remains challenging for local-update heuristics because rugged energy barriers impede relaxation across metastable states. Equivalent to zero-field toroidal Max-Cut problems, these spin-glass instances also serve as standard benchmarks for optimization heuristics. Many Monte Carlo approaches combine single-spin flips or cluster moves with temperature ladders or annealing schedules, yet even with tuned parameters, rarely achieve rapid, reliable ground-state convergence at scale. Here, we address the need for faster ground-state search through cooperation between replicas. We introduce ranked greedy cluster exchange (RGCX) and combine it with fixed-temperature Metropolis sweeps to form single-temperature RGCX. Replicas are ranked by cut to determine the pair-processing order. Each pair deterministically exchanges every disagreement cluster that raises the better replica's cut, retaining the complement and conserving the pair's summed cut. On the 20,000-spin Gset instance G81, the estimated runtime to reach the certified optimum with 99% success probability (TTS99) was 12.1 s on an 8-core desktop computer. With the same population size, exchange interval and temperature, the method reached the best known cuts on all 17 toroidal Gset graphs, including 9 certified optima. These findings advance ground-state search on large two-dimensional tori by establishing single-temperature RGCX as an efficient population-based method that combines ranked greedy cluster exchange with fixed-temperature Metropolis dynamics.

Optimization and Control.title: Random Matching Between Distinct Distributions in Two Dimensions
Optimization and Control.summary:
Given two independent $n$-point samples drawn from possibly distinct probability distributions on a compact 2-dimensional surface, we minimize the total squared distance over all perfect bipartite matchings. Under regularity assumptions, the expected matching cost minus $n$ times the squared 2-Wasserstein distance between the sampling distributions grows logarithmically with $n$. We determine this difference up to an additive $o(1)$ error, including the dependence of the logarithmic coefficient and constant term on geometry and sampling distributions, and establish the existence of a universal constant shared by these formulas.
  Our analysis expresses the expected matching cost in terms of the cost of transporting a heat-smoothed sample back to its original points. The reductions giving this relation hold in every dimension and for general costs under suitable assumptions, with consequences beyond the setting studied here. In two dimensions, the relation is exact up to an additive $o(1)$ error, so determining the matching cost amounts to evaluating the smoothing cost with the same accuracy. We obtain this evaluation by subdividing the domain and exploiting cancellations between the sample and its own smoothing.

Optimization and Control.title: A quantum central path algorithm for linear optimization
Optimization and Control.summary: We propose a novel quantum algorithm for solving linear optimization problems by quantum-mechanical simulation of the central path. While interior point methods follow the central path with an iterative algorithm that works with successive linearizations of the perturbed KKT conditions, we perform a simulation working directly with the nonlinear complementarity equations. Using a two-stage quantum eigenpath traversal schedule, this approach yields an algorithm for solving linear optimization problems involving $m$ constraints and $n$ variables to $\varepsilon$-optimality using $\widetilde{O}\!\left((m+n)^{3/2}\,\varepsilon^{-1}+(m+n)^{1/2}\,\varepsilon^{-3/2}\right)$ queries to an oracle that evaluates a potential function. In the standard gate model (i.e., without access to quantum RAM), our algorithm can obtain $\varepsilon$-precise solutions to LO problems using at most $$\widetilde{O}\!\left(\left[\frac{(m+n)^{3/2}}{\varepsilon} + \frac{(m+n)^{1/2}}{\varepsilon^{3/2}}\right] \cdot \mathrm{nnz}(A)\right)$$ elementary gates, where $\mathrm{nnz}(A)$ is the total number of non-zero elements found in the constraint matrix.
Optimization and Control.comment: 44 pages, 1 figure, appeared as a talk at QIP 2025

Optimization and Control.title: Numerical Investigation of Soft-to-Hard Convergence: Discretization, Admissibility, and Spectral Regularity
Optimization and Control.summary: This paper presents a numerical investigation of soft-to-hard terminal constraint convergence for optimal control problems governed by a second-order ordinary differential equation and the one-dimensional heat equation. The study complements the analytical convergence theory through comparisons with exact solutions and independently computed numerical approximations. For the heat equation, a fully discrete Crank--Nicolson finite-difference formulation is validated against exact modal solutions, exhibiting approximately second-order convergence in the terminal-state and midpoint-sampled control errors under simultaneous space-time mesh refinement. Numerical experiments demonstrate the predicted first-order penalty convergence for benchmark problems and investigate the admissibility threshold governing finite-energy exact terminal controllability. Additional modal experiments examine the dependence of terminal-error convergence rates on spectral regularity, illustrating intermediate rates consistent with the theoretical estimates and asymptotic predictions. The results provide computational evidence supporting the soft-to-hard convergence framework and clarify the roles of discretization, target admissibility, and spectral regularity.

Optimization and Control.title: Sums of two dependent uniform random variables: a characterization by joint tail bounds
Optimization and Control.summary: Which laws can the sum of two uniform random variables have when nothing is known about how they depend on each other? For three or more uniform summands, convex order gives the answer; for two it does not, and the question has been open. We show that the attainable laws are exactly those that satisfy a family of explicit joint bounds on sums of tail probabilities, one bound for each finite set of thresholds. For laws with a density at most one, convex order alone decides. For densities at most two, convex order implies the simplest of the joint bounds, and the constant two cannot be raised for single-threshold bounds. The number of thresholds a law needs is set by the spacing of its atoms, not by how many atoms it has.
Optimization and Control.comment: 25 pages, 1 table; 8-page supplementary material as an ancillary file. Code: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23231387. Companion paper: arXiv:2610.30058. v2: cites the companion paper by its arXiv identifier and states the two companion results used; code, data and results unchanged

Optimization and Control.title: Adaptive search with path-constrained mobile sensors using multi-arm bandits
Optimization and Control.summary: We study a constrained sequential decision problem for detecting regions of interest from noisy online measurements collected by a team of energy-constrained mobile sensors. The sensor motion is restricted to a precomputed set of feasible paths that satisfy mobility constraints, limited available energy by requiring return to charging stations, and avoidance of known obstacles. We cast the resulting active path selection as a multi-armed bandit problem and propose an iterative search algorithm that adaptively assigns paths using confidence bounds computed from the collected data. We also propose a graph-based method to construct low-cardinality path covers under the team's constraints. We establish finite-time and anytime probabilistic correctness guarantees for the proposed algorithm, derive non-asymptotic upper bounds on the times required to detect all regions of interest and to label all nodes, and show that these bounds match algorithm-independent lower bounds up to constant factors for a broad class of problem instances. Using numerical simulations, we illustrate the behavior of the proposed approach and the effect of path redundancy and team size on search performance.

Optimization and Control.title: Aerodynamic Shape Optimization of unsteady flapping wings
Optimization and Control.summary: This study introduces a new approach for building surrogate models, in the form of Reduced Order Models (ROMs), for PDE-constrained optimization. A physics-constrained data-driven framework is developed to transform large-scale non-linear optimization problems into ROM-constrained optimization problems. Unlike conventional methods, which suffer from instability of the forward sensitivity function, the proposed approach projects optimization problems to system dynamics optimization problems in Hilbert space to increase stability, diminish memory requirements, and lower computational cost. The present approach is applied to shape optimization of a 2D flapping wing section at $Re=2,400$, where the non-linear interaction of the wing with fluid includes chaotic flow structures. It is shown that the proposed approach can significantly enhance the time-averaged thrust force and propulsive efficiency by 37\% and 40\%, respectively. We also tested this approach for a 3D flapping wing and the results reveal the potential of the proposed approach for more complex optimal designs in the aerospace industry.

Optimization and Control.title: First-Order Bilevel Optimization for Non-truthful Auction Design
Optimization and Control.summary:
Automated mechanism design has enabled the learning of complex auction mechanisms using neural networks. However, designing non-truthful auctions remains challenging because bidders' equilibrium strategies depend on the auction mechanism and thus evolve as the mechanism is optimized.
  In this work, we formulate auction design as a Stackelberg game with multiple strategic followers and develop a fully first-order algorithm for revenue optimization in non-truthful auctions.
  We establish non-asymptotic guarantees for hypergradient approximation and show that, under standard smoothness and strong-monotonicity assumptions, our method reaches an $O(ε)$-stationary point using $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}(ε^{-2})$ first-order oracle calls.
  Experiments on symmetric and asymmetric single-item auctions, as well as multi-item auctions, show that our method converges faster than second- and zeroth-order baselines and scales better as the number of bidders increases. Our method also discovers auctions that achieve revenue close to truthful baselines. These results provide a scalable framework for automated mechanism design beyond truthful auctions.

Optimization and Control.title: Penalty-Based Smoothing and Accelerated Inertial Dynamics for Convex Supremum Optimization
Optimization and Control.summary: We study dual-penalty smoothing for convex functions with a finite-dimensional supremum representation. The regularization yields a differentiable surrogate with controlled approximation error, a single-valued dual maximizer, and explicit gradient formulas. We then study an accelerated inertial dynamic with vanishing damping driven by a time-dependent regularized function whose parameter decreases to zero. The global well-posedness of this system is not an immediate consequence of standard ODE theory, since the gradient of the regularized objective is in general only locally Lipschitz and its local Lipschitz modulus may deteriorate as the smoothing parameter vanishes. We therefore establish existence and uniqueness of global trajectories through a local well-posedness analysis and a continuation argument. Then, assuming that the original problem has a minimizer and under mild integrability conditions on the regularization schedule, we establish an accelerated $\mathcal{O}(t^{-2})$ decay estimate for the regularized and original objective values and, in the regime $α>3$, a sharper $o(t^{-2})$ decay together with weak convergence of trajectories to a minimizer of the original nonsmooth problem via an Opial-type argument. Applications to multiobjective optimization (through Chebyshev/max scalarization) and to distributionally robust optimization (via entropic regularization over ambiguity sets) illustrate the scope of the framework.

Optimization and Control.title: Finite-Sample LTI System Identification from a Misspecified Finite Model Set
Optimization and Control.summary: We consider the problem of finite-sample identification of an unknown LTI system from a finite hypothesis class. In contrast to existing results that assume the hypothesis class contains the true system, we consider the misspecified setting, where the true system does not belong to the hypothesis class. We first characterize the resulting estimation target and its dependence on the data-generation scheme. We then establish a finite-sample lower bound on the failure probability that any identification algorithm must incur. Finally, we analyze the robustness of an existing exponential weighting-based identification algorithm to the misspecification and derive a finite-sample upper bound on its failure probability. Our results illustrate when using a misspecified finite hypothesis class can provide an advantage over identification without prior knowledge of the candidate systems.

Optimization and Control.title: Terminal Localization of Empirical Reverse Diffusions under Singular Score Errors
Optimization and Control.summary: For a finite empirical target, the exact reverse diffusion is driven toward training points by an attraction whose strength diverges as the forward noising time decreases to zero. We study whether this terminal localization persists under progressively measurable score errors that may themselves be singular. For reverse Ornstein--Uhlenbeck diffusions, from an arbitrary initial law and under a deterministic error envelope \(E\) imposed along the perturbed trajectory satisfying \(t\int_t^T E(σ)/σ\,dσ\to0\), we prove almost-sure convergence to a training point, together with explicit uniform bounds on a terminal window with probability arbitrarily close to one. Every training point has positive terminal probability, although the terminal selection probabilities need not match the empirical weights. The results cover power-law errors \(E(t)=O(t^{-γ})\), \(0<γ<1\), including infinite squared-error energy. For suitable errors in this range, the exact and perturbed full path laws can be mutually singular while their terminal laws share the same finite support. For suitable switched perturbations at the critical scale \(t^{-1}\), arbitrarily small positive amplitudes can produce a nonzero terminal displacement with arbitrarily high probability. These results quantify stochastic robustness of empirical terminal attraction without requiring absolute continuity of the full path laws.

Optimization and Control.title: Gaussian Approximation and Multiplier Bootstrap for Federated Linear Stochastic Approximation
Optimization and Control.summary: In this paper, we establish Berry-Esseen-type bounds for federated linear stochastic approximation (LSA). Our results provide the first federated Gaussian approximations for LSA that explicitly capture communication-computation trade-offs and heterogeneity-aware error terms, quantifying the effects of local step size, number of local updates, and heterogeneity on convergence rates. We present results for both (i) constant step size regime and (ii) decreasing step size with an increasing number of local iterations, recovering the recent rates of Bonnerjee et al. [2025] as a special case. As a primary application of our results, we develop an online multiplier bootstrap procedure for inference on the last iterate, which avoids explicit estimation of the asymptotic covariance matrix, and obtain non-asymptotic validity guarantees for this procedure.
Optimization and Control.comment: The bootstrap validity theorem in the previous version was incorrect: it omitted a heterogeneity term of the same order as the leading fluctuation term. To address this issue, we now use the same bootstrap variables across clients, at the cost of losing the $N^{-1}$ factor in the leading term

Optimization and Control.title: AdaGrad-Diff: a Corrected Version of the Adaptive Gradient Algorithm for Composite Optimization
Optimization and Control.summary: Vanilla gradient methods are often highly sensitive to the choice of stepsize, which typically requires manual tuning. Adaptive methods alleviate this issue, with AdaGrad being a prominent example. In this work, we first show that, in composite convex optimization, AdaGrad may fail to exploit the Hölder-smoothness of the differentiable term, as its stepsizes may decrease too rapidly, leading to convergence rates arbitrarily close to the nonsmooth $\mathcal O(n^{-1/2})$ rate. Motivated by this limitation, we study AdaGrad-Diff, a block-wise extension of the UniSgd method considered by \cite{rodomanov2024universality}, which accumulates successive gradient differences rather than gradients themselves. In the deterministic Lipschitz-smooth setting, we prove summability of squared gradient differences without assuming bounded iterates, yielding weak convergence to a minimizer in Hilbert spaces. Moreover, we show that, under $ν$-Hölder-smoothness, stepsizes decay no faster than $n^{-(1-ν)/2}$, thereby avoiding AdaGrad's failure mechanism and recovering the standard $\mathcal O(n^{-(1+ν)/2})$ rate. The same approach recovers known stochastic convergence rates under a unified condition covering bounded variance and interpolation. Numerical experiments demonstrate that the proposed method is more robust than AdaGrad in several practically relevant settings.

Optimization and Control.title: A lifted entropy splitting lemma and applications
Optimization and Control.summary: We give a matrix lifting of the entropy-splitting theorem of Csiszár, Körner, Lovász, Marton, and Simonyi, and show several applications. We use it to prove the Cartesian-product inequality conjectured by Sinjorgo and Sotirov for the generalized Lovász theta number, and we also answer the saturation and convexification questions of Carli Silva, Coutinho, Oliveira, and Tunçel on the same theme. For the strong Hoffman bound, we answer a question of Wocjan, Elphick, and Darbari concerning orthogonal rank, and show that optimization over matrix weights gives exactly the ceiling of the theta number of the complement. Finally, we extend the lifting to diagonally invariant cones of positive semidefinite matrices, giving a proof of a conjecture by Kuryatnikova, Sotirov, and Vera, and giving a short proof, for all graphs, of a theta-based weakening of Fajtlowicz's graph-energy conjecture.

Optimization and Control.title: Equilibria in Motion: Stability, Tracking, and Convergence
Optimization and Control.summary: {We study nonautonomous systems whose equilibrium sets are nonisolated and move with time. Their motion is measured on each ball by a localized Attouch--Wets distance, which yields an equilibrium speed that may depend on the radius. The distance from a trajectory to the current equilibrium set is estimated in two ways: through a composite Lyapunov function compared with a power of this distance, and, without any Lyapunov function, through a decay condition on the frozen vector fields. In the first setting, we prove practical stability, and Lyapunov stability when the dissipation has no residual, a case that forces the equilibrium sets to be nested. In the second, we obtain, in the region where the decay condition holds, an explicit tracking estimate driven by the equilibrium speed and the inputs, and we prove asymptotic tracking whenever their averages over unit time intervals vanish, a condition that cannot be weakened among conditions on the speed alone. We also derive input-to-state stability bounds and explicit convergence rates. When the equilibrium speeds are integrable, the equilibrium sets converge in the Attouch--Wets sense to a limiting set at an explicit rate. If, moreover, the velocity is bounded by a multiple of the distance to the current equilibrium set, every trajectory remaining in the region considered has finite length and converges to a point of the limiting set; for a fixed equilibrium set, this yields semistability. The results are illustrated on a scalar example and on resource-allocation models with time-varying demand and with rotating weights.
Optimization and Control.comment: Revised and corrected version. Some statements and arguments have been corrected and strengthened; the main scope and conclusions of the paper remain unchanged

Optimization and Control.title: Convergence Analysis of Nesterov's Accelerated Gradient Descent under Relaxed Assumptions
Optimization and Control.summary: We study convergence rates of Nesterov's Accelerated Gradient Descent (NAG) method for convex optimization in both deterministic and stochastic settings. We focus on a more general smoothness condition raised from several machine learning problems empirically and theoretically. We show the accelerated convergence rate of order $\mathcal{O}\left(1/T^2\right)$ in terms of the function value gap, given access to exact gradients of objective functions, matching the optimal rate for standard smooth convex optimization in \citep{nesterov1983method}. Under the relaxed affine-variance noise assumption for stochastic optimization, we establish the high-probability convergence rate of order $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}\left(\sqrt{\log\left(1/δ\right)/T}\right)$ and this rate could improve to $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}\left(\log\left(1/δ\right)/T^2\right)$ when the noise parameters are sufficiently small. Here, $T$ denotes the total number of iterations and $δ$ is the probability margin. Up to logarithm factors, our probabilistic convergence rate reaches the same order of the expected rate obtained in \citep{ghadimi2016accelerated} where the assumptions of bounded variance noise and Lipschitz smoothness are required. We additionally establish the convergence rates of the studied algorithms in the non-convex setting.

Optimization and Control.title: Readiness-Constrained Pre-Islanding Dispatch for Military Microgrids
Optimization and Control.summary: Military installation energy readiness depends on having sufficient resources to sustain mission-critical loads throughout a prolonged utility outage. This paper develops a method to help operators manage energy resources during normal grid-connected operation while preserving islanded readiness. A robust viability kernel identifies combinations of battery energy, fuel, and load-shifting capability sufficient to sustain critical load under uncertain demand and photovoltaic generation. A probability bound translates stochastic generator start failures and recovery into a deterministic generator count selected to meet a specified availability requirement at islanding. Case studies for a fourteen-day islanding requirement at 0.999 islanding-entry availability show that advance warning of an outage can be used to prepare resources to meet a higher readiness requirement before islanding begins. The case studies further demonstrate that economic-only operation and the evaluated fixed battery reserve policy can fail to sustain critical load for the required duration, whereas enforcing the resource-dependent requirement preserves readiness at a modest increase in modeled grid-connected operating cost. These results demonstrate how active resource management can preserve long-duration energy readiness. The framework also helps commanders understand how readiness changes with operating conditions, even when the available resources remain the same.

Optimization and Control.title: A particle system approach towards the global well-posedness of master equations for potential mean field games of control
Optimization and Control.summary: This paper studies the $N$-particle systems as well as the HJB/master equations for a class of generalized mean field control (MFC) problems and the corresponding potential mean field games of control (MFGC). A local in time classical solution for the HJB equation is generated via a probabilistic approach based on the mean field maximum principle. Given an extension of the so called displacement convexity condition, we obtain the uniform estimates on the HJB equation for the $N$-particle system. Such estimates imply the displacement convexity/semi-concavity and thus the prior estimates on the solution to the HJB equation for generalized MFC problems. The global well-posedness of HJB/master equation for generalized MFC/potential MFGC is then proved thanks to the local well-posedness and the prior estimates. In view of the nature of the displacement convexity condition, such well-posedness is also true for the degenerated case. Our analysis on the $N$-particle system also induces an Lipschitz approximator to the optimal feedback function in generalized MFC/potential MFGC where an algebraic convergence rate is obtained. Furthermore, an alternative approximate Nash equilibrium is proposed based on the $N$-particle system, where the approximation error is quantified thanks to the aforementioned uniform estimates.

Optimization and Control.title: Data-driven Regularization for Inverse Problems
Optimization and Control.summary:
In many applications, we are interested in studying an object of interest $x$. However, its properties are often not directly measurable. Instead, we only observe $y = F(x)$, where the (known) function $F$ is referred to as the forward mapping. To infer about $x$ from the observation $y$, we seek an (approximate) inverse mapping $x \approx F^{-1}(y)$. This process is known as solving the inverse problem.
  In practice, the inverse mapping $F^{-1}$ may be ill-defined or discontinuous, which forces us to choose a certain solution from many possible ones based on prior assumptions on $x$. Such assumptions about $x$ are typically incorporated into the inversion process through regularization. Therefore, the first part of this course focuses on the classical regularization theory of inverse problems.
  In the second part, we transition to algorithmic approaches for solving inverse problems. The foundation for this lies in the variational formulation of inverse problems, where reconstructions are obtained by minimizing specific functionals. Here, we will explore key optimization principles, discuss their practical implementation, and examine how they contribute to robust reconstructions.
  Today, classical methods are often modified to incorporate data-driven machine learning techniques, which improve the empirical performance. However, this often comes at the cost of explainability or convergence guarantees. Such properties are critical, for example, in medical applications, where one wants to be confident that reconstructed abnormalities are of physical nature and not phantoms resulting from the method.
  For these reasons, we discuss a number of machine learning methods for inverse problems, such as unrolling techniques, learned regularizers and plug-and-play methods, and explore their performance guarantees.

Optimization and Control.title: Multi-split Multiple-sets Implicit Convex Feasibility Seeking As Split Inverse Problems
Optimization and Control.summary: We introduce a new class of problems, termed multi-split multiple-sets implicit convex feasibility problems (MSMS-ICFPs), define a proximity function for it and analyze its properties under certain assumptions on the involved general point-to-set operators. Additionally, we discuss its properties for a special class of point-to-set operators. For these kinds of point-to-set operators, we deploy a new iterative algorithm to solve the associated MSMS-ICFP and show that any sequence generated by it converges in norm to a solution of the MSMS-ICFP whenever a solution exists (i.e., in the consistent case). We also define a generalized proximity function for the MSMS-ICFP using the Bregman distance. Based on this function, we present a generalized simultaneous projection gradient algorithm for the split feasibility problem with multiple output sets, by examining various related results. We conclude by discussing several further special cases of the MSMS-ICFP.

Optimization and Control.title: When to spend privacy: optimal allocation in private learning
Optimization and Control.summary: Privacy accounting bounds the cumulative privacy cost of Differentially Private Stochastic Gradient Descent but does not determine how to allocate a fixed budget across iterations. We formulate the complete Gaussian noise-variance schedule as an open-loop control under a composed zero-Concentrated Differential Privacy constraint, explicitly accounting for schedule selection. For expected quadratic terminal tracking, we prove that every local minimizer exhausts the certified budget, yielding an exact-budget simplex formulation. We introduce Privacy-Budget Adjoint Mirror Descent (PB-AMD), combining pathwise adjoint gradients with entropic updates that preserve positivity, charge floors, and the prescribed budget. Under regularity and coercivity assumptions, we establish existence and budget stability of optimal schedules, design-to-training utility stability, and deterministic, stochastic, and sample-average stationarity guarantees. A linear-quadratic reduction yields an explicit square-root allocation law. Experiments demonstrate tracking improvements over several allocation rules and predictive improvements over uniform allocation in a learning-rate restart setting, where learning-rate allocation performs similarly. Comparisons at a common stationarity tolerance show lower schedule-optimization times than projected gradient descent on the tested problems. The framework connects certified privacy accounting with optimization through nonlinear training dynamics.

Optimization and Control.title: Iterative Methods for Solving New Generalized Absolute Value Equations
Optimization and Control.summary: In this paper, we propose two iterative methods, the modified Picard method (MPM) and the generalized Traub method (GTM), to solve a new generalized absolute value equation (NGAVE). We establish their convergence under appropriate assumptions. Additionally, numerical examples demonstrate the effectiveness and applicability of the developed algorithms.

Optimization and Control.title: Quadratic Returns for a Moving Water Tank: An Explicit Right Inverse and a Sylvester Representation
Optimization and Control.summary:
Coron's return method established local nonlinear controllability of a moving water tank in sufficiently large time. We study the quadratic response at uniform equilibrium, where the acceleration input in the linearized model cannot excite the Fourier modes of the fluid with even indices. At three one-way wave crossings ($T=3$), we construct a nonzero smooth acceleration, whose first two final-state coefficients vanish. A planar curve reduces this cancellation to a scalar identity. At this reference acceleration, two integrations give an explicit control correction that preserves the linear return and produces any given leading change in the quadratic final state. The correction maps periodic $H^r$ targets with zero mean to $H^r$ controls for every nonnegative integer $r$. A contraction argument also gives local exact solvability of the quadratic final-state equation. Finally, a time-dependent Sylvester equation provides an alternative representation of the coupling responsible for the second-order correction. The associated change of state coordinates involves one spatial derivative, while the control correction preserves regularity in appropriate Sobolev spaces. These results concern the first two variation equations only.
  Keywords: Controllability, control of partial differential equations, return method, Saint-Venant equations, Sylvester equations.

Optimization and Control.title: Stochastic Optimal Control Problems for the Cost-Optimal Management of a Standalone Microgrid
Optimization and Control.summary: In this paper, we consider a domestic standalone microgrid equipped with local renewable energy generation such as photovoltaic panels, consumption units, and battery storage to balance supply and demand and investigate the stochastic optimal control problem for its cost-optimal management. As a special feature, the manager does not have access to the power grid but has a local generator, making it possible to produce energy using fuel when needed. Such systems are very important for rural electrification, particularly in developing countries. However, these systems are very complex to control due to uncertainties in the weather and environmental conditions, which affect the energy generation and the energy demand. In addition, we assume that the battery and the fuel tank have limited capacities and that the fuel tank can only be filled once at the beginning of the planning period. This leads us to the so-called finite fuel problem. In addition, we allow the energy demand to not always be satisfied, and we impose penalties on unsatisfied demand, the so-called discomfort cost. The main goal is to minimize the expected aggregated cost of generating power using the generator and operating the system. This leads to a mathematical optimization problem. The problem is formulated as a discrete-time stochastic control problem and solved numerically using methods from the theory of Markov decision processes.

Optimization and Control.title: On convex envelopes of bilinear terms over polygonal domains
Optimization and Control.summary: We develop an algorithm for computing the convex envelope of the bilinear function $f(x,y)=xy$ over possibly nonconvex polygonal domains. Building on existing methods for convex polytopes, our approach uses the Karush-Kuhn-Tucker conditions and an analysis of the contact points between affine underestimators and the graph of $f$. Nonconvex domains admit additional contact configurations that prevent several simplifications available in the convex case. We resolve these configurations explicitly and show that the envelope admits a finite polyhedral subdivision with affine, quadratic, or rational expressions on its cells. For orthogonal polygons, whose edges are horizontal or vertical, we establish substantial reductions in the generator sets needed to compute the envelope. We also present methods for constructing such domains as relaxations of two-dimensional projections of nonlinear optimization problems. An illustrative example quantifies the loss in relaxation strength caused by convexifying the domain before computing the envelope. Computational experiments on MINLPLib instances show that cuts derived from orthogonal polygons strengthen root relaxations and reduce branch-and-bound nodes in aggregate.

Optimization and Control.title: Distributionally robust chance-constrained standard quadratic optimization with Wasserstein ambiguity
Optimization and Control.summary: The standard quadratic optimization problem consists of minimizing a quadratic form over the standard simplex. It has highly relevant applications ranging from portfolio optimization to machine learning. However, if the quadratic form is neither convex nor concave, this problem is NP-hard. We study a distributionally robust chance-constrained variant whose ambiguity set is a Wasserstein ball around the sampled distribution and make four contributions. First, although the problem is nonconvex in the decision variable, we exploit its linear dependence on the uncertain matrix to reduce the problem to a mixed-integer quadratic optimization problem. Second, we show that a judicious choice of matrix norm---the entrywise maximum norm---makes this reformulation both exact and tractable, and we describe the induced worst-case distribution. Third, our formulation is, by construction, the minimization of the worst-case Value-at-Risk of the random quadratic form; this unifies it with existing frameworks for uncertain standard quadratic optimization problems, in particular under chance constraints, and we identify natural settings in which it collapses to a single deterministic instance. Finally, we report numerical experiments on positive-definite and indefinite instances which quantify how the model parameters drive the optimal value and solution time, and expose the computational cost of indefiniteness.

Optimization and Control.title: State-constrained optimal control of the continuity equation and infinite-dimensional viscosity solutions
Optimization and Control.summary: We study a finite horizon optimal control problem for the continuity equation under a weighted integral state constraint on the mass outside a fixed set. The model is cast in a Hilbert framework for densities. On a suitable invariant compact subset, we prove that the value function is Lipschitz continuous and satisfies, by dynamic programming, the associated infinite dimensional constrained Hamilton Jacobi Bellman equation in viscosity sense (subsolution in the interior, supersolution up to the boundary). We finally prove a comparison principle and uniqueness in the Lipschitz class.

Optimization and Control.title: A Pricing-for-Integrality Primal Heuristic for Branch-and-Price: An Application to the Electric Vehicle Routing Problem with Time Windows and Charging Time Slots
Optimization and Control.summary: Branch-price-and-cut is the state-of-the-art exact method for solving many types of vehicle routing problems, and it is particularly effective for vehicle routing problems with time windows. A well-known challenge in branch-price-and-cut is that the generation of columns is guided by information from the linear relaxation of the master problem, with no guarantee that they will be useful from an integer perspective. As a consequence, high-quality primal solutions are often found only after significant cutting and branching, or the use of primal heuristics. In this work, based on the ideas of pricing-for-integrality, we propose a primal heuristic for branch-and-price and evaluate it on the electric vehicle routing problem with time windows extended with charging time slots. The heuristic first uses a destroy-and-repair phase to enrich the column pool and then applies a restricted master heuristic to obtain a primal solution. In the destroy-and-repair phase, route generation is guided by scaled dual values and heuristic feedback based on previously generated routes, with the aim of producing routes likely to contribute to high-quality integer solutions. Computational tests on the electric vehicle routing problem with time windows extended with charging time slots show that the proposed heuristic reduces the average optimality gap in the root node by around 60% compared to a restricted master heuristic and by around 25% - 30% compared to the implemented benchmark diving heuristic.

Optimization and Control.title: Transformation of Adaptive Multistage Sampling for Solving Finite-Horizon Markov Decision Processes with Unknown Model
Optimization and Control.summary: This work provides a learning approach to solving finite-horizon Markov decision processes (MDPs) when the underlying model of a given finite MDP is unknown to the decision maker. We transform the adaptive multistage sampling (AMS) algorithm into a sampling-free algorithm, called "adaptive multistage rollout (AMR)," for estimating the optimal value at an initial state when only the state set and the action set are known. AMR emulates the backward induction as in AMS but in a reinforcement learning (RL) setting. At each iteration, AMR generates a non-stationary policy to be used for exploration and rolls out the policy in order to obtain a single trajectory of experiences and traces it backwards in a non-recursive way while doing relevant updates only at visited states and for actions taken at the visited states. We show that AMR is asymptotically optimal such that the sequence of the expected absolute errors approaches zero and its convergence rate depends on the number of visits to each reachable state at each stage from the initial state, essentially transforming the result of AMS into the RL setting.
