We confirm that [4]'s elegant spectral characterizations are excellent approximations in the low correlated regime. At the same time, we also close the gap in the regimes with higher correlation levels where spectral methods deviate from the practical dynamics performance.

Probability.title: Bulk universality of scaling limits for the almost Hermitian Coulomb gas
Probability.summary: Inspired by the recent approach to edge universality of Cronvall and Wennman, we prove several local universality results for scaling limits in the bulk in the almost Hermitian regime, as well as associated results relating to reproducing kernel spaces of the Fock type.
Probability.comment: Some previous issues in the proofs have been fixed

Probability.title: Moments of Magic Squares: Line-Sum Conditions, a Permutation Threshold, and Random Energies
Probability.summary: Every semi-magic square of order $n$ satisfies the axial moment identities $\sum_{i,j}s_{ij}j^m=\sum_{i,j}s_{ij}i^m=M(n)\sum_jj^m$ for all $m\ge1$, where $M(n)=n(n^2+1)/2$. For real matrices the converse requires $1\le m\le n-1$, whereas for arrangements of $\{1,\dots,n^2\}$ fewer moments suffice once $n\ge14$. We define the permutation threshold $k^*(n)$ as the least $k$ such that every arrangement satisfying these identities for $1\le m\le k$ is semi-magic. In terms of the column-sum deviations $γ_j$, the degree-$k$ conditions state that $\sum_jγ_jt^j$ is divisible by $(t-1)^{k+1}$, linking $k^*(n)$ to the Prouhet--Tarry--Escott problem. While Schur's bound on real zeros gives $k^*(n)\le\sqrt{2(n-1)\log(n^4/4)}$, we prove the converse realisability bound $k^*(n)\ge(\sqrt2-o(1))\sqrt n$ (and $k^*(n)\ge(\sqrt6-o(1))\sqrt n$ when $4\mid n$) by perturbing semi-magic squares with complementary row pairs via horizontal swaps. We also show that $k^*(n)=n-1$ for $3\le n\le13$, $k^*(n)=n-2$ for $14\le n\le17$, and $k^*(n)\le n-3$ for $n\ge18$, and determine $k^*(n)$ for $18\le n\le40$ with computer assistance. Finally, at the $k=1$ level of the hierarchy, we specialise the Mantel--Hubert quadratic assignment variance formula to obtain exact means, variances, and limit laws under a uniform random arrangement for the full line-sum energy $E_{\mathrm{full}}$, for the four-term energy $E_4$ combining the first moments and the two diagonals, and for Loly's moment of inertia, and find that $|L_4|=14{,}639{,}440$ arrangements of order $4$ satisfy $E_4=0$.
Probability.comment: 27 pages, 3 figures, 5 tables; ancillary verification scripts and certificates in anc/

Probability.title: Phase-Space Realization of Stochastic Multivalued Dynamics with Gyroscopic Subdifferential Coupling
Probability.summary: We introduce a new framework for stochastic variational inequalities with oblique reflections generated by non-symmetric matrix coefficients. The loss of symmetry fundamentally changes the structure of the reflected dynamics: besides the dissipative component, it produces a genuinely gyroscopic component describing rotational effects that are invisible to the associated energy forms. To capture this hidden component, we consider planar obstacle problems and we lift the dynamics to an extended phase-space system, where the dissipative and gyroscopic mechanisms are naturally separated. This leads to a new notion of solution, for which we establish existence and uniqueness. The resulting framework allows for genuinely rotated reflections, which can lead to angle-controlled rotations.

Probability.title: The Characteristics of Finite Projections of Certain Stochastic Processes and Queues
Probability.summary: This thesis studies finite projections of transient regenerative processes, constructed by conditioning regeneration cycles to be finite. It develops comparisons between the original and projected laws, including finite-time bounds and best-approximation properties for specified metrics and comparison classes. Applications concern birth-and-death processes, Markov chains and semi-Markov processes, with explicit queueing examples. Structural results describe projections associated with different regeneration states, invariant measures and connections with Martin boundary kernels. The thesis also studies reconstruction of birth-and-death rates from passage-time laws and continued-fraction representations of Laplace-Stieltjes transforms for skip-free semi-Markov processes, together with truncation-error bounds. This is a corrected English edition of a Romanian doctoral thesis completed in 1998 and defended in 1999. The preface distinguishes the historical work from corrections and later additions made for this edition.
Probability.comment: 89 pages; corrected English edition (2026) of the author's Romanian doctoral thesis, State University of Moldova, 1998; defended 15 January 1999

Probability.title: Free energy and spectral edge of the SYK model
Probability.summary: Consider the Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev model with $N$ Majorana fermions and interaction order $q$. For even $4\leq q\ll \sqrt{N}$, we present a microscopic framework that determines the free energy limit at every fixed inverse temperature $β>0$. In particular, this gives the first rigorous derivation of the Schwinger-Dyson thermodynamics of the model. For all even $q\in \{4,6,...,N-4\}$, we further determine the asymptotic location of the largest eigenvalue, which answers a question posed by Feng-Tian-Wei \cite{FengTianWei1}. Consequently, we obtained the free energy limit along every sequence $β\equiv β_N\to\infty$.
Probability.comment: Generalized the results and streamlined the proof. 41 pages and 1 figure

Probability.title: Data-driven stochastic asymptotic regularization for ill-posed inverse problems with a posteriori and heuristic stopping
Probability.summary: A novel Data-driven STochastic Asymptotic Regularization (\texttt{D-STAR}) method is proposed for solving linear and nonlinear ill-posed inverse problems, which incorporates a data-driven drift and a stochastic diffusion mechanism. Both known and unknown noise level cases are accommodated by the method, thereby making the framework applicable to a broader range of practical inverse problems. For known noise level, a modified discrepancy principle is employed, whereas for unknown noise level, a heuristic stopping rule based solely on noisy data is developed. For each stopping rule, an appropriate diffusion term is defined and the well-posedness of the associated stochastic differential equation is demonstrated. The finite termination of \texttt{D-STAR} method under both stopping rules is established and its convergence to the exact solution in the noise-free setting is proved. For the noisy data, stability and the regularization property in the mean-square sense are further established. In addition, the uncertainty quantification of the proposed method and its comparison with the Stochastic Asymptotic Regularization (\texttt{SAR}) method under both rules are provided. Furthermore, it is shown that local minima arising in the Data-Driven Iteratively Regularized Landweber (\texttt{DDIRLI}) method may be escaped. Finally, detailed numerical experiments, including comparisons with existing \texttt{DDIRLI} and \texttt{SAR} methods, are presented on X-ray computed tomography and nonlinear schlieren tomography for both stopping rules, thereby demonstrating the performance of \texttt{D-STAR}.

Probability.title: Langevin Dynamics of Non-reciprocally Coupled Spherical Spin Glasses
Probability.summary: We analyze the limiting dynamics of two copies of a disordered mean-field spherical $p$-spin system coupled non-reciprocally to one another and initialized independently of the disorder. We prove that, on every finite time interval, as the system size tends to infinity, the empirical correlation and integrated response functions converge almost surely and in $L^q$ for $q \geq 1$, uniformly in time, to the unique non-random solution of a system of coupled integro-differential equations. For even $p$-spin models, we establish stationarity and exponential decay of the correlation and response functions in the high-temperature regime. In the special case of the spherical Sherrington--Kirkpatrick model, we derive explicit representations of the limiting correlation and integrated response functions. These representations allow us to characterize the long-time dynamics throughout the full range of temperatures. In particular, we prove the occurrence of aging in the low-temperature regime and fluctuation-dissipation behavior in the high-temperature regime, and provide a separate characterization of the dynamics at the critical temperature.

Probability.title: Averaged Annealed Markov Chains Achieve the Algorithmic Threshold for Tensor PCA, Part II: Langevin Dynamics
Probability.summary: We consider the tensor principal components analysis (tensor PCA) problem on the sphere, in which we are asked to recover an unknown vector in $\mathcal{S}_N=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^N:\lVert x\rVert^2=N\}$ from a noisy observation of its $k$-th tensor power, for a fixed $k\ge3$. Tensor PCA exhibits a well-studied information-computation gap: global algorithms such as spectral methods and sum-of-squares work above an algorithmic threshold, below which we know matching lower bounds (against these and some other restricted models of computation). In contrast, local algorithms such as Markov chains were only known to succeed from a random initialization at a polynomially larger signal-to-noise ratio, and were believed to be inferior to global algorithms for tensor PCA. Continuing the program initiated in Part I [arXiv:2610.16705], we show that spherical Langevin dynamics, when supplemented with annealing and ergodic averaging, achieves polynomial-time strong recovery above the algorithmic threshold from a uniformly random initialization. Together with Part I, our results demonstrate that local Markov chains can succeed all the way down to the algorithmic threshold from an uninformative cold start.
Probability.comment: Companion paper to arXiv:2610.16705 (Part I). 71 pages, 1 figure

Probability.title: Strong approximations for dependent random fields
Probability.summary: We establish strong Gaussian approximations for centered stationary random fields on $\mathbb Z^d$, $d\ge2$, represented as measurable functions of i.i.d.\ innovations. Under finite $p$th moments, $p>2$, and sufficiently fast decay of spatial dependence, we construct a single coupling of the field with an i.i.d.\ Gaussian field. Its partial sums, scaled by the long-run standard deviation, approximate those of the original field almost surely, uniformly over all rectangular prefixes and all observation scales. Over a cube of side length $n$, the approximation error is $O_{\mathrm{a.s.}}(n^{\max\{d/p,(d-1)/2\}})$ up to logarithmic factors. While $d/p$ is the familiar moment term, the surface term $(d-1)/2$, absent for independent planar arrays, emerges as a cost of dependence, and cannot be removed even for finite-range Gaussian fields. The assumptions accommodate nonlinear and noncausal fields without imposing mixing. The proof combines a permanent dyadic blocking, a local Gaussian coupling in tensor Haar coordinates driven by a Doob martingale with vanishing conditional third moments, and a comparison of the resulting dependent Gaussian blocks with white noise.

Probability.title: Two-neighbor lattice percolation percolates in all dimensions
Probability.summary: It is trivial that $1$-dimensional $2$-neighbor lattice percolation percolates. Coupier, Henry, Jahnel and Köppl proved the $2$-neighbor lattice percolation percolates in dimension 2; and then for sufficiently large dimensions, Bäumler, Jahnel, Köppl, Lodewijks, Reeves and Tóbiás showed this is still true. In this paper, we verify that the $2$-neighbor lattice percolation percolates in all dimensions $d\ge 3.$

Probability.title: Nonequilibrium Thermodynamics of Semilinear Stochastic Partial Differential Equations
Probability.summary: We develop a rigorous mathematical framework for the nonequilibrium thermodynamics of semilinear stochastic partial differential equations. The invariant Gaussian measure of the associated Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process, which need not be time-reversible, serves as the reference measure. We define thermodynamic quantities in terms of probability densities and derive the entropy balance equation. We obtain explicit expressions for the entropy production rate and prove that its vanishing in the stationary state is equivalent to time reversibility. Sample-path entropy production is identified with the logarithm of the Radon-Nikodym derivative of the forward path measure with respect to the time-reversed path measure and is shown to satisfy fluctuation theorems. For nonstationary systems, sample-path entropy production decomposes into housekeeping heat and free-energy dissipation, each satisfying an integral fluctuation theorem. Both have nonnegative expectations, and the mean free-energy dissipation equals the decrease in relative entropy with respect to the stationary distribution. The theory is applied to semilinear stochastic heat equations with spatially correlated noise, a random polymer model, a nonlinear model with a divergence-free drift, and two coupled stochastic heat equations in contact with heat baths at different temperatures.

Probability.title: Graph-diameter criteria and sharp dissipation in discrete Wasserstein-Fisher geometry
Probability.summary: We study the probability simplex of a finite connected weighted graph with an Onsager operator combining logarithmic-mean transport and mass-conserving Fisher reaction. For every fixed positive reaction parameter, we prove that the entropy Hessian has a finite global lower bound if and only if the original transport graph has diameter at most two. Near a boundary probability, the corresponding criterion is that its positive support reaches every vertex in at most two steps. The proof controls all potential directions under arbitrary multiscale boundary degeneration. For graphs of diameter at most two, the optimal lower bound is Lipschitz on bounded parameter intervals, including the pure-transport endpoint. We also determine the largest instantaneous logarithmic-amplitude dissipation function depending only on the graph and the current amplitude, and construct two-level probabilities attaining it. Its positivity has the same two-step criterion. As consequences, we obtain graph-dependent entropy-decay estimates and exact projective contraction bounds without assuming nonnegative entropic curvature.

Differential Geometry.title: The determinant of the Dirichlet-to-Neumann map for a surface with boundary and periods of holomorphic differentials on its double
Differential Geometry.summary:
Let $(M,g)$ be a smooth orientable $2d$ Riemannian manifold of genus $\mathfrak{g}$ with Riemannian metric $g$ and connected boundary $Γ$. Let $Λ$ be the Dirichlet-to-Neumann map on $Γ$ and let ${\rm det}_ζ(Λ)$ be its (modified, i. e. with zero mode excluded) $ζ$-regularized determinant. It is well-known that the quantity ${\rm det}_ζ(Λ)/|Γ|$ (where $|Γ|$ is the length of $Γ$) is a conformal invariant. It was shown by Edward and Wu (\cite{EV}) that this invariant equals one for $\mathfrak{g}=0$; in the case $\mathfrak{g}>0$ Guillarmou and Guillopé \cite{Guillarmou} found two explicit expressions for this invariant through the Rouelle and (respectively) the Selberg zeta-functions of the two surfaces of negative constant curvature from the conformal class of $(M,g)$: one is of infinite volume and complete whereas another has geodesic boundary.
  We present an elementary counterpart of the formulae of Guillarmou and Guillopé using the periods of holomorphic differentials on the double $2M$ of $M$ only. Our approach is based on the properties of the Hilbert transform of $M$ \cite{B,HilbKor} and the Kontsevich-Vishik-Friedlander-Guillemin regularization of the determinants of pseudodifferenial operators \cite{KV,Ww,F}. In particular, a connection between the length spectra of (uniformized) $M$, $2M$ and the periods of holomorphic differentials on $2M$ is established.

Differential Geometry.title: Synge's Theorem and a Sphere Theorem in Weighted Intermediate Ricci Curvature
Differential Geometry.summary: Using the tools developed by Kennard, Wylie, and Yeroshkin for weighted sectional curvature bounds, we generalize a theorem of Wilhelm to show that Synge's Theorem holds for manifolds with density that have positive weighted intermediate Ricci curvature and a sufficiently large first systole. Furthermore, we provide a sphere theorem for compact manifolds with positive weighted intermediate Ricci curvature.

Differential Geometry.title: The cross quadratic bisectional curvature of Kähler $C$-spaces of classical type
Differential Geometry.summary: In this paper, we show that any Kähler $C$-space of classical type has nonnegative cross quadratic bisectional curvature and positive dual cross quadratic bisectional curvature. As a consequence, such manifolds are Fano. This confirms a substantial part of a conjecture of Ni-Zheng (Conjecture 1.5 in \cite{NZ}).

Differential Geometry.title: Topology and regularity of small sub-Riemannian balls under an index condition
Differential Geometry.summary: We study the topology and regularity of small sub-Riemannian balls under an index condition on length-minimizing curves in the metric tangent space. We prove that sufficiently small spheres are Lipschitz hypersurfaces homeomorphic to Euclidean spheres, while closed balls are homeomorphic to Euclidean closed balls, and open balls are diffeomorphic to Euclidean open balls. These results improve the known ones and extend them beyond two-step distributions. The proof relies on uniform Lipschitz estimates for the distance, of independent interest.

Differential Geometry.title: Compactification of parabolic Hermitian--Einstein moduli spaces on complex surfaces
Differential Geometry.summary: Let $\overline{X}$ be a compact complex surface with a Gauduchon metric, and let $D\subset\overline{X}$ be a smooth connected divisor. We construct an Uhlenbeck compactification of the moduli space of rank-two parabolic Hermitian--Einstein connections with prescribed holomorphic determinant.

Differential Geometry.title: Mean-convex horizontal mean curvature flow in the Heisenberg group
Differential Geometry.summary: We study the arrival time equation of the mean-convex horizontal mean curvature flow in the Heisenberg group. We prove existence of viscosity solutions when the initial set is horizontally mean-convex and either non-characteristic, or axisymmetric and with horizontal mean curvature extending continuously across the characteristic set. A key ingredient is an approximation scheme by sets with prescribed Riemannian mean curvature, which preserves the mean-curvature bounds up to an arbitrarily small error. We further show that, when the evolving level sets form a generalized \(C^2\)-foliation, the horizontal mean curvature blows up around characteristic points. This provides an obstruction to self-similar evolution in the axisymmetric class considered above and, in particular, shows that the Pansu sphere cannot evolve self-similarly.

Differential Geometry.title: Analysis of blowup masses in constant-coefficient Toda systems: W-invariants and Weyl orbits
Differential Geometry.summary: We classify the local blowup masses of constant-coefficient Toda systems for all simple Lie algebras with one prescribed singular source, bounded component masses, and bounded boundary oscillations. We encode the source strengths and the blowup masses by two elements of the Cartan subalgebra: the grading element $p_μ$ and the mass element $q_σ$. We show that $p_μ-q_σ=wp_μ$ for some Weyl group element $w\in W$. The proof uses the Drinfeld-Sokolov gauge and the resulting holomorphic $W$-invariants for Toda systems. Asymptotic analysis near the source and on a shrinking circle enclosing the total local mass gives two evaluations of the leading Laurent coefficients of the $W$-invariants, which agree by holomorphicity. This agreement enables us to conclude the above Weyl-orbit result. In particular, the quadratic constraint is the local Pohozaev identity. Only with the full set of $W$-invariants can we strengthen earlier orbit-plus-integer restrictions to an exact Weyl-orbit characterization in the constant-coefficient setting. Together with the author's explicit families in [Nie], this determines all attainable local mass vectors.

Differential Geometry.title: The geometry of Floquet states
Differential Geometry.summary:
This paper studies the moduli space of "good" periodic Hamiltonians, i.e., periodic Hamiltonians with nondegenerate Floquet spectrum. The corresponding Floquet states determine a geometric model for the moduli space of such Hamiltonians. The model is expressed in terms of configuration spaces, flag manifolds, and principal bundles. A corollary of the main result is the complete determination of the rational cohomology ring of the space of good periodic Hamiltonians.
  The paper also considers the adiabatic driving of a 1-parameter family of good periodic Hamiltonians. We formulate two conjectures describing the resulting asymptotic quantum evolution. These are Floquet analogues of the adiabatic theorem in quantum mechanics.

Differential Geometry.title: Solitons on Statistical Manifolds and Their Submanifolds
Differential Geometry.summary:
Statistical manifolds, introduced by Amari in information geometry, carry a pair of dual torsion-free connections $(
abla,
abla^{*})$ together with a Riemannian metric. In this chapter we survey the theory of \emph{statistical solitons}, that is, vector fields and constants that solve the Ricci-soliton equation simultaneously for $
abla$ and $
abla^{*}$, together with the statistical analogue of almost quasi-Yamabe solitons. We discuss two principal settings: (i) statistical warped products $\R	imes_f N_2$ and $N_1	imes_f\R$ for (pseudo) Riemannian manifolds $N_{1}$ and $N_{2}$, where the soliton equation constrains the warping function; and (ii) statistical submanifolds of Kenmotsu statistical manifolds, where the position of the Reeb field $ξ$ relative to the submanifold and the presence of concircular or concurrent vector fields determine the Einstein, $η$-Einstein or quasi-Einstein character of the submanifold. We further review the results of Blaga and Chen on gradient solitons and statistical structures, in particular the connections $
abla^θ$ defined by a $1$-form, volume formulas and bounds for the Ricci tensor. We also describe Chen-type inequalities for statistical warped product submanifolds, which give the extrinsic context in which such solitons live. Key steps of the proofs, remarks on the sharpness of hypotheses, worked examples, and open problems are included.

Differential Geometry.title: Gel'fand's inverse problem under Ricci curvature bounds
Differential Geometry.summary: The classical Gel'fand's inverse problem asks whether a Riemannian manifold is uniquely determined by the knowledge of the heat kernel on any open subset of the manifold. We study this inverse problem in the non-smooth setting in the framework of ${\rm RCD}(K,N)$ spaces, namely, metric-measure spaces with synthetic Riemannian Ricci curvature bounded below by $K$ and dimension bounded above by $N$. We establish the unique solvability of Gel'fand's inverse problem for the class of compact ${\rm RCD}(K,N)$ spaces whose regular set admits Lipschitz Riemannian structure. As an application, we obtain the continuity of Gel'fand's inverse problem in the class of closed Riemannian manifolds with bounded Ricci curvature, diameter and volume bounded from below. We note that the results are new even for Einstein orbifolds and (weighted) Lipschitz Riemannian manifolds with non-smooth boundary.

Differential Geometry.title: Sobolev inequalities for sections and projections of log-concave functions
Differential Geometry.summary: Higher order sharp Sobolev and local Sobolev type inequalities for log-concave functions are established. The new inequalities directly imply the isoperimetric inequalities by Bollobás and Thomason in 1995, by Liakopoulos in 2019, and the recently discovered local isoperimetric inequalities from [1]. In order to do so, we make use of three ingredients. First, sets of functional inequalities proven by Alonso-Gutiérrez, Bernués, Brazitikos and Carbery in 2021. Second, a multidimensional polynomial optimization result that originated in [1] and was initiated by Bollobás and Thomason. Third, a new integral formula for the projection of a log-concave function that links the geometric part with the more functional versions via some dependence on the Hessian matrix restricted to subspaces.

Differential Geometry.title: Prescribed mean curvature surfaces of Riemann minimal type
Differential Geometry.summary: We construct analogues of Riemann minimal examples among surfaces in the Euclidean 3-space whose mean curvature is given by a prescribed function on the unit sphere in terms of their Gauss map. Specifically, we obtain a 2-parameter family of complete, properly embedded surfaces foliated by circles and straight lines and invariant under a nontrivial translation.

Differential Geometry.title: New explicit examples of Mannheim pair in $\mathbb{L}^3$
Differential Geometry.summary: In this paper, we construct explicit examples of Mannheim pairs, in the classical sense, in Minkowski 3-space $\mathbb{L}^3$, one for each of the five types of such pairs. In our main examples the Mannheim curve is neither a helix nor a slant helix. For each example we give the complete Frenet apparatus of both curves of the pair and their Cartesian coordinates in terms of elementary functions. The construction writes the tangent indicatrix in angular coordinates and uses a suitable auxiliary angle function, which reduces all the relevant integrals to elementary form; it is carried out both starting from the Mannheim curve and starting from its partner. In these coordinates, we also characterize the helices and the slant helices with timelike axis. We also prove, for the five types, that a Mannheim curve is a slant helix if and only if its partner is a helix, and we give an explicit example of such a pair.

Differential Geometry.title: Curvature-Dimension Conditions Along Discrete Refinement Sequences
Differential Geometry.summary: We introduce the sequence curvature--dimension condition $SCD(K,N)$ for complete refinement systems of finite metric probability spaces. The condition couples a transport action bound with entropy comparisons along a single probability section through the prescribed refinement layers. Within a bounded comparison range, we prove that midpoint comparisons on three consecutive layers characterize the condition on every fixed finite segment. If, in addition, the refinement sequence converges in the measured sense in its intrinsic bridge realization, then $SCD(K,N)$ is equivalent both to the vanishing of single-layer midpoint defects and to the entropic curvature--dimension condition $CD^{e}(K,N)$ of the limit. In the reverse direction, a $CD^{e}(K,N)$ bound on the limit yields quantitative recovery estimates that identify shrinking transport scales on which finite layers retain its second-order curvature comparison. These estimates are uniform over endpoint measures and include Dirac masses. Examples illustrate the effects of the refinement rule, the layer metrics and the reference measures.

Differential Geometry.title: The Willmore Energy Landscape of Spheres and Avoidable Singularities of the Willmore Flow
Differential Geometry.summary: We study the sublevel sets of the Willmore energy on the space of smoothly immersed $ 2 $-spheres in Euclidean $ 3 $-space. We show that the subset of immersions with energy at most $ 12π$ consists of four regular homotopy classes. Moreover, we show that in certain regular homotopy classes, all singularities of the Willmore flow are avoidable, that is, the initial surface admits a regular homotopy to a round sphere whose Willmore energy does not exceed that of the initial surface. This yields a classification of initial surfaces with energy at most $ 12π$ that lead to unavoidable singularities. As a further consequence, we obtain an extension of the Li-Yau inequality at $ 12π$ for a large class of immersed spheres without triple points. To prove these results, we glue together different instances of the Willmore flow and employ an invariant for triple-point-free immersed spheres.

Differential Geometry.title: Mass-type invariants in the presence of a cosmological constant
Differential Geometry.summary: In this paper, we introduce a new family of mass-type invariants for time-symmetric initial data in space-times satisfying the Dominant Energy Condition. For positive cosmological constant, these invariants, unlike the total Hawking mass, turn out to be genuinely effective in providing new characterizations of the de Sitter solution. From a theoretical standpoint, this opens a new perspective on how one might refine the rigidity statement originally proposed by Min-Oo in his well known conjecture, later refuted by the counterexamples of Brendle, Marques, and Neves. Via a formal limiting procedure, we also define another invariant, the 1-harmonic Mass, for which we independently prove a positive mass theorem and a Penrose-type inequality, thereby extending tools for probing space-time geometries in the presence of a positive cosmological constant.
Differential Geometry.comment: Minor modifications w.r.t. the previous version: a more detailed proof of the small-sphere-limit Theorem 3.8 has been inserted and a proof of the existence of the weak IMCF with outer obstacle starting from a pole has been added in the new Appendix C

Differential Geometry.title: Volumes of moduli spaces of flat surfaces
Differential Geometry.summary: We study the moduli spaces of flat surfaces with prescribed conical singularities. Veech showed that these spaces are diffeomorphic to the moduli spaces of marked Riemann surfaces, and endowed with a natural volume form depending on the orders of the singularities. We show that the volumes of these spaces are finite. Moreover we show that they are explicitely computable by induction on the Euler characteristics of the punctured surface for almost all orders of the singularities.

Differential Geometry.title: Carnot geodesics with Hölder controls
Differential Geometry.summary: We construct an explicit length-minimizing curve in a polynomial rank-two sub-Riemannian structure on $\R^4$. Its arclength parametrization is $C^{1,1/2}$ and is not $C^{1,α}$ near an interior point for any $α>1/2$. Minimality is proved by an approximate calibration chosen separately for each competitor. The example admits a minimizing lift to a rank-two Carnot group of step five. Generalizations are announced.

Differential Geometry.title: Backward Pseudolocality of $G_2$-Laplacian Flow
Differential Geometry.summary: In this paper, we establish a new estimate on the time-derivative of pointed Nash entropy and use it to give a new proof of backward pseudolocality for Ricci flow. The proof does not rely on Bamler's compactness theorem and structure theory concerning limits of Ricci flows. Our methods also work for other reasonable geometric flows, like the $G_2$-Laplacian, at a scale depending on its deviation from Ricci flow and its scalar curvature.

Differential Geometry.title: Pseudolocality of $G_2$-Laplacian Flow
Differential Geometry.summary: In this paper, we give a new proof of Perelman's pseudolocality theorem for Ricci flow, which does not rely on Perelman's Harnack-type inequality. The key step is an estimate relating initial local $μ$-entropy to pointed Nash entropy at later spacetime points. The argument also works for other reasonable geometric flows, like the $G_2$-Laplacian flow, at a scale depending on its deviation from Ricci flow and its scalar curvature lower bound. As a consequence, we can also prove the quantitative rigidity results concerning pointed Nash entropy due to Hein-Naber and Bamler for such geometric flows. In the appendix, we also show that the other results in Bamler's work (arXiv:2008.07093), when suitably modified, remain valid for Laplacian flow with bounded torsion. These include log-Sobolev/Poincaré inequality for conjugate heat kernel measure, heat kernel estimates, and dependence of the pointed Nash entropy on its basepoint.

Differential Geometry.title: Projective compactifications of hypersurface complements
Differential Geometry.summary: Let $U$ be a smooth affine variety of the form $U=\mathrm{P}^n\setminus H$, where $H\subset\mathrm{P}^n$ is a smooth connected hypersurface. We prove that every smooth projective compactification of the complex manifold $U$, by adding a smooth connected divisor, is isomorphic to $\mathrm{P}^n$. The proof uses the rational Reeb index of the normal circle bundle and positive $S^1$-equivariant symplectic homology. This paper is motivated by the work of Chi Li and Zhengyi Zhou, and makes a generalization to their result.

Differential Geometry.title: Einstein Metrics and Quantum Control on Symmetric Tensor Product Quotients
Differential Geometry.summary: Let $M_n=(\mathrm{PU}(2)^n\rtimes S_n)\backslash\mathrm{PU}(2^n)$ be the space of projective $n$-qubit unitaries modulo local unitaries and permutations of the qubits. We prove that for all sufficiently large $n$ the manifold $M_n$ carries exactly two $\mathrm{PU}(2^n)$-invariant Einstein metrics up to scaling. Both Einstein metrics have uniformly bounded diameter after normalizing two-qubit costs, although approximating a Haar-random unitary requires exponentially many two-qubit gates. In contrast, we construct non-Einstein metrics with nonnegative Ricci curvature and exponentially growing typical control distances, and determine the sharp curvature threshold for this family.

Differential Geometry.title: Kähler-Einstein toric submanifolds of the projective space
Differential Geometry.summary: We show that the Kähler-Einstein metrics on the four families of symmetric toric Fano manifolds due to Batyrev and Selivanova cannot be induced by immersions into projective spaces equipped with the Fubini-Study metric. We also show a similar conclusion for the non-symmetric examples discovered by Nill and Paffenholz. As an application we obtain that a centrally symmetric toric Fano manifold admits a Kähler-Einstein metric induced by a projective immersion if and only if it is a product of projective lines. These results confirm for each of these examples a broader conjecture characterizing the Kähler--Einstein metrics that can be induced by projective immersions.
Differential Geometry.comment: Final version, 29 pages, 3 figures. To appear in the Journal of Geometric Analysis

Differential Geometry.title: A Physics-Informed Neural Network for Geodesic Computation and Visualization of Geodesic Spheres on Riemannian Manifolds
Differential Geometry.summary:
Visualizing geodesic structures associated with general Riemannian metrics is a challenging problem in computational differential geometry. In this work, we present a computational framework for visualizing geodesics and geodesic spheres on a three-dimensional Riemannian manifold equipped with the metric $g=\text{diag}(1,x^2,1), x>0$. The associated Christoffel symbols and curvature tensors are computed symbolically, and the resulting geodesic equations are solved using both \texttt{SciPy}'s numerical integration method and a Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN). The two solutions are compared to assess the accuracy of the neural network approximation. We further develop geodesic spike diagrams and surface visualizations to illustrate the deformation of geodesic spheres relative to their Euclidean counterparts. Intrinsic Riemannian surface area and volume are estimated numerically using the induced metric and the Riemannian volume density, respectively. For the chosen metric and a geodesic ball of radius one, the computed area and volume are approximately
  $0.362\%$ and $0.364\%$ smaller than the corresponding Euclidean values at the base grid resolution. A grid-refinement study is also performed to examine the sensitivity of these estimates to numerical resolution. The proposed framework demonstrates how symbolic differential geometry, numerical integration, and PINNs can be combined to investigate and visualize geometric structures associated with Riemannian metrics.

Differential Geometry.title: On the $n$-dimensional Blaschke-Lebesgue Problem
Differential Geometry.summary: The classical Blaschke-Lebesgue problem seeks the convex body of minimal volume among all convex bodies of prescribed constant width. In this paper, we investigate the necessary conditions for volume minimizers of the $n$-dimensional Blaschke-Lebesgue problem via the inverse Gauss map and the inverse Weingarten transformation. We first introduce a generalized support function for hypersurfaces induced by the inverse Gauss map, characterize the Wigner caustic of constant width bodies, and accordingly construct convex bodies of constant width from prescribed functions. Building upon there results and applying the Brunn-Minkowski inequality, we establish a high-dimensional necessary condition: for almost every antipodal pair of a volume minimizer, one point is non-regular; at the other point, the minimum principal curvatures equals the reciprocal of the constant width. As an application, we provide a new proof for the two-dimensional Blaschke-Lebesgue theorem. Furthermore, we study the dimension-raising construction of Lachand-Robert and Oudet, and prove that every convex body produced by this construction satisfies our necessary condition. Finally, we put forward a conjecture stating that the sequence obtained by iterating this construction starting from a line segment yields minimizers for the Blaschke-Lebesgue problem for all dimensions.

Differential Geometry.title: A complete Kähler metric on $\mathbb{C}^n$ of nonnegative Ricci curvature with Euclidean volume growth and nonunique asymptotic cone
Differential Geometry.summary: We construct complete smooth Kähler metrics on $\mathbb{C}^n$ , $n\ge2$, with nonnegative Ricci curvature, Euclidean volume growth, and nonunique tangent cones at infinity. More generally, we prescribe the entire tangent cone set within a class of smooth Hopf cones, using a compact connected family of positive transverse Ricci forms on $\mathbb{C}\mathbb{P}^{n-1}$. We identify all metric blow-downs and their Ricci currents, compute the exact asymptotic volume ratio, and classify isometries between the model cones. In particular, the Kähler condition does not ensure uniqueness at infinity under nonnegative Ricci curvature and Euclidean volume growth, even in complex dimension two.
Differential Geometry.comment: The authors want to thank professor Gabor Szekelyhidi for drawing their attention to the related work of Arka Karmakar (https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.18432) in August

Differential Geometry.title: The Miyaoka-Yau inequality and the delta invariant for Fano varieties II -soliton case-
Differential Geometry.summary: Inspired by recent work of Inoue and Hallam-Lahdili, we prove an equivariant Miyaoka-Yau inequality with a correction term for smooth Fano manifolds admitting Kähler-Ricci solitons. It recovers the usual Miyaoka-Yau inequality in the Kähler-Einstein case. Our proof uses weighted equivariant Bogomolov-Gieseker and Langer inequalities for torsion-free sheaves, together with a weighted slope estimate for the canonical extension sheaf. We also construct toric examples showing that the existence of a soliton implies neither weighted semistability of the canonical extension sheaf nor nonnegativity of the equivariant Miyaoka-Yau number.
Differential Geometry.comment: v1: 54 pages; An earlier version of this paper was included as the second part of arXiv:2607.25181. The original manuscript has since been divided into two independent papers. Comments are welcome

Differential Geometry.title: Uniqueness of the weak solutions of the Yang-Mills flow in four dimensions
Differential Geometry.summary: We improve a parabolic version of Uhlenbeck's gauge fixing theorem for the Yang-Mills flow. This allows us to prove new existence of weak solutions of the Yang-Mills flow having with better properties than Struwe's weak solution on four manifolds in \cite {St2}. Finally, we apply the new parabolic version of Uhlenbeck's gauge fixing theorem to solve the Struwe problem in \cite {St2} and prove uniqueness of weak solutions to the Yang-Mills flow on compact four-manifolds with initial value $A_0 \in W^{1, 2}(M)$.

Differential Geometry.title: Graph-diameter criteria and sharp dissipation in discrete Wasserstein-Fisher geometry
Differential Geometry.summary: We study the probability simplex of a finite connected weighted graph with an Onsager operator combining logarithmic-mean transport and mass-conserving Fisher reaction. For every fixed positive reaction parameter, we prove that the entropy Hessian has a finite global lower bound if and only if the original transport graph has diameter at most two. Near a boundary probability, the corresponding criterion is that its positive support reaches every vertex in at most two steps. The proof controls all potential directions under arbitrary multiscale boundary degeneration. For graphs of diameter at most two, the optimal lower bound is Lipschitz on bounded parameter intervals, including the pure-transport endpoint. We also determine the largest instantaneous logarithmic-amplitude dissipation function depending only on the graph and the current amplitude, and construct two-level probabilities attaining it. Its positivity has the same two-step criterion. As consequences, we obtain graph-dependent entropy-decay estimates and exact projective contraction bounds without assuming nonnegative entropic curvature.

Differential Geometry.title: The Yang-Mills flow in vector bundles over higher dimensional Riemannian manifolds
Differential Geometry.summary: We develop a parabolic formulation of the Uhlenbeck gauge fixing theorem and use it to prove the maximal existence of the Yang-Mills flow in vector bundles over compact $n$-dimensional Riemannian manifolds for $n \geq 4$. We apply Moser's iteration technique \cite{Mo1} to give a new proof of the bound of the curvature. Using an idea of Hamilton on the Ricci flow \cite{Ha}, we also provide a new proof on uniform estimates of higher order derivatives. Furthermore, we investigate the blow-up of the Yang-Mills flow at the maximal existence time and improve an asymptotical result of Hong-Tian \cite{HT1}.

Differential Geometry.title: New Explicit Examples of Mannheim Pairs in $\mathbb{R}^3$
Differential Geometry.summary: In this paper, we construct new explicit parametrizations of Mannheim pairs in Euclidean 3-space. Unlike the known examples in the literature, which are essentially slant helices or general helices, the curve presented here is neither a helix nor a slant helix. We provide the full Frenet apparatus, the explicit Cartesian coordinates expressed in terms of elementary functions, and the corresponding Mannheim partner curve. The construction is based on a specific choice of the angular function that governs the curve's tangent indicatrix, leading to integrable expressions.

Geometric Topology.title: Non-concordant 2-links in simply-connected 4-manifolds
Geometric Topology.summary: We construct an infinite family of smooth 2-component links of 2-spheres $Σ_k\subset S^2\times S^2$ whose respective components are smoothly concordant but which are pairwise not topologically concordant in any topological $\mathbb{Z}$-homology cobordism. In particular, the $Σ_k$ are pairwise non-concordant in $(S^2\times S^2)\times[0,1]$.

Geometric Topology.title: $L$-Space Knots in $\mathfrak{sl}_{n}$-like Knot Floer Homology
Geometric Topology.summary: It has been of particular interest in recent years to relate categorifications of quantum knot invariants like the Jones polynomial to Floer-theoretic invariants like knot Floer homology using spectral sequences. In pursuit of Rasmussen's conjecture, Dowlin constructed a family of invariants with properties like those of Khovanov and Rozansky's $\mathfrak{sl}_n$-homology theories. In this paper, we explore these invariants for $L$-space knots and thin knots. In particular, for $n\geq 2$ the invariants of thin knots can be computed from a change of coefficients from the minus flavor of knot Floer homology, and the same holds for an $L$-space knot exactly when an explicit condition relating $n$ to its Alexander polynomial is satisfied.

Geometric Topology.title: Sharp dimension bounds for right-angled hyperbolic polytopes
Geometric Topology.summary: We determine the largest dimensions in which right-angled hyperbolic polytopes of finite volume can exist. The dimension is at most eight in general, and at most four when all vertices lie at infinity. Both bounds are attained, improving the previously known upper bounds of twelve and six. Our proofs use elementary properties of hyperbolic polytopes together with bounds for configurations of points on spheres.

Geometric Topology.title: Vietoris-Rips complexes of affine Coxeter groups
Geometric Topology.summary: We prove that all affine Coxeter groups admit contractible Vietoris-Rips complexes. More precisely, for any affine Coxeter group $W_a$ there exists a finite generating set $A$ such that $\mathcal{VR}_t(W_a;A)$ is contractible for all $t\ge 1$. We prove this as a special case of a more general result about certain groups. Let $G$ be a group and $H$ a subgroup. A subgroup $F\le G$ is a supplement of $H$ in $G$ if $G=HF$. We prove that for $H\le G$ with $F$ a supplement of $H$ in $G$, for generating sets $A_H$ and $A_G$ of $H$ and $G$ satisfying certain conditions involving $F$, the Vietoris-Rips complexes $\mathcal{VR}_t(G;A_G)$ and $\mathcal{VR}_t(H;A_H)$ are homotopy equivalent for all $t\ge 1$. In particular this applies to affine Coxeter groups, since free abelian groups admit contractible Vietoris-Rips complexes. Beyond these general results, we also investigate affine Coxeter groups $W_a$ specifically using the standard generating set $S$, and prove contractibility of $\mathcal{VR}_t(W_a;S)$ for large enough $t$.

Geometric Topology.title: An Unexpected Rational Blowdown
Geometric Topology.summary: The rational blowdown operation in 4-manifold topology replaces a neighborhood of a configuration of spheres by a rational homology ball. Such configurations typically arise from resolutions of surface singularities that admit rational homology disk smoothings. Conjecturally, all such singularities must be weighted homogeneous and belong to certain specific families: Stipsicz-Szabó--Wahl constructed QHD smoothings for these families and used Donaldson's theorem to obtain very restrictive necessary conditions on the resolution graphs for singularities with this property. In particular, these results, as well as subsequent work of Bhupal-Stipsicz, show that for certain resolution graphs, the canonical contact structure on the link of the singularity cannot admit a QHD symplectic filling. By contrast, we exhibit Stein rational homology disk fillings for the contact links of an infinite family of rational singularities that are not weighted homogeneous, producing a new symplectic rational blowdown. Inspiration for our construction comes from de Jong-van Straten's description of Milnor fibers of sandwiched singularities; we use the symplectic analog of de Jong-van Straten theory developed by the second and third authors. The unexpected Stein fillings are built using spinal open books and nearly Lefschetz fibrations.
Geometric Topology.comment: 29 pages, 35 figures, final version accepted to Journal of Topology

Geometric Topology.title: A marking graph for finite-type Artin groups
Geometric Topology.summary: Clean markings on surfaces were a key component in Masur and Minsky's hierarchy machinery, which proved to be a powerful tool in the study of mapping class groups. We construct a marking graph for irreducible finite-type Artin groups which is quasi-isometric to the group modulo its center, i.e., an element of $A_Γ/Z(A_Γ)$ is determined up to finite error by its action on one of our markings. To construct this graph, we construct suitable collections of transverse parabolic subgroups which extend the maximal simplices of the complex of irreducible parabolic subgroups to analogues of clean markings, and we define natural analogues of elementary moves.
Geometric Topology.comment: 58 pages. v2: minor corrections and improvements

Optimization and Control.title: A Practical GPU-Enhanced Matrix-Free Primal-Dual Method for Large-Scale Conic Programs
Optimization and Control.summary: In this paper, we introduce a practical GPU-enhanced matrix-free first-order method for solving large-scale conic programming problems, which we refer to as PDCS, standing for the Primal-Dual Conic Programming Solver. Problems that it solves include linear programs, second-order cone programs, convex quadratic programs, and exponential cone programs. The method avoids matrix factorizations and uses sparse matrix-vector multiplication as its core operation, which is memory-efficient and well suited for GPU acceleration. It builds on a variant of the primal-dual hybrid gradient method (PDHG) called reflected restarted Halpern PDHG with averaging, which we prove converges on general conic programs, and further incorporates several practical enhancements. Its GPU implementation, cuPDCS, uses customized computational schemes that assign cones of different types and sizes to different levels of the GPU architecture. Numerical experiments demonstrate that cuPDCS is generally more efficient than state-of-the-art commercial solvers and other first-order methods on large-scale conic program applications, including Fisher market equilibrium problems, Lasso regression, and multi-period portfolio optimization. cuPDCS also exhibits better scalability, efficiency, and robustness compared to other first-order methods on the conic program benchmark dataset CBLIB. These advantages are more pronounced in large-scale settings.

Optimization and Control.title: MOE-DGSCND: Multi-Objective Enterprise Green Supply Chain Network Design
Optimization and Control.summary: This paper introduces and studies the Multi-Objective Enterprise Doubly-Green Supply Chain Network Design (MOE-DGSCND) problem, an extension of Multi-Objective Supply Chain Network Design. The problem studied here is a three-objective combinatorial optimization problem that simultaneously minimizes total cost f1, carbon dioxide emissions f2 and customer dissatisfaction f3 over binary decisions regarding which distribution centers to open and how to assign customer zones to open facilities. The problem generalizes the capacitated facility location problem (CFLP) and is known to be NP-hard (Garey and Johnson, 1979). This paper formally specifies the decision variables, objective functions and constraints and investigates three solution approaches using a single numerical instance: (A) an exact weighted-sum integer linear programming (ILP) formulation solved with Python combinatorially and via PuLP, (B) three Fully Polynomial-Time Approximation Schemes (FPTAS) providing (1 + $ε$)-approximate solutions for $ε$ := 0.15 and (C) two baseline heuristics for comparison. On an instance with eight customers and five candidate distribution centers, the exact solver certifies the optimal (sampled) supported solutions across eight weight combinations, while the FPTAS-based approaches complete within milliseconds, compared to centiseconds for the exact ILP on this tiny non-stochastic instance.

Optimization and Control.title: Sharpness of Minima in Deep Matrix Factorization
Optimization and Control.summary: Understanding the loss-landscape geometry near a minimum is key to explaining the implicit bias of gradient-based methods in non-convex optimization problems such as deep neural network training and deep matrix factorization. A central quantity for characterizing this geometry is the maximum eigenvalue of the Hessian of the loss. Currently, its precise role has been obfuscated because no exact expressions for this sharpness measure were known in general settings. In this paper, we present the first exact expression for the maximum eigenvalue of the Hessian of the squared-error loss at any minimizer in deep matrix factorization problems, resolving an open question posed by Mulayoff and Michaeli [2020]. This expression reveals a fundamental property of the loss landscape in deep matrix factorization: It is sufficient, but not necessary, for flatness that, across all layers, the product of the spectral norms of the left and right intermediate factors equals a constant determined by the depth and the spectral norm of the target matrix. Most notably, in both depth-2 matrix factorization and deep overparameterized scalar factorization, we show that this condition is both necessary and sufficient for flatness, which implies that flat minima are spectral-norm balanced and not necessarily balanced in depth-2 matrix factorization. To complement our theory, we provide empirical verification, relying on our exact expression, of an escape phenomenon during gradient-based training near a minimizer of a deep matrix factorization problem.

Optimization and Control.title: Tunable Spatial Task Allocation with Application to Maritime Swarms
Optimization and Control.summary: In this chapter, we explore how a team of autonomous agents can flexibly reconfigure the distribution of its members across many spatially embedded tasks using a task allocation strategy grounded in a generalization of the recently proposed Nonlinear Opinion Dynamics model. Motivated by an adaptive maritime survey application, we couple opinion dynamics directly to spatial movement and examine how the emergent macroscopic allocation is shaped by the interplay between environmental geometry, nature of social interactions, and task demands. We illustrate in simulation how social coupling in the model tunes group cohesion, producing macroscopic allocation patterns ranging from maximally dispersed states, to intermediate semi-dispersed states with a smaller number of distinct subgroups, to maximally cohesive consensus states, in distinct and interpretable parameter regimes. Furthermore, we demonstrate with illustrative examples how a team can reconfigure itself in real time under changing task demands. For allocation scenarios with distance-based task preference and matched number of agents and tasks, we relate numerically the final allocation in the group to the Hungarian optimum, illustrating close-to-optimal performance. We illustrate performance of this method under realistic communication constraints in the MOOS-IvP-Multi simulation environment with simulated autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs). Together, these examples show how a common set of local interaction rules can support a large range of interpretable macroscopic allocation states and flexible transitions between them.

Optimization and Control.title: A Spectral Perspective on Stochastic Control Barrier Functions
Optimization and Control.summary: Stochastic control barrier functions (SCBFs) provide a safety-critical control framework for systems subject to stochastic disturbances by bounding the probability of remaining within a safe set. However, finding a valid SCBF that explicitly reflects the long-horizon behavior of the true safety probability remains a challenge. This paper addresses this issue by adopting a spectral perspective, utilizing the linear operator that governs the evolution of the closed-loop system's safety probability. We find that the dominant eigenpair of this Koopman-like operator encodes fundamental safety information of the stochastic system. The dominant eigenfunction is a natural and valid SCBF, with values that characterize relative asymptotic safety across initial states, while the dominant eigenvalue indicates the global asymptotic rate at which the safety probability decays. A practical algorithm for computation is proposed, termed power-policy iteration, which jointly estimates the dominant eigenpair while updating the backup policy with the aim of improving long-term safety. The method is validated using simulation experiments on safety-critical dynamics models.
Optimization and Control.comment: 16 pages, 8 figures. This work has been submitted to the IEEE for possible publication

Optimization and Control.title: Activate the Dual Cones: A Tight Reformulation of Conic ACOPF Constraints
Optimization and Control.summary: By exploiting the observed tightness of dual rotated second-order cone (RSOC) constraints, this paper transforms the dual of a conic ACOPF relaxation into an equivalent, non-conic problem where dual constraints are implicitly enforced through eliminated dual RSOC variables. To accomplish this, we apply the RSOC-based Jabr relaxation of ACOPF, pose its dual, and then show that all dual RSOC constraints must be tight (i.e., active) at optimality. We then construct a reduced dual maximization problem with only non-negativity constraints, avoiding the explicit RSOC inequality constraints. Numerical experiments confirm that the tight formulation recovers the same dual objective values as a mature conic solver (e.g., MOSEK via PowerModels) on various PGLib benchmark test systems (ranging from 3- to 1354-buses). The proposed formulation has useful performance benefits, compared with its conic counterpart, and it allows us to define a bounding function which provides a guaranteed lower bound on system cost. While this paper focuses on demonstrating the correctness and validity of the proposed structural simplification, it lays the groundwork for future GPU-accelerated first-order optimization methods which can exploit the unconstrained nature of the proposed formulation.

Optimization and Control.title: Topology and regularity of small sub-Riemannian balls under an index condition
Optimization and Control.summary: We study the topology and regularity of small sub-Riemannian balls under an index condition on length-minimizing curves in the metric tangent space. We prove that sufficiently small spheres are Lipschitz hypersurfaces homeomorphic to Euclidean spheres, while closed balls are homeomorphic to Euclidean closed balls, and open balls are diffeomorphic to Euclidean open balls. These results improve the known ones and extend them beyond two-step distributions. The proof relies on uniform Lipschitz estimates for the distance, of independent interest.

Optimization and Control.title: Quantum lower bounds for convex optimization and real matrix-vector query problems
Optimization and Control.summary: We (the author and the AI systems that did the heavy lifting) show that the quantum query complexity of minimizing a convex function over a convex subset of $\mathbb{R}^n$ with evaluation and membership queries is $\tildeΩ(n)$, nearly matching the best known upper bound. In particular, we show this even for quadratic minimization, which is equivalent to inverting an $n \times n$ real matrix using matrix-vector queries. We also show linear or nearly linear lower bounds on the quantum query complexity of computing the trace, the sign of the determinant, and the magnitude of the determinant of a real matrix in the matrix-vector query model. We use a novel quantum lower bound technique, the determinantal witness method, based on identifying a witness whose Fourier transform vanishes on low-rank matrices and that correlates well with the function being computed.
Optimization and Control.comment: 29 pages. v2: additional discussion of technical approach in introduction, minor corrections

Optimization and Control.title: Optimization-based lane-changing trajectory planning in mixed traffic with embedded input convex neural networks
Optimization and Control.summary: Lane-changing (LC) maneuvers are highly challenging vehicle interactions, with substantial implications for traffic safety and efficiency. Developing effective LC strategies for connected and automated vehicles in mixed traffic is complicated by the uncertainty associated with surrounding-vehicle behavior and the computational burden of embedding realistic prediction models within optimization schemes. To capture these complex interactions while retaining tractability, this study proposes a data-driven optimization framework that embeds neural network (NN) surrogates for safety and lateral comfort within a Bézier-curve-based trajectory planner. Specifically, the safety cost during the LC process is quantified via a surrogate composed of an input convex recurrent neural network (ICRNN) encoding the planned trajectory, a fully input convex neural network (FICNN) embedding the LC duration, and a partially input convex neural network (PICNN) decoder fusing them with historical traffic states; separately, another FICNN surrogate approximates the optimal lateral comfort cost as a function of the LC duration. Both surrogates are embedded via linear programming (LP) formulations, avoiding the binary variables required by conventional mixed-integer programming (MIP) approaches for NN-embedded optimization. We further theoretically establish their exactness at optimality and extend the framework to problems with additional analytical objective terms and multiple surrogates. Experiments on a hybrid dataset combining real-world and simulated trajectories demonstrate that the proposed method achieves surrogate accuracy competitive with unconstrained baselines while substantially improving optimization efficiency over conventional MIPs. Closed-loop simulations further show that the proposed planners markedly reduce the weighted planning cost and consistently outperform baseline methods.

Optimization and Control.title: Variable Metric Three Operator Splitting
Optimization and Control.summary:
To minimize the sum $f + g + h$ of three convex functions when $f$ is differentiable with a Lipschitz-continuous gradient,
  we present a proximal algorithm, variable-metric three operator splitting (VMTOS), a generalization of the three operator splitting (TOS) scheme of Davis and Yin.
  We establish convergence guarantees by controlling changes in the metric.
  The smallest saddle-point residual among the first $k$ primal-dual iterates is $\tilde{O}(k^{-1/2})$.
  When $f$ and the convex conjugate $h^*$ are strongly convex and the accepted metrics and their inverses are uniformly bounded, the rate improves to $\tilde{O}(β^k)$ for some $β\in (0,1)$.
  We develop a practical Barzilai--Borwein update for diagonal metrics that satisfies our bound on metric changes.
  Under the same strong convexity assumptions, this update guarantees the required uniform metric bounds, yielding R-linear convergence.
  Numerical experiments on benchmark optimization problems show that VMTOS is competitive with other proximal algorithms.

Optimization and Control.title: Controllability of Nonlocal Partial Differential Equations
Optimization and Control.summary: This chapter provides a short survey of recent developments in the controllability of nonlocal partial differential equations. We first review controllability results for evolution equations involving nonlocal spatial operators. Particular attention is devoted to unique continuation properties, observability inequalities, and Carleman estimates in establishing controllability properties. We then discuss controllability issues for partial differential equations with memory terms, highlighting how memory effects influence reachable states, null controllability, and exact controllability. We review and compare various analytical techniques developed to overcome the difficulties arising from the nonlocal structure. We also provide a critical assessment of some of these methods. Throughout the chapter, we emphasize the interplay between controllability and observability, the adaptation of classical control methods to nonlocal settings, and the distinctive phenomena that arise in comparison with local equations. We then discuss geometric inequalities and their role in the controllability of diffusion models. The chapter concludes with a discussion of current challenges and several open problems, aiming to provide directions for future research.

Optimization and Control.title: One Model, Two Roles: Emergent Specialization in a Shared Recurrent Transformer
Optimization and Control.summary: Can a shared-weight recurrent Transformer---one that repeatedly applies the same Transformer to update evolving latent states---develop distinct internal roles without being partitioned into separate modules? We study this in Asymmetric Input Recurrence (AIR), a minimal two-state reasoning architecture in which the same Transformer model is reused for both updates (per literature, L and H) and the only built-in difference in the update rule is that the encoded input is injected during L-updates but not H-updates. Across Sudoku-Extreme and Maze, decoded rollouts reveal a consistent split: $z_H$ behaves like a fully committed proposal state, whereas $z_L$ retains local uncertainty and shifting intermediate structure. Freeze interventions provide evidence of dynamical dependence between the two states, with responses that vary across tasks, intervention directions, and seeds. Ablations show that to induce specialization, the shared model needs to be able to tell the two update types apart, either from input injection asymmetry or from a separate level token. Mechanistically, attention analysis shows that L-updates are consistently more local than H-updates in both Sudoku and Maze. Together, these results show that, in a two-state recurrent setting, a clear state-identity signal can induce stable, related functional roles inside a shared-parameter recurrent Transformer. Code is available at https://github.com/juchengshen/air.
Optimization and Control.comment: Accepted at NeurIPS 2026. 29 pages, 18 figures, 13 tables

Optimization and Control.title: Continuous Envy-Free Allocation via Reciprocal Preference Matrices: An Alternative to Sperner-Based Discretization
Optimization and Control.summary: Fair allocation problems on a continuous simplex are often approached through Sperner-type discretizations: agents label mesh vertices according to their preferences and a fully labelled elementary triangle gives a discrete localization of a fair outcome. We develop a continuous alternative for three agents and three alternatives by representing preferences with multiplicatively consistent reciprocal pairwise-comparison matrices. Two independent ratios per agent induce exact linear indifference boundaries and turn envy-free allocation into a finite-dimensional feasibility problem. For the six possible assignments, we introduce an assignment score $Φ$ built from the agents' consistent priority vectors and prove that an incentive solution component is nonempty if and only if its assignment is the unique minimizer of $Φ$, whereas a disincentive solution component is nonempty if and only if its assignment is the unique maximizer. Consequently, the strict solution region is either empty or a unique convex preference region whose closure lies in the interior of the simplex. The weak solution set is never empty and degenerates exactly when $Φ$ has ties. We also compare the exact continuous formulation with Sperner-based discretization, including the boundary convention required in the disincentive model. Under exact consistency, the model uses six independent pairwise thresholds, whereas a regular triangular mesh with resolution $m$ contains $(m+1)(m+2)/2$ vertices. The method therefore exchanges a stronger parametric preference assumption for an exact continuous solution set and a resolution-independent elicitation stage.

Optimization and Control.title: Mixed-Precision GPU Acceleration for Large-Scale Minimum Enclosing Ball Problems
Optimization and Control.summary: A mixed-precision GPU-oriented optimization framework is developed for computing the minimum enclosing ball of a collection of balls. The approach is built on an equivalent second-order cone programming reformulation and a relative-type inexact proximal augmented Lagrangian method (ripALM), which provides a high-accuracy optimization backbone while solving the inner subproblems only to a progress-dependent relative accuracy. The proximal augmented Lagrangian inherits a constraint-wise separable structure: its objective, gradient, generalized Hessian, and multiplier updates can be efficiently evaluated on GPUs as parallel maps over the input balls followed by reductions. To further improve efficiency, a mixed-precision reduction strategy is introduced. A low-precision ripALM run identifies balls near the approximate boundary, a high-precision ripALM run refines the reduced problem, and a full a posteriori feasibility check detects and reintroduces any violated discarded balls. Thus, low precision is used only for screening and warm starting, while the final feasibility is enforced against the original problem. Experiments on synthetic and real-data instances show that the proposed methods can compute accurate solutions, with GPU execution providing substantial speedups and mixed-precision reduction further reducing running times on most tested instances.

Optimization and Control.title: Branch and Price for Railway Crew Scheduling: Benchmark Instances and Computational Study
Optimization and Control.summary: Railway crew scheduling consists of assigning a set of tasks to crew members in the form of feasible duties so as to minimise costs, and is one of the key planning problems faced by railway operators. While column generation is the dominant solution method, literature on exact branch-and-price approaches is scarce. Moreover, few publicly available benchmark instances exist. We conduct a systematic computational study of branch and price for railway crew scheduling, evaluating the contribution of branching rules, primal heuristics, and reduced cost fixing. To this end, we introduce a novel library of 100 benchmark instances, ranging in size from 90 to 3,016 tasks, each provided in a single-depot and a multi-depot variant. The instances are generated by mimicking the railway planning process, validated against data from Netherlands Railways, and publicly available with best known solutions and a solution checker. We report average optimality gaps below 1% across all instance sizes, driven primarily by the strong performance of primal heuristics, whereas branching and reduced cost fixing contribute little to closing the gap. Branch and price also outperforms a multi-commodity flow formulation, which fails to find a feasible solution on many of the smallest instances. Our findings provide support for the popularity of column generation-based primal heuristics, and show that improving the dual bound remains the main challenge for exact methods in railway crew scheduling.

Optimization and Control.title: A Retrospective-Approximation Interior-Point Method
Optimization and Control.summary: An algorithm is proposed, analyzed, and tested for solving nonlinearly constrained continuous optimization problem instances wherein the objective function is defined by an expectation over a random variable argument and the constraints include inequalities (and perhaps equalities) involving functions that may be nonconvex. The algorithm combines a retrospective-approximation strategy for handling the objective and an interior-point approach for handling the constraints. In each iteration of an outer loop, the objective is approximated by an empirical average over a set of realizations of the random variable argument and the resulting sampled problem is solved with an interior-point method that allows inexact search-direction computations for computational flexibility. Termination conditions for the interior-point method are tailored for those needed for convergence guarantees by the outer loop. Over the outer loop, the sample set is updated adaptively in such a manner that convergence guarantees for solving the original optimization problem can be assured. The results of numerical experiments are presented, which show that the proposed algorithm can outperform competing methods that have comparable theoretical guarantees.

Optimization and Control.title: A Feasible-Direction-Type Method for Nonconvex Optimization with Infeasible Starts
Optimization and Control.summary: We develop an infeasible-start extension of the Topkis--Veinott feasible-direction method for nonconvex composite optimization. At each main iteration, a strongly convex local model is used to obtain objective descent while limiting increases in constraint violation. A separate feasibility-reduction step is invoked when feasibility improvement is needed. Under a feasibility-reduction condition, we establish the standard first-order rate for reducing the Fritz John residual and constraint violation. We then verify that both proximal-gradient and regularized Gauss--Newton methods applied to minimizing the squared constraint-violation function satisfy the required feasibility-reduction property under a Polyak--Łojasiewicz condition. Numerical experiments compare the reduction methods, including an experimental prox-linear variant, and compare the scalar-regularized and curvature-enhanced subproblem formulations.

Optimization and Control.title: A Feasible Direction Method with Active-Set Identification for Derivative-Free Optimization
Optimization and Control.summary: We propose a model-based trust region method for derivative-free optimization with simulation-based inequality constraints. We are motivated by settings of simulation optimization in which both function evaluations at infeasible points may be unreliable and constraint evaluations are expensive. Our method maintains feasible incumbents and computes steps from a subproblem suitable for a feasible-direction method in order to encourage generation of feasible trial points. To reduce the computational cost of modeling the constraints, we describe an active-set estimation scheme that permits modeling with only a subset of constraints in each subproblem, as opposed to maintaining models of all constraints. We show that every limit point of the incumbents generated by our method is a Fritz-John point, and is additionally a KKT point under the Mangasarian-Fromovitz constraint qualification. Under standard nondegeneracy conditions, the active-set estimate identifies, within finite time, all constraints active at the limit point of the incumbents. Experiments on CUTEst problems show that our method generates feasible trial points more often than a comparable SQP-based approach and is competitive with an appropriate comparator in budgeted settings.

Optimization and Control.title: Safeguarded Neurally-Accelerated Preconditioning (SNAP) framework for Nonlinear Optimization
Optimization and Control.summary: We introduce the Safeguarded Neurally-Accelerated Preconditioning (SNAP) framework for hybridizing nonlinear optimization methods with pre-trained neural operators (NOs). SNAP targets parametric optimization problems arising from variational formulations of nonlinear partial differential equations (PDEs), where many parameter instances require repeated solves. Inspired by multilevel line-search methods, SNAP operates in cycles, combining classical optimization steps with a search direction generated by a pre-trained NO. Since NO-generated search directions carry no a priori descent guarantee, SNAP employs an a posteriori safeguard by accepting only corrections that satisfy prescribed descent and acceptance conditions. We prove global convergence of the SNAP algorithm and show that it preserves the convergence rate of the underlying optimization method independently of the employed NO architecture. Moreover, we also show that when the NO corrections are sufficiently accurate, SNAP converges faster, with the improvement directly related to the NO training error. To demonstrate SNAP's efficiency in practice, we run numerical experiments on a diverse set of nonlinear parametric optimization problems, including parametric minimal surface, Allen--Cahn, and nonlinear Helmholtz problems. The efficiency of SNAP is demonstrated by comparing two NO architectures, Fourier neural operator (FNO) and Transolver, and by using SNAP as a standalone solver and as a nonlinear preconditioner. Our numerical results show a substantial reduction in the number of required iterations, while demonstrating robustness and generalization across a wide range of problem parameters and mesh resolutions.

Optimization and Control.title: Rennala NSGD: Asynchronous Stochastic Optimization Beyond Euclidean Geometry
Optimization and Control.summary: The empirical success of matrix-aware optimizers, such as Muon (Jordan et al., 2024) and Shampoo (arXiv:1802.09568), highlights the potential of non-Euclidean geometry for deep learning, including large language model (LLM) training. Despite this progress, the theoretical understanding of stochastic optimization in general normed spaces remains limited, particularly in distributed settings. We analyze minibatch stochastic gradient descent (SGD) for smooth nonconvex optimization with respect to an arbitrary norm on a finite-dimensional space. Using the framework of $κ$-regular normed spaces (arXiv:0809.0813), we derive high-probability oracle complexity bounds under a light-tail condition stated directly in the dual norm induced by the update norm. The bounds make the dependence on geometry explicit through the regularity constant $κ$ of the dual space. In the Euclidean case, our bound recovers the standard minibatch SGD rate up to logarithmic factors. For some non-Euclidean geometries and noise models, it is sharper than bounds obtained by converting a Euclidean noise assumption, reducing a linear dimension dependence to a logarithmic one. Building on this framework, we introduce Rennala NSGD, a semi-asynchronous distributed algorithm, and establish wall-clock time complexity guarantees under fixed, heterogeneous worker computation times. In the Euclidean case ($κ=1$), our bound matches the parameter dependence of classical Rennala SGD up to logarithmic factors.
Optimization and Control.comment: Accepted at NeurIPS 2026. 111 pages, 2 algorithms, 3 tables

Optimization and Control.title: cuPDQPx: A GPU-Accelerated Restarted Halpern PDHG for Large-Scale Convex Quadratic Programming
Optimization and Control.summary: We present cuPDQPx, a GPU-accelerated, factorization-free first-order solver for large-scale convex quadratic programming (QP). Building on the restarted reflected Halpern primal-dual framework of cuPDLPx, we introduce an auxiliary-variable splitting that yields explicit updates without linearizing the quadratic objective or solving inner quadratic subproblems. A preconditioned proximal point interpretation yields both sublinear and linear fixed-point residual convergence guarantees. For practical efficiency, cuPDQPx integrates diagonal preconditioning, step-size selection, adaptive restart, and adaptive primal and quadratic weight updates. cuPDQPx is implemented in C and CUDA with optimized sparse matrix-vector products, kernel fusion, and CUDA Graphs. Numerical experiments on the Maros-Mészáros collection, a convex subset of QPLIB, and synthetic large-scale QPs demonstrate that cuPDQPx has strong numerical performance at both $10^{-4}$ and $10^{-8}$ tolerances.
